formulas.name: Global inflation
formulas.expression: soldPreDraft = Σ pick.preDraftAtPick ; expectedPoolRemaining = max(1, totalBudget − soldPreDraft) ; inflation = remainingLeague / expectedPoolRemaining, where remainingLeague = max(0, totalBudget − Σ paid)
formulas.inputs: team initialBudgets (Σ = totalBudget), recorded pick amounts, preDraftAtPick snapshots
formulas.outputRange: 0 to unbounded. Measured: with an exact-$1200 pool and 75%-of-fair hammer prices, inflation reads 58.20 at pick 67, 96.33 at pick 69, 144.00 at pick 70, 287.00 at pick 71. With the shipped $1211 default pool it collapses to 0.000 from pick 63 onward.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: preDraftAtPick falls back to the player's CURRENT preDraft (line 546-547), then to 0. A pick on a player deleted from the pool contributes 0 to soldPreDraft, silently deflating the denominator.
formulas.constants: max(1, …) denominator floor; max(0, …) numerator floor. No backend counterpart.
formulas.mathIssues: Numerator and denominator are on two different scales — team budgets vs board dollars. They coincide only because the synced pool happens to sum to $1200. The denominator → 0 as the pool is exhausted, so the ratio diverges hyperbolically exactly at the endgame. The max(1,…) clamp prevents division by zero but not the blowup.
formulas.validated: No. Tested only at the opening state and three single-pick perturbations (draft-logic.test.js:179-289).

formulas.name: Tier inflation
formulas.expression: heat(T) = Σ paid in T / Σ preDraftAtPick in T ; conf(T) = min(1, nPicks(T)/3) ; tierMult(T) = conf·heat + (1−conf)·1 ; combinedInflation = inflation × tierMult
formulas.inputs: picks bucketed by tierForPreDraft(preDraftAtPick)
formulas.outputRange: unbounded; a single $60→$200 S-tier pick with n=1 gives conf=0.333 and heat=3.33, i.e. tierMult 1.78
formulas.missingDataBehavior: heat=null and conf=0 when a tier has no picks → tierMult = 1.0 (no adjustment). Correct.
formulas.constants: TIER_CONFIDENCE_MIN_SAMPLES = 3 (line 66) — invented, no calibration cited. Not present in any backend code.
formulas.mathIssues: heat is uncapped in both directions. There is no shrinkage toward the global inflation figure, only toward 1.0, so a hot tier compounds with an already-hot global inflation multiplicatively.
formulas.validated: Partially — draft-logic.test.js:1124-1171 checks the blend algebra on synthetic 1–3 pick samples.

formulas.name: Budget advantage
formulas.expression: otherTeamsRemaining = max(0, remainingLeague − myRemaining) ; avgPerOtherTeam = otherTeamsRemaining / max(1, nTeams−1) ; BA = floor((myRemaining/avgPerOtherTeam) × 100)/100
formulas.inputs: per-team remaining dollars
formulas.outputRange: 0 to unbounded. Opening state on the shipped defaults: 417 / 71.18 = 5.86 raw, truncated to 5.85.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: avgPerOtherTeam ≤ 0 → BA = 1 (line 527-528).
formulas.constants: 2-decimal truncation, deliberately to match the Google Sheet cell-for-cell (comment lines 530-533).
formulas.mathIssues: Uses the MEAN of other teams' remaining dollars, while myWinningBid uses the MAX. The two ceilings in the same formula are inconsistent measures of the same field.
formulas.validated: Yes for the opening state — draft-logic.test.js:139.

formulas.name: Slot-adjusted effective budget
formulas.expression: effectiveBudget = 0 if slotsRemaining ≤ 0, else max(0, remaining − max(0, slotsRemaining − 1))
formulas.inputs: remaining dollars, slotsRemaining
formulas.missingDataBehavior: non-numeric coerces to 0.
formulas.constants: $1 reserve per other remaining slot.
formulas.mathIssues: Sound as written. Its input slotsRemaining is corrupted by the 6-slot clamp at line 1411 (see findings).
formulas.validated: Yes — draft-logic.test.js:984-1005.

formulas.name: Phase multiplier
formulas.expression: slotPressure = clamp(0,1, 1 − mySlotsRemaining/myInitialSlots) ; phaseMultiplier = 1 + slotPressure × 0.5
formulas.inputs: my slot counts
formulas.missingDataBehavior: myInitialSlots ≤ 0 → slotPressure = 0.
formulas.constants: PHASE_LATE_BOOST = 0.5 (line 60) — invented, no derivation or backtest cited. Not mirrored in any backend code.
formulas.mathIssues: Scales the bid UP as slots run out, which is the correct direction, but it is applied to theoreticalMaxBid which is already unconstrained by remaining budget — so it amplifies an already-unbounded number.
formulas.validated: Direction tested only — draft-logic.test.js:1172-1206.

formulas.name: Inflated fair / theoretical max bid / winning bid
formulas.expression: inflatedFair = floor(preDraft × inflation × tierMult) ; theoreticalMaxBid = floor(preDraft × (1 + aggression×(BA−1)) × inflation × tierMult × phaseMultiplier) ; myWinningBid = max(0, min(theoreticalMaxBid, max(1, topCompetitorMax + 1)))
formulas.inputs: preDraft, inflation, tierMult, aggression (default 0.09), BA, phaseMultiplier, topCompetitorMax
formulas.outputRange: Opening state, Jeremiyah Love: preDraft 135 → Fair $135, Enforce $108, Max Bid $193, Win at $69. Only 5 of 72 rows carry a nonzero fair−winBid surplus at open.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: preDraft coerces to 0 → every derived figure is 0.
formulas.constants: DEFAULT_AGGRESSION 0.09, DEFAULT_ENFORCE_PCT 0.8 (lines 45-46, both from the source Google Sheet). No calibration beyond "the sheet said so".
formulas.mathIssues: topCompetitorMax is a SINGLE league-wide scalar (lines 479-485), so "Win at" is the same number for every player whose ceiling it binds — measured: 9 of 72 rows share "Win at $69" at draft open. Neither myWinningBid nor theoreticalMaxBid is bounded by MY remaining dollars or MY remaining roster slots.
formulas.validated: Opening-state values pinned at draft-logic.test.js:155-178. Never validated against a budget or roster constraint.

formulas.name: Next-best-target EV
formulas.expression: surplus = max(0, inflatedFair − myWinningBid) ; tagWeight = 1.5 if target else 1.0 (avoid excluded) ; scarcityBoost = 10 × max(0, 0.3 − remainingRatio) if remainingRatio < 0.3 else 0 ; ev = surplus × tagWeight + scarcityBoost
formulas.inputs: enrichedPlayers, tierStats
formulas.outputRange: Measured at draft open: 66, 33, 21, 14, 4 for the top 5 — exactly inflatedFair − 69 for each. Only 5 rows survive the ev>0 filter.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: ev ≤ 0 and not target-tagged → row is dropped (line 1958), so most of the pool never appears.
formulas.constants: tagWeight 1.5, scarcity coefficient 10, TIER_SCARCITY_URGENT 0.3 — all invented, none calibrated, none mirrored in backend code.
formulas.mathIssues: Because theoreticalMaxBid = inflatedFair × (1 + aggression×(BA−1)) × phaseMultiplier, whenever BA > 1 the max bid exceeds fair, so surplus is ZERO for every player the competitor cap does not bind. For the players it does bind, myWinningBid is a constant, so ev = fair − constant, a monotone transform of preDraft. When BA < 1 the multiplier is a constant < 1, so ev = fair × constant — again monotone in preDraft. Verified empirically: the returned order is byte-identical to a plain preDraft-descending sort in both regimes. scarcityBoost is capped at 3, an order of magnitude below typical surplus, so it can only break near-ties.
formulas.validated: No. draft-logic.test.js:1623-1684 asserts orderings on 2–3 synthetic rows and never compares against a naive sort.

formulas.name: Nomination score
formulas.expression: phasePct = clamp(0,1, leagueSpentPct) ; gap = vendorDollar − ourDollar (require ≥1) ; gapPct = gap/ourDollar ; score = (1−phasePct)×vendorDollar + phasePct×(gapPct×100)
formulas.inputs: preDraft, ktcDollar or idpTradeCalcDollar, leagueSpentPct
formulas.outputRange: early-draft: raw vendor dollars ($1..$140); late-draft: percent overrate ×100
formulas.missingDataBehavior: ourDollar ≤ 0 or vendorDollar ≤ 0 → row skipped entirely. On a fresh page load, hydrateWorkspace strips ktcDollar/idpTradeCalcDollar (line 1714-1719), so the panel is empty until the auto-sync round-trips.
formulas.constants: gap ≥ 1 floor; ×100 scaling of gapPct to make it commensurate with dollars — an arbitrary unit bridge between two incompatible quantities.
formulas.mathIssues: The two blended terms have different units (dollars vs percent×100), so the crossover point is meaningless. More seriously, vendorDollar is systematically inflated by _vendor_dollars_for_rookies (measured 1.181x for KTC on live data), so `gap ≥ 1` is satisfied by essentially every KTC-covered rookie — 42 of 42 on live data.
formulas.validated: No. Tests supply hand-written vendor dollars that cannot expose the scale bias.

formulas.name: Best-value score
formulas.expression: qualify: gap = ourDollar − vendorDollar, require ≥1 ; gapPct = gap/vendorDollar ; sort desc. backfill: gap = ourDollar − vendorDollar (may be NEGATIVE) ; gapPct = gap/vendorDollar if vendorDollar>0 else 0 ; score = ourDollar ; sort by ourDollar desc.
formulas.inputs: same as nomination
formulas.outputRange: On live data: qualifying set is EMPTY (0/42 KTC, 0/21 IDP-only), so 100% of the ten rendered rows are backfill rows with gapPct ≤ 0.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: vendorDollar = 0 → gapPct = 0 and the row still renders with the green "underrates" badge and a rationale reading "no KTC comp — top remaining fair price".
formulas.constants: gap ≥ 1 floor; limit 10.
formulas.mathIssues: The backfill branch emits rows with negative gapPct into a list the UI renders as "KTC / IDPTC underrates vs our board" with a green minus-prefixed badge. page.jsx:2668 renders `−{Math.round(gapPct*100)}%`, so a backfill row with gapPct = −0.057 renders literally as "−-6%" and its tooltip reads "underrates by -6%".
formulas.validated: No. draft-logic.test.js:2661-2670 asserts the backfill exists and that gap ≤ 0, but no test covers how a negative gap renders.

formulas.name: Sheet Hill-curve rookie dollars
formulas.expression: decay = clip(0.6 × stdev(v[0..5])/mean(v[0..5]), 0.03, 0.08) ; w[i] = e^(−decay·i)·(1 − 0.2·e^(−0.12·i)) ; term1[i] = v[i]w[i]/Σvw ; excess[i] = max(0, spine[i]−1) ; term2[i] = excess[i]/Σexcess ; floor[i] = 1 + (1 if 48≤i<60) ; C[i] = floor[i] + (1200 − Σfloor)·(0.6·term1[i] + 0.4·term2[i]) ; half-dollar monotone rounding with K caps 4 (rows 49-60) / 2 (rows 61-72) and non-increasing constraint ; R1 carryover spread over the first M=12 rows
formulas.inputs: raw board values; spine = workbook column E2:E73 (median+mean of 2023-25 realised values ÷ 2)
formulas.outputRange: Reproduced exactly at n=72 against the workbook's own B column: [134.5, 100.5, 93.0, 80.5, 75.5, 68.5, 54.5, 53.5, 46.0, 44.5, 41.0, 35.5, …] = column L verbatim, Σ = 1200.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Workbook unreadable → flat spine of 1.0 and r5_bonus 0 (line 7121-7122), which silently changes term2 from a historical anchor to a uniform zero and shifts the whole curve. No stamp tells the caller this happened.
formulas.constants: 0.6/0.03/0.08 decay clip; 0.2 and 0.12 in the weight; 0.6/0.4 blend of decay vs spine; row windows 48-60 and 60-72; caps 4 and 2; M = 12. All are ports of one user's Google Sheet — not calibrated against draft outcomes anywhere in the repo. The spine IS empirically grounded (three seasons of realised values), the rest is not.
formulas.mathIssues: The row windows (48-60, 60-72) and M=12 hardcode a 12-team, 6-round draft. Called with any other n — which _vendor_dollars_for_rookies does on every request — those windows land on the wrong rounds or fall off the end entirely.
formulas.validated: No test in tests/ references this function. My reproduction confirms the port is faithful to the sheet; nothing confirms the sheet is right.

formulas.name: Vendor dollar conversion
formulas.expression: eligible = rookies with a positive raw value for that vendor ; sort desc by vendor raw ; dollars = _rookie_dollars_from_values(values, 1200) ; map name → dollars[rank]
formulas.inputs: our top-72 rookie pool with per-vendor canonicalSiteValues
formulas.outputRange: Live 2026-08-04: 42 KTC-eligible rows spend the full $1200 → 1.181x inflation vs our dollars on the same names. 63 IDPTC-eligible rows → 1.012x.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Vendor doesn't rank a rookie → no map entry → the frontend treats vendorDollar as 0 and (for bestValueOnBoard) backfills the row.
formulas.constants: total = DRAFT_TOTAL_BUDGET = 1200, unconditionally, regardless of row count.
formulas.mathIssues: The comment at lines 7063-7065 says "Pad to top_n so the formula stays calibrated against the same 72-row Hill curve the picks use. Vendors that don't rank a full 72 just leave the tail empty." No padding is performed. Measured effect of row count alone, holding values fixed: rank-1 dollar is $134.5 at n=72, $146.5 at n=30, $160.0 at n=20.
formulas.validated: No test coverage whatsoever.

formulas.name: Sleeper-derived pick value
formulas.expression: value = contract rankDerivedValue for "{season} Pick {round}.{slot:02d}", else flat = {1:7000, 2:4000, 3:2000, 4:1200, 5:700, 6:300}.get(round, 100) ; then scaled so all picks sum to $1200 by largest-remainder rounding
formulas.inputs: latest_contract_data, Sleeper rosters/users/traded_picks
formulas.outputRange: $0..$1200 total across 2 seasons × 4 rounds × N teams
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No contract row → the hardcoded flat table, indistinguishable in the payload from a real Hill-curve value.
formulas.constants: _TARGET_TOTAL_BUDGET 1200; draft_rounds default 4; num_teams default 12; the 7000/4000/2000/1200/700/300 table.
formulas.mathIssues: Verified against the live contract: 2026 Pick R.SS rows exist, 2027 Pick R.SS rows DO NOT (only 2027 Early/Mid/Late tier rows). So the entire second season resolves to the flat table. Summing the real 2026 values (156,703) against the fabricated 2027 values (170,400) gives the fabricated half 52.1% of the board — $625 of the $1,200. A fabricated 2027 first (7000) also outranks a real 2026 pick 1.06 (4945).
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_draft_capital_fallback.py:123 pins the flat fallback as intended behaviour rather than flagging it.

formulas.name: Effective auction power S-curve
formulas.expression: med = median(raw) ; mad = median(|raw − med|) ; spread = max(mad×1.4826, 0.01×grand/n) ; w[i] = raw[i]×(1 + 0.35·tanh((raw[i]−med)/spread/1.25)) ; w[leader] += 0.15·spread·tanh(lead/spread) ; scaled = w × (Σraw/Σw) ; largest-remainder round to Σraw
formulas.inputs: {team: raw auction dollars}
formulas.missingDataBehavior: <2 teams or grand ≤ 0 → identity. Degenerate spread → identity.
formulas.constants: AP_PREMIUM_GAIN 0.35, AP_CURVATURE 1.25, AP_LEAPFROG_WEIGHT 0.15, MAD scale 1.4826, spread floor 0.01×(grand/n). The docstring calls them "conservative defaults" and "priors"; Phase 2 (the Monte-Carlo mini-auction that would validate them) is explicitly unbuilt. Both copies carry the same values — no drift.
formulas.mathIssues: The docstring at src/api/auction_power.py:68-70 promises the per-team multiplier is "bounded to [1−gain, 1+gain]". That bound holds pre-normalization only. Measured continuous multipliers after renormalization: a 12-team field at [110,100×10,90] gives [1.3434 … 0.6462] and a whale field gives 0.5055 — both outside [0.65, 1.35]. Worse, the spread floor makes the lens MOST aggressive when the field is MOST equal: a 6-team field at [201,200,200,200,200,199] — a $2 real spread — is rendered as [227.8, 199.9×4, 172.5], a $55 spread.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_auction_power_parity.py exists but does not exercise the near-degenerate field.

formulas.name: Target Board portfolio buffer
formulas.expression: nonTargetSlotsLeft = max(0, mySlotsRemaining − remainingTargetCount) ; portfolioBuffer = myRemaining − Σ myWinningBid over remaining targets − nonTargetSlotsLeft
formulas.inputs: target board membership, myWinningBid per target, my budget and slots
formulas.outputRange: Measured: 2 slots left, $413 remaining, 6 targets whose winning bids sum to $414 → buffer −1 → "Short $1 — trim a target or lower your ceiling". The two most expensive targets I could actually take cost $138.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty board → status "idle".
formulas.constants: tight threshold $10 (line 856).
formulas.mathIssues: Sums the cost of ALL remaining targets regardless of how many roster slots I hold. It answers "can I afford my whole wishlist" — a question with no bearing on a draft where I can only take mySlotsRemaining of them. This is the only budget check on the page and it is the wrong one.
formulas.validated: No — draft-logic.test.js:1980-2049 never sets slots below target count.

formulas.name: Draft-review team grading
formulas.expression: ratio = Σ inflatedFair / Σ paid per team, sorted descending ; portfolioRatio same for my picks ; bestSteal / worstOverpay = argmax/argmin of (currentInflatedFair − paid)
formulas.inputs: picks, CURRENT enriched fair values
formulas.missingDataBehavior: paid = 0 → ratio 0; player missing from the pool → fair 0 and valueVsFair 0.
formulas.constants: none
formulas.mathIssues: Uses CURRENT inflated fair, so the whole leaderboard re-ranks after every subsequent pick — the grade of a completed pick is not stable. The docstring at line 2265-2267 acknowledges and defends this. Separately, a ratio metric rewards cheap picks disproportionately: $1 paid for a $2 player scores 2.00 and outranks $135 paid for a $200 player at 1.48.
formulas.validated: draft-logic.test.js:2778-2860.

findings.title: Every bid recommendation ignores my remaining budget and my remaining roster slots
findings.rootCause: theoreticalMaxBid is a function of preDraft, aggression, budget advantage, inflation and phase multiplier only; myWinningBid caps it against the richest RIVAL's effective budget. Neither reads myRemaining, mySlotsRemaining, or my own effectiveBudget. The class of number the page calls "Win at" is a competitor-ceiling estimate, not a feasible bid.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:717-731 — `const theoreticalMaxBid = Math.floor(preDraft * (1 + aggression * (budgetAdvantage - 1)) * combinedInflation * phaseMultiplier);` then `const myWinningBid = Math.max(0, Math.min(theoreticalMaxBid, winByCompetitor));` where `winByCompetitor = Math.max(1, competitorCeiling + 1)` and competitorCeiling is `topCompetitorMax`, computed at :479-485 by scanning only `if (i === myTeamIdx) continue;`. Reproduced: after spending all $417 across all 6 slots (myRemaining = 0, mySlotsRemaining = 0, my effectiveBudget = 0), the board still reports Kenyon Sadiq at Max Bid $90 / WIN AT $69, and Caleb Downs at Max Bid $76 / WIN AT $69.
findings.userImpact: The single number the module docstring designates as the headline figure (line 385: "The UI should surface myWinningBid as the headline figure") is unimplementable by the user it is shown to. A user with $12 left is told to bid $69. This is a recommender that does not optimize under, or even respect, the constraint it exists to manage.
findings.recommendedFix: Clamp both figures: `myWinningBid = min(theoreticalMaxBid, topCompetitorMax + 1, effectiveBudgetFor(myRemaining, mySlotsRemaining))`, and render a distinct state (e.g. "can't bid") when my effective budget is 0 rather than a dollar figure.

findings.title: "Next Best Targets" is a preDraft sort wearing an EV model's clothes
findings.rootCause: surplus = max(0, inflatedFair − myWinningBid). But myWinningBid = min(fair × k, C) where k = (1 + aggression×(BA−1)) × phaseMultiplier is a per-board constant and C = topCompetitorMax + 1 is a league-wide scalar. When k > 1 the max() is zero for everything below the cap; when k < 1 surplus = fair × (1−k), proportional to fair. In both regimes the ranking is a monotone function of preDraft.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1949-1957. Reproduced with the shipped defaults: at draft open nextBestTargets returns exactly 5 rows and `JSON.stringify(returned names) === JSON.stringify(top-5 by preDraft)` evaluates true. After forcing BA to 0, it returns 13 rows in the order Fernando Mendoza, Makai Lemon, Carnell Tate, Jordyn Tyson, Sonny Styles, Caleb Downs … — identical to the undrafted preDraft-descending order. The scarcityBoost term is capped at 10 × 0.3 = 3, versus surplus values in the tens.
findings.userImpact: A panel headed "Next Best Targets" with the subtitle "EV = (fair − winBid) × tag weight + scarcity boost" tells the user nothing the #-column ordering does not already tell them, while implying a value calculation happened. At draft open it shows 5 of 72 players because everything else scores exactly 0.
findings.recommendedFix: Either make surplus a genuine edge (fair minus an estimate of the player's actual clearing price — e.g. tier-heat-projected price, or the vendor dollar) or rename the panel to what it is. Do not ship a monotone re-labelling of an existing column as an EV model.

findings.title: Vendor "Market" dollars are inflated by row count, so KTC overrates literally every rookie it covers
findings.rootCause: _vendor_dollars_for_rookies calls _rookie_dollars_from_values with total=1200 over only the rookies that vendor prices. The Hill formula always distributes the full $1200 across whatever list it receives, so a vendor covering 42 of 72 rookies has its whole column scaled up by roughly 72/42 in aggregate.
findings.evidence: server.py:7058-7068. The comment at 7063-7065 claims a pad that the code does not perform: `# Pad to top_n so the formula stays calibrated against the same / # 72-row Hill curve the picks use.` followed immediately by `values = [r[key] for r in eligible]` and `dollars = _rookie_dollars_from_values(values, total)`. Measured on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json: 42 KTC-eligible rookies in the top-72 pool; Σ KTC dollars = 1200 vs Σ our dollars over the same 42 names = 1016, a 1.181x bias. Row-count-only effect holding values fixed: rank-1 = $134.5 at n=72, $146.5 at n=30, $160.0 at n=20.
findings.userImpact: All 42 KTC-covered rookies register as "KTC overrates us" and feed the "Good to nominate" panel; 25 of them would not after removing the bias. Symmetrically, ZERO rookies qualify for "Best value on the board" (0/42 on the KTC leg, 0/21 on the IDP-only leg), so that panel renders entirely from its backfill branch. The "Market" column on the rookie board carries the same bias.
findings.recommendedFix: Rank each vendor within the same 72-row frame — assign vendor-unranked rookies a value of 0 and keep the list length at 72 — or, simpler, renormalize each vendor's dollar map so it sums to Σ our dollars over the same names before comparing.

findings.title: Inflation diverges hyperbolically at the end of every draft, producing absurd late-draft prices
findings.rootCause: inflation = remainingLeague / max(1, totalBudget − soldPreDraft). The denominator is (team budgets) minus (board dollars) — two different accounting scales that happen to both total $1200 only in the synced case. As the pool is drafted, soldPreDraft → totalBudget and the denominator → 0.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:550-551 — `const expectedPoolRemaining = Math.max(1, totalBudget - soldPreDraft); const inflation = remainingLeague / expectedPoolRemaining;`. Reproduced with a pool summing to exactly $1200 and every pick hammering at 75% of fair: inflation reads 58.20 at pick 67, 96.33 at 69, 144.00 at 70, 287.00 at 71 — the last $1 rookie shows Fair $287 / Enforce $229. Reproduced with the shipped DEFAULT_ROOKIES pool (which sums to $1211, not $1200) and everyone paying 60% of fair: at pick 68 the raw denominator is −7, clamps to 1, and inflation = 475, rendering four $1 rookies at Fair $285 / Enforce $228 / Max Bid $1169.
findings.userImpact: The board becomes actively dangerous exactly at the moment it matters most — the endgame with money still on the table. A user following the Enforce column would bid $229 on a $1 dart. With the default seed pool the failure starts around pick 63 of 72.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute inflation over a bounded window (e.g. the last N picks) or floor the denominator at a meaningful fraction of the pool (e.g. max(0.05 × totalBudget, …)) and clamp the resulting multiplier to a sane band. Also reconcile the two scales: the denominator should be Σ preDraft of the whole pool, not the team-budget total.

findings.title: Sleeper-derived draft capital fabricates 52% of the board on live data — and the 503 guard added to prevent exactly this does not fire
findings.rootCause: build_sleeper_derived builds picks for current_season AND current_season+1, but the canonical contract carries slot-level rows only for the current class. Every next-season pick falls through _pick_value_from_contract to a hardcoded flat table. The endpoint's 503 guard fires only when there is NO contract at all.
findings.evidence: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:96-99 — `# Fallback: flat per-round value.  Round 1 ≈ 7000, Round 2 ≈ 4000, / flat = {1: 7000.0, 2: 4000.0, 3: 2000.0, 4: 1200.0, 5: 700.0, 6: 300.0}` reached from the loop at :175 `for season in (current_season, current_season + 1):`. Guard at server.py:8154 — `if not is_default_league and not latest_contract_data:`. Verified against exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json: 2026 Pick R.SS rows exist; 2027 Pick R.SS rows do not (only '2027 Early 1st' … '2027 Late 6th'). Σ real 2026 values (rounds 1-4) = 156,703 vs Σ fabricated 2027 = 170,400 → the fabricated half takes $625 of the $1,200. A fabricated 2027 first (7000) is priced above a real 2026 pick 1.06 (4945).
findings.userImpact: Every non-default league's draft-capital board — its per-team dollar totals, its bar chart, the budgets the /draft dashboard auto-loads, and the pick-stack values feeding /trade verdicts — is more than half invented, with no field distinguishing the invented rows. CLAUDE.md states this class of failure is "fixed"; it is not.
findings.recommendedFix: Return picks with `dollarValue: null` and a `unpricedPickYears` field when the contract cannot price them, and exclude them from teamTotals rather than filling from a table. Delete the flat table and the test that pins it (tests/api/test_draft_capital_fallback.py:123).

findings.title: Sleeper-derived path assigns draft slots by roster_id, so pick VALUES follow roster numbering rather than standings
findings.rootCause: The picks loop uses `original_rid = slot` as a stand-in, then prices each pick by that slot. The set of picks per owner is correct (Sleeper's traded_picks is keyed on the original owner's roster_id) but the slot each roster is credited with — and therefore its dollar value — is arbitrary.
findings.evidence: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:177-181 — `for slot in range(1, actual_num_teams + 1): / original_rid = slot  # stand-in: slot N = original owner roster N / current_rid = traded_map.get((season, round_n, original_rid), original_rid) / ... / value = _pick_value_from_contract(contract, season, round_n, slot)`. The comment at :170-173 asserts "we assume reverse standings — which for this view is fine (ordering is not the point, value + ownership is)" — but value IS slot-dependent, so ordering is precisely the point.
findings.userImpact: In any non-default league, roster_id 1 is permanently credited with the 1.01 dollar value and roster_id 12 with the 1.12 value, irrespective of actual standings. Per-team auction totals — the numbers /draft auto-loads as team budgets — are wrong by construction.
findings.recommendedFix: Derive the slot order from Sleeper's draft `slot_to_roster_id` (as the workbook path does at server.py:7661-7696) or from roster fpts when a draft object does not yet exist. If neither is available, refuse rather than invent an order.

findings.title: "Best value on the board" renders backfill rows as green underrate signals with a double-negative percentage
findings.rootCause: The backfill branch emits rows whose gap is ≤ 0 (the vendor values the player HIGHER than we do), and the renderer unconditionally prefixes a minus sign and applies the green "underrates" styling.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:2185-2186 — `const gap = ourDollar - vendorDollar; const gapPct = vendorDollar > 0 ? gap / vendorDollar : 0;` with no sign guard; rendered at frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:2659-2669 — `style={{ background: "rgba(74, 222, 128, 0.18)", color: "var(--green, #4ade80)" }} title={\`${vendorLabel} underrates by ${Math.round(gapPct * 100)}% ...\`}> −{Math.round(gapPct * 100)}%`. With live data producing zero qualifying rows, every rendered row takes this path: e.g. Jeremiyah Love at ours $132.0 vs KTC $140.0 renders the badge "−-6%" with the tooltip "KTC underrates by -6%".
findings.userImpact: A panel titled "Best value on the board" presents players the market prices ABOVE our board as green bargains, with a literally malformed "−-6%" badge. The signal is inverted for 100% of what a user currently sees.
findings.recommendedFix: Render backfill rows in a visually distinct, neutral style with the honest label already present in their rationale ("top remaining fair price"), and suppress the percentage badge when gapPct ≤ 0.

findings.title: Per-team pick counts are clamped to 6, so a team that trades for extra picks is modelled as if it had not
findings.rootCause: mergeDraftCapitalTeams clamps the feed-derived slot count with `Math.min(feedSlots, DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS)`, contradicting its own docstring three lines above.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1409-1413 — `const initialSlots = picksArray ? Number.isFinite(feedSlots) ? Math.min(feedSlots, DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS) : 0 : Math.min(priorSlots, DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS);` against the docstring at :1399-1402: "When the picks array is present, the slot count is authoritative." DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS = 6 (:53).
findings.userImpact: Slot count feeds effectiveBudgetFor (:294-299), so a team owning 9 picks reserves $5 instead of $8 and its effective budget is overstated — inflating topCompetitorMax and therefore every user-facing "Win at". For the USER's own team it is worse: after 6 picks slotsRemaining hits 0, slotPressure hits 1 (max phase multiplier) and my own effectiveBudget reads $0 while I still hold picks. The Sleeper-derived fallback returns ~8 picks per team (two seasons × 4 rounds), so every non-default league hits this on every load.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop the Math.min clamp on the feed branch. Keep DEFAULT_INITIAL_SLOTS as the pre-fetch default only.

findings.title: nominationCandidates' own docstring describes a different, unimplemented algorithm
findings.rootCause: The function was rewritten to a vendor-gap ranker; the original docstring block was left above the new body comment.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1985-2001 documents `expected_price(p) = p.inflatedFair`, `affordable(p) = min(expected_price, topCompetitorMax)`, `tag_weight: avoid → 1.8 / neutral → 1.0 / target → 0`, `risk_of_winning(p)`, and `score(p) = affordable × tag_weight × (1 − risk_factor)`. The body at :2034-2058 computes none of these: there is no risk factor, no 1.8 avoid weight, and the score is `(1 - phasePct) * vendorDollar + phasePct * gapPct * 100`. `drain` is computed at :2059-2061 and never rendered anywhere.
findings.userImpact: Anyone reading the module to understand or modify the nomination logic — including a future agent — will reason about a scoring model that does not exist. Avoid-tagged players get no preference at all despite the documented 1.8x weight.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete lines 1985-2001 and the unused `drain` field, or implement the documented model.

findings.title: The roster-needs strip claims positional shortages are factored into target priority; nothing reads them
findings.rootCause: computeRosterBreakdown's output is threaded into a chip renderer only. No scoring function takes a position argument.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:4810 — `positions below threshold, factored into target priority`. `needSet` is created at :3688-3691 and grep shows exactly two other uses: passing it into RookieBoard (:4933) and rendering a chip (:1408-1415, `{p.pos && needSet?.has(p.pos) && (NEED)}`). Neither nextBestTargets (draft-logic.js:1941-1976), playerRecommendation (:1839-1921), nominationCandidates (:2005-2088), bestValueOnBoard (:2118-2209) nor the bid math (:706-779) accepts or reads a position.
findings.userImpact: A user is told their roster gaps are influencing the recommendations. They are not. There is no positional need weighting anywhere in the draft engine.
findings.recommendedFix: Either add a need multiplier to nextBestTargets' EV (and calibrate it), or change the copy to "shown as a NEED chip on the board".

findings.title: DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS is invented and ignores the league's actual roster settings
findings.rootCause: The thresholds are hardcoded and the page never passes the league registry's rosterSettings.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:2421-2429 — `export const DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS = { QB: 3, RB: 4, WR: 5, TE: 2, DL: 3, LB: 3, DB: 3 };` with the docstring at :2413-2419 conceding "Values chosen to fit a 2-QB/2-RB/3-WR/1-TE + flex IDP starter shape common in SF leagues — adjust via options when a league's shape differs significantly." The page calls `computeRosterBreakdown(rosterPlayers || [], allPlayersArray || [])` at :3685 with no third argument, so the defaults always apply. CLAUDE.md documents `leagueKey → sleeperLeagueId + rosterSettings + idpEnabled` as the map the frontend relies on; it is not consulted here.
findings.userImpact: Every league sees the same needs regardless of its starter requirements. In a league with 1 QB the board flags a QB shortage at 2 QBs.
findings.recommendedFix: Derive positionMins from the resolved league's rosterSettings via useLeague, falling back to DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS only when unavailable.

findings.title: hydrateWorkspace silently discards position, assetClass and both vendor dollar fields on every page load
findings.rootCause: The players mapper in hydrateWorkspace projects only four fields, dropping everything replacePlayerPool carefully preserved.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1714-1719 — `return src.map((p, i) => ({ id: ..., rank: ..., name: ..., preDraft: ... }));` — no `pos`, no `assetClass`, no `ktcDollar`, no `idpTradeCalcDollar`. replacePlayerPool at :1579-1595 explicitly carries all four.
findings.userImpact: On every reload, until the /api/draft-capital auto-sync round-trips, the Market column is blank, the NEED chip cannot render (it gates on `p.pos`), and both the nomination and best-value panels are empty. If that fetch fails — an offline draft room, a backend blip mid-draft — they stay empty for the session with no error surfaced.
findings.recommendedFix: Carry pos/assetClass/ktcDollar/idpTradeCalcDollar through hydrateWorkspace.

findings.title: The live sync path never supplies assetClass, so the IDP/offense vendor routing falls back to a position string the fallback exists to work around
findings.rootCause: replacePlayerPool accepts assetClass and both routing helpers prefer it, but neither code path that actually runs supplies it.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:1580-1586 documents the intent: "Authoritative offense/IDP class from the live contract. `nominationCandidates` prefers this over `pos` so a rookie with a missing/blank `position` string is still routed to the right vendor." The auto-sync at frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:3623-3629 pushes `{name, preDraft, pos, ktcDollar, idpTradeCalcDollar}` — no assetClass. The manual sync's preferred serverPool branch hardcodes `assetClass: null` at :4306. The backend never stamps assetClass onto a pick row (server.py:8054-8061).
findings.userImpact: An IDP rookie whose contract `position` is blank routes to KTC, gets no vendor dollar, and drops out of both panels — the exact failure the assetClass field was added to prevent. classifyPos("") returns "other", which is not "idp", so the KTC branch wins.
findings.recommendedFix: Stamp `rookieAssetClass` on each pick in server.py:8054-8061 from _our_rookie_pool's already-captured `assetClass` (server.py:7030) and thread it through both sync paths.

findings.title: effectiveAuctionPower violates its own documented multiplier bound and amplifies near-equal fields the most
findings.rootCause: The [1−gain, 1+gain] bound applies to the pre-normalization multiplier; the subsequent rescale by Σraw/Σw moves the realized multiplier outside it. Separately, `spread` floors at 0.01×(grand/n), so when MAD is 0 — the natural state of a league before any pick trades — z-scores explode.
findings.evidence: src/api/auction_power.py:68-70 — "``premium_gain`` — max fractional swing of the S-curve. The per-team multiplier is bounded to ``[1 - gain, 1 + gain]`` so the lens can never wildly distort the trusted raw numbers." Production code at frontend/lib/auction-power.js:50 — `const spread = Math.max(mad * 1.4826, 0.01 * (grand / names.length));` and :64 — `const scaled = weighted.map((w) => w * (rawSum / wsum));`. Measured continuous multipliers: a 12-team field at [110, 100×10, 90] gives range [0.6462, 1.3434] and the $90 team is displayed at $58.2; a whale field [1000, 20×9, 10×2] gives 0.5055. A 6-team field at [201,200,200,200,200,199] — a $2 real spread — renders as [227.8, 199.9, 199.9, 199.9, 199.9, 172.5], a $55 spread.
findings.userImpact: The /league draft-capital chart's cyan effective-power marker overstates concentration in exactly the leagues that have none, and the same function feeds the /trade stack-effect adjustment (frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:807-808), so a fabricated concentration signal moves real trade verdicts.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply the bound after normalization (clamp `scaled[i]` to raw[i]×[1−gain, 1+gain] then re-normalize), and raise the spread floor so a field with negligible real dispersion returns near-identity.

findings.title: src/api/auction_power.py is documented as the source of truth but has no production caller
findings.rootCause: The lens was moved client-side; the Python module was kept for its Phase-2 spec and tests.
findings.evidence: src/api/auction_power.py:49-52 — "NOTE: the live UI lens is currently computed client-side from the raw per-team dollars (frontend ``_auction-power.js`` mirrors this module — keep them in lockstep).  This module remains the source of truth + the home of the Phase 2 simulation and the unit tests." `grep -rn effective_auction_power --include=*.py` returns only the definition and tests/api/test_auction_power_parity.py. Also note the docstring names the mirror `_auction-power.js`; the file is `frontend/lib/auction-power.js`.
findings.userImpact: Anyone changing the constants in the Python file to change what users see will change nothing. The constants are currently identical (0.35/1.25/0.15 in both) so there is no live drift, but the only thing preventing it is the parity test.
findings.recommendedFix: Either delete the Python module and move the constants + Phase-2 spec into the JS file, or serve the lens from the backend and delete the mirror.

findings.title: The Target Board budget check ignores the roster-slot limit and over-warns
findings.rootCause: portfolioBuffer subtracts the winning bid of every remaining target, without capping at how many the user can still draft.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:844-849 — `const nonTargetSlotsLeft = Math.max(0, mySlotsRemaining - tbTotals.remainingCount); const portfolioBuffer = myRemaining - tbTotals.remainingWinBid - nonTargetSlotsLeft;` where remainingWinBid (:837) sums all undrafted board slots. Reproduced: 2 slots remaining, $413 remaining, 6 targets summing to $414 → buffer −1 → "Short $1 — trim a target or lower your ceiling". The two most expensive targets I could actually take cost $138.
findings.userImpact: The one place on /draft that checks a budget constraint gives a false shortage warning whenever the wishlist is longer than the roster space — which is the normal way a target board is used (the cap is 6, and slots run down as the draft proceeds).
findings.recommendedFix: Sum only the top mySlotsRemaining targets by winning bid, and label the status accordingly.

findings.title: DEFAULT_ROOKIES sums to $1211 while its own comment claims $1200 — and the mismatch is what breaks late-draft inflation on a pristine board
findings.rootCause: Seed data drift; the comment was never updated and the test codified the wrong number as correct.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:177-179 — "Verbatim from the Inflation tab (columns A-C).  Sums to $1200 to keep / the league-wide accounting consistent with the sheet." Computed sum of DEFAULT_ROOKIES.preDraft = 1211 across 72 rows; DEFAULT_TEAMS budgets sum to 1200. frontend/__tests__/draft-logic.test.js:46 pins the real value: `it("72 rookies totaling $1211 of PreDraft value (CSV verbatim)")`.
findings.userImpact: On a pristine board (no successful draft-capital sync), the inflation denominator `1200 - soldPreDraft` goes negative from around pick 63 and clamps to 1, collapsing inflation to 0.000 and zeroing every remaining Fair / Enforce / Max Bid. Reproduced above.
findings.recommendedFix: Fix the comment, and separately make the inflation denominator use the pool's own sum rather than the team-budget total so the two can never diverge.

findings.title: Draft-capital team totals are summed from workbook column Q while the displayed per-pick dollars come from column L
findings.rootCause: The picks loop reads `dollar` from pick_values_per_slot (L2:L73) for the payload but accumulates `val` (the Q45:Q116 value) into team_totals_decimal.
findings.evidence: server.py:7973-7977 — `dollar = (float(pick_values_per_slot[overall_idx]) if overall_idx < len(pick_values_per_slot) else float(val))` stamped into `dollarValue`/`adjustedDollarValue`/`originalDollarValue` at :7985-7990 — then :8000-8001 `team_totals_decimal.setdefault(owner_team, 0.0); team_totals_decimal[owner_team] += float(val)`. The comment at :7971-7972 explicitly names L authoritative. Verified by direct xlsx parse: Q and L are currently identical for all 72 rows, so the divergence is latent, not live.
findings.userImpact: None today. The moment the user edits L without editing Q (the exact scenario the code comment at :7506-7511 anticipates — "Using L directly (instead of re-rounding the Q-column expansion-averaged values)"), a team's auctionDollars will stop equalling the sum of its own picks' dollarValue, silently.
findings.recommendedFix: Accumulate `dollar`, not `val`.

findings.title: The overpay warning in the draft modal renders a doubled dollar sign
findings.rootCause: A literal `$` in JSX text immediately precedes an expression whose formatter already prefixes `$`.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:809-811 — `The top rival can only bid $\n{fmt$(stats.topCompetitorMax)} — you don't need to pay more`. fmt$ returns `$68`, so the sentence renders "The top rival can only bid $$68".
findings.userImpact: Cosmetic, but it appears inside the single red warning the app shows before a user commits an overpay — the one message it most needs to be read carefully.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop the literal `$`.

findings.title: The Hill-curve rookie dollar formula and the vendor-dollar conversion have zero test coverage
findings.rootCause: tests/api/test_draft_capital.py covers workbook parsing, rounding and Sleeper overlay semantics but never the value-conversion functions.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "_rookie_dollars_from_values|_vendor_dollars_for_rookies" tests/` returns nothing. server.py:7133-7236 and 7038-7070 are both untested. Both are reachable on every /api/draft-capital cache miss (server.py:8016-8043).
findings.userImpact: The two functions that produce the PreDraft and Market columns — the anchors for every derived number on /draft — are unpinned. The missing-pad bug in _vendor_dollars_for_rookies would have been caught by a single test asserting that two vendors covering different row counts produce comparable dollars. Note the formula itself IS faithful: I reproduced n=72 output [134.5, 100.5, 93.0, 80.5, 75.5, 68.5, 54.5, 53.5, 46.0, 44.5, …] exactly against workbook column L.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a golden test pinning _rookie_dollars_from_values against the workbook's L column, and a test asserting vendor dollars for a 30-row and a 72-row vendor land on the same scale.

findings.title: isExpansion is hardcoded to slots 1-2
findings.rootCause: A league-specific expansion-draft artifact left as a literal.
findings.evidence: server.py:7994 — `"isExpansion": slot <= 2,` with no config lookup and no comment explaining which expansion it refers to. The Sleeper-derived path hardcodes the opposite: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:239 — `"isExpansion": False,`.
findings.userImpact: Any league using this endpoint has its first two picks of every round flagged as expansion picks. The two draft-capital paths disagree on the same field.
findings.recommendedFix: Move to league config or drop the field.

findings.title: PickProjectorPanel is mounted without a leagueKey, so it always projects the default league
findings.rootCause: The component accepts a leagueKey prop and threads it into the fetch, but the mount site passes nothing.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/league/sections/_pick-projector.jsx:47 — `export default function PickProjectorPanel({ leagueKey })` and :57-59 — `const qs = leagueKey ? \`?leagueKey=${encodeURIComponent(leagueKey)}\` : "";`. Mounted at frontend/app/league/sections/draft-capital.jsx:118 — `<PickProjectorPanel />`.
findings.userImpact: On a non-default league's /league page, the pick projector silently shows the default league's projected draft order beside that league's draft capital.
findings.recommendedFix: Pass the resolved league key through DraftCapitalSection.

findings.title: DEFAULT_TOTAL_BUDGET and DEFAULT_TEAM_COUNT are exported and never used
findings.rootCause: Superseded by the live draft-capital feed; the page hardcodes 1200 instead.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/draft-logic.js:43-44 — `export const DEFAULT_TOTAL_BUDGET = 1200; export const DEFAULT_TEAM_COUNT = 12;`. `grep -rn` across frontend/ finds no reference outside those two lines — not even in the test file. Meanwhile frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:4389 and :4412 pass a literal `1200` to rescaleValuesToBudget.
findings.userImpact: None functionally, but a reader will assume the budget constant is the single source and edit it with no effect. The real $1200 lives in three independent places: server.py:6730, src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:36, and the two literals in page.jsx.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the dead exports or wire the literals to them.

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. All conclusions below are from reading the code at commit 9c5d972 on branch claude/decision-intelligence-audit-wif47g. No file in the repository was modified. Numeric claims were reproduced in a scratchpad by (a) importing frontend/lib/draft-logic.js and frontend/lib/auction-power.js directly into node and driving them, (b) re-implementing server.py::_rookie_dollars_from_values in Python and checking it against the real workbook, and (c) parsing CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx via zipfile+ElementTree because openpyxl is not installed in this environment and installing packages was out of scope.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUSTWORTHY. Three things in this area are genuinely well-built and deserve to influence decisions:
1. The workbook path of /api/draft-capital (server.py:7474-8087). I verified column L2:L73 sums to exactly 1200.0 across 72 picks, that Q45:Q116 currently matches L element-for-element, and that the SUMIF team totals (Joel 180, Blaine 144.5, Jason 132.5, Roy 117.5, Collin 109.5, Eric 99.5, Kich 83, Ty 80.5, MaKayla 69.5, Joey 67.5, Brent 61.5, Ed 54.5) reproduce from the pick rows. tests/api/test_draft_capital.py backs this with 25 tests including eight isTraded/live-standings edge cases that read like they were each written after a real incident.
2. The Hill-curve port itself. My independent Python reimplementation of _rookie_dollars_from_values fed the workbook's own B column reproduces column L exactly: 134.5, 100.5, 93.0, 80.5, 75.5, 68.5, 54.5, 53.5, 46.0, 44.5, 41.0, 35.5, … The port is faithful. Whether the sheet is *right* is a separate, unanswered question — the spine (column E, median+mean of 2023-25 realised values ÷ 2) is the only empirically grounded input; the 0.6/0.4 blend, the decay clip, the R5 windows and the K caps are one person's curve-shaping.
3. The Par Sheet (draft-logic.js:873-987). Simple, correctly scoped, well tested (draft-logic.test.js:393-606), and it does not pretend to be more than bookkeeping.

THE CENTRAL PROBLEM. Nothing on /draft optimizes under a constraint. The page is presented as an auction *optimizer* — budget advantage, phase multiplier, effective budgets, EV ranking, portfolio buffer — but traced end to end there is exactly one budget check in the whole system (Target Board portfolioBuffer) and it asks the wrong question. The headline "Win at" number is computed without ever reading the user's own wallet or roster space; I confirmed a fully-spent, fully-rostered team is still told to bid $69. "Next Best Targets" is provably a preDraft sort. "Best value on the board" returns zero genuine signals on live data. What exists is a well-instrumented *ledger* with a recommendation skin painted on. The ledger half is fine. The recommendation half should not be trusted for a single bid.

DATA-DRIVEN VERSUS INVENTED. Of the constants that move numbers: the workbook spine and the L-column curve are data-derived; DEFAULT_AGGRESSION 0.09 and DEFAULT_ENFORCE_PCT 0.8 are ports of the user's own sheet settings (defensible as preferences, not calibration); everything else is invented with no cited derivation and no backtest — PHASE_LATE_BOOST 0.5, TIER_CONFIDENCE_MIN_SAMPLES 3, the S/A/B/C/D cutoffs 60/25/8/3/0, TIER_SCARCITY_URGENT 0.3, SPEND_UP_PRESSURE_MIN 0.6, SPEND_UP_MDV_FLOOR 10, NOMINATION_DECAY 0.8, TIER_INTEREST_MIN 0.2, the 0.3 collapse floor, tagWeight 1.5, the scarcity coefficient 10, DEFAULT_POSITION_MINS, the MDV heat bands 40/15, the alert thresholds (0.3, 0.4/$10, $10/25%, 0.7), and the three auction-power knobs (0.35/1.25/0.15 — whose own docstring calls the validating Phase 2 "spec only — DO NOT build here without sign-off"). The repo is honest about this in src/api/auction_power.py and dishonest about it nowhere; it simply never revisited them.

CLAUDE.md DISAGREEMENTS FOUND. (1) CLAUDE.md's /api/draft-capital section states the hardcoded 7000/4000/2000/1200 round table produced "a full board of invented numbers" and that "this is the case the 503 covers." The table is still live at src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:96-99 and, because the contract carries no next-season slot rows, it supplies 52% of the board on every non-default-league call regardless of whether a contract is loaded. The 503 covers only the no-contract case. (2) CLAUDE.md correctly states /draft stays market-priced and says so via ValueBasisNote — verified at page.jsx:4751. (3) CLAUDE.md correctly states the /draft Fund gap column joins by name only — verified. (4) CLAUDE.md's claim that KTC and IDPTradeCalc are directly comparable at a median ratio of 1.000 is consistent with what I measured on the rookie subset (the IDPTC dollar column came out at 1.012x ours, versus KTC at 1.181x, and that entire gap is explained by row count, not by scale incompatibility) — so the *premise* of the vendor comparison is sound; only the implementation is not.

IN-FILE DOC DISAGREEMENTS. server.py:7063-7065 claims a pad it does not perform. draft-logic.js:1399-1402 claims the feed slot count is authoritative three lines above the clamp that overrides it. draft-logic.js:1985-2001 documents an entirely different nomination algorithm from the one implemented below it. draft-logic.js:177-179 claims the seed pool sums to $1200; it sums to $1211 and the test says so. src/api/auction_power.py:68-70 claims a multiplier bound that renormalization breaks, and :50 names the mirror file `_auction-power.js` when it is `auction-power.js`. page.jsx:4810 claims roster needs are factored into target priority; nothing reads them.

NOT VERIFIED. I could not exercise the live /api/draft-capital endpoint (no running backend, no Sleeper reachability) so the workbook↔Sleeper join, the live-standings reshuffle and the traded-picks overlay are assessed from code plus their tests only. The /draft page's alert layer, triage auto-filter and live-sync conflict handling have no test file and were assessed from code only. /idptc-rookies has no test file. I did not measure whether the S/A/B/C/D tier cutoffs correspond to any real break in the dollar distribution.

STABILITY. Bid recommendations are not stable in the ordinary sense: every recorded pick changes global inflation, tier heat, budget advantage, topCompetitorMax and the phase multiplier, so every price on the board moves after every pick — which is by design. What is *not* by design is that the movement is unbounded: inflation is a ratio whose denominator goes to zero at draft end, so the last several picks are priced by a number that has diverged. The draft review is also unstable retrospectively (it grades completed picks against current fair value, so the leaderboard re-ranks after every subsequent pick); the docstring defends this, and it is a defensible choice, but it means a screenshot of the review at pick 60 will not match the same review at pick 72.
