findings.title: The Value column silently switches from the Hill-curve board to the raw scraper composite for 260 rows, and 158 of them display a LARGER number than the deepest genuinely-priced player
findings.rootCause: `_materializePlayerArrayRow` sets `full: Math.round(backendValue || rawValues.full)` where `rawValues.full = displayValue || finalAdjusted || overall`. When the canonical pipeline declines to price a row it stamps `rankDerivedValue: null` and `values.displayValue: null`, leaving `values.overall`/`values.finalAdjusted` holding the pre-pipeline scraper composite. The client promotes that number into the same column, with the same formatting, the same value-band badge and the same sort key as real Hill values.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1008 — `full: Math.round(backendValue || rawValues.full),` and the render at frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1050 — `const val = Math.round(row.rankDerivedValue || row.values?.full || 0);`. Live contract: Devin Bush `values={overall:2549, rawComposite:2549, finalAdjusted:2549, displayValue:null}`, `rankDerivedValue:null` → row displays 2,549, band 'D — Depth value (2000-3999)'. Malachi Moore, the last backend-ranked player (#740): `rankDerivedValue:757` → displays 757, band 'F — Fringe'. 260 of 1,072 rows take the fallback; 249 display a non-zero value; 158 display more than 757.
findings.userImpact: A user sorting or scanning by Value sees Devin Bush (a rotational LB the pipeline refused to price) at 2,549 — 3.4× the value of the deepest player the model actually priced. Sorting the board by Value descending places him at display position 224, interleaved among real top-225 assets while his rank cell reads '#905'. Any trade evaluated off the displayed number for one of these 216 players is evaluated on a scale the trade engines never use — `finder.py`, `suggestions.py`, `angle.py` and `waiver.py` all read `rankDerivedValue`, which is null here. The CSV export carries the same mixed column with no marker.
findings.recommendedFix: Stop substituting. Render '—' (or an explicit 'unpriced' state) whenever `rankDerivedValue` is null, and drop the `|| rawValues.full` leg at dynasty-data.js:1008 so `values.full` cannot carry a different scale than the sort key already uses. If the raw composite is genuinely wanted, it belongs in a separately-labelled column, not the one titled 'Value' with a Hill-curve tooltip.
findings.complexity: low — one expression in buildRows, one in the Value cell renderer, one in the exporter; the buildRows sort already treats these rows as valueless, so nothing downstream reorders.
findings.affectedSystems: buildRows playersArray + legacy materializers, /rankings Value column, valueBand badge, Value-column sort, Copy/CSV export, PlayerPopup 'Our Value' and value chain, PlayerPopup roster depth label.

findings.title: 216 players (20% of the board) carry a client-invented rank in the # column, and those numbers are array indices that count unranked picks
findings.rootCause: `buildRows` assigns `computedConsensusRank = i + 1` over the whole sorted array — including the 116 picks the backend deliberately left unranked — and then uses it as `r.rank` for any non-pick row the backend did not stamp.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1359-1373 — `rows.forEach((r, i) => { r.computedConsensusRank = i + 1; … } else { r.rank = r.computedConsensusRank; }`. Live: 740 rows carry a backend rank (max 740); 216 non-pick rows get client ranks #857-#1072. The # column therefore reads 738, 739, 740, then '—' for 44 picks, then jumps to 857. CLAUDE.md describes these as 'players past the backend's OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT (800)' — the backend's limit is 800 (data_contract.py:60) but it stamps only 740, so ranks 741-856 exist on no board at all.
findings.userImpact: A 216-row block of the board is numbered by the client. Those numbers feed `resolvedRank`, the rank sort, `positionRankByName` (so QB/RB/LB positional ranks past the priced board are client-derived), `isEligibleForAnalysis`, and every rank cap in edge-helpers. They are not comparable to backend ranks: they are offset by the pick count, and the 741-856 gap makes the discontinuity visible. Duplicate # values are not structurally prevented — they are avoided today only because the backend's 740-rank ceiling happens to leave a 71-slot gap.
findings.recommendedFix: Render '—' in the # column for any row without `canonicalConsensusRank`, exactly as picks already do (the branch exists at :1366). Keep `computedConsensusRank` if some caller needs a stable array position, but stop aliasing it to `rank`. If a numbered tail is wanted, the backend should stamp it.
findings.complexity: low in code (delete one else-branch), medium in blast radius — `resolvedRank`, the rank sort, positionRankByName and the edge rank caps all need to tolerate null.

findings.title: Four different thresholds turn the same backend signal into three contradictory BUY/SELL verdicts on screen simultaneously
findings.rootCause: `marketGapDirection` is stamped once by the backend with no threshold, then re-thresholded independently by three consumers: the Edge column recomputes the means and requires a 10-rank gap; PlayerPopup's banner requires 3; the advanced filter requires nothing.
findings.evidence: Backend: `src/api/data_contract.py:2788-2793` — `if diff > 0: return "retail_premium"` (no threshold). Edge column: `frontend/lib/display-helpers.js:164` — `if (diff < MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF) { … kind: "aligned" }` with `MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF = 10` (thresholds.js:46). Popup: `frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:968` — `if (!Number.isFinite(magnitude) || magnitude < MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP)` with `MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP = 3` (:949). Filter: `frontend/lib/player-filters.js:182-184` — `const want = c.edge === "buy" ? "consensus_premium" : "retail_premium"; if (dir !== want) return false;`. Measured on the live board: 136 of 420 rows with a backend direction render as HOLD/aligned in the Edge column; 79 rows show a 'Buy Low'/'Sell High' banner in PlayerPopup while the row that opened it says HOLD (Brock Bowers #2 SELL/HOLD, Lamar Jackson #10 BUY/HOLD, Joe Burrow #13 BUY/HOLD); 79 of 249 rows matched by the 'buy' filter and 57 of 171 matched by 'sell' display HOLD.
findings.userImpact: Filtering the board to 'Edge: buy' returns a list in which a third of the rows say HOLD in the Edge column. Clicking any of those opens a drawer with a green 'Buy Low' box. The user has no way to tell which threshold is the product's opinion.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one threshold and put it in one place. The cleanest version: have the backend stamp a `marketGapSignal` enum ('buy'|'sell'|'hold') alongside direction/magnitude, and make all three consumers read it. Failing that, delete the client re-derivation in `marketEdge` (it duplicates `_compute_market_gap` exactly) and drive the label, the popup and the filter from `marketGapMagnitude` against a single exported constant.
findings.complexity: medium — three call sites plus their tests; the arithmetic is already proven identical so only the gating changes.

findings.title: The Edge rail prints total source dispersion but labels it as the buy/sell gap
findings.rootCause: `topRetailPremium`/`topConsensusPremium` gate on `marketGapDirection` but format the detail string from `sourceRankSpread` — max-minus-min across all sources — instead of `marketGapMagnitude`, the retail-vs-consensus difference the label describes.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/edge-helpers.js:358 — ``detail: `Buy +${r.sourceRankSpread} ranks`,`` and :336 — ``detail: `Sell +${r.sourceRankSpread} ranks`,``. Live board: Kenneth Walker renders 'Buy +25 ranks'; his `marketGapMagnitude` is 0.6. Trevor Lawrence 'Buy +20 ranks' vs 3.5. Nico Collins 'Buy +23 ranks' vs 9.8. Jalen Hurts 'Buy +22 ranks' vs 10.1. 93 rows qualify for the buy rail.
findings.userImpact: The rail is the fastest-read surface on the page and its headline number is off by up to 40× in the wrong direction — it makes near-aligned players look like large mispricings. Kenneth Walker is presented as a 25-rank buy-low when retail and consensus differ by half a rank on him.
findings.recommendedFix: Use `Math.round(r.marketGapMagnitude)` in both detail strings, and make the `>= PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD` gate consistent with whatever the unified threshold from the previous finding becomes.
findings.complexity: low — two template strings, plus the filter predicate if the gate should also move to the gap.

findings.title: PlayerPopup's 'Value chain — how we got N' ends on a different number than N on 87% of rows, by a median of 282 points
findings.rootCause: `computeValueChain` reconstructs only the anchor and α-shrunk-subgroup stages, then the header claims those stages explain `values.full`. The live pipeline applies ~11 further stages after that point (TE basis conversion, market corridor clamp, single-source haircut, two-way boost, pick-year discount, pick tethering, count-aware aggregation). None are modelled and none is disclosed.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:612 — `const adjusted = Math.round(anchor + alpha * subgroupDelta);` and :1020 — ``Value chain — how we got {Math.round(values.full || 0).toLocaleString()}``. Measured across the live board: 885 of 1,015 rows with a chain end on a value different from the header. |Δ| p50 = 282, p90 = 878, p99 = 1,590, max = 3,029. Bijan Robinson (#3): header 'how we got 9,706', single chain stage reads 9,999. Drake Maye (#5): header 9,579, chain 9,058. Lamar Jackson (#10): header 8,904, chain 8,280.
findings.userImpact: This is the product's transparency surface — the thing a user opens to decide whether to trust a number. It presents an arithmetic derivation that does not arrive at the number, with no remainder row and no caveat. A user checking the math concludes either that the value is wrong or that the explanation is; both undermine every downstream trade decision the board informs.
findings.recommendedFix: Either (a) have the backend stamp an ordered `valueChain` array of {stage, value} covering every stage that actually ran — the pipeline already computes them — and render it verbatim, or (b) append an explicit final stage 'Post-blend adjustments' with the residual `values.full − lastStage` so the chain closes. Do not leave a chain that silently stops mid-pipeline.
findings.complexity: medium — (b) is a few lines in the component; (a) requires a contract field but is the honest fix and the only one that names which adjustment moved the number.

findings.title: PlayerPopup computes its own source-agreement verdict and contradicts the confidence badge on the row that opened it
findings.rootCause: `consensusText` computes a coefficient of variation over per-source value contributions with client thresholds 0.15/0.30, an entirely separate metric from the backend's percentile rank-spread bucketing.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:857-863 — `const cv = mean > 0 ? Math.sqrt(variance) / mean : 0; if (cv < 0.15) return 'Strong consensus …'; if (cv < 0.30) return 'Moderate agreement …'; return 'Sources disagree significantly …'`. Backend: `_compute_confidence_bucket` (data_contract.py:1895-1905) buckets on percentile spread vs 0.08/0.20, and `hasSourceDisagreement` (:7716-7719) tests percentile spread vs 0.10 + depth allowance. Live: 25 rows where the popup says 'Sources disagree significantly' while the badge says High confidence and hasSourceDisagreement is false (Carson Schwesinger #42, Sonny Styles #61, Myles Garrett #80, CJ Allen #144, Ernest Jones #192, Quay Walker #197); 22 rows where the popup says 'Strong consensus' while hasSourceDisagreement is true.
findings.userImpact: Myles Garrett shows a green 'High' confidence badge on the board and, one click later, an italic line reading 'Sources disagree significantly — high volatility player'. Two of the product's own trust signals openly disagree, on a metric the backend already computes and stamps.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete `consensusText` and render `row.confidenceLabel` plus `sourceRankPercentileSpread` — both already on the row. If a CV narrative is genuinely wanted, compute it on the backend so one number drives both surfaces.

findings.title: The methodology panel publishes a value formula that is neither the live curve nor the current fallback constants, understating the board by up to 16.6%
findings.rootCause: Hardcoded prose constants that were never updated when the pipeline moved to scope-level percentile curves and when the rank-form fallback was refit.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/board-sections.jsx:34 — `value = max(1, min(9999, round(1 + 9998 / (1 + ((rank-1)/45)^1.10))))`. Live pipeline: `percentile_to_value` (src/canonical/player_valuation.py:371-410) with `HILL_PERCENTILE_C = 0.1100`, `HILL_PERCENTILE_S = 1.110` (:126-127), scope-routed across four curves. The contract's own `hillCurves` block confirms offense midpoint 54.89 / slope 1.11, idp 41.417, global 55.888 / 0.725, rookie 76.347 / 0.885. The rank-form fallback that the prose's SHAPE matches uses midpoint 65.4 / slope 0.910 (:82-83). Reproduced numerically: rank 12 → 8,248 published vs 8,562 live; rank 50 → 4,766 vs 5,315 (549 points, 10.3%); rank 200 → 1,632 vs 1,932; rank 500 → 663 vs 795 (16.6%). The same stale pair is the fallback in HillCurveExplorer.jsx:50.
findings.userImpact: A user who reproduces the published formula to sanity-check the board gets numbers 10-17% below what the board shows through the entire mid-range, and concludes the values are inflated. The panel also asserts a single rank curve when the live board runs four scope-specific percentile curves against a fixed 500-rank reference.
findings.recommendedFix: Render the formula from the contract's `hillCurves` block, which HillCurveExplorer already receives — one curve per scope with the live c/s. Delete the hardcoded 45/1.10 in both places.

findings.title: Both the methodology panel and the confidence tooltip publish a confidence rule the backend retired; half the 'High' badges violate it
findings.rootCause: The frontend documents `_CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH`/`_MEDIUM` (30/80 ordinal spread), which the backend reaches only when percentile spread is unavailable. The live path buckets on percentile spread 0.08/0.20.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/board-sections.jsx:31 — 'High = 2+ sources, spread ≤ 30. Medium = 2+ sources, spread ≤ 80. Low = single source or spread > 80.' and frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:150-154 — the same text as the tooltip fallback. Backend `_compute_confidence_bucket` (data_contract.py:1895-1905): `if percentile_spread is not None: if percentile_spread <= _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_HIGH … elif source_rank_spread is not None: if source_rank_spread <= _CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH`. Live board: 50 of 108 'High' rows have `sourceRankSpread > 30` (max 485); 139 of 228 'Medium' rows have spread > 80 (max 507); 42 'Low' rows have spread ≤ 80 with 2+ sources. thresholds.js:8 still claims these constants 'mirror values in src/api/data_contract.py'.
findings.userImpact: About half of every confidence badge on the board is explained by a rule it demonstrably does not satisfy. On the mobile/compact view the backend's real `confidenceLabel` is pruned (compact_view.py:56), so mobile users see ONLY the wrong explanation.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace the prose with the percentile rule and the live constants (0.08 / 0.20 depth-adjusted), and stop pruning `confidenceLabel` in the compact view — it is a short string and it is the only correct explanation the client has. Update the thresholds.js header, which now documents a fallback branch as the live rule.

findings.title: The compact (mobile) view prunes four fields the rankings UI reads, flipping BUY/SELL labels and blanking the Consensus column
findings.rootCause: `compact_view._PRUNED_PLAYER_FIELDS` drops `effectiveSourceRanks`, `anomalyFlags`, `confidenceLabel` and `blendedSourceRank`, but `marketEdge`, `rowChips`, `confidenceExplain` and the Consensus column all consume them. `preferredDataView()` routes every small-viewport or low-memory device to that view.
findings.evidence: src/api/compact_view.py:51-70 lists all four in `_PRUNED_PLAYER_FIELDS`; frontend/lib/device-profile.js:103-108 — `if (isMobileProfile() || isSlowNetwork()) return "compact";`. Consumers: display-helpers.js:110-113 falls back from `effectiveSourceRanks` to the PRE-Hampel `sourceRanks`; rankings-helpers.js:144-147 needs `anomalyFlags`; page.jsx:1038-1040 renders `blendedSourceRank ?? '—'`. Measured by simulating the prune on the live board: 8 rows change their Edge verdict (Patrick Mahomes #22 '—'→'BUY', Emeka Egbuka #34 HOLD→SELL, Rashee Rice #69 HOLD→BUY, Jayden Daniels #12 '—'→'HOLD'); 52 rows lose their '!' anomaly chip; all 800 rows with a Consensus value render '—'.
findings.userImpact: The same player gets a different trade verdict on a phone than on a desktop, from the same account and the same scrape — and the backend's own comment at data_contract.py:7666-7672 says `effectiveSourceRanks` was published specifically so 'the same player could NOT show conflicting edge signals across UI surfaces'. The Consensus column is dead weight on mobile and its sort control does nothing.
findings.recommendedFix: Move `effectiveSourceRanks`, `anomalyFlags` (a short array), `confidenceLabel` (a short string) and `blendedSourceRank` (one float) out of `_PRUNED_PLAYER_FIELDS`; they are cheap relative to `sourceRankMeta`, which the compact view already keeps. Alternatively make the frontend hide the affected columns/labels when the payload declares `meta.view === 'compact'` rather than silently computing a different answer.
findings.complexity: low — a four-entry edit to the prune set, plus a compact-shape test update.

findings.title: The playersArray materializer drops isStructurallySingleSource and sourceAudit, making the 'solo' chip unreachable and degrading every '1-src' tooltip
findings.rootCause: `_materializeLegacyDictRow` copies both fields (:1234, :1238-1241); `_materializePlayerArrayRow` copies neither, despite the in-file instruction to keep the two materializers in lockstep. The array path is the live desktop path.
findings.evidence: Missing from frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:987-1129 (compare :1234 `isStructurallySingleSource: Boolean(player.isStructurallySingleSource),` and :1238 `sourceAudit: …` in the legacy materializer). Consumer: frontend/lib/rankings-helpers.js:130-143 — `if (row?.isSingleSource) { const reason = row?.sourceAudit?.reason || "single source"; … } else if (row?.isStructurallySingleSource) { chips.push({ label: "solo", … })`. Live contract stamps `isStructurallySingleSource` on 20 rows and `sourceAudit` on all 1,092. Executing buildRows on it: `row.isStructurallySingleSource defined? 0`, `row.sourceAudit defined? 0`, `rendered solo chips: 0`, `1-src chips: 75` — all 75 falling back to the literal string 'single source'. `isStructurallySingleSource` is even carried in `_DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS` (data_contract.py:8969), so the backend ships it on the override path too and the materializer still discards it.
findings.userImpact: The blue 'solo' chip — the distinction between 'only one board could ever cover this player' and 'other boards should have matched him and didn't' — never renders. 20 players are shown the amber matching-failure chip's semantics or nothing, and the 75 genuine failures show a tooltip that names no reason, which is the entire content of `sourceAudit.reason`.
findings.recommendedFix: Add both fields to `_materializePlayerArrayRow`, mirroring the legacy materializer exactly.

findings.title: The Sources column renders '16/15' on 30 rows because the eligible-source denominator ignores extraScopes
findings.rootCause: The denominator is recomputed on the client from `s.scope` alone. `idpTradeCalc` is registered with `scope: 'overall_idp'` and `extraScopes: ['overall_offense']` and does cover offense, so it contributes to the backend's `sourceCount` but is excluded from the client's eligible set.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1119-1127 — `if (s.scope === "overall_offense") return ["QB","RB","WR","TE","PICK"].includes(pos); if (s.scope === "overall_idp") return ["DL","LB","DB"].includes(pos); return false;`. Registry: dynasty-data.js:230-234 — `key: "idpTradeCalc", scope: "overall_idp", extraScopes: ["overall_offense"]`. Live board: 30 rows render numerator > denominator, all '16/15', all with `idpTradeCalc` present in `sourceRanks` (Jeremiyah Love RB, Carnell Tate WR, Fernando Mendoza QB, Jordyn Tyson WR, Makai Lemon WR, Kenyon Sadiq TE, Jadarian Price RB, Eli Stowers TE, …).
findings.userImpact: A column whose stated purpose is 'matched / structurally eligible' displays a ratio above 1. Separately, the denominator is inflated for everyone: rookie-only boards (`dlfRookieSf` depth 50, `flockFantasySfRookies`) count as eligible for every veteran, and rookie-EXCLUDING boards (`dlfIdp`, `fantasyProsIdp`, both `excludesRookies: true`) count as eligible for every rookie, so coverage looks systematically worse than it is.
findings.recommendedFix: Have the backend stamp `eligibleSourceCount` per row — it already knows the scope routing, the depth caps and the `excludesRookies` flags — and render it. If that is too heavy, at minimum include `extraScopes` in the client predicate and exclude rookie-only/rookie-excluding boards by the row's rookie flag.
findings.complexity: low for the extraScopes fix; medium for the honest backend-stamped version.

findings.title: Sorting the Consensus column descending puts 272 unrankable rows at the top of the board
findings.rootCause: The page's own comparator maps missing values to `Infinity` and multiplies by the direction sign, so nulls sort to whichever end the direction points. It bypasses `DataTable.sortRows`, which sinks nulls in both directions.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:592-594 — `va = a.blendedSourceRank ?? Infinity; vb = b.blendedSourceRank ?? Infinity; return (va - vb) * dir;` with `dir = sortAsc ? 1 : -1`. Contrast DataTable.jsx:143-147 — `// nulls last in BOTH directions … if (aNull || bNull) return compareValues(a, b) || x.i - y.i;` — which the page disables via `presorted` (page.jsx:1886). Executed on the live board: 272 rows have `blendedSourceRank == null`; descending places them at indices 0-271, led by '2026 Pick 5.01'. Two null rows produce `(Infinity - Infinity) * -1 = NaN`, an invalid comparator return.
findings.userImpact: One click on the 'Consensus' header buries the entire real board under 272 draft picks and unpriced players. The `rank` and `gap` sorts handle nulls correctly; this one and, in the opposite way, `value` do not.
findings.recommendedFix: Sink nulls in both directions in the page's comparator — the exact logic already exists in `DataTable.compareValues`; extract and reuse it rather than re-deriving per case.

findings.title: Hampel-rejected sources render identically to contributing ones, and their tooltip calls the discarded rank the 'effective rank'
findings.rootCause: `formatSourceCell` reads `row.sourceRanks` (the pre-Hampel map) and `sourceRankMeta[key].valueContribution`, and never consults `row.droppedSources`, which buildRows materializes and nothing renders.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/board-utils.js:46 — `const effectiveRank = row?.sourceRanks?.[src.key];` and :98-103 — ``title: `${src.displayName}: value ${primary}${effectiveRank != null ? `, effective rank #${effectiveRank}` : ""}…` ``. `droppedSources` is on the row (dynasty-data.js:1059-1061) and used only by edge-helpers.js:141-143 to count. Live: Brock Bowers (#2) has `droppedSources: ['fantasyProsSf','draftSharks']`; both cells render as normal — `fantasyProsSf` → '8,310 (#28)', `draftSharks` → '7,940 (#16)' — with tooltips reading 'effective rank #28' / 'effective rank #16'. 215 rows have at least one dropped source.
findings.userImpact: A user reading the source columns to understand why the blend landed where it did cannot see which votes were rejected. The word 'effective' in the tooltip asserts the opposite of what happened: these ranks were specifically excluded from the effective set the confidence, disagreement and gap signals were computed on.
findings.recommendedFix: Mark dropped sources in the cell (strikethrough / muted) and change their tooltip to say the vote was rejected by the outlier filter. The data is already on the row.

findings.title: The 'Market (retail-lean)' preset does the opposite of what its description says for IDPTC — and the test pins the wrong side
findings.rootCause: `presetToWeights` branches on the registry `isRetail` flag; only `ktcSfTep` carries it. The preset descriptions were written assuming IDPTC is retail (which display-helpers.js:292 also assumes, calling it 'the analogous retail anchor').
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/weight-presets.js:68-77 — `const isRetail = !!source.isRetail; if (key === "market") { weight = isRetail ? 2.0 : 0.5; }`; description at :49-51 — `"Retail (KTC, IDPTC) × 2.0, experts × 0.5."`. Registry: `idpTradeCalc` has `isRetail: false` (dynasty-data.js:239). Executed: market preset puts only `ktcSfTep` at 2.0; `idpTradeCalc` gets 0.5. Expert preset gives `idpTradeCalc` 1.5 while the description says retail gets 0.5. `frontend/__tests__/weight-presets.test.js:22-35` asserts the isRetail-driven behavior, so the discrepancy is cemented rather than caught.
findings.userImpact: A user in an IDP league who picks 'Market (retail-lean)' expecting the board to read like what their leaguemates negotiate against gets the IDP retail anchor DOWN-weighted to 0.5 and every IDP expert board weighted equally. The whole IDP half of the board moves the wrong way, and the label says it moved the right way.
findings.recommendedFix: Decide what 'retail' means once. Either flag `idpTradeCalc` as retail in both registries (which also fixes `_compute_market_gap` producing 'none' for every IDP row) or rewrite the two preset descriptions to name only KTC. The current state — the code says one thing, the label another, and display-helpers a third — is the worst of the three.
findings.complexity: low if the labels change; medium if the flag changes, since `_retail_source_keys()` feeds the backend's market-gap signal and would move every IDP row's direction.

findings.title: The 'Seller cash-out' ROS tag compares a 0-9999 value against a 0-86 value and can never fire
findings.rootCause: Scale mismatch between `dynastyValue` (the 1-9999 board) and `rosValue` (the ROS aggregate's 0-100-ish score).
findings.evidence: frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:108 — `if (veteran && isStrong && dynastyValue != null && dynastyValue < rosValue * 0.7) tags.push("Seller cash-out");` with `isStrong = rosValue >= 60` (:100) and `dynastyValue = row.values?.full ?? row.rankDerivedValue` (:142). Live `data/ros/aggregate/latest.json`: rosValue range 0.03-86.42 over 1,085 players. The condition therefore requires `dynastyValue < 60.5` while simultaneously requiring `rosValue >= 60`. Executed against the live board joined to the ROS aggregate: 2 matched veterans with rosValue ≥ 60, 0 fires. Also `row.values?.full ?? row.rankDerivedValue` never reaches the right operand — `values.full` is always a number after buildRows.
findings.userImpact: One of nine advertised contender-layer labels is dead. Low severity because the tag is explicitly informational and the section is gated behind `settings.showRosTags`, but it is a decision label the product claims to produce and does not.
findings.recommendedFix: Normalize before comparing — e.g. compare ROS rank against board rank, or scale `rosValue` onto the 1-9999 range — or delete the rule. All nine thresholds in `_tagsForPlayer` are frontend-only magic numbers with no backend counterpart and no test; they deserve a look as a group.

findings.title: Rank range filters exclude the 216 rows whose rank the # column shows
findings.rootCause: `rowMatches` reads `canonicalConsensusRank` while the table's # column and its rank sort read `resolvedRank` (backend rank, else the client ordinal).
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/player-filters.js:166-168 — `const rank = num(row.canonicalConsensusRank); if (c.rankMin != null && (rank === null || rank < c.rankMin)) return false;`. Compare frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:166-168 — `resolvedRank` returns `canonicalConsensusRank ?? computedConsensusRank`, which page.jsx:581-583 uses for the rank sort and :888 renders as `row.rank`.
findings.userImpact: A user filtering 'rank 1-2000' to include the whole board silently loses the 216 client-ranked rows, even though they visibly carry ranks 857-1072 in the column he is filtering on. The fail-closed rule at player-filters.js:15-19 is the right policy; the inconsistency is that the column and the filter disagree about what a rank is.
findings.recommendedFix: If the primary fix (render '—' for unranked rows) lands, this resolves itself. Otherwise make the filter use `resolvedRank`.

findings.title: /rankings/k routes to a board that is always empty by construction
findings.rootCause: `POSITION_ALIASES` maps `k` to `K`, but `classifyPos('K')` returns 'excluded' and both materializers drop excluded rows before the filter ever runs.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/[position]/page.jsx:30 — `k: "K",`; frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:131 — `if (p === "K" || UNSUPPORTED.has(p)) return "excluded";`; :946 — `if (cls === "excluded") return null;` and :1141 — `if (classifyPos(pos) === "excluded") return null;`. The route's own comment (:9) advertises '/k'.
findings.userImpact: A documented route lands on an empty board with the 'No players match these filters' empty state rather than the deliberate 404-avoidance redirect the file describes. Trivial, but it is a route the file claims works.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop `k` from `POSITION_ALIASES` so it falls into the unknown-position branch and redirects to the full board.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md and two in-file comments assert the legacy `players` dict is the default materializer path; desktop has requested `view=array` (no legacy dict) since device-profile landed
findings.rootCause: `preferredDataView()` returns 'array' for desktop and 'compact' for mobile; neither is the `view=app` runtime payload the 'legacy is default' claim was written for.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/device-profile.js:103-108 — `export function preferredDataView() { if (isMobileProfile() || isSlowNetwork()) return "compact"; return "array"; }`; consumed at dynasty-data.js:1461-1468. server.py:1969-1975 builds the array payload by `array_payload.pop("players", None)`. Contradicting claims: dynasty-data.js:1857-1860 — 'The legacy path is the DEFAULT one (server.py pops playersArray off the runtime payload), so an applier that writes only the first set … on the path that actually ships'; and CLAUDE.md's valuation-overlay section repeats it.
findings.userImpact: No live breakage — `applyValuationOverlay` defensively writes both key sets, and `mergeRankingsDelta`'s runtime-synthesis branch is unreachable in practice. The risk is to future maintainers: a change reasoned from 'legacy is the shipping path' would be reasoning about a path desktop users never take, and the two materializers have already drifted (previous finding).
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the comment and the CLAUDE.md paragraph to name the actual per-device views, and note that the array materializer is the desktop-shipping path.

notes:
METHOD AND CONFIDENCE. Every numeric claim above was produced by executing code, not by reading it. I built the real API contract from the committed scrape (`build_api_data_contract(exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json)` → 1,092 playersArray rows, `hillCurves` stamped, all 24 source CSVs present under CSVs/site_raw/), then ran the actual frontend ESM modules against it under Node 22 (they are dependency-free enough to import directly). Scratch files are under the scratchpad; the repository was not modified.

WHAT THE CLAIM SURVIVES. CLAUDE.md's "there is no frontend ranking engine, period" is TRUE in its strongest sense: no client code blends sources, no client code applies a Hill curve, and the override path genuinely round-trips through the backend — I verified that disabling 6 IDP sources moved the displayed rank on 912 of 1,072 rows with zero regressions in override-invariant fields. `RANKING_SOURCES` parity is real: I re-ran the parity assertion and got zero errors on all nine checked fields across 21 sources in matching order. The fail-fast guard works. The buildRows sort produces zero inversions against backend rank order.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SURVIVE. "buildRows trusts backend stamps verbatim and never recomputes VALUES" is false in one specific, high-consequence way: when the backend refuses to price a row, `dynasty-data.js:1008` substitutes the raw scraper composite and renders it in the Value column indistinguishably from a Hill value. That is not a recomputation, which is why the wording technically holds — it is a scale substitution, which is worse, because a recomputation would at least be on the right scale. 260 rows, 249 with a visible number, 158 of them larger than the deepest genuinely-priced player. Paired with the 216 client-assigned ranks and the 10-tier client fallback sitting under a 127-tier backend scale, the bottom 20% of the board is a client-authored artifact wearing the backend's formatting.

The second systemic pattern is threshold proliferation. One backend signal (`marketGapDirection`/`marketGapMagnitude`) is re-thresholded at 0, 3 and 10 by three consumers, and the Edge rail prints a fourth number (`sourceRankSpread`) under the buy/sell label. The backend's own comment at data_contract.py:7666-7672 says `effectiveSourceRanks` was published expressly to stop conflicting edge signals across surfaces — the compact view then prunes that field, so mobile and desktop disagree on 8 players' verdicts anyway.

The third is documentation that has drifted into being actively wrong at the point of display, not just in comments: the published Hill formula (10-17% low), the published confidence rule (violated by half the badges it explains), "Top 800 get a consensus rank" (740 live), and the value chain that ends 282 points (median) from the number it claims to derive.

WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE A DECISION. `rankDerivedValue` and `canonicalConsensusRank` where the backend actually stamped them — rows 1-740 — are clean end to end: computed once, transmitted, rendered verbatim, override-aware, and consistent between the sort key and the displayed value. Everything below rank 740 on this board is client-authored and should not be traded on. Every BUY/SELL/HOLD label on the page should be treated as one of four possible answers until the thresholds are unified. The value chain, the ROS tags and the popup's consensus narrative are not currently reliable enough to reason from.

NOT VERIFIED / NOT VERIFIABLE FROM REPOSITORY: the BDVM "Fund gap" column's live behavior (needs the running endpoint plus `data/bdvm/` snapshots, which are gitignored); the league-adjusted overlay's live factors (needs `/api/valuation/league-adjusted` and a roster snapshot) — I verified its client applier logic and version pin by reading only; `valuation-mode.js` has no test file I could find; `positionRankByName`, the Sources-column denominator, `formatSourceCell`, `confidenceExplain`, `computeValueChain`, `consensusText`, `_tagsForPlayer` and the page's sort switch have no test coverage I could locate.

ONE LATENT ISSUE NOT RAISED AS A FINDING: duplicate values in the `#` column are not structurally prevented — the client ordinal is `arrayIndex + 1` while backend ranks stop at 740, so the two number spaces are only separated by a coincidental 71-slot gap. I forced a deep player (#700) unranked and got client #772 with no collision, and forced a top player (#9) unranked with the same result. It does not fire on this contract, but nothing in the code guarantees that on the next one.

formulas.name: Verdict bands (2-team)
formulas.expression: gap = sideTotals[0].adjusted − sideTotals[1].adjusted; abs=|gap|. verdictFromGap: abs<350 'Near even'; <900 'Lean'; <1800 'Strong lean'; else 'Major gap'. meterVerdict: abs<350 FAIR; <900 SLIGHT EDGE; <1800 UNFAIR; else LOPSIDED. colorFromGap: |gap|<350 → neutral, else gap>0 green / gap<0 red.
formulas.inputs: the two adjusted side totals only
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty sides → both totals 0 → gap 0 → 'Near even' / FAIR. An empty trade renders as a fair trade.
formulas.constants: 350 / 900 / 1800. Declared as VERDICT_NEAR_EVEN / VERDICT_LEAN / VERDICT_STRONG_LEAN at :27-29 but meterVerdict re-hardcodes the same three literals at :1433-1435 and TradeMeter.jsx re-hardcodes 350 at :124, :137, :141, :181. No backend counterpart uses these numbers; src/trade/suggestions.py:161 uses 256/769 and says so explicitly.
formulas.mathIssues: Absolute thresholds on a scale where legitimate trades span 200 to 20,000 total points. Executed: sides [900] vs [450,450] → gap 334 → 'Near even' / FAIR while the percentage gap is 27%. Conversely a 350-point gap on a 20,000-point trade (1.75%) is labelled SLIGHT EDGE. The band is scale-blind.
formulas.validated: Bands are pinned by frontend/__tests__/trade-logic.test.js:84-133 and 1246-1266 — i.e. the constants are regression-locked, not calibrated against anything. No document in docs/ derives 350/900/1800.

formulas.name: KTC per-player raw adjustment (processV)
formulas.expression: s = (0.05·(value/t)^1.3 + 0.05·(value/(1.05·maxInTrade))^6 + 0.1)·value; if nerfIndex>0: s ·= max(0.6, 1 − 0.15·nerfIndex); if s<0: s /= 4
formulas.inputs: player value, max value in the trade, top-of-board reference t, nerf index
formulas.missingDataBehavior: value ≤ 0 or maxInTrade ≤ 0 or t ≤ 0 → returns 0 (the piece contributes nothing to VA but still contributes to the raw sum)
formulas.constants: t = KTC_T_REFERENCE = 10041 (hardcoded, trade-logic.js:258 — KTC's live top value + 80, not ours); KTC_MAX_PLAYER_VAL = 10000 (:249); variance = 5% (:264); nerf floor 0.6, step 0.15; 'small piece' = value < 0.5·maxInTrade (:377). Python copies use the identical literals (market_value_adjustment.py:15-17, ktc_va.py:26-28).
formulas.mathIssues: The constants are calibrated to KTC's published board. The trade meter feeds them OUR blended rankDerivedValue (including IDP and picks KTC never prices). The per-source breakdown correctly feeds KTC's own raw values (TradeSourceBreakdown.jsx:124-130) — so the same trade gets a VA computed on two different inputs on the same page.
formulas.validated: Yes, against the market it claims to replicate: I ran frontend/lib/trade-logic.js::ktcAdjustPackage over all 139 captured KTC trades in scripts/ktc_va_observations.json — 139/139 correct recipient side, mean absolute error 4.68 points, max 306, mean relative error 0.24%. Cross-runtime: JS vs src/trade/ktc_va.py = 0 differences; ktc_va.py vs src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py = 0 differences.

formulas.name: KTC virtual-player solver (reverseAdjust)
formulas.expression: two-phase iterative search for V with processV(V,·)≈rawDiff: seed n = max((rawDiff/seed)·maxInTrade·0.8, maxInTrade); l starts n/2; outer ≤10 steps with step d·l·0.75, then if d>0.05 an inner ≤10 steps with step d·l·0.25; converged when d ≤ 0.025
formulas.inputs: rawDiff, maxInTrade, t, nerfCount
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rawDiff ≤ 0 or maxInTrade ≤ 0 → 0
formulas.constants: 0.8 seed, 0.75/0.25 step factors, 0.025 convergence, 0.05 refinement trigger, 10 iteration caps, and a literal 10099 passed as t in the 'intensity flip' branches (:482, :513) instead of KTC_T_REFERENCE=10041 — this is faithful to KTC's source but is an undocumented second top-of-board constant.
formulas.mathIssues: Not a bisection; it can terminate on bestL rather than a converged value. Faithful to KTC, so not a defect against the stated goal.
formulas.validated: Covered by the 139-case fixture run above.

formulas.name: VA display gates
formulas.expression: displayed = (value ≠ 0 AND signCheck w) AND |value / (team1Total + team2Total)| ≥ 0.033; forced false when both sides have exactly one piece
formulas.inputs: computed VA, both raw totals, piece counts
formulas.missingDataBehavior: either side empty → {value:0, side:0, displayed:false} (:419-421)
formulas.constants: 0.033 (3.3% of combined volume) and the 1v1 suppression. Both mirrored verbatim in the Python ports.
formulas.mathIssues: None found; the 1v1 rule is what makes tradeGapAdjusted([A],[B]) equal the plain value difference.
formulas.validated: The 36 zero-VA cases in the KTC fixture all reproduce.

formulas.name: Adjusted side totals
formulas.expression: adjusted_i = raw_i + va_i − stack_i, where raw_i = Σ effectiveValue(asset), va_i is non-zero for at most one side (2-team) and stack_i is the auction-power premium delta
formulas.inputs: side assets, valueMode, stackContext
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no stackContext → computeStackAdjustments returns zeros (:781); missing sideTeams/leagueStacks/moves, an unresolved team on any involved side, or sumDollars ≤ 0 → zeros (:784-804)
formulas.constants: none beyond the VA and auction-power constants
formulas.mathIssues: The MINUS sign on stack is only coherent if a side's total is the cost of what it GIVES. computeSideFlows adds the same quantity (+stack, :1421) to a received-minus-given net. The two are algebraically consistent with each other ONLY under the give reading — which is the opposite of what the meter's winner label asserts (see findings).
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/trade-logic.test.js:1855-1895 pins the stack arithmetic. Not runnable here.

formulas.name: Draft-capital stack adjustment
formulas.expression: post = leagueStacks with each move's dollars moved from→to; k = Σboard/Σdollars; stack_i = [(effectivePower_after[team_i] − post[team_i]) − (effectivePower_before[team_i] − leagueStacks[team_i])] · k. effectivePower: spread = max(1.4826·MAD, 0.01·grand/N); weighted_v = v·(1 + 0.35·tanh((v−median)/spread/1.25)); leader gets += 0.15·spread·tanh(lead/spread); rescaled to preserve the league total.
formulas.inputs: per-team auction dollars, the routed pick moves, board value of each pick
formulas.outputRange: board points, typically small relative to the pick's own value
formulas.missingDataBehavior: any gate unmet → zeros; the verdict silently falls back to pure board value (page.jsx:549-552)
formulas.constants: AP_PREMIUM_GAIN 0.35, AP_CURVATURE 1.25, AP_LEAPFROG_WEIGHT 0.15, MAD scale 1.4826, floor 0.01·mean. Identical literals exist in src/api/auction_power.py:142-161, which the trade path never calls.
formulas.mathIssues: k converts dollars to board points using only the picks IN this trade, so a trade with one cheap pick sets the exchange rate for the whole stack effect. No sensitivity analysis found.
formulas.validated: No backtest or calibration document found for the premium/curvature/leapfrog constants — auction-power.js:1-12 defers to the Python module's docstring, which is a rationale, not a validation.

formulas.name: Percentage gap / winner text
formulas.expression: pctGap = round(|A−B| / max(A,B) · 100); winnerText = 'Even' unless pctGap ≥ 3, then '<bigger side> wins by pctGap%'
formulas.inputs: the two adjusted totals
formulas.missingDataBehavior: max ≤ 0 → 0 → 'Even'
formulas.constants: 3% winner-text floor (TradeMeter.jsx:57); TradeFairnessExplanation.jsx:121 uses the same 3% as its fair/lean switch; MIN_NOTABLE_GAP = 200 (TradeFairnessExplanation.jsx:52)
formulas.mathIssues: The badge next to it is absolute (350/900/1800). Executed: totals 20,000 vs 19,500 → badge 'SLIGHT EDGE', text 'Even', narration 'Sources broadly agree this trade is fair.' Three answers, one card.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/trade-logic.test.js:1270-1290 pins percentageGap only.

formulas.name: Side flow net (N-team)
formulas.expression: given_i = Σ effectiveValue(assets of side i); received_dest += same value routed by destinations (2-team: dest = 1−i); net_i = received_i − given_i + stack_i
formulas.inputs: sides, destinations map, stackContext
formulas.missingDataBehavior: invalid/self/out-of-range destination → defaultDestination (next side, circular) — a silently wrong route rather than an error
formulas.constants: none
formulas.mathIssues: For a 2-team trade this yields net_A = −(rawA−rawB), the exact negation of the sign the 2-team meter shows as 'Side A wins'. Executed: sides A=[9000], B=[6000] → flows [{given:9000, received:6000, net:−3000}, {given:6000, received:9000, net:+3000}] while TradeMeterTwoTeam reports gap +3000 for A.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/trade-logic.test.js:1352-1465.

formulas.name: Retro at-trade valuation
formulas.expression: for each non-pick item: point = last rankHistory sample with date ≤ tradeTs, else the EARLIEST sample; value = point.val if finite and >0 else valueFromRank(point.rank) else the item's CURRENT value. Picks: always the current value. atTradeNet = Σgot − Σgave.
formulas.inputs: trade items, historyLookup(name), trade timestamp ms
formulas.missingDataBehavior: three distinct fallbacks, stamped as source 'rankHistory' | 'current_fallback'. The earliest-sample fallback is stamped 'rankHistory' even though the sample post-dates the trade — the UI cannot tell the two apart.
formulas.constants: ±200 verdict threshold (:118-120)
formulas.mathIssues: atTradeNet mixes as-of player values with today's pick values, so any trade containing a pick is partly hindsight even in the 'at trade' leg. Combined with the 180-day fetch clamp (frontend/lib/value-history.js:32) against a 365-day default trade window (app/trades/page.jsx:386), trades older than the history window are graded 'at trade' using the oldest sample available.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/trade-retro-value.test.js:9-93 exercises all three sources. data/rank_history.jsonl is absent from the repo, so real coverage depth is Not Verifiable from Repository.

formulas.name: Historical trade grade
formulas.expression: netLinear = got.linear − gave.linear (TODAY's values); vaNet = ±ktcAdjustPackage(gotValues, gaveValues).value; netAdjusted = netLinear + vaNet; scale = max(got.linear + max(0,vaNet), gave.linear + max(0,−vaNet), 1); pctGap = netAdjusted/scale·100; grade: <3 A 'Fair trade'; win <8 A, <15 A−, <25 B+, else A+; loss <8 B+, <15 B, <25 C, <40 D, else F
formulas.inputs: trade side item labels resolved against the CURRENT board
formulas.missingDataBehavior: an unresolvable player or pick contributes 0 to that side's total (league-analysis.js:140, and the resolve miss path) — the trade is graded as if the asset were worthless, with no marker on the card
formulas.constants: 3 / 8 / 15 / 25 / 40 percent. Unrelated to /trade's 350/900/1800 points and to suggestions.py's 256/769.
formulas.mathIssues: Pure hindsight: league-analysis.js:132 and :146 both read row.values.full, i.e. today's board, for a trade up to 365 days old.
formulas.validated: No backtest. The percent bands appear nowhere in docs/.

formulas.name: Client Hill reconstruction (retro fallback)
formulas.expression: value = round(1 + span / (1 + ((rank−1)/midpoint)^slope)) with midpoint 65.4, slope 0.91, span 9998
formulas.inputs: rank
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rank ≤ 0 or non-finite → 0
formulas.constants: 65.4 / 0.91 / 9998. The docstring (:325-331) says a parity test asserts agreement with the Python constants; the same docstring records that the previous trio (45 / 1.1 / 9999) was wrong for an unknown period.
formulas.mathIssues: Only reached when a history point lacks `val`; src/api/rank_history.py:390-397 back-fills val server-side, so this should be unreachable in production.
formulas.validated: Claimed parity test — I did not locate a runnable one in this environment.

formulas.name: Roster-fit verdict (backend)
formulas.expression: verdict = accept if composite ≥ 20; 'lean accept' if ≥ 8; 'neutral' if > −8; 'lean decline' if > −20; else 'decline'. composite = 0.55·fit + 0.45·equity with fitNormalization 4000, equityNormalization 2500.
formulas.inputs: before/after roster assets, receiving/sending, equity, rosterSettings
formulas.missingDataBehavior: returns None when rosterSettings has no starter slots (:390-391) — the panel then renders without a Roster-fit block
formulas.constants: 20 / 8 / −8 / −20 and the weights, all from config/trade/team_impact.json
formulas.mathIssues: None found. Note the equity fed in is the raw board equity, not the VA-adjusted gap the meter shows, so the two verdicts on the same page rest on different equity numbers.
formulas.validated: Config-driven and test-covered in tests/; not runnable here.

formulas.name: Balancing candidate selection
formulas.expression: target = |gap|; return [] if target < 350; candidates = rows with 0 < value ≤ 1.3·target sorted by |value − target|, top 5
formulas.inputs: the VA+stack-inclusive gap, a roster-filtered candidate pool
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty pool → empty list; page falls back from the inferred team's roster to the whole board (page.jsx:752-755)
formulas.constants: 350 floor (VERDICT_NEAR_EVEN), 1.3 ceiling, 5 results
formulas.mathIssues: The gap is VA-inclusive but the candidate is chosen by raw value. Adding a piece changes the piece counts and therefore the VA, so the suggested balancer does not close the gap it was sized against — and on 1-for-many shapes the VA moves faster than the added raw value.
formulas.validated: Unit-tested for shape only.

formulas.name: Verdict bar position
formulas.inputs: gap
formulas.missingDataBehavior: gap 0 → 50
formulas.constants: maxGap 4000 default
formulas.mathIssues: Display only; saturates at ±4000, which the executed 1-for-many cases exceed routinely (VA alone reached 6671 on 9000 vs 1800×5).
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/trade-logic.test.js:849-860

findings.title: The trade verdict's direction is undefined: the meter calls the side with the BIGGER pile the winner, while every other part of the same page treats a side's pile as what that side GIVES AWAY
findings.rootCause: There is no single stated convention for what `sides[i].assets` means in a 2-team trade, and the codebase implements both. The verdict label picked one; the flow math, the stack lens, the simulator hand-off, the 3+-team meter and the side-card labels picked the other.
findings.evidence:
GIVE convention — frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:1392-1393 `const value = ...effectiveValue(asset...); result[i].given += value;` then `result[dest].received += value`; frontend/app/trade/trade-sections.jsx:808 `
Giving
` over `side.assets`; frontend/components/graphs/MultiTradeFlow.jsx:80 "Each side appears once on the left (giver)"; frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1313-1319 "Whichever side has more matches is 'my side' (I'm giving)" → those names are sent as `playersOut`; page.jsx:1587 applySuggestion puts the backend's `give` list on side 0. WIN-IS-BIGGER convention — frontend/components/trade/TradeMeter.jsx:37,58-60 `const gap = pwA - pwB; ... winnerText = gap > 0 ? \`${labelA} wins by ${pctGap}%\``; TradeFairnessExplanation.jsx:135 `const winnerLabel = overallGap > 0 ? labelA : labelB;`; page.jsx:2084-2085 `
{verdictFromGap(pwGap)}` with colorFromGap green for gap>0. The arithmetic settles which reading the math uses: trade-logic.js:843 `adjusted: rawA + adjA - stackA` subtracts a side's own stack GAIN, while :1421 `net = received - given + stack[i]` adds it — the two are consistent only if `adjusted` is a give-total. In 2-team mode nothing on screen says which it is: the 'Giving'/'Receiving' labels render only when `sides.length > 2` (trade-sections.jsx:807, 836).
findings.userImpact: Executed on the real module: sides A=[9000] vs B=[6000] produce `gap = +3000` → the sticky tray and meter show green on Side A and 'Side A wins by 33%', while `computeSideFlows` on the identical input returns `net_A = -3000` and the 3-side meter would render Side A as 'Losing value' in red. A user reading the headline verdict can be told the exact opposite of what the same page's flow numbers say. This is the single number the whole page exists to produce.
findings.recommendedFix: Declare one convention in code and in the 2-team UI (add the 'Giving'/'Receiving' labels unconditionally, or rename the meter output to 'Side A's package is worth N% more'), then align the loser: either flip TradeMeter.jsx:58-60 + TradeFairnessExplanation.jsx:135-136 + colorFromGap, or flip computeSideFlows/runSimulateTrade/MultiTradeFlow. Pin it with a test that asserts the sign of `sideTotals[0].adjusted - sideTotals[1].adjusted` against the sign of `computeSideFlows(...)[0].net`.
findings.complexity: low to change, high to decide — every downstream label and the stack sign depend on the choice

findings.title: Two share-link producers feed the same trade builder with opposite side semantics, so a trade opened from history simulates backwards
findings.rootCause: buildShareUrl/encodeTrade carries no field saying whether a side's player list is what the team gave or got, and the two producers made opposite choices.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:238-242 builds each share side from `side.got` — the comment at :233-234 says "Each calculator side mirrors what that team RECEIVED". frontend/app/arbitrage/page.jsx:84-88 builds `sides: [{name: myTeam, players: give}, {name: opponent, players: receive}]` — side 0 is what I GIVE. Both land in the same consumer via parseShareParam (frontend/lib/trade-share.js:148-161). frontend/lib/trade-share.js:83-92 encodes only `{n, p}` per side — no direction field.
findings.userImpact: Open a historical trade from /trades in the calculator and press the roster simulator: page.jsx:1314-1338 decides 'my side' by which side holds my roster's players and sends those as `playersOut`. Under the /trades encoding those are the players I RECEIVED, so /api/trade/simulate is asked to remove players I own and add players I already have — the 'Impact on my team' before/after deltas, starter deltas and accept/decline verdict are inverted. The same link from /arbitrage simulates correctly.
findings.recommendedFix: Add an explicit direction to the share schema (e.g. `d: "give"|"get"` per side, defaulting to the builder's declared convention) and bump SHARE_SCHEMA_VERSION, or normalise both producers to the same meaning. Add a round-trip test that encodes from /trades and asserts the resulting playersIn/playersOut of runSimulateTrade.

findings.title: Fairness bands are absolute points on a board whose trades span two orders of magnitude, so a 27% imbalance is labelled FAIR
findings.rootCause: verdictFromGap/meterVerdict switch on |gap| in raw board points with no normalisation by trade size, while the winner text and the narration beside them switch on percent.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:27-29 `const VERDICT_NEAR_EVEN = 350; const VERDICT_LEAN = 900; const VERDICT_STRONG_LEAN = 1800;` and :1432-1436 `if (absGap < 350) return { label: "FAIR" ... }`. Executed against the real module: `[900]` vs `[450,450]` → raw 900 vs 900, VA 334 to the single-piece side, gap 334 → verdictFromGap 'Near even', meterVerdict FAIR — with percentageGap = 27. In the other direction, totals of 20,000 vs 19,500 (1.75%) give gap 500 → 'SLIGHT EDGE'.
findings.userImpact: Depth-piece and pick-for-pick trades — the majority of real dynasty trades by count — are graded FAIR at imbalances a user would immediately reject, and elite-tier packages are flagged as unfair at differences inside any source's noise. Two users comparing a small trade and a big trade get labels that do not mean the same thing.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the band a function of trade size, e.g. classify on max(absolute floor, percent of max(sideA,sideB)) — the components already compute percentageGap. At minimum, publish the percentage next to the badge in every case rather than only when pctGap ≥ 3.

findings.title: One card shows three different fairness answers for the same trade
findings.rootCause: The verdict badge uses an absolute gap, the winner text uses a 3% floor, and the narration below uses a 3% fair/lean switch — all rendered together with no shared criterion.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/trade/TradeMeter.jsx:40 `const verdict = meterVerdict(absGap);` vs :57 `if (pctGap >= 3) { winnerText = ... }` vs frontend/components/trade/TradeFairnessExplanation.jsx:121-130 `if (pctGap < 3) { ... return "Sources broadly agree this trade is fair..." }`. Both are rendered from the same sideTotals at frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1950-1956 and :1979.
findings.userImpact: Totals 20,000 vs 19,500 render simultaneously as the badge 'SLIGHT EDGE', the text 'Even', and the sentence 'Sources broadly agree this trade is fair.' The user cannot tell which one is the verdict.
findings.recommendedFix: Derive all three from one classifier and pass the result down; the narration should take the badge's level as an input rather than recomputing fairness.

findings.title: Historical trade grades are pure hindsight — today's board applied to trades up to a year old — and the as-of correction is a secondary badge with three silent fallbacks
findings.rootCause: analyzeRawTrade values every asset at the current board; gradeRetro was layered on top as a badge instead of replacing the grade, and its own at-trade leg is incomplete.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:132 `value: row.values?.full || 0` (picks) and :146 `const baseVal = row.values?.full || 0` (players) — the live contract's current value. The headline is built from that: :394-395 `const pctGap = (netAdjusted / scale) * 100; const grade = gradeTradeHistorySide(...)`, rendered at frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:225-232 as '<team> won by X%' with letter grades from league-analysis.js:87-98. The as-of path exists but: frontend/lib/trade-retro-value.js:77-85 `if (it.isPick) { // Picks: lean on the current value ... const v = Number(it.val) || 0; ... source: "current" }`; :52-55 falls back to the EARLIEST sample when the trade predates coverage yet still stamps `source: "rankHistory"` (:91); and frontend/lib/value-history.js:32 `const key = String(Math.max(1, Math.min(180, Math.floor(days))));` clamps the request to 180 days while frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:386 defaults the trade window to 365 days and :394 asks for `{ days: 365 }`.
findings.userImpact: Every 'A+ / Fleeced / won by 38%' verdict on /trades is retrodiction: a player who broke out after the trade makes the acquirer look prescient and the sender look robbed, when at the time the deal may have been even. Trades older than 180 days additionally get an 'at trade' value taken from the oldest snapshot in the window — post-dating the trade — with no UI marker, so the 'Aged well/poorly' badge is itself partly hindsight. Any trade containing a pick is hindsight-priced even in the as-of leg.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the at-trade valuation the primary grade and demote today's value to the 'how it aged' column. Stop clamping to 180 in fetchRankHistory (the backend allows 1095 — server.py:3539, MAX_SNAPSHOTS = 365*3). Stamp a distinct source (e.g. 'earliest_available') when pointAt falls through to the earliest sample, surface it, and either persist per-pick value history or label pick legs as current-priced on the card.

findings.title: The Monte Carlo panel silently ignores the page's value mode and every per-player value override — the exact divergence its own docstring says it exists to prevent
findings.rootCause: TradeMeter accepts `valueMode` and `settings` props but its signature drops them, and it is handed the raw `sides` state rather than the override-applied copy the totals use.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/trade/TradeMeter.jsx:24 `export default function TradeMeter({ sides, sideTotals, flows }) {` — `valueMode`/`settings` are passed at frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1954-1955 and never destructured; :107 `<MonteCarloButton sides={sides} />` with no valueMode, so frontend/components/ui/MonteCarloButton.jsx:118 defaults `valueMode = "full"`. Separately, page.jsx:1951 passes `sides={sides}` while the totals at :638-661 are computed from `sidesWithOverrides` (:534-544, which stamps `customValue`), and effectiveValue honours `customValue` first (trade-logic.js:183). MonteCarloButton.jsx:1-21 states the requirement it is violating: "the per-player values sent to the simulator must match what the trade builder displays".
findings.userImpact: Switch the value mode to 'Raw' and the meter, the totals and the MC panel disagree — MC keeps simulating the 'full' board. Type a custom value for a player (a first-class feature with its own UI) and the meter uses it while MC does not, reproducing the meter-vs-MC mismatch (-4281 vs -632) the component was written to fix.
findings.recommendedFix: Destructure and forward `valueMode`/`settings` in TradeMeter, and pass `sidesWithOverrides` to TradeMeter (and to TradeSourceBreakdown at page.jsx:1994-1998, which has the same omission).

findings.title: RosTradeFitPanel compares a 0-9999 dynasty value against a 0-100 ROS value, making the 'Seller cash-out' tag effectively unreachable
findings.rootCause: The client re-implementation copied the Python predicate but feeds it a value on a different scale.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:75 `if (veteran && isStrong && dynastyValue != null && dynastyValue < rosValue * 0.7) tags.push("Seller cash-out");` with the input supplied at :127 `dynastyValue: row?.values?.full ?? row?.rankDerivedValue ?? null` — the board scale. The Python original expects the same 0-100 scale: src/ros/tags.py:73 uses the identical predicate and its test passes `dynasty_value=40` against `ros_value=70` (tests/ros/test_direction_and_tags.py:146-150, comment `# 40 < 70 * 0.7`). rosValue*0.7 can never exceed 70, so any player with a real board value fails the test.
findings.userImpact: The one tag whose entire purpose is 'sell this player now' never fires for a rostered player. Users see the panel and reasonably conclude no asset in the trade is a sell candidate.
findings.recommendedFix: Normalise dynastyValue to the ROS 0-100 scale (or compare percentiles) before the test, and add the parity test the file promises.

findings.title: RosTradeFitPanel fetches team buyer/seller directions, uses them to decide whether to render, and then never displays them
findings.rootCause: A render branch was removed or never written; the gate that depended on it was left in place.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:86 `const [directions, setDirections] = useState({ teams: [] });`, fetched at :92-95 from `/api/public/league/rosTradeDeadline`, then used exactly once: :138-139 `const hasDirections = (directions?.teams || []).length > 0; if (!hasAnyTags && !hasDirections) return null;`. `directions` appears nowhere in the JSX (lines 141-212). The `LABEL_COLOR` map at :48-56 ('Strong Buyer' … 'Strong Seller / Rebuilder') is never referenced.
findings.userImpact: A network request on every /trade visit for data that is never shown, and the panel renders a 'ROS Fit' card with zero tags whenever the directions payload happens to be non-empty — looking broken rather than empty.
findings.recommendedFix: Either render the per-team buyer/seller labels (the colour map is already written) or drop the fetch and the gate.

findings.title: A production-facing classifier is duplicated in JS while its Python original has no caller and no parity test
findings.rootCause: src/ros/tags.py was written as the source of truth and then bypassed by a client-side copy; the promised parity test was never added.
findings.evidence: grep for `tags_for_player` across the repo returns only its definition at src/ros/tags.py:32 and tests/ros/test_direction_and_tags.py — no route, no script, no src/ caller. The live implementation is frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:61-83, whose own comment at :58-60 reads "mirrors src/ros/tags.py::tags_for_player … Stays in sync via the parity test (PR-future)" — no such test exists.
findings.userImpact: The tested copy is not the copy users see. The thresholds happen to match today (60/80/rank 100/rank 50 and the same per-position veteran ages, src/ros/direction.py:24-36 vs RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:70), except for the dynasty-value scale bug above — which is precisely the class of drift a parity test would have caught.
findings.recommendedFix: Either expose tags_for_player through the existing ROS endpoint and have the panel render backend tags, or write the parity test (the source-registry parity test at tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py is the established pattern for parsing JS constants from Python).

findings.title: Three independent ports of the KTC Value Adjustment with no test tying two of them together
findings.rootCause: src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py was added for the finder without noticing src/trade/ktc_va.py already existed.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:407 `export function ktcAdjustPackage`, src/trade/ktc_va.py:146 `def ktc_adjust_package` ("Verbatim translation of the JS port"), src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py:1-7 `def ktc_adjust_package` ("a line-for-line Python port of the authoritative frontend implementation"). Consumers are split: ktc_va → suggestions.py:_va_gap, angle.py, monte_carlo.py:152; market_value_adjustment → finder_value_adjustment.py:16. Each has its own fixture test (tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py, tests/trade/test_finder_value_adjustment.py) and neither compares against the other. CLAUDE.md's Trade Engines section names neither module.
findings.userImpact: None today — I executed all 139 fixture trades through all three: JS vs ktc_va.py = 0 differences, ktc_va.py vs market_value_adjustment.py = 0 differences. The risk is a one-sided edit: the arbitrage engine and the trade suggestions would then grade the same package differently with both test suites green.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete one Python copy and re-point its consumer, or add a single cross-module parity test that runs the shared fixture through both entry points.

findings.title: Balancing suggestions are sized against a VA-inclusive gap but selected by raw value, so the suggested piece does not close the gap
findings.rootCause: findBalancers treats the gap as a linear quantity, but adding a piece changes the piece counts that drive the Value Adjustment.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:756 `const list = findBalancers(pwGap, pool, valueMode);` where `pwGap` comes from the adjusted totals (:708-712). frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:1256-1260 selects purely on `Number(r.values?.[valueMode] || 0)` sorted by `Math.abs(a.value - target)`. Executed illustration of the sensitivity: `[9000]` vs `[4500,4500]` has raw totals equal and gap 4681 (all VA); `[9000]` vs `[3000,3000,3000]` gap 6014 — adding a third piece to the behind side *widened* the gap by 1333 despite the raw totals staying equal.
findings.userImpact: On any 1-for-many shape, following the app's own balancing advice can move the verdict further from even, and the user has no way to see why.
findings.recommendedFix: Score candidates by the resulting gap — recompute adjustedSideTotals with the candidate appended and rank by |resulting gap| — rather than by |value − gap|. The candidate pool is already capped at a few hundred rows, so the cost is bounded.

findings.title: The main verdict feeds KTC's board-specific constants with our blended values, while the per-source table on the same page feeds them KTC's real values
findings.rootCause: ktcAdjustPackage hardcodes KTC's top-of-board reference and 'max player' ceiling; only one of its two call sites supplies inputs from that board.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:249-258 `const KTC_MAX_PLAYER_VAL = 10000; ... const KTC_T_REFERENCE = 10041;` with the justification "we can't observe the live top value at compute time". The verdict path feeds our board: trade-logic.js:212-216 `sortedSideValues` → `effectiveValue(r, valueMode)` → `row.values[valueMode]` (rankDerivedValue). The breakdown path deliberately does not: frontend/components/trade/TradeSourceBreakdown.jsx:97-104 "the V13 Value Adjustment formula and its empirical suppression thresholds … were calibrated against KTC's raw 0-9999 piece values. Feeding the formula the canonical Hill-blended valueContribution instead would mis-fire VA" and :126-129 reads `row.rawSourceValues.ktcSfTep`.
findings.userImpact: The headline verdict's consolidation premium — up to 6,671 points on the shapes I executed, more than half the raw side total — is computed on inputs the formula was never validated against, and the file's own comment states why that mis-fires. Nothing validates the VA on our board; the 139-case fixture only validates it on KTC's.
findings.recommendedFix: Either state and test the assumption that rankDerivedValue is scale-compatible with KTC's board (compare our top-500 against ktcSfTep and pin the ratio), or compute the meter's VA from ktcSfTep-equivalent values the way the breakdown does, falling back to the blend only for assets KTC does not price.

findings.title: Dead code carrying tests: multiTeamAnalysis, tradeGapAdjusted and the whole V13 VA path are exported, tested, and rendered nowhere
findings.rootCause: Superseded implementations were kept 'for backwards-compat' and never removed once the last consumer went away.
findings.evidence: grep across frontend excluding lib/trade-logic.js and __tests__: `multiTeamAnalysis` appears only in a comment at frontend/components/trade/TradeMeter.jsx:115 (its 'Overpaying'/'Getting a deal' labels at trade-logic.js:1470-1475 render nowhere); `tradeGapAdjusted` (trade-logic.js:883) has no app caller — /trade computes the same gap inline at app/trade/page.jsx:712; `_vaFromSortedSides` (:563), `ktcRawAdjustment` (:112), `ktcSolveForAddedValue` (:139) and `VA_SCARCITY_SLOPE`/`VA_SCARCITY_INTERCEPT`/`VA_SCARCITY_CAP`/`VA_PER_EXTRA_BOOST`/`VA_EFFECTIVE_CAP`/`VA_POSITION_DECAY` (:93-98, explicitly "unused at runtime") have no consumer outside the file and its tests.
findings.userImpact: None directly. The cost is that ~200 lines of superseded verdict math sit beside the live path with green tests, which is how a future edit lands in the wrong function — and frontend/__tests__/trade-logic.test.js:1293-1320 currently certifies behaviour no user can reach.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the V13 path and multiTeamAnalysis with their tests; keep tradeGapAdjusted only if a caller is restored.

findings.title: Docstrings and status docs describe behaviour the code does not implement
findings.rootCause: Comments were not updated when the features they describe were removed or moved to the backend.
findings.evidence: (1) frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:193-201 — displayValue's docstring claims it resolves the value "including the Apply Scoring Fit adjustment when the global toggle is on" and warns that effectiveValue "also applies the pick-year discount"; the implementation at :203-209 does neither, effectiveValue at :181-185 applies no discount (the file's own note at :152-162 says the discount is backend-only), and grep for `scoringFit|applyScoring` across frontend/lib, components and app returns nothing. (2) frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:149-152 carries the same phantom "When the user has Apply Scoring Fit on, IDP values shift by delta × weight" above a line that returns `baseVal` unchanged. (3) frontend/components/trade/TradeSourceBreakdown.jsx:7-8, 21 and :97 describe "the V13 Value Adjustment math" and its "empirical suppression thresholds (V13_SUPPRESS_RAW_DIFF…)" while the code calls valueAdjustmentFromSideArrays → ktcAdjustPackage, the KTC-native port that superseded V13 (trade-logic.js:552-559). (4) docs/status/blueprint-gap-analysis.md:88 records "No balancing suggestions" — findBalancers is implemented (trade-logic.js:1244) and rendered (app/trade/page.jsx:728-805). findings.title: The /trades header claims trades are 'graded at alpha=1.65' but alpha no longer touches the grade
findings.rootCause: The alpha-weighted net was demoted to a winner/loser sort key when the KTC VA path landed; the header text was left behind.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:488 renders `${analysis.analyzed.length} trades in the last ${windowDays} days, graded at alpha=${alpha}.` The grade comes from frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:394-395 `const pctGap = (netAdjusted / scale) * 100; const grade = gradeTradeHistorySide(...)` where netAdjusted = netLinear + vaNet (:386-387). netWeighted (the alpha term, :317 `weighted += Math.pow(Math.max(safeVal, 1), alpha)`) is used only at :418-421 to order winner/loser, and league-analysis.js:389-390 explicitly excludes it from the denominator because it "would crush all pcts toward zero".
findings.userImpact: Users tuning `settings.alpha` expect the grades to move; they do not, except for which side is labelled winner in a 3+-team deal.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop alpha from the header (or from settings entirely) and state the actual grading basis: linear net plus KTC value adjustment, at current board values.

notes:
DIRECT ANSWERS TO THE THREE QUESTIONS.

(1) Where the verdict comes from. The fair/win/lose verdict on /trade is computed ENTIRELY ON THE CLIENT from side value sums. Chain: rows (backend rankDerivedValue, via useDynastyData) → effectiveValue (trade-logic.js:181-185, honours a per-trade customValue override) → sideTotal → adjustedSideTotals (:824-846) which adds the client-computed KTC Value Adjustment and subtracts the client-computed draft-capital stack effect → gap = totals[0].adjusted − totals[1].adjusted (page.jsx:712) → verdictFromGap / meterVerdict / colorFromGap. No backend endpoint returns a fairness verdict for the builder. The only backend verdict rendered on /trade is a different question — team_impact's accept/lean accept/neutral/lean decline/decline roster-FIT verdict (src/trade/team_impact.py:318-328), shown in the 'Impact on <team>' panel after an explicit simulate, and it uses raw board equity, not the VA-adjusted gap. /arbitrage, /angle, the BDVM panel and the Monte Carlo panel are all backend-computed and displayed verbatim.

(2) Fairness bands. 350 / 900 / 1800 absolute board points, declared at frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:27-29 and re-hardcoded at :1433-1435 and in TradeMeter.jsx (350, four times). They are frontend literals with no config file, no backend counterpart and no derivation in docs/ — regression-pinned by frontend/__tests__/trade-logic.test.js, which locks them but does not justify them. Other surfaces use unrelated numbers for the same concept: percent bands 3/8/15/25/40 on /trades (league-analysis.js:87-98), 256/769 in src/trade/suggestions.py:161 (whose comment at :154-158 states the divergence is deliberate), 20/8/−8/−20 for team_impact in config/trade/team_impact.json, ±200 for the retro badge (trade-retro-value.js:118-120), and a 3% floor for the winner text and narration.

(3) Client-only premiums/penalties. The client applies TWO adjustments to the displayed verdict that the /api/trade/simulate response never sees: (a) the KTC consolidation/roster-spot premium — large, up to 6,671 points on the shapes I executed, more than half a side's raw total; the backend has the identical math in two Python modules and does apply it in suggestions, angle, finder and Monte Carlo, but not in the simulate endpoint whose panel sits on the same page; (b) the draft-capital stack effect, computed only in frontend/lib/auction-power.js (src/api/auction_power.py exists but no trade route calls it). Going the other way, the BACKEND owns things the client deliberately does not re-apply: the future-year pick discount (src/api/data_contract.py::_pick_year_discount_for, already baked into rankDerivedValue — the client comment at trade-logic.js:152-162 documents a past double-discount bug), the TE premium, and positional need/scarcity (the league-adjusted lens arrives as backend factors and the roster-fit score is backend-only). No positional-need multiplier is applied client-side to any trade value.

(4) Retro value / hindsight. The /trades HEADLINE is hindsight: every asset is priced at today's board (league-analysis.js:132, :146) for trades up to 365 days old, then graded A+..F. trade-retro-value.js does compute a genuine as-of value for players from server-stamped snapshot values (src/api/rank_history.py stamps `val` per date), but it only produces a secondary 'Aged well / Aged poorly / Stable' badge, prices PICKS at today's value even inside the at-trade total, silently substitutes the earliest available snapshot for trades that predate coverage while still labelling the source 'rankHistory', and is fed by a fetch that clamps the window to 180 days (value-history.js:32) against a 365-day trade window. So: the primary verdict is hindsight, and the correction is partial and unlabelled.

VERIFICATION STATUS AND LIMITS. I executed frontend/lib/trade-logic.js directly under node and reproduced every number quoted (VA magnitudes, band boundaries, the 2-team-vs-flow sign flip). I ran the 139-trade KTC fixture (scripts/ktc_va_observations.json) through the JS port and both Python ports: all three agree with each other exactly, and the JS port reproduces the real KTC captures with mean absolute error 4.68 points and correct recipient side on 139/139 — the port genuinely replicates KTC, on KTC's inputs. Test SUITES could not be run: frontend/node_modules is absent and python3 has no pytest module in this environment, so every 'tested' claim above means 'a test file exists and I read it', not 'it passes'. data/rank_history.jsonl is gitignored and absent, so live retro coverage depth is Not Verifiable from Repository. Whether our rankDerivedValue board is scale-compatible with the KTC constants baked into the VA is Not Verified — exports/latest/ contains the raw scraper artifact, not an /api/data contract, so I could not sample live rankDerivedValue.

WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE A REAL DECISION. Trust: the Value Adjustment magnitude (validated against the market it copies), the backend-computed arbitrage/angle/BDVM/team-impact payloads (displayed verbatim, no client math), and the per-source winner table (correctly feeds KTC's own values into KTC's formula). Do not trust without fixing: the direction of the 2-team verdict (finding 1), any grade on /trades (hindsight), the FAIR/UNFAIR label on small trades (scale-blind bands), the Monte Carlo panel whenever value mode or an override is in play, and the 'Seller cash-out' ROS tag (unreachable).
