formulas.name: Contention phase classification
formulas.expression: isHighValue = totalValue > median(all teams' totalValue); isYounger = medianAge < median(all teams' medianAge) [STRICT <]; (high,young)→Win-now, (high,old)→Contender, (low,young)→Rebuild, (low,old)→Mixed. totalValue = Σ of the top-25 players by value; medianAge = median age OF THOSE TOP 25 ONLY (:65-67).
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue (or values.full) and age per rostered player; the 12 teams in rawData.sleeper.teams
formulas.constants: TOP_N_FOR_VALUE = 25 (:29). No equivalent constant exists in any backend module — this concept is frontend-only.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A player with no value>0 is dropped (:63). A team with no ages gets medianAge=null and is forced to the 'older' side by design (:82-86). Value is `rankDerivedValue || values.full || 0` (:52).
formulas.mathIssues: THREE. (1) The comparison is strict `<`, and per-team median ages are integers, so teams landing exactly on the league median are all silently classified 'older'. Measured on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json: 5 of 12 teams have medianAge exactly 25.0 = the league median. (2) The age median is taken over the TOP 25 BY VALUE, systematically excluding the cheap young prospects that define a rebuild — the 12 rosters carry 44-58 players, so 33-38 players per team are excluded. (3) It is a forced median split: the classification is purely relative, so the top team in a league of rebuilders is 'Win-now'.
formulas.validated: NO. Replayed on the live snapshot (value proxied by `_finalAdjusted`, ages exact): Win-now 2, Contender 4, Mixed 6, Rebuild 0. Because `partnerships` (:117-136) requires at least one Rebuild team, the panel's 'Natural trade partners for you' block renders NOTHING on live data.

formulas.name: Contender/Rebuilder tier score
formulas.expression: score = starterValue*0.7 + depthValue*0.2 + (pickValue > 0 ? -pickValue*0.1 : 0), where totalValue INCLUDES pickValue (:1016) and depthValue = totalValue − starterValue (:1027). Substituting: score = 0.7*S + 0.2*playerDepth + 0.1*P. The net coefficient on pick value is +0.1, not −0.1.
formulas.inputs: playerMeta values (0-9999 board), resolved pick values, the league's rosterPositions
formulas.outputRange: unbounded; ~60k-200k on the live roster sizes
formulas.constants: 0.7 / 0.2 / −0.1; tier split at ceil(n/3) top and n−top bottom (:1042-1043). None of these three weights exists in any backend module. The nearest analogue, src/ros/team_strength.py:33-36, uses 0.72/0.18/0.05/0.05 with no negative term.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Players missing from playerMeta are skipped (:1004). Unresolved picks contribute 0 (:1015). With rosterPositions null, fillLineup returns available:false and starterValue is 0, so every team scores as pure depth — the docstring at :983-985 acknowledges this.
formulas.mathIssues: Sign error: picks are added to totalValue, flow into depthValue at +0.2, then penalised at −0.1, netting +0.1. The docstring (:974) says 'Pick surplus penalized at -10% (rebuild signal)' and the user-facing InfoTip (frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:522-525) says 'a pick-surplus penalty (-10%)'. Both are false. Verified numerically: score(S=60000, Dp=20000, P=0) = 46000; score(..., P=10000) = 47000; Δ/unit = +0.1000.
formulas.validated: NO test exists. Replayed on the live snapshot (approximate pick-label resolution, top-21-by-value as the starter proxy): correcting the sign moves 7 of 12 teams, including the #1 seed — the team holding 72 picks worth ~175k drops from rank 1 to rank 6.

formulas.name: Starter-slot fill
formulas.expression: Sort assets by value desc; pass 1 assigns strict slots (positionOf(p) === slot); pass 2 assigns flex slots (FLEX_POOLS[slot].has(positionOf(p))). Greedy, value-first, no backtracking.
formulas.inputs: assets, rosterPositions (or fallbackSlots), positionOf, valueFor
formulas.outputRange: {starters, bench, assignments, slotCount, unfilledSlots, available, usedFallback}
formulas.constants: NON_LINEUP_SLOTS = {BN, IR, TAXI} (:144); FLEX_POOLS (:69-101) covers 20 Sleeper slot aliases.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: With no rosterPositions and no fallbackSlots it returns available:false, starters:[], bench:everything — deliberately, so callers cannot read 'unknown lineup' as 'starts nobody' (:238-244). This is the correct posture and both callers surface it.
formulas.mathIssues: Greedy value-first fill is not globally optimal — a high-value SUPER_FLEX-eligible QB can be claimed by a strict QB slot in pass 1 in a way that leaves a worse total. In practice with SFLEX:1 the effect is small. `valueFor` defaults to `p.value` and the docstring at :230-234 warns that passing the wrong accessor silently produces an insertion-order fill; both live callers pass an explicit accessor.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/starter-slots.test.js is the most thorough test in this audit. Registry check: dynasty_main starters sum to 21 (config/leagues/registry.json:19-31), dynasty_new to 10.

formulas.name: Positional strength ratio
formulas.expression: myStrengths[g] = myTeam.byGroup[g] / mean(all teams' byGroup[g]); weakest = the 2 lowest of {QB,RB,WR,TE}; a target team qualifies at otherStrength >= 1.0; a target player qualifies at 1200 <= meta <= 8000; 'their need' fires at worstRatio < 1.0.
formulas.inputs: per-team byGroup totals at the current asset scope; computeGroupAverages (league-analysis.js:742-749)
formulas.outputRange: ratio, displayed as a percentage of league average
formulas.constants: 1.0 (target-team gate), 1200 / 8000 (player value band), 1500 (surplus chip floor, :421), top-2 weakest / strongest. All frontend-only; no backend counterpart.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: groupAvg[g] == 0 → strength defaults to 1 for the user (:379) but to 0 for other teams (:393), an asymmetry that would make every other team fail the >= 1.0 gate.
formulas.mathIssues: Ratio-to-MEAN over 12 teams is dominated by a single outlier; a median or z-score would be stable. The candidate pool is restricted to OFFENSE_GROUPS, so in an IDP league starting 3 DL + 3 LB + 3 DB, no defensive weakness can ever be named. The value band 1200-8000 excludes exactly the elite acquisitions a genuine positional hole would call for.
formulas.validated: NO test.

formulas.name: Trade grade — private path
formulas.expression: netAdjusted = (got.linear − gave.linear) + vaNet; gotEffective = got.linear + max(0, vaNet); gaveEffective = gave.linear + max(0, −vaNet); pctGap = netAdjusted / max(gotEffective, gaveEffective, 1) * 100. Letters at |pct| < 3 / 8 / 15 / 25 / 40.
formulas.inputs: resolved 0-9999 asset values per side; vaNet from ktcAdjustPackage
formulas.constants: 3 / 8 / 15 / 25 / 40; TRADE_ALPHA used only for the diagnostic `weighted` sums, deliberately EXCLUDED from pctGap — the comment at :388-390 says including alpha sums 'would crush all pcts toward zero'. The public grader does exactly what this comment forbids.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Unresolvable assets resolve to value 0 (:140, :184) and contribute max(0, v) = 0 to `linear` but max(v,1)^alpha = 1 to `weighted` (:320-322).
formulas.mathIssues: None internal. The defect is cross-surface — see findings.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/league-analysis.test.js:218-407. No cross-check against the public grader.

formulas.name: Trade grade — public path
formulas.expression: w_side = Σ max(value, 1)^1.65 over receivedAssets; pct = (max_w − min_w) / max_w * 100; letters at the SAME 3/8/15/25/40 thresholds.
formulas.inputs: per-asset valuation callable over each side's receivedAssets
formulas.outputRange: letter A+..F + label + colour, rendered publicly
formulas.constants: _GRADE_ALPHA = 1.65 (:49); _GRADE_PCT_FAIR/SLIGHT/GOOD/CLEAR/ROBBERY = 3/8/15/25/40 (:50-54). The thresholds are copied from the frontend; the pct they are applied to is not.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Non-finite values are floored to 0 then to 1 by max(val,1.0) (:108-118). All-zero sides grade as fair (:126-130).
formulas.mathIssues: The alpha exponent makes the pct a measure of CONCENTRATION, not of value imbalance. Verified numerically: a perfectly even 1×8000 for 2×4000 swap yields publicPct = 36.27 → 'A+ Big win' / 'D Robbery'; the private path yields pctGap = 0.00 → 'A Fair trade' on both sides. 1×6000 for 3×2000 yields publicPct = 51.04 (past the 'F Fleeced' line) versus private 0.00.
formulas.validated: tests/public_league/test_public_contract.py:363-436 tests NaN handling and 3-team extremes. NO test compares a trade's public grade to its private grade, so the header comment at activity.py:40-44 claiming they 'land in the same bucket' is unverified and false.

formulas.name: Luck delta and verdict
formulas.expression: expectedShare(week) = (beats + ties*0.5) / (n−1) over that week's SCORED rosters; expectedWins = Σ expectedShare; luckDelta = actualWins − expectedWins. Verdict: >1.0 Blessed, >0.3 Lucky, >-0.3 Deserved, >-1.0 Unlucky, else Cursed. Colour: >0.5 bright green, >0.1 pale green, <-0.5 red, <-0.1 orange.
formulas.inputs: per-week roster points and actual matchup results, regular season only
formulas.outputRange: luckDelta in wins, roughly ±5 over a career
formulas.constants: ±1.0 / ±0.3 for the word; ±0.5 / ±0.1 for the colour. Both frontend-only. The backend emits `luckPerGame` (luck.py:290) and the UI never reads it.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `metrics.is_scored` = points > 0 (src/public_league/metrics.py:57-59), so a roster at 0 is treated as not-yet-played and excluded from the all-play field entirely.
formulas.mathIssues: TWO. (1) The verdict bands are absolute wins applied identically to a 14-game season row and a ~45-game career row, so 'Blessed' is far easier to earn over a career. (2) The word and the colour disagree over three bands: at luckDelta = +0.2 the cell is pale green ('lucky') but reads 'Deserved'; at −0.2 it is orange ('unlucky') but reads 'Deserved'; at +0.6 it is the brightest green but reads only 'Lucky'.
formulas.validated: Arithmetic tested (tests/public_league/test_metrics_engines.py). Band choice never validated. Flip sensitivity: a single game moves luckDelta by up to 1.0, which spans the entire ±0.3 'Deserved' band — so the verdict changes on essentially any week's result, and DURING a live week (see findings).

formulas.name: Power ranking v1 composite
formulas.expression: power = 100 * (0.50*PPG_percentile + 0.25*last3avg_percentile + 0.25*allPlayShare_thisWeek), where PPG is accumulated in `career_state` OUTSIDE the season loop (:82-84) and is therefore a CAREER PPG across every season in the snapshot, while the all-play term is a SINGLE WEEK's share (:126-131) and `record` is a career W-L (:143-147).
formulas.inputs: weekly roster points, weekly all-play shares, actual W/L shares
formulas.constants: _W_PPG 0.50, _W_RECENT 0.25, _W_ALLPLAY 0.25, _RECENT_WINDOW 3 (:45-49). Compare src/ros/power_v2.py:64-75, which uses nine components with none of these weights.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: _percentile_rank returns 0.5 when n <= 1 (:57-58). Owners absent from a week simply do not appear in that week's ranking.
formulas.mathIssues: Three time scales are blended as if they were one: 50% on a multi-season career average, 25% on a 3-game window that resets each season, 25% on a single week. Because PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS defaults to 3 (src/public_league/sleeper_client.py:44), the dominant term can average ~45 games, so the 'weekly power ranking' is dominated by a number that barely moves week to week. The code's own comment at :126-130 admits the all-play shortcut ('simpler + still useful is current-week all-play share'). The module docstring at :6 says PPG is 'season-to-date'; the accumulator comment at :81 says 'career PPG-to-date'; the methodology string shown to the user (:214-219) says neither.
formulas.validated: NO.

formulas.name: Playoff-odds Monte Carlo
formulas.expression: For each of 10,000 sims: for each remaining week, sample each owner's score with replacement from their empirical weekly-score pool; award W/L/T; rank by (wins + 0.5*ties desc, pointsFor desc); count top-`spots` finishes. probability = made / num_sims.
formulas.inputs: per-owner scored regular-season weeks this season, the posted/inferred remaining schedule, playoff_spots
formulas.constants: DEFAULT_SIMS 10_000, MIN_SAMPLED_WEEKS 2, DEFAULT_PLAYOFF_SPOTS 6 (:66-74)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Owners with fewer than MIN_SAMPLED_WEEKS scored weeks get `scores + league_pool` (:638) — note this CONCATENATES, it does not replace. An owner with no data at all gets a flat [100.0] placeholder (:641-644), explicitly labelled uninformative.
formulas.mathIssues: MIN_SAMPLED_WEEKS = 2 means an owner with exactly 2 scored weeks is sampled from a 2-point empirical distribution for every remaining week — up to 12 weeks resampled from 2 observations. The module docstring at :44-46 justifies the guard as stopping 'a hot streak from a handful of weeks' getting amplified; 2 IS a handful. Also: `rng = rng or random.Random()` (:460) is unseeded, so the docstring claim at :6-7 that 'every input is explicit so the caller can reproduce a run' is false for the default path.
formulas.validated: Standard error at p=0.5, n=10,000 is 0.5pp, so refresh-to-refresh jitter is roughly ±1pp — small, and the frontend caches for 30 minutes (frontend/app/league/sections/power.jsx:299-333) specifically to keep it from visibly jittering. This module DOES guard live-week partial scores (`_matchup_is_final`, :123-147), unlike luck.py and power.py.

formulas.name: Rivalry index
formulas.expression: index = 5*playoffMeetings + 3*gamesDecidedByFive + 2*gamesDecidedByTen + 2*seasonsWhereSeriesSplit + 1*totalMeetings + 2*meetingsInMostRecentSeason
formulas.inputs: every head-to-head meeting in the snapshot window
formulas.constants: 5/3/2/2/1/2; closeness bands 5.0 and 10.0 points (:118-121). None of these appear in the UI.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Pairs that never met are simply absent.
formulas.mathIssues: gamesDecidedByFive is a strict SUBSET of gamesDecidedByTen (both counters increment for a ≤5-point game, :118-121), so a close game scores 3+2 = 5 before the +1 for the meeting itself. Verified: a single 3-point regular-season game this season scores 8; a 40-point blowout in the same slot scores 3. This is precisely the overlapping-window double-count that src/intel/signals.py:9-25 spends 17 lines of docstring condemning in the same repository.
formulas.validated: tests/public_league/test_metrics_engines.py:110 asserts one hand-computed value — it pins the arithmetic, not the design.

formulas.name: Buyer / Seller direction
formulas.expression: Ordered fall-through: (p>=.75 AND c>=.10)→Strong Buyer; (p>=.60 AND c>=.05)→Buyer; (.45<=p<.60)→Selective Buyer; (p<.10 AND c<.01 AND age_heavy)→Strong Seller; (p<.25 AND c<.02)→Seller; (.20<=p<.40)→Selective Seller; else→Hold / Evaluate.
formulas.inputs: playoff_odds_pct, championship_odds_pct, team_ros_strength_percentile, roster_age_profile
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing maps default the dimension to 0.0 (trade_deadline.py:62-64), which pushes a team with no data toward 'Seller'.
formulas.mathIssues: Enumerated the full decision surface. (1) `team_ros_strength_percentile` is bound at :78 and used ONLY in the display string at :120 — it does not affect a single branch, despite the docstring at :73-75 claiming 'a team's exact band can shift on age + roster strength'. (2) `build_team_directions` is only ever called with teams=None (trade_deadline.py:116), so roster_age_profile is always {} and age_heavy is always False — 'Strong Seller / Rebuilder' is UNREACHABLE in production, and frontend/app/league/sections/ros-trade-deadline.jsx:46 has a colour entry for a label that can never appear. (3) The `else` fallback swallows large regions: any team with playoff odds >= 0.60 but championship odds < 0.05 is told 'Hold / Evaluate — avoid extreme buy/sell'. Measured: at p=0.90, c=0.03 the label is 'Hold / Evaluate'. The documented 'Hold: 0.35 <= playoff < 0.55' band is realised as 0.40-0.45 only.
formulas.validated: No test file located.

formulas.name: Insider Trading confidence tier and signal strength
formulas.expression: tier: volume<=0→insufficient; (volume>=12 AND managers>=4 AND leagues>=3)→high; (volume>=5 AND managers>=2)→medium; else low. strength = clamp(net/volume, -1, 1) * volume/(volume+5) * managers/(managers+3) * managerQuality, ×100.
formulas.inputs: per-window buy/sell counts, unique managers, unique leagues
formulas.constants: _CONFIDENCE_HALF_VOLUME 5.0 (:69), _BREADTH_HALF_MANAGERS 3.0 (:79), tier cuts 12/4/3 and 5/2.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Assets present in one window and absent from another get an explicit zeroed window rather than a gap (:271-276) — deliberate, so the UI cannot render 'no data' where the answer is 'zero'.
formulas.mathIssues: None found. The design is defensible: net is normalised by volume so a 1-0 asset cannot outrank a 40-39 one on direction, breadth discounts one manager acting in six leagues, and windows are never summed (velocity is a ratio, :141-152). Verified: net=1/vol=1/mgr=1 → strength 4.17, tier 'low'; net=12/vol=12/mgr=4 → strength 40.34.
formulas.validated: tests/intel/test_signals.py including an explicit tier assertion. NOTE: `signalStrength` is emitted (:216) but the Insider Trading page never renders it — the board shows raw counts plus the tier badge only.

formulas.name: Scoring similarity score
formulas.expression: combined = Σ_pos |myShare − baselineShare| (pp) + 0.4 * |myFlex − baseFlex|/baseFlex*100; then piecewise-linear: combined<=2 → 95..100; <=5 → 85..94; <=10 → 75..84; <=20 → 60..74; else max(0, 60 − (combined−20)*2).
formulas.inputs: per-position value shares under the user's scoring vs a baseline, plus a top-96 flex blended score
formulas.constants: 0.4 flex weight; band edges 2/5/10/20; StatusBands excellent 0.5, good 1.5, slight 3.0, over 5.0 (:274-278).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: baseline_flex <= 0 → flex_dev = 0 (:349-352), i.e. a missing flex baseline silently improves the score.
formulas.mathIssues: The frontend re-derives card colours with `absDiffTone` using bands {lo:0.5, mid:1.5, hi:3} (frontend/app/league-comparison/sections/SummaryCards.jsx:177-183), which matches the backend's excellent/good/slight but has no equivalent of the backend's `over: 5.0` — so a 4pp difference renders red while the backend's own status text still reads 'High' rather than 'Too high'. Separately, `FlexMatchCard` calls absDiffTone with `{lo:1, mid:5}` (:148) leaving `b.hi` undefined, so `(b.hi || 3)` evaluates to 3 which is LESS than mid=5: the amber branch is unreachable for the flex card.
formulas.validated: No test located for similarity_score.

formulas.name: Age curve (median value by age)
formulas.expression: For each position family and each integer age in [20,36]: median(rankDerivedValue) over every board row at that rounded age with value > 0. Missing ages yield a null point which is then FILTERED OUT before pathing (:154-156), so the line bridges gaps invisibly.
formulas.inputs: the whole board (`rows` filtered to pos != PICK/K, frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:318-320) and the user's roster rows
formulas.constants: ageLo 20, ageHi 36 (:69-70). NO minimum bucket size.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: An age with zero rows produces a null point that is dropped and bridged. An age with ONE row produces a 'median' equal to that single player's value.
formulas.mathIssues: This is not an aging curve, it is a composition artifact. The board contains hundreds of near-zero-value 23-25 year olds and only a handful of 33+ year olds, so the median at the young ages is dragged down by roster filler while the median at the old ages is computed over a survivorship-selected handful of stars. The resulting curve can slope UPWARD with age, and the InfoTip at frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:341-347 instructs the user to sell RBs 'past the position's peak' based on it.
formulas.validated: NO. `ageCurveFor` aggregation is tested in frontend/__tests__/graphs.test.js; the statistical validity is not.

formulas.name: Draft-capital weighted score
formulas.expression: weightedScore = Σ pick_weight(round), where ROUND_WEIGHT = {1:4, 2:3, 3:2} and every other round returns 1.
formulas.inputs: the owner's currently-owned picks across the snapshot's draft years
formulas.constants: 4 / 3 / 2 / 1. These exist nowhere else in the codebase.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: round None → weight 0 (:23-24).
formulas.mathIssues: A linear 4:3:2:1 scale implies a 1st is worth exactly four 5th-rounders. The same application prices picks through the Hill curve on the live contract; the ratio there between an early 1st and a late-round pick is not 4:1. Two draft-capital scales, one authoritative and one invented, and the invented one is what a franchise's public page shows.
formulas.validated: NO.

formulas.name: Buy-low candidate selection
formulas.expression: candidates = rows not on my roster AND 0 < canonicalConsensusRank <= 150 AND value >= 3000 AND rankChange <= -3; pick argmax(-rankChange). Emitted with metric = 'short_drop_long_steady'.
formulas.inputs: board rows with rank, value, rankChange
formulas.constants: 150, 3000, -3. Frontend and backend agree exactly — one of the few verified parities in this audit.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Non-finite rankChange skips the row (:485-486).
formulas.mathIssues: The 'long steady' half is not implemented. The comment at :466-467 states the rule as '7d trend <= -3 (dipped), 30d trend still >= 0 (long-term fine)' and the metric string on both sides is `short_drop_long_steady`, but neither implementation reads a 30-day figure at all. A player in sustained structural decline is presented as a buy-low with a reason string that says 'window open before the market corrects'.
formulas.validated: NO test on either side.

formulas.name: Roster tier buckets
formulas.expression: value >= 8500 → elite; >= 6500 → high; >= 3000 → mid; else depth.
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue per rostered player (picks excluded on both sides)
formulas.constants: 8500 / 6500 / 3000, identical in both languages, with an explicit sync comment at terminal.py:47.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Players with value <= 0 are skipped from both the total and the tier counts (terminal.py:1459-1460; TeamCommandHeader.jsx:161-162).
formulas.mathIssues: None. Verified in sync at this commit.
formulas.validated: Not asserted by a test, but co-located constants with a sync comment on both sides.

findings.title: scoreTeamTiers' pick term has the wrong net sign: draft picks INCREASE a team's contender score by +0.1 per unit, while the UI tells the user they are penalised at -10%
findings.rootCause: `totalValue` accumulates pick value (frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:1016), then `depthValue = totalValue - starterValue` (:1027) carries that pick value into the +0.2 depth term, and the explicit -0.1 penalty is applied on top. Net coefficient on pick value is 0.2 - 0.1 = +0.1.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:1026-1028 — `const starterValue = starters.reduce((s, p) => s + p.meta, 0); const depthValue = totalValue - starterValue; const score = starterValue * 0.7 + depthValue * 0.2 + (pickValue > 0 ? -pickValue * 0.1 : 0);`  with :1016-1017 `totalValue += val; pickValue += val;`. The docstring at :974 says 'Pick surplus penalized at -10% (rebuild signal)'. The user-facing InfoTip at frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:522-525 says 'Teams are scored on starter quality (70%), roster depth (20%), and a pick-surplus penalty (-10%).'
findings.userImpact: The team hoarding the most draft capital — by definition the most rebuild-shaped roster in the league — is ranked as the strongest contender. Replayed on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json with an approximate pick-label resolver and a top-21-by-value starter proxy: the owner holding 72 picks worth ~175k ranks #1 as shipped and #6 with the sign corrected, and 7 of 12 teams change position. The tier boundaries are ceil(n/3), so teams cross the Contender/Mid-Tier/Rebuilder line on this error. A manager reading this card would conclude they are contending when the roster says rebuild.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute depth from PLAYER value only: `const depthValue = totalValue - pickValue - starterValue;` so the -0.1 term is the pick's only contribution. Then add a test that asserts `score(P>0) < score(P=0)` for the same player roster. If the intent is actually that picks are a mild positive, change the InfoTip and the docstring instead — but pick one.
findings.complexity: trivial — one line, plus a regression test

findings.title: The public trade grader applies the private grader's letter thresholds to a completely different quantity, so the same trade is 'Fair' on /trades and 'Robbery' on /league
findings.affectedSystems: Public trade grades on /league?tab=activity; private trade grades on /trades
findings.rootCause: `src/public_league/activity.py` grades on the alpha-exponentiated side totals — the exact quantity the private path's comment forbids — while reusing the private path's 3/8/15/25/40 letter cuts, which were calibrated for a linear-value percentage gap.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/activity.py:118 `total += pow(max(val, 1.0), _GRADE_ALPHA)` with `_GRADE_ALPHA = 1.65` (:49) and :131 `pct = ((max_w - min_w) / max_w) * 100.0`. Against frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:388-394: 'Don't include the alpha-powered weighted sums — those dominate by an order of magnitude and would crush all pcts toward zero.' followed by `const scale = Math.max(gotEffective, gaveEffective, 1); const pctGap = (netAdjusted / scale) * 100;`. The header comment at activity.py:40-44 claims 'a trade graded on the private /trades page lands in the same bucket on the public /league activity timeline.'
findings.userImpact: Reproduced numerically. A 1×8000-for-2×4000 swap (perfectly even on linear value) yields publicPct = 36.27 → 'A+ Big win' for one side and 'D Robbery' for the other, versus privatePct = 0.00 → 'A Fair trade' for both. A 1×6000-for-3×2000 swap yields publicPct = 51.04, past the 'F Fleeced' line, versus private 0.00. Every consolidation trade — the most common shape in dynasty — is publicly labelled a robbery. These letters and words appear on a PUBLIC page next to a named league-mate.
findings.recommendedFix: Grade the public feed on the same linear pct the private path uses: per-side net over the larger effective side total. Then add a parity test that runs the same synthetic trades through `_apply_trade_grades` and `analyzeRawTrade` and asserts identical letters — the claim in the header comment is currently untested in either direction.
findings.complexity: moderate — the public path only has `receivedAssets` per side, so the linear got/gave pairing has to be reconstructed; roughly a day with the parity test

findings.title: The 'Rebuild' phase is unreachable on live data, which silently kills the /phases page's headline trade-partner feature
findings.rootCause: Two compounding choices: (1) `medianAge < leagueMedians.age` uses a strict `<` against a median of integer-valued team medians, so every team tied at the median is classified 'older'; (2) the team's median age is computed over its TOP 25 PLAYERS BY VALUE, which excludes exactly the cheap young prospects that constitute a rebuild.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/team-phase.js:85-86 `const isYounger = medianAge != null && leagueMedians.age != null && medianAge < leagueMedians.age;` and :65-67 `const top = [...lookup].sort((a, b) => b.value - a.value).slice(0, TOP_N_FOR_VALUE); ... const ages = top.map((p) => p.age).filter(...)` with `TOP_N_FOR_VALUE = 25` (:29). Partnerships require rebuilders: :118 `const rebuilders = enriched.filter((t) => t.phase.key === 'rebuild');`
findings.userImpact: Replayed on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json (ages exact, value proxied by `_finalAdjusted`): league median team-age = 25.0 and FIVE of twelve teams have a top-25 median age of exactly 25.0 — all five are forced to the 'older' side. Resulting distribution: Win-now 2, Contender 4, Mixed 6, Rebuild 0. With zero rebuilders, `partnerships` is empty, so the 'Natural trade partners for you' block (TeamPhasePanel.jsx:161-188) renders nothing at all — the panel's stated reason for existing (team-phase.js:22-24) produces no output, and no message explains why. Rosters carry 44-58 players; the age median ignores 33-38 of them.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the FULL roster for the age median (measured on the same snapshot, full-roster medians tie the league median for only 3 of 12 teams instead of 5), and break the remaining ties explicitly rather than defaulting them to 'older' — e.g. classify Mixed when a team is within a stated tolerance of both medians. Add a test with a realistic 12-team integer age distribution; the existing 5 tests all use 2-3 synthetic teams and cannot see this.
findings.complexity: moderate — the fix is small but the classification semantics need a decision, and the panel should say something when a bucket is empty

findings.title: Luck score and Power rankings count in-progress weeks as finished games, so the verdict and the rank visibly change during Sunday afternoon and re-settle Monday night
findings.affectedSystems: Luck score + verdict on /league?tab=luck; Power rankings v1; ROS Power v2 (which reuses the same weekly-results components)
findings.rootCause: `metrics.is_scored` returns True for any roster with points > 0, so a team that has played Thursday is treated as having a final score while its opponent still sits at 0. `luck._season_weekly_scores` and `luck._actual_week_results` both accept those partials. The playoff-odds module guards exactly this case; luck.py and power.py do not.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/metrics.py:57-59 `def is_scored(entry): return matchup_points(entry) > 0`. src/public_league/luck.py:91-92 `if not metrics.is_scored(entry): continue` (all-play field shrinks to whoever has played) and :117 `if not metrics.is_scored(a) and not metrics.is_scored(b): continue` followed by :126-130, which awards a full 1.0 actual win to the side with points against a side at 0. Contrast src/public_league/playoff_odds.py:135-139: 'Both sides have points > 0 — the standard current-week gate. During a live week we require both sides to have posted scores before counting, otherwise a Thursday-only finish gets credited as a phantom win over an opponent still sitting at 0.' power.py:87 and :98 call the unguarded luck helpers directly.
findings.userImpact: The public snapshot TTL is 300 seconds (server.py:8379), so during a live NFL week these numbers recompute roughly every 5 minutes off partial scores. A phantom win moves luckDelta by up to 1.0, which is wider than the entire ±0.3 'Deserved' band — a manager can be 'Blessed' on Sunday evening and 'Unlucky' on Monday night with no game having changed hands. Power rank deltas move the same way. Nothing on either tab indicates the week is in progress.
findings.recommendedFix: Extract playoff_odds.py's `_matchup_is_final` into `metrics` and gate `luck._season_weekly_scores` / `_actual_week_results` on it, so the current week enters the aggregates only once both sides have posted. One implementation of 'is this game final' instead of two.
findings.complexity: moderate — the helper already exists and is tested; the work is threading it through two modules and adding a live-week fixture

findings.title: ROS Buyer/Seller direction: two of its four documented inputs have no effect, and one of its seven labels is unreachable in production
findings.rootCause: `team_ros_strength_percentile` is read into a local and used only to format a display string. `roster_age_profile` is always {} because `build_team_directions` is only ever called without a `teams` argument, so the age-gated branch can never fire.
findings.evidence: src/ros/direction.py:78 `strength_pct = team_ros_strength_percentile or 0.0` — its only other appearance is :120 inside the summary f-string; no branch at :80-115 reads it, yet the docstring at :73-75 claims 'a team's exact band can shift on age + roster strength'. src/ros/trade_deadline.py:112-116 — `def build_section(snapshot): _ = snapshot  # roster ages come from team_strength snapshot directly` then `return {'teams': build_team_directions()}` with no `teams=`. That makes `team_obj` None at trade_deadline.py:85, `roster_age = {}`, and `age_heavy = bool({}.get('vetCount', 0) >= 4)` = False at direction.py:77, so 'Strong Seller / Rebuilder' (:98-103) never fires. The comment 'roster ages come from team_strength snapshot directly' is false — `build_roster_age_profile` is never called in production.
findings.userImpact: Enumerated the full decision surface: the label is a pure function of playoff odds and championship odds, and the `else` fallback swallows large regions. A team at 90% playoff odds with 3% title odds is labelled 'Hold / Evaluate' with the recommendation 'Avoid extreme buy/sell' — the opposite of correct at a trade deadline. The documented 'Hold: 0.35 <= playoff < 0.55' band is realised as 0.40-0.45 only. The frontend carries a colour entry for 'Strong Seller / Rebuilder' (frontend/app/league/sections/ros-trade-deadline.jsx:46) that no user will ever see.
findings.recommendedFix: Either pass `teams` from the snapshot in `build_section` and give `strength_pct` a real role, or delete both parameters and rewrite the docstring to say the label is playoff-odds × championship-odds only. Then replace the `else` fallback with explicit terminal branches so a 90%-playoff team cannot land in 'Hold'.
findings.complexity: moderate — plumbing `teams` through is small; re-deriving the bands so the fallback is genuinely residual is a design decision

findings.title: Luck verdicts use absolute win thresholds across scopes and disagree with their own colour coding
findings.rootCause: `luckLabel` and `luckColor` are two independent frontend band sets over the same `luckDelta`, and neither normalises by games played even though the backend ships `luckPerGame`.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/league/sections/luck.jsx:34-41 `if (delta > 0.5) return '#2ecc71'; if (delta > 0.1) return '#7bdfb3'; if (delta < -0.5) return '#ff6b6b'; if (delta < -0.1) return '#ffab6b';` versus :43-50 `if (delta > 1.0) return 'Blessed'; if (delta > 0.3) return 'Lucky'; if (delta > -0.3) return 'Deserved'; if (delta > -1.0) return 'Unlucky'; return 'Cursed';`. Both are applied to the same rows whether the scope selector is 'career' or a single season (:300-304, :393). The backend emits `luckPerGame` at src/public_league/luck.py:290 and no frontend file reads it.
findings.userImpact: Enumerated the disagreement: luckDelta = +0.2 renders pale green (a 'lucky' colour) with the word 'Deserved'; -0.2 renders orange (an 'unlucky' colour) with the word 'Deserved'; +0.6 renders the brightest green with only 'Lucky'. Separately, a ~45-game career row and a 14-game season row share the same +1.0 'Blessed' cut, so 'Blessed' means roughly 2.2% of games over a career and 7.1% over a season — the career column systematically over-reports luck.
findings.recommendedFix: Drive the verdict off `luckPerGame` (already in the payload) with per-game bands, and derive the colour from the same band function so the word and the colour cannot disagree.

findings.title: Power rankings v1 blends three different time scales and presents a career record as a weekly one; three descriptions of the same formula disagree
findings.rootCause: `career_state` is declared outside the season loop and is never reset, so the 50%-weighted PPG term is a career average across up to `PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS` (default 3) seasons, while the all-play term is a single week and `recent_buffer` resets per season.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/power.py:82-84 `career_state: dict[...] = defaultdict(lambda: {'points': 0.0, 'games': 0, ...})` declared before `for season in seasons_sorted:` at :86, with the comment at :81 'Cross-season continuous accumulators (career PPG-to-date)'. Contrast the module docstring at :6: 'Points per game (PPG) — overall scoring strength, season-to-date.' The all-play term at :126-131 admits the shortcut in a comment: 'simpler + still useful is current-week all-play share'. `record` at :143-147 is `f'{round(career wins)}-{games - wins}'` — a career record rendered under a column headed just 'Record' next to '2026 week 5' (frontend/app/league/sections/power.jsx:226, 369). PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS defaults to 3 (src/public_league/sleeper_client.py:44).
findings.userImpact: A 'weekly power ranking' whose dominant 50% term averages ~45 games barely moves week to week, so the tab's week-over-week rank delta column is mostly noise from the 25% single-week all-play term. The 'Record' column shows a multi-season record where a reader expects the current season's. The methodology string the UI prints verbatim (power.py:214-219) says 'PPG percentile' and 'all-play win share' without disclosing that one is career-long and the other is one week.
findings.recommendedFix: Reset `career_state` per season (or rename every surface to say 'career'), and either accumulate all-play across the season to match, or state the single-week scope in the methodology string. Since v2 is now the default view (see the separate finding), consider retiring v1 rather than fixing it.
findings.complexity: trivial for the reset; the design question of which scope is intended is the real work

findings.title: The /settings hint for ROS Power Rankings says the opposite of the shipped default, and the ROS Playoff Odds toggle does nothing at all
findings.affectedSystems: Power rankings tab selection on /league; /settings ROS section
findings.rootCause: The default flipped to true in the settings registry but neither the hint text nor the LeagueClient comment was updated; and `useRosPlayoffOdds` was shipped as a live toggle with no consumer.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/useSettings.js:143 `useRosPowerRankings: true,` versus frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:761 hint 'Defaults off until you've validated v2 against a few weeks of standings.' and frontend/app/league/LeagueClient.jsx:99-100 comment 'useRosPowerRankings false until validated per-user'. For the second toggle: `useRosPlayoffOdds` appears exactly three times in the tree — useSettings.js:148 (default true), settings/page.jsx:765-766 (the switch), and nowhere else. Its own hint at :769 calls it a 'PR-future toggle'.
findings.userImpact: Users are shown the un-validated v2 power ranking by default while the settings page tells them v2 is off until they validate it — so nobody validates it and nobody knows they are looking at it. The playoff-odds toggle is a control that changes nothing; a user who flips it will believe the odds beneath it changed. As a side effect, the entire v1 Power path — including `public_league/power.py` and the `PlayoffOddsChart` component — is only reachable by turning a toggle off, which means the playoff-odds Monte Carlo is effectively dormant on the default experience.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the hint and the LeagueClient comment to match the default. Either wire `useRosPlayoffOdds` to the section swap it describes or remove the switch until it is wired — a settings control with no consumer is worse than a missing feature.
findings.complexity: trivial for the text; the odds swap is its own piece of work

findings.title: The buy-low insight's 'long steady' filter is never implemented, on either the frontend or the backend, while the metric name and the reason string both claim it
findings.rootCause: The two-legged rule was specified in a comment and a metric identifier but only the short-drop leg was written.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:466-467 `// Buy-low candidate: LEAGUE-wide — not on my roster, value >= 3000, // 7d trend <= -3 (dipped), 30d trend still >= 0 (long-term fine).` The filter chain at :469-492 checks roster membership, rank <= 150, value >= 3000 and `t7 <= -3` and stops — no 30-day figure is read anywhere in the block. Same on the backend: src/api/terminal.py:1109-1121 checks roster, rank, value and `rc > -3` only. Both emit `'metric': 'short_drop_long_steady'` (:502, terminal.py:1135).
findings.userImpact: A player in sustained structural decline — down on both the 7-day and 30-day windows — is presented as the roster's single named buy-low with the reason 'window open before the market corrects' (portfolio-insights.js:501). The filter that was supposed to exclude exactly that case does not exist. Note that both implementations use `rankChange` (last-scrape delta), not a 7-day trend, despite the comment calling it '7d'.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the 30-day leg on both sides using the `trend30` already computed for roster players, or rename the metric and rewrite the reason string to claim only what is checked. Add a test with a falling-on-both-windows fixture.

findings.title: 'Age curves' on /rosters are a board-composition artifact, not an aging model, and are captioned as a sell signal
findings.rootCause: The curve is the median value of every board row at each integer age, with no minimum bucket size and no correction for the fact that the population at each age is selected by survival.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/graphs/AgeCurveOverlay.jsx:53-61 — for each age it takes `median(bucket)` over whatever rows exist, and a bucket of size 1 yields that one player's value as the 'median'. Null points are dropped before pathing at :154-156, so a missing age is bridged with a straight line and no visual marker. The board handed in is the entire pool minus picks and kickers (frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:318-320). The InfoTip at :341-347 reads: 'Use it to spot aging risk: a cluster of RBs past the position's peak is a flag to sell; a cluster before it means you are set up for the window.'
findings.userImpact: The young end of every curve is dragged down by hundreds of near-zero-value 23-25 year old roster filler; the old end is computed over a handful of survivors who are, by construction, the ones still worth something. The curve can therefore slope upward with age and be read as 'this position peaks at 32'. A single 34-year-old on the board sets the entire age-34 'median'. The caption instructs the user to make sell decisions on it.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a minimum bucket size (say n >= 5) and render sub-threshold ages as a gap rather than bridging them; restrict the cohort to rows the board actually ranks rather than the full pool; and label the y-axis as 'median value of ranked players at this age' so the survivorship is visible. If a real aging curve is wanted, it needs a fit against realized production, not a cross-section of current market value.

findings.title: activity-feed.js's private trade builder cannot work against the real contract, and its unit test validates a fixture shape the scraper never emits
findings.rootCause: `tradeToEvent` reads a Sleeper-transaction shape (`roster_ids` / `adds` / `drops`, and `positions` keyed by player id to an object with `.name`), but the contract stores trades as `{week, timestamp, sides:[{team, got, gave, ownerId, rosterId}]}` and `sleeper.positions` as cleanedName → position string.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/activity-feed.js:46-53 `const positions = rawData?.sleeper?.positions || {}; for (const pid of [...Object.keys(adds), ...Object.keys(drops)]) { const meta = positions[pid]; const name = meta?.name || (typeof meta === 'string' ? meta : null);` — against 'Dynasty Scraper.py':1301 `'positions': position_map,` where position_map is built name→position ('Dynasty Scraper.py':1237-1247, 1284-1285). Trades are emitted at 'Dynasty Scraper.py':1556-1567 as `{'leagueId', 'week', 'timestamp', 'sides': [{'team','rosterId','ownerId','got','gave'}]}` — no `adds`, `drops`, `roster_ids` or `transaction_id`. Also :38 matches `String(t?.rosterId)` against roster ids, but teams carry `roster_id` ('Dynasty Scraper.py':1256) and nothing in src/api/data_contract.py stamps `rosterId`. The test fixture at frontend/__tests__/activity-feed.test.js:11-27 invents `positions: {'100': {name: 'Caleb Williams'}}` and `trades: [{roster_ids, adds, drops}]`.
findings.userImpact: None today — the function has zero production callers, and /league/activity correctly uses `buildPublicActivityEvents` (the comment at activity-feed.js:150-158 explains why). The impact is that a green test suite asserts this code works. Anyone reviving it for a private activity feed would ship a feed with no team names and no player names and see passing tests.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete `buildActivityEvents` and `tradeToEvent` along with their test, or rewrite both against the real `sides` shape and rebuild the fixture from an actual contract export. The same `rosterId` vs `roster_id` mismatch exists at frontend/lib/team-phase.js:71 (`String(team?.rosterId || '')`, always '') — harmless there today because TeamPhasePanel keys on ownerId, but worth fixing together.

findings.title: The League Edge Map's declared minimum-edge filter is dead code, and three surfaces gate the same 'market mispricing' concept on three different quantities
findings.affectedSystems: League Edge Map on /rosters; the /edge page; the backend market-gap stamp
findings.rootCause: `MIN_EDGE_PCT` was declared next to `buildLeagueEdgeMap` and never referenced; the actual gate lives in a different module on a different quantity, and a third surface uses a fourth quantity.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:827 `const MIN_EDGE_PCT = 3;` — grep over the whole frontend returns exactly one hit, its own declaration. The real gate is frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:949 `const MIN_EDGE_RANK_GAP = 3;` applied at :968 to `marketGapMagnitude` (a rank gap, not a percentage). The backend applies NO minimum at all — src/api/data_contract.py:2787-2793 returns a direction for any non-zero difference between the retail and consensus mean ranks. Meanwhile frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:142-144 gates the same buy/sell concept on `(r.sourceRankSpread ?? 0) >= PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD`.
findings.userImpact: A per-team 'sellEdge' is a raw sum of unbounded per-player percentages with no floor, so a team with many marginal 3-rank disagreements can out-rank a team with a genuinely mispriced star. The card's InfoTip (frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:575-580) presents this as 'Market price vs. our model, per team' with no indication of what qualifies. And a player who is a 'Sell' on /rosters may not appear on /edge at all, because the two pages gate on different numbers.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete `MIN_EDGE_PCT` or apply it. Then pick ONE definition of 'the market is mispricing this player' — rank gap or source spread — and route /rosters, /edge and the popup through it, the way `starter-slots.js` was made the one answer to 'who starts'.
findings.complexity: trivial to delete; moderate to unify

findings.title: Rivalry index double-counts close games through nested thresholds — the exact error the repo's own intel module devotes its docstring to condemning
findings.affectedSystems: Rivalry index on /league?tab=rivalries and /league/rivalry/[pair]; 'Top rival' on every franchise page
findings.rootCause: `gamesDecidedByFive` and `gamesDecidedByTen` are incremented by two independent `if` statements rather than an elif chain, so every ≤5-point game also counts as a ≤10-point game and is scored twice.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/rivalries.py:118-121 `if margin_abs <= 5.0 + 1e-9: rec['gamesDecidedByFive'] += 1` followed by `if margin_abs <= 10.0 + 1e-9: rec['gamesDecidedByTen'] += 1` — not elif. The index at :171-178 then weights both: `3 * gamesDecidedByFive + 2 * gamesDecidedByTen`. Compare src/intel/signals.py:16-25, which rejects the identical pattern: 'The windows are nested, so a movement one hour old is inside all three terms... One event, six counted.'
findings.userImpact: Verified: one 3-point regular-season game this season scores 8 index points (3 + 2 + 1 meeting + 2 recency); one 40-point blowout in the same slot scores 3. A single nail-biter is worth 2.7 blowouts. The index drives the rivalry ordering, the 'Top rival' link on every franchise page, and the featured rivalry in the /league Open Graph description — and none of the weights appear anywhere in the UI.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the bands disjoint (elif) or drop the ≤10 term. Publish the weights in the UI alongside the number, as the Power and Luck tabs already do with their 'How this is computed' cards.

findings.title: PlayoffOddsChart has no case for one of the backend's five schedule-certainty values, so the most-informed inference mode renders as 'Unknown schedule source'
findings.affectedSystems: Playoff odds chart on the v1 Power view
findings.rootCause: The component's certainty map was written against a four-value enum documented in its own header; the backend emits six values including `inferred_from_posted`.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/graphs/PlayoffOddsChart.jsx:33-40 handles `posted`, `partial`, `inferred`, `final`, `preseason` and falls through to `{ text: 'Unknown schedule source' }`. The header comment at :12-13 states the enum as '{posted, partial, inferred, final}'. src/public_league/playoff_odds.py:625 sets `schedule_certainty = 'inferred_from_posted'` when the remaining pairings were successfully inferred from the observed posted-week cycle (:260-314) — the strongest inference the module makes, stronger than the round-robin `inferred` fallback.
findings.userImpact: The badge tells the user the schedule source is unknown precisely when the simulator has done its best work, and it renders in the neutral grey used for 'Season complete' rather than a caution colour. Reachable only on the non-default v1 Power view, which limits exposure.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the case and update the header comment to the real six-value enum. A shared constant, or a test that asserts every value the backend can emit has a label, would prevent the next divergence.

findings.title: FranchiseTrajectory's x-axis encoding spends 78% of the chart width on empty offseasons
findings.rootCause: `encodeWeekKey` uses `season * 100 + week` as a linear x coordinate, so consecutive weeks are 1 apart while the gap from week 17 of one season to week 1 of the next is 84.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/graphs/FranchiseTrajectory.jsx:43-48 `return Number(season) * 100 + Number(week);` fed straight into `linearScale(tMin, tMax, 0, box.innerWidth)` at :77.
findings.userImpact: Computed for three 17-week seasons: total span 216 units, of which 48 (22.2%) is in-season and 168 (77.8%) is offseason gap. Each season's 17 weeks are compressed into roughly 7% of the chart width, with three-quarters of the plot showing straight lines through nothing. The season-boundary markers at :146-157 are drawn at the midpoint of those gaps, so they read as data.
findings.recommendedFix: Plot against the ordinal index of the point in the sorted series (which the code already has as the loop index), keeping the season-boundary markers to show where the breaks are.

findings.title: The flex card on /league-comparison has an unreachable colour band, and the position cards' colours diverge from the backend's own status bands
findings.rootCause: `absDiffTone` is called with a partial band object whose `mid` exceeds the default `hi`, and the frontend band set omits the backend's fourth threshold.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/league-comparison/sections/SummaryCards.jsx:177-183 `const b = bands || { lo: 0.5, mid: 1.5, hi: 3 }; ... if (d <= b.lo) green; if (d <= b.mid) cyan; if (d <= (b.hi || 3)) amber; return red;`. Called for flex at :148 as `absDiffTone(flex.relDiffPct, { lo: 1, mid: 5 })` — `b.hi` is undefined so `(b.hi || 3)` is 3, which is less than mid=5, making the amber branch unreachable. Separately the backend's `StatusBands` (src/league_comparison/metrics.py:274-278) carries a fourth threshold `over: 5.0` that the frontend has no equivalent for, so a 4pp difference renders red while `status_label` (:284-298) still returns 'High'/'Low' rather than 'Too high'/'Too low'.
findings.userImpact: Cosmetic but contradictory: the flex card jumps green → cyan → red with no warning state, and a position card can show a red delta next to a status word that is not the backend's most severe. On a page whose entire output is a judgement about whether scoring is distorted, the colour is doing as much work as the word.
findings.recommendedFix: Ship the backend's `StatusBands` values in the payload (the dataclass comment at :270-272 already says they are 'deliberately tunable in one place so the frontend methodology section can reference the exact same numbers' — so read them) and pass a complete band object for the flex card.

findings.title: 'Insider Trading' is an accusation-shaped name on a product that makes no accusation and therefore has no false-positive rate to report — the risk is entirely in the label
findings.affectedSystems: Insider Trading page, board and lead scores
findings.rootCause: Product naming. There is no collusion, tampering or wrongdoing detector anywhere in the tree.
findings.evidence: Grepped the full repository for collusion/insider detectors: the only hits are the product name itself (src/intel/__init__.py:6, src/intel/service.py:22, signals.py:1) and one unrelated comment in src/roster_intel/partner.py:585 mentioning 'collusion optics' as a reason a trade might be declined. The page renders exactly six observable counts per asset — buys, sells, net, volume, unique managers, unique leagues — plus a sample-strength tier (frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx:596-642). Its header explicitly disclaims a skill cohort at :480-484: 'These are the managers in this league, not a skill-filtered cohort.' The tier badge's tooltip at :68 says 'Sample strength: how much evidence sits behind this signal, not how strong the direction is.' The lead model publishes and RENDERS its own limitations (src/intel/leads.py:395-419 → frontend/components/InsiderLeads.jsx:380-387). The board is auditable to individual movements (:243-282, 'verify the count').
findings.userImpact: Bluntly: this is the best-evidenced system in the audit and it does not need a false-positive rate, because it asserts nothing falsifiable — every number is a count of a public transaction, with the underlying movements one click away. The exposure is reputational, not statistical: a page titled 'Insider Trading' that lists named league-mates and what they bought reads as an allegation to anyone who does not open it, and the page title is what gets screenshotted into a league chat. The confidence tier cuts (volume>=12/managers>=4/leagues>=3 for 'high', src/intel/signals.py:120-122) are unvalidated priors, but they gate a badge, not a claim.
findings.recommendedFix: Rename the product to what it measures — 'League-mate market activity' or 'Cross-league activity'. Keep everything else; the evidence discipline here (no window summing, volume never optional, rendered limitations, auditable receipts) is the pattern the rest of this audit's systems should be held to.

findings.title: Six exports in league-analysis.js and one whole config surface in team_assignment.py are inert
findings.rootCause: Accumulated dead code that reads as live configuration.
findings.evidence: Zero non-definition references anywhere in frontend/ for: `computePositionRanks` (league-analysis.js:752-762), `heatmapColor` (:765-772), `heatmapTextColor` (:774-782), `buildRosterIdNameMap` (:234-236), `MIN_EDGE_PCT` (:827), `filterTradesToRollingWindow` (:76-83, called internally only). `ordinal` and `POS_GROUP_LABELS` are imported at frontend/app/rosters/page.jsx:13, 20 and never used. In src/api/team_assignment.py:263 `thresholds = config['thresholds']` is bound inside the scorer and never read — the six rank thresholds at :92-100 (`eliteProductionTop10Rank`, `qbStarterPositionRank`, `skillStarterPositionRank`, `skillCommitteePositionRank`, `idpEliteSourcesPositionRank`, `idpStarterPositionRank`) and the weights `eliteProductionTop10` (:85) and `idpElite` (:89) have no effect on any score; the scorer branches on `depth_order == 1 / in (2,3)` instead (:280-310).
findings.userImpact: Low directly — only `assignmentMinPoints` reaches the UI (frontend/app/league/sections/team-assignment.jsx:244). The cost is that a config file presents eight tunable knobs of which six do nothing, so an operator tuning them will change JSON and see no movement. The team_assignment code is at least honest about the proxy at :299-303 ('depth-chart order as a stand-in for elite at position'); the config file is not.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the six dead exports and the two unused imports. In team_assignment.py either wire the thresholds or move them under a `_planned` key so it is obvious they are aspirational.

findings.title: Documentation claims that are false at this commit
findings.affectedSystems: team-phase / /phases; rivalries; scoreTeamTiers; public trade grading; playoff odds
findings.rootCause: Comments and docstrings not kept in step with the code or the config.
findings.evidence: (1) frontend/app/phases/page.jsx:19-20 — '/league/phases still resolves — see the redirect shim there.' There is no `frontend/app/league/phases` directory and no entry in next.config's `redirects()` (which contains only /draft-capital). The only handling is `MOVED_ROUTES` in frontend/lib/public-routes.js:92. (2) src/public_league/rivalries.py:3 and src/public_league/franchise.py:3 both say 'the 2-season window', and the rivalry page's empty state says 'in the last 2 seasons' (frontend/app/league/rivalry/[pair]/page.jsx:96) — but `PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS` defaults to 3 (src/public_league/sleeper_client.py:44) and is env-overridable. (3) src/public_league/playoff_odds.py:6-7 'no hidden state. Every input is explicit so the caller can reproduce a run' — `rng = rng or random.Random()` at :460 is unseeded on the production path. (4) src/public_league/activity.py:40-44 claims grade parity with the private path (contradicted above). (5) src/ros/trade_deadline.py:113 'roster ages come from team_strength snapshot directly' — they come from nowhere.
findings.userImpact: Each of these is a claim an engineer or auditor would otherwise take at face value; two of them (the grade-parity claim and the 2-season claim) reach users directly, the latter as a factual statement about what the page covers.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct each. For the season window, read `PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS` into the payload and render it rather than hardcoding '2' in prose.

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Every file named in the brief was read in full. Backend counterparts were read wherever a frontend surface turned out to be a pure renderer — which is most of `/league`, since the public pipeline computes server-side and the sections materialize verbatim. Formulas were replayed numerically where the arithmetic was non-obvious; scratch scripts live under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/44ce1dac-f26f-5532-81f8-776340c4b6a1/scratchpad. No repository file was modified.

LIVE-DATA CAVEAT. The only contract-shaped artifact in the tree is `exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json`, which is the raw scraper export: it carries the legacy `players` dict with `_finalAdjusted` but no `playersArray` and no `rankDerivedValue`. I used `_finalAdjusted` as the value proxy — the same proxy `frontend/lib/starter-slots.js:26-28` uses and labels as such. Consequences: the /phases AGE findings are exact (ages come straight through, unaffected by the value scale); the /phases Rebuild-is-empty result and the scoreTeamTiers reordering depend on the value scale and my approximate pick-label resolution (5-10 picks per team went unresolved), so treat those magnitudes as indicative and the SIGN of the pick coefficient as exact.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY SAFE TO ACT ON. Three systems earned it: `starter-slots.js` (one implementation, honest `available`/`usedFallback` flags, refuses rather than guessing, well tested); `src/intel/*` (Insider Trading — never sums overlapping windows, never shows net without volume, publishes and renders its own limitations, receipts one click away); and `player-name-match.js` (four named key families, a real cross-language parity fixture). The terminal's tier buckets and the buy-low/trade-chip thresholds are genuinely in sync between frontend and backend, which is worth noting because almost nothing else is.

WHAT IS NOT. The four highest-impact judgements a manager would act on — contention phase, contender/rebuilder tier, buyer/seller direction, and public trade grades — each contain a defect that inverts or erases the answer, and none of the four has a test that would catch it. `scoreTeamTiers` has zero test coverage of any kind.

CROSS-CUTTING PATTERN. The repository has THREE independent answers to "how good is this team" (`scoreTeamTiers` 0.7/0.2/-0.1 on dynasty market value; `ros/team_strength.py` 0.72/0.18/0.05/0.05 on ROS projections; `public_league/power.py` 0.50/0.25/0.25 on scoring history), TWO to "should this team buy or sell" (`team-phase.js` phases and `ros/direction.py` labels), TWO to "how contending is it" (`ros/championship.py` tiers and `ros/direction.py`), and TWO to "how good was this trade" (private and public graders, with the same letters on incompatible inputs). No surface reconciles any pair, and a user switching between `/phases`, `/rosters` and the `/league` ROS tabs can receive four different verdicts on the same roster in the same minute with nothing indicating they answer different questions.

A NOTE ON REFRESH NOISE, since the brief asked directly. Labels that flip on noise, ranked: (1) Luck verdict and Power rank — recomputed every 300s (server.py:8379) off partial live-week scores, and a single phantom win moves luckDelta by up to 1.0 against a ±0.3 "Deserved" band; (2) Contention phase — a forced median split with 5 of 12 teams sitting exactly on the age median, so any roster move across the median flips a label; (3) Contender/Rebuilder tier — the ceil(n/3) cut means the 4th and 8th teams flip on any value shift, and the pick-sign error makes those shifts larger than they should be; (4) Playoff odds — genuinely stable, roughly ±1pp at 10,000 sims, and the frontend caches 30 minutes specifically to suppress the residual jitter (frontend/app/league/sections/power.jsx:284-298). Insider Trading counts do not flip; they are counts.

NOT VERIFIABLE FROM REPOSITORY. Whether any of these classifications correlates with realized outcomes — there is no backtest for team-phase, scoreTeamTiers, the rivalry index, the power composites, the contender tiers, or the direction labels. The one precedent for doing it right exists and is cited in CLAUDE.md: `docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md` measured the league-adjusted board against realized 2025 scoring over 572 players, found "no difference detected", and the feature shipped as an off-by-default toggle as a result. None of the systems in this audit received that treatment, and several ship as the default view. Also not verifiable: whether `src/ros/power_v2.py`, `src/ros/championship.py`, `src/ros/direction.py`, `src/ros/team_strength.py`, `src/api/team_assignment.py` or `src/league_comparison/metrics.py::similarity_score` have any test coverage — no matching test files were located under tests/.

formulas.name: FAAB baseline (both languages)
formulas.expression: share = candidate_value / max(candidate_value, top_value_in_pool); aggressive_pct = 0.05 + 0.25 * share; aggressive = max(1, round(budget * aggressive_pct)); reasonable = max(1, round(aggressive * 0.70)); lowball = max(1, round(aggressive * 0.35))
formulas.inputs: candidate rankDerivedValue, league_budget, top_value_in_pool
formulas.constants: 0.05 floor share; 0.25 slope; 0.70 reasonable ratio; 0.35 lowball ratio; $1 floor. Every constant is duplicated verbatim in JS at waiver-logic.js:874-877 - same numbers, but Python round() is banker's rounding and JS Math.round() is half-up.
formulas.outputRange: 5%-30% of budget for aggressive; 3.5%-21% reasonable; 1.75%-10.5% lowball
formulas.missingDataBehavior: value <= 0 or budget <= 0 => (0,0,0). top_value_in_pool None => share = 1.0 => the FULL 30%.
formulas.mathIssues: This is a value percentile mapped onto a dollar scale, nothing more. No budget-remaining, no weeks left, no replacement level, no expected points. Because share is normalized to the pool maximum, the best available free agent ALWAYS prices at 30%/21%/10% regardless of absolute quality - measured: best FA on the live board is Marlin Klein at value 1905 (an unstartable TE) and _compute_faab_bid(1905, 100, 1905) = (30, 21, 10). The $1 floor also means a value-0.01 player still costs a dollar.
formulas.validated: Unit-tested for internal consistency (tests/trade/test_waiver.py:175-215; frontend/__tests__/waiver-pool-builder.test.js:193-220). Never validated against a realized winning bid. No backtest script exists.

formulas.name: JS/Python rounding divergence (measured)
formulas.expression: JS Math.round(x) = floor(x+0.5); Python round(x) = round-half-to-even
formulas.inputs: 600-point grid: budgets {50,100,200} x share {0.005..1.0}
formulas.constants: n/a
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a
formulas.mathIssues: 65 of 600 grid points (10.8%) return different dollars. Examples: (budget 100, value 2999.7, top 9999) -> JS (13,9,5) vs Python (12,8,4); (budget 50, value 9999) -> JS (15,11,5) vs Python (15,10,5). waiver-logic.js:851 calls itself a JS port of _compute_faab_bid; the port is not exact.
formulas.validated: Reproduced in scratchpad this session; no test in the repo covers it.

formulas.name: Value-gain modifier
formulas.expression: mod = clamp(1 + ((add_value - drop_value) / drop_value) * 0.5, 0.5, 1.8); standard = round(reasonable_base * mod)
formulas.inputs: add rankDerivedValue, drop rankDerivedValue
formulas.constants: 0.5 slope; floor 0.5; ceiling 1.8; drop_value <= 0 => 1.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No drop selected => 1.0 (no boost, no penalty)
formulas.mathIssues: The modifier is a RATIO, so it rewards trash-for-trash upgrades more than star upgrades: 500 -> 1500 gives 1+((1000/500)*0.5)=2.0 clamped to 1.8 (max boost), while 8000 -> 9000 gives 1.06. Measured live: Mitchell Evans (1770) over Kamari Ramsey (922) => x1.46, applied to a baseline that is already wrong (next entry).
formulas.validated: tests/trade/test_faab_recommender.py:53-92 (direction only)

formulas.name: Live bid-desk denominator (top_value_in_pool)
formulas.expression: top_pool_value = max(rankDerivedValue) over every contract row whose display name is not on a roster
formulas.inputs: contract playersArray + sleeper team player names
formulas.constants: none - no assetClass filter, no sourceCount filter, no position filter
formulas.missingDataBehavior: 0 => passed as None => share collapses to 1.0
formulas.mathIssues: DRAFT PICKS ARE IN THE POOL. Measured on the live 2026-08-04 contract: 427 unrostered rows, 144 of them assetClass=='pick'; top_pool_value = 7831.0 = '2026 Pick 1.01'; best genuine FA = 1905.0. _compute_faab_bid(1770, 100, 7831) = (11, 8, 4) vs (1770, 100, 1770) = (30, 21, 10).

formulas.name: Budget-environment scaling
formulas.expression: env = clamp((leagueMedianWinningBid / league_budget) / 0.08, 0.6, 1.6); standard = round(standard * env)
formulas.inputs: league analytics median winning bid, league budget

formulas.missingDataBehavior: Returns None (no scaling) on any missing input

Structurally unreachable for the non-default league: server.py:5003-5017 treats the single global public snapshot as unavailable when its root_league_id != the resolved league, so for dynasty_new both this and the position calibration can never fire and the bid is 100% the value-percentile formula.
