formulas.name: Rival expected bid
formulas.expression: exp = min(base_bid * agg * need_f * intel_f, base_bid * 2.5) * 1.15; exp = min(exp, opponent.faabRemaining)
formulas.inputs: neutral-pass standard bid (server.py:5219-5221), team aggression, roster need, intel, rival FAAB balance
formulas.constants: STACK_CAP_MULT 2.5; SAFETY_MARGIN 1.15; NEED_FACTORS need 1.0 / neutral 0.55 / surplus 0.25; AGG_CLAMP (0.5, 2.0); AGG_MIN_WINNING_BIDS 3; INTEL_PLAYER_FACTOR 1.25; INTEL_POSITION_FACTOR 1.10; INTEL_WINDOW_MS 14 days
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing balance => row flagged balanceUnknown and EXCLUDED from topRival/clearing; <3 winning bids => agg 1.0 + lowSample; no intel => 1.0 + note; fewer than half of rivals with balances => contention skipped entirely (server.py:5189)
formulas.mathIssues: Every rival estimate is a multiple of the same contaminated baseline, so the whole auction is modeled at ~1/2.4 scale. Simulated on the live contract with 11 rivals at $100 each: base 8 -> topRival $5, clearing $6 (4 neutral / 2 surplus need levels, agg 1.0 everywhere for lack of bid history). Also uses latest_contract_data for the opponent asset pool and position map (server.py:5227-5233) while the user's bid uses the valuation-lens-scoped contract.
formulas.validated: tests/trade/test_faab_contention.py

formulas.name: Aggression factor
formulas.expression: agg = clamp(owner.avgBid / leagueMedianWinningBid, 0.5, 2.0), requires winningCount >= 3
formulas.inputs: faab_analytics teamAggression (avgBid = totalSpent / winningCount, winning bids only)
formulas.constants: clamp (0.5, 2.0); min 3 winning bids
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Any missing/degenerate input => (1.0, lowSample=True)
formulas.mathIssues: Winning-bid-only selection bias is irreducible and the module says so + stamps estimateOnly, which is honest. But avgBid excludes $0 FA pickups from the mean while totalCount includes them, so two different denominators live in the same block (faab_analytics.py:246-271).
formulas.validated: tests/trade/test_faab_contention.py

formulas.name: Clearing price + value ceiling
formulas.expression: clearing = topRival + 1; dropoff = max(0, (add - next_best_same_pos_FA)/add); if dropoff < 0.15 -> value bid only; else ceiling = round(round(standard*1.40) * (1 + 0.5 * clamp(dropoff, 0, 0.5))); standard = clearing if clearing <= ceiling else max(standard, ceiling) + 'likely outbid' warning
formulas.inputs: contention.clearing, next_best_fa_value (server.py:4978-4984)
formulas.constants: _DROPOFF_GATE 0.15; _CEILING_DROPOFF_CLAMP 0.5; _CEILING_DROPOFF_SCALE 0.5; 1.40 aggressive multiple
formulas.outputRange: standard may rise to ceiling ~1.4x-1.75x itself
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No contention dict => leg skipped and a missing factor (weight 0.15) appended by server.py:5270-5278 with confidence recomputed
formulas.mathIssues: Sound in structure (first-price sealed auction, replaceability-gated). Measured live: Mitchell Evans has next-best-TE 1905 > 1770 => dropoff 0 => gate fires, 'value bid only' - correct behavior.
formulas.validated: tests/trade/test_faab_contention.py + tests/api/test_faab_recommend_endpoint.py

formulas.name: Marginal floor, cap, pacing, bracket
formulas.expression: if add <= drop: standard = min(standard, max(1, round(reasonable_base * 0.5))); if add < drop: standard = 0; cap_source = team_faab_remaining ?? league_budget; standard = min(standard, cap_source); conservative = round(standard * 0.70); aggressive = min(cap_source, round(standard * 1.40)); max = cap_source; warn if standard > 0.40 * cap_source
formulas.inputs: add/drop values, team remaining, league budget
formulas.constants: 0.5 marginal haircut; 0.70 conservative; 1.40 aggressive; _PACING_WARN_SHARE 0.40
formulas.missingDataBehavior: team_faab_remaining unknown => cap_source = league_budget, and max is still returned
formulas.mathIssues: max is rendered as 'your remaining' (FaabRecommendation.jsx:511-515) even when it is the league budget because the team's balance was never resolved - the two cases are indistinguishable on screen.
formulas.validated: tests/trade/test_faab_recommender.py:275-306

formulas.name: Confidence bucket
formulas.expression: realized_share = sum(weight of non-missing) / sum(weight); >=0.85 high, >=0.55 medium, else low
formulas.inputs: factor rows: baseline 0.35, value-gain 0.20, trending 0.15, league analytics 0.20, crowd 0.10, env 0.10, contention 0.15, cap 0.10
formulas.constants: 0.85 / 0.55 thresholds; weights above
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing inputs add weighted missing rows that pull the bucket down - this part is honest
formulas.mathIssues: Weights are only added when a factor CHANGES the number (the crowd blend adds no row when it no-ops, faab_recommender.py:422-431), so the denominator is not fixed and 'medium' is not comparable across two recommendations. Measured live with no analytics/trending: confidence = 'medium' on a bid whose only real input was the value baseline.
formulas.validated: tests/trade/test_faab_recommender.py:307-360

formulas.name: Waiver net gain + tiers (client)
formulas.expression: netGain = addValue - value(lowest roster player still beaten); tier by 2000/1000/250; dropConfidence by the same 2000/1000/250 against the best replacement
formulas.inputs: rowValue(row) = rankDerivedValue, else values.full
formulas.constants: 2000 / 1000 / 250 board points
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Value <= 0 rows dropped; candidate pool additionally drops confidenceBucket==='none' and sourceCount<2 - the ROSTER side applies neither gate
formulas.mathIssues: (1) Mixed scales: roster rows with no rankDerivedValue fall back to values.full, which buildRows fills from the raw scraper composite _finalAdjusted - measured ratio _finalAdjusted/rankDerivedValue over 805 players: median 1.099, p10 0.958, p90 1.268, max 1.704. (2) The 2000 smash threshold is unreachable: across all 12 rosters on the live board max netGain = 1284, so the page's 'Smash only' filter returns zero rows for every team.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/waiver-logic.test.js (synthetic fixtures only)

formulas.name: Analytics tier breakpoints (shipped, unconsumed)
formulas.expression: pct = bid/budget; tier1 >=0.20, tier2 >=0.10, tier3 >=0.03, tier4 else
formulas.inputs: historical winning bids
formulas.missingDataBehavior: budget <= 0 => tier4
formulas.mathIssues: Computed into tierBids and returned on every payload; no consumer anywhere in src/, server.py or frontend/.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_faab_analytics.py

findings.title: The live FAAB bid is a share of a DRAFT PICK's value - every recommended bid is ~2.4x too low
findings.rootCause: server.py:4960-4984 computes top_pool_value as the max rankDerivedValue over every contract row not on a roster, with no assetClass filter. Draft picks are rows in playersArray and are never on a team's players list, so they dominate the pool. That value becomes the denominator of the only real input to the bid (share = candidate/top, faab_recommender.py:322-326 -> waiver.py:89-91).
findings.evidence: server.py:4969-4977 - `for row in arr: ... rname = _norm(row.get("displayName")...); if not rname or rname in rostered_norms: continue; v = float(row.get("rankDerivedValue") or 0); if v > top_pool_value: top_pool_value = v`. Measured on the 2026-08-04 contract rebuilt via build_api_data_contract: 427 unrostered rows, 144 of them assetClass=='pick'; top_pool_value = 7831.0 = '2026 Pick 1.01'; best genuine free agent = 1905.0 (Marlin Klein, TE). _compute_faab_bid(1770, 100, 7831) = (11, 8, 4) vs (1770, 100, 1770) = (30, 21, 10).
findings.userImpact: For Mitchell Evans (best add on the live board) the desk recommends standard $12 / conservative $8 / aggressive $17. With a free-agent-only denominator the same code returns $29 / $20 / $41. Every user of the bid desk is told to bid roughly 40% of what this model's own arithmetic intends, on every player, all season. The error also propagates into the contention model, whose rival estimates are multiples of the same baseline (simulated topRival $5, clearing $6).
findings.recommendedFix: Filter the pool loop to genuine waiver-claimable rows before taking the max: skip assetClass=='pick' and mirror the sourceCount>=2 gate the rest of the waiver surface uses. Re-baseline the endpoint test fixtures, since every downstream dollar moves.
findings.complexity: low (2 lines) but requires re-baselining absolute-dollar test assertions

findings.title: The FAAB dollar figure is a value percentile mapped onto a dollar scale, not a bid derived from budget, replacement value, competition or expected contribution
findings.rootCause: The entire chain rests on aggressive_pct = 0.05 + 0.25 * (value / pool_max) (src/trade/waiver.py:91). Nothing in it references weeks remaining, roster need, starter vs bench slot, replacement level, points added, or budget already spent. Every later stage is a multiplier on that number.
findings.evidence: src/trade/waiver.py:86-95 - `share = candidate_value / top_v ...; aggressive_pct = 0.05 + 0.25 * share; aggressive = max(1, round(league_budget * aggressive_pct))`. Because share is normalized to the pool maximum, the top free agent always prices at exactly 30%/21%/10%: measured _compute_faab_bid(1905, 100, 1905) = (30, 21, 10), where 1905 is Marlin Klein, a TE outside every starting lineup on the live board. The one stage that could ground the number in observed prices, _position_calibration (faab_recommender.py:172-194), blends 50/50 with the position's historical AVERAGE regardless of player quality, needs >=3 samples, and is structurally unavailable for the non-default league (server.py:5003-5017).
findings.userImpact: The number is not defensible as a bid. It answers 'what fraction of the board's top asset is this player?' and prints a dollar sign on the answer. In a barren week it recommends 21% of budget for the least-bad option; in a week with a genuine league-winner on the wire it recommends the same 21%. There is no mechanism by which it can say 'bid nothing this week' other than the drop-side comparison.
findings.recommendedFix: Either re-anchor the baseline on an absolute quantity (value over this league's replacement level at that position, times a budget-per-remaining-week envelope), or stop labelling `standard` a recommendation and label it what it is - the share of budget implied by this player's board value.
findings.complexity: high - modeling decision, not a bug fix

findings.title: Two different FAAB dollar figures for the same player are rendered on the same page, and they disagree by 75%
findings.rootCause: /waivers renders a client-computed FAAB hint column (computeFaabHint) in the Best-moves table, normalized to the top of the DISPLAYED batch and a hard-coded $100 budget, while the bid desk above it renders the backend recommend_faab standard, normalized to the pick-contaminated whole-pool max. Neither knows the other exists.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/waivers/page.jsx:206-223 - `computeFaabHint(Number(m.addValue || ...), { leagueBudget: 100, topValueInPool: topAddValue })` with topAddValue = max addValue in moves (page.jsx:167-174). Measured on the live contract for team 'Blaine': the hint column prints $21 for Mitchell Evans (topValueInPool = 1770 = his own value => share 1.0 => 30% aggressive / 21% reasonable), while POST /api/waiver/faab-recommend returns standard: 12 for the same player and the same $100 budget. The unused backend suggestions route returns a third number, reasonable: 20.
findings.userImpact: A user reads $21 in the Best-moves table, clicks the same player into the calculator, and the bid desk says $12. Both are presented as this product's recommendation. The top row of that column also always reads $21/$30 by construction, because share is 1.0 for whoever leads the batch.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the hint column, or drive it from a batched call to the same recommender. If it stays it must at minimum read the league's real budget and be labelled a relative share, not a dollar recommendation.

findings.title: The waiver comparison subtracts raw scraper-composite values from canonical board values, and every headline drop recommendation is one of those rows
findings.rootCause: rowValue falls back to values.full when rankDerivedValue is absent (waiver-logic.js:196-205). On the default view=app payload buildRows takes the legacy-dict branch (server.py:1953-1954 strips playersArray from the runtime view), where values.full = rankDerivedValue || rawValues.full - i.e. _finalAdjusted, the raw scraper composite. The candidate pool guards against this (rowHasNoRealRank + sourceCount<2 at waiver-logic.js:341,363) but the ROSTER side applies neither gate (waiver-logic.js:547-554 checks only assetClass=='pick' and rowValue<=0).
findings.evidence: waiver-logic.js:201-204 - `const v = Number(row?.rankDerivedValue); if (Number.isFinite(v) && v > 0) return v; const v2 = Number(row?.values?.full); return ...`. Executed against the real contract with the real buildRows on a runtime-shaped payload: 12 of team Blaine's 52 matched roster rows carry rankDerivedValue null and are priced off _finalAdjusted (AJ Haulcy 1954, Divine Deablo 1913, James Pearce 1907, Cole Bishop 1876, Mack Hollins 1107, Derek Carr 888, Colton Hood 497...). The resulting top-5 Droppable rows are Colton Hood 497, Caden Curry 510, Dante McClellan 515, Bryan Thompson 744, Isaiah Williams 744 - ALL unstamped fallback rows. Scale mismatch over the 805 players carrying both numbers: _finalAdjusted/rankDerivedValue median 1.099, p10 0.958, p90 1.268, max 1.704.
findings.userImpact: Every 'Drop X' the page leads with is a number the canonical pipeline declined to stamp, subtracted from a canonical number to produce the net gain and the tier badge. The gating is one-sided: an unstamped player can only ever be DROPPED, never ADDED. The headline tier flips on this alone - with the fallback rows in, the top move is 'strong' (net 1273); with them out, 'considering' (net 848). CLAUDE.md records this exact scale-mixing as a defect already fixed in finder.py (WS-J F-6 / finding K); it survives here.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply the pool side's honesty gate to the roster side: either exclude rows the board cannot price and say so ('12 roster players unpriced'), or make rowValue return only rankDerivedValue and drop the values.full fallback.

findings.title: computeFaabHint is not a faithful port of _compute_faab_bid - 10.8% of the input grid returns different dollars
findings.rootCause: Python round() is round-half-to-even; JS Math.round() is round-half-up. Both implementations round three times (aggressive, reasonable, lowball).
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:851 claims 'JS port of ``src/trade/waiver.py::_compute_faab_bid``'. Executed both over a 600-point grid (budgets 50/100/200 x 200 share steps): 65 divergences. budget 100, value 2999.7, top 9999 -> JS (13,9,5), Python (12,8,4); budget 50, value 9999 -> JS (15,11,5), Python (15,10,5). No parity test exists (tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py covers the source registry, nothing covers this pair).
findings.userImpact: Small in dollars, but the two surfaces cannot be reconciled even after the denominators are fixed, and the docstring asserts a parity the code does not hold.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the JS copy (preferred - see the duplicate-figure finding) or implement explicit half-up rounding on the Python side plus a parity test in the style of test_source_registry_parity.py.

findings.title: The FAAB hint column hard-codes a $100 league budget
findings.rootCause: page.jsx passes { leagueBudget: 100 } literally, while the real budget is available two components away (leagueFaab.leagueBudget from /api/public/league/faabAnalytics, and selectedTeam.faabBudget from the Sleeper overlay).
findings.evidence: frontend/app/waivers/page.jsx:211-219 - `computeFaabHint(..., { leagueBudget: 100, topValueInPool: topAddValue })`, headerInfo at :222 'Quick baseline share of a $100 budget'. ManualAddDrop.jsx:99-124 renders the REAL budget in the same page's header strip. config/leagues/registry.json defines two active leagues; the default league's Sleeper settings carry waiver_budget: 100 (verified in exports/latest), the second league's budget is Not Verifiable from Repository.
findings.userImpact: In any league whose budget is not $100 the column is off by the budget ratio - half the true bid in a $200 league. The tooltip discloses the assumption, which is the only thing keeping this out of high severity.
findings.recommendedFix: Thread leagueFaab?.leagueBudget ?? selectedTeam?.faabBudget ?? 100 down from the page, or remove the column.

findings.title: The Max bid pill is labelled 'your remaining' even when it is the league budget
findings.rootCause: recommend_faab sets cap_source = team_faab_remaining if not None else league_budget and returns it as max (faab_recommender.py:530-550); the UI labels that tile unconditionally.
findings.evidence: src/trade/faab_recommender.py:533-534 - `cap_source = team_faab_remaining if team_faab_remaining is not None else league_budget`; frontend/components/waivers/FaabRecommendation.jsx:511-515 - `<StatTile label="Max" value={fmtBid(data?.max)} meta="your remaining" />`. team_faab_remaining is only set when teamOwnerId matches a CURRENT roster AND the overlay resolved an integer faabRemaining (server.py:5033-5044); the baked contract carries no faabRemaining at all (verified against exports/latest), so any overlay failure silently produces this state.
findings.userImpact: A user who has spent 90% of their budget can be shown 'Max $100 - your remaining' and bid money they do not have. The failure is silent: nothing else on the panel distinguishes the two cases.
findings.recommendedFix: Stamp which source produced the cap (maxSource: 'teamRemaining' | 'leagueBudget') and switch the tile's meta text on it - the same 'missing and present must not read the same' rule the codebase applies to valuationMode.

findings.title: /api/waiver/suggestions scales its bids off faabRemaining passed as the league BUDGET, and takes it from the request body
findings.rootCause: server.py reads faabRemaining from the POST body (default 100) and passes it as user_faab_remaining, which find_waiver_targets forwards as league_budget= into _compute_faab_bid.
findings.evidence: server.py:4805-4818 - `faab_remaining = int(body.get("faabRemaining", 100))` -> `user_faab_remaining=faab_remaining`; src/trade/waiver.py:195-207 - `if user_faab_remaining is None or user_faab_remaining <= 0: user_faab_remaining = 100` then `_compute_faab_bid(c.consensus_value, league_budget=user_faab_remaining, ...)`. The endpoint never consults the league registry or the Sleeper overlay for the real budget.
findings.userImpact: Zero today - the route has no caller (verified: no reference in frontend/, no Next bridge route under frontend/app/api/waiver/). But the code computes 30% of REMAINING where the formula's own comments say 30% of BUDGET, so any future caller inherits a silently different meaning. It also ignores idpEnabled: _BASE_POSITIONS (waiver.py:27-48) always includes DL/LB/DB, so an offense-only league would get IDP waiver targets.
findings.recommendedFix: Decide whether the parameter is a budget or a remaining balance and name it accordingly; resolve it from the league rather than the request body; gate IDP positions on league_cfg.idp_enabled.

findings.title: tierBids is computed and shipped on every analytics payload but consumed by nothing, while two docstrings claim it drives calibration
findings.rootCause: faab_analytics builds a four-tier bid histogram; the recommender's calibration reads only positionBids.
findings.evidence: src/api/faab_analytics.py:306 - `"tierBids": {label: _stats_block(vals) for label, vals in tier_bids.items()}`; the only other repo references are its own docstring line 198 and the tests. src/trade/faab_recommender.py:13-14 documents step 4 as 'League analytics calibration (blend with historical bid-by-pos+tier)' and src/api/faab_analytics.py:11-14 says it calibrates against 'similar position+tier'. _position_calibration (faab_recommender.py:183-194) reads positionBids[position] only. recentWins is likewise unconsumed.
findings.userImpact: The recommendation blends a $1 dart throw halfway toward the same position average as a league-winning claim, while the documentation says it is tier-aware. An auditor reading the docs concludes the bid is better grounded than it is.
findings.recommendedFix: Either implement tier matching (bucket the add by its own value percentile and blend against that tier's bids) or correct both docstrings to say 'position average, no tier matching'.

findings.title: The rival-contention model reads the unscoped market contract while the user's bid reads the valuation-lens-scoped one
findings.rootCause: The endpoint threads valuation_mode into _valuation_scoped_contract and uses the scoped arr for the add/drop values and pool max, but passes the module-global latest_contract_data to the contention estimator for the opponent asset pool and the player-position map.
findings.evidence: server.py:4892-4894 `contract, valuation_mode, valuation_note = await _valuation_scoped_contract(...)` and :4896 `arr = (contract or {}).get("playersArray")`, versus server.py:5227-5233 `contract=latest_contract_data, ... id_to_position=_faab_contention.player_position_map(latest_contract_data)`.
findings.userImpact: Under the league-adjusted lens the user's bid is priced on one board while rival need levels and the opponent asset pool come from another, yet the response stamps a single valuationMode for both. Second-order, since need levels are categorical.
findings.recommendedFix: Pass the scoped contract to estimate_rival_bids and player_position_map.

findings.title: The 'Smash only' upgrade filter and most of the min-gain slider are unreachable on live data
findings.rootCause: The tier thresholds are absolute board-point gaps (2000/1000/250) calibrated for starter-vs-bench swaps, but the waiver pool tops out far below the roster gap needed to clear them.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:43-47 `smash: 2000`; frontend/app/waivers/page.jsx:54-59 exposes `{ value: "smash", label: "Smash only" }`; page.jsx:666-674 ships a min-gain slider with max={5000}. Executed across all 12 rosters on the live contract: maximum netGain anywhere in the league = 1284; tier counts across all teams = {strong: 92, considering: 1013, marginal: 95, smash: 0}; the smash-filtered addable list is length 0 for every one of the 12 teams.
findings.userImpact: A user who selects 'Smash only' always gets 'No upgrades match your filters', which reads as a broken page rather than an empty answer. Roughly three quarters of the slider's travel is dead.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the thresholds relative (percentile of the roster's own value spread, or a fraction of the replacement-level gap) and bound the slider to the observed range.

findings.title: Player headshots in the add/drop picker read a field the default payload does not carry
findings.rootCause: ManualAddDrop reads r.raw?.playerId, but on the default view=app (legacy-dict) path row.raw is the legacy player object, which keys the Sleeper id as _sleeperId; the materialized row exposes it as row.playerId.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/waivers/ManualAddDrop.jsx:209 and :247 - `playerId={r.raw?.playerId}` / `playerId={row.raw?.playerId}`; frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1269 `raw: player` (legacy dict entry) and :1176 `playerId: String(player._sleeperId || "").trim() || null`. Verified against the built contract: players['Mitchell Evans'] has _sleeperId '12473' and no playerId key. FaabRecommendation.jsx:283 gets this right by falling back.
findings.userImpact: Cosmetic - the picker renders fallback avatars on the default payload path.
findings.recommendedFix: Use r.playerId || r.raw?.playerId in both call sites, matching FaabRecommendation.

notes:
METHOD: every number below was produced this session by rebuilding the live contract from exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json through src/api/data_contract.build_api_data_contract (1,092 rows), then executing the REAL frontend modules under node (frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js and frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js::buildRows against a runtime-shaped payload with playersArray stripped, which is what view=app serves per server.py:1953-1954) and the REAL backend modules under python. Nothing is inferred from a name or a docstring. Read-only; scratch files only in the session scratchpad.

CLAUDE.md VERIFICATION (line 739): "POST /api/waiver/suggestions | yes | no UI caller - /waivers computes client-side from contract rows, which already carry the lens" - VERIFIED TRUE on all three claims. (a) No caller: grep over frontend/ finds zero references and there is no Next bridge route under frontend/app/api/waiver/. (b) /waivers does compute client-side: useWaiverAnalysis -> computeWaiverAnalysis, pure, no fetch. (c) Rows carry the lens: useDynastyData.js:48,137,203 threads valuationMode into fetchDynastyData. docs/competitor-gap-analysis.md:135 says the same and is also correct.

YES, THERE ARE TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF EACH, AND THEY DO NOT AGREE.
Waiver value: computeWaiverAnalysis (roster-relative, no value floor, user rookie toggle, idpEnabled gate, confidenceBucket gate) vs find_waiver_targets (roster-independent, hard 500 floor, calendar rookie window Feb 1-May 11, position whitelist, per-position cap 6, no bucket gate). Same input contract, different populations: the client surfaced 103 addables for team Blaine; the backend returned 40 candidates across 7 position buckets for the same league. Neither is a superset of the other.
FAAB: three live numbers for Mitchell Evans (value 1770, $100 budget) - client hint column $21 reasonable / $30 aggressive; backend suggestions route $20 / $28; backend bid desk (the one users see) standard $12 / conservative $8 / aggressive $17. The spread is entirely explained by the denominator each picks for `share`: 1770 (batch max), 1905 (best FA), 7831 (a 2026 first-round pick).

THE FAAB DOLLAR FIGURE, END TO END: FaabRecommendation.jsx:418 POSTs {leagueKey, addPlayerName, dropPlayerName, teamOwnerId, valuationMode} -> server.py:4831 resolves the league, finds both rows by trim+lower name, reads rankDerivedValue for each, computes top_pool_value over unrostered rows (server.py:4967-4984), fetches the Sleeper teams overlay for FAAB balances, loads the public-league snapshot for bid history (league-guarded at :5003), reads Sleeper trending, reads the (empty) KTC crowd map, calls recommend_faab, then optionally runs a second pass with rival contention -> the panel renders four dollar pills verbatim. Every stage after the first is a multiplier or a clamp. The first stage is 0.05 + 0.25 * (this player's value / the pool's top value).
PLAINLY: the number is NOT defensible as a bid. It is a value percentile with a dollar sign attached. It is not derived from budget-per-remaining-week, replacement level, expected points added, or the user's own roster need (rival need is modeled; the user's is not). Competition IS modeled and the contention leg is the one genuinely well-built piece - but it is anchored on the same percentile baseline, so it scales the error rather than correcting it. On the live board that baseline is additionally divided by a draft pick, making every bid ~2.4x too low.

DISTINCTIONS. implemented + wired + rendered + live data: client waiver analysis, FAAB bid desk, contention (when balances resolve), league FAAB context panel. implemented + wired but NOT rendered: /api/waiver/suggestions, find_drop_candidates, /api/intel/waiver-interest, tierBids, recentWins. implemented but INERT on live data: KTC crowd blend (no ktcCrowd key in the export), intel factor (no data/intel/ in this checkout). NOT VERIFIABLE FROM REPOSITORY: whether rival faabRemaining resolves in production (data/public_league/ and the Sleeper overlay are runtime-only), the second league's waiver budget, and whether any league analytics samples exist at all (totalBidsAnalyzed).

VALIDATION STATUS: extensive mechanism tests exist (tests/trade/test_faab_recommender.py, test_faab_contention.py, tests/api/test_faab_recommend_endpoint.py 17 cases, tests/trade/test_waiver.py, frontend/__tests__/waiver-logic.test.js + waiver-pool-builder.test.js). NOT ONE asserts that a recommended dollar figure is correct, and there is no FAAB backtest anywhere in scripts/ (contrast scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py, which exists for the adjusted board). docs/competitor-gap-analysis.md:92-93 already marks both waiver rows "unverified" - honest, and this audit confirms it.

ONE NON-DEFECT WORTH KNOWING: the Best-moves table pairs 20 different adds with the SAME drop (all 20 live rows drop Colton Hood), because findBestDropMatch returns the roster minimum for nearly every add. That slate is not executable, but the panel subtitle states exactly what it does ("Each add appears once, paired with its lowest-value beaten roster player") and the Unique Upgrade Set panel exists for the executable version. Context, not a defect.

ALSO NOTED, NOT WAIVER-SPECIFIC: FaabRecommendation fetches "/api/waiver/faab-recommend" with no Next bridge route, so it only resolves in production where nginx routes /api/ to the backend (deploy/nginx/chaseupside-proxy.conf). Several other pages do the same (/api/terminal, /api/trade/simulate, /api/intel/*), so this is the app-wide pattern rather than a waiver defect - but the bid desk is unreachable in local `next dev`.

systems.name: Roster Buy/Sell/Hold signal engine (client)

formulas.name: Signal rule table (client and server, identical)
formulas.expression: RISK@100: alertCount>0 AND negativeImpactCount>0 AND trend7≤−3 | RISK@95: vol==high AND trend7≤−5 | SELL@80: trend7≤−3 AND trend30≠null AND trend30≤0 | SELL@78: negativeImpactCount>0 AND vol==high | MONITOR@65: alertCount>0 | MONITOR@62: vol==high | STRONG_HOLD@50: value≥7000 AND trend30≠null AND trend30≥0 AND vol∈{low,med} | BUY@40: trend7≥3 AND vol≠high | BUY@38: positiveImpactCount>0 AND rankChange>0 | else HOLD
formulas.inputs: trend7, trend30 (rank deltas from rank_history), volatility label, rankDerivedValue, rankChange, alert/negative/positive news counts
formulas.constants: −3, −5, 0, 7000, +3 — all identical on both sides; the retired MONITOR rule's confidence<0.35 exists in neither (retirement note at signal-engine.js:121-128 and terminal.py:907-935)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: trend7 null is coerced to 0 in JS (`?? 0`) and guarded with `is not None` in Python — arithmetically equivalent for these comparisons. trend30 null correctly blocks SELL and STRONG_HOLD on both sides. Volatility null blocks the vol rules. Total absence of data therefore lands on HOLD with the reason string "Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers."
formulas.validated: parity-tested (tests/fixtures/signal_parity_cases.json); correctness untested
formulas.mathIssues: No CONFLICT state. Opposing evidence is not averaged into Neutral — priority wins — but SELL@78 and BUY@38 can co-fire (negative + positive news on the same player with a positive rankChange) and the loser is only visible behind a "Why (2)" disclosure.

formulas.name: Window trend
formulas.expression: baseline = first point with t ≥ (t_latest − windowDays·86400000); trend = baseline.rank − latest.rank; null if no point in window; 0 if baseline is latest
formulas.inputs: per-player rank-history series
formulas.constants: windowDays ∈ {7, 30} for signals; {1,7,30} for /trending; {7,30,90,180} for PlayerMarketMovement
formulas.missingDataBehavior: returns null (correctly propagated as "unmeasured")
formulas.validated: reproduced numerically in scratchpad with node
formulas.mathIssues: The baseline is the OLDEST point inside the window, not a point ~windowDays old. Reproduced: a 3-point series spanning 2 days gives trend7 = trend30 = −6; a 2-point series gives trend7 = trend30 = −5. Whenever the log is shorter than the window, the 7d and 30d numbers are the SAME number, and the SELL rule's reason string still reads "7d trend −5 continues a 30d trend of −5".

formulas.name: Volatility (MAD of consecutive rank deltas)
formulas.expression: deltas[i] = |rank[i] − rank[i−1]| over points inside the window; mad = median(|d − median(d)|); label = low if mad ≤1, med if ≤4, else high
formulas.inputs: rank-history series, window 30
formulas.constants: 1, 4; minimum 3 points
formulas.missingDataBehavior: null (<3 points) — blocks the two vol rules rather than defaulting
formulas.validated: reproduced numerically
formulas.mathIssues: MAD of consecutive deltas measures jitter, not direction. A player falling a constant 6 ranks per day for 3 straight days produces mad = 0 and renders "Vol LOW" (reproduced). The metric is correct for its definition; the UI pill invites the opposite reading.

formulas.name: Market gap (retail vs consensus)
formulas.expression: retailMean = mean(effectiveSourceRanks[k] for k in {ktcSfTep}); consensusMean = mean(effectiveSourceRanks[k] for all other k); diff = consensusMean − retailMean; diff>0 → retail_premium, diff<0 → consensus_premium
formulas.inputs: effectiveSourceRanks (post-Hampel ordinal rank per source)
formulas.constants: Backend: NO minimum magnitude — any nonzero diff sets a direction. Frontend marketEdge/marketGapLabel: MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF = 10 (thresholds.js:46). Frontend idpMarketEdge: same 10, but with idpTradeCalc as the retail anchor and a hardcoded 4-key consensus set (display-helpers.js:294-299). These three numbers do NOT agree.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: returns ("none", None) when either side is empty — the honest abstention is implemented
formulas.validated: recomputed over the live 2026-08-04 contract (1,092 rows): 171 retail_premium, 249 consensus_premium, 672 none
formulas.mathIssues: The retail side is n=1 for EVERY offense row (only ktcSfTep carries is_retail). Verified: all 143 rows that reach the /edge Buy/Sell panels have exactly one retail source. It is a mean of one against a mean of ~12-15, and the ordinals being averaged come from boards of very different depth and format.

formulas.name: /edge Buy/Sell panel gate and ordering
formulas.expression: filter: marketGapDirection == retail_premium|consensus_premium AND sourceRankSpread ≥ PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD AND !quarantined AND 1 ≤ rank ≤ EDGE_PREMIUM_RANK_LIMIT; sort: sourceRankSpread DESC; slice 10
formulas.inputs: marketGapDirection, sourceRankSpread, rank
formulas.constants: PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD = 20, EDGE_PREMIUM_RANK_LIMIT = 250, EDGE_PREMIUM_LIMIT = 10 (thresholds.js:32, 70, 85). EDGE_CAUTION_RANK_LIMIT = 300. None of these exist in the backend.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `?? 0` on sourceRankSpread means an unmeasured spread reads as 0 and is excluded — conservative, correct
formulas.validated: recomputed on the live contract
formulas.mathIssues: sourceRankSpread is max−min across ALL sources; marketGapMagnitude is the retail-vs-consensus mean difference. The panel gates and ORDERS by the former while claiming the latter. Spearman(spread, gapMag) = 0.585 over the 143 qualifying rows; only 5 of the top 10 by spread are in the top 10 by gap.

formulas.name: Sharp signal strength
formulas.expression: strength = clamp(net/volume, −1, 1) × volume/(volume+5) × uniqueManagers/(uniqueManagers+3) × managerQuality × 100
formulas.inputs: net, volume, uniqueManagers, per-asset observation-weighted managerQuality
formulas.constants: _CONFIDENCE_HALF_VOLUME = 5.0, _BREADTH_HALF_MANAGERS = 3.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: volume ≤ 0 → 0.0 exactly
formulas.validated: reviewed; module docstring documents the double-counting bug it replaced
formulas.mathIssues: None found. A single observation scores ≈ ±4.2 (1×0.167×0.25×100), so a thin signal cannot lead a strength sort. This is the best-behaved formula in the layer.

formulas.name: Sharp confidence tier
formulas.expression: insufficient if volume ≤ 0; high if volume ≥12 AND managers ≥4 AND leagues ≥3; medium if volume ≥5 AND managers ≥2; else low
formulas.inputs: volume, uniqueManagers, uniqueLeagues
formulas.missingDataBehavior: explicit "insufficient" tier — the system can refuse
formulas.validated: reviewed
formulas.mathIssues: none

formulas.name: Sharp velocity
formulas.expression: velocity = (volume_48h / span_48h) / (volume_30d / span_30d); None when long-window volume < 3
formulas.inputs: two independently-queried windows
formulas.constants: minimum long_volume = 3
formulas.missingDataBehavior: returns None rather than inventing a large ratio from a tiny denominator
formulas.validated: reviewed

formulas.name: Insider lead score
formulas.expression: score = 100 × max(0, 0.34·interest + 0.26·fit + 0.18·need + 0.12·valueMatch + 0.10·activity − contradiction − lowSample)
formulas.inputs: cross-league InterestObservation, partner fit (normalised against FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MAX=50), roster need, matchable values (±18% tolerance), trade count vs league mean
formulas.constants: weights sum to exactly 1.00; MAX_CONTRADICTION_PENALTY 0.20; MAX_LOW_SAMPLE_PENALTY 0.12 (0.12 at volume 0, 0.096 at 1, 0.048 at 2, 0 at ≥3); value tolerance 0.18 degrading to 0 at 3× tolerance

formulas.name: BDVM buy/hold/sell
formulas.expression: alpha = (fundamental_balanced − market_value) × liquidity; STRONG_BUY if alpha>900 AND gap persisted ≥14d AND liquidity>0.5; BUY if alpha>400 (HOLD if not yet persistent); STRONG_SELL if p_collapse_1y>0.5 AND alpha<0, or alpha<−900; SELL if alpha<−400; else HOLD
formulas.inputs: fundamental value, market anchor, liquidity, gap persistence days, collapse probability
formulas.constants: 900 / 400 / −400 / −900 / 14 days / 0.5 liquidity / 0.5 collapse probability
formulas.missingDataBehavior: alpha None → NO_MARKET with a reason — a true refusal state, and NO_MARKET is excluded from ACTIONABLE_BDVM_SIGNALS

formulas.missingDataBehavior: players with <2 points are skipped; empty history returns empty lists with asOf null — an honest empty state
formulas.validated: code-read
formulas.mathIssues: `load_history(days=N)` slices `entries[-N:]` — the last N SNAPSHOTS, not N calendar days, and snapshots are appended only on a fresh scrape (server.py:1866-1868). series[0] is then used as the anchor with no date check. If scraping lapses, "vs 14d ago" silently compares against an arbitrarily older point while the panel subtitle still says "Rank deltas vs. 14d ago".

formulas.name: News classification
formulas.expression: if ALERT_RE matches → (alert, injury, negative); elif WATCH_RE matches → (watch, transaction|performance, positive); else → (info, news, neutral)
formulas.inputs: headline + description text
formulas.constants: 20 alert keywords incl. "questionable", "doubtful"; 15 watch keywords incl. "released", "waived", "traded", "contract"
formulas.missingDataBehavior: defaults to info/neutral — conservative
formulas.validated: code-read
formulas.mathIssues: Every watch-keyword headline is stamped impact="positive", including "released" and "waived". Every alert headline is stamped negative for EVERY player named in it, via match_players (_rss.py:120-147), which applies one impact to all substring matches.

formulas.name: Custom alert triggers
formulas.expression: value_crosses: fires when direction==above AND round(rankDerivedValue) ≥ threshold (or below AND ≤). rank_change: fires when |rankChange| ≥ minDelta
formulas.inputs: live contract row
formulas.constants: COOLDOWN_HOURS = 24; UI default threshold 6000, default minDelta 10
formulas.missingDataBehavior: non-numeric value or rankChange → skipped, no alert
formulas.validated: code-read
formulas.mathIssues: value_crosses holds no previous value, so it is a LEVEL test, not a crossing. A player permanently above the threshold re-fires every 24 hours forever. The module docstring (line 5) and the UI label ("crosses above") both assert a transition the code cannot detect.

findings.title: /edge "Sell signals" is a scoring-format artifact: 36 of 36 eligible tight ends are labelled SELL, and zero are labelled BUY
findings.rootCause: _compute_market_gap compares raw ordinal ranks between ktcSfTep (a TE-PREMIUM board, `is_tep_premium: True`, the sole is_retail source) and a consensus mean dominated by base-TE boards. The pipeline's TE basis conversion (te_premium.convert_te_value, data_contract.py:6451-6467) operates on VALUES inside the blend and never touches the ordinals fed to _compute_market_gap, so the format difference passes straight through into the buy/sell direction.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:2786-2792 `retail_mean = sum(retail_ranks) / len(retail_ranks)` … `diff = consensus_mean - retail_mean` … `if diff > 0: return "retail_premium"`. Recomputed on the live 2026-08-04 contract, direction by position for top-250 offense rows: TE {sell: 36}, QB {buy: 29, sell: 2}, RB {sell: 14, buy: 31}, WR {buy: 47, sell: 17}. Of the 50 rows that qualify for the Sell panel, 34 are TEs; 9 of the 10 actually rendered are TEs (Eli Raridon, Oscar Delp, Mason Taylor, Greg Dulcich, Hunter Henry, Pat Freiermuth, Dalton Schultz, AJ Barner, Max Klare). Excluding idpTradeCalc does not change it: still 36/36 sell.
findings.userImpact: A user who acts on /edge is told to sell every tight end on their roster and buy nearly every quarterback, every single day, forever. The signal carries no player-specific information at those positions — it is a restatement of which scoring format KTC publishes.
findings.recommendedFix: Either compare within-position ordinals, or convert the retail ordinal onto the consensus TE basis before differencing (the te_premium curve already exists), or suppress the direction when a position's sell/buy split is degenerate. At minimum, stop presenting a position-deterministic output as a per-player signal.

findings.title: /edge Buy/Sell panels gate and rank on sourceRankSpread, which is not the retail-vs-consensus gap they claim to show
findings.rootCause: The panels read marketGapDirection (retail vs consensus) for the SIGN but sourceRankSpread (max−min across all sources) for the MAGNITUDE and the sort. marketGapMagnitude — the field that actually measures the gap — is stamped by the backend and never read by this page.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:137-150 `r.marketGapDirection === "retail_premium" && (r.sourceRankSpread ?? 0) >= PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD` … `.sort((a, b) => (b.sourceRankSpread ?? 0) - (a.sourceRankSpread ?? 0))`; frontend/lib/edge-helpers.js:336 `detail: \`Sell +${r.sourceRankSpread} ranks\``; frontend/app/edge/edge-columns.jsx:84 `accessor: (r) => r.sourceRankSpread ?? null`. Backend stamps the correct field at src/api/data_contract.py:7723 `row["marketGapMagnitude"] = gap_mag`. Measured on the live contract over the 143 qualifying rows: Spearman(spread, gapMag) = 0.585; 60 rows (42%) have a real gap under 10 ranks and 29 (20%) under 5, minimum 0.08. De'Zhaun Stribling is rendered as the #3 Sell signal with spread 184 and a real retail-vs-consensus gap of 6 ranks — his spread comes from idpTradeCalc 288 vs dynastyDaddySf 104, two sources on the SAME side of the comparison.
findings.userImpact: The list is ordered by a quantity orthogonal to the claim in the panel title, and the per-row caption "Sell +184 ranks" is a number that does not describe any retail-vs-consensus gap.
findings.recommendedFix: Gate and sort on marketGapMagnitude, and render it in the Spread column (or add a separate Gap column) so the number under "Sell +N" is the gap being asserted.

findings.title: 38% of rows in /edge's Buy/Sell panels render as HOLD in the /rankings Edge column for the same player in the same session
findings.rootCause: Two independent definitions of the same BUY/SELL verb. /rankings requires |consensusMean − retailMean| ≥ 10 ordinal ranks; /edge requires only a nonzero difference plus sourceRankSpread ≥ 20 and board rank ≤ 250. Neither reads the other.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/display-helpers.js:164-171 `if (diff < MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF) { return { label: "aligned", … kind: "aligned" } }` → marketAction:241-248 maps aligned to `label: "HOLD"`; frontend/lib/thresholds.js:46 `export const MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF = 10;` versus frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:143 `(r.sourceRankSpread ?? 0) >= PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD` (=20). Recomputed on the live contract: of the 143 rows eligible for the /edge Buy/Sell panels, the /rankings Edge column reads HOLD for 55 of them (38%) — including A.J. Brown, C.J. Stroud, Christian McCaffrey, Bryce Young, Chris Olave. Among the 10 rows actually rendered per panel, De'Zhaun Stribling (gap 6) is the live contradiction.
findings.userImpact: The same payload gives contradictory trade verbs on two pages one click apart, with no indication that the two use different rules.
findings.recommendedFix: Make /edge call marketAction (or a shared predicate) so one threshold produces every BUY/SELL verb, and keep the extra rank/spread cuts as additional filters rather than as a second definition.

findings.title: A single source dropping out silently re-ranks most of the board, and the result is published as a real move with buy/sell framing
findings.rootCause: canonicalConsensusRank is a blend over whichever sources happened to produce a row this cycle. rankChange diffs against the previous build and /api/movers diffs against a historical snapshot; neither pass records or compares the SOURCE SET, so a change in inputs is indistinguishable from a change in the market.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:4729-4736 `prev = previous.get(name)` … `row["rankChange"] = prev - cur_rank` — no coverage term. Simulation on the live payload via `build_api_data_contract(raw, source_overrides={key: {'include': False}})` (which does not write the snapshot): dropping dlfSf changes canonicalConsensusRank for 438 of 740 ranked rows, 7 of them by ≥15 ranks (Marquise Brown −20, Deebo Samuel −19, DeMario Douglas −18); dropping yahooBoone changes 509 rows, 10 by ≥15 (Grant Calcaterra +57, Quinn Ewers +52, Riley Nowakowski +51, Dyami Brown −38). 15 is exactly the /api/movers default threshold (server.py:3378).
findings.userImpact: Rows appear in "Risers — buy-low candidates" / "Fallers — sell-high candidates", in the ticker, and in /trending, complete with a per-source breakdown, purely because a fetcher failed. Nothing on those surfaces distinguishes this from a market move.
findings.recommendedFix: Persist the contributing source set (or sourceCount) alongside each snapshot and suppress — or explicitly annotate — deltas for rows whose source set changed between the two endpoints.

findings.title: HOLD is returned for "we have no history at all" with the reason "Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers"
findings.rootCause: HOLD is the fallback when zero rules fire. Zero rules fire both when a player is genuinely quiet and when trend7, trend30 and volatility are all null. The engine has no insufficient-evidence state.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:195-203 `if (fired.length === 0) { return { signal: SIGNALS.HOLD, primary: null, reason: "Stable — no movement, volatility, or news triggers.", tag: "default_hold", fired: [] }; }`; identical at src/api/terminal.py:959-965. buildContext (:224-227) produces null trends whenever historyPoints is empty, and computeVolatility returns null below 3 points (value-history.js:110).
findings.userImpact: On a fresh deploy, after a rank_history.jsonl loss, or for any player the log does not cover, the entire roster renders as "Hold — Stable", asserting stability the system has no evidence for. data/rank_history.jsonl does not exist in this checkout at all, so this is the state a cold environment presents.
findings.recommendedFix: Add an explicit NO_DATA / INSUFFICIENT verdict when trend7, trend30 and volatility are all null and newsCount is 0, and render it distinctly from HOLD. BDVM already does exactly this with NO_MARKET (src/bdvm/market.py:197).

findings.title: SELL fires — and emails — on one day of movement while the reason claims a sustained 30-day downtrend
findings.rootCause: computeWindowTrend takes the earliest point INSIDE the window rather than a point windowDays old. When the log is shorter than 30 days, trend30 is numerically identical to trend7, so the "7d continues 30d" conjunction is satisfied by a single observation.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/value-history.js:94-100 `const cutoff = latest.t - windowDays * 86400_000; for (const p of points) { if (p.t >= cutoff) { baseline = p; break; } }`. Reproduced with node: a 2-point series 1 day apart gives trend7 = trend30 = −5; a 3-point series 2 days apart gives trend7 = trend30 = −6. The rule at signal-engine.js:85-88 then fires SELL with `reason: \`7d trend ${fmtDelta(c.trend7)} continues a 30d trend of ${fmtDelta(c.trend30)}.\`` SELL is in ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS (src/api/signal_alerts.py:57), so it is emailed.
findings.userImpact: Users are emailed a SELL on a 5-rank single-scrape wobble, with a rationale asserting a month-long pattern the data cannot support.
findings.recommendedFix: Require the baseline point to be at least ~windowDays old (or return null when the series does not span the window), and expose the actual span in the reason string.

findings.title: The Hampel outlier filter can manufacture the market gap that /edge then reports as a BUY signal
findings.rootCause: The blend drops outlier sources and stamps effectiveSourceRanks; the market-gap and IDP-edge computations both read the POST-drop map. When the dropped sources are the ones agreeing with the retail anchor, the surviving consensus mean is pulled away from retail and a large gap appears.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:7663-7672 `effective_source_ranks = {k: v for k, v in source_ranks.items() if k not in dropped_set}` … `gap_dir, gap_mag = _compute_market_gap(effective_source_ranks)` (:7721). Live row, Nick Bolton: `sourceRanks = {idpTradeCalc: 158, dlfIdp: 155, idpShow: 158, fantasyProsIdp: 66, draftSharksIdp: 97}`, `droppedSources = ['dlfIdp', 'idpShow']`, `effectiveSourceRanks = {idpTradeCalc: 158, fantasyProsIdp: 66, draftSharksIdp: 97}`. The two dropped sources agreed with IDPTC to within 3 ranks. /edge computes consensus mean 81.5 vs IDPTC 158 → diff 76 → "BUY" (display-helpers.js:319-397 reads effectiveSourceRanks first). 215 of 1,092 live rows carry droppedSources.
findings.userImpact: A 76-rank buy signal on a player where 3 of 5 sources agree within 3 ranks. The filter designed to protect the blend from outliers is being used as evidence of market disagreement.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute market gap from the untrimmed sourceRanks, or refuse to emit a direction when the drop set materially changes it, and surface droppedSources in the signal tooltip.

findings.title: idpTradeCalc's offense ranks sit a median 104 ranks below the rest of the consensus and flip the buy/sell verdict on 10.6% of offense rows
findings.rootCause: idpTradeCalc is registered under overall_idp with `extra_scopes: [SOURCE_SCOPE_OVERALL_OFFENSE]`, so its offense ordinals come from a combined offense+IDP board where defenders occupy slots. Those ordinals are then averaged as a peer with pure-offense boards inside the "expert consensus" mean.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:1039-1041 `"scope": SOURCE_SCOPE_OVERALL_IDP, "extra_scopes": [SOURCE_SCOPE_OVERALL_OFFENSE]`; _compute_market_gap:2780-2782 puts every non-retail key on the consensus side with no scope check. Measured over 386 live offense rows carrying both idpTradeCalc and ktcSfTep: idpTradeCalc's effective rank minus the mean of the other consensus sources is median +104.2 / mean +130.4. Dropping idpTradeCalc from the consensus flips the buy/sell direction on 41 of 386 rows (10.6%). Concrete rows: Hunter Henry idpTradeCalc 294 vs a 153-244 range for every other source; Eli Raridon 495 vs 163-276.
findings.userImpact: One structurally-deeper source biases every offense row toward "retail premium" (SELL), and on one row in ten it is solely responsible for the verdict the user is shown.
findings.recommendedFix: Exclude cross-scope contributions from the market-gap mean, or normalise each source's ordinal to a percentile of its own pool before averaging.

findings.title: News impact polarity is a keyword coin-flip: "released" and "waived" are stamped POSITIVE, and one item's impact is applied to every player it names
findings.rootCause: classify() returns a single (severity, kind, impact) triple per item from two ordered regexes, and match_players applies that one impact to every known name found by substring in the text.
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/_rss.py:46-61 `_WATCH_KEYWORDS = ("trade", "traded", "signs", "signed", "contract", …, "released", "waived", "claim", "claimed", "activated")`; :96-98 `if _WATCH_RE.search(text): … return "watch", kind, "positive"`; :28-45 `_ALERT_KEYWORDS` includes "questionable" and "doubtful" → `return "alert", "injury", "negative"` (:94-95); :139-146 `for name in known_names: … if (key in haystack) { out.append(PlayerMention(name=name, impact=impact)) }` — one `impact` argument for all matches. Consumers: signal-engine.js:233-239 and terminal.py:776-784 count these into positiveImpactCount / negativeImpactCount / alertCount, which drive BUY@38, SELL@78, RISK@100 and MONITOR@65 — all four of which are in ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS.
findings.userImpact: "Player X released by the Jets" produces a positive impact; combined with any upward rankChange it emails a BUY. A headline reading "X placed on IR; Y promoted to starter" stamps alert+negative on BOTH names, so the beneficiary Y can be emailed a RISK. A routine Wednesday "questionable" tag is an alert-severity injury event.
findings.recommendedFix: Split polarity from severity, resolve impact per mention (the sleeper provider already does this at providers/sleeper.py:214), and return neutral rather than positive when the keyword is direction-ambiguous.

findings.title: Four independent BUY/SELL label families run on the same players with four different threshold sets and no reconciliation
findings.rootCause: Each system was built against its own inputs and never cross-referenced. Two of the four email the user.
findings.evidence: (1) frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:29-36 + src/api/terminal.py:848-972 — RISK/SELL/MONITOR/STRONG_HOLD/BUY/HOLD from rank trend, volatility, news. (2) frontend/lib/display-helpers.js:205-255 — BUY/SELL/HOLD at |mean gap| ≥ 10 ranks. (3) frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:137-165 — Buy/Sell panels at spread ≥ 20 with any nonzero gap. (4) src/bdvm/market.py:185-225 — STRONG_BUY/BUY/HOLD/SELL/STRONG_SELL/NO_MARKET at alpha ±400/±900 with a 14-day persistence guard, flag default TRUE (src/api/feature_flags.py:225) and emailing via ACTIONABLE_BDVM_SIGNALS (src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py:43). A fifth vocabulary, idpMarketAction, adds BUY/SELL/HOLD for defenders with idpTradeCalc as "retail" — the opposite of the backend's retail definition.
findings.userImpact: The same player can simultaneously read BUY on /rankings, SELL on /bdvm, and Hold in the Signals panel, and the user can receive two contradictory emails in one sweep. Nothing on any surface names which concept produced which verb.
findings.recommendedFix: Namespace the verbs by concept in the UI ("Market edge: SELL" vs "Fundamentals: BUY" vs "Roster signal: Hold"), and add a cross-check that flags direct contradictions rather than shipping both.

findings.title: Dismissing a signal in the Signals panel does not silence it in the TopSignalsRail directly above
findings.rootCause: BuySellHold dismisses using the Sleeper-ID alias key when one exists, and user_kv stores only the single key it is handed. TopSignalsRail's dismissal check constructs only the display-name key.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/terminal/BuySellHold.jsx:279-285 `const key = entry.aliasSignalKey || entry.signalKey; dismissSignal(key, …)` — alias preferred; src/api/user_kv.py:471-479 writes exactly one key (`patch["dismissedSignalsByLeague"] = _merge_per_league_dismissals(existing, key, add={str(signal_key): expires_at})`). BuySellHold reads both keys (:147-152 `const expiresAt = Math.max(primaryExp, aliasExp);`) but TopSignalsRail:39-43 reads only `` `${name}::${tag}` ``. Every offense/IDP row carries a Sleeper ID (rawData.players[...]._sleeperId, BuySellHold.jsx:90-101), so the alias branch is the normal path.
findings.userImpact: The user dismisses a SELL, the panel hides it, and the same SELL card stays pinned at the top of the page.
findings.recommendedFix: Give TopSignalsRail the same two-key check, or store both keys on dismissal.

findings.title: Every card in TopSignalsRail is missing its position, value, 30-day delta and evidence line because four field names do not exist
findings.rootCause: The component reads fields off `verdict` that live on `entry`, and a `delta30d` / `evidence` shape the engine has never produced.
findings.evidence: evaluateRoster returns `{ row, context, verdict, news }` (frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:314). TopSignalsRail.jsx:50 `const d = Number(verdict?.context?.delta30d);` — `verdict` has no `context` key, and `buildContext` returns `trend30`, not `delta30d` (signal-engine.js:252). :56 `const v = Number(verdict?.context?.value);` — same missing path. :65 `const evidence = entry?.verdict?.evidence?.[0] || "";` — `evaluate` returns `{signal, primary, reason, tag, fired}`, no `evidence` (:206-217). :61 `entry?.row?.position` — buildRows emits `pos`, never `position` (frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:996, 1177). Repo-wide grep confirms `delta30d` appears on the signal path only in this file's comment and dead read, and `verdict.evidence` only here.
findings.userImpact: The rail promises "top 3 buy and sell candidates" and renders a badge and a name — no position, no value, no movement, no reason. The comment at :46-49 asserts buildContext sets delta30d, which is false.
findings.recommendedFix: Read `entry.context.trend30`, `entry.context.value`, `entry.context.pos` and `entry.verdict.reason`.

findings.title: MoversPanel labels risers as buy-low candidates and fallers as sell-high candidates — both inverted
findings.rootCause: Column headings assign a trade verb opposite to the direction of the data they head.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/terminal/MoversPanel.jsx:191-193 `Risers — buy-low candidates` over `risers = data?.risers || []`; :207-209 `Fallers — sell-high candidates` over `fallers`. server.py:3367 defines the terms unambiguously: "Risers = rank improved (number got smaller). Fallers = rank got worse." server.py:3495-3498 `if delta > 0: risers.append(entry) else: fallers.append(entry)` with `delta = r_then - r_now`.
findings.userImpact: The panel instructs the user to buy players whose price just went up and to sell players whose price just went down — the inverse of both phrases' meaning, on the terminal's most prominent movement widget.
findings.recommendedFix: Swap the two headings, or drop the trade verbs and label them "Risers" / "Fallers".

findings.title: "Value crosses threshold" alerts are level tests with no memory, and re-fire every 24 hours indefinitely
findings.rootCause: evaluate_alerts compares the current value against the threshold with no reference to the previous value, so it cannot detect a transition. The only limiter is a 24h cooldown.
findings.evidence: src/news/custom_alerts.py:224-231 `v = int(round(float(value)))` … `crossed = (direction == "above" and v >= threshold) or (direction == "below" and v <= threshold)`; :54 `COOLDOWN_HOURS = 24`; :149-160 `_is_cooldown` returns True only within 24h of the last fire. Module docstring :5 claims "fires when rankDerivedValue crosses a target"; the UI reads "crosses above" (frontend/components/CustomAlertsConfigurator.jsx:223).
findings.userImpact: A user who sets "alert me when Player X crosses above 6000" on a player already at 7500 gets an email every single day, forever. The alert channel trains the user to ignore it.
findings.recommendedFix: Persist the last observed value per (rule, player) alongside lastFiredAt and require a sign change of (value − threshold) between evaluations.

findings.title: /trending's "1 day" window is a ~2-hour delta, and the source comment asserts otherwise
findings.rootCause: rankChange is diffed against ranks_last.json, which is rewritten on every non-override contract build; the scrape cron is every 2 hours.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/movers.js:48-50 `if (windowDays <= 1) { const rc = Number(r.rankChange); … }` under a docstring at :31-40 reading "the 1-day case uses the contract's pre-stamped rankChange (which is the day-over-day delta the backend already computes)"; WINDOW_OPTIONS:20 `{ key: "1d", label: "1 day", days: 1 }`. src/api/data_contract.py:4710-4742 reads and rewrites the snapshot on the same build; .github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml:14 `- cron: "42 */2 * * *"`. MarketTicker gets this right ("fewer than 3 moves since last update", MarketTicker.jsx:126) and ScoutingIntel gets it right ("on the last scrape", portfolio-insights.js:501).
findings.userImpact: A 2-hour blip is presented under a "1 day" filter, overstating daily volatility on the page whose entire purpose is measuring movement.
findings.recommendedFix: Relabel the option "since last update" (matching the ticker) or compute a true 1-day delta from rank_history.

findings.title: Window labels across the movement surfaces count snapshots, not days, and degrade silently when scraping lapses
findings.rootCause: load_history slices the last N ENTRIES; entries are appended only on a fresh scrape and deduped to one per UTC date. /api/movers then anchors on series[0] with no date check at all.
findings.evidence: src/api/rank_history.py:368 `windowed = entries[-max(1, int(days)) :]`; server.py:3390 `history = _rank_history.load_history(days=window + 1)` then :3443-3444 `latest = series[-1]` / `anchor = series[0]`; append only on fresh scrape at server.py:1866-1868 `if is_fresh_scrape: _rank_history.append_snapshot(contract_payload)`. MoversPanel subtitle: `Rank deltas vs. ${windowDays}d ago` (MoversPanel.jsx:163). PlayerMarketMovement offers a 180d tab (:26) against a client cache clamped to 180 (`Math.min(180, …)`, value-history.js:32).
findings.userImpact: If the scraper misses days, "vs 14d ago" quietly becomes "vs however far back our 15 surviving snapshots reach" while still printing 14d. The frontend's own computeWindowTrend at least applies a real date cutoff; the server endpoint does not.
findings.recommendedFix: Filter by actual date in /api/movers and report the realised span (asOf already exists; add anchorDate) so the UI can print the window it actually measured.

findings.title: The /edge IDP methodology note names FootballGuys IDP, which is not a registered source, is not in the consensus key set, and has not fetched in 71 days
findings.rootCause: The on-screen note was written against an intended source list and never reconciled with the registry or the frontend constant.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:381 `note={\`Consensus = DLF IDP, IDP Show, FantasyPros IDP, FootballGuys IDP, DraftSharks IDP. Top ${IDP_TOP_LIMIT} by IDPTC only.\`}`. frontend/lib/display-helpers.js:294-299 `const IDP_CONSENSUS_KEYS = new Set(["dlfIdp", "idpShow", "fantasyProsIdp", "draftSharksIdp"]);` — four keys, no FootballGuys. Enumerating src/api/data_contract.py::_RANKING_SOURCES yields 21 keys, none named footballGuys*. No CSVs/site_raw/footballGuys*.csv exists. data/scrape_state/footballGuysIdp_last_success is 1712.5 hours old (71 days).
findings.userImpact: The user is told a five-source expert consensus backs an IDP buy/sell call that is actually computed from at most four, sometimes as few as two (Nick Bolton's live BUY rests on exactly 2).
findings.recommendedFix: Derive the note text from IDP_CONSENSUS_KEYS rather than hardcoding it, and surface the actual contributing count per row.

findings.title: The IDP Buy/Sell comparison averages effective ranks that are not on a common scale
findings.rootCause: idpTradeCalc contributes a direct ordinal while the expert boards contribute ladder-translated synthetic overall-IDP ranks. The translations disagree with each other by hundreds of positions, and idpMarketEdge averages them as peers against the untranslated anchor.
findings.evidence: Live row, Micah Parsons sourceRankMeta: `dlfIdp {rawRank: 3, effectiveRank: 47, method: 'exact', ladderDepth: 370}`, `idpShow {rawRank: 5, effectiveRank: 64}`, `fantasyProsIdp {rawRank: 54, effectiveRank: 242}`, `draftSharksIdp {rawRank: 130, effectiveRank: 528, method: 'ds_combined_cross_market'}`, `idpTradeCalc {rawRank: 64, effectiveRank: 64, method: 'direct'}`. frontend/lib/display-helpers.js:333-337 `const consensusRanks = Object.entries(ranks).filter(([k, v]) => IDP_CONSENSUS_KEYS.has(k) && v != null).map(([, v]) => Number(v));` then :368 `const consensusMean = consensusRanks.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / consensusRanks.length;`. Result: the four best IDP players in the pool (Abdul Carter, Micah Parsons, Jared Verse, Myles Garrett) are the four largest SELL signals, with gaps of 176, 156, 155 and 107 ranks.
findings.userImpact: The IDP sell list is a list of elite defenders, produced by translation spread rather than by market disagreement. Only 17 rows are evaluated at all, so the panel is small enough that these dominate it.
findings.recommendedFix: Compare percentile-of-own-pool rather than translated ordinals, or restrict the consensus set to sources sharing the anchor's scale.

findings.title: Both signal engines attribute other players' news impact to the player being evaluated
findings.rootCause: After selecting the items that mention a player, both engines iterate over ALL PlayerMentions in each item and increment the counters, rather than reading only the mention for the player under evaluation.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:233-239 `for (const it of items) { if (it.severity === "alert") alertCount += 1; for (const p of it.players || []) { if (p?.impact === "negative") negativeImpactCount += 1; else if (p?.impact === "positive") positiveImpactCount += 1; } }`; identical at src/api/terminal.py:776-784. `items` is `newsByPlayer.get(key)` (signal-engine.js:311) — items mentioning this player, but every co-mentioned player's impact is then counted for him.
findings.userImpact: An item naming five players inflates the counter fivefold. Combined with the uniform per-item polarity from _rss.py, a player merely named alongside an injured teammate inherits that item's negative impact and can be pushed to RISK or SELL. The counters are wrong on both engines identically, so the parity fixture cannot catch it.
findings.recommendedFix: Match the mention to the evaluated player before counting.

findings.title: edge-helpers.js states the Edge premium rank cap as 150 in one docstring and 250 in another; the constant is 250
findings.rootCause: A threshold bump (150 → 250) updated the constant and one docstring but not the other.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/edge-helpers.js:33-34 "inside the top ``EDGE_PREMIUM_RANK_LIMIT`` (150 today) on the blended board" versus :318-320 "Capped at the top ``EDGE_PREMIUM_RANK_LIMIT`` (250)". frontend/lib/thresholds.js:70 `export const EDGE_PREMIUM_RANK_LIMIT = 250;` with a comment at :61 recording the bump.
findings.userImpact: A maintainer reasoning about the eligible universe from the first docstring is off by 100 ranks.
findings.recommendedFix: Interpolate the constant into both docstrings or drop the parenthetical values.

findings.title: MARKET_PREMIUM_SPREAD is imported by edge-helpers and never used
findings.rootCause: The "Market premium: X" action label was removed (documented at edge-helpers.js:71-78) but its threshold import was left behind.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/edge-helpers.js:17 `MARKET_PREMIUM_SPREAD,` in the import block; no other occurrence in the file. Defined at frontend/lib/thresholds.js:29 with the comment "Minimum spread for a row to qualify as a 'market premium' (action label)" — describing a label that no longer exists.
findings.userImpact: None at runtime. A reader will assume a 30-rank market-premium label is live when nothing computes it.
findings.recommendedFix: Remove the import and either delete the constant or mark it retired.

findings.title: Sharp Tracker's /api/sharp/market route exists only as an import side-effect and is invisible in server.py
findings.rootCause: src/sharp/service.py registers the route at module import time by reaching into whichever of sys.modules['server'] / sys.modules['__main__'] holds the app.
findings.evidence: src/sharp/service.py:150-163 `_server_app()` scanning `("server", "__main__")`; :242 `app.add_api_route("/api/sharp/market", get_market, methods=["GET"], name="get_sharp_market")`; :249 bare `_register_http_routes()` at module scope. Only `/api/sharp/cohort` is declared in server.py (:12571). The docstring itself records a prior production incident where the module lookup silently skipped registration while cohort kept working.
findings.userImpact: The page's main table 503s with no error trail if the import ordering ever changes again, while the header stats keep rendering — the exact failure the code comment describes.
findings.recommendedFix: Declare both routes in server.py, or have server.py call _register_http_routes(app) explicitly with the app passed in.

findings.title: Sharp Tracker's live data cannot be verified and one enabled ingestion source is 71 days stale
findings.rootCause: The platform ledger lives under a gitignored data/intel/ directory absent from this checkout; separately, the footballGuys fetchers have not recorded a success since late May.
findings.evidence: src/intel/ledger.py:77-89 `default_path()` resolves from `store.DATA_DIR`; no data/intel directory exists in the repo. data/scrape_state/footballGuys_last_success, footballGuysSf_last_success and footballGuysIdp_last_success all evaluate to 1712.5 hours old, against 1.8-4.4 hours for all 28 other stamps. SourceHealthStrip.jsx:55-57 would tone these red (`if (ageHours >= 12) return "down";`) but only inside the collapsed detail panel (:202-222).
findings.userImpact: Sharp Tracker's status ('has live data') is Not Verifiable from Repository. The stale footballGuys stamps are invisible unless a user expands the source health strip.
findings.recommendedFix: Either retire the footballGuys fetchers or fix them; surface any source over 24h stale in the collapsed strip summary, not only in the expansion.

notes:
METHOD. I rebuilt the live API contract in the scratchpad from the tracked scraper export (exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json, scrapeTimestamp 2026-08-04T03:56:40Z) by calling src.api.data_contract.build_api_data_contract, producing 1,092 playersArray rows with 21 sources present. Every quantitative claim above (position splits, spread-vs-gap correlation, source-drop sensitivity, Hampel examples, idpTradeCalc offset) is measured on that payload, not inferred. Source-drop simulations used source_overrides={key:{'include':False}}, which sets write_snapshot=False and therefore did not touch data/snapshots/ranks_last.json. `git status` is clean; no tracked file was modified. Formula reproductions for computeWindowTrend/computeVolatility were run in node.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY GOOD. Three things in this layer are built to a materially higher standard than the rest and should not be swept up in remediation: src/intel/signals.py (the Sharp metrics — its docstring documents and fixes a real overlapping-window double-count, sample confidence and breadth factors are principled, and confidence_tier can say "insufficient"); src/intel/leads.py plus InsiderLeads.jsx (weights sum to 1.00, penalties for thin and contradictory evidence, an explicit machine-readable limitations block that the UI renders rather than hides); and src/bdvm/market.py::buy_hold_sell (NO_MARKET is a genuine refusal state, and the 14-day gap-persistence guard is the only momentum guard anywhere in the layer). The signal-engine/terminal.py rule-table parity work is also real — I checked all nine rules line by line and they agree exactly, including the trend30 null guards.

CIRCULARITY, ANSWERED DIRECTLY. "Consensus Edge" does not compare our board against an external consensus. It compares ONE of our board's own inputs (ktcSfTep) against the mean of THE REST of our board's own inputs. Every source on both sides is a blend voter at weight 1.0 (src/api/data_contract.py:1004+, all weights 1.0 by policy). With a median 12 consensus sources per row, our published board is roughly 1/13 retail and 12/13 "consensus" — measured Spearman(board rank, consensus-mean rank) = 0.965 and Spearman(board rank, KTC rank) = 0.981 over 389 offense rows. So a "Buy signal" says "the sources that already set ~92% of our number disagree with the one that set the other ~8%." That is internally coherent as a statement about KTC, but the page's framing ("the expert consensus values these much higher than KTC", edge/page.jsx:370) invites the reader to treat our board as an independent third party. It is not. Compounding this, two of the sources on the "expert consensus" side are themselves retail trade calculators — idpTradeCalc (which CLAUDE.md itself calls "the retail IDP authority") and fantasyCalc — so the word "expert" is doing work the source set does not support.

EVIDENCE MINIMUM, ANSWERED DIRECTLY. Yes, a signal can fire off one source, one day, or one headline. The retail side of every offense market gap is n=1 by construction (verified: all 143 displayed edge signals). SELL fires on a single day-over-day move whenever the history log is shorter than 30 days. BUY fires on one keyword-classified headline plus one positive rank tick. RISK fires on one headline containing "questionable". All four are in ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS and reach email.

CONFLICT STATE, ANSWERED DIRECTLY. Nothing is averaged into a misleading Neutral — the rule engine resolves by integer priority and preserves the losing rules in verdict.fired, which the card exposes behind a "Why (N)" button. But there is no CONFLICT label: SELL@78 (negative news + high vol) and BUY@38 (positive news + rising rank) can co-fire on the same player and the user sees only "Sell". Across systems it is worse — there is no mechanism at all that notices when /rankings says BUY and /bdvm says SELL on the same player in the same session.

REFUSAL, ANSWERED DIRECTLY. Partially. BDVM's NO_MARKET, Sharp's "insufficient" tier, marketEdge's "unranked"/"expert only"/"retail only" kinds, InsiderLeads' abstaining fit column, and news-service's explicit unavailable state are all real refusals, correctly implemented. The roster signal engine is the gap: it cannot distinguish "quiet" from "we have no history", and returns HOLD with a positive assertion of stability either way.

NOT VERIFIABLE FROM REPOSITORY. (a) data/rank_history.jsonl is absent, so the real depth and continuity of the log — which every 7d/30d/90d/180d number depends on — cannot be checked; if it is short, findings 6 and 17 are pervasive rather than occasional. (b) data/intel/ is absent, so whether Sharp Tracker has any movements in production is unknown. (c) I could not exercise the Next.js frontend, so "rendered to a user" is established by reading the render path, not by observing a browser.

ONE ARCHITECTURAL OBSERVATION. CLAUDE.md's strongest rule — "no frontend ranking engine, period" — is honoured for VALUES and RANKS, and the valuation-overlay design shows it was taken seriously. It has no equivalent for LABELS. marketAction, idpMarketAction, the /edge panels, actionLabel, cautionLabels, the lenses and the screens all compute user-facing verdicts client-side, with thresholds that exist nowhere in Python and that no parity test covers. tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py pins the source registry across the boundary and frontend/__tests__/thresholds.test.js pins the confidence cutoffs; nothing pins MARKET_GAP_MIN_DIFF, PREMIUM_SUMMARY_SPREAD, EDGE_PREMIUM_RANK_LIMIT or IDP_CONSENSUS_KEYS against anything. That is where the three critical contradictions above live.

BOTTOM LINE ON WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE REAL DECISIONS. Trust: Sharp Tracker's strength/confidence/velocity; the Insider lead score; BDVM's alpha-based signal; the backend confidence buckets and disagreement flags. Treat as diagnostics only: sourceRankSpread, marketConfidence (structurally capped at 0.59375 — the code already documents this and retired the rule that read it), the volatility pill. Do not trade on as currently presented: the /edge Buy/Sell panels (position-deterministic, mis-ranked, and contradicted by /rankings on 38% of rows), the /edge IDP Buy/Sell panels (scale-mismatched, ~17 rows evaluated), MoversPanel's buy-low/sell-high framing (inverted), any rankChange-derived "1 day" move (2-hour window, no source-set guard), and any BUY/SELL/RISK whose reason cites news polarity (keyword coin-flip, cross-attributed across every player in the item).
