formulas.name: Compare page "Quick verdict" gap + prescription
formulas.expression:
v1 = effectiveValue(row1,"full") ; v2 = effectiveValue(row2,"full")
diff   = round(|v1 − v2|)
pctGap = round( diff / max(v1,v2) × 100 )
tone   = pctGap < 5 ? cyan : pctGap < 12 ? amber : red
text   = pctGap < 5  → "Effectively even — fair 1-for-1."
         pctGap < 12 → "Slight lean — small balancer would close the gap."
         else        → "Stretch — needs a meaningful add-on to balance."
formulas.inputs: row.values.full for two players (backend rankDerivedValue after any override rebuild). Range 0..9999.
formulas.constants: 5 and 12 are inline literals at :382 and :388-390. Neither appears in frontend/lib/thresholds.js — the file whose header (:1-12) declares itself "Single source of truth for numeric thresholds" and lists which backend constants to keep in sync. Neither appears anywhere in Python. There is no backend counterpart with a different value; there is no backend counterpart at all.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: effectiveValue returns Number(row.values?.[mode] || 0) — an unpriced player becomes 0, not null. With v1=5000, v2=0: winnerName=row1, pctGap = round(5000/5000×100) = 100 → red, "Stretch". An unpriced player is rendered as a 100%-loss, not as unpriced. With BOTH at 0 the winner is null and it prints "Dead even — both at 0."
formulas.mathIssues: pctGap normalises by max(v1,v2), so the same absolute gap reads very differently up and down the board and the prescription bands are effectively rank-dependent. Reproduced: (9500,9000)→5% amber; (2000,1900)→5% amber; (500,440)→12% red. A 60-point gap at the bottom of the board triggers "needs a meaningful add-on" while a 500-point gap at the top reads "fair 1-for-1".
formulas.validated: No. No backtest, no test file, no reference in docs/.

formulas.name: Compare page "30d trend"
formulas.expression:
history    = row.rankHistory (array of {date, rank})
earliest   = history[0].rank
latest     = history[history.length−1].rank
trajectory = (earliest && latest) ? earliest − latest : null
render: >0 → "▲ n" green ; <0 → "▼ |n|" red ; ==0 → "flat" grey
formulas.inputs: backend-stamped rankHistory (rank ordinals + dates)
formulas.constants: The string "30d" is a hardcoded label at :111 with nothing enforcing it.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: history null/empty → trajectory null → renders "—". A SINGLE history point makes earliest === latest → trajectory 0 → renders "flat" in the same grey as a genuinely unchanged rank. "I have one observation" and "this player did not move in a month" are the same pixel.
formulas.mathIssues: The window is not 30 days. src/api/rank_history.py:368 `windowed = entries[-max(1, int(days)) :]` takes the last 30 SNAPSHOT LINES; rank_history.py:453-457 computes `missingDays` precisely because snapshots are not daily. Separately, rank_history.py:471-472: "Players who don't appear in every snapshot get gaps" — so history[0] is the first snapshot in which THAT player was ranked, which for a newly-ranked player can be yesterday. Each point carries a `date` and the page ignores it.
formulas.validated: Not Verifiable from Repository — data/rank_history.jsonl is not in the checkout (`ls data/rank_history.jsonl` → No such file), so the real snapshot cadence and per-player series length cannot be measured here.

formulas.name: Hill curve evaluator (frontend)
formulas.expression:
hillValue(r,{midpoint,slope}):
  r = max(1, rank)
  exponent = ((r − 1) / midpoint) ^ slope
  return clamp( round( 1 + 9998 / (1 + exponent) ), 1, 9999 )
formulas.inputs: rank; backend-stamped midpoint/slope from contract.hillCurves
formulas.constants: The `1 + 9998/(…)` form is the frontend's own. The backend (src/canonical/player_valuation.py:409) is `9999.0 / (1.0 + (p/midpoint)**slope)` — plain 9999, no +1. The component's own header comment at :16-17 states the backend form as `V(r) = 9999 / (1 + ((r−1)/midpoint)^slope)`, i.e. the file documents a formula it does not implement.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: normalizeCurves drops entries lacking a finite positive midpoint/slope (:77-85). If the result is EMPTY it falls back to DEFAULT_CURVES (:166) — see the next entry.
formulas.mathIssues:
Two divergences, both reproduced in the scratchpad:
(a) the +1/9998 form: difference from Python is e/(1+e) → at most 1 point out of 9999. Measured on the offense curve (c=0.1100,s=1.110) at ranks 1,2,10,55,100,300,500: diffs 0,0,+1,0,+1,+1,+1. Negligible.
(b) NO RANK CLAMP. Python clamps p to 1.0 at referenceN=500; the frontend keeps evaluating past 500. Measured (global curve, midpoint 55.888, slope 0.725): r=600 frontend 1520 vs backend 1698 (−178); r=700 1381 vs 1698 (−317); r=800 1270 vs 1698 (−428); r=1000 1101 vs 1698 (−597). Offense curve: r=800 488 vs 794 (−306). xMax at :158-159 is max(maxRank,300) taken from the live board, and the backend's OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT is 800 — so the drawn curve routinely extends ~300 ranks past where the engine flattens, and the scatter sits visibly ABOVE the curve there for a reason that is an artifact of this file, not a model residual.
formulas.validated: No — the component is mocked to null in the only test that touches it (frontend/__tests__/components/RankingsBoard.test.jsx:110).

formulas.name: Hill curve fallback constants
formulas.expression: DEFAULT_CURVES = [{ key:"global", label:"Global", midpoint: 45, slope: 1.1 }]
formulas.inputs: none — literal
formulas.constants: midpoint 45 / slope 1.1. The REAL rank-form constants (c × (500−1), s) are: global 55.888/0.725, offense 54.890/1.110, idp 41.417/1.110, rookie 76.347/0.885 (src/canonical/player_valuation.py:118-119,126-127,133-134,158-159 with _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N=500 at data_contract.py:4933). 45/1.1 matches NONE of the four.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: This IS the missing-data behavior — and it renders a fabricated curve under the label "Global", visually indistinguishable from the real one.
formulas.validated: No.

formulas.name: TE-premium: which multiplier the engine actually applies
formulas.location: src/api/data_contract.py:6450-6467 (gate) and :7192-7207 (branch); frontend trigger at frontend/components/useSettings.js:35 + frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:893-897, 1987, 2043
formulas.expression:
backend:
  te_basis_conversion = feature_flag("te_basis_conversion") AND NOT tep_multiplier_is_override
  if row_is_TE and source not in KTC_EXEMPT and source in tep_boosted:
      value = te_basis_conversion ? convert_te_value(value, base→tepp)
                                  : value × effective_non_tep_multiplier

convert_te_value(v) = v × min(2.0531, max(1.209206, 1 + 43.555794·v^-0.632839))

frontend:
  tepMultiplierIsCustomized(t) = (t !== null && t !== undefined && isFinite(Number(t)))
  customized = sitesCustomized || tepCustomized || tepNativeCustomized
  if (tepCustomized) body.tep_multiplier = tepMultiplier   // → backend source "override"
formulas.inputs: settings.tepMultiplier (localStorage, default 1.15); each source's per-row TE value on the 0-9999 scale
formulas.constants: _TE_BLANKET_NON_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER = 1.15 (data_contract.py:5635). Curve a=43.555794, k=0.632839, floor=1.209206, ceiling=2.0531 (config/weights/te_premium_curve.json). SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier = 1.15 — a FINITE NUMBER, not null (frontend/components/useSettings.js:35), plus a one-time migration at useSettings.js:181-190 that PROMOTES any persisted null to 1.15.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a
formulas.mathIssues: Reproduced (curve ÷ flat, per base value): 9000→+5.1%, 7000→+5.1%, 5000→+5.1%, 3000→+10.8%, 2000→+17.8%, 1000→+34.8%, 600→+53.1%, 400→+72.4%, 200→+78.5%. Because SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier is 1.15 and tepMultiplierIsCustomized(1.15) === true (verified by executing the two verbatim predicates in node: {sitesCustomized:false, tepCustomized:true, customized:true}), EVERY browser session with untouched settings POSTs tep_multiplier=1.15, which sets tep_multiplier_source="override" (data_contract.py:8524-8526) → tep_multiplier_is_override=True (:8662,:8686) → the `if not tep_multiplier_is_override` gate at :6452 never opens → the measured curve is never used on any board a UI user sees.
formulas.validated: The CURVE itself is validated (n=73, r²=0.9411 log-space, median abs err ratio 0.0226, per te_premium_curve.json). Whether it ever reaches a user is not tested anywhere.

formulas.name: Settings source "Covered" / "Live"
formulas.expression:
covered[src] = count of rows r where isFinite(Number(r.canonicalSites[src])) && > 0
live[src]    = covered[src] > 0
formulas.inputs: buildRows rows' canonicalSites map
formulas.constants: none
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A source absent from every row's canonicalSites → covered 0 → "Idle" grey. Indistinguishable from "this source is disabled" and from "this source failed to scrape".
formulas.mathIssues: Measures contract PRESENCE, not scrape FRESHNESS. A source whose CSV last succeeded three weeks ago still has values baked into the contract and paints green "Live" here while /tools/source-health paints it red (SourceHealthStrip.jsx:62 `if (ageHours >= 12) return "down"`).
formulas.validated: No.

formulas.name: Source health tone

if runtime.failed_sources includes src  → "down"
if runtime.partial_sources includes src → "warn"
if ageHours == null → "flat"
if ageHours >= 12 → "down" ; if ageHours >= 4 → "warn" ; else "up"

formulas.mathIssues: none

formulas.name: Trade Coverage summary counters
formulas.expression:
withTrades    = |{teams : (d30.tradesSeen||0) + (d90.tradesSeen||0) > 0}|
lowCoverage   = |{teams : any of d30/d90/d180 has reason=="low_history_coverage"}|

It is only compared to zero so the boolean result is still correct, but the expression is wrong as written and breaks the moment anyone renders `seen` itself.

formulas.inputs: row.values.full
formulas.constants: none

The comment describes code that no longer exists (see useSettings.js:69-71, "(Removed) pickCurrentYear … now backend-owned"), and /players/compare:69,370-371 uses effectiveValue for display in apparent violation of an instruction that is itself stale. In practice the two agree because customValue is only ever set on /trade's row copies (app/trade/page.jsx:541 is the sole writer).
formulas.validated: n/a

findings.title: The measured TE-premium curve (ADR-015) is structurally unreachable from the UI: the default settings object forces the override path on every session
findings.rootCause: SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier is the finite number 1.15, not the null sentinel that means "let the backend derive/curve it". tepMultiplierIsCustomized returns true for any finite number, so fetchDynastyData takes the override POST path for every user with untouched settings and sends tep_multiplier: 1.15. The backend stamps that as source="override", and the curve gate is `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:` — so the curve never runs on any board a browser renders. A one-time migration actively converts persisted null (the old auto value) INTO 1.15.
findings.evidence:
frontend/components/useSettings.js:35 `tepMultiplier: 1.15,               // 1.15 default; 1.0..1.5 = explicit operator override`
frontend/components/useSettings.js:184-188 `if (merged.tepMultiplier == null || merged.tepMultiplier === 1.0 || merged.tepMultiplier === 1.25) { merged.tepMultiplier = 1.15; }`
frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:893-897 `export function tepMultiplierIsCustomized(tepMultiplier) { if (tepMultiplier === null || tepMultiplier === undefined) return false; const n = Number(tepMultiplier); return Number.isFinite(n); }`
frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1987 `const tepCustomized = tepMultiplierIsCustomized(tepMultiplier);` → :1989 `const customized = sitesCustomized || tepCustomized || tepNativeCustomized;` → :2042-2044 `if (tepCustomized) { body.tep_multiplier = tepMultiplier; }`
src/api/data_contract.py:8524-8526 `else: tep_multiplier_effective = float(tep_multiplier); tep_multiplier_source = "override"`
src/api/data_contract.py:8686 `tep_multiplier_is_override=(tep_multiplier_source == "override"),`
src/api/data_contract.py:6450-6452 `te_basis_conversion = False` / `_convert_te_value = None` / `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:`
src/api/data_contract.py:7194-7207 `if te_basis_conversion: value = min(float(_convert_te_value(value, from_basis=_TE_SOURCE_DEFAULT_BASIS, to_basis=_BOARD_TE_BASIS)), 9999.0) ... else: value = min(value * effective_non_tep_multiplier, 9999.0)`
Executed the two predicates verbatim in node against SETTINGS_DEFAULTS: `{sitesCustomized:false, tepCustomized:true, tepNativeCustomized:false, customized:true}` → `POST body: { tep_multiplier: 1.15 }`.
findings.userImpact: Every TE on the rendered board is priced with the flat 1.15 rather than KTC's measured uplift. Reproduced ratio of curve to flat, by base value: 9000→+5.1%, 5000→+5.1%, 3000→+10.8%, 2000→+17.8%, 1000→+34.8%, 600→+53.1%, 400→+72.4%, 200→+78.5%. Mid- and low-board tight ends are systematically undervalued in the trade calculator, the arbitrage finder, waivers and the draft board — every engine reads the same rankDerivedValue. It also means CLAUDE.md's ADR-015 description of the live pipeline, and the claimed rollback lever RISKIT_FEATURE_TE_BASIS_CONVERSION=0, describe a code path no user reaches; setting that flag to 0 would change nothing observable.
findings.recommendedFix: Set SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier to null and change the migration at useSettings.js:181-190 to promote 1.15 → null (the reverse of what it does now), so an untouched install rides the derived/curve path. Add a test asserting siteOverridesAreCustomized({}) === false && tepMultiplierIsCustomized(SETTINGS_DEFAULTS.tepMultiplier) === false — i.e. that default settings do not force the override endpoint at all. Side benefit: this also removes a full override POST (~1.25 MB uncompressed per CLAUDE.md's delta figure) from every cold page load.

findings.title: /settings "Reset to default" silently switches the TE math and then reports the two states identically
findings.rootCause: The reset button writes the literal 1.15 (an explicit override) where its sibling native-TEP button correctly writes null. tepIsDefault then treats an explicit 1.15 as "default", so the reset link disappears and the caption reads "Default …× — applied to non-TEP sources on TE rows" — the same caption shown in the genuine auto state, which uses a different multiplier. There is no way back to auto from this control.
findings.evidence:
frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:425 `onClick={() => update("tepMultiplier", 1.15)}` — the non-native reset
frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:480 `onClick={() => update("tepNativeMultiplier", null)}` — the native reset, which does it correctly
frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:249-252 `const tepIsDefault = settings?.tepMultiplier === null || settings?.tepMultiplier === undefined || Number(settings?.tepMultiplier) === 1.15;`
frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:408-410 `{tepIsDefault ? \`Default ${tepDefault.toFixed(2)}× — applied to non-TEP sources on TE rows\` : …}`
frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:427 `Reset to default ({tepDefault.toFixed(2)}×)` — the label interpolates the BACKEND-derived default while the handler writes the hardcoded 1.15
frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:236-239 `const tepDefault = (() => { const v = Number(rawData?.rankingsOverride?.tepMultiplierDerived); …`
findings.userImpact: Two behaviors, one label. Where the backend-derived default is not 1.15 (a league with a positive bonus_rec_te: src/api/data_contract.py:8515-8517 `if sleeper_real and sleeper_bonus > 0.0: tep_multiplier_derived = _derive_tep_multiplier_from_league(...)`), the button reads "Reset to default (1.30×)" and writes 1.15 — a 13% understatement of every non-TEP source's TE contribution, presented as the default. For this platform's own league the derived value is 1.15 (_TE_BLANKET_NON_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER, data_contract.py:5635) so the LABEL happens to match, but the curve-vs-flat switch described in the previous finding fires either way.
findings.recommendedFix: `onClick={() => update("tepMultiplier", null)}` at :425, matching :480. Then tepIsDefault should be `settings?.tepMultiplier == null` only — drop the `=== 1.15` clause, so an operator who deliberately types 1.15 is still shown as customized (they have in fact changed the engine's behavior).

findings.title: Hill Curve Explorer draws the curve ~300 ranks past where the engine stops, so a chart artifact reads as a model residual
findings.rootCause: The backend clamps rank→percentile at _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N = 500 (p ≤ 1.0), so every player past rank 500 shares the curve's tail value. The frontend evaluator has no such clamp and keeps descending, while its x-domain is driven by the live board's max rank (backend OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT is 800).
findings.evidence:
frontend/components/graphs/HillCurveExplorer.jsx:39-43 `function hillValue(rank, { midpoint, slope }) { const r = Math.max(1, rank); const exponent = Math.pow((r - 1) / midpoint, slope); return Math.max(1, Math.min(9999, Math.round(1 + 9998 / (1 + exponent)))); }` — no reference-N clamp
frontend/components/graphs/HillCurveExplorer.jsx:158-159 `const maxRank = ranked.reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.rank), 300); const xMax = Math.max(maxRank, 300);`
src/canonical/player_valuation.py:406 `p = max(0.0, min(1.0, float(percentile)))`
src/api/data_contract.py:4881 `p = (float(rank) - 1.0) / max(1.0, float(_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N - 1))` with :4933 `_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N: int = 500`
frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1518-1520 (the InfoTip telling the reader how to interpret it): "The curve is the canonical rank-to-value shape; each dot is where a player actually lands after per-source aggregation."
findings.userImpact: Reproduced on the global curve (midpoint 55.888, slope 0.725): the drawn curve reads 1520 at rank 600, 1381 at 700, 1270 at 800, while the engine holds 1698 flat from rank 500 onward — a −178 / −317 / −428 gap. On the offense curve at rank 800 it is 488 vs 794. Every deep player therefore plots ABOVE the curve by a growing margin, which under the panel's own explanation reads as "the blend systematically overprices the back half of the board". It is the chart's missing clamp.
findings.recommendedFix: Clamp inside hillValue the way Python does — p = Math.min(1, (r−1)/(referenceN−1)) using the referenceN the backend already stamps on each curve entry (_build_hill_curves_block emits `referenceN`, data_contract.py:4979) — and evaluate 9999/(1+(p/c)^s) from the stamped c/s rather than the rank-form re-derivation. That also removes the ±1 form divergence.

findings.title: HillCurveExplorer ships a fabricated fallback curve labelled "Global" that matches none of the four real scopes
findings.rootCause: DEFAULT_CURVES is a single hardcoded entry {midpoint: 45, slope: 1.1} used whenever normalizeCurves yields nothing. It renders with the label "Global" and the same styling as a real curve, with nothing on screen distinguishing it.
findings.evidence:
frontend/components/graphs/HillCurveExplorer.jsx:45-50 `// Fallback only — used when the contract hasn't stamped \`\`hillCurves\`\` … const DEFAULT_CURVES = [ { key: "global", label: "Global", midpoint: 45, slope: 1.1 }, ];`
frontend/components/graphs/HillCurveExplorer.jsx:164-167 `const renderableCurves = (() => { const normalized = normalizeCurves(curves); return normalized.length > 0 ? normalized : DEFAULT_CURVES; })();`
frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1529 `curves={rawData?.hillCurves}`
Real rank-form constants (c × 499): global 55.888/0.725, offense 54.890/1.110, idp 41.417/1.110, rookie 76.347/0.885 — src/canonical/player_valuation.py:118-119,126-127,133-134,158-159.
findings.userImpact: Reproduced against the real global curve: rank 10 → 8544 vs 7898 (+8.2%); rank 100 → 2959 vs 3978 (−25.6%); rank 300 → 1108 vs 2286 (−51.5%); rank 500 → 663 vs 1698 (−61.0%). A viewer reading dot-vs-curve residuals off the fallback would conclude the blend badly overprices everything past rank 50. Reachability: hillCurves survives the array, runtime/app and compact views (server.py:1952-1953 pops only playersArray; src/api/compact_view.py:41-47 _PRUNED_CONTRACT_FIELDS does not list it), so the fallback fires only on a stale cached payload or a pre-_build_hill_curves_block contract — narrow, but it fires silently.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete DEFAULT_CURVES and render an explicit empty state ("curve constants not stamped on this payload") when normalizeCurves returns nothing. A methodology chart that invents its own methodology is worse than an absent chart.

findings.title: On mobile, /players/compare renders synthetic ladder-translated ranks under the label "Per-source ranks" — the exact number three registry comments forbid displaying
findings.rootCause: The page falls back from sourceOriginalRanks (the publisher's own rank) to sourceRanks (the canonical/synthetic encoding). sourceOriginalRanks is pruned from the compact view, and device-profile.preferredDataView() requests compact for every mobile or slow-network client.
findings.evidence:
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:80 `const sourceRanks = row.sourceOriginalRanks || row.sourceRanks || {};`
src/api/compact_view.py:50-57 `_PRUNED_PLAYER_FIELDS = frozenset({ "droppedSources", "effectiveSourceRanks", "sourceOriginalRanks", "anomalyFlags", "confidenceLabel", … "blendedSourceRank", … })`
frontend/lib/device-profile.js:103-107 `export function preferredDataView() { if (isMobileProfile() || isSlowNetwork()) { return "compact"; } return "array"; }`
frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:255 `// the UI must render sourceOriginalRanks.dlfSf, never the synthetic.`
frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:523 `// value, via \`\`sourceOriginalRanks.dynastyDaddySf\`\`.`
frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:678 `// renders Boone's published rank via \`\`sourceOriginalRanks.yahooBoone\`\``
findings.userImpact: On a phone the "Per-source ranks · best on top" chips show internally-derived ranks presented as "DLF SF says #14". For rank-signal sources these are ladder-translated positions in combined-pool space, not the number DLF published. The same payload also nulls the "Blended rank" stat (blendedSourceRank pruned) and removes the confidence + anomaly-flags block entirely (confidenceLabel, anomalyFlags pruned) — the page loses roughly a third of its content on mobile with no indication anything is missing.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop the `|| row.sourceRanks` fallback; render "—" plus a one-line "published per-source ranks are not in the mobile payload" note when sourceOriginalRanks is absent. Same for blendedSourceRank. Alternatively restore these three fields to the compact view for this route, but the honest-absence path is cheaper and matches the codebase's stated fail-visible posture.

findings.title: /players/compare renders unpriced players as a 0 and issues a trade prescription off it
findings.rootCause: effectiveValue coalesces a missing value to 0 rather than null, and the verdict block does no null check before computing the gap or emitting advice.
findings.evidence:
frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:184 `return Number(row.values?.[valueMode] || 0);`
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:69 `const value = Math.round(effectiveValue(row, valueMode, settings) || 0);` → :107 `<Stat label="Value" value={value.toLocaleString()} accent />`
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:370-374 `const v1 = effectiveValue(row1, "full", settings) || 0; const v2 = …; const diff = Math.round(Math.abs(v1 - v2)); … const pctGap = Math.round((diff / Math.max(v1, v2)) * 100);`
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:378-379 `Dead even — both at {fmtNumber(v1, 0)}.`
findings.userImpact: A player the board declines to price shows "Value 0" — indistinguishable from a worthless asset — and the verdict then reads "<other player> leads by 5,000 (100%). Stretch — needs a meaningful add-on to balance." Two unpriced players produce "Dead even — both at 0." The rest of the codebase is explicit that this is the wrong contract: dynasty-data.js:1014-1015 "Missing confidence stays NULL, never 0 (audit N2, 2026-07-29)", and bdvm.js:273-275 formatBdvmValue returns an em-dash for non-finite.
findings.recommendedFix: Treat a non-finite or zero values.full as unpriced: render "—" for the Value stat and suppress the Quick verdict panel entirely rather than emitting advice from a fabricated zero.

findings.title: /players/compare's fairness bands are uncalibrated inline constants that exist nowhere else in the codebase
findings.rootCause: The 5% and 12% cut points and their prose prescriptions are literals in the render function. frontend/lib/thresholds.js exists specifically to hold shared cut points and to mirror the backend's; these are not in it, and nothing on the backend produces a comparable verdict.
findings.evidence:
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:382 `const tone = pctGap < 5 ? "var(--cyan)" : pctGap < 12 ? "var(--amber)" : "var(--red)";`
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:388-392 `{pctGap < 5 ? "Effectively even — fair 1-for-1." : pctGap < 12 ? "Slight lean — small balancer would close the gap." : "Stretch — needs a meaningful add-on to balance."}`
frontend/lib/thresholds.js:1-12 `// Single source of truth for numeric thresholds used across Rankings, Edge, and Finder surfaces. … When changing a threshold here, check whether the backend equivalent needs to match:` — and the file contains no compare-page entry.
findings.userImpact: Normalising by max(v1,v2) makes the bands rank-dependent: reproduced, (9500 vs 9000) = 5% → amber "slight lean", while (500 vs 440) = 12% → red "needs a meaningful add-on". A 500-point gap at the top of the board is called fairer than a 60-point gap at the bottom. The panel is titled "Quick verdict" and reads as a fairness ruling; it is a percentage of the larger number with two guessed cut points.
findings.recommendedFix: Either move the bands into lib/thresholds.js with a stated derivation and a test, or drop the prescriptive prose and show the raw gap, letting /trade's TradeMeter (which has real engine backing) own the verdict. Do not ship an unbacked fairness call under the word "verdict".

findings.title: The command palette and /more offer every admin-only destination to every signed-in user, defeating the filter the top bar and mobile chrome apply
findings.rootCause: paletteTargets() spreads SYSTEM_MODEL.items unfiltered, and /more builds its group list from SYSTEM_MODEL directly. Neither calls systemItemsFor({isAdmin}) — the function that exists for exactly this and that the other two nav surfaces do call.
findings.evidence:
frontend/lib/nav-model.js:241-244 `{ href: "/tools/source-health", …, adminOnly: true, … }` … `{ href: "/admin", label: "Admin", hint: "Operator flags + actions", section: "Ops", adminOnly: true }`
frontend/lib/nav-model.js:235-240 `// Ops surfaces are ADMIN-ONLY in the nav. … the menu showed all four to every signed-in user — so a guest-pass holder saw a "Admin" entry, clicked it, and got a wall. Offering a door that is always locked is worse than not showing the door.`
frontend/lib/nav-model.js:316-319 `for (const item of [ ...flattenNav(NAV_MODEL), ...SYSTEM_MODEL.items.map((i) => ({ ...i, group: "System" })), … ])` — paletteTargets takes no isAdmin parameter at all
frontend/components/shell/CommandPalette.jsx:42 `const targets = paletteTargets();`
frontend/app/more/page.jsx:19 `const groups = [...NAV_MODEL, SYSTEM_MODEL];`
Contrast: frontend/components/shell/TopBar.jsx:58 `const systemItems = systemItemsFor({ isAdmin });` and frontend/components/shell/MobileChrome.jsx:106 `? [...NAV_MODEL, { ...SYSTEM_MODEL, items: systemItemsFor({ isAdmin }) }]`
findings.userImpact: Any signed-in non-admin (including a guest-pass holder) pressing Cmd+K and typing "admin", "scraper" or "health" is offered Admin, Source Health, ROS Data Health and Trade Coverage; /more lists all four unconditionally. This is precisely the regression nav-model.js:235-240 documents as fixed. /more's own docstring claims it "can never drift from the real navigation" (more/page.jsx:9-11) while being one of the two surfaces that drifted.
findings.recommendedFix: Give paletteTargets({ isAdmin }) the same filter and thread isAdmin from useAuthContext into CommandPalette; change more/page.jsx:19 to `[...NAV_MODEL, { ...SYSTEM_MODEL, items: systemItemsFor({ isAdmin }) }]`. Add a nav-model test asserting all four surfaces return identical item sets for a given isAdmin.

findings.title: /admin renders the full operator dashboard to any signed-in user because its only load-time gate is a PUBLIC endpoint
findings.rootCause: The page's authorization story is "if any endpoint returns 403, show Not authorized", but the only endpoint it fetches on mount is /api/status, which is on the backend's public allowlist. Page-level access is Next middleware, which checks only that a session cookie is PRESENT.
findings.evidence:
frontend/app/admin/page.jsx:7-11 `* Access is gated server-side by \`\`PRIVATE_APP_ALLOWED_USERNAMES\`\` — non-admin sessions get 403 from the admin endpoints.  This page renders a friendly "Not authorized" message if any endpoint returns 403.`
frontend/app/admin/page.jsx:31-32 `const res = await fetch("/api/status"); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(\`HTTP ${res.status}\`);` — the sole load-time fetch
frontend/app/admin/page.jsx:83 `if (err) { … }` — the "Not authorized" branch, reachable only from that fetch
server.py:2732-2736 `_PUBLIC_API_EXACT = frozenset({ "/api/health", "/api/status", …` — /api/status requires no session at all
frontend/middleware.js:50 `if (request.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE)) return NextResponse.next();` with :21-23 "Presence of the session cookie, not its validity."
findings.userImpact: A guest-pass holder navigating to /admin (reachable via the palette per the previous finding) sees the live feature-flag table with gate status, the raw idMappingCoverage and nflDataProvider JSON dumps, ServerStatusPanel (player counts, last/next scrape, contract version, uptime failure counts) and the three action buttons including "Force-logout ALL sessions". The actions themselves 403; the observability surface does not. No player values leak — /api/data is gated — but the docstring's claim is false and the page presents itself as authorized.
findings.recommendedFix: Fetch an actually-admin-gated endpoint on mount (e.g. GET the guest-pass list) and gate the whole render on its status, or expose an isAdmin flag from /api/auth/status and short-circuit in the component. The nav filter is not an access control.

findings.title: Three ops pages fetch /api paths that have no Next bridge route, so they are dead under `next dev` while working in production
findings.rootCause: The bridge-route layer covers an arbitrary 30 endpoints. In production nginx sends all of /api/* to FastAPI so the gap is invisible; locally, Next serves /api/* itself and any uncovered path 404s. Nothing states the inclusion criterion and no test enumerates it.
findings.evidence:
`find frontend/app/api -type f` returns exactly 30 route.js files; none is `terminal`, none is under ros/.
frontend/app/tools/trade-coverage/page.jsx:33 `const res = await fetch(\`/api/terminal?${params.toString()}\`, {` — no frontend/app/api/terminal route exists
frontend/app/tools/ros-data-health/page.jsx:12 `import { fetchRosSources, fetchRosHealth } from "@/lib/ros-data";` and :77 `const res = await fetch("/api/ros/refresh", { method: "POST" });` — /api/ros/* has no bridge route
deploy/nginx/chaseupside-proxy.conf: `location /api/ { proxy_pass http://dynasty_backend; … }` (the only /api rule) vs `location / { proxy_pass http://dynasty_frontend; … }`
Other client-fetched paths with no bridge (from a full grep of app/, components/, lib/): /api/data, /api/health, /api/leagues, /api/auth/login, /api/user/state, /api/user/signals/{dismiss,restore}, /api/custom-alerts, /api/intel/leads, /api/push/{public-key,subscribe,unsubscribe}, /api/trade/{simulate,simulate-mc,export-ktc}, /api/waiver/faab-recommend, /api/ros/{status,sources,health,refresh,player-values,team-strength}, /api/admin/*.
findings.userImpact: Local development and any nginx-free deployment exercise a different surface than production: /tools/trade-coverage renders "Loading team list…" forever, /tools/ros-data-health shows its "ROS health unavailable" empty state, and ~25 other endpoints fail. This is the environment in which changes to these pages get reviewed.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one posture and enforce it with a test: either (a) delete the 30 bridge routes and require a local proxy for dev, or (b) add a single catch-all frontend/app/api/[...path]/route.js forwarding method, query, body and cookie, and delete the 30 bespoke files. Today's half-covered middle is the worst of the three.

findings.title: Bridge routes are inconsistent about forwarding the session cookie, so dev-mode league resolution and auth differ per endpoint
findings.rootCause: Cookie forwarding was added ad hoc. The shared helper lib/backend-proxy.js never forwards cookies at all, so every route built on it is anonymous to the backend.
findings.evidence:
frontend/lib/backend-proxy.js:27 `const res = await fetch(url.toString(), { cache: "no-store", signal: ctl.signal });` and :46-52 `fetch(url.toString(), { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify(body), signal: ctl.signal, cache: "no-store" });` — no Cookie header in either
Forwards cookie: dynasty-data (:65-66), trade/finder (:27,:33), angle/find (:18,:24), angle/packages (:18,:29), rankings/overrides (:44-46), valuation/league-adjusted (:37-39), sleeper/draft/picks (:22,:29), auth/status (:7,:15), auth/logout (:5,:14)
Does NOT forward cookie: trade/suggestions (:20-26), trade/import-ktc (:37-43), draft-capital (via proxyGet), bdvm/values, bdvm/roster, bdvm/trades, bdvm/trade-eval (all via proxyGet/proxyPost), sharp/market, sharp/cohort, ros/pick-projections, league-comparison, news, status, scrape
CLAUDE.md's own resolver spec: server.py::_resolve_league_for_request picks "2. the authenticated user's activeLeagueKey from user_kv" — which requires the cookie.
findings.userImpact: In dev, POST /api/trade/suggestions (a roster-aware, league-scoped, auth-requiring engine) reaches the backend with no session: the resolver falls through to the registry default league and the private gate sees an anonymous caller. Same for the four BDVM routes and draft-capital. A developer validating multi-league behavior locally is testing the default league regardless of what they selected. POST /api/scrape also forwards nothing, so the dev bridge cannot authenticate an operator action.
findings.recommendedFix: Add cookie forwarding to proxyGet/proxyPost (accept the request and copy its cookie header), which fixes eight routes at once, then patch the four hand-rolled routes that still omit it. Or fold everything into the catch-all proposed above.

findings.title: /settings' "Live" badge measures contract presence, not scrape freshness, and contradicts /tools/source-health for the same source
findings.rootCause: Two independent definitions of "is this source live" exist in the frontend with no shared constant: /settings derives it from whether any player row carries a positive value for that source in the current contract; /tools/source-health derives it from the scrape runtime's failure lists and per-source file age.
findings.evidence:
frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:290-297 `for (const r of rows || []) { const cs = r?.canonicalSites; … const v = Number(cs[src.key]); if (Number.isFinite(v) && v > 0) { coverage.set(src.key, (coverage.get(src.key) || 0) + 1); } }`
frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:309-310 `covered,` / `live: covered > 0,`
frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:1130-1131 `const statusLabel = src.live ? "Live" : "Idle"; const statusColor = src.live ? "var(--green)" : "var(--subtext)";`
frontend/components/SourceHealthStrip.jsx:55-65 `if (runtime?.failed_sources?.includes(source)) return "down"; if (runtime?.partial_sources?.includes(source)) return "warn"; … if (ageHours >= 12) return "down"; if (ageHours >= 4) return "warn"; return "up";`
findings.userImpact: A source whose scrape has been failing for days still contributes its last-good values to the contract, so /settings paints it green "Live" with a healthy row count while /tools/source-health paints the same source red. The user tuning source weights — the decision this page exists for — is told a stale source is live. The page also cannot distinguish "disabled" from "failed": both land on grey "Idle".
findings.recommendedFix: Rename the /settings column to "Rows in board" and drop the Live/Idle badge, or join /api/status source_health into the settings table and render the same tone function as SourceHealthStrip. Extract the freshness thresholds into lib/thresholds.js so the three ops surfaces (4h/12h in SourceHealthStrip.jsx:62-64, 6h/24h at ros-data-health/page.jsx:34, 12h at :44) stop disagreeing.

findings.title: The compare page's "30d trend" is not a 30-day window and cannot distinguish one observation from no movement
findings.rootCause: The label is a hardcoded string; the underlying series is the last 30 SNAPSHOT lines (not calendar days) filtered to the snapshots in which this specific player was ranked. The page differences the first and last elements and ignores the `date` field each point carries.
findings.evidence:
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:73-76 `const history = Array.isArray(row.rankHistory) ? row.rankHistory : null; const earliest = history && history.length > 0 ? history[0].rank : null; const latest = history && history.length > 0 ? history[history.length - 1].rank : null; const trajectory = (earliest && latest) ? earliest - latest : null;`
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:111 `label="30d trend"`
src/api/rank_history.py:368 `windowed = entries[-max(1, int(days)) :]`
src/api/rank_history.py:471-472 `Players who don't appear in every snapshot get gaps.  The frontend sparkline path handles gaps; no imputation here.`
src/api/rank_history.py:453-457 `"spanDays": span_days,` / `"missingDays": max(0, span_days - len(dates)),` — the backend explicitly models missed days
server.py:1882 `stamped = _rank_history.stamp_contract_with_history(contract_payload)` — called with the default days=30
findings.userImpact: The arrow's window silently varies per player and per snapshot cadence. A player first ranked yesterday has a single point → earliest === latest → the cell renders "flat" in the neutral colour, identical to a player genuinely unchanged over a month. A gap in the scrape schedule stretches the "30d" window past 30 days with no change to the label.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute the window from the series' own dates (history[0].date … history.at(-1).date) and label it with the real span, e.g. "Δ over 27d". Require history.length >= 2 before rendering any arrow; below that render "—", not "flat".

findings.title: /design renders fabricated player values, team totals and league ranks with no on-screen disclaimer
findings.rootCause: The design gallery composes its component demos from hardcoded arrays and literals. The only "sample" marker is a code comment and one DataTable caption; the StatTile, Meter and Sparkline sections carry none.
findings.evidence:
frontend/app/design/DesignGallery.jsx:40-47 `/* ── sample data (display only) ── */ const SAMPLE_ROWS = [ { id: 1, rank: 1, name: "Justin Jefferson", pos: "WR", team: "MIN", value: 9541, delta: 128, trend: [92, 93, 95, 94, 96, 97] }, { id: 2, rank: 2, name: "Ja'Marr Chase", … value: 9430, delta: -64, … }, … ]`
frontend/app/design/DesignGallery.jsx:340-353 `<StatTile … value="48,210" movement={<Movement delta={340} confidence={0.8} />} />` / `<StatTile label="League rank" value="#2" meta="of 12" />` / `value="6,120"` / `<StatTile label="Open trades" value="3" />`
frontend/app/design/DesignGallery.jsx:504-506 `<Meter value={9541} max={10000} label="Jefferson value" />` / `<Meter value={6120} max={10000} label="Draft capital" />` / `<Meter value={2870} max={10000} label="Bench depth" />`
frontend/app/design/DesignGallery.jsx:526-529 `<StatTile bare label="Value" value="9,541" … />` / `<Sparkline values={[88, 90, 91, 93, 96, 97]} label="Jefferson 6-week value trend" … />`
Only mitigations found: the code comment at :40 and `caption="Sample value board: …"` at :375. A case-insensitive grep for sample|demo|placeholder|fake|mock|fixture finds no other user-visible disclaimer.
findings.userImpact: Low. The route is private (absent from PUBLIC_EXACT/PUBLIC_PREFIXES in lib/public-routes.js), noindexed (page.jsx:11-14), and in no nav model — but it is reachable by URL for any signed-in user, and "Justin Jefferson 9541, ▲128" is the exact shape of a real board row. This is the answer to "list every fixture rendered as if live": /design is the only whole-page instance in the audited set.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a persistent banner at the top of DesignGallery: "All numbers on this page are fabricated component fixtures." One <Banner tone="warning"> — the primitive is already imported at :10.

findings.title: trade-logic's displayValue docstring warns against a behavior effectiveValue does not have, and the compare page does the opposite
findings.rootCause: The pick-year discount moved to the backend (documented at useSettings.js:69-71 "(Removed) pickCurrentYear — the future-year pick discount … are now backend-owned") but the warning comment describing it stayed.
findings.evidence:
frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:196-199 `* Use this anywhere a row's "Our Value" number is shown (picker * cells, sort comparators, headers).  Don't use \`\`effectiveValue\`\` * directly for display — it also applies the pick-year discount * which is trade-math-only, not display.`
frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:181-185 — the entire function body: `if (row.customValue != null && row.customValue > 0) return row.customValue; return Number(row.values?.[valueMode] || 0);` — no discount anywhere
frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:69, 370-371 use effectiveValue for display
frontend/components/useSettings.js:69-71 `// (Removed) pickCurrentYear — the future-year pick discount and its // self-rolling current draft year are now backend-owned // (src/api/data_contract.py); the frontend no longer re-discounts.`
findings.userImpact: None today — the two functions return the same number for every row useDynastyData produces, because customValue is written only on /trade's own row copies (app/trade/page.jsx:541 is the single writer). The risk is a future reader trusting the comment.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the stale clause; state the real difference (effectiveValue honors a per-player trade override, displayValue does not).

findings.title: Dead duplicate of fmtPassExpiry left behind in /settings after the guest-pass panel moved to /admin
findings.rootCause: Incomplete move. The comment block and helper survived; the component and its call sites did not.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:1549-1564 `function fmtPassExpiry(epoch) { … }` — and `grep -n "fmtPassExpiry\|GuestPass" frontend/app/settings/page.jsx` returns only line 1549, the definition itself. The live copy is in frontend/components/admin/GuestPassPanel.jsx (used at :267 and :325). The orphaned comment block at frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:1540-1548 documents /api/admin/guest-passes endpoints on a page that no longer calls them.
findings.userImpact: None at runtime — dead code in a 1,564-line file. Two copies of a formatter is how they drift.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:1540-1564.

findings.title: Trade Coverage's "Had trades in window" sums two overlapping windows
findings.rootCause: The 90-day window contains the 30-day window; the counter adds their tradesSeen before testing.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/tools/trade-coverage/page.jsx:126-127 `const seen = (r.d30?.tradesSeen || 0) + (r.d90?.tradesSeen || 0); if (seen > 0) withTradesCount += 1;`
findings.userImpact: None today, because the sum is only compared to zero and the boolean result is correct. It is wrong as an expression and produces a nonsense number the moment anyone renders `seen` itself.
findings.recommendedFix: `if ((r.d90?.tradesSeen || 0) > 0 || (r.d30?.tradesSeen || 0) > 0)`.

findings.title: Command palette renders "0" for a player the board has not priced
findings.rootCause: `|| 0` coalesce on a possibly-absent value, in a surface that otherwise handles a missing rank gracefully.
findings.evidence: frontend/components/shell/CommandPalette.jsx:213-215 ` {Math.round(r.values?.full || 0).toLocaleString()} ` Contrast the same component's rank handling at :210 `{rank < Infinity ? \` · #${rank}\` : ""}` — absence is handled correctly there.
findings.userImpact: An unpriced asset shows "0" in the search list beside genuinely-priced players. Minor, but the same absent-becomes-zero class as the compare page's Value stat.
findings.recommendedFix: `{Number.isFinite(r.values?.full) ? Math.round(r.values.full).toLocaleString() : "—"}`.

findings.title: Backend comment states a TE default that contradicts the constant three lines away
findings.rootCause: Stale example block left after the default changed from 1.25 to 1.15.
findings.evidence:
src/api/data_contract.py:8500-8503 `#   * TEP-1.5 league (bonus_rec_te=0.5) → derived 1.15` / `#   * TEP-2.0 league (bonus_rec_te=1.0) → derived 1.30` / `#   * Non-TEP / no Sleeper context       → derived 1.25 (default)`
src/api/data_contract.py:5635 `_TE_BLANKET_NON_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER: float = 1.15`
src/api/data_contract.py:8518-8519 `else: tep_multiplier_derived = _TE_BLANKET_NON_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER`
The surrounding prose at :8495-8498 correctly says "fall back to the hardcoded _TE_BLANKET_NON_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER (1.15)" — so the function contradicts itself within eight lines.
findings.userImpact: None at runtime. It is load-bearing for anyone auditing the /settings TEP control, because 1.25 is also the value the frontend migration at useSettings.js:186 treats as a stale default to be overwritten.
findings.recommendedFix: Change the third bullet to 1.15.

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Every file named in the task was read in full or, for the two large ones (frontend/app/settings/page.jsx at 1,564 lines and frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js), read across every region containing arithmetic, thresholds, color-by-value, or fetch construction. All 30 frontend/app/api route.js files were read end to end. Cross-checks against Python used src/api/data_contract.py, src/canonical/player_valuation.py, src/api/rank_history.py, src/api/compact_view.py, src/league_intel/te_premium.py, config/weights/te_premium_curve.json, server.py and deploy/nginx/chaseupside-proxy.conf. Three formulas were reproduced numerically in the scratchpad: the Hill curve frontend-vs-Python and fallback-vs-real; the TE curve vs the flat 1.15; and the settings-default customization predicates, executed verbatim in node.

DIRECT ANSWER — "every place a fixture, mock, sample, or hardcoded array is rendered to the user as if it were live data". Exactly two in the audited surface, plus one near-miss.
1. frontend/app/design/DesignGallery.jsx — SAMPLE_ROWS (:41-47) plus hardcoded StatTile / Meter / Sparkline literals (:310-314, :340-353, :499-506, :526-529). Real player names with plausible board values; no on-screen disclaimer outside one DataTable caption. Private and noindexed.
2. frontend/components/graphs/HillCurveExplorer.jsx:48-50 — DEFAULT_CURVES, a fabricated Hill curve (midpoint 45, slope 1.1) matching none of the four real scopes, rendered under the label "Global" and styled identically to a real curve. This one appears on /rankings, a production decision surface.
Near-miss: frontend/app/api/dynasty-data/route.js:170-189 and :249-252 load a disk snapshot (exports/latest/dynasty_data_YYYY-MM-DD.json, newest by mtime) and serve it with no staleness marker when the backend is unreachable. That is genuine historical data rather than a fixture, and it is unreachable in production (nginx routes /api/ to FastAPI), so I am not counting it — but a dev session can silently render a weeks-old board with no indication.

DIRECT ANSWER — "any bridge route that transforms rather than proxies". None. All 30 are pass-through: they forward status and body and at most select which query params to forward. The only non-proxy behavior in the layer is the dynasty-data disk fallback above. Error paths are consistently shaped as JSON the client can read rather than thrown.

CHART AXIS HONESTY. HillCurveExplorer uses a full 0-9999 y-axis and a linear rank x-axis from 1 — not truncated, no index rebasing. chart-primitives.js linearScale / ticks / chartBox are correct and take their domain from the caller, so they cannot truncate on their own. The one misleading chart behavior found is the missing rank clamp described in the findings, which is a domain-extension problem rather than an axis problem.

FIVE THINGS I COULD NOT VERIFY.
- Live rankHistory cadence and per-player series length: data/rank_history.jsonl is gitignored and absent from this checkout, so the real "30d" window cannot be measured. Not Verifiable from Repository.
- Whether the te_basis_conversion feature flag is enabled in the deployed environment. It does not change the critical finding — the frontend forces the override path regardless — but the flag's own state is env-driven and not in the repo.
- Whether /api/ros/health and /api/ros/refresh are admin-gated. Not read this pass.
- Test-coverage claims in module headers (chart-primitives.test.js at chart-primitives.js:16, nav-model tests at nav-model.js:36, bdvm-lib.test.js per CLAUDE.md) were not opened; reported as claimed, not confirmed.
- Whether frontend/lib/api-retry.js's "4 call sites" (:17) is still accurate.

WHAT DESERVES TO INFLUENCE REAL DECISIONS, bluntly.
Trustworthy in this surface: frontend/lib/bdvm.js (genuinely a pure materializer — the cleanest module audited), frontend/lib/chart-primitives.js, frontend/lib/player-images.js, all 30 bridge routes as transport, frontend/lib/public-routes.js and middleware.js.
Do not act on: /players/compare's "Quick verdict" — two uncalibrated inline constants and a denominator choice that make the same absolute gap read "fair" at the top of the board and "stretch" at the bottom, with unpriced players scored as zero. The page is fine as a side-by-side data view and should not be issuing prescriptions.
Read with a correction: the /rankings Hill curve panel below rank 500, and /settings' Live badge.
And the one that changes real numbers: every tight end on the live board is priced with a flat 1.15 instead of the measured 1.209-2.053 curve, because the default settings object ships a finite 1.15 that trips the override gate. One-line fix; it moves mid- and low-board TE values by 18-78%.

formulas.name: Per-source freshness age
formulas.location: scripts/watchdog_freshness.py:52-93 and server.py:1542-1610 (_per_source_freshness) — two copies of the same rule
formulas.expression: last_epoch = float(read('data/scrape_state/{key}_last_success')) if parseable else csv_path.stat().st_mtime;  age_hours = max(0, (now - last_epoch) / 3600)
formulas.inputs: per-source stamp file content (unix epoch, written by run_fetcher/stamp_if_present in scheduled-refresh.yml), else CSV mtime
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Stamp missing AND CSV missing → the source is silently OMITTED from the freshness map entirely (watchdog_freshness.py:83-84 `except OSError: continue`). It is not reported stale; it disappears. Only a totally empty map trips the 'registry broken' error.
formulas.constants: none
formulas.validated: Executed in this audit: 22/22 sources fresh, 0 hard-stale. Measured ages at 2026-08-04T08:32Z — dlf* 2.0h, idpShow 2.0h, most sources 4.6h, sleeper 4.6h.
formulas.mathIssues: Stamp content is preferred over mtime specifically because actions/checkout resets mtimes; that reasoning is correct. But it means a stamp written for a CSV that was never rewritten reports freshness for stale content — which is exactly why stamp_if_present gates on `-nt $SCRAPE_START_MARKER`.

formulas.name: Stale classification (hard vs soft vs fresh)
formulas.expression: threshold = thresholds[exact_key] if present else thresholds[vendor_prefix] if prefix matches at a word boundary else 24;  stale = age > threshold;  escalated = soft_escalate_hours > 0 and age > soft_escalate_hours;  bucket = soft_stale if (is_soft(src) and not escalated) else hard_stale
formulas.inputs: age_hours, config/source_staleness.json
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Unlisted source → default 24h.
formulas.constants: 24h for all 14 listed vendors; softEscalateHours = 72; soft list = ['idpShow'] only. All three constants live only in config/source_staleness.json and _DEFAULT_STALENESS_HOURS (source_health_alerts.py:46-62) — the Python default dict and the JSON agree on 24 for the 11 keys they share; the JSON adds fantasyNavigator and pfkDynasty which the Python default omits (harmless, JSON wins).
formulas.validated: Yes — single implementation shared by CI watchdog and live alert engine, by design.
formulas.mathIssues: None. The soft-escalation cap is a genuinely good design: 'soft' cannot silently mean 'unmonitored forever'.

formulas.name: Partial-scrape promotion guard
formulas.expression: block_promotion  ⇔  total_sites > 0  AND  site_count < total_sites / 2,  where site_count = |{s in result['sites'] : s.playerCount > 0}|
formulas.inputs: result['sites'] from Dynasty Scraper.py
formulas.missingDataBehavior: total_sites == 0 → guard disabled entirely, partial result promoted.
formulas.constants: the divisor 2 (i.e. the '50%' policy). Documented in docs/ops/failure-handling-and-fallbacks.md and docs/ops/current-automation-state.md as '<50% of sites'.
formulas.validated: Reproduced numerically in this audit against the live payload. exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json contains exactly 2 site entries: [{key:'ktc',playerCount:500},{key:'idpTradeCalc',playerCount:900}]. Threshold = 2/2 = 1.0. Blocks only when site_count ∈ {0}. site_count = 1 (KTC dead, IDPTC alive) → 1 < 1.0 is FALSE → PROMOTED.
formulas.mathIssues: The guard's population is only the legacy in-scraper SITES dict (KTC + IDPTradeCalc). The ~20 sources fetched by scripts/fetch_*.py never appear in result['sites'], so their total collapse contributes nothing to site_count and cannot trigger the guard. With 4 sites the guard blocks at <=1; with 8 at <=3; with the real 22 it would block at <=10. At 2 it degenerates to 'block only on total loss'.

formulas.name: 24h scrape success rate
formulas.location: server.py:1104-1124 (_scrape_success_rate_24h), exposed at server.py:4207 inside get_status()
formulas.expression: recent = [e in scrape_history : (now - e.ts) <= 86400];  rate = |{e in recent : e.outcome == 'success'}| / |recent|,  or None when |recent| == 0
formulas.inputs: the in-memory scrape_history ring
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No entries in 24h → {'total':0,'success':0,'failure':0,'rate':None}.
formulas.constants: 86400s window.
formulas.validated: Read at server.py:4207. Consumed correctly by health-check.yml:76-90, which warns when rate < 0.5 and total >= 2.
formulas.mathIssues: A partial scrape that the R-3 guard BLOCKED still calls _mark_scrape_success (server.py:2380) which calls _record_scrape_history('success', …). So a run of consecutive blocked-partial scrapes scores a 100% success rate. The metric measures 'the scraper function returned' not 'good data was published'.

formulas.name: Ops alert — scrape rate (DEAD)
formulas.expression: rate = status_payload.get('scrape_success_rate_24h');  if rate is None → no alert;  r = float(rate);  alert iff r < 0.5, severity critical iff r < 0.25
formulas.inputs: _scrape_status_payload()
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Returns None (no alert) on a missing key OR on a TypeError/ValueError from float().
formulas.constants: 0.5 warning threshold, 0.25 critical threshold
formulas.validated: Traced and reproduced. _scrape_status_payload() (server.py:1266-1304) returns `dict(scrape_status)` plus exactly three added keys — stall_threshold_sec, run_timeout_sec, status_summary. The scrape_status global's key set (server.py init) is: running, is_running, hung, stalled, interrupted, interrupted_at, started_at, finished_at, last_heartbeat, last_scrape, last_success_at, last_failure_at, last_duration_sec, next_scrape, error, last_error, current_step, current_source, progress_step_index, progress_step_total, worker_id, scrape_count, run_events, enabled, target_url, last_check, last_ok, last_http_status, consecutive_failures. `scrape_success_rate_24h` is NOT among them; grep shows _scrape_success_rate_24h() is called from exactly ONE place, server.py:4207, inside the get_status() HTTP handler. So `rate` is always None and the function always returns None on the first branch. Belt and braces: even if the key were added, get_status stamps it as a DICT, and `float({'total':10,'rate':0.2})` raises TypeError — verified in this audit — which the except clause swallows into another None.
formulas.mathIssues: The alert can never fire under any production condition. Two independent reasons.

formulas.name: Ops alert — data staleness
formulas.expression: data_age_hours = (now_utc - parse(latest_data_source['loadedAt'])) / 3600;  alert iff data_age_hours > 3 * SCRAPE_INTERVAL_HOURS
formulas.inputs: latest_data_source['loadedAt']
formulas.missingDataBehavior: loadedAt absent or unparseable → data_age_hours stays None → no alert.
formulas.constants: multiplier 3; SCRAPE_INTERVAL_HOURS = 2 → 6h threshold.
formulas.validated: Wired correctly. This is the ONE ops-alert leg that can actually catch a stalled data pipeline.
formulas.mathIssues: `loadedAt` is stamped by _set_latest_data_source on every prime, INCLUDING a startup prime from the on-disk cache. A restart therefore resets the age to zero without a successful scrape — the exact mechanism dynasty-healthcheck.sh:96-100 refuses to trigger on purpose. So a crash-loop plus healthcheck restarts would keep this alert quiet.

formulas.name: Ops alert — circuit breaker
formulas.expression: alert for each circuit c where c.state == 'open' AND c.stateAgeSec >= 600
formulas.inputs: src.utils.circuit_breaker.snapshot_all()
formulas.missingDataBehavior: stateAgeSec is None → skipped silently.
formulas.constants: 600 seconds (10 min)
formulas.validated: Wired correctly.
formulas.mathIssues: None.

formulas.name: Ops alert cooldown / recovery
formulas.expression: fire iff (now - state[category].firedAt) >= 14400;  recovery emitted once per category when category ∉ active_categories and not state[category].recoveryFired
formulas.inputs: user_kv state under the synthetic user _system_ops_alerts
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No prior state → firedAt 0 → fires.
formulas.constants: _ALERT_COOLDOWN_SEC = 4*3600 = 14400

formulas.mathIssues: None.

formulas.name: Backup freshness
formulas.location: server.py:1635-1676 (_backup_freshness_uncached); consumed at server.py:4196 and health-check.yml:158-186
formulas.expression: newest = max(mtime of *.sqlite.gz under /var/backups/riskit/daily ∪ /home/dynasty/backups/riskit/daily);  age_h = (now - newest)/3600;  dbCount = |distinct db-name prefixes sharing the newest file's date stamp|

formulas.missingDataBehavior: No files found → newestBackupAgeHours = null, which health-check.yml treats as a HARD FAILURE ('No SQLite backups … user_kv, session_store and guest_passes are UNPROTECTED'). Correct: absence is loud, not silent.
formulas.constants: MAX_AGE_HOURS = 30 in health-check.yml:161 (nightly at 02:00 + slack); dbCount < 3 → warning only. server.py:4472 separately narrates 'Expected a fresh backup within 24h' — 24 vs 30 is an inconsistency between two consumers of the same number.
formulas.validated: Indirectly: health-check.yml has 29/30 recent green runs and this step exits 1 on failure, so a <30h backup existed at 2026-08-04T03:34Z.
formulas.mathIssues: The glob covers only /var/backups/riskit and the /home/dynasty fallback. deploy/backup/riskit-state-backup.sh writes to /var/backups/riskit-state (BACKUP_ROOT, line 65) with a different layout (daily/YYYY-MM-DD/ directories, not *.sqlite.gz at the daily/ root). That second backup system is 100% invisible to this metric — if system A dies and system B keeps running, monitoring reports UNPROTECTED.

formulas.name: Served-board source coverage gate
formulas.expression: covered = |{k : status.served_source_coverage[k] >= 5}|;  fail iff served_source_coverage missing/empty OR covered < 8
formulas.inputs: GET /api/status → served_source_coverage
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Key absent or empty → HARD FAIL with the explicit message 'the live board is the bare 3-source legacy export, not the enriched blend'. Excellent: this is the one check that distinguishes 'degraded' from 'looks normal'.
formulas.constants: MIN_PER_SOURCE = 5 (comment says it mirrors watchdog_contract_coverage._MIN_COVERAGE); MIN_SOURCES = 8 (healthy ~16-21, degraded ~3)
formulas.validated: Not independently re-derived against a live /api/status in this audit (endpoint is auth-gated). The 8-vs-3 separation is wide and the reasoning in the comment is sound.
formulas.mathIssues: MIN_PER_SOURCE = 5 is duplicated as a literal here rather than imported from watchdog_contract_coverage — a silent drift pair.

formulas.name: Liveness watchdog restart rule
formulas.expression: rc = curl exit code for http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health (25s timeout);  if rc == 0: failures := 0 (any HTTP status counts as alive; a 503 sets a log-only degraded marker);  else failures := failures + 1;  if failures >= 3: systemctl reset-failed && systemctl restart, then failures := 0
formulas.inputs: curl exit code, /run/dynasty-healthcheck/consecutive-failures
formulas.missingDataBehavior: State file unreadable or non-numeric → treated as 0 (read_failures:66-71). A wiped /run therefore forgives an in-progress outage; acceptable since /run is cleared only on reboot.
formulas.constants: HEALTH_FAIL_THRESHOLD = 3 (~3 minutes of no HTTP response at 60s cadence); HEALTH_CURL_TIMEOUT = 25s
formulas.validated: Not executed (production-only script). The liveness/health split is explicitly and correctly reasoned: restarting on an app-level 503 would clear the in-memory scrape error and reload the disk cache with a fresh loadedAt, flipping health green WITHOUT a successful scrape.
formulas.mathIssues: None. This is the best-reasoned piece of ops code in the repository.

formulas.name: Sharp production smoke poll budget
formulas.expression: for attempt in 1..80: poll; sleep 30 → 79 × 30s ≈ 39.5 min of wall clock;  healthy ⇔ records.managersWithRecords > 0 AND len(market.assets) > 0 AND market.cohort.provisionalManagers > 0;  loop-else → status = 'degraded_timeout'

formulas.outputRange: one of waiting | deploy_failed | population_in_progress | endpoint_retry | healthy | degraded_timeout

formulas.validated: Reproduced from the live job log (job 91858761506, 2026-08-04T00:40:12Z → 01:20:43Z): attempts=80, all recorded errors 'HTTP Error 401: Unauthorized', cohort {}, ffpcMarket {}, status 'degraded_timeout'.
formulas.mathIssues: The 'healthy' predicate requires BOTH platforms. Even with the 401 fixed, the Sleeper side alone (382 qualified managers, proven live) would still report population_in_progress unless FFPC also has assets. The workflow conflates 'Sharp works' with 'FFPC works'.

Cross-check frontend/app/market/sharp-tracker/page.jsx:284 which correctly reads market.coverage.unmappedAssets.
