findings.title: Every Sharp diagnostic workflow is structurally incapable of committing its artifact — `git add` on a path that .gitignore excludes
findings.rootCause: .gitignore:45 is a bare `data/` with narrow negations only for `data/ros/`. All four Sharp workflows that are supposed to record production state write to `data/ops/` and stage it with a PLAIN `git add`, not `git add -f` (which is what scheduled-refresh.yml correctly uses for data/scrape_state, data/player_map and data/sleeper_last_good.json). `git add` on an ignored path exits 1, and every one of these steps runs under GitHub's default `bash -e`, so the step aborts.
findings.evidence: `.gitignore:45: data/`. verify-sharp-production.yml:163 `git add data/ops/sharp-production-smoke.json`; force-sharp-production-now.yml:257 `git add data/ops/sharp-force-production-live.json`; trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml:136 `git add data/ops/sharp-no-environment-result.json`; trigger-sharp-now-via-merge.yml:130 `git add data/ops/sharp-merge-trigger-result.json`. `git check-ignore -v data/ops/sharp-production-smoke.json` → `.gitignore:45:data/`. Reproduced in a scratch repo: plain `git add` exit=1, `git add -f` exit=0. `git ls-files data/ops` → 0 files. Live proof from Actions job 91858761506 (2026-08-04T01:20:44Z): `The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: data / hint: Use -f if you really want to add them. / ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.`
findings.userImpact: There is no durable record anywhere of whether Sharp Tracker is populated. The 'Enforce healthy population' gate (verify-sharp-production.yml:167-175) is SKIPPED on every run because the commit step dies first, so the workflow's actual verdict has never once been evaluated. 79 runs, zero successes.
findings.recommendedFix: Change all four to `git add -f -- data/ops/...`, exactly as scheduled-refresh.yml:522 already does. Move the 'Enforce healthy population' step BEFORE the commit step so the verdict is evaluated even if persistence fails.

findings.title: The Sharp production smoke polls auth-gated endpoints anonymously — 80/80 attempts return 401
findings.rootCause: `_private_api_gate` 401s every `/api/*` path not on the public allowlist. `/api/sharp/*` is not on it: `_PUBLIC_API_EXACT` (server.py:2732-2767) lists health/status/uptime/metrics/leagues/rankings-sources/auth-*/scaffold-status/draft-capital/news, and `_PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES` (server.py:2788-2796) is only `/api/public/league` and `/api/league/articles`. verify-sharp-production.yml fetches `https://chaseupside.com/api/sharp/cohort` and `/api/sharp/market` with nothing but a User-Agent header.
findings.evidence: verify-sharp-production.yml:55-64 `fetch_json` sends only `User-Agent` and `Cache-Control`. server.py:2801-2809 `_is_public_api_path` returns False for `/api/sharp/cohort`. Actions job 91858761506 result JSON: `"attempts": 80`, ten recorded errors all `{"message": "HTTP Error 401: Unauthorized", "type": "HTTPError"}` for attempts 71-80, `"status": "degraded_timeout"`, `"cohort": {}`, `"ffpcMarket": {}`.
findings.userImpact: The job burns ~40 minutes of runner time on every push to main and every deploy completion, produces a guaranteed-useless result, and has done so 79 times. Worse: because it always ends in `degraded_timeout` and then dies on the gitignore, a genuine Sharp outage and a healthy Sharp are indistinguishable from CI.
findings.recommendedFix: Either add a bearer-token path to the Sharp endpoints (the pattern already exists — `_SELF_AUTHED_API_EXACT` at server.py:2770-2786 for signal-alerts/custom-alerts) and send it from the workflow, or drop the HTTP probe entirely and read the numbers over SSH the way sharp-records-bootstrap.yml already successfully does.

findings.title: The '<50% of sites' partial-scrape guard degenerates to 'block only on total loss' because `sites` has exactly 2 entries
findings.rootCause: The guard divides by `total_sites`, but `result['sites']` is populated only by the legacy in-scraper SITES dict, which today is KTC + IDPTradeCalc. The ~20 sources fetched by scripts/fetch_*.py in scheduled-refresh.yml never appear there, so their health cannot influence the guard.
findings.evidence: server.py:2362 `if total_sites > 0 and site_count < total_sites / 2:`. Live payload exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json `sites` = `[{"key":"ktc","label":"KTC","max":9999,"playerCount":500},{"key":"idpTradeCalc","label":"IDPTradeCalc","max":9999.0,"playerCount":900}]` — len 2. Reproduced numerically: total_sites=2 → threshold 1.0 → blocks only when site_count == 0; site_count=1 → `1 < 1.0` is False → promoted.
findings.userImpact: KTC is the anchor board for the entire value scale (it is the TE++ basis anchor per CLAUDE.md step 5a, and one of only two _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES). If KTC dies and IDPTradeCalc survives, the scrape publishes anyway — with a board missing its anchor — and the operator gets no 'PARTIAL SCRAPE NOT PROMOTED' email. docs/ops/failure-handling-and-fallbacks.md tells the operator this case is 'Not promoted — blocked by guard'. It is not.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute site_count/total_sites over the full `_SOURCE_CSV_PATHS` registry (or over `siteStats`), not over the 2-entry legacy `sites` array. Separately, keep a hard floor: never promote a board where `ktc` or `ktcSfTep` returned zero rows.

findings.title: The ops 'scrape success rate < 50%' alert can never fire — it reads a key its input never contains
findings.rootCause: `ops_alerts.check_and_alert` is called with `status_payload=_scrape_status_payload()`, but `scrape_success_rate_24h` is produced only inside the `get_status()` HTTP handler, not in `_scrape_status_payload()`. `.get()` returns None and `_check_scrape_rate` returns on its first branch. Even if the key were added, get_status stamps it as a dict and `float(dict)` raises TypeError, which the except clause swallows into another None.
findings.evidence: src/api/ops_alerts.py:45-50 `rate = status_payload.get('scrape_success_rate_24h'); if rate is None: return None; try: r = float(rate) except (TypeError, ValueError): return None`. server.py:11588 `status_payload = _scrape_status_payload()`. server.py:1266-1304 `_scrape_status_payload` returns `dict(scrape_status)` + stall_threshold_sec + run_timeout_sec + status_summary — no rate key; the scrape_status global's key list contains no such key. `grep -n _scrape_success_rate_24h server.py` → only the definition at 1104 and one call at 4207, inside `async def get_status()`. Reproduced: `float({'total':10,'success':2,'failure':8,'rate':0.2})` → TypeError.
findings.userImpact: The headline operator alert for 'the scraper is failing' is dead. Combined with the finding below (blocked partial scrapes are recorded as successes), there is no email path at all that fires on a sustained ingestion failure. Only the CI staleness watchdog would catch it, ~24h later.
findings.recommendedFix: Pass `{**_scrape_status_payload(), 'scrape_success_rate_24h': _scrape_success_rate_24h()}` at server.py:11588, and change `_check_scrape_rate` to read `rate['rate']` when given a dict. Add a unit test that asserts the alert fires for a 0.2 rate.

findings.title: A blocked partial scrape is recorded as a SUCCESS in scrape history
findings.rootCause: The R-3 guard path calls `_mark_scrape_success(...)` before returning the old data, and `_mark_scrape_success` calls `_record_scrape_history('success', ...)` and increments `_metrics['scrape_total']`.
findings.evidence: server.py:2380 `_mark_scrape_success(elapsed, player_count, site_count, total_sites)` inside the `if total_sites > 0 and site_count < total_sites / 2:` block, immediately before `return latest_data  # Return existing data, not the partial result` (server.py:2388). `_mark_scrape_success` (server.py definition) sets `last_success_at`, records `_record_scrape_event('scrape_succeeded', ...)` and `_record_scrape_history('success', ...)`.
findings.userImpact: `scrape_success_rate_24h` reads 100% while every single scrape is being rejected as degraded. health-check.yml:88-89 warns only when `rate < 0.5`, so its warning is suppressed too. The one metric an operator would look at to answer 'is ingestion healthy?' is measuring the wrong event.
findings.recommendedFix: Record `_record_scrape_history('partial', ...)` (or 'blocked') on that path and count it as a non-success in `_scrape_success_rate_24h`. The email alert already fires here, so the only change is the bookkeeping.

findings.title: The Sleeper freshness stamp is written by the scraper and read by nothing
findings.rootCause: `_stamp_sleeper_success` writes `data/scrape_state/sleeper_last_success` explicitly so a Sleeper outage 'still trips the existing freshness watchdog'. But both freshness readers iterate `_SOURCE_CSV_PATHS`, whose 22 keys do not include `sleeper` (Sleeper produces no CSV).
findings.evidence: Dynasty Scraper.py:889-892 docstring: 'Stamp data/scrape_state/sleeper_last_success on a successful live fetch so a prolonged Sleeper outage still trips the existing freshness watchdog even though the scrape no longer hard-fails.' `grep -rn sleeper_last_success` across .py/.yml/.js finds ONLY the writer in Dynasty Scraper.py — zero readers. `python -c 'from src.api.data_contract import _SOURCE_CSV_PATHS; print(sorted(_SOURCE_CSV_PATHS))'` → 22 keys, no 'sleeper'. watchdog_freshness.py:66 `for src_key, entry in _SOURCE_CSV_PATHS.items()`; server.py:1584 the same loop. Live file content: `1785815666.7993538`.
findings.userImpact: A total Sleeper outage is invisible to every monitor. The scraper correctly restores the last-good roster block and correctly refuses to stamp — but nothing consumes the non-stamp, so the board silently serves rosters of arbitrary age labelled as current, with no age field anywhere in the contract, no /api/status entry, and no banner. Trade suggestions, the terminal, angle-finder and draft capital all key off those rosters.
findings.recommendedFix: Either register a virtual `sleeper` entry in the freshness map (a CSV-less source with a 6h threshold), or stamp `sleeperSnapshotAgeHours` onto `meta` in the contract and surface it in the existing stale-source banner. The age is already computed at Dynasty Scraper.py:911 and thrown away.

findings.title: apply_hardening.sh is never invoked by any automation, so the liveness watchdog, uptime probe and state-backup timers are manual-install-only
findings.rootCause: deploy.sh's timer gap-filler globs `${APP_DIR}/deploy/systemd/*.timer.template` only. dynasty-healthcheck.timer, riskit-state-backup.timer and riskit-uptime.timer are NOT `.template` files and live partly outside deploy/systemd/, so they fall outside that glob. Their only installer is apply_hardening.sh, which nothing calls.
findings.evidence: deploy/deploy.sh:690 `for timer_template in "${APP_DIR}"/deploy/systemd/*.timer.template; do`. deploy/apply_hardening.sh:280-289 installs dynasty-healthcheck.timer, riskit-state-backup.timer and riskit-uptime.timer; :307-309 enables them. `grep -rn apply_hardening deploy/ .github/workflows/` returns only documentation strings and the script's own usage banner (`sudo bash deploy/apply_hardening.sh`) — no caller.
findings.userImpact: The three most important safety nets on the box (auto-restart on a wedged process, external uptime probe, second backup) are in the same category as the BDVM timer that deploy.sh:678-682 records as having 'never run once' on the live host. Whether they are installed today is Not Verifiable from Repository, and nothing in CI would notice if they were removed.
findings.recommendedFix: Either extend the gap-filler in deploy.sh to also check the three non-template units, or have deploy.sh invoke apply_hardening.sh in its idempotent no-op mode. Add the three timers to the health-check.yml surface the way backup_health already is.

findings.title: server.py's backup-freshness probe cannot see the second backup system
findings.rootCause: Two independent nightly backup systems exist with different roots and different layouts, and the monitoring probe only globs the first one's root.
findings.evidence: server.py:1646-1648 globs exactly `Path('/var/backups/riskit/daily')` and `Path('/home/dynasty/backups/riskit/daily')` for `*.sqlite.gz`. deploy/backup/riskit-state-backup.sh:65 `BACKUP_ROOT="${BACKUP_ROOT:-/var/backups/riskit-state}"`, :105 `FINAL_DEST="${BACKUP_ROOT}/daily/${DATE_STAMP}"` — a DIRECTORY per date, not `*.sqlite.gz` at the daily/ root. Timers: riskit-backup.timer 02:00 UTC, riskit-state-backup.timer 02:30 UTC.
findings.userImpact: If system A's timer dies while system B keeps working, health-check.yml:168-175 hard-fails with 'No SQLite backups … user_kv, session_store and guest_passes are UNPROTECTED' — a false alarm. If B dies while A works, nobody ever knows. Two systems, one visible, backing up the same three databases 30 minutes apart.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one. If both must stay, teach `_backup_freshness_uncached` about the riskit-state layout and report the two roots separately.

findings.title: src/api/espn_schema_drift.py is dead code with a config file, a test, an architecture-doc entry, and no callers
findings.rootCause: The module was written and never wired into any request path, timer or workflow. Its remediation instructions point at a script that does not exist.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn espn_schema --include=*.py --include=*.yml --include=*.json .` finds: the module itself, config/espn_schema_baseline.json, tests/api/test_espn_schema_drift.py, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:69, and docs/competitor-gap-analysis.md:179 which already lists it under 'No callers'. src/api/espn_schema_drift.py:166 emits `python3 scripts/update_espn_schema_baseline.py`; `ls scripts/update_espn_schema_baseline.py` → No such file or directory.
findings.userImpact: ESPN endpoint drift is unmonitored despite a config file and an ARCHITECTURE.md entry implying otherwise. An operator reading the docs would believe this is covered.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete it, or wire `run_drift_check` into the daily signal-alerts sweep alongside ops_alerts and source_health_alerts (the piggyback pattern is already established at server.py:11578-11630) and write the missing baseline-update script.

findings.title: ops_alerts.py's docstring advertises two checks that do not exist
findings.rootCause: The module docstring was written against a wider design than was implemented.
findings.evidence: src/api/ops_alerts.py:6-10 lists five conditions including 'Signal-alert cron hasn't run in > 36h (expected every 12h)' and 'Session-store SQLite integrity check fails'. `check_and_alert` (:207-244) calls exactly four helpers: `_check_scrape_rate`, `_check_circuit_breakers`, `_check_contract_health`, `_check_data_freshness`. There is no cron-liveness helper and no SQLite helper anywhere in the file.
findings.userImpact: Nothing detects that the signal-alert sweep itself has stopped — which would silently disable ops alerts, source-staleness alerts, BDVM alerts and news-event ingestion all at once, since all four piggyback on it (server.py:11578-11630). The docstring's '(expected every 12h)' also contradicts the actual timer, which is daily at 15:00 UTC (dynasty-signal-alerts.timer.template).
findings.recommendedFix: Implement the cron-liveness check (it is the highest-value missing alert in the system — one timer failing takes out four alerting subsystems), or delete the two lines from the docstring.

findings.title: startup_validation's `fatal` flag is never acted on
findings.rootCause: The module documents that the caller decides whether to exit on a fatal check; the caller stores the summary and boots regardless.
findings.evidence: src/api/startup_validation.py:14-16 'Fatal conditions are separately signalled via ``CheckResult.fatal = True`` so the caller can decide to exit.' server.py:2577-2591 is the only caller: it assigns `_startup_checks_summary = _sv.summary(_startup_checks)` and continues into step 1. `grep -n 'fatal' server.py` returns only the literal dict keys at :715, :2590 and the /api/status passthrough at :4506 — no branch. Additionally both env checks pass `required=False` (:159-160), so `check_env_var` can never set fatal, leaving only a league-registry load exception (:141-147).
findings.userImpact: Low in practice — degraded boot is the right default for this app — but the documented contract is not the implemented one, and `startupChecks.fatal` on /api/status is a number no consumer reacts to.
findings.recommendedFix: Either delete the sentence and the `fatal` field, or have the lifespan log at CRITICAL and set a flag that makes /api/health return 503 while fatal > 0.

findings.title: docs/ops/* and docs/automation-audit.md describe an automation topology that no longer exists
findings.rootCause: Four ops documents dated 2026-03-14 and 2026-04-25 were never revised as the platform moved to 21 workflows plus a dozen systemd timers.
findings.evidence: docs/ops/current-automation-state.md: 'There is no external cron, no systemd timer for scraping' — contradicted by scheduled-refresh.yml (cron 42 */2, 1049 runs) and deploy/systemd/dynasty-{dlf,idpshow}-fetch.timer; 'no nginx/caddy config in repo' (§9.6) — contradicted by deploy/nginx/{chaseupside.com,chaseupside-proxy,riskittogetthebrisket.org}.conf; §2.2 lists Jenkins stages 'Ingest via scripts/source_pull.py', 'Canonical Build', 'League Refresh', 'Publish Report' — none of which are in the Jenkinsfile (its stages are Checkout, Git Info, Validate, Identity Resolve, Backend Smoke, API Contract Check, Frontend Build, Regression Harness). docs/ops/schedules-and-cadence.md:15 'Every 6 hours Jenkins canonical pipeline (Jenkinsfile cron)' and its table entry `H H/6 * * *` — the Jenkinsfile has NO `triggers` block at all; its only `options` are timestamps() and disableConcurrentBuilds(). docs/automation-audit.md:47-58 states the cron is `42 */3 * * *` (it is `42 */2`), lists FootballGuys as a live fetched source (scheduled-refresh.yml:275 has an orphan FootballGuys comment block with NO command following it, and footballGuys is absent from `_RANKING_SOURCES`), and states fetch_dynasty_nerds.py / fetch_yahoo_boone.py / fetch_fantasypros_offense.py / fetch_fantasypros_idp.py are 'NOT wired to any workflow' — all four are now wired at scheduled-refresh.yml:339-341 and :350.
findings.userImpact: An operator planning a response to an incident from these documents would look for a Jenkins cron that does not run, would believe a partial scrape is blocked when it is not, and would not know that 21 GitHub workflows and 12 systemd timers exist.
findings.recommendedFix: Regenerate docs/ops/current-automation-state.md and schedules-and-cadence.md from the actual workflow and timer inventory, and stamp them with the commit they were generated at so future drift is detectable.

findings.title: Nineteen orphaned one-off workflows remain registered and active in GitHub Actions after being deleted from the repository
findings.rootCause: Each debugging attempt on 2026-07-31 shipped a new `on: push` workflow file to main; the files were later removed from the tree but GitHub retains the workflow registration.
findings.evidence: GitHub Actions API `list_workflows` reports total_count 42; `ls .github/workflows/` in the tree at 9c5d972 shows 21 files. The extras, all created 2026-07-31T06:54 → 2026-08-01T08:55 EDT except one from 2026-08-03: materialize-ffpc-implementation, format-unified-ffpc-branch, materialize-sharp-production, trigger-sharp-materializer, format-ffpc-config-test, pr-live-sharp-repair, pr-live-sharp-route-probe, autoformat-sharp-681, patch-sharp-records-client-681, patch-ledger-lock-safety, pr-recover-sharp-ledger-production, patch-sharp-explicit-route-registration, verify-sharp-route-hotfix-pr, patch-sharp-explicit-startup-registration, materialize-sharp-public-api-access, verify-sharp-422-fix, materialize-curated-industry-sharps, materialize-sharp-hide-picks, faab-freshness-hotfix. Several of the surviving five are `on: push` filtered to their OWN path (force-sharp-production-now.yml:4-7, trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml:4-7, trigger-sharp-now-via-merge.yml:4-7), which is the mechanism that made 'edit the file to re-run it' work.
findings.userImpact: Any of these can be re-armed by resurrecting its file. Three of them SSH into production with sudo and run `git reset --hard origin/main` + `systemctl restart` (trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml:78-87, trigger-sharp-now-via-merge.yml:53-63, force-sharp-production-now.yml:61-75). trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml deliberately has no `environment: production` gate, so it uses repository-level secrets with no approval step.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the five surviving one-offs from the tree and disable the 19 orphans in the Actions UI. Replace the whole family with one `workflow_dispatch`-only 'production maintenance' workflow that takes an action name as an input.

findings.title: `verify-sharp-production.yml` reads `dataQuality.unmappedAssets`, which the market payload does not emit
findings.rootCause: Field-name drift between the workflow's expectation and src/sharp/market.py's actual shape, masked by an `or {}` guard.
findings.evidence: verify-sharp-production.yml:117-119 `"unmappedAssets": (market.get("dataQuality") or {}).get("unmappedAssets", 0)`. Executing `market_payload(...)` in this audit returned top-level keys `['status','generatedAt','methodologyVersion','query','assets','cohort','coverage','formula']` — no `dataQuality` at all — and `dataQuality` printed as `null`. The real field is `coverage.unmappedAssets`, which frontend/app/market/sharp-tracker/page.jsx:284 reads correctly.
findings.userImpact: The smoke's unmappedAssets reading is a hardcoded 0 rather than an error. Minor today because the whole job never completes, but it would silently under-report FFPC mapping gaps if the 401 and gitignore issues were fixed.
findings.recommendedFix: Read `(market.get('coverage') or {}).get('unmappedAssets', 0)`.

findings.title: The Refit Hill Curves audit trail has no entry since 2026-07-28, and 6 of its 13 scheduled runs failed
findings.rootCause: Not determined from the repository. The workflow itself declares that a missing weekly entry IS the failure signal.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/refit-hill-curves.yml:135-140 'The registry is the audit trail: a dated entry every time the gate runs, whatever the verdict… a MISSING weekly entry is itself the signal that this workflow stopped running.' scripts/auto_refit_hill_curves.py:279-296 appends a version on every non-dry-run with exit code != 2. GitHub Actions API: 20 runs total; scheduled runs on 2026-06-16, 06-30, 07-07, 07-14 and 07-21 all conclusion=failure; the last run of any kind is #20 on 2026-07-28T09:06:48Z (success). config/model_registry/hill_scope_masters.json contains only v1 (retired) and v2 (champion, fittedAt 2026-07-28T09:08:00Z, producer 'scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py @ 3df9cc4', promoted by hand 2026-07-29T23:35:35Z) — no v3. The 2026-08-04 06:17 UTC fire had not appeared as of 08:33 UTC.
findings.userImpact: The Hill percentile masters are step 3 of the live value pipeline — they convert every player's percentile into their displayed value. The mechanism that is supposed to detect drift in them weekly has produced no evidence of running in a week, and failed roughly half the time before that. The champion constants in production are from a 2026-07-28 fit.
findings.recommendedFix: Pull the logs for the five failed scheduled runs (29815628107, 29318161638, 28857908803, 28436256895, 27614678772) and fix the recurring cause; the driver already distinguishes exit 2 (error) from exit 1 (promotable) so the failure mode should be readable from the job summary. Add a staleness assertion: fail if the newest registry entry is older than 10 days.

findings.title: Weekly Matchup Narratives has failed 24 of 26 runs and its two 'successes' are the skip path
findings.rootCause: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was never configured; the workflow was later changed to turn the missing secret into a green skip instead of a red run.
findings.evidence: GitHub Actions API: 26 runs, 24 failure / 2 success (2026-07-28T16:06:51Z and 2026-07-29T15:09:41Z). .github/workflows/weekly-narratives.yml:80-96 comment 'When the secret is absent/empty every weekly run fails with "ERROR: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set" (8 straight failures as of 2026-07-25) … surface it as a loud skip instead of a red run', with every subsequent step gated on `steps.keycheck.outputs.have_key == 'true'`. Only artifacts in the tree: exports/narratives/2025/week-17/preview-1.json (generatedAt 2025-12-24T13:00:00+00:00) and recap-1.json (2025-12-30T14:00:00+00:00), model claude-opus-4-7, one matchup each.
findings.userImpact: Low — it is August, there are no matchups. But /league/articles has served the same two December-2025 articles for eight months and the workflow now reports green while producing nothing, so the condition will not be noticed before the season starts.
findings.recommendedFix: Set the secret, or gate the crons on the NFL season so the workflow is genuinely dormant rather than skipping-and-passing.

findings.title: The Sharp Sleeper crawler exhausts its call budget on every pass and never completes
findings.rootCause: A fixed per-run request budget against a 250-member selection that needs more calls than the budget allows.
findings.evidence: Actions job 91858718467 (2026-08-04T01:20:50Z) prod journal, two consecutive dynasty-sharp-activity.service runs: 2026-08-03T23:14:10Z and 2026-08-04T01:20:36Z, both `"status": "success"` but both `"budgetExhausted": true, "completed": false, "callsUsed": 2499`, `"memberCount": 250`, movementsSeen 3485→170 inserted and 3691→206 inserted. Coverage moved transactions 2339→2400 and movements 3894→4100 while managers stayed 16,001 and leagues 6,880.
findings.userImpact: 382 'qualified managers' are qualified on partial evidence — whichever subset of the member list the budget reached before running out. The systemd unit reports success, so nothing surfaces the incompleteness. Any Sharp market signal shown to a user is computed over an unmeasured sample.
findings.recommendedFix: Persist a resume cursor so successive passes cover the whole member list, and stamp `completed`/`callsUsed` into the /api/sharp/cohort payload so the incompleteness is visible where the numbers are read.

findings.title: Dangling FootballGuys comment block in scheduled-refresh.yml with no fetcher, and orphan stamps in data/scrape_state
findings.rootCause: The FootballGuys fetcher was removed but its comment header and its stale stamps were left behind.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml:275-278 is a four-line 'Fetch FootballGuys league-synced rankings (offense + IDP)' comment followed directly by the DraftSharks comment at :280 — no `run_fetcher` call. `data/scrape_state/footballGuys{,Sf,Idp}_last_success` all contain 1779666437 = 2026-05-24T23:47:17Z, 1712 hours (71 days) stale. `grep -n footballGuys src/api/data_contract.py` returns only literal strings inside coverage-gap annotations; footballGuys is absent from `_RANKING_SOURCES` and from `_SOURCE_CSV_PATHS` (22 keys, verified), so the watchdog never checks them.
findings.userImpact: None functionally — the source is fully retired and correctly deregistered. But a reader of the workflow sees a comment implying a fetcher runs, and `ls data/scrape_state/` shows three sources 71 days stale, which is a false alarm during an incident.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the comment block and the three orphan stamp files.

findings.title: `dynasty-custom-alerts.timer` says 'Hourly' and fires every two hours
findings.rootCause: Description not updated when the OnCalendar was changed.
findings.evidence: deploy/systemd/dynasty-custom-alerts.timer.template: `Description=Hourly custom-alert sweep for __SERVICE_NAME__` immediately above `OnCalendar=*-*-* 0/2:13:00 UTC`.
findings.userImpact: `systemctl list-timers` shows a description that contradicts the schedule. Trivial, but it is the line an operator reads first when triaging alert latency.

findings.title: The FFPC Sharp timer ships twice, from two directories, with identical schedules
findings.rootCause: A second copy under deploy/ffpc-systemd/ was added alongside the deploy/systemd/ one and neither was removed.
findings.evidence: deploy/systemd/dynasty-ffpc-sharp.timer.template and deploy/ffpc-systemd/chase-upside-ffpc-sharp.timer.template both contain `Description=Daily FFPC public Sharp ingestion for __SERVICE_NAME__`, `OnCalendar=*-*-* 05:20:00 UTC`, `RandomizedDelaySec=900`, `Persistent=true`. deploy/deploy.sh:690's gap-filler globs only deploy/systemd/*.timer.template, so the ffpc-systemd copy is installed only by deploy/install-ffpc-sharp-service.sh, which the trigger workflows call directly.
findings.userImpact: Two installers can render two unit names for the same job. If both are ever enabled the FFPC crawl runs twice at 05:20 against myffpc.com with a 100-request budget each.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete deploy/ffpc-systemd/ and have install-ffpc-sharp-service.sh render from deploy/systemd/.

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Read-only. No file in /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket was created, modified or deleted; the only writes were to a scratch git repo under the sandbox scratchpad, used to empirically reproduce git's behavior on a gitignored path. Commit 9c5d972, branch claude/decision-intelligence-audit-wif47g, audit clock 2026-08-04T08:32Z.

A HARD LIMIT ON GIT EVIDENCE. The working copy is a SHALLOW clone: `.git/shallow` exists, `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → true, `git rev-list --count HEAD` → 51, oldest reachable commit 2026-08-03T03:07:44. That is roughly 27 hours of history. Every "git log of the artifacts it writes" conclusion below is therefore bounded to 2026-08-03/04 unless I supplemented it. I did supplement it: the GitHub Actions API (read-only) gave real run histories, conclusions and job logs, which is where most of the decisive evidence in this report comes from. Where I could not get that, I have written "Not Verified" or "Not Verifiable from Repository" rather than inferring.

A SECOND HARD LIMIT. `.gitignore:45` is a bare `data/`. Every production-side artifact of the Sharp tracker (`data/intel/`), BDVM (`data/bdvm/`), player context (`data/playerctx/`) and the ops diagnostics (`data/ops/`) is structurally invisible to this repository. None of those directories exists in the working tree. For those subsystems the repo can only tell you what is *configured*; it can never tell you what *ran*. That is not an incidental gitignore rule — it is the reason the Sharp verification apparatus was built, and the reason it does not work.

WHAT I DID NOT COVER. Run histories for prod-e2e-smoke, public-league-warmup, smoke-test, e2e, intel-refresh, deploy and the three audit-* workflows were not retrieved (the Actions API responses exceed the tool's size limit and each one costs a separate paged fetch). They are marked "configured for deployment" rather than "confirmed operational" for exactly that reason — not because I found anything wrong with them. Their trigger wiring, failure handling and rolling-issue plumbing I did read in full and it is sound.

THE FIVE SHARP WORKFLOWS — WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED. The five named in the task are the surviving visible fragment of a much larger event. The GitHub Actions API reports 42 registered workflows against 21 files in the tree. Nineteen of the extras were created between 2026-07-31T06:54 and 2026-08-01T08:55 EDT and every one is Sharp-related. Read in creation order, their names are a debugging transcript:

  06:54 sharp-records-bootstrap  →  08:25 materialize-ffpc-implementation  →  17:24 materialize-sharp-production
  →  17:26 trigger-sharp-materializer  →  18:06 verify-sharp-production
  →  19:45 force-sharp-production-now      (environment: production; ran once, FAILED)
  →  19:50 check-sharp-production-now      (workflow_dispatch; read-only, writes nothing)
  →  19:53 trigger-sharp-now-via-merge     (environment: production, merge-triggered; ran once, FAILED after 33s)
  →  19:58 trigger-sharp-no-environment    (environment gate REMOVED; ran once, FAILED after 61s)
  →  20:02 pr-live-sharp-repair  →  20:04 pr-live-sharp-route-probe
  →  21:53 patch-sharp-explicit-route-registration  →  22:21 patch-sharp-explicit-startup-registration
  →  23:19 materialize-sharp-public-api-access  →  23:55 verify-sharp-422-fix

The operational problem that produced them is visible in that sequence and confirmed in the code. The operator had exactly one way to execute a command on the production box — push a workflow file to main — and each attempt hit a different gate. `force-sharp-production-now` and `trigger-sharp-now-via-merge` both declare `environment: production`, which requires the environment's secrets and any approval rule attached to it; `trigger-sharp-no-environment.yml` drops that key entirely and opens by probing whether repository-level DEPLOY_* secrets even exist (lines 40-64) — that is somebody eliminating a hypothesis. Meanwhile the endpoint being probed was moving under them: `/api/sharp/market` is not an `@app.get` at all, it is injected at import time by `src/sharp/service.py::_register_http_routes` via a `sys.modules['server'] or sys.modules['__main__']` lookup, and that function's own docstrings record two production failures — the `__main__` case "silently skipped the market route registration while the explicitly declared cohort endpoint continued to work" (:151-158) and a function-local `Request` import that "made FastAPI treat `request` as a required query parameter and return 422 for every real market request" (:174-178). Hence `patch-sharp-explicit-route-registration`, then `patch-sharp-explicit-startup-registration`, then `verify-sharp-422-fix`. The pattern is not carelessness; it is a person with no interactive access to production, debugging a route-registration bug through a 5-minute CI round trip, leaving one workflow behind per hypothesis.

IS THE SHARP PIPELINE PRODUCING DATA TODAY? Yes on the Sleeper side, and I can prove it — but not from anything the project built to prove it. The proof is a journal excerpt that leaked into the `Bootstrap Sharp Records` job log (Actions job 91858718467, run #45, 2026-08-04T00:39Z, conclusion success). As of 2026-08-04T01:20:36Z production holds 16,001 observed managers across 6,880 leagues, 11,777 evidence managers, 7,480 manager records, 2,021 evaluable and 382 qualified managers, 2,400 transactions and 4,100 movements in the ledger; `dynasty-sharp-activity.service` completed two passes (23:14:10Z and 01:20:36Z) inserting 170 and 206 movements; the script's closing line is "[sharp-bootstrap] Sharp Tracker is populated with 382 qualified manager(s) and their Sleeper activity." The FFPC half is Not Verifiable from Repository, and that is precisely what `verify-sharp-production.yml` exists to check.

That workflow has run 79 times and succeeded zero times, and it never will in its current form, because of two independent structural blockers. First, it polls `https://chaseupside.com/api/sharp/cohort` and `/api/sharp/market` with no credentials, and `/api/sharp/*` is not on the public allowlist (`_PUBLIC_API_EXACT` / `_PUBLIC_API_PREFIXES`, server.py:2732-2796) — the 2026-08-04T00:40 run logged `HTTP Error 401: Unauthorized` on all 80 attempts across 40 minutes and ended `degraded_timeout` with empty `cohort` and `ffpcMarket`. Second, its next step stages `data/ops/sharp-production-smoke.json` with a plain `git add` against a `.gitignore` that excludes `data/`, so it dies with exit 1 and the `Enforce healthy population` step — the one that would actually render a verdict — is skipped every single time. Note the irony of the sequencing: the run that produced hard proof of a live Sharp cohort (`sharp-records-bootstrap`, run #45) and the run that concluded Sharp is `degraded_timeout` (`verify-sharp-production`, run #79) were triggered by the SAME deploy completion, seconds apart, on 2026-08-04T00:39.

WHAT HAPPENS ON A FAILED REFRESH. The design is genuinely good and the implementation is mostly faithful to it, with two holes.
  • Total scrape failure or timeout → `latest_data` is not reassigned, the server keeps serving the last successful board, an email fires. Correct.
  • Sleeper outage → `data/sleeper_last_good.json` is restored and success is deliberately NOT stamped (Dynasty Scraper.py:1660-1680). A *partial* Sleeper fetch — rosters returned but the league endpoint didn't, so `rosterPositions` is empty — is explicitly refused as a last-good candidate and only the lineup slots are spliced in from cache. That is a subtle failure mode handled with real care. The hole is downstream: the computed snapshot age is printed to a console nobody reads and never enters the contract, and the `sleeper_last_success` stamp it deliberately withholds is read by nothing at all (22-key `_SOURCE_CSV_PATHS` has no `sleeper` entry). So the answer to your question is: **stale rosters, labelled as current, with no age anywhere in the payload and no monitor watching.**
  • Sleeper `/players/nfl` outage → `data/player_map/team_map_last_good.json` supplies team/age/yearsExp so the frontend's fail-closed filters don't empty the board. Live artifact, `generated_at` 2026-08-04T03:56:40Z. Correct, and the dual `teams`/`players` key layout is deliberately backward-compatible across the change that introduced it.
  • Partial scrape → the documented "<50% of sites, blocked from promotion" guard is real code (server.py:2362) operating on a two-element array. Threshold 1.0. It blocks only at total loss. And the blocked path records a *success* in scrape history.
  • Never: zeros. I found no path that publishes zeros or fabricated values. The one place that could have — `_pick_value_from_contract`'s hardcoded 7000/4000/2000/1200 round table — is already documented in CLAUDE.md as removed and replaced with a 503.

MONITORING VS ALERTING, HONESTLY. Monitored *and* alerting: source staleness (CI watchdog red X + rolling `stale-sources` issue + email), identity collisions (rolling issue), rank-form drift (issue), E2E journeys (rolling issue), intel refresh (rolling issue). Monitored, alerting only if prod env vars happen to be set: contract health, circuit breakers, data age, per-source email alerts, uptime. Monitored with no alert channel at all: Hampel drop rates (audit-dropped-sources opens no issue — a red X on a Monday cron nobody is watching). Claimed but dead: scrape success rate (`_check_scrape_rate` can never fire), ESPN schema drift (zero callers), signal-alert cron liveness (advertised in a docstring, never implemented). Not monitored: FFPC ingestion, BDVM snapshot freshness, playerctx freshness, the second backup system, whether the daily signal-alerts sweep — on which four alerting subsystems piggyback — ran at all.

THE ONE THING I'D FIX FIRST. Not the Sharp workflows. `git add -f` is a one-character fix and Sharp is a side feature. The urgent pair is the partial-scrape guard reading a 2-element array and `_check_scrape_rate` reading a key that does not exist. Together they mean: KTC can die, the board can ship without its anchor, the success rate can read 100%, and no email is sent. Those are the numbers that decide trades.

formulas.name: Hill percentile -> value (OFFENSE master)
formulas.inputs: blended percentile position within a fixed 500-rank reference pool
formulas.constants: HILL_PERCENTILE_C=0.1100, HILL_PERCENTILE_S=1.110 (player_valuation.py:126-127); GLOBAL 0.1120/0.725 (:118-119); IDP 0.0830/1.110 (:133-134); ROOKIE 0.1530/0.885 (:158-159, fit-only, `routed: False`); _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N=500 (data_contract.py:4933). ALL EIGHT are literally pinned in tests/canonical/test_hill_percentile_constants_tripwire.py:_PINNED, and the tripwire ALSO cross-checks the registry's regex reader (`hill_masters.read_committed_constants`) against the Python values.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: p is clamped to [0,1]; ranks past 500 all collapse to the same tail value. Verified: I drove 560 synthetic rows through the pipeline and rows at rank 510 and 559 receive identical `_blendedValueUncapped`, exactly as test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py::test_pipeline_flattens_every_rank_past_the_reference asserts.
formulas.mathIssues: none found
formulas.validated: YES — I executed percentile_to_value at 10 ranks and got 1:9999, 5:9481, 12:8561, 24:7242, 50:5314, 100:3419, 150:2481, 200:1931, 300:1322, 400:996, matching _PINNED_OFFENSE_VALUES exactly.

formulas.name: Count-aware mean-median blend
formulas.expression: n==1 -> passthrough, MAD None; n==2 -> mean, MAD = half-range; n in {3,4} -> (mean + median)/2, MAD = mean(|v-mean|); n>=5 -> drop one max + one min, then (trimmed mean + trimmed median)/2
formulas.inputs: list of per-source normalized 0-9999 votes
formulas.constants: the 1/2/3-4/5 breakpoints — pinned only by test case structure, not by a named constant
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty list -> (0.0, None). Pinned at test_count_aware_blend.py:38-40.
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: YES — hard-gated, fully numeric, with worked arithmetic in comments and explicit OLD-RULE contrast cases (`center == 4000` under the untrimmed rule vs 3000 under the retired trimmed rule, :74-81). This is the model the rest of the repo should follow.

formulas.name: Single-source haircut
formulas.expression: if row is not a pick and rests on exactly one post-Hampel source: rankDerivedValue = int(blend * 0.30); _blendedValueUncapped = int(round(blend * 0.30))
formulas.inputs: blended value, post-Hampel source count, assetClass
formulas.constants: _SINGLE_SOURCE_VALUE_RETENTION = 0.30 — literally pinned at tests/api/test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py:91. Also hardcoded as prose '0.30' in src/trade/finder.py:72 and :423, where it is NOT pinned.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: a row with one source keeps 30%; a row with zero priced sources is excluded from ranking entirely (test_data_contract.py::test_zero_ktc_excluded).
formulas.mathIssues: note the deliberate asymmetry: rankDerivedValue truncates, _blendedValueUncapped rounds. Both are pinned.
formulas.validated: YES — I executed it: Solo Guy (ktcSfTep=5000 only) -> 1500, singleSourceValuePenaltyApplied True; Duo Guy (5000+5000) -> 5000, no flag.

formulas.name: Hierarchical anchor + alpha shrinkage
formulas.expression: IDP and picks: center = anchor + 0.10 * (subgroup_center - anchor). Offense: center = count_aware_mean_median(all_values), alphaShrinkage stamped 0.0
formulas.inputs: cross-market anchor value, subgroup blend value, assetClass
formulas.constants: _ALPHA_SHRINKAGE = 0.10 — literally pinned at test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py:154
formulas.missingDataBehavior: offense rows stamp alphaShrinkage 0.0 rather than omitting it, so 'not shrunk' and 'field missing' are distinguishable.
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: YES — I executed a 3-row fixture and confirmed alphaShrinkage stamps 0.0 on offense. The IDP branch is pinned by reconstructing the stamped value from stamped diagnostics (`anchor + 0.10*delta` within abs=1), which is partly circular but is backstopped by the independent assertion that the subgroup is pulled >50% of the way back to the anchor (:167-169).

formulas.name: Value-direct source voting
formulas.expression: contribution = raw / site_max * 9999 for ktcSfTep and idpTradeCalc only; every other source votes rank -> percentile -> Hill
formulas.inputs: raw site value, that site's observed max in the pool
formulas.constants: _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES = frozenset({'ktcSfTep','idpTradeCalc'}) — pinned as an exact set equality at test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py:216
formulas.missingDataBehavior: a source absent for a row simply does not vote; there is no zero-fill. Pinned by test_golden_dataset_invariants.py::test_zero_and_negative_source_values_do_not_become_real_votes.
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: YES — the linearity consequence is asserted with real numbers (5000 -> 1500, 2500 -> 750 under the haircut) AND contrasted against the rank path, which must NOT be linear.

formulas.name: Multiplicative future-year pick discount
formulas.expression: pick value *= factor(year_offset); offset 0 -> 1.00, offset 1 -> 0.82, offset 2 -> 0.66
formulas.inputs: pick name year vs current_rookie_draft_year()
formulas.constants: 0.82 and 0.66 are literally pinned at test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py:395-397 and :414
formulas.missingDataBehavior: offset 0 leaves the row untouched and stamps NO pickYearDiscount key at all (pinned :400-408); a player row whose name starts with a future year is never discounted (gated on assetClass=='pick', pinned :417-428).
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: YES — I executed it. current_rookie_draft_year() returns 2027 as of 2026-08-04, and 2027/2028/2029 Pick 1.01 at identical 7000 votes produce 7000 / 5740 / 4620. Note CLAUDE.md's pipeline prose still talks about '2026 picks'.

formulas.name: Market corridor clamp (IDP only)
formulas.expression: IDP rows only: clamp the blended value into a P90 drift band around the market anchor, hard-capped at band 0.15
formulas.inputs: blended value, anchor market value, confidence bucket
formulas.constants: _MARKET_CORRIDOR_MAX_BAND_BY_ASSET_CLASS['idp'] = 0.15 — literally pinned at test_market_corridor_clamp.py:531, AND the absence of an 'offense' key is pinned at :536
formulas.missingDataBehavior: a row with no resolvable anchor source is left unclamped.
formulas.mathIssues: The clamp's own source comments still justify it as containing 'the IDP calibration runaway', a mechanism that no longer exists — CLAUDE.md itself flags this rationale as stale. The clamp still does real work.
formulas.validated: YES — 31 tests, all passing in my environment (`Ran 31 tests ... OK`), with exact pins on clamped outputs (1500 -> 4500 up, -> 5500 down) and on the anchor-source preference order.

formulas.name: FAAB base bid
formulas.expression: share = value / max(value, top_value_in_pool); aggressive = max(1, round(budget * (0.05 + 0.25*share))); reasonable = max(1, round(aggressive*0.70)); lowball = max(1, round(aggressive*0.35))
formulas.inputs: candidate board value, pool top value, user's remaining FAAB
formulas.constants: 0.05 floor, 0.25 band, 0.70, 0.35 — pinned only through worked examples (30/21/10, 18, 15, 12), not as named constants
formulas.missingDataBehavior: value<=0 or budget<=0 -> (0,0,0) — an explicit triple-zero, not a crash and not a 1. Pinned at test_waiver.py:209-211. Missing user FAAB falls back to a 100 budget (pinned).
formulas.mathIssues: lowball uses banker's rounding (30*0.35=10.5 -> 10); the test acknowledges this and asserts `low == round(30*0.35)` rather than a literal, which is the one place it dodges.
formulas.validated: YES — worked examples are exact and cover the budget-scaling axis.

formulas.name: KTC Value Adjustment port
formulas.expression: port of KTC.com's proprietary package-VA algorithm
formulas.inputs: two lists of KTC player values
formulas.outputRange: KTC points, suppressed below a threshold
formulas.constants: KTC_MAX_PLAYER_VAL 10000, KTC_T_REFERENCE 10041, KTC_VARIANCE_PCT 5 — all in src/trade/ktc_va.py, none referenced by any test
formulas.missingDataBehavior: result.displayed False -> the caller treats the VA as 0.
formulas.mathIssues: none detectable — measured against the real site
formulas.validated: YES, EXTERNALLY. I ran the 139-observation fixture: RMS 26.59 against the bound of 50. Recipient-side selection and suppression are asserted at 100% agreement.

formulas.name: Exact league scoring
formulas.expression: sum over 141 scoring keys of stat_value * rate, using the league's own settings blob
formulas.inputs: raw nflverse/Sleeper stat line + config/leagues scoring settings
formulas.constants: 141 scoring keys, asserted as a count at tests/league_intel/test_config.py (`len(cfg.scoring_settings) == 141`) and the league id pinned literally
formulas.missingDataBehavior: a stat key absent from the line contributes nothing; a scoring key absent from settings contributes nothing. The negative-control test at test_golden_scoring.py:90 asserts that deleting a scoring key CHANGES the answer, which is what stops silent zero-fill from passing.
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: YES, EXTERNALLY. 16 archetype player-weeks vs Sleeper's own awarded points — I ran them, 0 failures at abs tolerance 0.011. Two full team-weeks match Sleeper's awarded team total.

formulas.name: BDVM trade value (per strategy currency)
formulas.expression: CES-composed surplus over dynamic replacement, discounted by survival/risk, scaled per strategy profile (contender/balanced/rebuilder/risk-neutral)
formulas.inputs: projected FPG, age, games, sigma, archetype, career load, kappa, RiskProfile, positional pool
formulas.constants: content-hashed paramSetId over config/bdvm/params_v1.json; the config's own comment calls these 'priors, not validated truth'
formulas.missingDataBehavior: a player without a projection or age is returned `unpriced` WITH A REASON rather than imputed — this is the repo's best missing-data discipline and it is test-pinned in tests/bdvm/test_service.py.
formulas.mathIssues: none found
formulas.validated: YES, EXTERNALLY. 13 archetypes' (contender, balanced, rebuilder) triples, 7 replacement levels (QB 12.40 ... DB 6.17), 7 startable-slot counts and 4 probability rows all reproduce the published Appendix C. `Ran 7 tests ... OK` in my environment.

formulas.name: Trade suggestion rank score
formulas.expression: score = min(give_total, receive_total)/1000 + fairness_bonus + confidence_bonus + need_severity + edge_bonus + (1.5 if opponent_fit) - 1.0*count(receive at surplus position)
formulas.inputs: suggestion totals, fairness label, confidence label, roster analysis
formulas.constants: _FAIRNESS_RANK_BONUS, _CONFIDENCE_RANK_BONUS, _EDGE_RANK_BONUS dicts + literals 2.0/1.0 need severity, 1.5 opp fit, 1.0 overflow — NONE of these is pinned by any test
formulas.missingDataBehavior: roster=None silently zeroes need_severity AND overflow_penalty. tests/test_trade_suggestions.py::test_breakdown_sums_to_total (:750) sums only six of the seven components and passes roster=None, so the overflow term is never exercised in that test.
formulas.mathIssues: Not a bug, but the ranking is a hand-tuned linear sum with no validation of any kind. Every test is a strict inequality between two hand-built suggestions.
formulas.validated: NO — ordinal only. Doubling any bonus weight leaves the suite green.

formulas.name: Sharp Score composite
formulas.expression: performance = sum(w_i * percentile_i)/sum(w_i) over {winPct .30, playoffRate .25, championshipRate .20, medianFinishPercentile .15, pointsForPercentile .10}; roster quality and consistency composed similarly; clamped to [0,1]
formulas.inputs: manager record across dynasty leagues, league population percentiles
formulas.constants: every weight above lives in config/sharp/scoring_v2.json with defaults duplicated in code (`float(sub.get('winPct', 0.30))`). None is pinned by a test. Gates minCompletedSeasons 2, minDynastyLeagues 2, minLeagueAgeSeasons 2, minCompletedGames 24, minWinPct 0.52, maxAbandonedRosterRate 0.34 — only asserted through eligibility-reason strings, not values.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: missing sub-metrics drop out of the weighted mean (total_w shrinks), so a manager with one observed metric is scored on that metric alone at full weight — this rescaling is not tested.
formulas.mathIssues: The code duplicates every config default as an inline literal, so a config edit that misspells a key silently falls back to the old weight with no error. Nothing tests config/code agreement for this file (contrast tests/api/test_config_parity.py which does exactly that for other configs).
formulas.validated: NO. Config comment: 'Weights are PRIORS chosen for defensibility, not values validated against an outcome dataset.'

formulas.name: Playoff odds Monte Carlo
formulas.expression: simulate remaining weeks by sampling each owner's weekly score from their own sampled distribution (or the league pool when below MIN_SAMPLED_WEEKS), count playoff qualifications / DEFAULT_SIMS
formulas.inputs: posted/inferred schedule, per-owner weekly scores, playoff spots
formulas.constants: DEFAULT_SIMS, DEFAULT_PLAYOFF_SPOTS 6, MIN_SAMPLED_WEEKS, DEFAULT_PLAYOFF_WEEK_START 15 — asserted only as `>= 1000`, `>= 1`, `>= 1` at test_playoff_odds.py:118-120
formulas.missingDataBehavior: preseason returns playoffProbability None (NOT 0.0) for every owner and numSims 0 — correctly distinguished and pinned at :405-412. Below MIN_SAMPLED_WEEKS an owner falls back to the league-wide pool.
formulas.mathIssues: none found in the plumbing
formulas.validated: NO. In 756 lines of tests the probability is only bounded [0,1], forced to {0,1} once the season is final, and required deterministic under a seeded RNG. There is no case with an analytically known answer (e.g. two identical teams -> 0.5).

formulas.name: Trade finder confidence + arbitrage edge
formulas.expression: board edge vs market anchor, gated by ELITE_THRESHOLD/JUNK_THRESHOLD/MIN_MARKET_VALUE, scaled by SINGLE_SOURCE_DISCOUNT and a source-count confidence ramp
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue (our board), ktcSfTep or idpTradeCalc (market), source count, roster shape
formulas.constants: ELITE_THRESHOLD 6600, MARKET_TOP_N_FILTER 150, MAX_BOARD_LOSS -175, JUNK_THRESHOLD 350, MIN_MARKET_VALUE 500, MULTI_FOR_ONE_MIN_RATIO 0.55, ELITE_MULTI_MIN_RATIO 0.65, PACKAGE_ANCHOR_MIN_PCT 0.35, PARTIAL_MARKET_ARBITRAGE_CAP 8.0, CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE 5, BOARD_TO_COMPOSITE_K 0.875, ROSTER_SURPLUS_THRESHOLD 4, ROSTER_WEAK_THRESHOLD 1 — ZERO of these has a literal pin in any test; six are referenced by no test at all.
