findings.title: A 100%-synthetic test module for the core blend function is exempted from the blocking CI gate by a filename-matching rule
findings.rootCause: tests/conftest.py applies the `livedata` marker by FILE BASENAME, not by whether the test actually touches live data. `tests/api/test_data_contract.py` is on the list but reads no live file — every fixture in it is an inline dict.
findings.evidence: tests/conftest.py:104 lists `"test_data_contract.py",` inside `_LIVEDATA_MODULES`; :123-133 `def pytest_collection_modifyitems(...)  fname = item.path.name ... if fname in _LIVEDATA_MODULES: item.add_marker(pytest.mark.livedata)`. The module itself is pure: `def _minimal_raw_payload(): return {"players": {"Josh Allen": {...}}}` (test_data_contract.py:13-36) and its only mention of a live path is inside a docstring ("``rawSourceValues.ktcSfTep`` mirrors ``CSVs/site_raw/ktcSfTep.csv``", :599-600). CI runs `python -m pytest tests/ -x -q --tb=short -m "not livedata"` (pr-validation.yml:161) as the hard gate and `-m livedata` with `continue-on-error: true` (:163-178).
findings.userImpact: 33 tests covering `_compute_unified_rankings` — rank assignment, value-direct voting, the single-source haircut, OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT, legacy-dict mirroring, IDP integrity guardrails, hillCurves stamping, rawSourceValues pass-through — cannot fail a pull request. I ran them: `Ran 33 tests in 1.025s OK`. They pass today and they always would have; nothing tells anyone if they stop. The same applies to `tests/adapters/test_dlf_scraper.py` (9 tests, loads scripts/fetch_dlf.py and parses HTML strings — no network, no CSV read; its own docstring says 'These tests exercise the offline-safe pure functions') and `tests/scripts/test_fetch_flock_fantasy_rookies.py` (24 tests, all tempfile-based). That is 66 offline tests in the advisory tier out of 264 total deselected functions.
findings.recommendedFix: Split the three modules the way test_pick_rookie_anchor was already split, or replace the basename list with a marker applied at the test level. Then extend `tests/test_livedata_policy.py` — which today only checks that entries name EXISTING files (:66-73) — to also assert that each exempted module actually references `exports/` or `CSVs/`.

findings.title: Pipeline stage 11, a genuine post-blend override of rankDerivedValue, has no test at all
findings.rootCause: `_apply_two_way_player_boost` was added without tests and no coverage gate exists.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:4776-4790: `_TWO_WAY_PLAYERS: dict[str, str] = {"Travis Hunter": "DB"}` and `def _apply_two_way_player_boost(players_array, players_by_name) -> None: ... use max(offense, alt) as the final ``rankDerivedValue```. Repo-wide grep of tests/ for `_apply_two_way_player_boost` returns nothing; grep for `_TWO_WAY_PLAYERS` returns nothing. The nine hits for 'Travis Hunter' in tests/ are all unrelated (BDVM Clay projections, source history fixtures, pool builder).
findings.userImpact: CLAUDE.md describes this as 'A genuine post-blend OVERRIDE: rankDerivedValue becomes max(offense value, alt-position-family value), written to both the row and the legacy dict.' It runs after the corridor clamp and before the pick passes. If it silently stopped firing, started firing on the wrong family, or wrote to only one of the two destinations, no test in the repository would notice. Compare stage 10 (corridor clamp), which has 31 dedicated tests.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a synthetic case to tests/api/test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py: one row named 'Travis Hunter' with a low offense blend and a high DB blend, asserting the max is taken, that it is mirrored into the legacy dict, and that a non-listed player is untouched.

findings.title: The Sharp Score's entire weight vector is unpinned; every test is an inequality
findings.rootCause: tests/sharp/test_score.py was written to assert product rules (gates fire, no single signal dominates, score != confidence) and never to assert the composition.
findings.evidence: tests/sharp/test_score.py, 256 lines, contains no numeric equality on a score. The strongest numeric assertions are `assert lucky < 0.25` (:133), `assert 0.0 <= entry.confidence <= 1.0` (:142), `assert cfg["qualification"]["minScorePercentile"] >= 0.67` (:244), `assert S.percentile_rank(1.0, [1.0]*10) == 0.5` (:249). Meanwhile src/sharp/score.py:284-313 composes `parts.append((float(sub.get("winPct", 0.30)), p))`, `... ("playoffRate", 0.25)`, `... ("championshipRate", 0.20)`, `... ("medianFinishPercentile", 0.15)`, `... ("pointsForPercentile", 0.10)` and config/sharp/scoring_v2.json carries the same numbers.
findings.userImpact: You could swap the winPct and championshipRate weights, or set them all to 0.2, and the suite stays green. The config's own header admits the weights are 'PRIORS chosen for defensibility, not values validated against an outcome dataset' — so there is neither a validation nor a change-detector. A Sharp Score shown to a user is an unvalidated hand-weighted sum with no regression barrier. Secondary hazard: every weight is duplicated as an inline `sub.get(key, default)` fallback, so a typo in the JSON key silently reverts to the code default with no error.
findings.recommendedFix: Add one hand-computed end-to-end case (a manager record with known percentiles -> an exact expected score) plus a config/code parity test in the style of tests/api/test_config_parity.py.

findings.title: The playoff-odds Monte Carlo has 756 lines of tests and no known-answer case
findings.rootCause: The test file grew around the scheduling and record-accumulation plumbing, which is genuinely intricate, and never came back to the probability itself.
findings.evidence: tests/public_league/test_playoff_odds.py:30-54 is the whole probability contract: `self.assertIn("season", result)` ... `self.assertGreaterEqual(owner["playoffProbability"], 0.0)`, `self.assertLessEqual(owner["playoffProbability"], 1.0)`, `self.assertEqual(r1["owners"], r2["owners"])` (determinism under a seeded RNG). The only other probability assertion is `self.assertIn(owner["playoffProbability"], (0.0, 1.0))` for a completed season (:68). src/public_league/playoff_odds.py is 712 lines.
findings.userImpact: A sign flip in the scoring-sample draw, a swapped tiebreak, or a wrong playoff-spot cutoff would all still produce numbers inside [0,1] that are deterministic under a seed — and would pass. The percentage a league member reads on /league is an unvalidated simulation output. (The scheduling half IS well tested, and the preseason `playoffProbability is None` discipline at :405-412 is correct and pinned.)
findings.recommendedFix: Add a symmetric case: N identical owners with identical score distributions and N/2 playoff spots must return ~0.5 each within Monte Carlo error; and a dominance case: one owner with a strictly higher distribution must have strictly higher odds.

findings.title: The KTC reconciliation guard — the only thing measuring our curve against the real market — cannot fail a PR, and spent three months red without anyone noticing
findings.rootCause: It reads CSVs/site_raw/ktc.csv, so it is (correctly) livedata-marked; but the model-registry promotion path rewrites the Hill constants and re-baselines nothing.
findings.evidence: tests/canonical/test_ktc_reconciliation.py:107-118 (the file's own admission): 'The previous baseline dated from 2026-04-20 and had gone stale ... **All 10 cases were failing on `main`** and nobody saw it, because this module is auto-marked `livedata` ... so CI runs it `continue-on-error`.' tests/conftest.py:112 lists it. It is currently GREEN — I re-ran all 10 cases against the committed ktc.csv (464 player rows): rank 1 pct 0.00 (band 0.0±3.0), rank 12 pct 13.09 (12.3±3.0), rank 150 pct -11.93 (-11.8±5.0), rank 400 pct -0.40 (0.0±10.0); 0 failures.
findings.userImpact: The staleness half is now covered — tests/canonical/test_hill_percentile_constants_tripwire.py:200-230 REGEX-PARSES PINNED_DELTAS out of this file and fails the hard gate if the `ours` column drifts, which is a genuinely clever fix. But the DRIFT half (the pct_diff bands, i.e. 'has the market moved away from us') still cannot block anything. A structural KTC tail shift, which the file's own comments say is 'a signal, not a regression — break CI, investigate', will not break CI.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep it advisory but add an alerting leg (an idempotent tracking issue, the pattern e2e.yml already uses) so an advisory failure is visible rather than buried in a `continue-on-error` step's log.

findings.title: 23 of ~346 module-level numeric constants in src/ have a literal pin; roughly 150 are referenced by no test at all
findings.rootCause: The repo's dominant test idiom is to import the constant symbolically and assert against it, which is right for values that are legitimately refit but makes every threshold change invisible.
findings.evidence: I scanned every `^NAME = <number>` at module scope in src/**/*.py and cross-referenced against the full text of tests/. Literally pinned (23): _ALPHA_SHRINKAGE 0.10, _SINGLE_SOURCE_VALUE_RETENTION 0.30, _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N 500, _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA 0.0, _HAMPEL_K 2.75, _HAMPEL_MIN_N 4, _HAMPEL_MIN_THRESHOLD 1000.0, _TE_BLANKET_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER 1.10, _TE_BLANKET_NON_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER 1.15, BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER 150, MAX_BALANCERS 2, MAX_GIVE_PLAYER_APPEARANCES 2, MIN_WAIVER_VALUE 500, CARDINAL_MIN_DYNAMIC_RANGE 3.0, DEFAULT_BAND 2, FULL_SEASON_WEEKS 17, MIN_GAMES_FOR_PPG 8, MIN_STORIES_FOR_DIGEST 2, PER_MEMBER_LEAGUE_CAP 25 and four schema versions. Referenced by NO test: MARKET_TOP_N_FILTER 150 (src/trade/finder.py:132), ELITE_MULTI_MIN_RATIO 0.65, MULTI_FOR_ONE_MIN_RATIO 0.55, PACKAGE_ANCHOR_MIN_PCT 0.35, JUNK_THRESHOLD 350, MIN_MARKET_VALUE 500, CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE 5, PARTIAL_MARKET_ARBITRAGE_CAP 8.0, ROSTER_SURPLUS_THRESHOLD 4 (all src/trade/finder.py); FAIRNESS_TOLERANCE 769, HIGH_DISPERSION_CV 0.12, LOW_DISPERSION_CV 0.04, CONSOLIDATION_MIN_UPGRADE_RATIO 0.70, CONSOLIDATION_MAX_OVERPAY_RATIO 0.30, MAX_SUGGESTIONS_PER_TYPE 8 (src/trade/suggestions.py); MATCH_QUARANTINE_THRESHOLD 0.90 (src/identity/matcher.py); DEFAULT_SIMULATIONS 10000, ODDS_SE_TOLERANCE 0.005, DEPTH_VARIANCE_LIFT_MAX 0.15 (src/ros/playoff_sim.py); MARKET_FAIRNESS_TOLERANCE_PCT 12.0, MIN_GAIN_EACH_SIDE 150.0 (src/bdvm/roster.py); IMPROVED_WEIGHT_* (five weights, src/league_comparison/metrics.py).
findings.userImpact: A threshold change — the single most common way a decision system silently changes its answers — is caught in the canonical pipeline and essentially nowhere else. `MATCH_QUARANTINE_THRESHOLD` is the most alarming: it decides whether a fuzzy player match is accepted into the board or quarantined, and no test mentions it.
findings.recommendedFix: Extend the tripwire pattern that already exists for the Hill constants (test_hill_percentile_constants_tripwire.py, test_rank_form_constants_tripwire.py) to the trade-engine and identity thresholds. One dumb equality module per subsystem, with the same 'if this fires, here is what else must move' guidance text.

findings.title: The frontend suite is 92.6% non-numeric and 75 of 97 files contain no numeric expectation at all
findings.rootCause: The frontend is meant to be a pure materializer, so most specs assert render/shape. But several files own real arithmetic that is not covered.
findings.evidence: Across frontend/__tests__/**/*.test.js{,x}: 3,173 `expect(...)` calls, of which 235 match a numeric-literal matcher (`toBeCloseTo`, `toBe(<float>)`, `toBe(<3+ digit int>)`, `toEqual(<float>)`). 75 of 97 files have zero. The numeric mass is concentrated in four files: draft-logic.test.js (63), trade-logic.test.js (51), dynasty-data.test.js (22), site-overrides.test.js (21). Contrast waiver-logic.test.js: 99 expects, 1 numeric — yet frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js is what /waivers actually computes from (CLAUDE.md: '`/waivers` computes client-side from contract rows'). Similarly public-league.test.js, news-filters.test.js, sharp-unified-market.test.js: 0 numeric each.
findings.userImpact: The one page whose numbers are genuinely computed on the client — /waivers — has essentially no client-side arithmetic coverage, while the backend `POST /api/waiver/suggestions` path that IS well tested has, per CLAUDE.md, 'no UI caller'. The tested path and the shipped path are different code.
findings.recommendedFix: Port the numeric cases from tests/trade/test_waiver.py::TestFaabBidArithmetic into frontend/__tests__/waiver-logic.test.js so both sides of the duplicated logic are pinned to the same numbers, in the style already used for name-key-parity and signal-engine-parity.

findings.title: 157 runtime `skipTest`/`pytest.skip` calls can turn a red test green with no signal
findings.rootCause: Data-dependent tests self-skip when their input is absent rather than failing or being marked.
findings.evidence: Counted across tests/: 157 skip calls in 30 files. Worst offenders: tests/api/test_launch_readiness.py 26 (`self.skipTest("No live data")` at :67,:94,:102,... :464), test_single_curve_live.py 17, tests/api/test_draft_capital.py 17 (`self.skipTest("Workbook unavailable")` at :383,:433,:484,:677,:715,:773,:834,:869,:899,:936,:977 and `skipTest(f"Unavailable: {result['error']}")` at :120,:134,:142,:189,:788,:1039), test_source_monitoring.py 15, test_picks_end_to_end.py 12. tests/api/test_identity_validation.py:570,:623 skip on `"Exception set is empty"`. tests/api/test_fantasypros_idp_integration.py:412,:419,:426 skip unless the `LIVE_API_FIXTURE` env var points at a file — that variable is set in no workflow.
findings.userImpact: test_draft_capital.py is NOT livedata-marked, so it sits in the blocking tier — but 17 of its tests, including `test_traded_pick_moves_dollars_between_teams` which is the only check that a Sleeper-traded pick moves auction dollars in the correct direction, evaporate silently if openpyxl or the workbook is missing. A skipped test and a passing test look identical in `pytest -q` output. Nothing in any workflow asserts a minimum collected/passed count.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a floor assertion to the CI step (`pytest ... | tail -1` parsed for a minimum passed count, or a session-scoped fixture that fails if more than N tests skipped). Convert `skipTest` on committed artifacts (the workbook, exports/latest) into hard failures — those files are git-tracked, so their absence IS a defect.

findings.title: A hard-gated test shells out to `python -m pytest` as a subprocess, coupling the gate to the test runner's own availability
findings.rootCause: tests/ros/test_isolation.py re-runs another test file rather than importing the function it wants to check.
findings.evidence: tests/ros/test_isolation.py:106-130: `result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", "tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py::test_fixture_overall_rms_under_50", "-q", "--tb=line"], ... timeout=60)` then `self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, f"KTC VA fixture regression: {result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}")`.
findings.userImpact: This was the single failing test in my run (`AssertionError: 1 != 0 : KTC VA fixture regression: ... No module named pytest`). It double-counts a check that already runs in the same session, adds up to 60s of wall clock, and fails for environmental reasons unrelated to ROS isolation. The underlying check is fine — I verified it independently: RMS 26.59 against the bound of 50.
findings.recommendedFix: Import `ktc_adjust_package` and the fixture directly, or delete the duplicate — tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py already runs in the same pytest session.

findings.title: The `livedata` marker is applied by filename with no namespacing, and four basenames already collide across directories
findings.evidence: tests/conftest.py:127-132: `fname = item.path.name ... if fname in _LIVEDATA_MODULES`. Existing basename collisions in tests/: `test_calibration.py` (tests/league_intel/, tests/canonical/), `test_replacement.py` (tests/bdvm/, tests/league_intel/), `test_service.py` (five copies: bdvm, intel, playerctx, news, league_comparison), `test_store.py` (intel, playerctx). None currently collides with a `_LIVEDATA_MODULES` entry, so this is latent, not active.
findings.userImpact: The day someone adds e.g. `tests/scripts/test_data_contract.py`, it is silently exempted from the blocking gate. The failure mode is invisible: the test collects, reports as deselected, and reads as 'not applicable'.
findings.recommendedFix: Key on the repo-relative path, or move to real per-test markers.

findings.title: Two golden fixtures are regenerated from the code under test and pin nothing about correctness — one says so in a comment
findings.rootCause: Change-detector tests written in golden-file style.
findings.evidence: tests/canonical/test_player_valuation.py:122-131: 'Re-baselined 2026-07-30 for the re-tuned rank-form constants ... If they change again, **regenerate this dict from the constants** rather than hand-editing it' — followed by `expected = {1: 9999, 2: 9781, ... 500: 1360}`. I confirmed all ten reproduce exactly, which is expected: the dict is the function's own output. Similarly docs/research/bdvm-v1/reference/examples_output.txt is the output of run_examples.py in the same directory, and tests/bdvm/test_reference_parity.py:35-49 diffs one against the other.
findings.userImpact: Neither validates a formula. Both are legitimate as FREEZE guards — the rank-form dict makes an unannounced constant edit loud, and the BDVM one stops anyone editing the acceptance fixture — and both are honest about it in their docstrings. The concern is only that they read like validation. Note the BDVM case is saved by provenance: the reference implementation was independently transcribed from a published PDF and its numbers were token-verified against Appendix C (README.md: '956/956 tokens identical, 0 mismatches'), so tests/bdvm/test_engine_parity.py IS a real external check on src/bdvm even though test_reference_parity.py is not.
findings.recommendedFix: None needed beyond what is already written; the docstrings are accurate. Do not let either be cited as evidence the math is right.

findings.title: The E2E suite gates nothing pre-merge and its visual half is disabled in the only workflow that runs it
findings.rootCause: Deliberate — the suite is slow — but the consequence is that no browser-level check blocks a merge.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/e2e.yml triggers: `schedule: - cron: "23 6 * * *"` and `workflow_dispatch: {}`, with the header comment 'Triggers: manual dispatch + nightly cron ONLY — deliberately NOT on every PR.' Within that run, `SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION: "1"` is set and `--ignore-snapshots` is passed; tests/e2e/specs/chart-visual-regression.spec.js:174 and public-league-visual.spec.js:122 both gate on `!!process.env.SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION`. prod-e2e-smoke.yml runs only `tests/e2e/specs/public-league.spec.js` on `cron: "17 */4 * * *"`. smoke-test.yml's production-smoke job is conditional: `if: ${{ vars.PROD_PUBLIC_URL != '' }}` — an unset repo variable makes the whole job vanish rather than fail.
findings.userImpact: The 14 Playwright specs — the only tests that exercise real page rendering, sorting, filtering, popups, and settings round-trip — can be broken for up to 24 hours before anything says so, and pixel comparisons never run in CI at all. Two of the workflow's own comments document that an earlier duplicate-YAML-key bug made every scheduled e2e run a startup failure, i.e. 'the scheduled E2E run appeared healthy while never executing' — the same class of silence.
findings.recommendedFix: Run a 2-3 spec critical-smoke subset on PRs (critical-smoke.spec.js already exists and is scoped for this), leaving the full suite nightly.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md overstates coverage in two places its own workflow file already corrects
findings.rootCause: Documentation written ahead of the code, then partially fixed only in the workflow's comments.
findings.evidence: pr-validation.yml:41-49 (a comment, not the doc) records: 'NOTE (2026-07-29 audit): the "+ vitest" in that sentence was aspirational until this date — no vitest step existed in any workflow' and pr-validation.yml:243-252: 'These 80+ files / ~1,390 assertions existed since the frontend was built and ran in NO workflow ... The comment at the top of this job claimed the gate was "full pytest + vitest + lint", so the gap read as covered.' The vitest step now exists at :253-259 — but only in pr-validation.yml; deploy.yml has no `npm test` step (its steps are the pytest gate at :116-137 and a bundle-size gate at :187). Separately, CLAUDE.md's Live Value Pipeline section describes stage 10 as `_apply_idp_calibration_post_pass` reading `config/idp_calibration.json` — tests/api/test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py:520-540 asserts `not hasattr(dc, "_apply_idp_calibration_post_pass")` and that the config file does not exist; I confirmed neither is in the tree.
findings.userImpact: A reader trusting CLAUDE.md would believe the frontend was gated for the whole period it was not, and would look for an IDP calibration pass that was removed. CLAUDE.md does flag the idp_calibration retirement in a later paragraph, so that one is self-contradictory rather than simply wrong.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the vitest step to deploy.yml (post-merge parity), and reconcile CLAUDE.md's stage-10 paragraph with the code it already retracts three lines later.

findings.title: `pytest -x` means a green run proves less than it appears to, and a conflicted PR gets zero checks
findings.rootCause: Both the PR gate and the deploy gate use `-x` (stop on first failure); GitHub cannot schedule a `pull_request` run for a PR whose merge ref will not build.
findings.evidence: pr-validation.yml:161 and deploy.yml:127 both run `python -m pytest tests/ -x -q --tb=short -m "not livedata"`. pr-validation.yml:24-40 documents the second half in its own words: 'When the PR has merge conflicts that ref cannot be created, so the run is never scheduled — the PR sits with NO checks at all, which on the merge page reads identically to checks having passed. Observed on #625 (2026-07-29) ... The mitigation is branch protection, not this file.'
findings.userImpact: `-x` is only a reporting cost (a green run still means everything passed), but it means one flaky failure hides every subsequent failure from the log, which slows exactly the triage that matters. The zero-checks case is the real one and is Not Verifiable from Repository — whether a ruleset requiring the `Validate PR` check exists is a GitHub setting, not a file. Without it, an ungated PR is indistinguishable from a passing one.
findings.recommendedFix: Confirm branch protection requires the `Validate PR` check. Consider dropping `-x` in favour of `--maxfail=5` so a run surfaces more than one failure.

notes:
SAMPLING METHOD (three passes, all reproducible)

1. Whole-population scan. A script walked every `tests/**/test_*.py` (378 files) and counted assertion statements matching `^\s*(assert\b|self\.assert\w+\(|self\.fail\()`, then flagged an assertion as "numeric" if it contained `approx`/`assertAlmostEqual`, or compared against a float literal, or against a 2+-digit integer that is not an HTTP status. Result: 11,749 assertions total, 1,464 numeric (12.5%); 146 files with >=3 numeric, 64 with 1-2, 168 with none. 5,355 `def test_` functions. All 106 zero-`assert` files are unittest-style (`self.assertX`), not empty. Raw data at /tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/rows2.json.

2. Manual stratified read. `random.seed(42); random.sample(rows, 24)` — I then read every assertion line in each of the 24. Classification: ~9-10/24 (≈40%) genuinely pin formula arithmetic (bdvm/test_scoring, league_intel/test_adjustment, model_registry/test_promotion, public_league/test_metrics_engines, public_league/test_power, canonical/test_confidence_intervals, trade/test_finder_canonical_board, canonical/test_rank_form_constants_tripwire, api/test_source_native_values); ~14/24 (≈58%) are parse/shape/static-lint (adapters/test_fitzmaurice_scraper, deploy/test_timers_are_utc, nfl_data/test_windows_tzdata_declared, public_league/test_player_position_is_memoized, news/test_sleeper_provider, scripts/test_crawl_ffpc_sharp_fixture, intel/test_crawler …). That ≈40% agrees with the automated 39% (146/378), so I report **roughly 145-150 of the 378 as numeric-behaviour modules and ~230 as shape/smoke/parse/static**.

3. Targeted deep read of every decision system named in the brief, plus a constant-pinning scan: I extracted every `^NAME = <number>` at module scope across src/**/*.py (~346 constants) and searched the full text of tests/ for either `NAME == <literal>` or `== <literal> … NAME`. 23 pinned, ~150 referenced by no test at all.

WHAT I COULD ACTUALLY EXECUTE
pytest and fastapi are absent, but python3 is present and most `src/` modules import cleanly. So beyond reading, I RAN things:
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -p "test_*.py"` → **Ran 1435 tests, 1 failure, 212 errors, 21 skipped**. All 212 errors are `ModuleNotFoundError: pytest` (154) or `fastapi` (58) at import; none is a real defect. The single failure is tests/ros/test_isolation.py shelling out to pytest (finding #9). So the ~1,435 unittest-style tests collectible here are green on this commit.
- Reproduced the Hill percentile curve at 10 ranks — exact match to the tripwire pins.
- Reproduced `_compute_unified_rankings` end to end on synthetic rows — single-source haircut (5000→1500), n=2 mean (5000), pick-year discount (7000 / 5740 / 4620), alpha 0.10, lambda 0.0, refN 500 — all matching tests/api/test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py exactly.
- Re-ran the 10 KTC reconciliation cases against the committed ktc.csv (464 rows): all green today.
- Re-ran the 16 league_intel golden scoring cases against Sleeper's own awarded points: 0 failures at abs 0.011.
- Re-ran the 139-trade KTC VA fixture: RMS 26.59 vs bound 50.
- `python3 -m unittest tests.bdvm.test_engine_parity` → Ran 7, OK (Appendix-C parity holds).
- `python3 -m unittest tests.api.test_data_contract` → Ran 33, OK; `tests.api.test_market_corridor_clamp` → Ran 31, OK.

WHICH TESTS ACTUALLY GATE A MERGE
Only `.github/workflows/pr-validation.yml` job `Validate PR`. Blocking: pip check, scripts/check_env.py, py_compile (3 files), `ruff format --check .`, `ruff check` on changed .py, runtime import gate, `pytest tests/ -x -q -m "not livedata"`, `npm test` (vitest, both projects — added 2026-07-29), `next build` + bundle budget. Non-blocking: `pytest -m livedata` (continue-on-error). Conditional/no-op: the API contract check runs only `if ls dynasty_data_*.json` succeeds. deploy.yml re-runs the same pytest gate post-merge but has NO vitest step. e2e.yml, prod-e2e-smoke.yml and smoke-test.yml are cron/dispatch only and gate nothing pre-merge.
pyproject.toml has NO `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` section (52 lines total, only ruff + a mypy scaffold that no CI step runs). There is no pytest.ini/setup.cfg/tox.ini. The `livedata` marker is registered at runtime in tests/conftest.py:118-122.

TIERS OF EVIDENCE, RANKED
Externally validated (a real-world oracle, independent of the code): league_intel exact scoring vs Sleeper's awarded points; KTC VA port vs 139 captured site trades; BDVM engine vs published Appendix C.
Deterministically pinned (a change breaks the build, correctness assumed): the 8 Hill percentile constants + 10 curve outputs; every stage constant in test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py; the corridor clamp band; the FAAB base bid; the count-aware blend breakpoints.
Invariant-tested (would catch a sign flip, not a magnitude change): test_golden_dataset_invariants.py monotonicity; league_intel factor bounds; trade rank_score ordinals; sharp score ordinals; lead score ordinals.
Shape/smoke only: news (8 numeric assertions across 15 files), public_league probabilities, most of tests/scripts, tests/deploy, tests/platforms, and 75 of 97 frontend files.

THE SUITE'S OWN SELF-AWARENESS IS UNUSUALLY HIGH AND SHOULD BE TRUSTED AS A MAP
tests/test_livedata_policy.py audits the exemption list; test_hill_percentile_constants_tripwire.py audits the KTC guard's staleness by regex-parsing it; test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py's docstring states plainly that before it existed 'the stage arithmetic below … had **no CI-blocking test at all**'; pr-validation.yml admits vitest was aspirational for months. Where this audit disagrees with the repo's own notes it is because those mechanisms are incomplete (basename-based exemption, no offline-content check), not because they are wrong.

WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE A REAL FANTASY DECISION
Trust: the market board value (rankDerivedValue) and its stage arithmetic; the Hill curve; exact league scoring; the KTC VA displayed on /trade; BDVM's fundamental values ON SYNTHETIC INPUT (its live inputs are Not Verifiable from Repository — data/bdvm/ is absent here). Treat as directional only: trade-suggestion ordering, finder confidence, Sharp Score, playoff odds, lead strength, news severity, ROS simulation outputs — every one is an unpinned hand-weighted composite whose weights the repo itself labels priors.
