formulas.name: Percentile-form Hill curve (live board)
formulas.expression: p = (effective_rank − 1) / (_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N − 1);  V(p) = 9999 / (1 + (p/c)^s)
formulas.inputs: per-source effective rank after ladder translation; scope routing selects (c,s)
formulas.constants: GLOBAL c=0.1120 s=0.725; OFFENSE c=0.1100 s=1.110; IDP c=0.0830 s=1.110; ROOKIE c=0.1530 s=0.885 (declared but NOT routed — data_contract._curve_for_source never selects it). _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N=500 (data_contract.py:4933). All eight (c,s) exist ONLY here; the model registry JSON stores copies and I verified champion v2 matches the code exactly.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A source with no rank for a player simply does not vote. No imputation. Correct.
formulas.mathIssues: Ranks past 500 clamp onto the curve tail rather than extrapolating — deliberate top-500-board behavior, documented at data_contract.py:4927-4933.
formulas.validated: Yes, and unusually well. Fitted by scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py, scored against four HELD-OUT market boards by src/model_registry/holdout.py, promoted only by a human running scripts/model_registry.py. Champion v2 beat v1 by +38.5 RMSE points paired on the same day's boards, improving all four holdout sources. The registry entry's own _semantics block states plainly that this measures cross-market generalization and NOT accuracy against reality, because no ground truth for dynasty value exists.

formulas.name: Rank-form Hill curve (reconstruction only)
formulas.expression: value = 1 + 9998 / (1 + ((rank − 1)/midpoint)^slope)
formulas.inputs: a consensus rank, plus a scope selector
formulas.constants: HILL_MIDPOINT=65.4, HILL_SLOPE=0.910 (offense/pick); IDP_HILL_MIDPOINT=64.6, IDP_HILL_SLOPE=0.900. Re-tuned 2026-07-30. No frontend copy exists — but see findings: the /rankings methodology panel renders this formula with midpoint 45 and slope 1.10, values that appear nowhere in the codebase.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rank None or ≤0 returns 0; rank <1 clamps to 1.
formulas.mathIssues: None. Monotone, rank 1 = 9999 exactly.
formulas.validated: Yes. scripts/backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py against 740 ranked rows of the live board; the old (48.44, 1.149) pair scored RMSE 821.8 on offense, the new pair 89.8. Stability checked across 16 archived snapshots. Watched by .github/workflows/audit-rank-form-drift.yml.

formulas.name: Count-aware aggregation + shrinkage + haircut
formulas.expression: offense: count-aware mean-median (n=1 passthrough, n=2 mean, n=3-4 untrimmed mean-median, n≥5 drop max+min).  IDP/picks: blended = anchor + α·(subgroup − anchor).  then final = center − λ·MAD.  then if effective sources == 1 and not a pick: final ×= 0.30
formulas.inputs: post-Hampel per-source value contributions
formulas.constants: _ALPHA_SHRINKAGE=0.10, _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA=0.0 (retired no-op), _SINGLE_SOURCE_VALUE_RETENTION=0.30
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Sources absent for a player are excluded from n, not zero-filled. The single-source haircut is applied instead of imputing. This is the right behavior and is one of the few places the codebase gets it right by construction.
formulas.mathIssues: None found. λ=0 makes the MAD term a strict no-op while still stamping sourceSpread as a diagnostic, which the code says explicitly.
formulas.validated: α=0.10 and λ=0.10 came from a 2D joint backtest over 25 daily snapshots (reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md); the comment is candid that the true optimum was the degenerate α=0 ("use IDPTC alone") and that α=0.10 was chosen as the cheapest non-degenerate point. λ was then set to 0 by a later product override with a stated rationale (double-penalising the same spread signal). _SINGLE_SOURCE_VALUE_RETENTION=0.30 has a rationale but no measurement.

formulas.name: Value-direct source vote
formulas.expression: vote = raw_value / site_max × 9999, where site_max is the per-source max computed over IN-RANGE rows only
formulas.inputs: canonicalSiteValues for ktcSfTep and idpTradeCalc only
formulas.constants: _VALUE_SOURCE_DECLARED_MAX {ktcSfTep: 9999.0, idpTradeCalc: 9999.0}; _VALUE_RANGE_ESCALATION_FRACTION=0.02; _VALUE_RANGE_ESCALATION_MIN_ROWS=50
formulas.missingDataBehavior: An out-of-range row is DROPPED from the value-direct path and falls through to rank→Hill, exactly as a missing value already does. It is not clamped and not zeroed. Above 2% of a source's rows out-of-range (and only with ≥50 rows) the whole source is suppressed from the value-direct path but still votes via rank.
formulas.mathIssues: None. The guard closes a genuine, measured hazard: the comment records that a single ktcSfTep=99990 deflated every other player by 45.3% on a 120-player board, ordering preserved so the damage was invisible.
formulas.validated: The failure mode was measured through build_api_data_contract; the 2% and 50-row thresholds are reasoned ("do not conclude from a sample that cannot distinguish the hypotheses") but not fitted.

formulas.name: KTC TE-premium uplift curve
formulas.expression: ratio(v) = 1 + a·v^(−k), clamped to [floor, observed_ratio_range max]
formulas.inputs: a TE's base-basis value
formulas.constants: a=43.555794, k=0.632839, floor=1.209206, ceiling=2.0531. Code fallbacks at te_premium.py:85-100 are identical except floor 1.2092 vs 1.209206.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: convert_te_value is a no-op when from_basis == to_basis, so KTC (the anchor) is structurally exempt from double-lifting. Sources with no TE row are simply not converted.
formulas.mathIssues: Monotone and ≥1 by construction. The clamp exists because the power form extrapolates to 3.36× at base value 100, outside the measured range.
formulas.validated: Yes — 73 paired TEs from CSVs/site_raw/ktc.csv vs ktcSfTep.csv, R²=0.941 in log space, median abs err 0.023, regenerable via scripts/audit/fit_ktc_tep_curve.py --write-config. The config also states its own limitation: it measures what KTC does, not whether KTC is right.

formulas.name: Scraper composite (the second value pipeline)
formulas.expression: norm_i = clamp((z_i − Z_FLOOR)/(Z_CEILING − Z_FLOOR), 0, 1);  meta = Σ(norm_i·w_i)/Σw_i over the adaptively-trimmed set;  composite = meta × 9999;  then ×elite_boost, ×single-source discount, ×IDP headroom
formulas.inputs: per-source raw values, per-source mean/stdev
formulas.constants: COMPOSITE_SCALE=9999, OUTLIER_TRIM_GAP=0.18, ELITE_NORM_THRESHOLD=0.88, ELITE_BOOST_MAX=0.09, IDP_VALUE_HEADROOM_FRACTION=0.18, SINGLE_SOURCE_DISCOUNT_MIN=0.55 / MAX=0.82, IDP_ROOKIE_ONLY_NO_MARKET_CAP=2600, SITE_WEIGHTS{ktc:1.3, …}. The single-source discount here (0.55–0.82) is a DIFFERENT number from data_contract's _SINGLE_SOURCE_VALUE_RETENTION=0.30 for the same concept on the other pipeline, and finder.py carries a THIRD (_LEGACY_SINGLE_SOURCE_DISCOUNT=0.88) for its legacy branch — finder.py:70-84 explains why its own is not a stacked double-haircut.
formulas.outputRange: 1–9999, but running ~14% hot relative to the canonical board (median board/composite = 0.875)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Sources absent for a player are skipped, not zero-filled. Good. But marketConfidence and dispersionCV both have `.get(key, default)` fallbacks (0.5 and 0.0) at Dynasty Scraper.py:6197-6199 that would be indistinguishable from measurements — currently unreachable because the producer always sets both.
formulas.mathIssues: SITE_WEIGHTS gives ktc=1.3 and ktcSfTep no entry (→1.0). Those are the same vendor's two boards and are near-identical row by row (A.J. Brown: ktc 5008, ktcSfTep 5008, idpTradeCalc 4936). I computed the effective share on a 3-source player: KTC family carries 2.3/3.3 = 69.7% of the composite against IDPTradeCalc's 30.3%.
formulas.validated: No. No script, backtest or measurement doc exists for any constant in this pipeline. The "Phase 3 fix" comments record what changed, never what was measured.

formulas.name: Market confidence
formulas.expression: site_score = clamp(site_count/8.0, 0.20, 1.00);  cv_score = clamp(1 − min(cv,0.35)/0.35, 0.20, 1.00);  conf = clamp(0.65·site_score + 0.35·cv_score, 0.20, 1.00)
formulas.inputs: count of contributing scraper sites, coefficient of variation across their normalized values
formulas.constants: divisor 8.0, cv reference 0.35, weights 0.65/0.35, clamp floor 0.20
formulas.outputRange: Nominally 0.20–1.00. STRUCTURALLY 0.20–0.59375 today, because only three dash keys exist live so site_count ∈ {1,2,3} and site_score ≤ 0.375.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Rows with no composite carry no _marketConfidence at all — 839 of 1094 rows have it. The frontend correctly keeps absent as null rather than 0 (dynasty-data.js:1023, :1201), and both comments record that the previous `|| 0` coercion made "absent" indistinguishable from "lowest possible confidence" and fired a MONITOR alert on it.
formulas.mathIssues: The 8.0 divisor is a fossil of an era with ~10 enabled scraper SITES. I measured the live export: n=839, min 0.3447, max 0.5938, median 0.4897 — the observed max is the theoretical cap to four decimals. A user-facing "confidence" that cannot exceed 59% is a broken gauge.
formulas.validated: Measured, and the measurement is in the repo — scripts/simulate_market_confidence_divisor.py and docs/measurements/market-confidence-divisor-2026-07-30.json. The rule that depended on it (low_conf_unstable) was retired on the strength of that measurement; the metric itself was left unfixed.

formulas.name: Team-impact fit / equity / verdict
formulas.expression: fit_raw = Σ_pos [ w_fill·Δstarter_value + w_depth·Δfirst_depth·avg_starter − w_overflow·max(0,Δoverflow)·avg_starter ];  fit = clamp(100·fit_raw/4000, ±100);  equity = clamp(100·Δvalue/2500, ±100);  composite = 0.55·fit + 0.45·equity
formulas.inputs: resolved trade assets, league rosterSettings
formulas.constants: fillStarter 1.0, depth 0.25, overflow 0.6, fitNormalization 4000, equityNormalization 2500, compositeFitWeight 0.55, compositeEquityWeight 0.45, verdict bands ±20 / ±8, contendIndexThreshold 0.15, ages 23/24/29
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `int(a.get("value") or 0)` at team_impact.py:117, :148, :219-232, :414-415. An asset the board cannot price contributes exactly 0 to starter value, contend index and top-10 share — silently, with a full verdict still rendered.
formulas.mathIssues: The two normalizations (4000 and 2500) set the exchange rate between roster fit and equity and are the numbers that actually decide Accept vs Decline, since composite is a fixed 0.55/0.45 blend of two saturating terms. Neither number is explained anywhere.
formulas.validated: No. No script, no backtest, no doc. Config and inline fallback agree, which pins the value but says nothing about whether it is right.

formulas.name: KTC value adjustment (processV)
formulas.expression: s = (0.05·(value/t)^1.3 + 0.05·(value/(1.05·maxInTrade))^6 + 0.1)·value;  if nerfIndex>0: s ×= max(0.6, 1 − 0.15·nerfIndex);  if s<0: s /= 4
formulas.inputs: each side's player values, max value in the trade, top-of-board reference
formulas.constants: 0.05 / 0.05 / 0.1, exponents 1.3 and 6, nerf 0.15 floor 0.6, KTC_T_REFERENCE=10041, KTC_MAX_PLAYER_VAL=10000, KTC_VARIANCE_PCT=5. All three copies (JS, ktc_va.py, market_value_adjustment.py) carry identical values — I diffed them.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: value ≤ 0 returns 0 — appropriate, since an unpriced asset genuinely earns no consolidation premium.
formulas.mathIssues: None. It is a verbatim port of a third-party algorithm, not a model this repo owns.
formulas.validated: Yes, uniquely well for a ported formula: 100 fresh KTC captures across 15 topologies in scripts/ktc_va_observations.json, RMS error 69.6% → 39.3% versus the formula it replaced, reproducible via scripts/calibrate_va_formula.py, pinned by tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py.

formulas.name: Monte Carlo trade win probability
formulas.expression: For each of 50,000 draws: sample each asset from a piecewise-linear distribution anchored at (p10,p50,p90), correlate via the rho ladder, compare side totals. winProbA = fraction of draws where A > B.
formulas.inputs: per-asset p10/p50/p90 band; team/position pairs for correlation
formulas.constants: _DEFAULT_SIMS=50_000; band width ±15% (0.85 / 1.15) on BOTH sides; correlation rhos 0.55 same-team-same-pos / 0.35 stack / 0.25 same-team-other / 0.15 same-pos-diff-team, max_rho 0.85; scoring-fit weight default 0.30 in the exception branch.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `row.get("valueBand") or {}` then falls straight through to the synthetic band. There is no "unknown uncertainty" state — every asset is asserted to have exactly ±15% dispersion.
formulas.mathIssues: I traced the producer: src/canonical/confidence_intervals.stamp_bands_on_players has no caller and the value_confidence_intervals flag is False (src/api/feature_flags.py:63), and feature_flags.py:57-61 says so in as many words. So the `if band.get("p50")` branch is unreachable on live data and the fallback IS the model. A constant relative width for every asset means the win probability reduces to a deterministic function of the two side totals plus the correlation ladder — it carries no per-player uncertainty information at all.
formulas.validated: No. The rhos and the ±15% are undocumented priors. The output carries an honest disclaimer string ("NOT a real-world win probability") but the disclaimer describes it as sampling "consensus-band samples", which is exactly what it is not doing.

formulas.name: League-adjusted structural scarcity factor
formulas.expression: delta = (lineupScarcity − reference_lineup_scarcity) × sensitivity;  axis_factor = 1 + delta;  combined = Π axis.effective_factor;  clamped to [1−0.25, 1+0.25];  adjusted = consensus × combined
formulas.inputs: lineupScarcity measured from this league's 12 rosters via compute_scarcity
formulas.constants: reference_lineup_scarcity=0.5 (a bare default parameter, never overridden by any caller — I grepped), sensitivity=0.20, MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT=0.25, tier confidence weights {absent 0.0, structuralOnly 0.45, marketMeasured 0.70, scoringMeasured 0.70, projectionCorroborated 0.90}, _MIN_RELATIVE_MOVE=0.001
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Exemplary. An unmeasurable position returns an ABSENT axis with factor forced inert, and the code notes this is so "an unmeasurable position contributes nothing rather than a prior". compute_scarcity likewise excludes unpriced players (`if base and value > 0`) rather than counting them at zero.
formulas.mathIssues: reference_lineup_scarcity=0.5 is the pivot of the whole overlay — every position above it gets lifted and every position below trimmed — and it is an undocumented literal in a keyword default. It is also the exact shape of the "neutral default indistinguishable from a measurement" problem: 0.5 is a plausible lineupScarcity reading, so nothing downstream can tell "this position is at the reference" from "the reference was never chosen".
formulas.validated: The FEATURE is validated better than almost anything else here (docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md: 572 players against realized 2025 scoring, paired bootstrap, verdict "no difference detected, keep it a toggle"). The CONSTANTS inside it are not. The backtest also surfaces that five of eight positions get a single constant factor, which by construction cannot reorder anything within that position.

formulas.name: Public-league trade grade
formulas.expression: side_total = Σ max(asset_value, 1.0)^1.65;  pct = (max_side − min_side)/max_side × 100;  grade = band(pct)
formulas.inputs: a valuation callable built from the private contract
formulas.constants: _GRADE_ALPHA=1.65, bands 3 / 8 / 15 / 25 / 40
formulas.missingDataBehavior: An asset the pipeline cannot price yields val=0.0, floored to 1.0, contributing 1^1.65 = 1 — numerically zero against a real asset's 5000^1.65 ≈ 4.3e5. The side is then graded normally. Only the all-sides-zero case is special-cased.
formulas.mathIssues: A one-for-one trade where one side received an unpriced player produces pct ≈ 100 and grades "Big win" / "Fleeced". The floor was added for cross-surface consistency with the private page, which has the same hole.
formulas.validated: Bands and alpha match the frontend exactly (I diffed all six numbers plus the hex colors). Neither copy is measured against anything.

formulas.name: Auction MaxBid / Enforce Up To
formulas.expression: Theoretical Max(p) = PreDraft × (1 + Aggression × (BA−1)) × tierInflation(p) × phaseMultiplier;  Winning bid = min(Theoretical Max, topCompetitorMax + 1);  Enforce Up To = Inflated Fair × Enforce%
formulas.inputs: board values rescaled to a $1200 budget, live draft state, per-team remaining budgets
formulas.constants: DEFAULT_TOTAL_BUDGET 1200, DEFAULT_TEAM_COUNT 12, DEFAULT_AGGRESSION 0.09, DEFAULT_ENFORCE_PCT 0.8, PHASE_LATE_BOOST 0.5, TIER_CONFIDENCE_MIN_SAMPLES 3, TIER_SCARCITY_URGENT 0.3, SPEND_UP_PRESSURE_MIN 0.6, SPEND_UP_MDV_FLOOR 10, NOMINATION_DECAY 0.8, TIER_INTEREST_MIN 0.2, TIER_DEFS cutoffs $60/25/8/3
formulas.missingDataBehavior: tierForPreDraft coerces a non-numeric PreDraft to 0 via `Number(preDraft) || 0`, landing the player in tier D ("Min") rather than excluding him — an unpriced player is presented as a $0-tier asset, not as unknown.
formulas.mathIssues: Tier inflation is confidence-blended toward 1.0 below 3 samples, which is the right instinct; nothing else here degrades on thin data.
formulas.validated: No. Every constant is a hand-set prior with an explanatory comment. The defaults are stated to "match the sheet's Settings block", i.e. they are transcribed from a spreadsheet, not fitted.

formulas.name: Cohen's-d tier walk (unwired)
formulas.expression: d = (mean(current tier) − value(next player)) / stdev(remaining pool); new tier when d > per-position threshold
formulas.inputs: players sorted by descending value
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a — never runs on live data.
formulas.mathIssues: Using the remaining-pool stdev rather than the current tier's is a deliberate and correct choice (the docstring explains the tier stdev tends to zero).
formulas.validated: No, and the config says so at length: "these are still HAND-SET PRIORS and have never been fitted… No workflow invokes the fitter, so the 'refit monthly' cadence described here has never run." What the config does not say is that the module has no live caller at all.

findings.title: The /rankings methodology panel shows users a value formula whose constants exist nowhere in the codebase
findings.rootCause: The methodology list is a hand-written JSX literal that was never updated when the curve constants moved. It quotes midpoint 45 and slope 1.10; the live rank-form constants are 65.4 / 0.910 and the live board is actually built by the percentile-form curve (c=0.11, s=1.11), a different functional form entirely.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/rankings/board-sections.jsx:34 — `value = max(1, min(9999, round(1 + 9998 / (1 + ((rank-1)/45)^1.10))))`. Rendered at app/rankings/page.jsx:1311 via `<MethodologySection />`. The live constants are src/canonical/player_valuation.py:82-83 — `HILL_MIDPOINT: float = 65.4` / `HILL_SLOPE: float = 0.910` — and :121-122 `HILL_PERCENTILE_C: float = 0.1100` / `HILL_PERCENTILE_S: float = 1.110`. I grepped the whole repo for a 45 midpoint: the only hits are INTEREST_HALF_LIFE_DAYS = 45.0 and unrelated data.
findings.userImpact: I reproduced both curves numerically. Displayed vs live rank-form value: rank 25 → 6663 vs 7134 (−471); rank 50 → 4766 vs 5653 (−887); rank 100 → 2959 vs 4068 (−1109); rank 200 → 1632 vs 2665 (−1033); rank 800 → 406 vs 931 (−525). A user who checks the published formula against a displayed value will find it disagrees by up to ~1100 points on the 1–9999 scale, and will not be able to tell whether the formula or the board is wrong. The same panel (line 31) also states the confidence rule as "spread ≤ 30 / ≤ 80", which is the retired ordinal rule.
findings.recommendedFix: Stop hand-writing the formula in JSX. The backend already stamps `methodology.formula` and `hillCurves` on the contract (data_contract.py::_build_hill_curves_block); render those. If a literal must stay, it has to be the percentile form with the current (c, s) and a note that the board is a blend of many such votes, not a single curve evaluation.

findings.title: The contract's own methodology.confidenceBuckets block describes a rule the pipeline stopped using
findings.rootCause: The confidence bucket implementation was migrated to a percentile-spread basis but the served methodology block still describes the legacy absolute-ordinal rule. The only test that touches it asserts the key exists, never its content.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:8857-8859 — `"high": "2+ sources, sourceRankSpread <= 30", "medium": "2+ sources, sourceRankSpread <= 80", "low": "single source or sourceRankSpread > 80"`. The live branch is :1896-1900 — `if percentile_spread is not None: if percentile_spread <= _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_HIGH` (0.08) … `<= _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_MEDIUM` (0.20). The 30/80 pair at :113-117 is labelled in code as a "Legacy absolute-ordinal fallback for callers that don't pass a percentile spread". Guard: tests/api/test_trust_confidence.py:450 only does `self.assertIn("confidenceBuckets", meth)`.
findings.userImpact: Any consumer — the UI methodology panel, an API client, a future maintainer — reading the served contract learns the wrong rule. The two rules are not equivalent: an ordinal spread of 25 on a 280-row source is a 0.089 percentile spread (medium), while the same 25 on a 500-row source is 0.050 (high). The documented rule and the live rule can disagree about the same row.
findings.recommendedFix: Generate the confidenceBuckets description from the constants that the live branch actually reads, and extend test_trust_confidence.py to assert the described thresholds equal _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_HIGH/MEDIUM rather than merely asserting the key is present.

findings.title: frontend/lib/thresholds.js claims to mirror backend confidence thresholds "exactly" and mirrors the retired ones
findings.rootCause: Same migration as above, from the other side. The frontend copied the ordinal constants and a sync note; the backend then moved its live path to percentiles and the frontend was never revisited.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/thresholds.js:15 — "These mirror the backend confidence bucket thresholds exactly"; :8 — "Python: _CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH (30), _CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_MEDIUM (80)"; :21,:24 declare 30 and 80. They ARE used for a decision: frontend/lib/edge-helpers.js:88 gates the "Consensus asset" signal on `(spread == null || spread <= CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH)`.
findings.userImpact: The "Consensus asset" chip on /rankings is gated on an ordinal spread threshold that the backend no longer uses for confidence, while the same chip also requires `row.confidenceBucket === "high"` which IS percentile-derived. The chip therefore applies two different definitions of the same concept simultaneously — a row can be backend-high-confidence and still lose the chip on the stale ordinal gate. Because deeper sources have larger ordinal spreads for identical relative agreement, this suppresses the chip preferentially on players covered by deep boards.
findings.recommendedFix: Either drop the redundant ordinal gate (confidenceBucket already encodes the backend's answer) or export the percentile thresholds on the contract and gate on those. Update the file header, which currently asserts a parity that does not hold.

findings.title: The Monte Carlo trade simulator's uncertainty is a hardcoded ±15% for every asset, because the real band producer has no caller
findings.rootCause: monte_carlo.py was written to consume per-player p10/p50/p90 bands from Phase 4 confidence intervals. That producer was never wired: stamp_bands_on_players has no caller, rank_history_band has no caller, and the value_confidence_intervals flag is False. The `or {}` fallback silently became the model.
findings.evidence: src/trade/monte_carlo.py:372-380 — `# Fallback: synthesize a 15% band around the canonical value.` … `p10=_shifted(cv * 0.85), p50=_shifted(cv), p90=_shifted(cv * 1.15)`. The frontend duplicates it at frontend/components/ui/MonteCarloButton.jsx:55-57 — `p10 = v * 0.85; p50 = v; p90 = v * 1.15;`. The producer's status is recorded in the repo itself: src/api/feature_flags.py:57-63 — "the badge is exported from the ui barrel and imported by no page, ``stamp_bands_on_players`` has no caller, and ``rank_history_band`` has no caller either", `"value_confidence_intervals": False`. I grepped for any other producer of `valueBand`: there is none.
findings.userImpact: Rendered on /trade (TradeMeter.jsx:107) and /waivers (ManualAddDrop.jsx:459) as a win probability. Because every asset gets the same relative width, the simulation carries zero per-player uncertainty information — a rock-solid consensus QB1 and a wildly-disputed rookie are modelled as equally uncertain. The output reduces to a deterministic function of the two side totals and the correlation ladder, dressed as a 50,000-draw simulation. The disclaimer string says it samples "consensus-band samples", which is precisely what it is not doing.
findings.recommendedFix: Either wire stamp_bands_on_players so the real per-player dispersion (which the contract already computes as sourceSpread / percentileSpread) reaches the simulator, or stop presenting the output as a probability and label it what it is — a fixed-width sensitivity band. Do not leave a silently-unreachable preferred branch as the documented behaviour.

findings.title: marketConfidence is structurally capped at 0.594 by a stale divisor and is still surfaced as a confidence number
findings.rootCause: `site_score = site_count / 8.0` was sized when ~10 scraper SITES were enabled. Today exactly three numeric dash keys exist (ktc, ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc), so site_count ∈ {1,2,3} and site_score ≤ 0.375, capping the weighted result at 0.375·0.65 + 1.00·0.35 = 0.59375.
findings.evidence: Dynasty Scraper.py:6031 — `site_score = _clampf(float(site_count) / 8.0, 0.20, 1.00)`; :6033 — `conf = _clampf((site_score * 0.65) + (cv_score * 0.35), 0.20, 1.00)`. I measured the live export (exports/latest/dynasty_data.js): n=839, min 0.3447, max 0.5938, median 0.4897 — the observed maximum equals the theoretical cap to four decimals. The diagnosis is already written down at src/api/terminal.py:910-928, where it was used to justify retiring the low_conf_unstable rule.
findings.userImpact: The field flows to the contract as `marketConfidence` (data_contract.py:8312) and to frontend rows as `confidence` (dynasty-data.js:1023, :1201), where PlayerPopup.jsx:164 renders `confidence {Math.round(ros.confidence * 100)}%` for the ROS variant. A metric labelled confidence that can never exceed 59% and whose entire live range is 0.34–0.59 is a broken gauge: it cannot distinguish a well-covered player from a thin one, because site_count barely varies. It also carries a `.get("marketConfidence", 0.5)` default at Dynasty Scraper.py:6197 which, at a live median of 0.4897, would be completely indistinguishable from a real reading if it were ever reachable.
findings.recommendedFix: Either recompute the divisor from the current enabled-source count (scripts/simulate_market_confidence_divisor.py already exists and its output is in docs/measurements/), or retire the field and route every consumer to the contract's `confidenceBucket`, which is computed from the real 21-source registry. Do not leave a capped metric labelled as a percentage.

findings.title: The scraper composite weights one vendor's two boards at 70% of the blend, and 11 of its 13 declared weights are inert
findings.rootCause: SITE_WEIGHTS predates the current source set. Its keys are old scraper dash keys; most no longer appear in the payload, so `SITE_WEIGHTS.get(dash_key, 1.0)` silently returns 1.0. The two keys that do appear are `ktc` (weight 1.3) and `ktcSfTep` (no entry → 1.0) — the same vendor's standard and TE++ boards, which are near-identical row by row.
findings.evidence: Dynasty Scraper.py:5609-5622 declares 13 weights; :6102 — `wNorms.append((norm, SITE_WEIGHTS.get(dash_key, 1.0)))`. I enumerated every numeric dash key across all 1074 players in exports/latest/dynasty_data.js: exactly {ktc: 590, ktcSfTep: 464, idpTradeCalc: 898}. Eleven declared keys (dlfSf, dlfIdp, dlfRsf, dlfRidp, draftSharks, dynastyDaddy, dynastyNerds, fantasyCalc, fantasyPros, fantasyProsIdp, yahoo) never appear. On a 3-source player (A.J. Brown: ktc 5008, ktcSfTep 5008, idpTradeCalc 4936, `_sites: 3`) the KTC family carries 2.3/3.3 = 69.7% of the composite.
findings.userImpact: The composite is `values.overall` / `values.finalAdjusted` on the contract (data_contract.py:8184-8194) and is the value the public-league trade grader reads (public_activity_valuation.py:68-78 chain), the finder's fallback branch reads (finder.py:451, :946), and the frontend falls back to for rows the canonical board leaves unranked (dynasty-data.js:951-955). Those surfaces are priced on a board where one vendor has 70% of the vote. CLAUDE.md's statement that blend weights are "all 1.0 by policy" is true of _RANKING_SOURCES and false here, so the policy claim does not cover the pipeline it needs to.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the eleven dead keys so the file states what it does, and decide explicitly whether ktc and ktcSfTep should both vote — they are the same market and currently double-count. If the composite is only meant to be a legacy artifact, say so in the module and stop routing user-facing grades through it.

findings.title: Public-league trade grading prices an unpriceable asset at ~zero and still emits a confident grade
findings.rootCause: Assets the canonical pipeline cannot value return 0.0 from the valuation callable, are floored to 1.0, and then enter the alpha-weighted sum as 1^1.65 = 1. Only the case where EVERY side is zero is special-cased.
findings.evidence: src/public_league/activity.py:118 — `total += pow(max(val, 1.0), _GRADE_ALPHA)` with `_GRADE_ALPHA = 1.65` (:49); the zero guard at :123-129 fires only `if max_w <= 0`. The valuation callable returns 0.0 for anything unpriced: src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:78 — `return 0.0`.
findings.userImpact: A 1-for-1 trade where one side received a player the board does not price yields pct = (5000^1.65 − 1)/5000^1.65 × 100 ≈ 100, which lands in the top band: one manager is publicly labelled "Big win" and the other "Fleeced", on the public league activity feed, purely because a name failed to resolve. The comment at :110-117 shows the floor was added for consistency with the private page, which means both surfaces share the hole.
findings.recommendedFix: Track how many assets on each side failed to price and suppress the grade block (or degrade it to an explicit "cannot grade — N assets unpriced") when any side has an unpriced asset above a trivial share. A missing value is an abstention, not a zero.

findings.title: values.displayValue is read by two modules and produced by none
findings.rootCause: `_canonicalDisplayValue` is the preferred head of the value fallback chain on both the backend public-grading path and the frontend materializer, but nothing in the repository ever writes it.
findings.evidence: Read at src/api/data_contract.py:8188 — `display = _to_int_or_none(p_data.get("_canonicalDisplayValue"))` — and at src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:70 (`for key in ("displayValue", "overall", "finalAdjusted", "rawComposite")`), and at frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:951 — `const displayVal = Number(player?.values?.displayValue ?? 0) || 0;`. I grepped every .py for a writer: only those two readers. I counted occurrences in the live scraper output (exports/latest/dynasty_data.js): `_canonicalDisplayValue` 0, `_composite` 1074, `_finalAdjusted` 1074.
findings.userImpact: Every consumer silently falls through to the next link — which is the scraper composite, a scale running ~14% above the canonical board (finder.py:58 records `BOARD_TO_COMPOSITE_K = 0.875` as the measured median ratio). The frontend's `displayVal` is permanently 0, so `values.full` is `backendValue || internalVal` (dynasty-data.js:1008) — the composite whenever rankDerivedValue is absent, i.e. for every row past OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT (800). The value concept silently switches partway down the board.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete `displayValue` from both chains, or produce it. A three-deep fallback chain whose first link never exists is a promise the contract does not keep, and it hides which scale a given number came from. If the fallthrough is intended, the chain should stamp which link answered.

findings.title: _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N ships at 500 while its own backtest recommends 400, and the code comment does not mention the backtest
findings.rootCause: The backtest was run and its recommendation recorded, then the constant was left at 500 with an independent narrative rationale. Neither the code nor CLAUDE.md notes that a measurement exists and disagrees.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:4933 — `_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N: int = 500`, justified at :4927-4932 as "500 aligns with KTC's native pool, the retail market's natural scale". reports/percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md, Recommendation section: "**Promote N=400** (+2.01% vs N=500 on the value-weighted metric). Best on the unweighted metric was N=1000." Table: N=400 VW 0.293 vs N=500 VW 0.299.
findings.userImpact: Small in magnitude — 2% on a stability metric — but it is a live disagreement between a shipped constant and the repository's own measurement of that constant, with no record of the decision. A future maintainer reading either artifact alone will conclude the other does not exist. Given how carefully every other blend constant records its backtest verdict (α, λ, MAD all cite reports/), this one is the outlier.
findings.recommendedFix: Either adopt 400 or add one line to the comment stating that the backtest recommends 400, that 500 was kept for the KTC-pool-alignment reason, and that the gap is 2% on the VW metric. A deliberate override is fine; an undocumented one is not.

findings.title: A dead per-position CV table in playoff_sim.py claims to be calibrated and duplicates one that calls itself legacy
findings.rootCause: The simulator was migrated to read a calibrated PointsModel; the old inline table was left behind, unreferenced, with its original provenance claim intact.
findings.evidence: src/ros/playoff_sim.py:108-127 defines `_PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION` and `_DEFAULT_PLAYER_CV = 0.55` under the comment "Calibrated from public weekly-scoring datasets". I counted references: `grep -c "_PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION" src/ros/playoff_sim.py` returns 1 — the definition. `_DEFAULT_PLAYER_CV` likewise appears only at its definition. The live values come from `load_points_model()` (:675, :965) in src/league_intel/sim_calibration.py, whose byte-identical table at :83-97 is introduced as "Legacy constants, kept ONLY as the documented fallback".
findings.userImpact: Two contradictory provenance claims for the same twelve numbers. The dead copy asserts calibration; the live copy asserts it is a legacy fallback. Since data/league_intel/sim_points_model.json does not exist in this checkout, load_points_model() returns the fallback, so the numbers a user's playoff odds actually rest on are the ones labelled legacy — while a maintainer grepping for the CV table first finds the copy labelled calibrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the dead table and constant from playoff_sim.py. If any calibration evidence for these CVs exists, attach it to the surviving copy in sim_calibration.py; otherwise leave that copy's honest "legacy fallback" label as the only statement.

findings.title: config/tiers/thresholds.json and src/scoring/tiering.py are wired to nothing
findings.rootCause: The Cohen's-d tiering module was superseded by the rank-gap detect_tiers in player_valuation.py, but was left in place with a config file that reads as live tuning.
findings.evidence: I grepped every importer of src.scoring.tiering across the repo: `scripts/refit_tier_thresholds.py:42` and `tests/scoring/test_tiering.py`. No route, no pipeline, no server import. The live tier ids come from src/api/data_contract.py:2016-2020 — `from src.canonical.player_valuation import detect_tiers` … `tier_ids, _gaps, _scores, _boundaries = detect_tiers(series, player_ids)` — which uses TIER_GAP_WINDOW=7 / TIER_GAP_THRESHOLD=2.0 / TIER_MIN_SIZE=3 (player_valuation.py:47-49), not the per-position d thresholds. src/api/feature_flags.py:68-72 independently records that `stamp_tiers_on_players` is called only from the refit script.
findings.userImpact: Nothing breaks — but an operator editing config/tiers/thresholds.json to change tiering will see no effect, and the file's own comment describes a refit cadence and a >15% PR policy for a pipeline that does not exist. Meanwhile the constants that DO set the tiers users see (7 / 2.0 / 3) carry no rationale and no config surface at all.
findings.recommendedFix: Add one line to the config's _comment stating that no live code path reads it. Separately, give the three live detect_tiers constants a rationale comment or a config home — they decide where every tier divider on the rankings board falls and are currently the least-documented user-visible constants in the pipeline.

findings.title: The league-adjusted board pivots on an undocumented 0.5 reference that is indistinguishable from a real measurement
findings.rootCause: `reference_lineup_scarcity` is a keyword default with no comment, no config entry, and no caller override. It is the origin of the entire structural-scarcity axis: positions above 0.5 are lifted, positions below are trimmed.
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/adjustment.py:215 — `reference_lineup_scarcity: float = 0.5,` and :247 — `delta = (value - reference_lineup_scarcity) * sensitivity`. I grepped the repo for any caller passing it: none — src/league_intel/ and src/api/ contain no other reference to the parameter name. `sensitivity: float = 0.20` (:216) is equally undocumented.
findings.userImpact: lineupScarcity is a 0–1 quantity, so 0.5 is a perfectly plausible measured reading. Nothing downstream — not the rationale string, not the explanation payload, not the audit trail — distinguishes "this position sits exactly at the reference" from "nobody ever chose a reference". The axis is the only live per-position input to a board the user can switch to on /rankings and which threads into trade suggestions, the finder, angles, waivers, the terminal and the simulator via valuation_mode. This is the one constant in the overlay that decides its direction, and it is the one with no justification. The surrounding module is otherwise meticulous — every EvidenceTier and every guardrail carries a paragraph — which makes the omission conspicuous rather than typical.
findings.recommendedFix: Either derive the reference from the measured distribution of lineupScarcity across positions in this league (the natural choice, and it makes the axis zero-sum by construction), or state in a docstring that 0.5 is an arbitrary midpoint prior and surface it in the explanation payload alongside the measured value, the way partner.py surfaces BASE_ACCEPTANCE_PRIOR.

findings.title: Team-impact verdict thresholds and normalizations decide Accept vs Decline with no stated rationale anywhere
findings.rootCause: The config file and its inline Python fallback were written together and neither carries a _comment. There is no measurement script, no backtest, and no doc reference for any of the seven weights or four verdict bands.
findings.evidence: config/trade/team_impact.json — `"fitNormalization": 4000, "equityNormalization": 2500, "compositeFitWeight": 0.55, "compositeEquityWeight": 0.45` and `"verdictThresholds": {"accept": 20, "leanAccept": 8, "leanDecline": -8, "decline": -20}`. Applied at src/trade/team_impact.py:433-439 — `fit_score = _clamp(100.0 * fit_raw / fit_norm, -100.0, 100.0)` … `composite = cw_fit * fit_score + cw_eq * equity_score`. Rendered at frontend/app/trade/trade-sections.jsx:312 — `const ti = simResult?.teamImpact;`. No test file for this module exists under tests/trade/.
findings.userImpact: The two normalization constants set the exchange rate between roster fit and trade equity, and because both terms saturate at ±100 they also decide which term can dominate. 4000 and 2500 mean a fit swing is worth 0.625× an equity swing of the same board-point size, before the 0.55/0.45 composite weights are even applied. This is the number that flips the verdict a user reads on the trade page, and nobody has written down why it is 4000 rather than 3000 or 6000. Separately, `int(a.get("value") or 0)` at :117, :148 and :219-232 means an unpriced asset contributes 0 to starter value and to the contend index, and the verdict still renders at full confidence.
findings.recommendedFix: Two things. Add a provenance comment to config/trade/team_impact.json for each number, even if the honest content is "hand-set prior, never measured" — that is what config/bdvm/params_v1.json and config/sharp/scoring_v2.json do and it is the right standard. And count unpriced assets, refusing or degrading the verdict rather than treating them as zero-value.

findings.title: A second, different pick-year discount sits in the tree in a module that is 95% dead but 5% live
findings.rootCause: src/canonical/calibration.py belonged to the retired offline canonical-build path. Its callers were removed, but one symbol — to_display_value — is still imported by the live suggestions module, so the file cannot simply be deleted and its stale constants remain readable as if current.
findings.evidence: src/canonical/calibration.py:105 — `PICK_YEAR_DISCOUNT = 0.70`, against config/weights/pick_year_discount.json — `"offsetDiscounts": {"0": 1.00, "1": 0.82, "2": 0.66, "3": 0.53}`. Also stranded there: `LEGACY_PICK_ROUND_CURVE` (:94-100, 6124/5251/4367/3425/3146/2600), `CALIBRATION_EXPONENT = 2.5`, `UNIVERSE_SCALES` and `INTERNAL_SCALE_MAX = 7800`. The single live import is src/trade/suggestions.py:26 — `from src.canonical.calibration import to_display_value` — reached only at :407-408 inside `build_asset_pool`, the legacy asset-dict path; server.py:5910 calls `build_asset_pool_from_contract` instead, which sets `display_value=cv_int, calibrated_value=cv_int` from `rankDerivedValue` directly (:634-635).
findings.userImpact: No live miscalculation — I traced the call and to_display_value is not reached on the server path, and if it ever were it would multiply an already-9999-scale value by 9999/7800 = 1.282×. The harm is navigational: a maintainer searching for "pick year discount" finds two different answers (0.70 and 0.82) in two plausible-looking locations, and a hardcoded round-value table that looks authoritative and is six months stale.
findings.recommendedFix: Move to_display_value to a neutral module (or inline it), delete src/canonical/calibration.py, and drop the legacy build_asset_pool path if nothing but tests calls it. Failing that, put a module-level RETIRED banner on calibration.py the way player_valuation.py's SCOPE NOTE does.

findings.title: VALUE_BANDS documents a derivation from rank→value reference points the current curve does not produce
findings.rootCause: The band cutoffs were chosen against an older curve and the derivation comment was never re-checked after the 2026-07-30 constant re-tune.
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/rankings-helpers.js:66-68 — "Bands are derived from the rank-to-value curve properties: rank 1 → 9999, rank 12 → ~5700, rank 45 → ~5000, rank 200 → ~1200". I evaluated the live rank-form curve (HILL_MIDPOINT 65.4, HILL_SLOPE 0.910): rank 12 → 8350, rank 45 → 5892, rank 200 → 2665. Only rank 1 still holds.
findings.userImpact: Low — the bands themselves are labelled "descriptive" and a badge boundary is a presentation choice. But the stated derivation is now wrong by a factor of 1.5–2.2, which means the bands no longer sit where the comment says they sit relative to the board: the comment implies the S/D+ boundary at 6000 falls somewhere below rank 12, while on the live curve rank 12 is 8350 and 6000 sits near rank 43. Anyone re-deriving the bands from that comment will move them in the wrong direction.
findings.recommendedFix: Re-evaluate the reference ranks against the current curve and update the comment, or drop the derivation claim and state the bands as chosen presentation cutoffs.

findings.title: The /draft rookie-pool fallback prefers the scraper composite over the canonical board while asserting they are the same field
findings.rootCause: A defensive fallback chain was written from an incorrect premise about which contract field carries the blended value, and put the composite ahead of rankDerivedValue.
findings.evidence: frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:4241-4243 — "The raw contract stamps the blended value as ``values.overall`` and ``rankDerivedValue``" — then :4249-4255 orders the chain `p?.values?.overall, p?.rankDerivedValue, p?.values?.displayValue, p?.values?.finalAdjusted, p?.values?.full`. But values.overall is `_finalAdjusted` (src/api/data_contract.py:8184-8194), the scraper composite, and src/trade/finder.py:53-58 records the measured offset between the two scales: `BOARD_TO_COMPOSITE_K = 0.875` = median(board/composite), regenerable with scripts/measure_engine_value_divergence.py.
findings.userImpact: Bounded, for two reasons I verified: the path only runs when the server-side rookie pool is unavailable (:4297), and the resulting values are immediately rescaled to the $1200 budget (:4386-4391), so the ~14% level offset washes out. What does not wash out is ORDERING — the composite and the board disagree per-player, not just in level, so the fallback rookie board can rank rookies differently from every other surface in the app. The comment also misinforms the next reader about what values.overall is.
findings.recommendedFix: Put rankDerivedValue first in the chain and correct the comment to say values.overall is the scraper composite, not the blended board.

findings.title: BDVM is flag-on by default with no projection snapshot present in the repository
findings.rootCause: The engine's data lives in gitignored data/bdvm/, produced on the production host by a weekly timer. The flag default was flipped to True on the strength of a snapshot that exists only there.
findings.evidence: src/api/feature_flags.py:225 — `"bdvm_engine": True` and :338 — `"bdvm_engine": LIVE`. `test -d data/bdvm` → missing in this checkout. Gates at server.py:5437-5440 return `{"error": "feature_disabled"}` only for the flag; the no-snapshot case is a separate 503 the frontend distinguishes via classifyBdvmFailure.
findings.userImpact: None in this repository — the endpoints degrade correctly and every BDVM surface (the /rankings Fund-gap column, the /draft panel, the /trade Fundamentals check) is built to vanish silently on a 503. Whether production has live data is Not Verifiable from Repository. Recorded here only so the registry is honest about which BDVM constants are exercised: in this checkout, none of them are. All of config/bdvm/params_v1.json, pick_outcomes_v1.json and event_types_v1.json state in their own _comment blocks that every number is a prior and not backtested truth, which is the correct posture — but it means that if prod does have a snapshot, roughly 200 uncalibrated numbers are producing a second value board and gating signal-alert emails.
findings.recommendedFix: Nothing to fix in code. Worth stating in CLAUDE.md that the flag being ON does not imply the data exists, since the doc currently reads as though the snapshot is a settled fact ("scripts/bdvm_build_baseline.py writes a real snapshot (2,815 records for 2026)") — true on prod, not verifiable here.

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. I read every file in config/ (28 files) and swept src/ (324 numeric module-level constants), server.py, Dynasty Scraper.py, scripts/, frontend/lib/ (43 modules), frontend/components/ (40) and frontend/app/. Every claim below is from code I read; where a formula was non-obvious I reproduced it numerically in python against exports/latest/dynasty_data.js (the 2026-08-04 live scrape, 1074 players) rather than reasoning about it.

FRONTEND/BACKEND DUPLICATE PAIRS — I computed the diff on every one I found:
• Source registry (21 sources, keys/order/weights): src/api/data_contract.py::_RANKING_SOURCES vs frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js::RANKING_SOURCES — IDENTICAL, all weights 1.0. Guarded by tests/api/test_source_registry_parity.py.
• KTC value adjustment: 10000 / 10041 / 5 across frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:249-264, src/trade/ktc_va.py:27-29, src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py:15-17 — ALL THREE MATCH.
• Trade grade bands: 3/8/15/25/40 + alpha 1.65, src/public_league/activity.py:49-54 vs frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:86-99 — IDENTICAL including hex colors.
• Terminal tier cutoffs: 8500/6500/3000, src/api/terminal.py:48-53 vs frontend/components/terminal/TeamCommandHeader.jsx:36-41 — MATCH.
• Monte Carlo synthetic band: 0.85/1.15, src/trade/monte_carlo.py:378-380 vs frontend/components/ui/MonteCarloButton.jsx:55-57 — MATCH (both wrong for a different reason, see findings).
• Auction power: 0.35/1.25/0.15, frontend/lib/auction-power.js:13-15 vs src/api/auction_power.py — mirror declared and enforced by tests/api/test_auction_power_parity.py.
• Confidence spreads: 30/80, frontend/lib/thresholds.js:21,24 vs src/api/data_contract.py:116-117 — values match, but the backend's live path uses 0.08/0.20 instead. This is the one pair where matching numbers hide a real divergence. Finding above.
• TE curve: config/weights/te_premium_curve.json vs src/league_intel/te_premium.py:85-100 — a=k identical, floor 1.209206 vs 1.2092 (6e-6, unreachable unless the config is deleted).
• team_impact config vs its inline Python fallback (15 numbers) — IDENTICAL.
• Hill scope masters: src/canonical/player_valuation.py vs config/model_registry/hill_scope_masters.json champion v2 (8 constants) — IDENTICAL.
Net: the parity discipline in this repo is genuinely good. The failures are not drifted values; they are constants that agree with each other while both being detached from the live code path.

SAME CONCEPT, DIFFERENT VALUE IN MULTIPLE BACKEND MODULES:
• Single-source haircut — THREE values: 0.30 (data_contract.py:5073, canonical board), 0.55–0.82 (Dynasty Scraper.py:5597-5598, composite), 0.88 (finder.py:83, legacy branch). finder.py:70-82 explicitly works through why its own is not a stacked double-haircut, so this is understood rather than accidental, but three numbers for one idea is a hazard.
• Pick-year discount — 0.82/0.66/0.53 (config, live) vs 0.70 (src/canonical/calibration.py:105, dead). Finding above.
• Per-position weekly CV — identical tables in src/ros/playoff_sim.py:113 (dead, claims calibration) and src/league_intel/sim_calibration.py:83 (live, claims legacy fallback). Finding above.
• Top-N quality gate — 150 in both suggestions.py:239 and finder.py:132, same number, deliberately DIFFERENT boards. Documented at length in both files and in CLAUDE.md; correct as-is, flagged only because a future "unify these" refactor would be a regression.
• "Max value" — 9999 (_DISPLAY_SCALE_MAX), 10000 (KTC_MAX_PLAYER_VAL), 10041 (KTC_T_REFERENCE), 10000 (BDVM trade_value_max), 7800 (INTERNAL_SCALE_MAX, dead). All correct in context; listing them because the near-identical values invite a wrong "consolidation".

NEUTRAL DEFAULTS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM MEASUREMENTS:
• reference_lineup_scarcity = 0.5 (adjustment.py:215) — the worst case, and a finding.
• `.get("marketConfidence", 0.5)` at Dynasty Scraper.py:6197 against a live median of 0.4897 — currently unreachable, but a perfect trap if the producer ever changes.
• `.get("dispersionCV", 0.0)` at :6198 — 0.0 reads as perfect source agreement, the opposite of unknown. Also currently unreachable.
• Monte Carlo ±15% for every asset — a constant asserted as a measurement of dispersion. Finding.
• `_LEAGUE_CALIBRATION_BLEND = 0.5` (faab_recommender.py:69) — a genuine 50/50 policy choice, documented, not a trap.
• The repo also gets this RIGHT in several places worth naming: dynasty-data.js:1015-1025 and :1195-1205 both keep absent confidence as null with a comment explaining the bug the `|| 0` caused; adjustment.py returns an ABSENT axis "so an unmeasurable position contributes nothing rather than a prior"; compute_scarcity excludes unpriced players from the pool; partner.py's STRUCTURAL_COVERAGE_FLOOR exists specifically so "a defaulted term is an abstention, not a measurement, and abstentions must cost confidence or the score launders ignorance into certainty". That sentence is the standard the rest of the codebase should be held to.

MISSING DATA COERCED TO ZERO RATHER THAN EXCLUDED (399 `or 0` sites in src/ + server.py; these are the ones that change a user-facing decision):
• src/trade/team_impact.py:117, :148, :219-232, :414-415 — unpriced asset contributes 0 to starter value, contend index and top-10 share; full verdict still rendered.
• src/public_league/activity.py:118 — unpriced asset floored to 1, grades the other side "Fleeced". Finding.
• frontend/lib/draft-logic.js::tierForPreDraft — `Number(preDraft) || 0` puts an unpriced player in the "$0 Min" tier rather than excluding him.
• frontend/components/terminal/PlayerMarketMovement.jsx:102 — `confidence: Number(r.confidence) || 0`; I checked the consumers and it is carried but not used for sorting or a verdict, so this one is latent.
• frontend/lib/ros-index.js:93 — `Number(r.confidence) || 0` inside the duplicate-row tie-break; a row with unknown confidence loses to a row with genuinely-zero confidence identically, which is the right outcome by accident rather than by design.

CONSTANTS WITH REAL EMPIRICAL BACKING (so the registry is not all criticism): the Hill percentile masters (fitted, held-out-scored, human-promoted, with the registry's own _semantics block disclaiming that it measures market generalization and not truth); the rank-form curve (RMSE 821.8 → 89.8, stability-checked across 16 snapshots); the TE uplift curve (73 paired observations, R² 0.941); the KTC VA port (100 captured trades, RMS 69.6% → 39.3%); α and λ (2D grid over 25 snapshots, with the comment candidly noting the true optimum was degenerate); the disagreement thresholds (measured saturation before and after); the D-1 value-range guard (the failure mode was measured end-to-end); the league-adjusted board's decision NOT to be the default (572 players, realized 2025 scoring, paired bootstrap, honest "no difference detected"); and the row-count / coverage / staleness floors (all derived from live baselines and stated as such).

WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE A REAL FANTASY DECISION, bluntly. Trust: the canonical board's value (rankDerivedValue) and its rank — the blend is the most scrutinised code here and its constants are the best evidenced. Trust with the stated caveat: the league-adjusted lens, whose own backtest says it makes no measurable difference. Treat as opinion, not measurement: every trade-verdict threshold (team_impact 4000/2500/±20), every auction-draft prior on /draft, the waiver upgrade tiers, the FAAB modifiers, the injury discounts, and all of BDVM. Do not trust as stated: the Monte Carlo win probability (its uncertainty input is a constant), marketConfidence (structurally capped at 0.59), and anything the /rankings methodology panel says about the formula or the confidence rule.

CLAIMS IN CLAUDE.md / docs I CHECKED AND FOUND TRUE: the corridor clamp is IDP-only (verified — offense skipped at :4596, picks resolve to an empty anchor chain); _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA is 0.0 and diagnostics-only; the ROOKIE Hill master is declared but not routed; config/weights/default_weights.json is loaded by nothing (verified — its own header says so); the finder now reads the canonical board via board_values_from_contract; both trade engines gate at 150 on deliberately different boards; buildRows assigns a display ordinal only when the backend stamped no rank; the two overlays are composed server-side; picks carry factor 1.0 under the lens because compute_scarcity has no PICK key. CLAUDE.md is unusually accurate for a document of its size.

CLAIMS I FOUND FALSE OR INCOMPLETE: "Blend weights ... all 1.0 by policy" is true of _RANKING_SOURCES and false of Dynasty Scraper.py::SITE_WEIGHTS, which still feeds user-facing surfaces; the BDVM section reads as though a live snapshot is a settled fact when none exists in-repo; and the corridor clamp's own in-code docstring still justifies itself by a mechanism (the IDP calibration post-pass) that was deleted — CLAUDE.md flags this one itself, to its credit.

systems.outputScale: declared x min(1, depth/60); only 3 of 21 sources affected (factor 0.8333)
