formulas.name: Hill percentile curve (live board)
formulas.expression: p = clamp((rank-1)/(referenceN-1), 0, 1); V(p) = clamp(9999 / (1 + (p/c)^s), 1, 9999)
formulas.inputs: per-source dense ordinal rank; referenceN fixed at 500
formulas.constants: referenceN=500 (_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N). Scope masters, all verified equal to model-registry champion v2: OFFENSE c=0.11 s=1.11; IDP c=0.083 s=1.11; GLOBAL c=0.112 s=0.725; ROOKIE c=0.153 s=0.885 (refit tooling only). NO conflicting backend copy.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: a source with no rank for a row simply does not vote; a 0 from a source is treated as no opinion, never as a value
formulas.validated: Holdout-scored via src/model_registry/holdout.py; promotion is human-gated. NOT validated against realized fantasy outcomes.
formulas.mathIssues: Ranks past 500 clamp to p=1.0, so every player at rank 500 and rank 700 receives the identical value (verified: both 794 on OFFENSE). This is deliberate top-500-board behaviour but means the curve carries no information below rank 500 — the ordering past there comes entirely from the blend, not the curve.

formulas.name: Legacy rank-form Hill curve (reconstruction only)
formulas.expression: value = 1 + 9998 / (1 + ((max(1,rank)-1)/midpoint)^slope)
formulas.inputs: a historical consensus rank + scope
formulas.constants: OFFENSE midpoint=65.4 slope=0.910; IDP midpoint=64.6 slope=0.900. JS copy now agrees (65.4 / 0.91 / span 9998), pinned by tests/api/test_rank_form_frontend_parity.py. Three copies existed until 2026-07-30; the JS one was wrong on all three values (45 / 1.1 / ceiling 10000).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rank None or <=0 returns 0
formulas.validated: YES, and re-tuned. Fit against rankDerivedValue rather than retail source boards (the old 45/1.10 pair scored RMSE 821.8 on offense). I ran scripts/check_rank_form_drift.py on today's board: offense rmse 88.9 vs achievable floor 88.8; idp 74.5 vs 74.5. Alarmed weekly.
formulas.mathIssues: docs/idp-ranking-model.md:105 still publishes the retired 45 / 1.10 constants as the live board formula.

formulas.name: Count-aware mean-median blend
formulas.expression: n=1 -> passthrough; n=2 -> mean, MAD=half-range; n=3-4 -> (mean+median)/2 untrimmed; n>=5 -> drop one min + one max observation, then (mean+median)/2
formulas.inputs: per-source Hill values surviving Hampel, plus declared weights
formulas.constants: trim boundary n>=5; equal-weight epsilon 1e-9; weighted median uses cumulative-weight with midpoint interpolation on an exact half split
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty list -> (0.0, None); mismatched weight length or non-positive total weight falls back to the unweighted blend rather than raising — a malformed override cannot take down the board
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_weighted_blend.py proves equal-weight parity is bit-for-bit. Not outcome-validated.
formulas.mathIssues: Trimming is observation-based even in the weighted variant (by value, ignoring weight). Deliberate, to preserve exact equal-weight parity, but it means a heavily-weighted source can still be the trimmed extreme.

formulas.name: Hierarchical anchor + alpha shrinkage
formulas.expression: center = anchor_value + ALPHA * (subgroup_blend - anchor_value)
formulas.inputs: cross-market anchor value, subgroup (IDP or pick) blend
formulas.constants: ALPHA = 0.10. Applied to IDP and picks ONLY; offense takes the flat count-aware blend. Pick rows widen the anchor set to include ktcSfTep so KTC and IDPTC average as peer pick markets.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no anchor -> alphaShrinkage stamped 0.0 and the subgroup blend is used directly
formulas.validated: No. 0.10 is a judgment constant. docs/python-coverage-audit.md W-3 records that it had NO CI-blocking test before 2026-07-29 (only livedata-deselected modules referenced it).

formulas.name: Hampel per-player outlier filter
formulas.expression: drop v where |v - median| > max(K*MAD, MIN_THRESHOLD); refuse to leave fewer than 2 survivors; skip entirely when n < MIN_N
formulas.inputs: the per-source Hill values for one row
formulas.outputRange: a subset of the input set
formulas.constants: K=2.75, MIN_N=4, MIN_THRESHOLD=1000.0 Hill points. No backend duplicate.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n<4 -> no filtering at all
formulas.validated: No — K=2.75 is the textbook Hampel default, not fitted here.

formulas.name: Single-source retention haircut
formulas.expression: if surviving_source_count == 1 and not is_pick: blended_value *= 0.30
formulas.inputs: post-Hampel source count
formulas.constants: 0.30. Note src/trade/finder.py:83 keeps a SEPARATE legacy 0.88 discount (_LEGACY_SINGLE_SOURCE_DISCOUNT) for its composite fallback path — two different single-source discounts coexist by design, on two different scales.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a
formulas.validated: No. Observable (7500 -> 2250 in the golden fixture) but the magnitude is a judgment call.
formulas.mathIssues: Interacts with the source-family problem: a rookie appearing on dlfSf + dlfRookieSf + flockFantasySf + flockFantasySfRookies counts as 4 sources from 2 publishers, so it never takes the haircut. Finding P, deferred.

formulas.name: KTC TE++ uplift curve
formulas.expression: uplift(v) = clamp(1 + a * v^(-k), floor, observed_max); tepp = min(v * uplift(v), 9999)
formulas.inputs: a TE's per-source Hill value contribution, from_basis, to_basis
formulas.outputRange: multiplier in [1.2092, 2.0531] before the 9999 ceiling clamp
formulas.constants: a=43.555794, k=0.632839, floor=1.209206, observed_ratio_range [1.2092, 2.0531]. Fitted on 73 TEs appearing on both ktc.csv and ktcSfTep.csv, R2 0.941 log-space, median abs ratio err 0.0226. Board basis constant _BOARD_TE_BASIS='tepp'; source default 'base'. ktcSfTep exempt.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: convert_te_value raises on an unmeasured basis pair rather than interpolating; from==to is a no-op, which IS the double-count guard
formulas.validated: MEASURED, and I reproduced it exactly: base 8169 -> tepp 9878.0038 (matches Brock Bowers' real KTC pair 8169/9878); round-trip returns 8169.0. Live board: 552 contributions across 86 TE rows, multiplier min 1.1017 / median 1.3933 / max 1.6367.
formulas.mathIssues: The min(…, 9999) ceiling clamp silently pushes the EFFECTIVE uplift below the documented 1.2092 floor for the top TEs. Measured: 5 contributions on 2 players (Brock Bowers 1.1017, Trey McBride 1.185). Small, but CLAUDE.md's '1.209 at the top of the board' is not what runs.

formulas.name: Coverage weight (computed, never applied)
formulas.location: src/api/data_contract.py:7235 (computed), :6988-6991 (explicitly excluded), :8834-8842 (published as DIAGNOSTIC ONLY), :8770 (published as APPLIED)
formulas.expression: effective_weight = declared_weight * min(1, depth / 60)
formulas.inputs: declared registry weight, declared source depth
formulas.constants: min_full_depth = 60. Affects exactly 3 of 21 sources (dlfRookieSf, dlfRookieIdp, flockFantasySfRookies, all depth 50 -> 0.8333).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: depth None -> factor 1.0
formulas.validated: Impact measured but the change was rejected: 297 of 1094 rows move, 221 ranks change, max value delta 1072.
formulas.mathIssues: The SAME contract payload describes this formula as applied (methodology.description) and as never applied (methodology.idpTranslation.coverageWeight). See finding 1.

formulas.name: Confidence bucket rule (live)
formulas.location: src/api/data_contract.py:1896-1905; constants :111-117; called with percentile_spread at :7735-7739
formulas.expression: if source_count >= 2 and percentile_spread is not None: high if ps <= 0.08, medium if ps <= 0.20, else low; single source or no spread -> low; source_count 0 -> none
formulas.inputs: len(effectiveSourceRanks), sourceRankPercentileSpread
formulas.constants: _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_HIGH=0.08, _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_MEDIUM=0.20 (LIVE). _CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH=30, _CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_MEDIUM=80 are the LEGACY ordinal fallback, only reachable when percentile_spread is None — and they are what the contract publishes.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: unranked rows (past OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT=800) get 'none' — 183 rows today; picks take a separate _compute_pick_confidence path
formulas.validated: I verified code self-consistency across all 1092 rows: 0 unexplained mismatches against the percentile rule. The PUBLISHED rule misclassifies 237 of 712 ranked non-pick rows (33.3%) — 139 low->medium, 28 medium->low, 28 low->high, 19 high->medium, 14 high->low, 9 medium->high.
formulas.mathIssues: Three unrelated 'confidence' definitions ship under one word: this one; src/trade/suggestions.py:811 (_confidence_from_sources: >=6 high, >=3 medium — a raw count, no spread); and src/ros/aggregate.py:243-249.

formulas.name: Market confidence (scraper composite)
formulas.expression: site_score = clamp(site_count/8.0, 0.20, 1.00); cv_score = clamp(1 - min(cv,0.35)/0.35, 0.20, 1.00); conf = clamp(0.65*site_score + 0.35*cv_score, 0.20, 1.00)
formulas.inputs: count of the scraper's own per-player dash keys, coefficient of variation of normalised values
formulas.constants: divisor 8.0 is a fossil of a ~10-enabled-SITES era. Today SITES has exactly 2 enabled (KTC, IDPTradeCalc) emitting 3 dash keys, so site_count is in {1,2,3} and site_score is confined to {0.20, 0.25, 0.375}. Structural ceiling = 0.375*0.65 + 1.00*0.35 = 0.59375; observed max across 838 players is 0.594.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: absent -> None, deliberately NOT coerced to 0 (256 of 1094 rows carry none)
formulas.validated: Measured and RETIRED as a decision input. Every candidate divisor (5, 4, 3) puts 0 players below the old 0.35 threshold. Survives as a diagnostic only.
formulas.mathIssues: Still live in one place: src/trade/finder.py lines 451 and 946 on the degraded/legacy composite path. Never touches rankDerivedValue.

formulas.name: Pick-year discount
formulas.location: src/api/data_contract.py:6003-6060, applied at :7514 (Phase 3a, BEFORE the global sort)
formulas.expression: offset = pick_year - current_rookie_draft_year(); factor = offsetDiscounts[offset] if present else fallbackBase^offset; value *= clamp(factor, 0.05, 1.0)
formulas.inputs: pick year parsed from the canonical name; the observed current draft year
formulas.constants: offset 0 -> 1.00, 1 -> 0.82, 2 -> 0.66, 3 -> 0.53; fallbackBase 0.8; rollover May 15
formulas.missingDataBehavior: currentDraftYear resolution order is config override -> value derived from the scrape's own slot-pick names -> date fallback. I verified in-process that the derivation (data_contract.py:8578) runs BEFORE _compute_unified_rankings (:8654), and returns 2026 from live data where the date fallback would have said 2027. No ordering bug.
formulas.validated: No. The discount ladder is a judgment prior. Live effect: 2027 Early 1st = 5786, 2028 = 3351, 2029 = 2668.

formulas.name: Draft-capital Sleeper fallback pick value
formulas.expression: value = contract[displayName == f'{season} Pick {round}.{slot:02d}'].rankDerivedValue, else flat[round]; then dollar_i = value_i * (1200 / sum(values))
formulas.inputs: the in-memory contract, the requested league's Sleeper rosters and traded picks
formulas.constants: flat = {1:7000, 2:4000, 3:2000, 4:1200, 5:700, 6:300}, default 100 — ALL invented, none Hill-calibrated
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Silent. A pick name absent from the contract takes the flat value with no flag, no log line and no field distinguishing it in the response.
formulas.validated: NO. I measured it on today's contract: 48 of 96 picks resolve, 48 fall through. The invented half is 170,400 of 317,420 raw points = 53.7% of the $1200 budget, and because the board is renormalised to 1200 it also rescales the 48 real values.
formulas.mathIssues: 2027 1.12 is priced at 7000, above the real 2026 1.02 (6185) and just under the real 2026 1.01 (7831). The entire 2027 pick market is flat.

formulas.name: Monte Carlo trade win probability
formulas.expression: per player draw ~ triangular/normal over (p10, p50, p90) with shared latent factors for same NFL team (rho 0.25) and same position group (rho 0.10); winProbA = fraction of n_sims draws where sum(A) > sum(B)
formulas.inputs: per-side player values and a p10/p50/p90 band
formulas.constants: n_sims default 50000 (frontend sends 20000), sameTeamRho 0.25, samePosGroupRho 0.10. THE BAND CONSTANTS ARE p10 = v*0.85 and p90 = v*1.15, hardcoded in the frontend.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: build_trade_player 'prefers the Phase 4 valueBand, falls back to +/-15%' — but valueBand is present on 0 of 1092 live contract rows, so the fallback is the only path taken.
formulas.validated: NO. I reproduced it: 5000-vs-4500 -> winProbA 0.7304; the same trade with the 4500 asset relabelled as a single-source DL -> 0.7153 (the tiny difference is the position-group correlation term, not any difference in evidence). 5000-vs-4900 -> 0.5534.
formulas.mathIssues: The band bears no relation to actual source disagreement. Real relative dispersion on the live board (hillValueSpread / rankDerivedValue over 733 rows) is p10 0.061, median 0.174, p90 0.450, max 1.138 — a 7x range that the simulator flattens to a constant 0.15.

formulas.name: KTC Value Adjustment
formulas.expression: processV(v, max_in_trade, t, nerf) = (0.05*(v/t)^1.3 + 0.05*(v/(1.05*max_in_trade))^6 + 0.1) * v, scaled by max(0.6, 1-0.15*nerf); reverseAdjust solves iteratively for a virtual player (tolerance 0.025, <=10 iterations)
formulas.inputs: individual piece values on each side
formulas.outputRange: integer VA added to the lighter side
formulas.constants: KTC_MAX_PLAYER_VAL=10000, KTC_T_REFERENCE=10041, KTC_VARIANCE_PCT=5 — all lifted verbatim from KTC's site.min.js
formulas.missingDataBehavior: v<=0 or max<=0 returns 0
formulas.validated: Parity-validated against the JS port over a 139-trade fixture to +/-1 (tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py). NOT validated as correct — it is KTC's curve, applied to our 1-9999 board (finding O: endpoints 0.4% apart, so scale is fine; curvature is unvalidated).

formulas.name: Baseline FAAB bid
formulas.expression: share = v / max(v, top_value_in_pool); aggressive = max(1, round(budget * (0.05 + 0.25*share))); reasonable = max(1, round(aggressive*0.70)); lowball = max(1, round(aggressive*0.35))
formulas.inputs: candidate rankDerivedValue, league budget, top value in the addable pool
formulas.constants: 0.05 floor, 0.25 slope, 0.70, 0.35 — all judgment priors. Both copies carry identical constants.
formulas.validated: NO. Never checked against realized winning bids.
formulas.mathIssues: Python round() is banker's, JS Math.round() is half-up. I swept the value range (budget 100, top 9999): 600 of 9900 candidate values produce a different bid — e.g. value 3800 gives reasonable=$10 in Python and $11 in JS, a 10% divergence on the same player. No parity test exists. D4 describes this as 'off-by-one bids on exact halves', which understates it.

formulas.name: ROS rank-to-score
formulas.expression: rank_score = 100 * (ln(N+1) - ln(r)) / ln(N+1)
formulas.inputs: 1-indexed rank within a source, total ranked
formulas.constants: none beyond the log base
formulas.missingDataBehavior: invalid or r>N returns 0.0 rather than raising
formulas.validated: Correct as written. But CONFIRMED finding A: this is a normalized log-rank INDEX, not points, and downstream names (lineupScore, startingLineupScore) implied otherwise. DraftSharks' real projection is parsed and then discarded (aggregate.py:170-175 documents the discard explicitly).

formulas.name: ROS aggregate confidence
formulas.expression: 0.45*min(1, source_count/4) + 0.35*max(0, 1 - stddev/30) + 0.20*(1 - stale_count/total_count)
formulas.inputs: distinct contributing sources, population stdev of raw scores, stale contributor share
formulas.constants: saturation at 4 sources, SD_REFERENCE=30. Matches docs/ros-engine.md exactly.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: total_count 0 -> freshness_factor 0.0
formulas.validated: No. Note the per-source dedup guard at :160-172: the DraftSharks adapter concatenated two of the vendor's own boards over an identical 978-player universe, taking 67.4% of the blend against an intended 50.8% and inflating sourceCount/confidence on 939 of 1084 players for a year before it was caught (2026-07-30).

formulas.name: ROS team strength composite
formulas.expression: 0.72*starting_lineup_strength + 0.18*best_ball_depth_strength + 0.05*positional_coverage + 0.05*health_availability
formulas.inputs: exact Kuhn bipartite lineup solve over rosValue
formulas.missingDataBehavior: unmapped players surface in the 'Unmapped (no ROS read)' expandable rather than scoring 0
formulas.validated: No. The optimiser is exactly correct; its objective (sum of a log-rank index) is the wrong quantity.

formulas.name: Competitive window affinities
formulas.expression: affinity_i = softmax(-distance_i^2 / T) over five hand-placed anchor states
formulas.inputs: roster age/value/lineup-score axes
formulas.constants: T = 0.18; five anchor positions, all hand-placed
formulas.missingDataBehavior: notes field records 'no state cleared 30%' and the lineupScoreRank proxy stamp — this was being DROPPED by gameplan.py and is now restored
formulas.validated: NO, and correctly renamed. Nothing — no anchor, axis weight or temperature — was fitted to an observed outcome. Summing to 1 does not make it a probability.

formulas.name: Trade partner fit score
formulas.expression: logit path: logit(BASE) + fairness + need + window + history + manager, capped; final = 0.65*(BASE + conf*(est - BASE)) + 0.35*conf*structural
formulas.inputs: fairness, need, window, history, manager evidence tier
formulas.constants: BASE_ACCEPTANCE_PRIOR=0.18; MAX_CONFIDENCE_WITHOUT_DECISION_DATA=0.45 (never binds); _EVIDENCE_CONFIDENCE {ABSENT 0.05, SHAPE_ONLY 0.30, HISTORY_INFORMED 0.40, DECISION_CALIBRATED 0.85}
formulas.missingDataBehavior: the manager term is gated by manager_evidence, which requires both accept AND reject data that Sleeper does not expose, so it contributes exactly zero
formulas.validated: Bounds VERIFIED NUMERICALLY: FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MIN=7.24, MAX=43.12, _MAX_REACHABLE_CONFIDENCE=0.40. DECISION_CALIBRATED (0.85) is unreachable, so 57% of the nominal scale can never be produced. Bounds are derived from the caps, not declared, so they cannot drift.
formulas.mathIssues: need and window each enter twice — once through the capped logit path (weight 0.65) and once through the UNCAPPED structural term (weight 0.35*confidence). The module's stated 'fairness strongest at 1.40' budget describes the estimate, not the ranking score; on fit_score, need outweighs fairness. Documented at the assembly site, kept deliberately.

formulas.name: Effective auction power
formulas.expression: effective_i proportional to T_i * (1 + GAIN * tanh(z_i / CURVATURE)) + leapfrog, renormalised so the league total is preserved
formulas.inputs: per-team pick-dollar totals
formulas.constants: GAIN, CURVATURE, leapfrog term — duplicated in both copies, now bound by tests/api/test_auction_power_parity.py
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a
formulas.validated: No. Explicitly a 'closed-form S-curve heuristic' (Phase 1); the module's own docstring names a Monte-Carlo replacement as Phase 2, not built.

formulas.name: Sharp Score
formulas.expression: score = 0.36*performance + 0.22*rosterQuality + 0.22*multiLeagueConsistency + 0.12*longevity + 0.08*activity + championshipBonus - uncertaintyPenalty
formulas.inputs: completed seasons, win%, playoff/championship rate, roster value relative to league mean, cross-league variance
formulas.outputRange: components percentile-normalised within the evaluable population; bonus 0..0.12, penalty 0..0.25
formulas.constants: gates minCompletedSeasons 2, minDynastyLeagues 2, minLeagueAgeSeasons 2, minCompletedGames 24, minWinPct 0.52, maxAbandonedRosterRate 0.34, requireRecentActivityDays 400; qualify at minScorePercentile 0.75 AND minConfidence 0.55; champ bonus 1->0.06, 2->0.08, 3+->0.10 capped 0.12; championship rate beta-binomial shrunk with priorN=6
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Explicitly good: unknown fields stay unknown and are never converted to zero; failing a gate yields evaluable:false WITH a reason; observable/record-bearing/evaluable/qualified are reported as four separate populations
formulas.validated: NOT VERIFIABLE FROM REPOSITORY. Score and confidence are correctly never blended. But data/intel/ledger.sqlite3 in this checkout has 0 rows in every table (sleeper_users, leagues, manager_seasons, transactions, asset_movements all 0), so the doc's live coverage figures cannot be reproduced here.

formulas.name: BDVM fundamental value
formulas.location: src/bdvm/engine.py, curves.py, survival.py, surplus.py, trade_math.py; config/bdvm/params_v1.json
formulas.expression: projection posterior -> flex-aware dynamic replacement -> age curve (asymmetric Gaussian) x survival hazard -> surplus (option | truncated | plain) -> CES package_value per strategy currency
formulas.inputs: immutable projection snapshots under data/bdvm/projections/, age, structured events
formulas.constants: ALL are declared priors. Age peaks QB_pocket 30.0 / RB 25.0 / WR 27.0 / TE 27.5; base_hazard RB [[24,0.11],[26,0.15],[27,0.22],[28,0.30],[29,0.38],[99,0.50]]; cv_base QB 0.26 RB 0.36 CB 0.40; hazard clip [0.02, 0.85]; unknown_true_position_sigma_mult 1.1; news-event confidence 0.45 (below the 0.5 gate, so a headline can only widen sigma). The file's own _comment: 'EVERY number here is a STARTING PRIOR ... NOT backtested truth.'
formulas.missingDataBehavior: BEST IN THE REPOSITORY. No projection or no age -> the player is returned 'unpriced' WITH a reason, never imputed. No snapshot -> status no_projection_snapshot rather than a fabricated board. Unresolvable trade asset refs are listed in `unresolved` per side, never priced at zero.
formulas.validated: NO — and the implementation report says so: rolling-origin backtests, baselines B0-B4 and the option-value ablation MEASUREMENT are all 'awaiting data'. Only the ablation machinery exists. Engine parity against the frozen Appendix-C reference is pinned by tests/bdvm/test_engine_parity.py, but that validates reproduction, not accuracy. data/bdvm/ does not exist in this checkout, so I could not execute any of it.

formulas.name: In-season posterior blend (BDVM)
formulas.expression: w = n_prior / (n_prior + weeks_played); mu = w*prior + (1-w)*realized; sigma shrinks by sqrt(w_prior)
formulas.inputs: nflverse weekly rows scored under this league's exact settings (REG weeks only)
formulas.constants: n_prior = 6 (offense), 8 (IDP)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Preseason is an exact no-op (meta.inSeason.active = false). Fetch FAILURES are returned but never memoized, so a transient blip cannot pin the board to preseason values until midnight. Distinct players colliding on a normalized name are dropped (chimera guard).
formulas.validated: Not verifiable here (no data). The season selector correctly uses current_nfl_season (Sept-Dec -> year, Jan -> year-1) and NOT currentDraftYear, which points one season ahead for the whole Sept-Jan window and would make the posterior structurally unreachable.

findings.title: The shipped /api/data contract describes a weighting formula the blend does not apply — and contradicts itself two fields later
findings.rootCause: The 2026-07-29 audit corrected methodology.formula (the Hill expression) and added an honest coverageWeight block, but left methodology.description untouched. The description still asserts the depth-scaled weighting as live.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:8768-8774 ships: "blended across sources with a coverage-aware weighted mean: declared weight is scaled by min(1, depth / {min_depth}) so shallow lists contribute less than deep full-board sources". The code at :6988-6991 says the opposite in the same file: "the depth-based ``coverage_weight`` factor stays a stamped diagnostic (``sourceRankMeta.effectiveWeight``) and is NOT applied here", and :7246-7248 stamps it as "the depth-scaled coverage DIAGNOSTIC ... never applied to the blend". The SAME payload contradicts itself at :8834-8842: "DIAGNOSTIC ONLY: ... It is never applied to the blend". I confirmed on a live rebuild that methodology.description carries the false text verbatim.
findings.userImpact: Any consumer of the versioned contract — including a future maintainer reading the payload rather than the source — believes shallow rookie lists are down-weighted. They are not: all 21 sources vote at weight 1.0. Someone 'restoring' the documented behaviour would move 297 of 1094 rows and 221 ranks with zero accuracy evidence, which is precisely the failure docs/open-modeling-decisions.md §1 was written to prevent.
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite methodology.description's blend sentence to the count-aware mean-median + Hampel + alpha-shrinkage sequence the code runs, and add a test that fails if the string mentions depth scaling while coverage_weight has no call site in the blend loop.

findings.title: The contract publishes the wrong confidence-bucket rule; it misclassifies a third of the board
findings.rootCause: _compute_confidence_bucket has two branches — a percentile branch and a legacy absolute-ordinal fallback. The live call always supplies percentile_spread, so the percentile branch always wins, but the published documentation describes the fallback.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:8856-8860 publishes {"high": "2+ sources, sourceRankSpread <= 30", "medium": "2+ sources, sourceRankSpread <= 80", "low": "single source or sourceRankSpread > 80"}. The live path is :7735-7739, which passes percentile_spread=percentile_spread, so :1896-1899 decides on _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_HIGH=0.08 / _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_MEDIUM=0.20 (:111-112) instead. Measured on a rebuild of exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json: of 712 ranked non-pick rows, the published rule gives a DIFFERENT bucket for 237 (33.3%) — 139 low->medium, 28 medium->low, 28 low->high, 19 high->medium, 14 high->low, 9 medium->high. Worked example: Alex Anzalone has sourceRankSpread 17 (published rule: 'high') but sourceRankPercentileSpread 0.4599, so the code returns 'low'.
findings.userImpact: confidenceBucket gates /edge eligibility (edge-columns.jsx:127, page.jsx:116, :227), the /rankings single-source-risk screen, and the ConfidenceValueScatter. A user or integrator reasoning about why a player is 'low confidence' from the contract's own published rule will be wrong for a third of the board, and will look at the wrong field (sourceRankSpread instead of sourceRankPercentileSpread).
findings.recommendedFix: Publish the percentile thresholds as the primary rule and label the ordinal pair as the fallback that only applies when percentile_spread is absent. Generate the strings from the constants so they cannot drift.

findings.title: The Monte Carlo win probability is computed from a fabricated ±15% band, and the UI tells the user it came from real source disagreement
findings.rootCause: The simulator was designed to consume Phase 4 valueBand, but stamp_bands_on_players was never wired into the contract builder. The frontend's fallback branch — a hardcoded ±15% — is therefore the only branch ever taken, while the user-facing explainer still describes the intended design.
findings.evidence: src/canonical/confidence_intervals.py:224 stamp_bands_on_players has ZERO non-test callers (grep across src/, server.py, scripts/). Measured on a live rebuild: valueBand present on 0 of 1092 playersArray rows. frontend/components/ui/MonteCarloButton.jsx:43-54 therefore always takes the else branch: `p10 = v * 0.85; p50 = v; p90 = v * 1.15;`. The explainer at :231-240 tells the user: "For each player, our 6+ ranking sources don't fully agree on value — a player worth 8,500 by one source might be 7,900 by another. We sample 20,000 times from this disagreement range". src/trade/monte_carlo.py:8 repeats the claim ("each with a ``valueBand`` from Phase 4"). I reproduced the output: a 5000-vs-4500 one-for-one returns winProbA 0.7304; relabelling the 4500 asset as a single-source DL moves it only to 0.7153. Real dispersion on the live board is p10 0.061 / median 0.174 / p90 0.450 (hillValueSpread ÷ rankDerivedValue, 733 rows) — the constant 0.15 is ~2.5x too wide for the tightest decile and ~3x too narrow for the most-contested.
findings.userImpact: '73% chance Side A wins' is rendered on /trade (TradeMeter.jsx:107) and /waivers (ManualAddDrop.jsx:459) as a probabilistic verdict. It is a deterministic function of the value gap and roster shape. A one-source rookie IDP and a twelve-source consensus RB1 carry identical uncertainty. Separately, server.py:11197 states the backend `disclaimer` field is PART OF THE CONTRACT and 'the frontend MUST render the disclaimer somewhere visible' — the frontend never reads it and substitutes its own, stronger, false explanation.
findings.recommendedFix: Either (a) wire stamp_bands_on_players into build_api_data_contract so valueBand carries real per-player dispersion — sourceSpread and hillValueSpread are already stamped, so the input exists — or (b) if that is deferred, rewrite the explainer to say the band is a uniform ±15% modelling assumption, and render the backend's disclaimer as the contract requires.

findings.title: /api/draft-capital's non-default-league board is 53.7% invented numbers, indistinguishable from Hill-calibrated ones
findings.rootCause: _pick_value_from_contract falls through to a hardcoded per-round table whenever a pick name is absent from the contract. The 503 guard added in the 2026-07-29 pass only covers 'no contract at all', so a loaded contract that simply does not name next-season slot picks still produces a full board of fabricated values — and the $1200 renormalisation propagates the invention into the real half.
findings.evidence: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:96-99: `flat = {1: 7000.0, 2: 4000.0, 3: 2000.0, 4: 1200.0, 5: 700.0, 6: 300.0}` returned with no flag. The loop at :174-181 builds picks for `(current_season, current_season + 1)`. Measured against a live rebuild: of the 96 (season, round, slot) tuples, 48 resolve from the contract and 48 fall through — the contract names 2026 slot picks but no 2027 slot picks. Raw totals: 2026 = 147,020, 2027 = 170,400, so the invented half is 53.7% of the pool. :196-200 then scales everything by 1200/317420, so the fabricated values set the denominator for the real ones. Concretely, every 2027 1st is priced at 7000 — above the real 2026 1.02 (6185). server.py:8143-8150 confirms the guard's scope: "SCOPE, DELIBERATELY NARROW. This fires only when there is NO contract". config/leagues/registry.json has two active leagues, so dynasty_new takes this path today.
findings.userImpact: On /draft for the second league, every team's draft-capital dollar figure is driven by a table that says all 2027 1sts are worth the same, and the response carries no field marking which values are real. CLAUDE.md's D-2 note states the invented-numbers case 'is fixed' and 'is the case the 503 covers' — a reader would conclude this is closed.
findings.recommendedFix: Stamp a per-pick `valueSource: "contract" | "flat_fallback"` and surface a count in the payload; better, drop unresolvable picks from the normalisation denominator so the fabricated half cannot rescale the real one. At minimum correct CLAUDE.md so the residual is visible.

findings.title: docs/idp-ranking-model.md is materially false about how IDP values are produced — 0 of 740 rows match its published formula
findings.rootCause: The document is the standalone methodology reference for IDP valuation and has not been updated through the percentile-curve migration, the removal of the frontend ranker, or the coverage-weight decision.
findings.evidence: Three independent false claims. (1) :21 names `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js::computeUnifiedRanks` as the frontend fallback mirror — grep for computeUnifiedRanks across frontend/ returns NOTHING; CLAUDE.md records the ~280-line fallback was removed. (2) :105 publishes `value = max(1, min(9999, round(1 + 9998 / (1 + ((rank - 1) / 45) ^ 1.10))))` as the live conversion and :149/:171 claim `rankDerivedValue` is 'Hill-curve value at canonicalConsensusRank'. I tested this against 740 ranked rows on the live board: ZERO exact matches, median absolute error 819.5 on a 1-9999 scale, max 1212. The constants 45 / 1.10 are also the retired ones — the live rank-form pair is 65.4 / 0.910 (player_valuation.py:82-83) and the live board uses the percentile form, not the rank form, at all. (3) :113-129 documents `effective_weight = declared_weight * min(1, depth / 60)` as the blend weight, with the worked consequence 'a top-20 positional list contributes 20/60 ≈ 0.333 of its declared weight' — data_contract.py:6988-6991 states this is never applied.
findings.userImpact: A developer or reviewer reasoning about IDP valuation from the repository's own dedicated methodology document gets the wrong curve, the wrong constants, the wrong blend, and a frontend module that does not exist. This is the document someone would open specifically to check whether IDP numbers deserve trust.
findings.recommendedFix: Retire the formula and blending sections and point them at CLAUDE.md's pipeline steps 2-9 plus player_valuation.percentile_to_value; keep PARTS 2-3 (the backbone and translation tables), which I verified are still accurate.

findings.title: docs/architecture/live-value-pipeline-trace.md's source table is stale in a way that would corrupt any weighting analysis
findings.rootCause: The table was codified from the 2026-04-20 audit and never re-synced when sources were added and removed.

The doc names `ktc` (registry key is `ktcSfTep`), `footballGuysSf` and `footballGuysIdp` — none exist in the registry; the 2026-07-29 audit §10 records FootballGuys as REMOVED. Worst, :59 gives `idpTradeCalc` weight **2.0**; the live registry value is 1.0, and every source is 1.0 by policy.
findings.userImpact: The document opens with 'This is a reference for what actually runs in production'. Anyone reasoning about which sources dominate the blend — the single most common analysis someone would run on this pipeline — would conclude the IDP backbone carries double voice. It does not.

findings.title: BDVM's living implementation report says the engine defaults OFF; it has defaulted ON since 2026-07-28
findings.rootCause: Flag flipped in feature_flags.py without updating the report CLAUDE.md points at as BDVM's authority, or the backlog entry.
findings.evidence: docs/research/bdvm-v1/IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md:129 — "The feature flag `bdvm_engine` defaults OFF; production behavior is bit-identical until it is flipped." And :388 — "`bdvm_engine` (default **False**) in the central registry". UNIMPLEMENTED_BACKLOG.md:48 repeats it — "a projection-driven fundamental engine beside the market board, flag `bdvm_engine` OFF". The live default is src/api/feature_flags.py:225: `"bdvm_engine": True`, classified LIVE in _GATE_STATUS.
findings.userImpact: BDVM is not inert. With the flag on it renders a 'Fund gap' column on /rankings and /draft, a Fundamentals panel on /trade, the whole /bdvm page, and it emails signal alerts. Every one of its numbers rests on constants that config/bdvm/params_v1.json itself labels 'a STARTING PRIOR ... NOT backtested truth', and the report's own §20 says the backtests are 'awaiting data'. A reader who believes the engine is off will not scrutinise those numbers before they reach a trade decision.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct both lines and the backlog row. The feature_flags.py registry is the only place that has stayed honest — consider generating flag-state prose from feature_flags.snapshot().

findings.title: The collaborative audit's durable record says the TE work is 'Built but deliberately NOT wired'; it shipped the same week
findings.rootCause: IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md is the branch-scoped record of what landed and was frozen at its base commit; the TE conversion shipped 2026-07-27 in a different branch.
findings.evidence: docs/collaborative-model-audit/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md:37 — heading "## Built but deliberately NOT wired — TE", followed by "The KTC TE++ curve and the league-scoring measurement both exist, are tested, and change nothing in the live value path yet" and a 3-step 'What wiring it needs' checklist. It is wired: src/api/feature_flags.py:141 `"te_basis_conversion": True` (classified LIVE), and src/api/data_contract.py:7195-7205 calls `_convert_te_value(value, from_basis="base", to_basis="tepp")` in Phase 2a. I measured it running on the live board: 552 source-contributions converted across 86 TE rows, multiplier median 1.3933. ADR-015 in docs/league-intelligence/DECISIONS.md:532 records it as SHIPPED.
findings.userImpact: This directory is explicitly framed as 'the durable record of what survived verification'. Its own headline claim about the single largest value move of that audit is now false, and its 'What wiring it needs' checklist invites someone to re-do work that is done — which, given the double-count guard is structural rather than conventional, would be an easy way to lift every TE twice.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a SHIPPED banner to that section pointing at ADR-015, as CLAIM_REGISTRY.md finding G already does for its own superseded adjudication.

findings.title: HANDOFF.md's 'Known issues, re-verified 2026-07-29' list contains items that were already fixed and are measurably false
findings.rootCause: HANDOFF.md was rewritten specifically because the previous version drifted, and its new known-issues list claims 'Only items confirmed against current code'. Two of the eight were not re-confirmed.
findings.evidence: HANDOFF.md:138 — "`data/ros/aggregate/latest.json` has **6 duplicate player rows** ... and 16 rows with non-lowercase `canonicalName`; 40 of 666 rostered players fail to match." I measured today's file: 1085 players, **0** duplicate canonicalNames (the 16 non-lowercase names are still real). HANDOFF.md:142 — "`test_anchor_curve_extrapolation_monotone` **fails on `main`** — Chase Young ties at rank 107 against a strictly-increasing assertion." The test at tests/api/test_fantasypros_idp_integration.py:261-300 now asserts `assertGreaterEqual` with an in-code note explaining exactly this ('This was ``assertGreater`` and failed intermittently on main'), plus a non-vacuity guard requiring the curve not collapse. UNIMPLEMENTED_BACKLOG.md:499 records both as fixed in #592/#599 — two days BEFORE HANDOFF.md's re-verification date.
findings.userImpact: HANDOFF.md is the first document a new contributor is pointed at, and it exists because the previous one misled people. A false 'a real failure that is invisible' entry sends someone chasing a fixed bug; more corrosively, it undermines the six items on that list that ARE still true (the login rate-limit gap, the global alert cooldown, the unauthenticated localhost SMTP path, KTC_TradeDB/WaiverDB running partial).

findings.title: CLAUDE.md declares defect D-2 resolved while the code it cites says the opposite, and omits the substantive risk
findings.rootCause: CLAUDE.md was updated to close the doc-vs-code disagreement by choosing 'fix the doc', but the code comment and docs/python-coverage-audit.md were not brought along, and the cross-scoring-profile leak was dropped from the summary.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md's draft-capital block states "This resolves Defect D-2 (docs/python-coverage-audit.md), which was open between '503 per this table' and 'keep the fallback and fix the doc'. Fixing the doc is the answer, and this is it." server.py:8143-8150 says the opposite: "The mismatch case is Defect D-2 ... an OPEN product decision ... and ``tests/api/test_league_isolation_invariants.py`` pins today's behaviour explicitly rather than pre-empting it." docs/python-coverage-audit.md still heads the section "D-2 ... *(UNRESOLVED — documented, not fixed)*". Neither CLAUDE.md's version mentions what that audit flagged as 'the subtler issue': the fallback prices League B's picks from League A's contract with NO scoring-profile guard — I confirmed there is no scoring_profile check anywhere in the handler range server.py:8090-8250, while /api/data does 503 on a profile mismatch.
findings.userImpact: Three documents give three different states for the same defect. The one a new contributor is told is 'the authority' reports it closed and omits the failure mode: with the two leagues on different scoring profiles, League B's draft board would be priced off League A's rankings, silently.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one status and propagate it. Whatever the disposition, CLAUDE.md should name the cross-profile pick-value path, since that is the part with a real wrong-number consequence.

findings.title: FAAB bid diverges between the Python endpoint and the JS client hint on 6.1% of the value range — larger than the register records
findings.rootCause: Byte-identical formulas, different rounding semantics: Python's round() is banker's, JS Math.round() is half-up. The 0.70 and 0.35 multipliers manufacture exact-half products across wide contiguous value bands, so the divergence is not the rare edge case the register implies.
findings.evidence: src/trade/waiver.py:92-94 — `aggressive = max(1, round(league_budget * aggressive_pct)); reasonable = max(1, round(aggressive * 0.70)); lowball = max(1, round(aggressive * 0.35))`. frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:874-877 is the same expression with Math.round. I swept candidate values 100..9999 at budget 100 / top 9999: 600 of 9900 values diverge. Example: value 3800 gives Python (15, 10, 5) and JS (15, 11, 5) — a $10 vs $11 'reasonable' bid, 10% apart, on a 100-dollar budget. No parity test exists (grep for computeFaabHint under tests/ and frontend/__tests__/ finds only waiver-pool-builder.test.js). Registered as D4 with the description 'Off-by-one bids on exact halves', severity Medium, 'before new features? No'.
findings.userImpact: /waivers renders the client hint on every bestMoves row while the FaabRecommendation panel calls the Python endpoint for the selected pair. The same player can show two different recommended bids on one screen.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one rounding convention (half-up matches user intuition and the JS side) and add a fixture-driven parity test the way tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py does for the VA. Update D4's description to 'a contiguous 6% of the value range', not 'exact halves'.

findings.title: Four documents describe scaffold endpoints that do not exist
findings.rootCause: The offline canonical pipeline and promotion-readiness surface were retired; the routes went with them but the setup docs and runbooks still curl them.
findings.evidence: server.py registers exactly six scaffold routes (:4656 status, :4723 raw, :4732 league, :4741 identity, :6456 validation, :6472 report). README.md:180 lists `GET /api/scaffold/canonical`. docs/runbooks/production-activation-runbook.md:78 and :87 curl `/api/scaffold/canonical` and `/api/scaffold/promotion` respectively. docs/status/CURRENT_STATE.md:49 states "Runtime endpoint at `GET /api/scaffold/promotion` returns live readiness status". Neither path exists anywhere in server.py or src/.
findings.userImpact: The runbook is an operational activation checklist — two of its verification steps cannot succeed, which either blocks an activation or, worse, gets skipped and trains the operator to ignore failing steps.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the three dead references. docs/status/CURRENT_STATE.md is a 2026-03-22 snapshot describing an architecture that was retired wholesale (canonical shadow pipeline, Static/ frontend, 5-of-11 sources) — it should be moved to an archive directory or given the same 'this is a dated snapshot' banner docs/competitor-gap-analysis.md uses well.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's TE floor claim is contradicted by the pipeline's own ceiling clamp
findings.rootCause: The uplift curve is applied as min(convert(v), 9999.0). For the highest-valued TEs the converted contribution exceeds the scale ceiling and is truncated, so the realised multiplier falls below the curve's measured floor.
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:7196-7204 wraps the conversion in `min(float(_convert_te_value(...)), 9999.0)`. config/weights/te_premium_curve.json sets floor 1.209206. CLAUDE.md step 5a states the uplift is "1.209 at the top of the board rising toward 2.05 down it". Measured on the live board: 5 of 552 converted contributions land below 1.2092 — Brock Bowers at 1.1017 across fantasyCalc, pfkDynasty and dynastyDaddySf, 1.168 on otcffbSf, and Trey McBride at 1.185 on pfkDynasty; every one has valueContribution exactly 9999.
findings.userImpact: Small (2 players), and the clamp is deliberate and well-reasoned in code ('the premium must reposition TEs within the scale, not break it'). But it means the elite TEs — the ones a TE-premium correction most affects in trade value — receive systematically less uplift than the documentation states, and the direction is the opposite of what a reader would assume.
findings.recommendedFix: One clause in CLAUDE.md step 5a noting the 9999 clamp truncates the uplift for top-of-board TEs, with the measured realised minimum.

findings.title: Three unrelated quantities ship to users under the single word 'confidence'
findings.rootCause: Independent subsystems each named their own quality metric 'confidence' with no shared vocabulary or namespacing.
findings.evidence: (1) src/api/data_contract.py:1896-1899 — board confidenceBucket, decided on percentile spread with 2+ sources. (2) src/trade/suggestions.py:811-818 — `_confidence_from_sources`: >=6 sources 'high', >=3 'medium', else 'low'; a raw count with no agreement term, used at :1067 and :1128 to label trade suggestions and to feed a +2/+1/0 rank_score bonus. (3) src/ros/aggregate.py:243-249 — a 0.45/0.35/0.20 composite of count, agreement and freshness. Plus the retired-but-still-stamped `marketConfidence`, structurally capped at 0.59375. A player can be 'low' confidence on the board (wide percentile spread) and 'high' confidence in a trade suggestion (6+ sources) simultaneously.
findings.userImpact: On /trade a suggestion carries a confidence label produced by a rule that ignores whether the sources agree; the /rankings badge for the same player is produced by a rule that is entirely about agreement. Nothing on either surface distinguishes them.
findings.recommendedFix: Rename suggestions.py's to `sourceBreadth` (which is what it measures) and ROS's to `rosConfidence`. Reserve 'confidence' for the board bucket.

findings.title: src/api/auction_power.py presents itself as the implementation of a live user-facing number; it has no importer
findings.rootCause: The Python module was written first and framed as the source of truth; the shipping implementation is the JS copy.
findings.evidence: src/api/auction_power.py:1-31 opens "Effective auction power — a relative draft-capital concentration lens ... PHASE 1 (implemented here): a closed-form S-curve heuristic". Grep for `src.api.auction_power` across server.py, src/ and scripts/ returns 0 non-test references (2 test references). The live path is frontend/lib/auction-power.js, imported by frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:13, frontend/app/league/sections/draft-capital.jsx:12 and _trade-simulator.jsx:12. UNIMPLEMENTED_BACKLOG.md:499 records the fix as 'Python source of truth and the JS the user actually sees had duplicate constants and no parity guard. Added'.
findings.userImpact: Bounded — tests/api/test_auction_power_parity.py does bind the constants, so the numbers agree today. But the parity test's Python side is a module that never runs, so a change to the live JS that also updates the dead Python passes green while a change to the live JS alone fails for a reason that reads as 'the backend disagrees' when there is no backend.
findings.recommendedFix: Either import the Python module somewhere real or relabel its docstring as a reference implementation for the parity test, the way src/adapters/base.py and docs/research/bdvm-v1/reference/ are labelled.

findings.title: Eleven decision-support modules carry authoritative docstrings and zero production importers
findings.rootCause: Accumulated abandonment; several are already dispositioned in the audits but the modules still read as live.
findings.evidence: Verified by grep for `src.<module>` across server.py, src/ and scripts/, excluding tests and self-references — 0 non-test references each: src/api/chat.py (351 lines), src/api/espn_schema_drift.py, src/news/unified_signal_engine.py, src/league_intel/calibration.py, src/league_intel/twin.py, src/canonical/rank_history_band.py, src/scoring/archetype_model.py, src/api/auction_power.py, src/trade/correlation_matrix.py, src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py, src/trade/finder_value_adjustment.py. src/league_intel/sim.py is reached only from twin.py, which is itself unreached, so the pair is jointly dead. src/league_intel/calibration.py carries 20 test references while having zero production ones.
findings.userImpact: UNIMPLEMENTED_BACKLOG.md §10 lists 'Which TE calibration system survives: src/league_intel/te_premium.py vs src/league_intel/calibration.py' as an open operator decision — the answer is already in the import graph (calibration.py cannot affect a request), and nobody checked. A tested-but-unreachable module is the most misleading artifact in a codebase because coverage and green tests both signal health.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply the reachability classification that src/api/feature_flags.py::_GATE_STATUS already does for flags — a checked table rather than prose — and let tests/api/test_feature_flag_reachability.py's sibling fail when a module joins the orphan set without being labelled.

findings.title: docs/intel/SHARP_SCORE.md presents live coverage figures that cannot be reproduced from the repository
findings.rootCause: The ledger is gitignored, so the doc's measurements have no in-repo artifact backing them (unlike docs/measurements/*.json, which do).
findings.evidence: docs/intel/SHARP_SCORE.md:140-152 — "Measured coverage (live, 2026-07-29) ... Managers found 356 | Leagues found 689 | signal-eligible 485 | sharp-eligible 344". The store is data/intel/ledger.sqlite3, gitignored per .gitignore:45. In this checkout every table has 0 rows: sleeper_users 0, leagues 0, platform_managers 0, manager_seasons 0, transactions 0, asset_movements 0, canonical_assets 0. /market/sharp-tracker (page.jsx:122, :141) renders from this store.
findings.userImpact: Not a defect in the code — the endpoint is designed to return an explicit status rather than 503, and the methodology doc is otherwise the most epistemically careful in the repository (score and confidence never blended, four populations reported separately, unknowns never zeroed). But the coverage numbers are the one part a reader cannot check, and they are the part that decides whether the Sharp signal has any statistical base at all. Status here: Not Verifiable from Repository.
findings.recommendedFix: Emit the cohort census to docs/measurements/sharp-coverage-<date>.json the way the board backtests do, so the claim has a committed artifact.

notes:
METHOD AND LIMITS. I rebuilt the live contract offline from exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json through the real entry point (build_api_data_contract, 1.3s, 1092 rows) and measured against it rather than reasoning from code shape — that is where the confidence-bucket 33.3%, the draft-capital 53.7%, the valueBand 0-of-1092 and the TE-clamp numbers come from. I could NOT run the test suite: pytest is not installed and installing packages was prohibited, so every test claim below is a static count of `def test_` plus file existence, never an execution result. data/bdvm/ does not exist in this checkout and data/intel/ledger.sqlite3 is empty, so BDVM and Sharp Score are Not Verifiable from Repository for live behaviour. I made no modifications to the repository; scratch files went to the session scratchpad only.

WHAT THE DOCS GET RIGHT, WHICH MATTERS FOR CALIBRATING THE ABOVE. This repository is unusually honest, and most of what I checked held. Every core CLAUDE.md constant verified exactly: _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N=500, _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA=0.0, _SINGLE_SOURCE_VALUE_RETENTION=0.30, _ALPHA_SHRINKAGE=0.10, _TWO_WAY_PLAYERS={'Travis Hunter':'DB'}, _MARKET_CORRIDOR_MAX_BAND_BY_ASSET_CLASS={'idp':0.15}, _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES={'ktcSfTep','idpTradeCalc'}, 21 sources all at weight 1.0. The model-registry champion v2 parameters equal the live imported Hill constants exactly. FR-3b reproduces to four decimals (base 8169 -> tepp 9878.0038). FR-7's reachable bounds reproduce exactly (7.24 / 43.12, max confidence 0.40 so the 0.45 cap never binds). D6 reproduces exactly (19 of 21 columnLabel mismatches). The 2026-07-29 audit's fixes are all present in code: weighted_count_aware_mean_median_blend, _MIN_ASSET_VALUE_COMPOSITE_SCALE, the offense-only branch swap, the vitest step in pr-validation.yml, rank_to_value_for_scope shared by terminal and rank_history, buildHistoryLookup in signal-engine.js, low_conf_unstable retired from both engines. I ran scripts/check_rank_form_drift.py live: offense excess +0.1, idp +0.0 against a 25.0 budget, both green.

KNOWN-OPEN DEFECTS I VERIFIED STILL OPEN — do not re-report these as novel. D4 FAAB rounding (open, quantified above at 6.1%, no parity test). D6 columnLabel 19/21 (open, exactly as documented). D1 ~9 backend + 4 frontend name normalizers (open). D8 legacy rank-form family outside the registry (resolved by re-tune + tripwire + drift alarm, all verified working). D9 never-invalidated module caches (open). D11/D12/D13 (open). Finding E removal-cost surplus (open, deferred). Finding N mixed-market sum in finder.py (open, product decision). Finding P source families — no notion of source families exists anywhere in the tree, confirmed; DLF x4, FantasyPros x3, Flock x2, DraftSharks x2 all count as independent (open). Finding Q no persisted player-week actuals for OUR board's own history — this is the root cause of everything: it is why all 21 sources sit at weight 1.0, why dynamic_source_weights is off, why BDVM's backtests are 'awaiting data', and why PROJECTION_CORROBORATED is an unreachable evidence tier. The coverageWeight question is closed to 'do not apply' with measurements. usage_signals is correctly off with a measured 17.8% weekly fire rate.

ALREADY-CLOSED ITEMS THE BACKLOG STILL LISTS AS OPEN. UNIMPLEMENTED_BACKLOG.md:491 (§9 row 6) says 'finder.py has no UI caller — OPEN as a FEATURE'. It has one: frontend/app/arbitrage/page.jsx:181 POSTs /api/trade/finder, and the page's header comment says so explicitly. §9 rows 2 and 18 are likewise closed (see finding 9).

LOAD-BEARING DOCS (a developer would be misled without them, and they are accurate): CLAUDE.md (with the D-2 and TE-floor corrections above), src/api/feature_flags.py's _GATE_STATUS table — the single most trustworthy artifact in the repo because it is data re-measured by a test rather than prose, docs/open-modeling-decisions.md, docs/audits/complete-codebase-audit-2026-07-29.md, docs/collaborative-model-audit/{CLAIM_REGISTRY,FORMULA_REGISTRY,EXPERIMENT_LOG}.md, docs/python-coverage-audit.md, docs/reception-banding.md, docs/per-touch-efficiency.md, docs/first-down-signal.md, docs/playerctx.md, docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md + docs/measurements/*.json, docs/ros-engine.md, docs/league-intelligence/DECISIONS.md, docs/intel/SHARP_SCORE.md (methodology half).

STALE ARTIFACTS THAT SHOULD BE RETIRED OR BANNERED: docs/idp-ranking-model.md (actively false — highest priority), docs/architecture/live-value-pipeline-trace.md source table, docs/status/CURRENT_STATE.md (2026-03-22, describes a retired architecture), docs/status/* generally (a 2026-03-22/23 phase-log set describing the shadow canonical pipeline), docs/runbooks/production-activation-runbook.md (curls two dead endpoints), README.md's scaffold list, docs/collaborative-model-audit/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md's TE section, and HANDOFF.md's known-issues items 7-8. docs/competitor-gap-analysis.md and docs/route-usability-audit.md are correctly self-labelled dated snapshots and should stay as such.

BLUNT ANSWER TO 'WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE REAL DECISIONS'. Trust with confidence: rankDerivedValue's INTERNAL coherence — monotone, bounded, deterministic, robust to one dissenting source, missing data never becomes zero, one value per player, backed by a 23-invariant golden suite; and the legacy rank-form reconstruction, which is the only curve in the repo with a tested drift alarm that I watched pass. Trust as ORDERING, not as magnitude: the board's only measured relationship to reality is Spearman rho 0.562 against realized 2025 scoring (n=572) — decent for ranking, meaningless as a claim that a 6,000 player is worth 1.5x a 4,000 one. Treat as opinion, not measurement: every trade-engine threshold (256/769/2000/6600/700/150), every FAAB multiplier, every Buy/Sell/Hold trigger (trend7<=-3, MAD 'high'), the competitive-window anchors and temperature, and every BDVM Part-6 prior — none is fitted to an outcome, and the code mostly says so. Do not trust at all until fixed: the Monte Carlo win probability (fabricated uncertainty, and the UI actively claims otherwise), the non-default-league draft-capital board (53.7% invented), and the contract's own published confidence rule (wrong for a third of the board). The single structural limit on all of it is finding Q: the platform cannot backtest its own value changes because it has never persisted its own historical board output. Until that exists, every weight in this system is 1.0 by policy, not by evidence — which the repository, to its credit, says out loud.

subsystem: Core live valuation pipeline — `src/api/data_contract.py::_compute_unified_rankings` and everything it calls (rank→percentile→Hill, value-direct voting, scope routing, TE basis conversion, Hampel, anchor+α, count-aware aggregation, single-source haircut, market corridor clamp, two-way boost, pick year discount, pick tethering, final sort). Audited at commit 9c5d972 by reading the source and by rebuilding the real contract from `exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json` + `CSVs/site_raw/*` in a scratchpad copy (1,092 rows, 740 ranked). Every worked number below reproduces the live payload exactly.
