formulas.name: Rank → percentile (with tail clamp)
formulas.expression: denom = _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N = 500;  p = (effective_rank − 1) / (denom − 1) = (r−1)/499;  p = max(0.0, min(1.0, p))
formulas.inputs: effective_rank (int, post-ladder / post-combined-rank). Same denominator for every source and every scope — `_percentile_denom_for_source` at :6413-6414 returns the constant unconditionally.
formulas.constants: _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N = 500 (data_contract.py:4933). Hand-selected: reports/percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md recommends N=400 (+2.01% on its metric) and the code still ships 500. The metric is 'value-weighted rank change' — a STABILITY metric, not accuracy.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A source with no rank for a player is simply absent from `source_ranks`; no percentile is computed and the source contributes nothing. Never zeroed, never imputed.
formulas.mathIssues: Every rank > 500 collapses to p = 1.0 — a hard plateau. Live board: draftSharksIdp 173/274 votes (63.1%) all equal 1698; idpShow 165/280 (58.9%) all equal 594; fantasyProsIdp 48/166 (28.9%) = 594; dlfIdp 16/137 = 594; dlfRookieIdp 7/25 = 594; flockFantasySfRookies 9/70 = 794 or 1300; draftSharks 23/383 = 1698 or 1868. 443 per-source votes carry zero discriminating information.
formulas.validated: reports/percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md — stability only; a plateau is maximally stable, so the metric cannot detect this failure mode.

formulas.name: Hill percentile → value
formulas.expression: V(p) = 9999 / (1 + (p / c)^s), clamped to [DISPLAY_SCALE_MIN, 9999]; V(0) ≡ 9999 by short-circuit
formulas.inputs: p from the previous formula; (c, s) from `_curve_for_source` (data_contract.py:6390-6396)
formulas.constants: GLOBAL c=0.1120 s=0.725; OFFENSE c=0.1100 s=1.110; IDP c=0.0830 s=1.110; ROOKIE c=0.1530 s=0.885 (player_valuation.py:118-159). Tail values at p=1.0: GLOBAL 1698, OFFENSE 794, IDP 594, ROOKIE 1596.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a — only called when a rank exists.
formulas.mathIssues: Worked example: offense rank 100 → p = 99/499 = 0.19840 → V = 9999/(1+(0.19840/0.11)^1.11) = 3419.05 → 3419, matching the live stamp. The three routed curves sit on three different effective scales relative to the market values they are averaged with — see finding F-1.
formulas.validated: scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py refits weekly; challengers scored via src/model_registry/holdout.py; promotion is manual. No accuracy validation of the live blend output against realized outcomes exists in-repo.

formulas.name: Scope routing
formulas.expression: if src.is_cross_market → GLOBAL;  elif src.scope == overall_idp → IDP;  else → OFFENSE
formulas.inputs: registry flags is_cross_market and scope
formulas.constants: none beyond the curve constants
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a
formulas.mathIssues: `is_cross_market` is tested FIRST, so draftSharksIdp (scope=overall_idp, is_cross_market=True) takes the GLOBAL curve rather than the IDP curve. Live consequence: on an IDP row the anchor mixes a GLOBAL-curve vote (median 1.34× the market at the same rank) with an IDP-curve subgroup (median 0.48×). ROOKIE is never routed — verified routed=False and 0 live uses.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py:290-301 asserts the routed set is exactly {global, offense, idp}

formulas.name: Value-direct normalization
formulas.expression: in_range = 0 ≤ raw ≤ declared_max;  if source suppressed OR not in_range → Hill(p);  elif raw > 0 and site_max > 0 → value = raw / site_max × 9999;  else → Hill(p)
formulas.inputs: canonicalSiteValues[source] raw value; site_max = max in-range value for that source across the whole board
formulas.constants: _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES = frozenset({'ktcSfTep','idpTradeCalc'}) (:5110-5171). _VALUE_SOURCE_DECLARED_MAX = {ktcSfTep: 9999.0, idpTradeCalc: 9999.0} (:5173-5182). Escalation fraction 0.02 (:5184); minimum rows 50 (:5194).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: raw None, ≤ 0, or out-of-range → silently falls back to the Hill path at that source's effective rank. The source still votes; it just votes on a different scale.
formulas.mathIssues: Live site_max is exactly 9999 for both sources, so the transform is the identity (verified: ktcSfTep raw 5595 → valueContribution 5595). The fallback branch is the mechanism by which a value-direct source votes on the market scale for some rows and the curve scale for others inside the same blend.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py:228-252 pins the exact source set and linearity (raw 5000/9999 → 5000, raw 2500/9999 → 2500)

formulas.name: TE basis conversion (non-TEP sources)
formulas.inputs: v = the source's post-Hill (or post-value-direct) contribution for a TE row; from_basis 'base', to_basis _BOARD_TE_BASIS='tepp'
formulas.outputRange: multiplier in [1.209, 2.053] before the 9999 ceiling truncates it
formulas.constants: a=43.555794, k=0.632839, floor=1.209206, ceiling=2.0531 (config/weights/te_premium_curve.json, fitted on 73 KTC base-vs-TE++ observations, r² 0.9411 log-space)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: v ≤ 0 or non-finite → returns v unchanged. Flag off or ImportError → falls back to the flat 1.15 with a WARNING (:6452-6465). An explicit operator slider bypasses the curve entirely.
formulas.mathIssues: Worked example: v = 794 → uplift = 1 + 43.555794·794^−0.632839 = 1.63669 → 1299.53 → 1300, matching a live flockFantasySfRookies contribution. The DECLARED range 1.209-2.053 is not what the board shows: observed per-source tepMultiplier spans 1.1017 to 1.6367. The 1.10 low end is the 9999 ceiling truncating elite TEs (9999/9078 = 1.1015); 2.053 is never reached. The curve is measured on KTC's NATIVE base values and applied to Hill-curve contributions from other publishers; te_premium.py's own `_limitation` note flags this and nothing validates it.
formulas.validated: config/weights/te_premium_curve.json carries fit statistics; no downstream validation of the applied result

formulas.name: TE flat multipliers
formulas.expression: TEP-native sources (is_tep_premium=True, excluding ktc/ktcSfTep): value ← min(v × 1.10, 9999).  Non-TEP with the basis flag off: value ← min(v × 1.15, 9999).  ktc / ktcSfTep: no multiplier at all.
formulas.inputs: registry is_tep_premium flag; row position == 'TE'
formulas.constants: _TE_BLANKET_NON_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER = 1.15, _TE_BLANKET_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER = 1.10, _TE_BLANKET_KTC_EXEMPT_KEYS = {ktc, ktcSfTep}
formulas.missingDataBehavior: non-TE rows untouched by either multiplier
formulas.mathIssues: DOUBLE-COUNT CHECK PASSED. The if/elif at :7195 and :7208 is mutually exclusive by construction, ktcSfTep is exempt, and convert_te_value is a structural no-op when from == to. Live verification across 83 TE rows: 0 ktcSfTep TE rows carry any tep stamp; every other source carries exactly one (basis conversion on 10 sources, flat 1.10 on draftSharks / dynastyNerdsSfTep / fantasyProsFitzmaurice / idpTradeCalc / yahooBoone). The 1.10 applied to TEP-native boards is an UNMEASURED prior — te_premium.py refuses to interpolate tep↔tepp, yet the pipeline multiplies 1.10 anyway.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Per-player Hampel outlier rejection
formulas.expression: med = median(values);  MAD = median(|v − med|);  threshold = max(2.75 · MAD, 1000.0);  drop v where |v − med| > threshold.  Guards: n < 4 → no filtering;  if survivors < 2 → revert to the full set.
formulas.inputs: the (source_key, value) pairs for one player, post-TE-multiplier
formulas.outputRange: kept subset plus dropped key list
formulas.constants: _HAMPEL_K = 2.75, _HAMPEL_MIN_N = 4, _HAMPEL_MIN_THRESHOLD = 1000.0 (:231-233)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: pick rows bypass the filter entirely (`not row_is_pick` at :7294)
formulas.mathIssues: Because it operates on values that are on incommensurable scales (F-1), it systematically ejects the designated anchor. Live drop rates on IDP rows: idpTradeCalc 82/293 = 28.0%, draftSharksIdp 69/274 = 25.2%, versus ≤2.5% for every offense rank-signal source. The filter is performing scale correction, not outlier rejection.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_hampel_filter.py — 271 lines pinning the constants and synthetic drop/keep behaviour; nothing about live per-source drop rates

formulas.name: Count-aware mean-median blend
formulas.expression: n=1 → v;  n=2 → (v1+v2)/2 with MAD = |v1−v2|/2;  n=3-4 → used = all, center = (mean(used) + median(used))/2;  n≥5 → used = sorted[1:-1], center = (mean(used) + median(used))/2.  MAD = mean(|v − mean(used)|) over used.
formulas.inputs: list of per-source value contributions
formulas.constants: trim threshold n≥5; drop exactly one max and one min
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty list → (0.0, None)
formulas.mathIssues: Worked example (Dallas Turner subgroup, n=3): [1899, 673, 2417] → mean 1663.0, median 1899.0 → center 1781.0, reproducing the live subgroupBlendValue exactly. Minor internal inconsistency: the MAD is measured around the MEAN, not around the center actually used.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_count_aware_blend.py — 167 lines pinning every count branch and the MAD-set correspondence

formulas.name: Weighted count-aware blend
formulas.expression: if all weights equal (max−min ≤ 1e-9) → delegate to the unweighted blend (bit-for-bit parity).  Else: pairs sorted by value; used = pairs[1:-1] if n≥5 else pairs; w_mean = Σvw/Σw; center = (w_mean + weighted_median(used))/2 (n=2 → w_mean alone).
formulas.inputs: values plus declared weights from blend_weight_by_source
formulas.constants: registry weights are all 1.0, so the default board ALWAYS takes the equal-weight delegate branch
formulas.missingDataBehavior: length mismatch or Σw ≤ 0 → falls back to the unweighted blend rather than failing
formulas.mathIssues: Trimming stays observation-based (one max, one min by value) rather than weight-based, deliberately, to preserve equal-weight parity. Only reachable when a user moves a /settings slider.
formulas.validated: none found for the unequal-weight path

formulas.name: Hierarchical anchor + α-shrinkage
formulas.expression: use_hierarchical = row_is_pick OR position ∈ {DL,LB,DB}.  anchor = weighted_count_aware(cross-market survivors).  subgroup = weighted_count_aware(everything else).  center = anchor + 0.10 · (subgroup − anchor).  If only one side exists that side IS the center; if neither, center = 0.0.  Offense: center = weighted_count_aware(ALL values), α stamped 0.0.
formulas.inputs: post-Hampel value lists split by `_anchor_key_sets` (:2662-2697)
formulas.constants: _ALPHA_SHRINKAGE = 0.10 (:5025-5057). cross_market_keys = {idpTradeCalc, draftSharks, draftSharksIdp}; pick_anchor_keys additionally includes ktcSfTep. Anchor membership requires a strictly positive effective weight.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: anchor None and subgroup None → center 0.0 and the row cannot rank. Anchor absent → the subgroup becomes the whole answer with no shrinkage at all.
formulas.mathIssues: Worked example (Dallas Turner, IDP): anchor 1865 (n=1 after idpTradeCalc was Hampel-dropped), subgroup 1781 → 1865 + 0.10·(1781−1865) = 1856.6 → 1856, reproducing the live pre-clamp value. STRUCTURAL DEAD BRANCH: on picks the subgroup is empty for 144/144 live rows (only ktcSfTep and idpTradeCalc price picks and both are anchors), so α is never applied to a pick — the stage reduces to mean(KTC, IDPTC).
formulas.validated: reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md — the report states the stability optimum is the degenerate α=0 and that α=0.10 was a product judgement, not a measured optimum

formulas.name: λ·MAD volatility penalty (RETIRED)
formulas.expression: if MAD is not None and λ > 0 and not pick: penalty = min(center, λ · MAD);  blended = max(0, center − penalty)
formulas.inputs: unweighted MAD across all post-Hampel values
formulas.constants: _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA = 0.0 — a strict no-op
formulas.missingDataBehavior: MAD None → penalty 0
formulas.mathIssues: Verified inert: madPenaltyApplied is non-null on 0 of 1,092 live rows. CLAUDE.md step 8 is accurate here.
formulas.validated: reports/mad_lambda_backtest_full.md (stability metric)

formulas.name: Single-source haircut
formulas.expression: if not pick and len(post-Hampel values) ≤ 1:  blended ← blended × 0.30;  _blendedValueUncapped restamped with the same haircut
formulas.inputs: post-Hampel survivor count
formulas.constants: _SINGLE_SOURCE_VALUE_RETENTION = 0.30 (:5073-5103)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: picks exempt by design (they ride a CV-based confidence path instead)
formulas.mathIssues: INTERACTION WITH THE COUNT-AWARE AGGREGATION IS CORRECT. Hampel can never reduce a set below 2 (the `len(kept) < 2 → revert` guard at :6151), so len ≤ 1 means the row genuinely had one contributing source; the count-aware blend already passed that value through unchanged at n=1, so the haircut is applied exactly once to exactly the right number. Live: 35 rows haircut and all 35 fall outside OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT, so none publishes a value. I specifically tested whether the corridor clamp reverses the haircut (it would re-anchor a 30%-value row to anchor×0.85) — 0 of 35 are clamped because none is ranked. Latent, not live.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_valuation_pipeline_stages.py:90-141 asserts 5000→1500, the uncapped restamp, and the pick exemption

formulas.name: Market corridor clamp
formulas.expression: skip if no rank OR assetClass == 'offense' OR no anchor.  drift = |value − anchor| / anchor.  band = P90 of drift within the row's confidenceBucket (overall P90 if the bucket has < 30 rows);  band = min(band, 0.15) for assetClass 'idp'.  if drift > band: value ← anchor × (1 + band) when value > anchor, else anchor × (1 − band).
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue; anchor from `_market_anchor_for_row` (:4451-4542, chain idpTradeCalc → dlfIdp → idpShow → fantasyProsIdp, then median of contributions, then single-source fallback)
formulas.constants: _MARKET_CORRIDOR_PERCENTILE = 0.90, _MARKET_CORRIDOR_MIN_BUCKET_N = 30, _MARKET_CORRIDOR_MAX_BAND_BY_ASSET_CLASS = {'idp': 0.15}
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no anchor at all → the row is skipped and never clamped. Picks have no entry in _MARKET_ANCHOR_FALLBACKS so they are skipped structurally.
formulas.mathIssues: IDP-ONLY CLAIM VERIFIED: 128/128 live clamps are assetClass 'idp'; 0 offense; 0 pick. Worked example: Dallas Turner value 1856, anchor 4164, band 0.15, value < anchor → 4164 × 0.85 = 3539.4 → 3539, matching the live stamp. cappedByMaxBand is True on 128/128, so the per-bucket P90 never sets the operative band. Consequence: all 293 ranked IDP rows carrying an IDPTC contribution end up within 15.1% of IDPTC (p50 drift 0.122, p90 0.150, max 0.151).
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_market_corridor_clamp.py pins the mechanics; nothing pins the fraction of the board it moves

formulas.name: Two-way player boost
formulas.expression: For each name in _TWO_WAY_PLAYERS, for each alt-family source: if canonicalSiteValues[k] ≥ 500000 → rank = (1000000 − syn)/100 and alt_v = Hill((rank−1)/499) on the alt-family curve; else alt_v = syn / max_native × 9999.  alt_value = ARITHMETIC MEAN of alt_v.  rankDerivedValue ← max(current, alt_value).
formulas.inputs: canonicalSiteValues of every scope=overall_idp (or overall_offense) source
formulas.constants: _TWO_WAY_PLAYERS = {'Travis Hunter': 'DB'}; native/rank discriminator _RANK_TO_SYNTHETIC_VALUE_OFFSET × 50 = 500000
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no alt values → no boost and no stamp; alt ≤ current → stamp applied:false
formulas.mathIssues: LIVE AND FIRING: Travis Hunter 3055 → 6570 (+115%) from a plain 3-source mean over {dlfIdp, idpShow, idpTradeCalc}. That mean combines one value-direct contribution with two IDP-Hill contributions — exactly the incommensurable pair from F-1 — and bypasses Hampel, the count-aware blend, the α-shrinkage, the single-source haircut and the corridor clamp. It runs at :7830, AFTER the clamp, so the result is bounded by nothing.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Pick future-year discount
formulas.expression: offset = pick_year − current_rookie_draft_year().  offset ≤ 0 → 1.0.  else offsetDiscounts[str(offset)] if present, else legacy discounts[year], else clamp(0.80^offset, 0.05, 1.0).  value ← value × mult, applied to the PRE-SORT blended value.
formulas.inputs: year parsed from the pick's canonical name; config/weights/pick_year_discount.json
formulas.constants: offsetDiscounts {0:1.00, 1:0.82, 2:0.66, 3:0.53}; fallbackBase 0.80; rollover May 15. No provenance, fit, or backtest recorded anywhere in config/, reports/, or docs/.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: unparseable year → 1.0. Missing or malformed config → a bare except at :4090-4093 substitutes {offsetDiscounts: {}, fallbackBase: 0.80}, silently changing the ladder to 0.80/0.64/0.512 with no log line.
formulas.mathIssues: Worked example: 2027 Early 1st, anchor = mean(KTC 7061, IDPTC 7052) = 7056.5 → × 0.82 = 5786.3 → 5786, matching the live stamp. ORDERING VERIFIED: the discount at Phase 3a (:7513) precedes the Phase 4 sort (:7519), and tethering at Phase 5.2b (:7853) follows both. No ordering bug — current-year picks always take factor 1.0, so the tether overwrite can never collide with a discount. The problem is the magnitude, not the order: see finding F-5.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Draft-day projection (discount inversion)
formulas.expression: projected = round(rankDerivedValue / pickYearDiscount);  gain = max(0, projected − rdv);  gainPct = round(gain / rdv × 100)
formulas.inputs: final post-tether rankDerivedValue and the stamped discount
formulas.constants: discount clamped to (0, 1.0]; an absent stamp is treated as 1.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rdv ≤ 0 or no parseable year → no stamp at all
formulas.mathIssues: It is the exact inverse of a hand-picked constant, so it inherits every problem the discount has. Live: 2029 Early 1st projects to 5034 — a forecast derived from cloned 2028 vendor values.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Pick rookie tethering
formulas.expression: rookies sorted by (−pool_value, canonicalConsensusRank) where pool_value = rankDerivedValue or _blendedValueUncapped.  idx = (round − 1) × league_size + (slot − 1).  rankDerivedValue ← rookies[idx] pool_value, OVERWRITING the blend outright.
formulas.inputs: merged offense+IDP rookie list; league_size from `_resolve_league_roster_count`; anchor_year from current_rookie_draft_year()
formulas.constants: _ROOKIE_ANCHOR_ROUNDS = 6; _ROOKIE_ANCHOR_LEAGUE_SIZE_DEFAULT = 12
formulas.missingDataBehavior: idx beyond the rookie pool → the pick keeps its blended value; anchor_val ≤ 0 → skipped. If the Sleeper fetch fails the league size silently falls back to 12, which silently re-maps every pick to a different rookie.
formulas.mathIssues: Live: 72 of the 90 2026 pick rows tethered (2026 Pick 1.01 → Jeremiyah Love 7831; 2026 Pick 2.01 → Jacob Rodriguez 3544). compact_ranks_and_tiers then clears their canonicalConsensusRank (:2107-2111) so they carry a value but no rank — which is why the ranked board is 740 rows and not 800.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_pick_rookie_anchor_core.py

formulas.name: Rookie ladder translation with tail extrapolation
formulas.expression: ladder = sorted reference-source ranks of every rookie in the universe.  if 1 ≤ k ≤ len(ladder) → ladder[k−1].  else slope = max(1.0, (ladder[−1] − ladder[−min(10,n)]) / (min(10,n) − 1));  result = max(1, ladder[−1] + round((k − len(ladder)) · slope)).
formulas.inputs: within-class rookie rank; reference ladder (dlfRookieSf→ktcSfTep, dlfRookieIdp→idpTradeCalc, flockFantasySfRookies→ktcSfTep)
formulas.constants: tail window 10 entries; slope floored at 1.0; the ladder must have ≥ 3 entries or the source falls through untranslated
formulas.missingDataBehavior: reference source inactive or fewer than 3 covered rookies → NO translation and the raw within-class rank goes straight to the Hill curve, meaning the #1 rookie would be priced as the #1 overall player. Silent — no flag, no log.
formulas.mathIssues: Extrapolated ranks routinely exceed 500 and hit the p=1.0 plateau: flockFantasySfRookies has 9 of 70 votes sitting at 794 or 1300.

formulas.name: Shared-market IDP crosswalk
formulas.expression: effective_rank = translate_position_rank(raw_idp_rank, backbone.shared_idp_ladder())
formulas.inputs: IDP-only ordinal; IDPTC's combined offense+IDP ladder built by build_backbone_from_rows
formulas.constants: needs_shared_market_translation = True on dlfIdp, fantasyProsIdp and idpShow only
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no backbone → an empty IdpBackbone(), translation degrades to pass-through, and `idpBackboneFallback` is stamped on the row
formulas.mathIssues: Verified live: all three sources stamp method 'exact' with sharedMarketTranslated=True on 100% of their rows. This is what makes the F-1 comparison a genuine like-for-like measurement rather than an artifact of two different rank spaces.

formulas.name: DraftSharks combined cross-market rank
formulas.expression: gather (raw 3D Value+, row_idx, source_key) across BOTH DS CSVs; sort by (−value, row_idx, key); assign combined_rank = 1..N and overwrite both sources' effective ranks
formulas.inputs: draftSharksSf.csv and draftSharksIdp.csv column `3D Value +`
formulas.constants: none
formulas.missingDataBehavior: DS values may be negative (~50% of the CSV tail) and are deliberately NOT filtered — the `val <= 0` gate is relaxed for _DS_COMBINED_RANK_KEYS at :6651-6652 — so they sort to the tail instead of being dropped.
formulas.mathIssues: 864 combined entries against a 500 percentile denominator means 196 votes (23%) plateau at the GLOBAL tail value 1698. Restricted to IDP rows, 173 of 274 DS votes (63%) are the identical number.

formulas.name: Excludes-rookies dynamic gate
formulas.expression: if src.excludes_rookies and row.rookie and raw_rank > pool_size × 0.80 → skip this source's contribution entirely
formulas.inputs: raw within-source rank; the source's Phase 1 pool size
formulas.constants: 0.80 bottom-quintile cut; set on dlfIdp and fantasyProsIdp
formulas.missingDataBehavior: the skip is silent — the source appears as absent rather than as suppressed
formulas.mathIssues: `source_pool_sizes[source_key]` is assigned at :6672, before the ranking loop that reads it, so the value is correct. No defect found.

formulas.name: Percentile rank spread (disagreement statistic)
formulas.expression: pct_k = clamp(rawRank_k / pool_size_k, 0, 1) for each contributing source;  spread = sorted[−2] − sorted[1] if n ≥ 5, else max − min
formulas.inputs: RAW ranks (deliberately, not effective ranks) plus auto-detected pool sizes
formulas.constants: _PERCENTILE_SPREAD_TRIM_MIN_N = 5
formulas.missingDataBehavior: fewer than 2 sources → None; a source with pool size ≤ 0 is skipped
formulas.mathIssues: none found — this is the one place in the file that correctly normalizes ranks by their own pool depth before comparing them

formulas.name: Depth allowance and disagreement thresholds
formulas.expression: allowance = min(rank / total_ranked, 0.25);  hasSourceDisagreement = spread > 0.10 + allowance;  suspicious_disagreement = spread > 0.20 + allowance.  Both recomputed after compaction using the FINAL rank and final pool size.
formulas.inputs: percentile spread; final canonicalConsensusRank; final ranked-pool size
formulas.constants: _DISAGREEMENT_BASE_THRESHOLD 0.10, _SUSPICIOUS_PCT_BASE_THRESHOLD 0.20, _DISAGREEMENT_DEPTH_ALLOWANCE_CAP 0.25
formulas.missingDataBehavior: non-numeric spread or rank → the Phase 4 provisional flags are left in place
formulas.mathIssues: none found

formulas.name: Confidence bucket (players)
formulas.expression: if n ≥ 2: percentile_spread ≤ 0.08 → high;  ≤ 0.20 → medium.  Otherwise n ≥ 1 → low;  n = 0 → none.
formulas.inputs: post-Hampel source count; percentile spread (legacy callers pass an absolute ordinal spread instead)
formulas.constants: _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_HIGH 0.08, _CONFIDENCE_PERCENTILE_MEDIUM 0.20; legacy ordinal fallbacks 30 and 80
formulas.missingDataBehavior: percentile_spread None → falls back to the absolute ordinal rule, which is not depth-normalized
formulas.mathIssues: Feeds the corridor clamp's bucket selection — which is then overridden by the 0.15 hard cap in 100% of live clamps, so the bucket choice has no effect on the IDP board today.

formulas.name: Confidence bucket (picks, CV-based)
formulas.expression: effective_count = Σ(0.5 if key == 'ktcSfTep' and slot-specific else 1.0) over keys with raw > 0.  cv = sqrt(Σ(v−mean)²/n) / mean (population sd).  high if count ≥ 1.5 and cv ≤ 0.15;  medium if count ≥ 1.0 and cv ≤ 0.30;  else low.
formulas.inputs: canonicalSiteValues for {ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc, dlfSf, dynastyNerdsSfTep, dlfIdp, fantasyProsIdp}
formulas.constants: 0.5 partial credit for synthesized KTC slot values; cv cuts 0.15 and 0.30
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no raw values → 'none' (68 live rows); a single value → cv None → 'low'
formulas.mathIssues: Four of the six keys read (dlfSf, dynastyNerdsSfTep, dlfIdp, fantasyProsIdp) are RANK-SIGNAL sources whose canonicalSiteValues slot holds a six-digit synthetic encoding 999900 − rank×100 — precisely the arithmetic `rank_signal_source_keys()` at :1723-1735 exists to forbid. Latent today (0 of 144 live pick rows carry any of the four) but dlfRookieSf already stamps six-digit values on 110 rows including synthetic pick slots.

formulas.name: Gap-based tier detection
formulas.expression: series = [−rankDerivedValue] in rank order; detect_tiers runs a rolling-median gap normalization and opens a new tier at each outsized gap. No cap on tier count.
formulas.inputs: the compacted board values
formulas.constants: internal to detect_tiers (not audited here)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty board → []
formulas.mathIssues: Overwrites the Phase 4 `_tier_id_from_rank` rank-band stamp entirely, so the fixed 12/36/72/120/200/350/500/650/800 boundaries never reach the client for ranked rows.

formulas.name: Market gap (retail vs consensus)
formulas.expression: retail_mean = mean(ranks of is_retail sources = {ktcSfTep});  consensus_mean = mean(all other ranks);  diff = consensus_mean − retail_mean;  > 0 → retail_premium, < 0 → consensus_premium, 0 → none.
formulas.inputs: post-Hampel effective ranks
formulas.constants: the retail set is derived from is_retail, today only ktcSfTep
formulas.missingDataBehavior: either side empty → ('none', None)
formulas.mathIssues: It averages ranks that live in different pools (a 137-deep dlfIdp rank alongside a 424-deep ktcSfTep rank) without normalizing by depth — unlike `_percentile_rank_spread`, which explicitly does. The magnitude is not comparable across players with different coverage.

formulas.name: Final sort and rank assignment
formulas.expression: sort by (−blended_value, canonicalName.lower());  take the first OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT = 800;  derived = int(norm_val);  canonicalConsensusRank = i + 1
formulas.inputs: post-discount blended values
formulas.constants: OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT = 800 (:60)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rows with no source ranks never enter row_normalized and receive NO rankDerivedValue and NO rank — they vanish from the board silently (live: 1,092 rows in, 740 ranked out, 352 with no value at all).
formulas.mathIssues: `int(norm_val)` TRUNCATES where every neighbouring stamp uses round() (compare :7440, :7452, :4649) — a systematic sub-1-point downward bias.

formulas.name: Compaction re-sort (the one ranker)
formulas.expression: candidates = rows with a truthy canonicalConsensusRank;  sort by (−rankDerivedValue, prior rank);  skip current-year slot picks (rank and tier set to None);  renumber 1..N contiguously; then re-derive tiers.
formulas.inputs: post-clamp, post-boost, post-tether values
formulas.constants: anchor_year from current_rookie_draft_year(); copy_rows=False on the canonical path, True for the league overlay
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rows without a prior rank are excluded from the candidate set entirely
formulas.mathIssues: Only rows that ALREADY held a rank are re-ranked, so a post-sort value change can reorder inside the top 800 but can never promote a row from outside it. A clamp that raises a value by 91% (Dallas Turner) cannot pull in a row the pre-clamp sort excluded — the board is closed at the moment of the Phase 4 sort, before three value-moving stages run.

findings.title: The three routed Hill curves are on different scales from the market values they are averaged with — the IDP master pays ~48% of the IDP market at the same rank
findings.evidence:
Measured on a contract rebuilt from the live 2026-08-04 payload. For each row I compared a source's vote at its own effective rank against the retail market value at that same rank:

  IDP master (c=0.083, s=1.110) vs idpTradeCalc raw, n=293:   p10 0.36  median 0.48  p90 0.76
  OFFENSE master (c=0.110, s=1.110) vs ktcSfTep raw, n=391:   p10 0.68  median 0.76  p90 1.00
  GLOBAL master (c=0.112, s=0.725) vs idpTradeCalc raw, n=293: p10 0.88  median 1.34  p90 2.17

The IDP-only sources are ladder-translated into IDPTC's combined-rank space (sharedMarketTranslated: true, method 'exact', on 100% of dlfIdp/idpShow/fantasyProsIdp rows), so these are like-for-like. Dallas Turner, five sources all at the SAME combined rank 117:
  idpTradeCalc  valueContribution 4164  (value_direct, src/api/data_contract.py:7131)
  idpShow       valueContribution 2417  (rank_hill, IDP master)
  dlfIdp 1899   fantasyProsIdp 673   draftSharksIdp 1865 (GLOBAL master)

Root cause is in the fit, not the blend. scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:366-372 fits the IDP master on `_load_idptc_idp_values()` — IDPTC's IDP-ONLY slice — and `_percentile_pairs` (:201-207) renormalizes so the top IDP = 9999 with p = i/(n−1) over that slice (n=370 live, top IDP raw = 6444). At runtime the same curve is evaluated at p = (combined_pool_rank − 1)/499 (src/api/data_contract.py:7108-7113) and its output is averaged against combined-pool values where 9999 means the top OFFENSE player. Two coordinate changes, neither compensated.
findings.userImpact: Every IDP value on the board is produced by averaging numbers that mean different things. The pipeline's own designated IDP anchor is treated as an outlier and discarded on 28% of IDP rows, the blend lands systematically low, and a post-hoc clamp then drags 44% of IDP rows back to the retail number — so the multi-source IDP consensus the product advertises does not survive to the output. Any IDP trade valuation, waiver bid or package sum built on these numbers is arithmetic over incommensurable units.
findings.recommendedFix: Fit and evaluate in the same coordinate system. Either (a) fit the IDP master on the IDPTC IDP slice indexed by COMBINED-pool rank and normalized against the combined-pool top (so the top IDP fits at ~6444/9999, not 9999/9999), or (b) drop the separate IDP master and route IDP rank-signal sources through the GLOBAL master, which is already fit on combined-pool data. Then add a build-time assertion that for each routed curve, median(Hill(anchor_rank) / anchor_raw_value) sits in [0.9, 1.1] — that one check catches this and catches a future refit drifting.
findings.affectedSystems: rankDerivedValue for all 398 IDP rows and (at 0.76×) all 550 offense rows; canonicalConsensusRank; Hampel filter; corridor clamp; every downstream trade, waiver and terminal engine

findings.title: The Hampel filter ejects the designated IDP anchor on 28% of IDP rows
findings.evidence:
src/api/data_contract.py:7293-7300 runs `_hampel_filter_per_player` over the mixed-scale value list before aggregation. Per-source drop rates on the live board, restricted to assetClass 'idp':

  idpTradeCalc    82/293 = 28.0%   ← the registry's is_backbone:True, is_cross_market:True IDP anchor
  draftSharksIdp  69/274 = 25.2%   ← the other cross-market anchor
  fantasyProsIdp   4/166 =  2.4%
  idpShow          6/280 =  2.1%
  dlfIdp           1/137 =  0.7%

Every offense rank-signal source sits at ≤2.5%. The two sources being ejected are exactly the two that are NOT on the IDP-Hill scale. Dallas Turner carries `droppedSources: ['idpTradeCalc']`, after which `cross_market_values` collapses to the single DS vote 1865, so `anchorValue` = 1865 and the α-blend yields 1865 + 0.10·(1781−1865) = 1856.6 → 1856 — reproduced exactly from the stamped payload.
findings.userImpact: On more than a quarter of IDP players the pipeline discards the retail IDP market entirely, then computes an 'anchor' from whatever is left — frequently a single DraftSharks vote that is itself sitting on the 1698 tail plateau. The anchorValue / subgroupDelta / alphaShrinkage stamps rendered in the value-chain UI describe a hierarchy that did not actually happen.
findings.recommendedFix: Fix the scale (previous finding) — drop rates should fall to the ~2% seen on offense once the votes are commensurable. Independently, make the filter refuse to drop a source flagged is_backbone or is_cross_market without emitting a loud diagnostic, and add a build watchdog that fails when any single source's drop rate exceeds ~10%.
findings.affectedSystems: anchorValue, subgroupBlendValue, rankDerivedValue, droppedSources, effectiveSourceRanks, confidenceBucket, marketGapDirection

findings.title: The corridor clamp's hard 0.15 cap binds on 100% of clamps, making the IDP board IDPTradeCalc ±15% by construction
findings.evidence:
src/api/data_contract.py:4626-4632 caps the band at _MARKET_CORRIDOR_MAX_BAND_BY_ASSET_CLASS['idp'] = 0.15 whenever the empirical bucket P90 exceeds it. Live board: 128 rows clamped, ALL assetClass 'idp', ALL with bandPct 0.15 and cappedByMaxBand true, anchor idpTradeCalc on 127 of 128. That is 43.5% of the 294 ranked IDP rows. Median relative value change 23.7%, max 114.9%. Largest moves — Dallas Turner 1856→3539 (+91%), Devin Lloyd 1381→2968 (+115%), Nick Emmanwori 1710→3064 (+79%) — are all clamped UP, i.e. the clamp is repairing the systematic low bias from F-1, not containing outliers.
Across all 293 ranked IDP rows carrying an IDPTC contribution, drift from IDPTC is p50 0.122, p90 0.150, max 0.151 — every row is inside ±15.1%.
The per-bucket-P90 machinery (_MARKET_CORRIDOR_MIN_BUCKET_N = 30, _percentile(..., 0.90)) never sets the operative band on this build.
findings.userImpact: The IDP half of the board is a thin wrapper around one vendor. Five sources are ingested, blended, Hampel-filtered and α-shrunk, and the result is then forced into a ±15% envelope around IDPTradeCalc. A user choosing this platform for multi-source IDP consensus is getting IDPTC. Worse, the clamp is silently masking a calibration bug, so fixing that bug without revisiting the clamp will move the board again.
findings.recommendedFix: Do not tune the clamp. Fix F-1 first, then re-derive the band from the corrected drift distribution and check whether a clamp is needed at all. If it is kept, publish cappedByMaxBand counts in the build summary and fail the build when the cap binds on more than a small fraction of rows — that is the signal that the blend and the anchor disagree structurally.
findings.affectedSystems: rankDerivedValue for 128 IDP rows; canonicalConsensusRank via the compaction re-sort; trade, waiver and terminal engines

findings.title: Ranks past 500 collapse to a single value — 443 per-source votes on the live board carry zero information
findings.evidence:
src/api/data_contract.py:7113 `p = max(0.0, min(1.0, p))`, with `_percentile_denom_for_source` (:6413) returning the constant 500 for every source. Any effective rank > 500 maps to p = 1.0 and therefore to one curve tail value: GLOBAL 1698, OFFENSE 794, IDP 594, ROOKIE 1596.
Plateau measured on the live board (votes past rank 500 / total votes, and the distinct values they take):
  draftSharksIdp        173/274 = 63.1%  → all 1698
  idpShow               165/280 = 58.9%  → all 594
  fantasyProsIdp         48/166 = 28.9%  → all 594
  dlfRookieIdp            7/25  = 28.0%  → all 594
  dlfIdp                 16/137 = 11.7%  → all 594
  flockFantasySfRookies   9/70  = 12.9%  → 794 or 1300 (TE-lifted)
  draftSharks            23/383 =  6.0%  → 1698 or 1868 (TE-lifted)
Maximum observed effective rank is 902 (idpTradeCalc, which escapes via the value-direct path) and 878 (idpShow, which does not). Ranks 501 and 878 from the same source cast identical votes.
reports/percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md selected N using 'value-weighted rank change' — a stability metric. A plateau is maximally stable, so the selection procedure structurally cannot see this failure. The same report recommends N=400 and the code ships 500.
findings.userImpact: On the deep IDP board a source that ranks a player 520th and one that ranks him 870th are indistinguishable. Ordering below roughly rank 500 is decided by which sources happen to cover a player rather than by what they say — and that is exactly the region where waiver and deep-bench decisions live.
findings.recommendedFix: Either extend the reference N to the real maximum effective rank (~900), or let the tail continue past p = 1.0 using the curve's natural asymptote so ordering survives. Add a build-time assertion that no source contributes the same value to more than a small fraction of its covered rows.
findings.affectedSystems: every rank-signal source's valueContribution; blended values for deep IDP and deep rookie rows; the Hampel filter, which sees artificial ties

findings.title: The future-year pick discount is applied on top of vendor values that already price the year, in the opposite direction
findings.evidence:
Both pick markets price a 2027 Early 1st ABOVE a 2026 Early 1st:
  CSVs/site_raw/ktcSfTep.csv:     2026 Early 1st 5595,  2027 Early 1st 7061,  2028 Early 1st 5122
  CSVs/site_raw/idpTradeCalc.csv: 2026 Early 1st 5554,  2027 Early 1st 7052,  2028 Early 1st 5034
The pipeline treats 2026 as offset 0 (factor 1.00) and multiplies 0.82 / 0.66 / 0.53 onto later years (src/api/data_contract.py:6027, config/weights/pick_year_discount.json). Live result:
  2027 Early 1st: blended anchor 7056 → published 5786  (−18% vs both markets)
  2028 Early 1st: blended anchor 5078 → published 3351  (−34%)
  2029 Early 1st: cloned 2028 values 5034 → published 2668 (−47%, and no vendor prices 2029 at all)
The stated justification is contradicted by the current data. The code comment at src/api/data_contract.py:3993-3995 asserts 'There is no real future-year discount in the source data — KTC and IDPTC price 2027/2028 picks only marginally below 2026'; the live CSVs show 2027 priced 26% ABOVE 2026.
Compounding this, the two baseline-year resolvers DISAGREE on this build: `_derive_current_draft_year_from_names` returns 2026 (72 '2026 Pick R.SS' rows still present) while the date-derived fallback returns 2027 (today 2026-08-04 is past the May 15 rollover, src/api/data_contract.py:4265-4270). The data-derived value wins, and the market's own relative pricing of 2027 over 2026 is consistent with the date-derived answer being correct.
No backtest, fit or provenance for 0.82/0.66/0.53 exists anywhere in config/, reports/ or docs/.
findings.userImpact: Forward draft capital is systematically under-priced against every source that prices it — 18% on 2027 firsts, 34% on 2028. Any trade in which the user sends future picks is scored as a win by the calculator when the market says otherwise. If the baseline year is also off by one, the error compounds.
findings.recommendedFix: Establish whether the vendor pick values are 'at-draft' or 'today' values. They are almost certainly 'today' values — that is what a trade calculator publishes — in which case the discount is pure double counting and should be removed for years the vendors actually price, retained only for synthesized years like 2029. Separately, reconcile the two draft-year resolvers and fail loudly when they disagree instead of silently preferring one.
findings.affectedSystems: 36 future-year pick rows (2027 and 2028 real, 2029 synthetic); pickProjectedDraftValue; trade simulator; draft capital board

findings.title: Three publishers vote twice on the same player
findings.evidence:
Rows carrying two votes from the same publisher, counted on the live board:
  fantasyProsSf + fantasyProsFitzmaurice: 298 rows — and the overlap is TOTAL, all 299 Fitzmaurice names appear in the 540-row FantasyPros SF file
  flockFantasySf + flockFantasySfRookies:  63 rows
  dlfSf + dlfRookieSf:                     33 rows
  dlfIdp + dlfRookieIdp:                   12 rows
Each pair enters `all_values` as two independent observations at weight 1.0 (src/api/data_contract.py:7215-7228), affecting both the mean and the n≥5 trim boundary. The registry explicitly documents removing exactly this problem for KTC — 'Historically we registered both as separate blend sources, which double-counted KTC's signal' (src/api/data_contract.py:1006-1018) — and standard `ktc` was demoted to display-only. That reasoning was never applied to FantasyPros, Flock or DLF.
findings.userImpact: FantasyPros gets roughly double the voice of any other publisher on the top ~300 offense players. Since FantasyPros ECR is itself a consensus that plausibly includes Fitzmaurice, one analyst may be counted three times. Rookies get an extra DLF and an extra Flock vote, biasing exactly the cohort the pick-tethering pass depends on for all 72 current-year pick values.
findings.recommendedFix: Decide per publisher whether the second board is genuinely independent. If it is not, demote it to display-only like `ktc`, or halve both votes' weights so the publisher contributes one vote in total. `blend_weight_by_source` already supports fractional weights, so this is a registry edit rather than a code change.
findings.affectedSystems: offense blended values (298 rows), rookie blended values, and therefore pick tethering targets

findings.title: Every constant in the blend was selected against a stability metric; no accuracy validation of the live board exists
findings.evidence: reports/percentile_reference_n_backtest_full.md, reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md, reports/mad_lambda_backtest_full.md and reports/soft_fallback_backtest_full.md all optimize 'value-weighted rank change' — day-to-day board churn. The α report states the problem outright: 'this metric rewards stability. The stability optimum drifts toward α=0 and λ=0 — use the anchor source alone, ignore the 15 other sources. That's product-bad.' α=0.10 was a product judgement, not a measurement. The percentile-N report recommends 400; the code ships 500 (src/api/data_contract.py:4933). The corridor band 0.15, the single-source retention 0.30, Hampel K=2.75 and its 1000-point floor, the TE-native 1.10, and the pick discounts 0.82/0.66/0.53 have no backtest at all in-repo. The only accuracy-style backtest present — docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md — covers the league-adjusted overlay, not this pipeline.
findings.userImpact: There is no evidence in the repository that any number this pipeline produces is more accurate than reading IDPTradeCalc and KeepTradeCut directly. A stability metric always prefers whatever ignores the most information, which is why every tuned constant has drifted toward the degenerate solution and why the corridor clamp — which reduces the IDP board to one vendor ±15% — reads as an improvement rather than as an alarm.
findings.recommendedFix: Build one accuracy harness before tuning anything else: score board values as of date T against realized outcomes, or against forward market movement over T+30/T+90, per asset class. src/model_registry/holdout.py already implements this pattern for the Hill refit — extend it to the blend constants and re-run α, the corridor band and the pick discounts against it.

findings.title: The two-way player boost overrides the whole pipeline with a plain three-source mean and is live at +115%
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:4894 `alt_value = sum(alt_source_values) / len(alt_source_values)` — an unweighted arithmetic mean — then :4903 `row['rankDerivedValue'] = boosted`. Live payload: Travis Hunter `twoWayPlayerBoost: {applied: true, altFamilyValue: 6570, primaryFamilyValue: 3055, sourcesConsidered: ['dlfIdp','idpShow','idpTradeCalc']}` — a +115% override on a single player. The mean combines idpTradeCalc's value-direct number with dlfIdp's and idpShow's IDP-Hill numbers, the exact incommensurable pair from F-1. It runs at :7830, AFTER `_apply_market_corridor_clamp`, and bypasses the Hampel filter, the count-aware blend, the α-shrinkage and the single-source haircut. No test file covers it.
findings.userImpact: One player's board value — and every trade evaluated against him — is set by a code path carrying none of the pipeline's own robustness machinery. Doubling a top-100 asset's value with an untested three-line mean is a large silent exposure, and the table is designed to grow.
findings.recommendedFix: Route the alt-family values through `_hampel_filter_per_player` and `count_aware_mean_median_blend` like every other row, and move the boost to BEFORE the corridor clamp so the result is subject to the same market-sanity envelope. Add a test pinning the Travis Hunter path.
findings.affectedSystems: rankDerivedValue for _TWO_WAY_PLAYERS members; canonicalConsensusRank via compaction

findings.title: 2029 pick values are a re-discounted clone of 2028 and are presented identically to market-priced rows
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:4154-4231 clones the nearest published future year's raw source values under the missing year's names. Live: 18 rows for 2029, e.g. `2029 Early 1st` with canonicalSiteValues {ktc: 5122, idpTradeCalc: 5034} — byte-identical to 2028's — then × 0.53 → rankDerivedValue 2668 at board rank 204. Only idpTradeCalc actually votes: the clone runs at :8583, before `_enrich_from_source_csvs` at :8619, so no ktcSfTep key is grafted on and `ktc` is display-only — making these single-anchor rows (anchorValue 5034 = the IDPTC clone exactly). `_stamp_pick_value_projections` then publishes pickProjectedDraftValue 5034 for 2029, a forecast derived from an invented number.

Stamp `syntheticSource: true` on the row (the `_SYNTHETIC_FAR_FUTURE_PICK_NAMES` set already tracks them for the single-source allowlist) and surface it in the UI and in every engine's output, and suppress pickProjectedDraftValue for years with no market data.

findings.title: `_compute_pick_confidence` does unguarded arithmetic on four rank-signal sources' synthetic encodings
findings.evidence:
src/api/data_contract.py:5952-5960 reads canonicalSiteValues for `dlfSf`, `dynastyNerdsSfTep`, `dlfIdp` and `fantasyProsIdp` and feeds them into a coefficient of variation alongside the real 0-9999 values of ktcSfTep and idpTradeCalc. All four are `signal: rank` sources whose slot holds 999900 − rank×100. `rank_signal_source_keys()` at :1723-1735 exists specifically to prevent this: '⚠ Any consumer doing arithmetic over canonicalSiteValues MUST either skip these keys or read sourceRankMeta[key].valueContribution instead — mixing the six-digit encodings with native 0-9999 values has produced two real bugs.'
Currently latent: 0 of 144 live pick rows carry any of those four keys (verified). But the mechanism is live elsewhere — dlfRookieSf stamps six-digit synthetic values on 110 rows including synthetic pick-slot rows — so one registry or enrichment change makes every affected pick's CV ≈ 1.4 and forces bucket 'low'.
findings.userImpact: None today. One edit away from silently degrading every pick's confidence chip to 'low'.
findings.recommendedFix: Filter the key list through `rank_signal_source_keys()`, or read sourceRankMeta[key].valueContribution instead of the raw slot, before computing mean and stdev. Add a unit test with a rank-signal value present.
findings.affectedSystems: confidenceBucket and confidenceLabel on pick rows

findings.title: `valueContributionPath` is stamped from source membership, not from the branch actually taken
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:7243-7248 stamps 'value_direct' whenever `source_key in _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES and value_source_max[source_key] > 0`. But the branch at :7126-7130 routes a row down the Hill path when the source is in `value_range_suppressed` (D-1 escalation C) or when that row's value is out of range — and `value_source_max` remains > 0 in both cases. An entirely suppressed source would therefore report 'value_direct' on every row while every row actually used 'rank_hill'. Live: 0 mis-stamps (no out-of-range values on this build), so it is latent.
findings.userImpact: The value-chain audit panel and any audit script reading this field would be told the wrong thing precisely during the incident the D-1 guard exists to handle.
findings.recommendedFix: Set a local `path` variable inside the branch that actually executes and stamp that variable.

findings.title: `derived = int(norm_val)` truncates where every neighbouring stamp rounds
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:7645 `derived = int(norm_val)` — truncation toward zero. Contrast :7440 `int(round(blended_value))` for _blendedValueUncapped, :7452 `int(round(anchor_value))`, and :4649 `int(round(clamped_f))` in the clamp. Introduces a systematic downward bias of up to 1 point on every published value.
findings.userImpact: Under 0.05% on any single value; practically nil. Recorded because it means rankDerivedValue and _blendedValueUncapped can differ by 1 for the same unmodified row, which will eventually confuse someone diffing them.
findings.recommendedFix: `derived = int(round(norm_val))`.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's pipeline description is mechanically accurate but omits every place a stage is inert or dominant
findings.evidence:
I checked each numbered claim in CLAUDE.md's 'Live Value Pipeline' against the code and the live payload. CONFIRMED CORRECT: the 500 reference and its tail clamp; value-direct limited to exactly {ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc}; scope routing including ROOKIE routed=False; the TE double-count guard (0 ktcSfTep TE rows carry a tep stamp across 83 TE rows); α=0.10 on IDP and picks only with offense flat; the count-aware n=1/2/3-4/≥5 boundaries; λ=0 retired (madPenaltyApplied null on 1,092/1,092 rows); softFallbackCount diagnostic-only; the 30% single-source haircut; corridor clamp IDP-only (128/128); two-way boost running after the clamp; discount at Phase 3a before the sort and tethering at Phase 5.2b after it; registry weights all 1.0; default_weights.json unread.
GAPS, each material to reading a number off the board:
  1. Step 10 states the 0.15 cap without saying it binds on 100% of clamps, so the documented 'P90 drift band per confidence bucket' is inert in production.
  2. Step 6 says picks use anchor + α-shrinkage; the subgroup is empty on 144/144 live pick rows, so α is never applied to a pick — the stage is mean(KTC, IDPTC).
  3. Step 5a says the TE uplift runs '1.209 at the top of the board rising toward 2.05 down it'; the live observed range is 1.1017 to 1.6367, the low end produced by the 9999 ceiling clamp and 2.05 never reached.
  4. Nothing anywhere records that the three routed curves sit on different scales from the market values they are blended with (F-1).
  5. src/api/data_contract.py:3993-3995 asserts KTC and IDPTC 'price 2027/2028 picks only marginally below 2026'; both CSVs today price 2027 26% ABOVE 2026.
findings.userImpact: A reader following CLAUDE.md would believe the IDP board is a five-source consensus with a light outlier guard. It is IDPTradeCalc ±15%, with three of the five sources voting on a half-scale curve.
findings.recommendedFix: After fixing F-1 and F-3, restate steps 6 and 10 with the measured behaviour, correct the 2026-vs-2027 pick claim at :3993, and record the observed TE uplift range. Publish cappedByMaxBand counts and per-source Hampel drop rates in the build summary so drift like this is visible without rebuilding the contract by hand.

notes:
METHOD. I read the full blend path in src/api/data_contract.py (registry :1004-1699, helpers :164-6282, `_compute_unified_rankings` :6284-8022) plus src/canonical/player_valuation.py, src/league_intel/te_premium.py, src/canonical/idp_backbone.py and scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py. To get past reading, I copied src/, config/, CSVs/, exports/ and scripts/ into the scratchpad and ran `build_api_data_contract` on the real 2026-08-04 export there. That was deliberate: `_stamp_rank_changes` WRITES data/snapshots/ranks_last.json from inside `_compute_unified_rankings`, so running the pipeline in place would have modified the repository. Nothing under /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket was written. Every quantitative claim above comes from that rebuilt contract (1,092 rows; 550 offense / 398 IDP / 144 pick; 740 ranked).

FOUR EXACT REPRODUCTIONS, offered as proof the trace is right rather than merely plausible.
  Dallas Turner α-blend: subgroup [1899, 673, 2417] at n=3 → mean 1663.0, median 1899.0, center 1781.0 (matches the stamped subgroupBlendValue 1781); anchor 1865 (idpTradeCalc Hampel-dropped, DS alone survives); 1865 + 0.10·(1781−1865) = 1856.6 → 1856 (matches marketCorridorClamp.originalValue).
  Corridor clamp: 4164 × 0.85 = 3539.4 → 3539 (matches clampedValue).
  Pick discount: (7061 + 7052)/2 = 7056.5 (matches anchorValue 7056) × 0.82 = 5786.3 → 5786 (matches rankDerivedValue).
  TE basis lift: 794 × (1 + 43.555794·794^−0.632839) = 794 × 1.63669 = 1299.5 → 1300 (matches an observed flockFantasySfRookies TE contribution).

WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE DECISIONS. Offense values are defensible. The OFFENSE master tracks KTC closely (median 0.76× at equal rank, exactly 1.00 at the top of the board), the final offense board runs 1.04× KTC across ranks 1-50 decaying to roughly 0.83× by ranks 250-500, and no offense row is clamped. That mid-board compression is a curve-shape divergence worth knowing for package math but it does not invalidate ordering. IDP values do NOT currently deserve to influence decisions independently of IDPTradeCalc: every ranked IDP row carrying an IDPTC contribution sits within 15.1% of IDPTC by construction, 43.5% of them were forced there by the clamp, and three of the five IDP sources vote on a curve calibrated to roughly half the scale of the values they are averaged against. Pick values for years the vendors actually price are marked down 18-34% below every source that prices them. 2029 pick values contain no 2029 information at all.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY. (1) Whether the vendors' pick values are 'today' prices or 'at-draft' prices. This is the crux of the double-discount finding and it is not answerable from the repository — the market data (2027 Early 1st priced 26% above 2026 on both KTC and IDPTC) strongly implies 'today', but I am reporting the arithmetic, not asserting the vendor's semantics. (2) Whether the active rookie draft on 2026-08-04 is really 2026. `_derive_current_draft_year_from_names` says 2026 (72 slot-pick rows present) while the date fallback says 2027; they disagree and nothing reconciles them. If 2027 is correct, every future pick is over-discounted by an additional year and the 72 tethered picks are anchored to an already-drafted class. (3) Whether FantasyPros ECR includes Fitzmaurice as a panelist — if it does, that analyst is counted three times on 298 rows. (4) Whether the `is_tep_premium: True` tags on draftSharks/idpTradeCalc/yahooBoone and the `False` on fantasyCalc are correct; these are unverifiable claims about vendor board configuration, and te_premium.py explicitly refuses to interpolate the tep↔tepp conversion those tags trigger while the pipeline multiplies a flat 1.10 anyway.

DEAD, DORMANT OR INERT CODE FOUND. Phase 1c FootballGuys CSV-rank restoration (:6802-6862) — key set empty on every build, 0 rows carry method 'csv_combined_cross_market'; the code comment already documents this honestly. `coverage_weight` (idp_backbone.py:307) — stamped as effectiveWeight, never applied, and 1.0 for every registered source regardless. `_MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA` — 0.0, with madPenaltyApplied null on 1,092/1,092 rows. `_MARKET_ANCHOR_FALLBACKS['offense']` — a five-source chain that can never be reached because offense rows are excluded at :4596. The per-bucket P90 band in the corridor clamp — computed on every build and overridden by the 0.15 cap on 128/128 clamps. `tep_native_correction` — accepted as a parameter and explicitly discarded at :6425. α-shrinkage on picks — the subgroup is empty on 144/144 rows. The ROOKIE Hill master — fit weekly, routed never.

MISSING-DATA BEHAVIOUR, CONSOLIDATED (asked directly). A source missing for a player is DROPPED, never zeroed and never imputed: the key is absent from `source_ranks`, the source contributes to no list, and the only trace is `softFallbackCount`, which is explicitly excluded from the math (:7318-7347). A source value of ≤ 0 is treated as 'unranked' and dropped at :6650-6652, with a deliberate carve-out for the DraftSharks combined-rank keys whose scale legitimately goes negative. A value-direct source with a missing, zero, or out-of-range raw value silently falls back to the Hill path for that row (:7126-7138) — so the same source can vote on the market scale for one player and the curve scale for another inside one blend. A player with no source coverage at all never enters `row_normalized` and receives neither a value nor a rank; on this build that is 352 of 1,092 rows, including all 35 single-source-haircut rows. The one place data absence produces a NUMBER rather than an absence is the corridor clamp's stage-3 fallback (:4530-4542), which anchors a row to the median of whatever contributions exist, or to a single source's contribution labelled `single_source_fallback`.
