formulas.name: Confidence bucket (non-pick rows)
formulas.expression:
if source_count >= 2 and percentile_spread is not None:
    <= 0.08 -> "high"; <= 0.20 -> "medium"
elif source_count >= 2 and source_rank_spread is not None:   # LEGACY, unreachable in production
    <= 30 -> "high"; <= 80 -> "medium"
fall through: source_count >= 1 -> "low"; else "none"
formulas.inputs: source_count = len(effective_source_ranks), post-Hampel matched sources (count); percentile_spread from _percentile_rank_spread (0-1); source_rank_spread = max-min of effective ordinals (rank units, dead branch). Quarantine may later downgrade high/medium to low (:3049-3052).
formulas.outputRange: {high, medium, low, none}. Live 740 ranked: high 108, medium 228, low 404; 304 unranked 'none'.
formulas.constants: 0.08 / 0.20 hand-picked; the 0.20 is justified only by aligning to the suspicious_disagreement threshold, itself hand-picked. 30 / 80 retained explicitly "so their existing expectations still hold" (:114-116) — i.e. kept for tests. No calibration artifact for any of the four exists in the repo.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Unmatched sources are simply absent from percentile_spread, so missing coverage can RAISE the bucket. softFallbackCount is never an input. percentile_spread None (fewer than 2 sources with positive pool size) -> falls through to 'low'. source_count 0 -> 'none'.
formulas.validated: none found. tests/api/test_trust_confidence.py::TestConfidenceBucket exercises only the dead absolute-ordinal branch (all 7 cases omit percentile_spread).
formulas.mathIssues: Source count contributes nothing past the >=2 gate: 288 of 404 'low' rows have >=5 sources, only 7 are single-source, yet all read 'Low — single source or wide disagreement'. Counterexample: CJ Donaldson RB, 2 of 16 eligible sources matched (softFallbackCount 14), ranks {fantasyProsSf 433, draftSharks 393 raw}, pools ~473/~420 -> 0.9154 vs 0.9357 -> spread 0.0247 -> 'high', while the two value votes are 919 and 1698 (85% apart).

formulas.name: Percentile rank spread (the disagreement statistic)
formulas.expression:
for each matched source k:
    raw_rank = meta[k].rawRank or meta[k].effectiveRank or effective_rank
    depth    = source_pool_sizes[k] or meta[k].depth or 0     # skip when <= 0
    pct[k]   = clamp(raw_rank / depth, 0, 1)
if len(pct) < 2: None
if len(pct) >= 5: sorted(pct)[-2] - sorted(pct)[1]            # trim one per side
else:             max(pct) - min(pct)
formulas.inputs: Raw pre-translation per-source ordinal rank and the auto-detected per-source pool size from Phase 1 (:6671). Live pool sizes span dlfSf 278 to idpTradeCalc 902.
formulas.constants: _PERCENTILE_SPREAD_TRIM_MIN_N = 5 — the only constant in the audit scope with a measurement behind it (:130-138 cites a 2026-07-25 audit: top-200 disagreement 143 -> ~40, suspicious 82 -> ~15). Live top-200 counts are now 10 and 6, so it no longer reproduces.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A source with pool size 0 is skipped (`continue` :3974); a source that did not rank the player never enters the loop. Both shrink the measured disagreement, so missing data narrows the statistic.
formulas.validated: partial — trim behavior pinned by tests/api/test_disagreement_trimming.py via _compute_anomaly_flags only; the cited measurement is not reproducible on the current board.
formulas.mathIssues: Trimming at n>=5 discards the two most informative observations, so a genuine 2-vs-N split reads tight. Dividing by pool size makes 'rank 433 of 473' and 'rank 393 of 420' agreement even when the resulting Hill values differ by 85%.

formulas.name: Depth-aware disagreement allowance and the two flags
formulas.expression:
allowance = min(max(rank / ranked_pool_size, 0), 0.25)
hasSourceDisagreement   = percentile_spread > 0.10 + allowance
suspicious_disagreement = percentile_spread > 0.20 + allowance
formulas.inputs: percentile_spread (0-1); canonicalConsensusRank; ranked pool size — 800 in Phase 4, re-stamped against final_total = 740.
formulas.outputRange: booleans. Live: 135 and 52 of 740; top-200: 10 and 6.
formulas.constants: 0.10 base, 0.20 suspicious, 0.25 allowance cap — all hand-picked. The 0.25 cap makes the 'linear' allowance a constant for every row past rank 185 (0.25 x 740), i.e. 555 of 740 rows (75%).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: percentile_spread None -> both flags False. Absent disagreement evidence reads as agreement, not unknown.
formulas.validated: none found for the thresholds.
formulas.mathIssues: Of the 555 rows past saturation, 497 exceed the 0.10 base threshold but only 127 fire — the constant +0.25 suppresses 370. The legacy fallback (absolute spread > 150 ordinals, :2016-2019) is unreachable because percentile_spread is always supplied.

formulas.name: Pick confidence (CV of raw pick-source values)
formulas.expression:
raw_values = [v for k in (ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc, dlfSf, dynastyNerdsSfTep, dlfIdp, fantasyProsIdp) if canonicalSiteValues[k] > 0]
effective_count = sum(0.5 if k == "ktcSfTep" and is_slot_specific else 1.0)
mean = sum/n;  cv = sqrt(sum((v-mean)^2)/n)/mean        # population sd; n<2 -> cv None
cv None -> "low";  count >= 1.5 and cv <= 0.15 -> "high";  count >= 1.0 and cv <= 0.30 -> "medium";  else "low"
formulas.inputs: Raw native-scale source values (0-9999) for at most six keys; is_slot_specific from _parse_pick_slot.
formulas.outputRange: {high, medium, low, none}. Live: every future-year generic tier pick lands 'high' (ktcSfTep 1.0 + idpTradeCalc 1.0 = 2.0, cv <= 0.15).
formulas.constants: 0.5 KTC-slot discount, 1.5/1.0 count gates, 0.15/0.30 CV cuts — all hand-picked, no fitting artifact.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No values -> ('none','None — no pick source values'). Exactly one -> cv None -> 'low'. Sources outside the six-key list contribute nothing and never lower the bucket.
formulas.validated: none found — no test pins _compute_pick_confidence.
formulas.mathIssues: With only two real pick markets, 'high' means 'the two sources that exist agree within 15%'. 21 pick rows carry softFallbackCount 12 alongside a 'high' badge. The key list is hardcoded and does not track _RANKING_SOURCES.

formulas.name: Gap-based tier detection (authoritative tier IDs)
formulas.expression:
series[i] = -rankDerivedValue[i]
gap[i]    = value[i] - value[i+1]
rm[i]     = median(gap[max(0,i-7) : min(n,i+8)])
score[i]  = gap[i]/rm[i] if rm[i] > 1e-9 else (1.0 if gap[i] < 1e-9 else 3.0)
break after i iff score[i] >= 2.0 AND players_since_last_break >= 3
formulas.inputs: Compacted rankDerivedValue series in rank order (0-9999); canonicalName as the id.
formulas.outputRange: 1..N uncapped. Live: 127 tiers over 740 rows; tier size min 3 / median 5 / mean 5.83 / max 15.
formulas.constants: TIER_GAP_WINDOW 7, TIER_GAP_THRESHOLD 2.0, TIER_MIN_SIZE 3 — hand-picked, no fit script or backtest in the tree.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `-float(r.get('rankDerivedValue') or 0)` coerces missing to 0, which would manufacture a huge gap; in practice only ranked rows are fed and all have positive values (min 757 live).
formulas.validated: none found for these constants. tests/scoring/test_tiering.py tests a DIFFERENT implementation (src/scoring/tiering.py, Cohen's-d, per-position) that is not on this path.
formulas.mathIssues: score is scale-free, so a break fires on the same RELATIVE gap whether the drop is 400 points or 8. Live boundary drops: median 8 points / 0.45%, 96 of 126 under 1%, 50 at <= 5 points. Worked example at the exact rank the docstring names: break after rank 311, values 1957 -> 1945, gap 12, local gaps [5,3,2,1,1,4,0,12,6,5,3,8,12,2,2], rolling median 3, score 12/3 = 4.00 >= 2.0 -> break. The docstring at :2094-2098 says a 3-point drop at 312->313 must NOT be a boundary.

formulas.name: Rank-based tier ladder
formulas.inputs: canonicalConsensusRank only.
formulas.constants: 12/36/72/120/200/350/500/650/800 — justified solely as mirroring frontend/lib/rankings-helpers.js::rankBasedTierId, i.e. a hardcode mirroring a hardcode.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Every rank maps to a tier; the frontend fallback assigns tier 10 to any row past 800, including rows the backend deliberately left unranked.
formulas.validated: none found beyond a shape assertion that ranked rows carry canonicalTierId.
formulas.mathIssues: Dead for ranked rows — overwritten by gap detection in the same build. Survives only as the frontend fallback, where it labels deliberately-unranked rows 'Tier 10' rather than 'Unranked'.

formulas.name: compact_ranks_and_tiers — the one ranker
formulas.expression:
candidates = [r for r in rows if r["canonicalConsensusRank"]]
sort key   = (-int(rankDerivedValue or 0), int(canonicalConsensusRank))
for r in order:
    if assetClass == "pick" and _parse_pick_slot(name).year == anchor_year:
        rank = None; tier = None; continue
    new_rank += 1; r.canonicalConsensusRank = new_rank
then canonicalTierId = _compute_value_based_tier_ids(kept rows)
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue (0-9999), prior rank as tiebreak, assetClass, canonicalName, anchor_year = current_rookie_draft_year().
formulas.outputRange: Contiguous 1..N. Live: 800 stamped in Phase 4 -> 740 returned (60 dropped: 2026 anchor slot picks + suppressed generics).
formulas.constants: none beyond anchor_year.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `int(rankDerivedValue or 0)` sorts a missing value to the bottom rather than excluding it; only rows with a truthy prior rank are candidates.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_ranking_coherence.py and test_single_authority.py assert contiguity, uniqueness and rank/value monotonicity, but both sort by rank first so neither pins array order. tests/league_intel/test_publish.py pins caller-row isolation and anchor-slot-pick exclusion.
formulas.mathIssues: Returns only ranked rows; overlay.py:100-113 documents that serving that subset drops 353 of 1093 rows including every 2026 pick, hence copy_rows=False over its own copies. 72 unranked rows retain a positive rankDerivedValue by design.

formulas.name: Market gap direction and magnitude
formulas.inputs: Effective (post-Hampel, post-translation) ordinal ranks. UNNORMALIZED — mixes a 278-deep board with a 902-deep one.
formulas.outputRange: enum + magnitude in raw ordinal-rank units. Live: none 672, consensus_premium 249, retail_premium 171.
formulas.constants: the is_retail registry flag — exactly one source carries it (ktcSfTep). The registry comment :985-994 claims adding a second retail source is a pure registry change and 'the gap logic generalizes'.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Either side empty -> ('none', None). IDP rows never carry ktcSfTep so every IDP row is permanently 'none'; /edge works around this with a separate IDPTC-anchored path (frontend/app/edge/page.jsx:169-180).
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_trust_confidence.py has ~8 cases, all on synthetic equal-depth rank dicts, structurally blind to the defect. No backtest.
formulas.mathIssues: Averaging ordinals across pools of different depth — the exact error _percentile_rank_spread's docstring warns about. Dalton Kincaid raw gap +9.38 vs pool-normalized +33.47. Across 422 rows carrying a gap, 215 (50.9%) change sign under normalization: offense 183/389 (47.0%), picks 32/33 (97.0%).

formulas.name: Market corridor clamp (the only live value band)
formulas.expression:
# offense exempt; anchor = ktcSfTep (offense) / idpTradeCalc (idp) with a fallback chain
drift  = |rankDerivedValue - anchor| / anchor
band_b = P90(drift within confidence bucket) if n_bucket >= 30 else P90(drift over whole board)
band   = min(band_b, 0.15)
if drift > band: rankDerivedValue = round(anchor * (1 +/- band))    # direction preserved
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue (0-9999), the anchor's native-scale value from canonicalSiteValues, confidenceBucket, assetClass.
formulas.outputRange: Inside [anchor*0.85, anchor*1.15]. Live: 128 rows clamped, all IDP, all at band 0.15, cappedByMaxBand True on every one.
formulas.constants: _MARKET_CORRIDOR_PERCENTILE 0.90, _MARKET_CORRIDOR_MIN_BUCKET_N 30, idp max band 0.15. The first two are inert; 0.15 is hand-picked and justified narratively at :4409-4415.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No resolvable anchor -> row skipped entirely (no clamp, no stamp), so a row the market does not price is never contained. Unranked rows skipped (:4595).
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_market_corridor_clamp.py pins the mechanism on synthetic rows — not the 0.15 choice, and not the fact that the cap always binds.
formulas.mathIssues: The dynamic per-bucket band never binds: measured bucket P90s are high 0.5423 (n=29), medium 0.4805 (n=91), low 0.5119 (n=174), overall 0.5096 — all 3.2-3.6x the cap. Worked example: Abdul Carter DL, anchor 5409, blend 3532, drift 0.347 > 0.15 -> clamped to 5409*0.85 = 4598. 128 of 294 ranked IDP rows (43.5%) clamped. The clamp reads confidenceBucket (computed pre-clamp) and derives its band from the same board it modifies.

formulas.name: Single-source value haircut
formulas.expression:
if not row_is_pick and len(all_values) <= 1:
    blended_value *= 0.30
    _blendedValueUncapped = round(blended_value)
    singleSourceValuePenaltyApplied = True
formulas.inputs: all_values = post-Hampel per-source Hill contributions.
formulas.outputRange: 30% of the uncorroborated blend. Live: 75 rows isSingleSource True, 195 rows sourceCount 1.
formulas.constants: 0.30 retention — hand-picked; CLAUDE.md states it as policy with no derivation.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: The one place where missing coverage correctly and heavily penalizes the number. Applies to the VALUE but not to confidenceBucket, which reaches 'low' by a separate rule.
formulas.validated: none found for the 0.30 figure; tests/api/test_data_contract.py checks the stamp exists.
formulas.mathIssues: Picks are exempt, so a pick resting on one market keeps full value. The flag is absent from _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS and goes stale under overrides (empirically changes on 1 row when ktcSfTep+dlfSf are disabled).

formulas.name: softFallbackCount (coverage transparency metric)
formulas.expression:
count = 0
for src in active_sources:                                  # override-aware
    if src.key in source_ranks: continue
    if row_is_pick and src.needs_rookie_translation: continue
    if not any(_scope_eligible(row_pos, s, src.position_group) for s in [src.scope]+src.extra_scopes): continue
    if source_pool_sizes.get(src.key, 0) <= 0: continue
    count += 1
formulas.inputs: Override-filtered active source registry, matched source_ranks, row position, per-source pool sizes.
formulas.constants: none.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: This IS the missing-data metric. It is computed correctly, stamped, shipped in the delta, and read by nothing that produces a verdict — no confidence rule, no anomaly flag, no clamp. compact_view.py:64 prunes it entirely on mobile.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.mathIssues: Arithmetic correct; the defect is inertness. 24 'high'-confidence rows carry softFallbackCount >= 5, and the comment at :7310-7318 deliberately chose to keep it 'purely as a transparency metric ... without that signal touching the math'.

formulas.name: sourceSpread / hillValueSpread / madPenaltyApplied
formulas.expression:
_, source_mad   = _trimmed_mean_median(all_values)         # UNWEIGHTED MAD
mad_penalty     = min(center, LAMBDA * source_mad) if LAMBDA > 0 and not pick else 0.0   # LAMBDA == 0.0
blended_value   = max(0, center - mad_penalty)
sourceSpread    = round(source_mad, 2)
hillValueSpread = round(stdev(all_values), 2) if len(all_values) >= 2 else None
formulas.inputs: all_values = post-Hampel per-source Hill contributions on 0-9999.
formulas.outputRange: Hill points. Example: CJ Donaldson sourceSpread 389.5, hillValueSpread 550.84 against a value of 1308.
formulas.constants: _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA = 0.0 since 2026-04-20 — the penalty is off, so madPenaltyApplied is None on every row.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Fewer than 2 contributions -> hillValueSpread None. Uncovered sources are absent, so both statistics understate disagreement in proportion to missing coverage.
formulas.validated: n/a — pure diagnostics.
formulas.mathIssues: hillValueSpread is the statistic that would make confidenceBucket measure VALUE agreement, computed on the same row and then unused. Relative dispersion by bucket: high median 0.064 / p90 0.421, medium 0.129 / 0.423, low 0.195 / 0.450 — medians separate, tails do not. 20 of 107 'high' rows exceed 0.30. madPenaltyApplied is a permanent None retained only because 'frontend builds still read the key' (:7474-7476).

formulas.name: Expected sources / isSingleSource / sourceAudit
formulas.expression:
for src in _RANKING_SOURCES:                                # NEVER consults source_overrides
    skip unless _scope_eligible(pos, src.scope, src.position_group)
    skip if is_rookie and src.excludes_rookies
    skip if src.needs_rookie_translation and (not is_rookie or pos == "PICK")
    skip if src.depth and player_effective_rank > round(depth * 1.25)
isSingleSource             = len(source_ranks) == 1 and len(expected_keys) > 1
isStructurallySingleSource = len(source_ranks) == 1 and len(expected_keys) <= 1
reason in {no_source_match, structurally_single_source, matching_failure_other_sources_eligible, partial_coverage, fully_matched}
formulas.inputs: Position, rookie flag, best matched rank as a depth probe, the full source registry.
formulas.outputRange: Two key sets + a reason enum. Live: 75 isSingleSource rows.
formulas.constants: the 1.25 depth-headroom multiplier — hand-picked.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Depth and rookie pruning correctly stop structurally-impossible coverage from reading as a matching failure (documented at :3894-3921 with the Colston Loveland case).
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_expected_sources.py.
formulas.mathIssues: Override-blind: with sources disabled, expectedSources still lists them, unmatchedSources counts them as failures, and isSingleSource fires on a deliberate configuration. sourceAudit is absent from the delta while isSingleSource is present, so the boolean and its explanation disagree.

formulas.name: rankChange (movement vs the previous build)
formulas.expression:
previous = json.load(data/snapshots/ranks_last.json)   # {canonicalName: rank}, NO timestamp
rankChange = previous[name] - canonicalConsensusRank   if previous[name] is a positive int else None
if write_snapshot:  overwrite the file with {name: current_rank}
write_snapshot = not source_overrides                  # ignores _for_delta and both TEP knobs
formulas.inputs: canonicalName, canonicalConsensusRank, the flat name->rank JSON snapshot.
formulas.outputRange: Signed integer (positive = up) or None. Stamped only on tiered_rows, so unranked rows never carry it.
formulas.constants: none.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing/unparseable snapshot or an absent name -> None (correct: newly ranked is not zero movement). Snapshot write failure is swallowed silently (:4746-4750).
formulas.validated: none found — no test covers _stamp_rank_changes.
formulas.mathIssues: normalize_source_overrides returns {} for a TEP-only body (reserved-key skip :2374-2378) and for the explicit enabled_sources shape with everything enabled (:2366), so those requests reach write_snapshot=True and clobber the shared baseline. rankChange is absent from _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS while canonicalConsensusRank is present; rebuilding with two sources disabled against a seeded snapshot produced 571 rows with non-zero rankChange (max +370, Eric Rivers). The snapshot carries no timestamp, so 'since the previous scrape' is unverifiable from the artifact.

formulas.name: /api/movers riser/faller selection
formulas.expression:
history = rank_history.load_history(days=window+1)     # last window+1 SNAPSHOTS, not days
for each series with len >= 2:
    r_now = series[-1].rank;  r_then = series[0].rank
    delta = r_then - r_now                              # positive = rose
    keep iff |delta| >= threshold
risers sorted by -delta, fallers by delta, sliced to limit
formulas.inputs: data/rank_history.jsonl series; live contract rows for team/position/value enrichment.
formulas.outputRange: window clamped [2,90] default 14; threshold >= 1 default 15; limit clamped [1,50] default 10.
formulas.constants: 14 / 15 / 10 — hand-picked; nothing establishes that a 15-rank move is the level at which movement becomes actionable.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty history -> empty lists with asOf None (honest). Fewer than 2 snapshots -> skipped. A player absent from the contract still emits with null position/team/value.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.mathIssues: series[0] is the first snapshot in which THAT player appears in the window, so the comparison horizon varies per player while the response stamps a single window value. currentSourceRanks contains absolute ranks copied from sourceOriginalRanks (:3470-3476) despite the docstring calling it perSourceDelta (:3362) and describing a delta breakdown (:3369-3371).

formulas.name: Rank-history persistence and value backfill
formulas.expression:
key   = f"{canonicalName}::{assetClass}"                  # assetClass inferred if absent (:216-249)
entry = {"date": YYYY-MM-DD UTC, "ranks": {key: rank}, "values": {key: rankDerivedValue}}
append: drop existing line with the same date, append, sort, trim to last 1095
load:   windowed = entries[-days:]                        # SNAPSHOTS, not calendar days
        val = stored_values[key] else rank_to_value_for_scope(rank, scope_from_key_suffix)
formulas.inputs: Contract playersArray (rank + rankDerivedValue), UTC date.
formulas.constants: 1095 retention and the 30-day default window — both documented with reasoning at :78-92.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Only rows with a positive integer rank are captured, so an unranked player leaves a gap rather than a zero. Corrupt JSONL lines are skipped, not fatal (:257-263). Legacy entries lacking a values block are back-filled from rank and the reconstruction is NOT flagged on the returned point — unlike source_history, which sets derived: true.
formulas.validated: coverage() (:405-470) reports snapshots/spanDays/missingDays/staleDays so a stall is detectable, but nothing asserts against a real log, and neither log file exists in this checkout.
formulas.mathIssues: Date dedup with last-write-wins means only the final scrape of each day survives the 2-hourly refresh — a board is reconstructable as-of a DATE, not as-of a scrape, and intraday movement is unrecoverable. `days` is a snapshot count, so with gaps the returned window spans more calendar time than the parameter name implies.

formulas.name: Source-history persistence and derived-blend reconstruction
formulas.expression:
sources[k] = rawSourceValues[k]                   for k in {"ktcSfTep"}
           = sourceRankMeta[k].valueContribution                          # normal path
           = canonicalSiteValues[k]               only if meta yielded nothing
then drop k in {"ktc"} and drop scope-mismatched k
load: value = blended if persisted else round(median(positive source values)) with derived=True
backfill only: sourceRanks derived by sorting each source column desc, ties by player key
formulas.inputs: Contract rows; historical dynasty_data_*.json exports for backfill.
formulas.constants: MAX_SNAPSHOTS 1095; DEFAULT_HISTORY_WINDOW_DAYS 180; _RETIRED_FROM_CHART_KEYS {"ktc"}; _RAW_VALUE_PREFERRED_KEYS {"ktcSfTep"}.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: The most honest module in scope: a reconstructed blend is flagged derived: true and disclosed as 'within ~5% for most players'; a derived per-source rank never overwrites a contract-stamped one (:400-406); scope-mismatched values are masked at BOTH write and read time so pre-fix snapshots are corrected on read.
formulas.validated: none found for the '~5%' accuracy claim.
formulas.mathIssues: Same date-dedup and snapshot-vs-days issues as rank_history. The module header states 180-snapshot retention and 15 MB against a constant of 1095 / ~90 MB. _norm_name_key is coupled cross-language to frontend/lib/value-history.js::buildHistoryLookup with only a prose warning.

formulas.name: Rankings delta payload
formulas.inputs: Raw scraper payload, source overrides, TEP multipliers, optional league-adjusted factors.
formulas.outputRange: ~1.25 MB uncompressed vs ~4 MB full; 55 per-player fields.
formulas.constants: the 55-entry field tuple.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `if field in row` — an absent field is omitted and the frontend merge keeps the base value. There is no explicit null, so 'unchanged' and 'not computed for this board' are indistinguishable on the wire.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_source_overrides.py::TestBuildRankingsDeltaPayload pins shape, byte bounds and that every LISTED field round-trips — it cannot detect an omission.
formulas.mathIssues: Empirically incomplete. Rebuilding with {ktcSfTep: off, dlfSf: off} and diffing against the default board, these change but are not listed: sourceAudit (510 rows), pickRookieAnchor (56), twoWayPlayerBoost (1), singleSourceValuePenaltyApplied (1); rankChange changes on 571 rows once a snapshot exists. Conversely marketConfidence IS listed but is a scraper pass-through no override can move.

formulas.name: apply_valuation_factors (league-adjusted composition)
formulas.inputs: Per-player scarcity factors keyed by display name; the freshly built override board.
formulas.outputRange: count of re-valued rows; rows mutated in place.
formulas.constants: none.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A player absent from the factor map keeps their market value and is ranked against adjusted peers — a silently mixed board. valuationAdjustment is stamped whether or not anything moved (:9138-9147), correctly distinguishing 'applied, moved nothing' from 'never applied'.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/valuation-overlay.test.js; tests/league_intel/test_publish.py; tests/api/test_valuation_mode_threading.py statically requires every handler applying the lens to stamp valuationMode.
formulas.mathIssues: Name-keyed, so a cross-universe collision applies one position's scarcity factor to both rows. Mutates in place; the docstring correctly warns callers must own the list.

formulas.name: Compact view pruning
formulas.inputs: The full contract payload.
formulas.outputRange: Non-destructive copy stamped meta.view = 'compact'. Selected by frontend/lib/device-profile.js:103-107 for mobile or slow networks.
formulas.constants: the three frozensets.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Pruned fields are absent, not null, so a mobile client cannot distinguish 'pruned' from 'never computed' without reading meta.view.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_compact_view.py asserts poolAudit is dropped and the original unmutated — a subset of the prune list.
formulas.mathIssues: No math. The docstring lists 6 of 18 pruned player fields. Keeping confidenceBucket while dropping confidenceLabel and anomalyFlags leaves the mobile confidence badge uninterpretable and hides quarantine reasons while `quarantined` survives.

formulas.name: Injury-to-value discount
formulas.expression:
if month(now_ms) in {2,3,4,5,6,7,8}: return 0% with offseasonSuppressed=True
base  = {alert: 4.0, watch: 2.0, info: 0.5}[severity]
pos   = {RB:1.20, WR:1.00, TE:0.90, QB:0.70, DL/LB/DB/IDP/DE/DT/CB/S:0.80, else 1.00}
age   = 0.80 if rookie else {<=25:0.80, <=28:1.00, <=31:1.20, else 1.40}   # unknown age -> 1.00
decay = 1 - age_ms/(30*24*3600*1000) clamped [0,1]
discount = min(5.0, round(base*pos*age*decay, 2))          # worst-case item wins
adjustedValue = max(1, round(rankDerivedValue * (100-discount)/100))
formulas.inputs: News items with severity and ts/timestamp; row pos, age, rookie flag, rankDerivedValue; now_ms.
formulas.constants: 4.0/2.0/0.5 base, five position multipliers, four age multipliers, 30-day decay window, 5.0 cap, Feb-Aug offseason set — every one hand-picked. The header is explicit that this is 'a codified rulebook ... derived from the well-known fantasy-football conventional wisdom', not a fit.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Unknown news timestamp -> decay 1.0 ('assume brand new so the decay doesn't under-discount') — conservative. Unknown/zero age -> multiplier 1.00, i.e. NEUTRAL, not penalized. An item tagging any affected player impact == 'positive' is skipped entirely even at alert severity (:246-253).
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_injury_impact.py — 13 tests pin the 5% cap, half-decay at 15 days, zero at 30, positive-impact skip, worst-case selection and the offseason month boundary. The constants are pinned; nothing validates them against realized price moves.
formulas.mathIssues: Worked examples at now = 2026-10-15: RB/33/alert/1h -> 4.0 x 1.20 x 1.40 x 0.9986 = 6.71 capped to 5.0%; RB/27/alert -> 4.79%; QB/24/alert -> 2.24%; WR/27/watch -> 2.00%; WR/27/info -> 0.50%; DB/30/alert -> 3.83%; RB/27/alert at 360h -> decay 0.5 -> 2.40%. The cap binds only for RB age >= 32 at alert. At the repo's current date (2026-08-04) the offseason gate returns 0% for a torn ACL, so the subsystem is a no-op today.

formulas.name: Effective auction power (S-curve draft-capital lens)
formulas.expression:
median  = median(raw);  mad = median(|raw - median|)
spread  = max(mad * 1.4826, 0.01 * (grand_total / n))
weighted_i = raw_i * (1 + 0.35 * tanh(((raw_i - median)/spread) / 1.25))
weighted[leader] += 0.15 * spread * tanh((raw_leader - raw_runner)/spread)
scaled  = weighted * (sum(raw)/sum(weighted))
return largest-remainder rounding of scaled to exactly round(sum(raw))
formulas.inputs: {team: raw draft-capital dollars}. League pool is a fixed $1200 over 72 picks.
formulas.outputRange: Integer dollars summing to the raw league total; per-team multiplier bounded [0.65, 1.35] pre-rounding.
formulas.constants: premium_gain 0.35, curvature 1.25, leapfrog_weight 0.15 — labelled 'Conservative defaults' (:70) with no fit. 1.4826 is the standard MAD-to-sigma constant. The 0.01*(total/n) floor prevents z-score blowup on a degenerate field.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Identity (raw totals, rounded) when disabled, fewer than 2 teams, grand_total <= 0, or a non-positive weighted sum — an uninformative field provably returns untouched numbers.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_auction_power.py pins zero-sum, the band, identity cases and enabled=False. tests/api/test_auction_power_parity.py regex-scrapes the three JS constants and compares them to the dataclass, and states at :21-27 that it deliberately does NOT compare outputs. No backtest against completed drafts; the module's Phase 2 note (:37-50) says the heuristic should eventually be replaced by a simulated mini-auction gated on such a backtest.
formulas.mathIssues: The Python implementation has no non-test caller — live numbers come from the JS mirror, so a structural (non-constant) divergence is untested. Rounding can violate the stated band for sub-$5 holdings (the parity test documents a $1 team rounding to 0); irrelevant at realistic draft capital.

formulas.name: FAAB tier bucketing and league bid statistics
formulas.expression:
tier = first label in ((tier1,0.20),(tier2,0.10),(tier3,0.03),(tier4,0.0)) with bid/league_budget >= breakpoint
per_player_bid = bid / max(1, len(adds))
stats_block    = {avg: fmean(v), min, max, count}  or  {0.0, 0, 0, 0} when empty
team avgBid    = totalSpent / winningCount
leagueAvg/Median over all bids > 0
formulas.inputs: Sleeper waiver/free_agent transactions (settings.waiver_bid), snapshot.nfl_players for position, current-season waiver_budget (fallback 100).
formulas.outputRange: Dollar statistics scaled to the league budget; tierBids / positionBids / teamAggression / recentWins (<=25) / playerHistory.
formulas.constants: 0.20 / 0.10 / 0.03 breakpoints (commented 'Calibrated for a 100-budget league' but not fit to anything); budget fallback 100; recent_limit 25.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty stats collapse to zeros, so 'no bids' and 'average $0' are the same value; leagueAvg/Median default to 0.0. Both live consumers guard correctly — src/trade/faab_recommender.py:186-189 requires count >= 3 and :217-222 a positive median plus a minimum bid count; frontend/components/waivers/ManualAddDrop.jsx:113-119 tests avg > 0. Unresolvable player ids yield position None and drop from positionBids but stay in playerHistory.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_faab_analytics.py exists; no calibration of the breakpoints. Failed bids are structurally unavailable from Sleeper and the module says so (:29-32), so every statistic is winner-biased.
formulas.mathIssues: _tier_for_bid's docstring promises zero-bid pickups reach tier4, but the caller gates on bid > 0 (:213-215) so tierBids never contains one. Multi-add transactions split the bid evenly across positions, attributing a WR's share of a claim to an RB in the same claim.

formulas.name: Public trade grading (valuation bridge + alpha weighting)
formulas.expression:
value(asset) = by_id[playerId] -> by_name[playerName.lower()] -> 0.0                        # players
             = first hit of {Mid,Early,Late} x round-label, then Pick R.{06,02,10}, else 0.0  # picks
side_total = sum(max(value, 1.0) ** 1.65)
pct = ((max_w - min_w)/max_w) * 100
pct < 3 -> all sides A/Fair; else top side gets the winner grade, bottom the loser grade,
middles Fair; bands 3 / 8 / 15 / 25 / 40
formulas.inputs: Public trade-side asset dicts {kind, playerId, playerName, season, round}; the cached private contract's values bundle and pickAliases.
formulas.outputRange: {grade, color, label} per side; A+ / A / A- / B+ / B / C / D / F.
formulas.constants: _GRADE_ALPHA 1.65; _GRADE_PCT_FAIR 3.0, SLIGHT 8.0, GOOD 15.0, CLEAR 25.0, ROBBERY 40.0; tier-center slots Early=2, Mid=6, Late=10. All mirror frontend/lib/league-analysis.js and trade-logic.js by prose contract, with no parity test.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Silently 0.0 for any unresolved player or pick, then floored to 1.0 before exponentiation — a side that received an unpriced asset is graded as having received essentially nothing, with no `unresolved` reporting. All-zero -> graded 'Fair' (activity.py:125-129). NaN/inf sanitized to 0.0 (:105-107). Suppressed generic-tier pick rows excluded (:126). 352 of 1092 live rows are unranked and many carry no positive values bundle.
formulas.validated: none found for the alpha or the bands.
formulas.mathIssues: pct is computed on the alpha-exponentiated totals, so the labelled percentages are not value percentages: 5000 vs 4000 (a 20% value gap) gives 1 - 0.8^1.65 = 31.0% -> 'Big win' (>= 25), and the 3% 'Fair trade' band corresponds to a raw gap of about 1.8%. Winner/loser assignment uses float equality (weighted[i] == max_w), so exactly-tied sides fall through to the fair grade.

formulas.name: Pick draft-value projection
formulas.expression:
projected = round(rankDerivedValue / pickYearDiscount)    # discount defaults to 1.0, clamped to (0,1]
gain      = max(0, projected - rankDerivedValue)
gainPct   = round(gain / rankDerivedValue * 100)
formulas.inputs: Post-blend, post-anchor rankDerivedValue; the multiplicative year discount from config/weights/pick_year_discount.json stamped at :6104-6107.
formulas.constants: the discount table in config/weights/pick_year_discount.json (docstring cites 0.82 for a 2027 first).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No parseable year or non-positive value -> no stamp at all. A discount outside (0,1] is coerced to 1.0, producing a zero-gain projection rather than a wrong one.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_pick_refinement.py covers the discount and refinement passes; nothing validates the premise that a pick's undiscounted value today equals its value on draft day.
formulas.mathIssues: A pure inversion of the discount, so it reproduces the pre-discount blend exactly and forecasts nothing beyond 'the discount will unwind'. Current-year picks land with no pickYearDiscount stamp and project to their own value with zero gain, which is correct.

formulas.name: Pick slot monotonization
formulas.expression:
bucket slot picks by YEAR (not current year only)
tuples = sorted [(rank, value, tier, blendedSourceRank, sourceRankSpread, percentileSpread)] by rank
picks_sorted = sorted picks by (round, slot)
zip(tuples, picks_sorted) -> reassign the tuple onto the pick
formulas.inputs: Ranked slot-pick rows and their existing rank/value/tier/spread stamps.
formulas.outputRange: A permutation; global rank/value monotonicity preserved by construction. Live: 48 picks monotonized, 0 of which remain ranked.
formulas.constants: none.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Picks without a rank are skipped (:5364-5367) so the pass never reassigns across the OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT boundary.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_pick_refinement.py.
formulas.mathIssues: Moves rank/value/tier and three spread diagnostics onto a different pick name but leaves confidenceBucket, confidenceLabel, sourceRanks, sourceRankMeta, sourceSpread, hillValueSpread, anomalyFlags, hasSourceDisagreement, marketGap* and canonicalSiteValues behind. Latent only — all 48 monotonized picks are current-year slot picks whose ranks compact_ranks_and_tiers subsequently clears, so no inconsistent row reaches the ranked board today.

formulas.name: Identity confidence
formulas.expression:
if playerId.strip(): return 1.00, "canonical_id"
pos_matches = (assetClass=="offense" and has_off_val and not has_idp_val)
           or (assetClass=="idp"     and has_idp_val and not has_off_val)
           or (assetClass=="pick")
if pos and pos_matches:                    return 0.95, "position_source_aligned"
if pos and (has_off_val or has_idp_val):   return 0.85, "partial_evidence"
return 0.70, "name_only"
formulas.inputs: playerId presence, position string, assetClass, positive values under _OFFENSE_SIGNAL_KEYS / _IDP_SIGNAL_KEYS.
formulas.constants: 1.00 / 0.95 / 0.85 / 0.70 — hand-picked, no calibration.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Nothing known -> 0.70, the floor. There is no value below 0.70 and no 'unknown', so a row with no id, no position and no source values still reads 70% confident.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_identity_validation.py covers the quarantine flags; no test pins the numeric scores against observed join accuracy.
formulas.mathIssues: The id branch returns 1.00 unconditionally and never checks that the id is correct — precisely what the collision checks exist to doubt. A row flagged name_collision_cross_universe still scores 1.00 if it has an id.

formulas.name: Quarantine and confidence degradation
formulas.inputs: anomalyFlags accumulated by six checks (position-aware duplicate identity, cross-universe collision, position/source contradiction, unsupported position, no valid source values, identity confidence).
formulas.outputRange: quarantined boolean + possible downgrade. Live: 1 quarantined of 1092; crossUniverseCollisionCount 0, duplicateCanonicalIdentityCount 0, nearNameMismatchCount 0.
formulas.constants: OFFENSE_TO_IDP_VALIDATION_EXCEPTIONS = {"Josh Johnson", "Elijah Mitchell"}; _NEAR_NAME_VALUE_RATIO_THRESHOLD 3.0 (dead).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no_valid_source_values fires only when a row has NO positive source value AND a positive rankDerivedValue — a row with neither value nor rank raises nothing and is not quarantined.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_identity_validation.py pins clean/OL/degradation cases; nothing pins the exception-list semantics.
formulas.mathIssues: name_collision_cross_universe is deliberately not a quarantine flag, but the Check 1 comment (:2941-2944) claims the exception list CAUSES quarantine when it in fact suppresses the downstream contradiction flag (:2996-2999, :3005-3008). Check 3's near-name rule is removed and its constant is orphaned.

formulas.name: marketConfidence / marketDispersionCV (scraper pass-through)
formulas.expression:
cv         = stdev(norm_vals)/mean(norm_vals)
site_score = clamp(site_count / 8.0, 0.20, 1.00)
cv_score   = clamp(1 - min(cv, 0.35)/0.35, 0.20, 1.00)
conf       = clamp(0.65*site_score + 0.35*cv_score, 0.20, 1.00)
formulas.inputs: z-normalized per-site values and the site count from the LEGACY scraper composite path — not the canonical blend's source set.
formulas.outputRange: Nominally 0.20-1.00. Live over 839 rows: min 0.3447, p10 0.480, median 0.4897, p90 0.5637, max 0.5938, with 375 rows at exactly 0.48. 253 rows carry no value.
formulas.constants: the /8.0 divisor (from a larger dash-key era), the 0.35 CV cap and the 0.65/0.35 weights — all hand-picked.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Absent rather than zero on the frontend row — frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1013-1025: 'Missing confidence stays NULL, never 0 (audit N2, 2026-07-29)', because coercing to 0 previously fired a MONITOR rule on rows that merely lacked the field.
formulas.validated: none. The one rule consuming it, monitor.low_conf_unstable (< 0.35), was retired 2026-07-30 for exactly this reason — frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:121-127.
formulas.mathIssues: Structurally capped near 0.59, so a 0-1-labelled measure occupies about a third of its range and is near-constant. frontend/components/ds/Badge.jsx:76-83 buckets at 0.67/0.34 — thresholds this field can never cross upward, so everything would read 'medium'. It is in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS despite being a pass-through no override can change.

formulas.name: Value confidence intervals (p10/p50/p90 source-consensus bands) — DEAD
formulas.inputs: sourceRanks and rankDerivedValue per row; per-source weights default 1.0.
formulas.outputRange: Three values on 0-9999 plus a method string.
formulas.constants: the 10/50/90 percentiles.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Explicit insufficient_sources method rather than a fabricated band. The header (:8-18) is unusually honest: 'this is **not** a predictive confidence interval ... UI must label it source consensus range'.
formulas.validated: tests/canonical/test_confidence_intervals.py and test_rank_history_band.py exercise the math, but the code has no production caller.
formulas.mathIssues: None reachable. src/api/feature_flags.py:55-63 and :356-362 record that stamp_bands_on_players has no caller, rank_history_band has no caller, ValueBandBadge is mounted on no page, and there is no is_enabled('value_confidence_intervals') call anywhere — dead at all three layers.

formulas.name: Positional tiering (Cohen's-d) — DEAD, and a second tier implementation
formulas.expression: per-position walk down rankDerivedValue; split when the standardized gap (Cohen's d against pooled SD) exceeds a per-position threshold; pooled SD == 0 -> single tier
formulas.inputs: rows of {name, pos, rankDerivedValue}; per-position thresholds from config.
formulas.constants: per-position thresholds loaded from config with defaults, fitted by a grid search in scripts/refit_tier_thresholds.py — the only fitted tier constants in the repo.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Uniform values -> everyone in tier 1 rather than everyone in their own tier (pinned by test_uniform_values_all_one_tier).
formulas.validated: tests/scoring/test_tiering.py — 14 tests covering the walk, the zero-SD fallback, the grid-search fitter and drift detection. The best-tested tiering code in the repo, and the one that is not wired.
formulas.mathIssues: None reachable. feature_flags.py:64-72 records that TierDivider renders only on /draft off a locally computed p.tier and the backend never stamps tierId. The tier IDs users see come from the untested gap detector instead.

findings.title: marketGapDirection ("Buy"/"Sell" on /edge) averages ordinal ranks across source pools of different depth — 47% of offense rows and 97% of pick rows flip sign under pool normalization
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:2789-2796 `retail_mean = sum(retail_ranks)/len(retail_ranks)`, `consensus_mean = sum(consensus_ranks)/len(consensus_ranks)`, `diff = consensus_mean - retail_mean`. Called at :7721 with `effective_source_ranks` — raw ordinals, no pool normalization. The same file's `_percentile_rank_spread` docstring (:3944-3952) says this is invalid: "an effective spread of 100 doesn't mean the sources disagree, it means one is on a 1-185 scale and the other is on a 1-600 scale." Observed max ranks per source on the live board: dlfSf 278 ... ktcSfTep 498 ... idpTradeCalc 902. Dalton Kincaid: retail 99, raw consensus mean 108.38 -> +9.38 'retail_premium'; rescaled to a common 500-row pool, consensus 132.87 vs retail 99.40 -> +33.47. Across 422 rows carrying a gap, 215 (50.9%) change sign under normalization: offense 183/389 (47.0%), picks 32/33 (97.0%). Rendered as an action word at frontend/app/edge/edge-columns.jsx:114-115.
findings.userImpact: The /edge Buy/Sell column is close to a coin flip on direction. A user acting on 'Buy' is as likely to be buying a player the expert pool rates BELOW retail. Pick rows are almost uniformly mislabeled.
findings.recommendedFix: Normalize each rank by `source_pool_sizes[key]` before averaging — the pool sizes are already computed at :6671 and already passed to `_percentile_rank_spread`. Thread them into `_compute_market_gap` and express magnitude in percentile points. Until then suppress the column for picks.

findings.title: Gap-based tier detection produces 127 tiers on a 740-row board; the median boundary is an 8-point value drop (0.45%) — exactly the case the docstring says must not be a boundary
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:2094-2098: "a 400-point drop from rank 12->13 is a boundary; a 3-point drop from 312->313 is not." `_compute_value_based_tier_ids` (:1992-2022) feeds the whole board to `detect_tiers`, which normalizes each gap by a rolling median (`score = g / rm`, player_valuation.py:239) and breaks at `score >= 2.0` (:49) with `min_tier_size 3` (:50). Scale-free, so tiers fire at the same rate at every depth. Live: 127 tiers, size min 3 / median 5 / mean 5.83 / max 15. Boundary drops: min 0.07%, median 0.45%, p90 1.95%, max 4.18%; 96 of 126 under 1%; 50 at <=5 points. Worked example at the named rank: break after 311 (Ben Sinnott 1957 -> Deshaun Watson 1945), gap 12, local gaps [5,3,2,1,1,4,0,12,6,5,3,8,12,2,2], rolling median 3, score 4.00.
findings.userImpact: Tier badges and separator rows on /rankings (page.jsx:904, :1943) partition the board every ~6 players on differences well under 1% of value. A user reading a tier break as a value cliff is reading noise.
findings.recommendedFix: Add an absolute or relative floor — require the raw gap to also exceed some fraction of the local value level (e.g. 3-5%) before a rolling-median score can fire — or cap tier count and re-fit TIER_GAP_THRESHOLD against a stated target tier size. Neither constant is calibrated today.
findings.affectedSystems: detect_tiers; _compute_value_based_tier_ids / compact_ranks_and_tiers; /rankings tier column and separators; league-adjusted overlay (same function)

findings.title: The corridor clamp's per-bucket P90 band is inert: the hardcoded 0.15 cap wins on 128 of 128 clamped rows, so 43.5% of ranked IDP values are pinned to ±15% of IDPTradeCalc
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:4573-4576 claims "Band width is empirical — P90 of |final - market| / market computed within each confidence bucket on THIS board build." At :4630-4634 `if max_band is not None and band > max_band: band = max_band` with 0.15 for idp (:4418-4420). Live: 128 clamped rows, `Counter(bandPct) == {0.15: 128}`, `cappedByMaxBand True` on every one. Measured drift P90 per bucket: high 0.5423 (n=29), medium 0.4805 (n=91), low 0.5119 (n=174), overall 0.5096 — all 3.2-3.6x the cap. 128 of 294 ranked IDP rows (43.5%) clamped. Example: Abdul Carter DL 3532 -> 4598 against anchor 5409.
findings.userImpact: For nearly half the ranked IDP board the four-source blend cannot move a player more than 15% from IDPTradeCalc — the published value is IDPTC with a haircut, not a blend. confidenceBucket has zero influence on the clamp despite being presented as the governing input; median drift is actually HIGHER for 'high' (0.221) than 'low' (0.122).
findings.recommendedFix: Either drop the dead per-bucket P90 machinery and document the clamp honestly as '±15% of IDPTradeCalc', or raise/remove the cap so the empirical band binds. Also refresh the rationale at :4586-4588, which still cites the retired IDP calibration post-pass (`_apply_idp_calibration_post_pass` and `config/idp_calibration.json` are both absent from the tree; CLAUDE.md already flags this).
findings.affectedSystems: _apply_market_corridor_clamp; every IDP rankDerivedValue; trade suggestions, finder, angles, waivers, terminal, BDVM market layer

findings.title: confidenceBucket can be RAISED by missing data: a row covered by 2 of 16 eligible sources is labeled "High — multi-source, tight agreement"
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:1893-1903 decides on `source_count >= 2` plus `percentile_spread <= 0.08`. `_percentile_rank_spread` (:3938-3985) is computed only over sources that ranked the player, so uncovered sources drop out of the statistic entirely. `softFallbackCount` (:7345) is never an input. Live: CJ Donaldson RB — sourceCount 2, softFallbackCount 14, sourceAudit.reason 'partial_coverage', 8 of 9 expected offense sources unmatched, sourceRanks {fantasyProsSf 433, draftSharks 541}, sourceRankPercentileSpread 0.0247 -> 'high' / 'High — multi-source, tight agreement'. Harrison Wallace WR and Noah Whittington RB are identical in shape. 24 of the 108 'high' rows have sourceCount <= 3 AND softFallbackCount >= 5.
findings.userImpact: The confidence badge on /rankings and /edge, and the `confidenceBucket === 'high'` filters at edge/page.jsx:116 and :227, promote thinly-covered deep-board rows into the top-trust bucket. Missing evidence reads as agreement.
findings.recommendedFix: Make coverage an explicit input: degrade the bucket when `sourceCount / (sourceCount + softFallbackCount)` is low, or cap at 'medium' when softFallbackCount exceeds sourceCount. Both fields are already on the row.
findings.affectedSystems: _compute_confidence_bucket; /rankings confidence column, filter and sort; /edge high-confidence sections; corridor clamp bucket lookup

findings.title: confidenceBucket measures percentile-rank agreement, not agreement about the value it labels — 20 of 107 'high' rows have value dispersion above 30% of the published value
findings.evidence: The input is `_percentile_rank_spread` (:3938), computed on raw ordinals over pool size. The number the badge sits beside is `rankDerivedValue`, blended from `sourceRankMeta[k].valueContribution`. Different spaces — and the row already carries the value-space statistic, `hillValueSpread` (:7484), which is not consulted. CJ Donaldson: pctSpread 0.0247 -> 'high', contributions 919 vs 1698 (85% apart), hillValueSpread 550.84 against a value of 1308. Board-wide relative dispersion (hillValueSpread / rankDerivedValue): medians separate correctly (high 0.064, medium 0.129, low 0.195) but the p90 is effectively identical across all three (0.421 / 0.423 / 0.450). 20 of 107 'high' rows exceed 0.30 (e.g. Jadon Canady DB, value 871, stdev 665.39, pctSpread 0.0072).
findings.userImpact: 'High — multi-source, tight agreement' is true of the ranks and false of the value on a meaningful minority of rows. A user sizing a trade off a 'high' badge can be looking at a value the contributing sources disagree about by 85%.
findings.recommendedFix: Blend `hillValueSpread / rankDerivedValue` into the bucket alongside percentile spread, or rename the label to what it measures ('tight rank agreement') and surface value dispersion separately.

findings.title: `_stamp_rank_changes` writes the shared canonical rank snapshot on any build without source overrides — including TEP-only override requests and delta builds, contradicting its own docstring
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:7903-7906 `_stamp_rank_changes(tiered_rows, write_snapshot=not source_overrides)`. The docstring at :4703-4706 claims 'write_snapshot=False is used on override / delta-payload builds', but `_for_delta` is never consulted here (it exists at :8435 and is checked only at :8639, :8714, :8914). `normalize_source_overrides` returns {} for a TEP-only body (reserved-key skip :2374-2378) and for the explicit enabled_sources shape with everything enabled (:2366). server.py:3786/:3789 then pass `overrides if overrides else None`, so those requests reach write_snapshot=True. frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:2040-2043 posts `body.tep_multiplier` whenever `tepMultiplierIsCustomized` is true, which holds for any finite number.
findings.userImpact: One user moving the TE-premium slider on /settings overwrites data/snapshots/ranks_last.json with their private board's ranks. Every other user's rankChange arrows — labelled 'since the previous scrape' at rankings/page.jsx:892 — are then diffed against that user's board until the next scrape, with no error anywhere.
findings.recommendedFix: Gate on the full override surface: `write_snapshot = not source_overrides and not _for_delta and tep_multiplier is None and tep_native_multiplier is None`. Better, move the write out of build_api_data_contract and let only the fresh-scrape promotion call it — server.py:1867 already has the is_fresh_scrape gate.
findings.affectedSystems: _stamp_rank_changes; data/snapshots/ranks_last.json; rankChange on every /rankings row; board-sections.jsx:70-74

findings.title: `rankChange` is override-sensitive but absent from `_DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS`, so a user with custom source weights sees the default board's movement arrows beside override ranks
findings.evidence: `_DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS` (:8948-8996) includes canonicalConsensusRank but not rankChange, which is `previous_rank - canonicalConsensusRank` (:4734-4736) and therefore moves whenever the rank does. Reproduced: seeding ranks_last.json from the default board and rebuilding with {'ktcSfTep': include False, 'dlfSf': include False} yields 571 rows with non-zero rankChange (Eric Rivers +370, Emmanuel Henderson +310). On the delta path mergeRankingsDelta keeps the base contract's stale value; on the view=full path the override-derived value IS delivered and the UI renders it as 'moved up 370 since the previous scrape' (rankings/page.jsx:892).
findings.userImpact: Movement arrows either describe a board the user is not looking at, or attribute the user's own source toggle to market movement. Both are wrong claims presented as market data.
findings.recommendedFix: Add rankChange to _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS, and null it (or stamp a rankChangeBasis marker) on any build with source_overrides/tep_multiplier set, since no snapshot of that board exists to diff against.
findings.affectedSystems: build_rankings_delta_payload; frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js::mergeRankingsDelta; /rankings movement column and movers rail

findings.title: `sourceAudit` changes on 510 rows under a source override but is not in the delta — the Source Audit panel shows the default board's coverage beside override-adjusted values
findings.evidence: sourceAudit is stamped at :7625-7635 from override-filtered source_ranks and is absent from _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS. Empirical diff of a default build vs {'ktcSfTep': off, 'dlfSf': off}: fields that change but are not in the delta list — sourceAudit 510 rows, pickRookieAnchor 56, twoWayPlayerBoost 1, singleSourceValuePenaltyApplied 1. Compounding it, `_expected_sources_for_position` (:3861-3936) iterates _RANKING_SOURCES unconditionally and never consults source_overrides, so expectedSources/unmatchedSources count user-disabled sources as coverage failures and `isSingleSource = len(source_ranks)==1 and len(expected_keys)>1` (:7635) fires on a deliberate configuration. isSingleSource IS in the delta, so the boolean and the block that explains it disagree.
findings.userImpact: With custom weights active the audit popover attributes coverage to sources the user turned off and reports 'matching_failure_other_sources_eligible' for a deliberate choice; the 1-src warning badge fires on rows that are single-source by design.
findings.recommendedFix: Add sourceAudit and singleSourceValuePenaltyApplied to _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS and pass the active-source set into _expected_sources_for_position.

findings.title: /api/movers emits absolute per-source ranks under a field the docstring calls a per-source delta, and the "window" is not honored per player
findings.evidence: server.py:3466-3479 copies `row['sourceOriginalRanks']` values verbatim (`per_source_delta[str(src_key)] = int(src_rank)`) — no subtraction — and emits it at :3492 as `"currentSourceRanks"`. The docstring documents `"perSourceDelta"` (:3362) and describes 'a per-source rank delta breakdown so the user can see which sources drove the move' (:3369-3371). Separately :3390 `load_history(days=window+1)` returns the last window+1 SNAPSHOTS (rank_history.py:352) and :3444 takes `anchor = series[0]`, the first snapshot in which THAT player appears — so horizons vary per player while the response stamps a single `"window": 14`.
findings.userImpact: The per-source breakdown answers a different question than the label claims. Risers/fallers mix comparison horizons, so a player who merely appeared on the board recently competes with a genuine 14-day mover.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute a real delta (source_value_history.jsonl already carries per-source ranks) or rename the field and fix the docstring. For the window, select the anchor by date proximity to `latest_date - window`, drop players whose series does not span it, or stamp the per-entry observed span.

findings.title: players/compare renders every market gap in red — it tests for a direction value the backend never emits
findings.evidence: `_compute_market_gap` returns only 'retail_premium', 'consensus_premium' or 'none' (src/api/data_contract.py:2790-2796). frontend/app/players/compare/page.jsx:172: `color: row.marketGapDirection === "buy" ? "var(--green)" : "var(--red)"`. 'buy' is unreachable, so the branch is always false and the value always renders red, printed uppercase as RETAIL_PREMIUM / CONSENSUS_PREMIUM (:173).
findings.userImpact: A consensus premium (buy-low) is colored identically to a retail premium (sell-high). The color — the fastest-read part of the row — carries no information and points the wrong way half the time.
findings.recommendedFix: Test `=== "consensus_premium"` for green and map the enum to the same Buy/Sell words /edge already uses (edge-columns.jsx:114-115).

findings.title: Unresolvable assets are silently valued at zero in public trade grading, and the grade thresholds are percentages of an alpha-exponentiated scale, not of value
findings.evidence: src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:172 `return by_name.get(name.lower(), 0.0)` and :162 `return 0.0` when pick probes miss; no unresolved list is returned. src/public_league/activity.py:117 floors each asset at 1 before `pow(max(val,1.0), 1.65)` (:47), so an unpriced asset contributes 1 against a real player's ~2,000,000. The bridge drops every pickGenericSuppressed row (:126) and every row without a positive values bundle; 352 of 1092 live rows are unranked. Threshold semantics: `pct = ((max_w - min_w)/max_w)*100` on exponentiated totals — 5000 vs 4000 (a 20% value gap) gives 1 - 0.8^1.65 = 31.0% -> 'Big win' (>= 25); the 3% 'Fair' band corresponds to a ~1.8% raw gap.
findings.userImpact: A public /league trade where one side received an unpriced player is graded as receiving nothing — an F/'Fleeced' badge on a possibly fair trade. Grades are also harsher than the labeled percentages imply, and nothing on the payload distinguishes a fully-priced grade from a partial one.
findings.recommendedFix: Return an `unresolved` list per side (src/api/bdvm_api.py's trade-eval already does exactly this) and suppress the grade block when any side has unresolved assets. Separately, compute pct on pre-alpha values or rename the constants to match the scale they apply to.

findings.title: injury_impact's docstring documents a 60% cap and an injury-type rulebook; the code caps at 5% and never inspects injury type — and on today's date every discount is zero
findings.evidence: src/api/injury_impact.py:64 'Values are capped at 60% total discount' and :187 `"appliedDiscountPct": float (0-60)`, against `_MAX_DISCOUNT_PCT: float = 5.0` at :90. The header example '-15% (ACL, RB, >=25)' (:17-18) is unreachable twice: 15% exceeds the cap, and the code reads only `item['severity']` (:243-245) — no injury-type parsing exists, so 'Achilles, ACL, spinal' (:49) describes what the upstream news service already classified. Worked at now = 2026-10-15: RB/33/alert/1h -> 4.0 x 1.20 x 1.40 x 0.9986 = 6.71 capped to 5.0%; RB/27/alert 4.79%; QB/24/alert 2.24%; WR watch 2.0%; WR info 0.5%; RB alert at 360h -> decay 0.5 -> 2.4%. `_OFFSEASON_MONTHS = {2..8}` (:100) means at 2026-08-04 a torn ACL returns appliedDiscountPct 0.0 with offseasonSuppressed True.
findings.userImpact: Anyone reading the module or the `(0-60)` return contract sizes the feature an order of magnitude wrong. The InjuryChip is a no-op for seven months a year, which is by design but invisible unless the caller reads offseasonSuppressed.
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite the header to state the 5% cap, drop the injury-type language or implement it, and fix the (0-60) range. The behavior is already pinned by tests/api/test_injury_impact.py — only the prose is wrong.

findings.title: `_compute_confidence_bucket`'s unit tests exercise only the legacy absolute-ordinal branch that production never takes
findings.evidence: Every case in tests/api/test_trust_confidence.py::TestConfidenceBucket calls `_compute_confidence_bucket(2, 20.0)` / (2,30.0) / (2,50.0) / (2,80.0) / (2,100.0) / (1,None) / (0,None) — all with percentile_spread omitted, i.e. the `elif source_rank_spread is not None` branch guarded by _CONFIDENCE_SPREAD_HIGH/MEDIUM (30/80) at :1900-1905. The live call site at :7712-7716 always passes percentile_spread, so production always takes the 0.08/0.20 branch at :1895-1899. Repo-wide grep for percentile_spread in tests/ returns only tests/api/test_disagreement_trimming.py:89-97, which tests _compute_anomaly_flags.
findings.userImpact: The 0.08 / 0.20 thresholds that decide every confidence badge on the live board are unpinned — changing either would fail no test.
findings.recommendedFix: Add cases passing percentile_spread at and around 0.08 and 0.20, including the coverage-perverse case (source_count 2, percentile_spread 0.02), so the intended behavior is stated rather than inherited.

findings.title: `assert_ranking_coherence` is documented as a build-pipeline safety rail but no build calls it, and run on playersArray as stored it returns 1125 errors
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:9286-9288: 'This function is the hard safety rail: the build pipeline and regression tests should call it and fail on any error.' Callers: only src/league_intel/overlay.py:119 (which passes the rank-ordered return of compact_ranks_and_tiers) and two test files. `validate_api_data_contract` (:9348) never invokes it. Run on the live contract's playersArray in stored order: 1125 errors, e.g. '#98 2027 Late 1st: rank not strictly increasing (prev #441 2027 Early 4th)'. Sorting by canonicalConsensusRank first: 0 errors — which is what both tests do (test_ranking_coherence.py:71-73).
findings.userImpact: The canonical board is never coherence-checked at build time; only the optional overlay path is. A regression inverting rank vs value on the market board would ship — validate_api_data_contract reported ok=True, status=healthy, errors=0 on this build.
findings.recommendedFix: Call it from build_api_data_contract on the rank-ordered tiered_rows that compact_ranks_and_tiers already returns (:7892) and surface the result in contractHealth. Fix the docstring to state the rank-ordered precondition.

findings.title: `coverageAudit` validates against `ktc`, a source that no longer votes, with a min-sources threshold of 1 — it passes 300/300 and 250/250 by construction
findings.evidence: Live coverageAudit: `{'thresholds': {'topOffenseN': 300, 'topIdpN': 250, 'offenseMinSources': 1, 'idpMinSources': 1}, 'expectedSites': {'offense': ['ktc'], 'idp': ['idpTradeCalc']}, 'offense': {'evaluated': 300, 'passPlayers': 300, 'deficitPlayers': 0}}`. `ktc` is absent from _RANKING_SOURCES (registry: ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc, dlfSf, dlfRookieSf, dlfIdp, dlfRookieIdp, idpShow, dynastyNerdsSfTep, fantasyCalc, otcffbSf, fantasyNavigatorSf, pfkDynasty, dynastyDaddySf, fantasyProsSf, fantasyProsIdp, fantasyProsFitzmaurice, flockFantasySf, flockFantasySfRookies, yahooBoone, draftSharks, draftSharksIdp); data_contract.py:7803-7806 records standard ktc was removed from the blend 2026-04-28. Produced by the scraper and passed through verbatim.
findings.userImpact: The coverage guard cannot detect a real coverage collapse: at 1 required source out of 20 live, it would keep reporting 0 deficits until the board lost 19 of them.
findings.recommendedFix: Point expectedSites at the live registry via get_ranking_source_keys() and raise the threshold to something that can fail, or delete the block — no frontend surface reads it.

findings.title: `poolAudit` ships on the ~4MB contract with no consumer anywhere in the stack
findings.evidence: Produced at Dynasty Scraper.py:7309 and passed through untouched — grep in src/api/data_contract.py finds only a docstring mention (:9065) plus the prune entries at compact_view.py:43 and in the delta. Repo-wide grep for poolAudit under frontend/ returns zero hits outside exports/latest/dynasty_data.js. The live block carries idp_trade_calc_unmatched_names with 163 entries plus three 20-name samples.
findings.userImpact: Bytes on every full-view /api/data response for data nothing reads, and — more importantly — 163 unmatched IDPTC names are a real identity-join signal that no surface, alert or dashboard consumes.
findings.recommendedFix: Wire the unmatched counts into contractHealth or the existing src/api/source_health_alerts.py, or move the block behind a debug view alongside the compact-view prune.

findings.title: `marketConfidence` is a 0-1-shaped field structurally confined to 0.34-0.59, with 375 of 839 rows at one value, and is listed in the delta as if overrides could move it
findings.evidence: Dynasty Scraper.py:6029-6034: `site_score = clamp(site_count/8.0, 0.20, 1.00)`, `cv_score = clamp(1 - min(cv,0.35)/0.35, 0.20, 1.00)`, `conf = clamp(0.65*site_score + 0.35*cv_score, 0.20, 1.00)`. The /8.0 divisor dates from a ~10-dash-key era. Live over 839 rows: min 0.3447, p10 0.480, median 0.4897, p90 0.5637, max 0.5938; 375 rows at exactly 0.48; 253 rows have none. frontend/lib/signal-engine.js:121-127 records that its one consumer (monitor.low_conf_unstable, `< 0.35`) was retired 2026-07-30 for exactly this reason. It is nonetheless in _DELTA_PLAYER_FIELDS (:8977) though it is a scraper pass-through, and frontend/components/ds/Badge.jsx:76-83 buckets confidence at 0.67/0.34 — thresholds this field can never cross upward.
findings.userImpact: Any surface rendering row.confidence shows a number that looks like a probability but occupies a third of its nominal range and is near-constant. Currently consumed only as an unused row field, so the impact is latent.
findings.recommendedFix: Recalibrate the /8.0 divisor against the live source count and re-derive the Badge thresholds, or drop the field from the contract and the delta list. Do not leave a 0-1-labelled measure that cannot reach either end.

findings.title: `identityConfidence` is a four-valued indicator of "does this row have a Sleeper ID" presented as a 0-1 confidence score
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:2814-2852: `if has_id: return 1.00, "canonical_id"` — unconditional whenever playerId is non-empty, with no check that the ID resolves to the right person; then 0.95 / 0.85 / 0.70 from position-vs-source agreement. Live: 937 rows at 1.00, 144 at 0.95 (picks, via the `asset_class == "pick"` short-circuit at :2842), 11 at 0.70. The 0.85 branch never fires. Values are hand-picked; nothing calibrates them against observed mis-joins.
findings.userImpact: The score cannot distinguish a correct Sleeper join from an incorrect one — the exact failure the collision checks exist to catch — yet reads as 100% certainty. A row flagged name_collision_cross_universe still scores 1.00 if it has an ID.
findings.recommendedFix: Express it as the categorical it is (identityMethod already does) and drop the numeric, or make the ID branch conditional on the row not carrying a collision/contradiction flag.

findings.title: The cross-universe collision comment inverts what the exception list does, and the retired near-name rule left a dead constant
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:2941-2944: 'We surface them for visibility but only quarantine when the collision is a *known* entity confusion (see OFFENSE_TO_IDP_VALIDATION_EXCEPTIONS).' In fact name_collision_cross_universe is not in _QUARANTINE_FLAGS (:262-267) so it never quarantines, and `is_known_collision` is used only to `pass` — to SUPPRESS the position_source_contradiction flag (:2996-2999, :3005-3008). Separately `_NEAR_NAME_VALUE_RATIO_THRESHOLD = 3.0` at :246 is dead: Check 3 was removed (:3011-3016), near_name_pairs is permanently [] and nearNameMismatchCount is hardcoded 0 (:3055-3057).
findings.userImpact: A reader auditing why a collision did or did not quarantine gets the inverted rule. Live impact nil — the board has 0 cross-universe collisions and 1 quarantined row (unsupported_position).
findings.recommendedFix: Reword the Check 1 comment to say the exception list suppresses the downstream contradiction flag, and delete _NEAR_NAME_VALUE_RATIO_THRESHOLD.

findings.title: compact_view.py's docstring lists 6 pruned player fields; the code prunes 18, including the entire post-blend audit block
findings.evidence: src/api/compact_view.py:11-13 names droppedSources, effectiveSourceRanks, sourceOriginalRanks, anomalyFlags, confidenceLabel, pickDetails. `_PRUNED_PLAYER_FIELDS` (:52-71) additionally drops marketCorridorClamp, twoWayPlayerBoost, subgroupBlendValue, subgroupDelta, alphaShrinkage, softFallbackCount, hillValueSpread, marketDispersionCV, blendedSourceRank, madPenaltyApplied, anchorValue. Mobile and slow-network clients take this view (frontend/lib/device-profile.js:103-107).
findings.userImpact: On mobile the confidence badge renders a bucket with no confidenceLabel to explain it, quarantine reasons (anomalyFlags) are invisible while the quarantined boolean survives, and the value-chain transparency panel has no inputs — none of which the docstring warns about.
findings.recommendedFix: Regenerate the docstring list from _PRUNED_PLAYER_FIELDS, and reconsider keeping confidenceLabel — a short string that is the only thing making the badge interpretable.

findings.title: The contract advertises a frontend value-recompute fallback that was removed
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:8399-8401 stamps `valueAuthority.mode = "backend_authoritative_with_explicit_frontend_fallback"` and `fallbackPolicy = "frontend_recompute_only_when_backend_value_fields_missing"` on every full-view payload. frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:931-939 documents the opposite — the ~280-line computeUnifiedRanks fallback 'was removed' and buildRows now 'fails fast' to an empty array. CLAUDE.md's 'Fail-fast on missing stamps' section agrees with the frontend.
findings.userImpact: A consumer reading the contract's self-description expects graceful client degradation when stamps are missing. It does not degrade — it renders a 'no players' banner.
findings.recommendedFix: Change the two strings to describe fail-fast (mode 'backend_authoritative', fallbackPolicy 'fail_fast_no_client_recompute').

findings.title: `_tier_id_from_rank` boundaries and `OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT` are unsourced magic numbers, and the rank limit no longer describes the delivered board
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:2024-2054: boundaries 12/36/72/120/200/350/500/650/800 justified solely as mirroring frontend rankBasedTierId — a hardcode mirroring a hardcode. `OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT = 800` (:62) sits under a comment block (:45-60) describing a two-source era ('The two active sources (KTC and IDPTradeCalc)... every player has exactly one source') that 21 registered sources invalidated. Live: Phase 4 stamps 800, compaction clears 60, so the published board is 740 — 352 of 1092 rows unranked (offense 132, pick 116, idp 104), 72 of which retain a rankDerivedValue and 251 a _blendedValueUncapped (max 1110 for a non-pick, against a minimum ranked value of 757).
findings.userImpact: _tier_id_from_rank survives only as the frontend fallback for unranked rows, where it labels deliberately-unranked players 'Tier 10'. And roughly two dozen unranked non-pick rows carry blended values above the board's minimum ranked value, so the 800 cut is not a clean value threshold.
findings.recommendedFix: Refresh the OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT comment to the current source set and state whether the cut is a rank cap or a value floor. If the tier ladder is only a fallback, delete it and render 'Unranked'.

findings.title: `_reassign_pick_slot_order` permutes rank, value, tier and three spread diagnostics between picks but leaves confidence, source ranks, flags and site values behind
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:5378-5418 moves canonicalConsensusRank, rankDerivedValue, canonicalTierId, blendedSourceRank, sourceRankSpread and sourceRankPercentileSpread onto a different pick name. Not moved: confidenceBucket, confidenceLabel, sourceRanks, sourceRankMeta, sourceSpread, hillValueSpread, anomalyFlags, hasSourceDisagreement, marketGapDirection/Magnitude, canonicalSiteValues. Verified not to bite today — all 48 monotonized picks are current-year slot picks whose ranks compact_ranks_and_tiers then clears (monotonized AND ranked: 0). The pass buckets by year, not by current year, so a future-year slot-pick source would expose it.
findings.userImpact: None today. Latent: if any source publishes future-year slot picks, those rows would carry a confidence block and per-source ranks describing a different pick than their value.
findings.recommendedFix: Move the full diagnostic set with the tuple, or move none of it and recompute the spreads after the permutation. Add a regression that ranks a future-year slot pick.

findings.title: `src/api/auction_power.py` is documented as the source of truth but has no non-test caller; the live numbers come from a JS reimplementation pinned only at the constant level
findings.evidence: Grep for effective_auction_power outside its module returns only tests/api/test_auction_power.py and test_auction_power_parity.py. The live callers are frontend/lib/auction-power.js::effectiveAuctionPower, imported by app/league/sections/draft-capital.jsx:12, _trade-simulator.jsx:12 and lib/trade-logic.js:13. The parity test states its own limit at :21-27 ('WHY CONSTANTS AND NOT OUTPUTS ... this pins the three knobs exactly') — it regex-scrapes AP_PREMIUM_GAIN / AP_CURVATURE / AP_LEAPFROG_WEIGHT and never compares outputs. The constants (0.35 / 1.25 / 0.15) are labelled 'Conservative defaults' at :70 with no fit, and the module's own Phase 2 note (:37-50) concedes the heuristic is untested against real drafts.
findings.userImpact: A structural change on either side — a different spread estimator, changed renormalization, changed rounding — passes every test. The lens redistributes up to ±35% of a team's draft capital in the UI on constants nobody fit.
findings.recommendedFix: Run the JS through node in the parity test and compare outputs on fixed inputs, or delete the Python module and move the invariant tests to the JS side so there is one implementation. Label the effective column as a heuristic until the Phase 2 backtest exists.
findings.affectedSystems: src/api/auction_power.py; frontend/lib/auction-power.js; /league draft-capital and trade simulator

findings.title: FAAB tier breakpoints are described as "calibrated" but are hand-picked, and the zero-bid comment contradicts the caller
findings.evidence: src/api/faab_analytics.py:43-50: '# Calibrated for a 100-budget league' above `_TIER_BREAKPOINTS_PCT = (("tier1",0.20),("tier2",0.10),("tier3",0.03),("tier4",0.0))` — round percentages with no fitting procedure in the tree. `_tier_for_bid`'s docstring (:88-90) says it 'Floors at tier4 so zero-bid FA pickups still appear in the bid history', but the only caller gates on `if bid > 0` before calling it (:213-215). `_stats_block` (:117-128) returns {avg 0.0, min 0, max 0, count 0} for an empty list and leagueAvg/Median default to 0.0 (:283-287), so 'no data' and 'average bid of $0' are the same value.
findings.userImpact: Low today — both consumers guard correctly (faab_recommender.py:186-189 requires count >= 3, :217-222 a positive median plus a minimum bid count; ManualAddDrop.jsx:113-119 tests avg > 0). The risk is a future consumer reading avg without checking count.
findings.recommendedFix: Return None rather than 0.0 for empty stats blocks, fix the zero-bid comment, and either document the breakpoints as chosen conventions or fit them to the league's own bid distribution.

findings.title: The depth-aware disagreement allowance is a flat constant for 75% of the board, suppressing the flag on 370 rows whose spread exceeds the base threshold
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:164-177 returns `min(max(consensus_percentile,0), 0.25)` with the cap at :161. With 740 ranked rows the allowance saturates at rank 185, so 555 rows (75.0%) share one constant threshold of 0.35 rather than a depth-varying one. Of those, 497 exceed the 0.10 base threshold but only 127 carry hasSourceDisagreement. Board totals: 135 disagreement, 52 suspicious; top-200: 10 and 6, versus the constant's own docstring target of 'top-200 disagreement drops 143 -> ~40 and suspicious_disagreement 82 -> ~15' (:147-149).
findings.userImpact: The caution flag is now far below the level the tuning note aimed at in the top 200 (10 vs ~40) and is a fixed-threshold flag everywhere else. Rows at 0.30 percentile spread on the deep board show no caution at all.
findings.recommendedFix: Re-measure the top-200 flag rate against the stated ~40 target and either retune _DISAGREEMENT_BASE_THRESHOLD or update the note; consider tracking the observed median spread by depth decile instead of capping at a constant.

findings.title: Building the contract writes to disk as a side effect, so a read-shaped operation destroys the only record of the previous board's ranks
findings.evidence: build_api_data_contract -> `_stamp_rank_changes(..., write_snapshot=True)` (src/api/data_contract.py:7903) -> `snap_path.write_text(...)` (:4744), where snap_path is data/snapshots/ranks_last.json (:4688-4691). Observed directly: invoking build_api_data_contract once on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json during this read-only audit CREATED data/snapshots/ranks_last.json (14,673 bytes) where no data/snapshots directory had existed. The write is a full overwrite, not an append; there is no timestamp in the file to distinguish generations; and failure is swallowed silently (:4746-4750).
findings.userImpact: Any script, test or ad-hoc analysis that constructs a contract destroys the rank baseline production's rankChange column diffs against. Combined with the override-path write, the file has multiple uncoordinated writers and no way to tell which board produced it.
findings.recommendedFix: Separate the read (stamp rankChange from the snapshot) from the write (persist this board's ranks) and let only the fresh-scrape promotion call the writer — server.py:1867 already has the gate. Stamp generatedAt and the source board identity into the file.
