notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. I built the real contract twice from exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json (the live scraper payload at HEAD) via build_api_data_contract, plus a third build with two sources disabled and a fourth with a seeded rank snapshot. Every distribution quoted is measured on those outputs (1,092 rows, 740 ranked), not inferred from names or docs.

REPO STATE. The first build created data/snapshots/ranks_last.json as a side effect of _stamp_rank_changes — a directory that did not previously exist. I removed it and restored the tree; `git status --porcelain` is empty and `ls data/` matches the pre-audit listing exactly. All later builds ran with the snapshot writer patched off. That side effect is itself reported as a finding: constructing a contract is not a read-only operation. Scratch files live only in the session scratchpad.

CLASSIFICATION SUMMARY.
- VALIDATED AGAINST ANYTHING: nothing in scope. Not one confidence threshold, tier constant, injury multiplier, auction-power knob, FAAB breakpoint or trade-grade band has a fit script, backtest or calibration artifact. The nearest exception is _PERCENTILE_SPREAD_TRIM_MIN_N = 5, which cites a real 2026-07-25 measurement — and that measurement no longer reproduces (it targeted ~40 top-200 disagreement rows; live is 10).
- IMPLEMENTED + ROUTED + CONSUMED + LIVE DATA: confidenceBucket, canonicalTierId, rank stamping, marketGapDirection, rankChange, softFallbackCount, sourceSpread/hillValueSpread, sourceAudit/isSingleSource, market corridor clamp, delta payload, compact view, dataFreshness, injury impact (in-season only), public trade grading.
- ROUTED BUT NOT CONSUMED BY ANY FRONTEND: poolAudit (zero hits under frontend/), coverageAudit, valueAuthority.
- IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT ROUTED: src/api/auction_power.py (no non-test caller; the live math is the JS mirror); assert_ranking_coherence on the canonical path.
- DEAD AT EVERY LAYER: src/canonical/confidence_intervals.py value bands + rank_history_band + ValueBandBadge; src/scoring/tiering.py positional tiers. src/api/feature_flags.py:55-72 and :356-362 already document both accurately — that file is the most reliable prose in the repository and I found no claim in it the code contradicted.
- NOT VERIFIABLE FROM REPOSITORY: whether data/rank_history.jsonl and data/source_value_history.jsonl exist in production and how deep they run (neither is in this checkout; data/ is gitignored with 8,174 force-tracked files and neither log is among them). The whole movers/sparkline/value-history surface is therefore Not Verified for live data. rank_history.coverage() exists precisely to answer this and is not wired to any alert. Also not verifiable: FAAB inputs — no data/public_league snapshot on disk.

ONE THING I INITIALLY GOT WRONG, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-FOUND. My first build reported dataFreshness ages matching CSV mtimes rather than the data/scrape_state stamps, which would have meant idpTradeCalc was being served stale at 9.09h. It did NOT reproduce: a second build and a direct _build_source_timestamps() call both read the stamps correctly (idpTradeCalc 3.29h, fresh). The first run almost certainly predated the sandbox materializing data/scrape_state. I am not reporting a freshness defect. What is worth recording is the shape of the risk: the `except (OSError, ValueError): pass` at :931-932 means any stamp-read problem degrades silently to CSV mtime, and a git-checkout mtime is meaningless as freshness — the fallback is not observable from the payload.

DOC-VS-CODE DISAGREEMENTS FOUND (each reported as a finding): injury_impact's 60%-cap and injury-type rulebook vs a 5% cap and severity-only logic; source_history's 180-snapshot/15MB header vs 1095/90MB in the same file; /api/movers' perSourceDelta docstring vs a currentSourceRanks field of absolute ranks; _stamp_rank_changes' claim that delta builds do not write the snapshot; valueAuthority advertising a frontend recompute that CLAUDE.md and dynasty-data.js both say was removed; compact_view's 6-field prune list vs 18; the cross-universe collision comment inverting what the exception list does; the corridor clamp's rationale citing a retired IDP calibration pass (CLAUDE.md already flags this); _compute_anomaly_flags retiring missing_source_distortion while the catalogue at :183-190 still lists it; _tier_id_from_rank / OVERALL_RANK_LIMIT comments describing a two-source era. CLAUDE.md itself held up well — the Live Value Pipeline ordering, the pick-stage correction, the buildRows display-ordinal nuance and the _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA = 0.0 note all matched the code.

WHAT SURPRISED ME. Three things. (1) The codebase diagnosed the ordinal-scale problem correctly for confidence buckets in July 2026 — the _percentile_rank_spread docstring is a precise statement of it — and then left _compute_market_gap averaging raw ordinals four hundred lines away, feeding the one column on the site that literally says "Buy" and "Sell". (2) The fix is usually already on the row: hillValueSpread would cure the confidence bucket's value-blindness, softFallbackCount its coverage-blindness, and source_pool_sizes the market gap. All three are computed, stamped, shipped, and read by nothing that produces a verdict. (3) The best-tested tier implementation in the repo (src/scoring/tiering.py — 14 tests, a grid-search fitter, drift detection) is dormant, while the one producing the 127 tiers users actually see has no test on its constants at all.

WHAT DESERVES TO INFLUENCE A REAL DECISION, on this evidence: rankDerivedValue for offense rows; sourceAudit and softFallbackCount as raw coverage facts; sourceSpread/hillValueSpread as raw dispersion facts; the rank/source history logs IF they exist in production, with the caveat that they are date-granular and last-write-wins. I would NOT act on marketGapDirection, canonicalTierId boundaries, identityConfidence, marketConfidence, IDP values inside the ±15% IDPTC corridor, or a public trade grade on a trade containing an unpriced asset.

formulas.name: Percentile-form Hill curve (LIVE board, step 2→3)
formulas.expression:
p = clamp((r − 1) / (N − 1), 0, 1)   with N = _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N = 500, fixed for every source (src/api/data_contract.py:4933)
V(p) = 9999 / (1 + (p / c)^s)
V(0) := 9999 exactly (short-circuit at :407-408)
result = clamp(round(V), 1, 9999)
formulas.inputs: r = the source's rank for this player after ladder/crosswalk translation (dimensionless ordinal); c, s = the scope master pair selected by _curve_for_source (data_contract.py:6401-6407: is_cross_market → GLOBAL, scope==overall_idp → IDP, else OFFENSE)
formulas.constants: GLOBAL c=0.1120 s=0.725 | OFFENSE c=0.1100 s=1.110 | IDP c=0.0830 s=1.110 | ROOKIE c=0.1530 s=0.885 (player_valuation.py:118,119,126,127,133,134,158,159). All eight are FITTED, not hand-picked. ROOKIE is fitted but NOT routed (data_contract.py:4990 stamps routed=False). Champion registry v2, promoted 2026-07-29 (config/model_registry/hill_scope_masters.json:84-91,149).
formulas.outputRange: 1..9999; the OFFENSE master bottoms out at 794 because p saturates at 1.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No missing-input branch — the function takes a percentile, so absence is handled upstream. The important behaviour is the clamp: any rank past 500 maps to p=1.0 and receives an identical tail value. I measured rank 500 → 794 and rank 800 → 794. Deliberate top-500-board behaviour per CLAUDE.md, but it means every row past 500 is value-tied by construction, which then feeds the tier detector's degenerate branch.
formulas.mathIssues: p=0 short-circuits before the exponentiation, so no 0^negative. No division-by-zero (c is a positive literal). The p=1 clamp is genuine information loss below rank 500, not an edge case.
formulas.validated: OFFENSE (c,s) only, by src/model_registry/holdout.py — and that criterion is not independent (findings 1 and 2). GLOBAL, IDP and ROOKIE have NO out-of-sample check of any kind; hill_masters.py:206-209 says so explicitly: 'only these two of the eight have a genuine out-of-sample check today'.

formulas.name: Rank-form Hill curve (reconstruction / fallback)
formulas.expression:
effective_rank = max(1, r)
V = 1 + 9998 / (1 + ((effective_rank − 1) / midpoint)^slope)
result = clamp(round(V), 1, 9999)
scope routing: scope.lower()=='idp' → IDP pair; everything else, INCLUDING picks → offense pair
formulas.inputs: r = canonicalConsensusRank, which the comment at :88-91 notes is a single GLOBAL ordinal over the whole board (so offense, IDP and picks all lie on one relation by construction)
formulas.constants: HILL_MIDPOINT=65.4, HILL_SLOPE=0.910 (:82-83); IDP_HILL_MIDPOINT=64.6, IDP_HILL_SLOPE=0.900 (:102-103). Re-tuned 2026-07-30 from 48.44/1.149 and 69.50/0.945.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rank None or ≤ 0 returns 0 (:304-305) — OUTSIDE the declared 1..9999 display range, and it will read as a real (worthless) value to any caller that does not special-case it.
formulas.mathIssues: r is clamped to ≥ 1 so the fractional exponent never sees a negative base. Returning 0 rather than None on missing input is the only real hazard.
formulas.validated: In-sample only. The constants were fit BY scripts/backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py AGAINST rankDerivedValue on the served board, then scored on the same 740 rows. The table at :339-345 comparing 'legacy_scope 83.8' to 'best-fit per scope 83.4' is a curve compared to its own optimum on its own fitting data — no holdout, no temporal split. The script is explicit that this is 'a CONSISTENCY test, not a predictive-accuracy test' (backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py:26-33).

formulas.name: Per-source Hill fit (grid search + refine)
formulas.expression:
pairs = [( i/(n−1), values[i]/values[0] × 9999 ) for i in 0..n−1]   over values sorted DESC and truncated to the top 400
minimise SSE = Σ (v − 9999/(1+(p/c)^s))²
coarse grid: c ∈ {0.005 + 0.005k, k=0..99} = 0.005..0.500 ; s ∈ {0.4 + 0.02k, k=0..105} = 0.4..2.5
refine: c ± {0.002, 0.001, 0} × s ± {0.01, 0.005, 0}
formulas.inputs: one source's published value column, positive values only, descending
formulas.constants: top-400 truncation; the grid bounds and refine offsets above — all hand-chosen with no stated derivation
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Non-numeric cells are skipped by the except at :96-98; zero and negative values are dropped at :99. A source with fewer than 2 usable rows returns [] and is dropped from its scope with a printed line only — the master is then fit on the survivors with no error and no record of the loss in the JSON output.
formulas.mathIssues: The refine step is a fixed ±2-cell box around the coarse optimum, so only local improvement is reachable. More importantly the coarse grid's 0.005 spacing in c is coarse relative to the criterion's sensitivity — promotion.py:41-45 states a 0.001 c shift moves the holdout criterion by ~13 points, so the fit's own quantisation is worth ~65 criterion points, well above the 25-point promotion margin.
formulas.validated: Per-source RMSEs are printed but never gated. Re-running the fit today, the six OFFENSE per-source fits span c=0.064 (DraftSharks) to c=0.207 (Fitzmaurice) — a 3.2x spread being averaged as if the sources were peers.

formulas.name: Scope-master combination
formulas.expression:
grid = sorted(unique( {i/2000 : i=1..49} ∪ {i/200 : i=1..199} ))    — 248 points, fine at the top of the curve
V*(p) = (1/J) Σ_j 9999/(1+(p/c_j)^s_j)      ← unweighted MEAN of the per-source FITTED curves
(c*, s*) = _fit( [(p, V*(p)) for p in grid] )   ← a Hill re-fit to the averaged curve
formulas.inputs: the J per-source (c_j, s_j) fits for that scope
formulas.constants: grid definition above; J = 6 (OFFENSE), 2 (GLOBAL), 2 (IDP), 2 (ROOKIE after three of five slices silently skip)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Returns None when a scope has zero per-source fits; main() prints '(no per-source fits)' and OMITS that constant from --json-out. auto_refit_hill_curves.py:234-237 then catches the omission and exits EXIT_ERROR. This degrades safely.
formulas.mathIssues: The master is fit to SYNTHETIC data — the mean of fitted curves, not the underlying observations. So the printed 'master-fit rmse' (12.5 to 29.0 today) measures how well one Hill approximates an average of Hills and says nothing about how well it describes any real board. The docstring's argument for the mean over trimmed mean-median ('with n=3 sources, trimmed mean-median degenerates to the middle source') is sound, but with J=2 for GLOBAL, IDP and ROOKIE the mean is a two-point average, so one bad source moves the master by half its error.
formulas.validated: no

formulas.name: Held-out criterion (the promotion gate)
formulas.expression:
per source: pairs = [( i/(n−1), values[i]/values[0] × 9999 )] over the top-400 descending positive values
RMSE_source = sqrt( (1/n) Σ (hill(p,c,s) − v)² )
criterion = (1/|S|) Σ_{s∈S} RMSE_s          ← unweighted MEAN across sources, not pooled (the docstring at :168-171 explains why: pooling would let a 400-row board outvote a 100-row one)
formulas.inputs: the four holdout CSVs' value columns; the (c, s) pair being scored
formulas.constants: FIT_TOP_N=400 (:84) matched to the fit's truncation; MIN_ROWS_FOR_SCORING=100 (:85); holdout set = {FantasyCalc, OTCFFB, PFKDynasty, FantasyNavigator} (:74-79); training set = the six offense boards (:58-65)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: The best in the audited set. A missing CSV or fewer than 100 priced rows is recorded in `skipped` and excluded from the mean; if NO board can be scored the function RAISES HoldoutError rather than returning a pass (:267-271, 'refusing to report a passing evaluation with no evidence behind it'); an explicitly EMPTY holdout dict is honoured rather than silently defaulted (:226-229); and train/holdout overlap raises both by label and by file path (:231-243).
formulas.mathIssues: Arithmetically clean. The defect is semantic and structural — see findings 1, 2 and 5.
formulas.validated: I reproduced it on today's CSVs: champion (0.1100, 1.110) → 799.4823 {FantasyCalc 776.8, FantasyNavigator 1148.5, OTCFFB 1030.2, PFKDynasty 242.3, n=399/400/400/400}; retired v1 (0.118, 1.17) → 838.4392. The registry's stored v2 figure is 787.8416 (hill_scope_masters.json:105) — an 11.6-point drift on IDENTICAL parameters in 7 days, purely from data movement.

formulas.name: Promotion decision
formulas.expression:
improvement = champion_criterion − challenger_criterion
champion_criterion is None   → REJECT ('an unmeasured incumbent is unknown, not beaten')
improvement ≤ −250           → REJECT + ALARM (points at the fit or its inputs, not the curve)
improvement < 25             → REJECT (ties go to the incumbent)
otherwise                    → PROMOTABLE
formulas.inputs: two criterion values, which the design requires to be PAIRED (scored on one snapshot)
formulas.constants: PROMOTION_MARGIN=25.0 (:46), justified by a stated 30-snapshot paired-delta study with worst sd 1.51 so ~16x the noise floor; REGRESSION_ALARM=250.0 (:51)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: champion_criterion None produces an explicit REJECT with a stated reason (:102-113), not a default win for the challenger. Correct, and rare.
formulas.mathIssues: The margin is only meaningful on a paired comparison. auto_refit_hill_curves.py:255-256 satisfies that by re-scoring both curves live; scripts/model_registry.py:190-196 does NOT — see finding 4.
formulas.validated: The 30-snapshot noise study in the docstring is stated but its data is not in the repo — Not Verifiable from Repository.

formulas.name: Scope drift (whether the gate runs at all)
formulas.expression:
drift[scope] = sqrt( (1/8) Σ_{p ∈ {0.01,0.05,0.10,0.20,0.30,0.50,0.70,0.90}} ( V_new(p) − V_old(p) )² )
if max(drift over all four scopes) ≤ 50 and not --force:  exit 0 WITHOUT evaluating the gate
formulas.inputs: the committed constants versus the freshly fitted ones
formulas.constants: DRIFT_RMSE_THRESHOLD=50.0 and an 8-point DRIFT_GRID (:90-91). No stated derivation for either.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A challenger missing any of the eight names errors at :234-237. A registry champion that disagrees with the committed constants errors at :204-212 with 'the registry is not describing what is deployed' — a genuinely good guard against comparing against the wrong incumbent.
formulas.mathIssues: The threshold takes the MAX over all four scopes, but the gate that follows scores only the OFFENSE pair. So an IDP-only drift opens the gate, an OFFENSE question is answered, and the verdict governs all eight constants.
formulas.validated: I ran the fit on today's data and computed the driver's own metric: GLOBAL 0.00, OFFENSE 34.34, IDP 326.57, ROOKIE 275.52. Max 326.57, so the gate WOULD open today on IDP drift, and would be adjudicated by a 22.4-point OFFENSE improvement that misses the 25-point margin (verdict REJECTED, exit 0, challenger recorded).

formulas.name: Rank-gap tier break score (LIVE tiering)
formulas.expression:
raw_gap[i]   = series[i+1] − series[i]              (series = −rankDerivedValue, so gaps are value DROPS)
rm[i]        = median( raw_gap[max(0,i−7) : min(n, i+8)] )
gap_score[i] = raw_gap[i] / rm[i]        if rm[i] > 1e-9
             = 1.0                       if rm[i] ≤ 1e-9 and raw_gap[i] < 1e-9
             = gap_threshold + 1.0        otherwise      ← FORCES a break
break after i  ⟺  gap_score[i] ≥ 2.0 AND players_since_last_break ≥ 3
formulas.inputs: the compacted board's rankDerivedValue series, descending; data_contract.py:2018 negates it so the detector sees ascending distance-from-best
formulas.constants: TIER_GAP_WINDOW=7, TIER_GAP_THRESHOLD=2.0, TIER_MIN_SIZE=3 (:48-50). Hand-set: no fitter, no config file, no test pins them.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A missing or None rankDerivedValue becomes 0 at data_contract.py:2018 (`-float(r.get('rankDerivedValue') or 0)`), so it sorts to the top of the negated series and manufactures a spurious gap. n=0 and n=1 are handled explicitly (:224-227).
formulas.mathIssues: The degenerate branch at :239 forces a tier break whenever the local median gap is zero but the current gap is not. Because the percentile curve ties every row past rank 500 at 794, the local median IS zero through the deep tail, so every transition off a tie block becomes a forced break, and tier IDs are uncapped by design (data_contract.py:2010-2012).
formulas.validated: no

formulas.name: Cohen's-d tiering (dormant second engine)
formulas.expression:
d = |mean(current tier so far) − candidate_value| / pooled_sd
pooled_sd = population stdev of the values REMAINING in the position pool (explicitly NOT the tier's own sd)
new tier ⟺ d > threshold[position]
formulas.inputs: rows carrying pos and rankDerivedValue (falling back to values.full then value)
formulas.constants: config/tiers/thresholds.json: QB 0.35, RB 0.22, WR 0.22, TE 0.35, DL 0.30, LB 0.30, DB 0.30, PICK 2.0 — byte-identical to the module defaults at :46-58. HAND-PICKED and never fitted; the config's own _comment says exactly that.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: pooled_sd ≤ 0 returns d = 0.0 (:81-82), so every player joins the current tier — a degenerate pool silently produces ONE tier rather than raising. load_thresholds falls back to module defaults on a missing, unparseable or wrong-shaped config (:87-113), which is safe but means a corrupted config is indistinguishable from an absent one.
formulas.mathIssues: This is not Cohen's d. Cohen's d compares two group means using a pooled sd of those two groups; here mean_B is a single point and the denominator is the sd of a third population (the unassigned remainder). The quantity is a z-score of a candidate against a running mean, scaled by an unrelated dispersion. The name overstates its statistical standing.
formulas.validated: no, and unreachable in production — no importer, and feature_flags.py:372 marks positional_tiers NO_GATE

formulas.name: Tier threshold 'fit'
formulas.inputs: contract player rows loaded from data/latest_contract.json
formulas.constants: grids QB/TE (0.2,0.6,0.02), RB/WR (0.1,0.5,0.02), DL/LB/DB (0.2,0.6,0.04); target TIER COUNTS QB 4-6, RB 8-12, WR 8-12, TE 4-6, DL/LB/DB 4-8 — all hand-picked
formulas.outputRange: one threshold per position, within its grid
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A position with fewer than 3 rows is skipped and simply absent from the returned dict (:250-252); scripts/refit_tier_thresholds.py:139-147 then writes that dict WHOLESALE, so a sparse position silently disappears from the config and falls back to the module prior. The script's own top-level missing-input handling is correct: no contract → log + exit 2 (:107-111).
formulas.mathIssues: This is not a fit to data. It searches for the threshold that yields a hand-chosen number of tiers, so the 'measurement' is the analyst's aesthetic preference laundered through a grid search. PICK has no grid entry, so a successful run deletes PICK=2.0 from the config.
formulas.validated: Never run. Its only input, data/latest_contract.json, does not exist (verified on disk), and no workflow invokes the script (grep over .github/ returns nothing) — both facts are already conceded in config/tiers/thresholds.json:1.

formulas.name: IDP ladder translation and extrapolation
formulas.expression:
integer pr within ladder → ladder[pr−1]                                     (EXACT)
fractional 1 ≤ pr ≤ n    → ladder[⌊pr⌋−1] + (ladder[⌊pr⌋] − ladder[⌊pr⌋−1]) × frac   (INTERPOLATED)
pr > n                   → ladder[−1] + step × (pr − n), where step = mean of the last min(5, n−1) ladder diffs, floored at 1.0, and the result is forced strictly greater than ladder[−1]   (EXTRAPOLATED)
formulas.inputs: a within-position rank; the backbone ladder built from the trusted full-board source's per-player values
formulas.constants: tail window 5; minimum step 1.0; min_synthetic_rank 1
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty ladder passes the raw rank through unchanged and tags TRANSLATION_FALLBACK so the caller can attach a caution flag (:250-252) — honest, and the tag is the point. Non-numeric pr becomes 1.0; pr < 1 becomes 1.0.
formulas.mathIssues: Monotonicity is explicitly forced at :290-291, and the 5-diff tail mean prevents one wild spacing from blowing up the projection. Sound.
formulas.validated: Unit-tested for shape only (tests/canonical/test_idp_backbone.py). No data validation that the resulting synthetic ranks produce sensible cross-market values.

formulas.name: Coverage weight
formulas.expression: w = max(0, declared_weight);  depth is None → w;  depth ≤ 0 → 0;  else w × min(1, depth / 60)
formulas.inputs: the source's declared weight and declared depth
formulas.constants: MIN_FULL_COVERAGE_DEPTH = 60 — the docstring concedes '60 was chosen as a sensible "fully covered" threshold', i.e. hand-picked
formulas.missingDataBehavior: depth None returns the weight unchanged; a non-numeric depth also returns it unchanged (both are treated as 'overall list, no down-weighting')
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: Inert today by the module's own admission (:320-324): every registered source declares depth ≥ 62, so the factor is 1.0 everywhere. 'Do not assume shallow-source down-weighting is active today.'

formulas.name: Legacy piecewise calibration curve
formulas.expression:
percentile = (depth − (rank − 1)) / depth        ← rank 1 gives p = 1.0, deepest gives 1/depth
if p ≥ knee:  calibrated = round(scale × p^2.5)
else:         calibrated = round( scale × knee^2.5 × (p / knee) )    ← linear ramp to the origin
clamped to [0, scale];  K/P/OL capped at 600
formulas.inputs: blended_value ordering within a universe
formulas.constants: exponent 2.5, knee 0.65 offense / 0.80 IDP, scales offense_vet 7800 / offense_rookie 7000 / idp_vet 5500 / idp_rookie 5000, PICK_CEILING 7500, NON_FANTASY_CEILING 600. The sweep history at :39-43 (v1→v4 with tier-agreement percentages) is stated but the producing script, calibration_sweep.py, is not in the repo.
formulas.outputRange: 0..7800 internal, remapped to 1..9999 by to_display_value (:75-85, display = round(calibrated × 9999 / 7800))
formulas.missingDataBehavior: depth 0 breaks out of the loop leaving calibrated_value unset; such assets are then skipped in the display remap at :345-348, so display_value simply never appears rather than defaulting to a number.
formulas.mathIssues: Guarded against double-calibration by a hard RuntimeError on canonical-pipeline-tagged assets (:266-277), naming the offending asset — a good guard. INTERNAL_SCALE_MAX is a second literal 7800 (:72) that must equal UNIVERSE_SCALES['offense_vet'] and is only kept in sync by a comment.
formulas.validated: Tier-agreement percentages are quoted in the comment; the producing sweep script is absent — Not Verifiable from Repository. Dormant in production regardless.

formulas.name: Legacy pick round curve
formulas.expression:
base = LEGACY_PICK_ROUND_CURVE[round]
early → ×1.15,  late → ×0.85
slot ≤ 4:  base = early_val×(1−frac) + (early_val+200)×frac,  frac = (4−slot)/4
slot ≥ 9:  base = round_val×(1−frac) + late_val×frac,          frac = (slot−8)/4
year > current_year:  base × 0.70^(year − current_year)
result = clamp(base, 100, 7500)
formulas.inputs: a pick name parsed by _parse_pick_info into {year, round, slot, tier}
formulas.constants: round medians 6124 / 5251 / 4367 / 3425 / 3146 / 2600; tier ±15%; PICK_YEAR_DISCOUNT 0.70; an unexplained +200 slot bump at :185
formulas.missingDataBehavior: WRONG DIRECTION: an unrecognised round falls back to min(keys)=1 (:164-165), so an unparseable pick is priced as a FIRST-ROUNDER — the most expensive possible wrong answer. Dormant, so no live impact, but the failure mode is inverted.
formulas.mathIssues: Slots 5-8 match neither branch and take the flat round median, producing a discontinuity at the slot 4/5 and 8/9 boundaries. The +200 term is undocumented.
formulas.validated: no

formulas.name: Weighted percentile (value bands)
formulas.expression: position_i = (cum_before_i + w_i/2) / Σw × 100 ;  linear interpolation between the bracketing positions ; clamp outside the first/last
formulas.inputs: per-source values and weights
formulas.constants: p10 / p50 / p90; min_sources=3; fallback bands ×0.85/×1.15 ('insufficient_sources') and ×0.80/×1.20 ('fallback_narrow')
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Documented and honest. Fewer than 3 sources returns a ±15% band tagged method='insufficient_sources'; a band that fails to bracket the canonical value returns ±20% centred on canonical tagged 'fallback_narrow'; the normal case is tagged 'bracket'. Every path stamps the method so a consumer can tell a measurement from a placeholder. A missing rank_to_value map silently falls back to a hardcoded `10000 − rank×20` proxy (:144), documented as test-only.
formulas.mathIssues: The `source_weights` argument is silently ignored: :178-187 rebuilds every pair at weight 1.0 and the following `for src, wt in source_weights.items()` loop has an empty body (only the guard's `continue`). Passing weights produces identical output to passing none.
formulas.validated: no; the ±15% band is justified as 'the typical inter-source spread for well-ranked players in our historical data' with no in-repo evidence

formulas.name: Spearman plus paired bootstrap (adjusted-board holdout)
formulas.expression:
ranks with ties averaged; rho = Σ(rx−mx)(ry−my) / sqrt( Σ(rx−mx)² · Σ(ry−my)² )
bootstrap: 2000 seeded resamples, the SAME index set scoring both arms; delta_b = rho_adjusted(b) − rho_market(b)
win_rate = #{delta_b > 0} / 2000 ;  CI = [delta_(0.025), delta_(0.975)]
verdict: movers < min_players//2 → INCONCLUSIVE ; ci_low > 0 → ADJUSTED WINS ; ci_high < 0 → MARKET WINS ; else NO DIFFERENCE DETECTED
formulas.inputs: market value, adjusted value, and realized fantasy points under the league's exact scoring, per player
formulas.constants: iterations 2000, seed 20260728, min_players 30, per-position minimum 10
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Rows missing any of market/adjusted/actual are dropped; fewer than 30 joined rows returns a BoardComparison whose verdict STRING says so rather than a number (:193-197); n < 10 in the bootstrap returns (0.5, 0, 0), an explicit no-signal value; spearman returns 0.0 on degenerate input rather than raising, because 'a diagnostic must not be the thing that fails'. The best missing-data handling in the audited set.
formulas.mathIssues: The CI index `int(0.975×len)−1` is a percentile-index convention, off by at most one sample in 2000. The `movers` guard is the important part — it prevents a null result from being read as evidence about the adjustment when the adjustment barely applied.
formulas.validated: Yes, and honestly scoped — :15-30 states up front that it is not a forecast test and that any lookahead in the board is common-mode and cancels in the paired difference.

formulas.name: Band trend classification
formulas.expression:
spread_t = p90_t − p10_t ;  lookback = min(30, len−1)
change = spread[−1] − spread[−lookback−1] ;  pct = change / spread[−lookback−1]
pct ≤ −0.10 → converging ;  pct ≥ +0.10 → diverging ;  else stable
formulas.inputs: a chronological series of {date, valueBand{p10, p50, p90}} snapshots
formulas.constants: window_days 30; ±10% thresholds — hand-picked
formulas.outputRange: one of three labels, plus the spread series
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty or unusable input returns None (not a fabricated flat trend); a single snapshot returns trend='stable' with change None; an older spread of 0 leaves pct None and trend 'stable'. Correct.
formulas.mathIssues: `window_days` is applied as a count of SNAPSHOTS, not days, so the field named spreadChange30d spans 30 weeks on a weekly series. Dormant.
formulas.validated: no

formulas.name: Provenance fingerprint
formulas.expression: sha256 of each training file, truncated to 16 hex characters, recorded per source label
formulas.inputs: the six OFFENSE training CSVs, resolved via hill_masters.training_input_paths()
formulas.constants: 16-character truncation
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Correct and deliberate: a missing input is recorded as 'missing' rather than skipped, explicitly so that a version fitted on five sources cannot be mistaken for one fitted on six (:64-69).
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: I compared the champion's recorded fingerprints against today's CSVs: 5 of 6 have changed (DraftSharks d474c81d→cf033e2c, DynastyDaddy 4d2cd2d8→67e36512, DynastyNerds d8d10d6f→6ff8a520, Fitzmaurice caf3ef48→a834e5f3, KTC e4ffc49a→e5dffe2c); YahooBoone 8687353a0fcbb9ee is byte-identical to both v1 (2026-07-26) and v2 (2026-07-28). The champion's stored criterion is therefore not reproducible from today's tree — a strength of the design, in that it tells you so, and the reason finding 4 matters.

findings.title: The 'held-out' boards are live inputs to the blend the curve serves — the benchmark is not independent of the system it grades
findings.evidence: src/model_registry/holdout.py:74-79 defines the holdout set as FantasyCalc (CSVs/site_raw/fantasyCalc.csv), OTCFFB (otcffbSf.csv), PFKDynasty (pfkDynasty.csv) and FantasyNavigator (fantasyNavigatorSf.csv). All four are registered LIVE BLEND SOURCES: src/api/data_contract.py:1302 ("key": "fantasyCalc"), :1327 ("key": "otcffbSf"), :1361 ("key": "fantasyNavigatorSf"), :1388 ("key": "pfkDynasty"). I enumerated runtime routing from _RANKING_SOURCES + _curve_for_source (data_contract.py:6401-6407): all four route to the OFFENSE master — the exact pair the holdout scores. Player overlap between the six training boards' top-400 and each holdout board's top-400, measured on today's CSVs: FantasyCalc 395/399 (99.0%), OTCFFB 393/398 (98.7%), PFKDynasty 399/400 (99.8%), FantasyNavigator 362/400 (90.5%). FantasyNavigator is worse than 'another market': data_contract.py:548-552 records that its values are KTC-DERIVED (rows carry ktc_player_id), so a transform of a training board is being used as a holdout. The module concedes half the problem (holdout.py:33-40, 'Every holdout source is another consensus market, correlated with the training sources by construction') but never says they are blend inputs; CLAUDE.md drops even that caveat, describing the gate as 'dynasty boards the fit never reads'.
findings.userImpact: Every claim of the form 'the new curve generalizes better' means only 'the curve reproduces the published value shape of four boards whose ranks we already vote into our own board'. It is a self-consistency measurement presented as validation. A user reading /rankings has no way to know the constants behind every displayed value were selected by a benchmark built from the pipeline's own inputs.
findings.recommendedFix: Either (a) rename the criterion and every surface reporting it to 'cross-market shape consistency', and state in holdout.py, the registry's _semantics block and CLAUDE.md that all four boards are blend inputs and that one is KTC-derived; or (b) hold out a board that is NOT in _RANKING_SOURCES, and add a mechanism test asserting set(OFFENSE_HOLDOUT_SOURCES) is disjoint from {s['key'] for s in _RANKING_SOURCES} — the same shape as the existing by-path guard at holdout.py:237-243, which already proves the team knows how to write this check.
findings.affectedSystems: Hill scope masters, model registry, promotion gate, every displayed player value

findings.title: The gate rewards precisely the property the pipeline rejected for those same four boards
findings.evidence: All four holdout boards were moved OFF the value-direct path because their published value curves decay faster than our consensus and the Hampel filter discarded most of their votes: data_contract.py:364-381 (fantasyCalc, 'crowd values decay much *faster* down the board than the KTC-anchored Hill consensus', 54.9%→58% drop rate), :395-406 (otcffbSf, 'decay even faster', 55.6%→86%), :548-556 (fantasyNavigatorSf, 'exactly the profile that put fantasyCalc/otcffbSf outside the Hampel window'), :569-580 (pfkDynasty, value scale 'hand-shaped and unvalidated against our consensus decay'). None appears in _VALUE_BASED_SOURCES (data_contract.py:5110-5117 = {ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc} only). The holdout criterion is squared error against exactly those discarded value curves, so minimising it pulls the OFFENSE master toward the decay shape the blend deliberately refuses. I searched the criterion surface (c ∈ [0.060,0.200] × s ∈ [0.60,2.00]): its optimum on today's data is c=0.071, s=1.20 at criterion 480.02 — 319 points better than the champion's 799.48. Under that curve the board deflates by 6.2% at rank 12, 13.5% at 24, 24.0% at 50, 34.0% at 100, 42.0% at 200 and 49.5% at 500. The optimum also makes the one hand-maintained human board WORSE (PFKDynasty 242.3→800.5) while improving the three crowd boards (FantasyCalc 776.8→305.3, FantasyNavigator 1148.5→487.5, OTCFFB 1030.2→326.7) — the unweighted 4-source mean at holdout.py:274 is dominated by the crowd curves. The champion trajectory has moved monotonically toward that optimum: c 0.118 (v1) → 0.110 (v2) → 0.108 (today's fit).
findings.userImpact: The only automated quality signal on the most load-bearing constants in the repo has a systematic preferred direction that contradicts a documented, measured design decision. Followed to its optimum it would cut mid- and deep-board values by a third to a half, silently repricing every trade evaluation, every FAAB bid and every tier boundary.
findings.recommendedFix: Score the holdout on RANK correlation (Spearman) rather than value RMSE — these boards were kept as rank signals precisely because their ordering is trusted and their levels are not, and board_holdout.py:32-39 already argues that case for the other backtest. Alternatively weight the human board against the crowd boards explicitly and state the weighting. Either way, print the criterion's own optimum alongside every verdict so a reviewer can see how far the gate wants to travel.
findings.affectedSystems: promotion gate, OFFENSE Hill master, all downstream values

findings.title: Six of eight production constants ship on the back of a gate that measures two of them
findings.evidence: src/model_registry/hill_masters.py:206-209: VALIDATED_PARAMS = ('HILL_PERCENTILE_C', 'HILL_PERCENTILE_S'), commented 'only these two of the eight have a genuine out-of-sample check today'. auto_refit_hill_curves.py:255-256 scores only that pair and :265 decides on it. But the recorded challenger carries all eight (:281-291, params=fitted), scripts/model_registry.py:208 promotes the whole ModelVersion, and :244 write_committed_constants(champ.params) writes all eight (hill_masters.py:233-244 iterates CONSTANT_NAMES and raises if any is missing). Meanwhile the drift check deciding whether the gate runs takes the MAX over all four scopes (auto_refit_hill_curves.py:242). I ran the fit on today's CSVs and computed the driver's own drift metric: GLOBAL 0.00, OFFENSE 34.34, IDP 326.57, ROOKIE 275.52. So today the gate opens on a 326-point IDP move and is adjudicated by a 22.4-point OFFENSE improvement. Concretely, today's IDP challenger (c=0.0850, s=0.935) differs from the committed pair (0.0830, 1.110) by −3.5% at rank ~6, +13.3% at ~101, +21.4% at ~151, +33.6% at ~250, +42.6% at ~350 and +52.8% at rank 500.
findings.userImpact: An IDP or GLOBAL curve change of arbitrary size can reach production on the strength of an OFFENSE-only verdict. Nobody measures whether the IDP board improved; the +52.8% deep-IDP move above would have shipped unexamined had the offense pair cleared 25 points.
findings.recommendedFix: Either gate per scope (an IDP holdout is constructible — IDPTC's IDP slice trains that master and draftSharksIdp could be held out) or make promotion partial: promote only the validated pair, and require a separately-reasoned human action for the other six. At minimum, print the unvalidated scopes' drift in the promotion issue body and refuse to `apply` a version whose unvalidated constants moved beyond a stated bound.
findings.affectedSystems: IDP board, GLOBAL cross-market anchor, ROOKIE fit tooling

findings.title: `model_registry.py validate` performs the unpaired cross-snapshot comparison the design explicitly forbids
findings.evidence: scripts/model_registry.py:190-196 reads BOTH criteria out of the registry file — champ_crit = (champ.holdout or {}).get('criterion'); chal_crit = (challenger.holdout or {}).get('criterion') — then calls decide_promotion. Neither is re-scored. src/model_registry/promotion.py:7-29 states the rule this breaks: 'A rule that compared this week's challenger to last week's champion SCORE would be reading five days of market drift as model quality ... the comparison is always made on ONE snapshot with both curves scored against it.' The registry records having been bitten by exactly this — hill_scope_masters.json:75: 'holdout re-scored 2026-07-29 against that day's boards (849.8 -> 819.7). The prior figure was measured 2026-07-26 and was NOT comparable to challenger v2's 2026-07-28 score: promotion.py requires a PAIRED comparison because the criterion's absolute level drifts ~68 points week to week.' And this is the path the automation hands to humans: auto_refit_hill_curves.py:313-318 prints 'python3 scripts/model_registry.py validate {target}' as step 1 of the promotion recipe. Measured today: the champion's stored criterion is 787.8416 but re-scoring the identical (0.1100, 1.110) on today's CSVs gives 799.4823 — 11.6 points, 46% of the 25-point margin, in 7 days, from data movement alone. Five of six training fingerprints have changed since v2 was fitted.
findings.userImpact: A challenger can clear the promotion margin on market drift rather than model quality, and the human-facing command is the one that permits it. The auto-driver's comparison is correct (it re-scores both at :255-256), so the safe path and the documented path disagree — the worst possible arrangement, because the documented one is the one a human will follow at 2am.
findings.recommendedFix: Make cmd_validate re-score BOTH champion and challenger via evaluate_offense_master before calling decide_promotion, exactly as the driver does; refuse, or loudly warn, if the challenger's recorded trainingInputs fingerprints no longer match the CSVs on disk. Add a test asserting that a stored-vs-fresh comparison is not reachable.

findings.title: The IDP master is fit on sources that never use it and applied to sources it was never fit on — the overlap is zero
findings.evidence: The fit assigns the IDP scope to IDPTradeCalc's IDP slice and DraftSharks-IDP (scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:27-32, :77-83, :367-383). At runtime _curve_for_source (data_contract.py:6401-6407) tests is_cross_market FIRST and routes those sources to GLOBAL — and both idpTradeCalc (data_contract.py:1064) and draftSharksIdp (:1700) set is_cross_market=True. I enumerated the routing from the live registry: the IDP master's actual consumers are dlfIdp, dlfRookieIdp, idpShow and fantasyProsIdp — all four are signal=rank (data_contract.py:287-305, :346-349, plus the derived is_rank_signal at :1713-1720) and none publishes a value column at all. The intersection of {sources that train the IDP master} and {sources that use the IDP master} is therefore empty.
findings.userImpact: The curve converting every IDP expert board's rank into a value is calibrated to the value distribution of two boards that take a different curve. There is no reason to expect it to be right, and no measurement anywhere that would notice if it were not — the IDP pair is also outside VALIDATED_PARAMS.
findings.recommendedFix: Have the fit's scope assignment call the same routing predicate the runtime uses, or at minimum add a test asserting every source in the fit's scope dicts routes to the master it trains. Then decide deliberately what the IDP curve should be fit against, given that its consumers publish only ranks.
findings.affectedSystems: IDP board values, IDP trade evaluation, IDP tiering

findings.title: The OFFENSE master is fit on value columns that the live blend discards
findings.evidence: Training set (holdout.py:58-65, mirroring fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:59-72): KTC(ktc.csv), DynastyDaddy, DynastyNerds, YahooBoone, Fitzmaurice, DraftSharks(draftSharksSf.csv). At runtime: ktc.csv is NOT a blend source at all — data_contract.py:1014-1019 records that the standard `ktc` vote was dropped 2026-04-28 and only `ktcSfTep` votes; dynastyDaddySf, dynastyNerdsSfTep, yahooBoone and fantasyProsFitzmaurice are all signal=rank (data_contract.py:322-325, :429-432, :475-478, :495-498) so their value columns never enter the blend; draftSharks is is_cross_market and takes the GLOBAL curve. Net: of the six boards whose published values determine HILL_PERCENTILE_C/S, none contributes a value to the blend through the OFFENSE curve, and the only source that votes value-direct through that curve — ktcSfTep (data_contract.py:5110-5117) — is not a training source.
findings.userImpact: The OFFENSE curve is calibrated to a signal the pipeline explicitly stopped using, then applied to fourteen rank-signal sources whose value distributions were never consulted. This is documented nowhere, and the fit script's own docstring (fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:5-6, 'value-based sources are the training set for the rank-to-value conversion system') was true in April 2026 and is no longer.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the fit script's docstring and CLAUDE.md to state what the training signal is relative to what the blend actually consumes, and reconsider whether ktc.csv belongs in the training set at all — its presence is currently load-bearing only as the justification, repeated in three separate docstrings, for why the gate had to move off it.

findings.title: DraftSharks trains three scope masters and uses neither of the two it dominates
findings.evidence: draftSharksSf.csv trains the OFFENSE master (fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:71), draftSharksIdp.csv trains the IDP master (:82), and the two concatenated train the GLOBAL master (:150-166, :354-362). At runtime both registry entries carry is_cross_market=True (data_contract.py:1670, :1700) plus ds_combined_rank_partner (:1666, :1697), documented at :1663-1665 as routing 'both through the GLOBAL Hill master'. So DraftSharks casts one of six votes in the OFFENSE master and one of two in the IDP master while consuming neither. In the IDP master it is half the input.
findings.userImpact: A single vendor's value shape has outsized, unintended influence on two curves it does not use. Today its per-source OFFENSE fit is c=0.064 against Fitzmaurice's c=0.207 — a 3.2x spread averaged as if the six boards were peers, with the extreme contributed by a source that will not use the result.
findings.recommendedFix: Assign fit scopes from the same predicate the runtime uses (is_cross_market → GLOBAL) rather than from a hand-maintained parallel dict in the fit script.

findings.title: Tier thresholds are hand-set priors with no fitter that can run, and the fitter would not fit them to data anyway
findings.evidence: config/tiers/thresholds.json holds QB 0.35, RB 0.22, WR 0.22, TE 0.35, DL/LB/DB 0.30, PICK 2.0 — byte-identical to the module defaults at src/scoring/tiering.py:46-58. The config's own _comment (line 1) is accurate: 'these are still HAND-SET PRIORS and have never been fitted ... No workflow in .github/workflows/ invokes the fitter, so the refit monthly cadence described here has never run.' I confirmed both halves: grep for refit_tier_thresholds across .github/ returns nothing, and the script's only input, data/latest_contract.json (scripts/refit_tier_thresholds.py:96), does not exist — the script logs an error and returns exit 2 at :107-111. Beyond that, the fitter is not a fit: src/scoring/tiering.py:213-272 grid-searches for the threshold whose resulting TIER COUNT lands nearest the midpoint of a hand-chosen target range (QB 4-6, RB 8-12, WR 8-12, TE 4-6, DL/LB/DB 4-8) with a +10 penalty for landing outside it. PICK has no grid entry, so a successful run returns a dict without PICK and scripts/refit_tier_thresholds.py:139-147 writes it wholesale, deleting the 2.0 threshold from the config.
findings.userImpact: No live impact — the entire Cohen's-d path is dormant (no production importer; feature_flags.py:372 marks positional_tiers NO_GATE and :358-361 documents it as dead at all three layers). The risk is interpretive: the file's presence and the word 'refit' invite a future reader to treat these numbers as measured.
findings.recommendedFix: Either delete the module and its config, or if it is to be revived: fix the PICK grid gap, rename fit_thresholds_grid_search to something that says what it does (target_tier_count_search), and state in the docstring that the target ranges are an analyst's preference, not an estimand.

findings.title: Rank-form reconstruction constants are fit to the pipeline's own output and scored on the same rows — the quoted RMSEs are in-sample
findings.evidence: src/canonical/player_valuation.py:71-72: 'Fit by scripts/backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py, per scope, against rankDerivedValue on the served board.' The comparison table at :339-345 reports legacy_scope 83.8 overall against 'best-fit per scope 83.4' and concludes at :353 that 'The re-tuned pair now sits ON the achievable floor'. Both arms are computed on the same 740 rows of the same board — scripts/backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py:38-44 lists candidate 6 as 'a rank-form curve fit to THIS board, reported as the achievable floor'. There is no train/test split and no temporal holdout. To the script's credit it says plainly (:26-33) that this is 'a CONSISTENCY test, not a predictive-accuracy test'.
findings.userImpact: 'RMSE 89.8, on the achievable floor' reads as a validation result and is not one. It establishes only that a two-parameter curve can reproduce the board it was fit to. Anyone citing it as evidence that the reconstruction path is accurate would be overstating it — and these values do reach users, through terminal team-value and rank-history charts.
findings.recommendedFix: Label the numbers in-sample where they appear in player_valuation.py:339-345. If a real check is wanted, fit on one archived snapshot and score on another — the module already notes that 16 archived snapshots spanning 2026-07-16 to 07-30 exist.
findings.affectedSystems: terminal value fallback, rank-history backfill, frontend value-history charts

findings.title: The ROOKIE master silently loses three of its five intended training slices, and would ingest synthetic rank encodings if it found them
findings.evidence: scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:387-406 intends to fit KTC, IDPTC, Boone, Fitzmaurice and DraftSharks rookie slices; _load_rookie_values (:169-198) reads them from the snapshot's `_canonicalSiteValues` dict. Running the fitter today: 'Boone-Rookie (only 0 rookies with values; skipping)', and likewise Fitzmaurice-Rookie and DraftSharks-Rookie. Cause: the snapshot's _canonicalSiteValues carries only three keys — I counted across exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json's 1,074 players: idpTradeCalc 814, ktc 464, ktcSfTep 464, nothing else — despite 181 rookie-flagged rows being present. The 2026-04-21 expansion has therefore never contributed. Worse, if those keys ever did appear they would be the synthetic rank encodings (999900 − rank×100) that data_contract.py:1723-1734 warns about by name ('Any consumer doing arithmetic over canonicalSiteValues MUST either skip these keys ... mixing the six-digit encodings with native 0-9999 values has produced two real bugs'), because all three are rank-signal sources — and _load_rookie_values does exactly that arithmetic. Note also the inconsistency within one file: _load_idptc_idp_values (:139) reads p.get('idpTradeCalc') off the player dict while _load_rookie_values (:189) reads p['_canonicalSiteValues'].
findings.userImpact: Low today, because the ROOKIE master is not routed (data_contract.py:4990 stamps routed=False and CLAUDE.md calls it refit tooling only). But the constant is maintained weekly and recorded in the registry as if fitted from five sources, and player_valuation.py:156-157 states 'routing the curve is a live option'.
findings.recommendedFix: Have _load_rookie_values skip any key in rank_signal_source_keys(), and raise rather than print when a configured slice yields zero rows, so a permanently-dead input cannot masquerade as a routine skip. Unify the two snapshot accessors.

findings.title: compute_value_band's source_weights argument is accepted and silently discarded
findings.evidence: src/canonical/confidence_intervals.py:177-187: the branch builds pairs_w.append((v, 1.0)) for every pair regardless of weight, then runs `for src, wt in source_weights.items(): if not isinstance(wt, (int, float)): continue` — a loop whose entire body is the guard — then assigns pairs = pairs_w. Passing weights yields output identical to passing none. The module docstring at :31-33 promises 'Weights default to 1.0 per source; the dynamic-weights module in Phase 10 can override.'
findings.userImpact: None today (dormant; feature_flags.py:63 value_confidence_intervals=False, :358-361 records it dead at all three layers). A future caller enabling the flag with per-source weights would get uniform weighting, no error, and a band it believes is weighted.
findings.recommendedFix: Implement the weighting or delete the parameter. A parameter that is accepted and discarded is worse than one that does not exist.

findings.title: scripts/fit_hill_curve_from_market.py is stale in three independent ways
findings.evidence: (1) Its IDP path globs REPO.glob('dynasty_data_*.json') at :234-238 — the repository ROOT. No such file exists there; the sibling fitter looks in data/ then exports/latest (fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:112). So `--universe idp` always prints 'no snapshot found at dynasty_data_*.json' and then 'No sources loaded; aborting.' (2) It prints 'Current (ours) midpoint=45.00 slope=1.100' at :357 and evaluates _hill(r, 45, 1.1) at :374, while the live constants are HILL_MIDPOINT=65.4 / HILL_SLOPE=0.910 (player_valuation.py:82-83) — the operator's comparison baseline is simply wrong. (3) Line 344 is dead code: simple_m = sum(m for *_, _m, _s, _ in () or ()) or 0.0, immediately overwritten at :345. Its docstring still directs the reader to use its output to update HILL_MIDPOINT/HILL_SLOPE, but player_valuation.py:71 says those are now fit by scripts/backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py, and :60-69 explains at length why fitting individual retail boards is the wrong target for a reconstruction curve.
findings.userImpact: An operator following the module docstring would fit against the wrong target, compare against a wrong baseline, and get nothing at all on the IDP path.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the script (backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py supersedes it), or fix all three and point its docstring at the current owner of those constants.

findings.title: src/model_registry/__init__.py still describes the removed autonomous-commit behaviour as current
findings.evidence: src/model_registry/__init__.py:396-400: 'The Hill scope masters are the live example: eight constants in src/canonical/player_valuation.py refit weekly by .github/workflows/refit-hill-curves.yml and committed to main without review.' That is the defect the package exists to remove, stated in the present tense in the package's own docstring. The code disagrees on every point: the workflow commits only config/model_registry/ (refit-hill-curves.yml:151, pinned by tests/model_registry/test_refit_path_characterisation.py:97-103), the driver contains no writer and cannot import one (hill_masters.py:167-173; test_refit_path_characterisation.py:66-76 asserts both), and `apply` is a human command. The same docstring's 'Modules' list (:410-415) omits board_holdout and hill_masters.
findings.userImpact: A reader auditing the promotion path from the package docstring would conclude the prohibition is being violated when it is in fact enforced — the inverse of the usual doc-drift failure, and equally misleading.
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite the Scope paragraph in the past tense and list all five modules.

findings.title: No temporal validation exists anywhere in the calibration path
findings.evidence: Every measurement in this subsystem is computed on one day's scrape. The fit reads CSVs/site_raw/*.csv (fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:56-83) and the gate reads CSVs/site_raw/*.csv (holdout.py:74-79) — the same directory, refreshed by the same job, on the same run. auto_refit_hill_curves.py:255-256 scores champion and challenger against that single snapshot, which is correct for pairing but means there is no out-of-time arm at all. The only forward-looking check in the audited set is board_holdout.py, and it disclaims being one (:15-30): 'this is NOT a forecast test — it cannot tell you whether either board predicts the future ... would need board snapshots taken before a season that this repo does not keep.' The registry's provenance fingerprints prove the data moves (5 of 6 training inputs changed in 7 days) but nothing scores across that movement.
findings.userImpact: Nothing in the registry can distinguish 'this curve describes dynasty markets' from 'this curve described dynasty markets on 2026-07-28'. The 68-point week-to-week criterion drift cited in promotion.py:9-13 is the size of that unmeasured axis, against a 25-point promotion margin.
findings.recommendedFix: Archive the four holdout CSVs on each refit — they are 9-18 KB each — and add a second criterion scored on the previous run's boards. That turns the current 'is this stable?' hand-waving into a number, using data the workflow already has in hand.

findings.title: No registry entry recorded since 2026-07-29 despite drift far above the threshold
findings.evidence: config/model_registry/hill_scope_masters.json:4 updatedAt 2026-07-29T23:35:35Z; latest version v2 fittedAt 2026-07-28. The workflow runs Tuesdays 06:17 UTC (refit-hill-curves.yml:32) and records a challenger on EVERY run where drift exceeds the threshold, whatever the verdict (auto_refit_hill_curves.py:279-295); the workflow comment at :136-140 states 'a MISSING weekly entry is itself the signal that this workflow stopped running'. 2026-07-28 and 2026-08-04 are both Tuesdays, and today's fit produces max drift 326.57, far above the 50-point threshold, so a v3 entry should exist. It does not. HOWEVER: git history is squashed to a single commit (9c5d972) so run history is not recoverable, and HEAD was committed at 06:32 UTC — only 15 minutes after the cron fires — so the run may simply not have completed. NOT VERIFIED either way.
findings.userImpact: If the workflow has stopped, the repository's only designed detector for that is the absence of an entry, and nothing actively alerts on absence.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a staleness check on hill_scope_masters.json:updatedAt to an existing health workflow, so 'the refit stopped running' produces a signal rather than a silence.

notes:
METHOD AND REPRODUCTIONS. Everything below was produced by running code against the repository at 9c5d972. Nothing in the repository was created, modified or deleted.

1. Hill formula reproduction. percentile_to_value with the live OFFENSE pair at N=500 reproduces the tripwire's ten pinned values exactly: rank 1 -> 9999, 5 -> 9481, 12 -> 8561, 24 -> 7242, 50 -> 5314, 100 -> 3419, 150 -> 2481, 200 -> 1931, 300 -> 1322, 400 -> 996. It also confirms the tail clamp: rank 500 -> 794 and rank 800 -> 794 (identical). tests/canonical/test_ktc_reconciliation.py's PINNED_DELTAS carries the same ten numbers, so the tripwire's cross-file link is currently satisfied.

2. Holdout criterion reproduction on today's CSVs. Champion (0.1100, 1.110) -> 799.4823 {FantasyCalc 776.8 n=399, FantasyNavigator 1148.5 n=400, OTCFFB 1030.2 n=400, PFKDynasty 242.3 n=400, nothing skipped}. Retired v1 (0.118, 1.17) -> 838.4392. The registry's stored v2 figure is 787.8416. Same parameters, 11.6-point drift in seven days.

3. Full fit re-run on today's data: OFFENSE c*=0.1080 s*=1.110, GLOBAL c*=0.1120 s*=0.725 (unchanged), IDP c*=0.0850 s*=0.935, ROOKIE c*=0.1290 s*=0.860. Driver drift metric: GLOBAL 0.00, OFFENSE 34.34, IDP 326.57, ROOKIE 275.52. The gate would open on IDP drift and be decided by a 22.4-point OFFENSE improvement that misses the 25-point margin: verdict REJECTED, exit 0, challenger recorded.

4. Criterion surface search over c in [0.060, 0.200] x s in [0.60, 2.00]: optimum c=0.071, s=1.20 at criterion 480.02, which is 319 points better than the champion.

5. Train/holdout player overlap, top-400 by normalized name: FantasyCalc 395/399 (99.0%), OTCFFB 393/398 (98.7%), PFKDynasty 399/400 (99.8%), FantasyNavigator 362/400 (90.5%), against a training union of 598 distinct names.

6. Runtime curve routing, enumerated from the live _RANKING_SOURCES: GLOBAL = {idpTradeCalc, draftSharks, draftSharksIdp}; IDP = {dlfIdp, dlfRookieIdp, idpShow, fantasyProsIdp}, all rank-signal; OFFENSE = the remaining fourteen, of which only ktcSfTep is value-direct.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY.
- pytest is not installed in this environment, so no test was executed. Every test claim in this report comes from reading the test source; where the assertion was arithmetic I reproduced it by hand (the tripwire's ten values and its PINNED_DELTAS cross-check both pass).
- Git history is squashed to one commit, so workflow run history, promotion history and CSV publish history are Not Verifiable from Repository. CSV mtimes reflect checkout and refresh times, not vendor publishes; I used the registry's content fingerprints instead, which is precisely what they exist for.
- The 30-snapshot paired-delta noise study quoted in promotion.py:9-29, the sole justification for PROMOTION_MARGIN=25.0, is not in the repo. Not Verifiable.
- The calibration sweep history in calibration.py:39-43 references calibration_sweep.py, which is not in the repo. Not Verifiable.
- normalization_validator.py:18-26 claims three consumers; I verified only server.py:4292 (/api/status). The claimed data_contract.py build-time call and /api/admin/normalization/check endpoint were not located.

WHAT SURPRISED ME, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.
This is the most self-aware subsystem in the repository. holdout.py refuses to score when the split is violated, by label AND by file path, and refuses to report a pass when no board is scorable. promotion.py gives ties to the incumbent and treats an unmeasured champion as unknown rather than beaten. versioning.py records missing training inputs rather than omitting them, for a stated reason. hill_masters.py:167-173 keeps the file writer physically unreachable from the refit, and a test asserts the driver cannot even import it. board_holdout.py volunteers its own limits before anyone asks. The documented human gating is real: I traced it, and the workflow commits nothing but the registry JSON.

And yet the thing all that machinery protects is a criterion built from the pipeline's own inputs, pointing in a direction the pipeline explicitly rejected for those same inputs. The guard rails are excellent; they are guarding a measurement that cannot answer the question it is asked. holdout.py:33-40 gets halfway there, saying the criterion measures generalization rather than accuracy, but it never says the four boards are blend sources, and CLAUDE.md drops even that. The honest one-line summary for a reader is: this curve reproduces the shape of four retail boards, four boards whose ranks we also vote into our own board, and nobody has measured whether any of it is right.

ADDITIONAL DOC-VS-CODE DISAGREEMENTS (the first three are filed as findings; the rest are listed here for completeness):
- src/model_registry/__init__.py:396-400 describes the removed autonomous-commit path in the present tense, and its Modules list omits board_holdout and hill_masters.
- scripts/fit_hill_curve_from_market.py directs the reader to update constants a different script now owns, and prints a baseline (45.00 / 1.100) that has not been live for some time.
- scripts/backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py:19-20 still names 48.44/1.149 and 69.50/0.945 as the live rank-form constants; player_valuation.py:82-83 and :102-103 say 65.4/0.910 and 64.6/0.900.
- src/scoring/tiering.py:19 points at scripts/fit_tier_thresholds.py, which does not exist; config/tiers/thresholds.json:1 explicitly corrects this and names refit_tier_thresholds.py. The config is right and the module docstring is stale.
- scripts/fit_hill_curve_percentile.py:5-6 still calls value-based sources 'the training set for the rank-to-value conversion system', which stopped being an accurate description of the blend on 2026-04-22 and 2026-07-25 when six sources moved to the rank path.
- Worth preserving, not fixing: player_valuation.py:146-157 (ROOKIE is not routed) and :88-101 (the offense/IDP rank-form split is not evidence of two economies) are unusually good self-corrections that a future tidy-up should leave alone.

DEAD OR DORMANT CODE CONFIRMED: src/canonical/confidence_intervals.py and src/canonical/rank_history_band.py (no production importer, flag off, badge mounted nowhere); src/scoring/tiering.py and config/tiers/thresholds.json (no production importer — Dynasty Scraper.py:67 imports from src.scoring but not tiering, and src/scoring/__init__.py does not export it); src/canonical/calibration.py (reachable only through suggestions.build_asset_pool, documented at suggestions.py:378-383 as the legacy non-production entry point); scripts/fit_hill_curve_from_market.py; scripts/refit_tier_thresholds.py (no input, no scheduler); the ROOKIE Hill master (fit weekly, routed nowhere); idp_backbone.coverage_weight (mathematically inert at every currently registered depth).
