formulas.name: Finder arbitrage score
formulas.expression:
board_gain_norm = board_delta / max(give_model, 1)
arbitrage = board_gain_norm*50 + opp_appeal*30 + 10*(board_delta > 0)
if coverage == "partial": arbitrage = min(arbitrage*0.3, 8.0)
confidence = min(1, mean(source_count)/5) * (1.0 if full else 0.7)
arbitrage *= 0.7 + 0.3*confidence
arbitrage += min(1, min(give_model,recv_model)/5000) * 5
arbitrage += -(len(give)+len(receive) - 2) * 3
arbitrage += roster_fit_bonus   # +1.0 per shed-surplus give, +1.5 per fill-need receive
formulas.inputs: board_delta and give_model in board points (rankDerivedValue); opp_appeal dimensionless ratio; source_count from players[name]["_sites"] (an integer 1-3 on live data, NOT the 1-14 blend count)
formulas.constants: 50 board-edge weight, 30 ktc-appeal weight, 10 positive bonus, 0.3 partial demotion, 8.0 partial cap, 5 CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE, 0.7 partial-coverage confidence, 0.7/0.3 confidence floor+slope, 5000 value-scale divisor, 5 value-scale weight, 3 per-piece simplicity penalty, 4/1 ROSTER_SURPLUS/WEAK thresholds. All hand-picked; no calibration artifact exists in the repo.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: source_count==0 for every asset → source_confidence hard-coded to 1.0 (finder.py:745-747, "Unknown source counts — assume reasonable"). Missing market value → asset dropped by the top-N gate before scoring. Missing board value → asset dropped entirely (finder.py:432-434).
formulas.mathIssues: The board-edge term dominates. Measured over 449 live results across all 12 teams: median boardEdge 15.97 vs median ktcAppeal 2.12; the opponent-appeal term contributes a median 7.1% of the pre-multiplier score. An arbitrage score should be gated by opponent appeal, not swamped by own-side gain — this ranking systematically promotes the MOST lopsided proposal that clears the opp_appeal>0 sign gate. Separately, source_count reads `_sites` (max 3 live) instead of `sourceCount` (max 14), so source_confidence ≤ 0.6 for every asset and the confidence multiplier is a constant 0.88 with the tier constant "moderate" — a field that carries zero information.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Finder opponent appeal
formulas.expression:
opp_appeal = (give_market_total - recv_market_total) / max(recv_market_total, 1)
reject if opp_appeal <= 0   # "opponent must STRICTLY WIN"
formulas.inputs: market totals in KTC/IDPTradeCalc points, AFTER the monkey-patched package Value Adjustment has been added to one side
formulas.constants: none
formulas.missingDataBehavior: partial coverage → unpriced assets contribute 0 to the sum, so a package with one unpriced piece understates its own side and can manufacture appeal. Reachable only when market_top_n=0.
formulas.mathIssues: The give_market_total this reads is not the raw market sum. finder_value_adjustment.py:44 clones the largest give asset with `market_value = value + adjustment`. On the live top result (give Josh Allen, receive Burrow + Mahomes) raw give KTC = 9,987 and receive = 13,702 — the opponent is losing 3,715 points — but VA adds +3,863 to the give side, yielding 13,850 vs 13,702 and opp_appeal = +0.011. The gate is satisfied entirely by the adjustment.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Finder multi-for-one guards (one-directional)
formulas.expression:
if len(give) > len(receive):
    reject if give_model < recv_model * 0.55            # MULTI_FOR_ONE_MIN_RATIO
    if max(recv) >= 6600: reject if give_model < recv_model * 0.65   # ELITE_MULTI_MIN_RATIO
    reject if max(give) < max(recv) * 0.35             # PACKAGE_ANCHOR_MIN_PCT
formulas.inputs: board-scale model values
formulas.constants: 0.55, 6600 (ELITE_THRESHOLD, rescaled from 7500 by k=0.875), 0.65, 0.35
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a
formulas.mathIssues: The entire guard block is inside `if len(give) > len(receive)`. The opposite shape — give 1, receive 2 — has NO ratio guard, NO elite guard and NO anchor guard. Live consequence: across all 12 teams the engine returned 441 1-for-2 trades and 8 1-for-1 trades, and ZERO 2-for-1 trades. The guarded direction is extinct; the unguarded direction is 98.2% of output.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Finder threshold rescaling from composite to board scale
formulas.expression:
BOARD_TO_COMPOSITE_K = 0.875 (median board/composite over 803 paired assets)
MIN_ASSET_VALUE = round(800 * 0.875) = 700
MAX_BOARD_LOSS  = round(-200 * 0.875) = -175
JUNK_THRESHOLD  = round(400 * 0.875) = 350
ELITE_THRESHOLD = round(7500 * 0.875) = 6562 → shipped as 6600
_MIN_ASSET_VALUE_COMPOSITE_SCALE = round(700 / 0.875) = 800
formulas.inputs: the pre-migration composite-scale constants
formulas.constants: k = 0.875 (p10 0.775, p90 1.056), regenerable with scripts/measure_engine_value_divergence.py
formulas.missingDataBehavior: MIN_MARKET_VALUE (500) deliberately NOT rescaled because it gates retail values
formulas.mathIssues: 6600 is not 7500*0.875 (=6562.5); it is rounded up past the stated method. Minor, but the comment claims "scale by the measured k, then round". MIN_ASSET_VALUE is compared against `model_value` at finder.py:818/832/852, not against the offense-only value used in scoring — a small scale inconsistency in the gate vs the score.
formulas.validated: the k measurement is cited but the measuring script's output is not committed in the repo

formulas.name: KTC package Value Adjustment (processV core)
formulas.expression:
processV(v, maxInTrade, t, nerfIndex) =
  (0.05*(v/t)^1.3 + 0.05*(v/(1.05*maxInTrade))^6 + 0.1) * v
  * (max(0.6, 1 - 0.15*nerfIndex) if nerfIndex > 0 else 1)
t = 10041 (KTC_T_REFERENCE), max player value 10000, variance gate 5%.
Display suppressed if 1-for-1, or |value|/(total1+total2) < 0.033.
formulas.inputs: raw per-piece values on a 0-10000 scale
formulas.outputRange: integer points added to one side
formulas.constants: 0.05, 1.3, 0.05, 6, 0.1, 0.6, 0.15, t=10041, 10000, 5% variance, 3.3% display floor. Lifted verbatim from keeptradecut.com/js/site.min.js — reverse-engineered, not derived.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: values ≤ 0 are filtered out of both lists; empty side → KtcVAResult.empty()
formulas.mathIssues: Two full copies of a 300-line iterative solver in one package (src/trade/ktc_va.py and src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py) with only ktc_va pinned by the 139-trade parity fixture. Verified numerically that both return 3863 for give=[9987], recv=[7395,6307], so they currently agree — but nothing enforces that they keep agreeing.
formulas.validated: tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py runs 139 observed KTC trades through Python and JS and asserts ±1 agreement. This validates FIDELITY TO KTC, not correctness of KTC's premium as a dynasty-value model.

formulas.name: Suggestions fairness gap (VA-adjusted)
formulas.expression:
gap = round(give_adj − recv_adj) where (give_adj, recv_adj) = ktc_va.adjusted_pair_totals(give_pieces, recv_pieces)
fairness = "even" if |gap| < 256, "lean" if |gap| < 769, else "stretch"
formulas.inputs: individual board display values (0-9999), NOT pre-summed
formulas.constants: 256 and 769 (FAIRNESS_TOLERANCE). The in-file comment at :153-160 states 769's origin is "undocumented legacy tuning". 256 is undocumented entirely.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: an empty side returns raw sums with zero VA
formulas.mathIssues: Verified numerically: give=[3000,2600] recv=[5400] has raw gap +200 but va_gap = −2258 and label "stretch"; give=[4000,1000] recv=[5200] has raw gap −200 but va_gap = −2504. The VA can invert the sign and inflate magnitude by an order of magnitude. The serializer at suggestions.py:1767-1769 then emits giveTotal=5600, receiveTotal=5400 and gap=−2258 in the same object — three numbers that do not reconcile for any reader.
formulas.validated: tests/test_trade_suggestions.py:180-192 pin only the label boundaries (255→even, 500→lean, 800→stretch), not the VA behavior

formulas.name: Suggestion rank score
formulas.expression:
rank_score = min(give_total, receive_total)/1000
           + {even:3.0, lean:1.0, stretch:0.0}[fairness]
           + {high:2.0, medium:1.0, low:0.0}[confidence]
           + need_severity (2.0 if starter_count==0 at a needed pos, else 1.0 if below need)
           + {market_discount:1.5, market_premium:1.0, high_dispersion:0.5}[edge]
           + 1.5 if opponent_fit
           − 1.0 per received asset at a surplus position
formulas.inputs: board points, category labels
formulas.missingDataBehavior: roster=None → need_severity and overflow_penalty both 0; missing edge → 0
formulas.mathIssues: need_severity and overflow_penalty at :882 and :921 read DEFAULT_STARTER_NEEDS, not the league-aware starter_needs that reached analyze_roster. A dynasty_new user (1 TE, no IDP) gets need severity scored against dynasty_main's 2 TE + 9 IDP lineup.
formulas.validated: none found — no backtest of whether higher rank_score correlates with anything

formulas.name: Confidence tier from source count
formulas.expression: high if source_count >= 6; medium if >= 3; low otherwise
formulas.inputs: len of post-Hampel effective source values (suggestions.py:602-621 — uses sourceRankMeta[key].valueContribution when present, else the raw canonicalSiteValues slot)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no sources → 0 → "low"
formulas.mathIssues: This is the correct field (the board's blend count, live max 14) — unlike finder.py:419 which reads the scraper's `_sites` (live max 3) for the same concept. Two engines, one concept, two incompatible answers.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Suggestions market-dispersion edge
formulas.expression:
CV = population_stdev(effective source values) / mean
HIGH_DISPERSION_CV = 0.12, LOW_DISPERSION_CV = 0.04
market_discount  if max(recv CV) >= 0.12 and gap < 0
high_dispersion  if max(recv CV) >= 0.12 and gap >= 0
market_premium   if mean(give CV) <= 0.04 and mean(recv CV) >= 0.096
market_premium   if max(give CV) >= 0.12 and gap > 0
formulas.inputs: per-source value contributions on the 0-9999 scale
formulas.missingDataBehavior: fewer than 2 sources or mean ≤ 0 → CV None → the asset contributes nothing to the edge test (suggestions.py:305-314)
formulas.mathIssues: `gap` here is the VA-adjusted gap, so a consolidation package's VA can flip market_discount ↔ high_dispersion for the identical underlying dispersion. The thresholds 0.12/0.04 are asserted, not fitted.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Angle arbitrage score (single-player)
formulas.expression:
my_gain_pct     = 100 * (my_val_target − my_val_selected) / my_val_selected
market_gain_pct = 100 * (market_val_target − market_val_selected) / market_val_selected
keep if my_gain_pct >= 5.0 and market_gain_pct <= 5.0
arb_score = my_gain_pct − market_gain_pct
formulas.inputs: my_val from rankDerivedValue; market_val from canonicalSiteValues[idpTradeCalc] for DL/LB/DB, [ktcSfTep] (falling back to [ktc]) otherwise
formulas.constants: min_my_gain_pct 5.0, max_market_gain_pct 5.0, limit 50 — all defaults in the signature, overridable per request
formulas.missingDataBehavior: _value_pair returns None when either value is missing or ≤ 0 → candidate silently skipped (angle.py:340-345). The SELECTED player missing a value produces an explicit warning and an empty candidate list — a genuine refuses-to-answer path.
formulas.mathIssues: When the selected player is offense and a candidate is IDP (or vice versa), market_gain_pct differences an idpTradeCalc number against a ktcSfTep number. The module docstring at angle.py:69-72 says the 1-for-1 path is fine because "there is no cross-market sum to constrain" — but a DIFFERENCE across two markets carries the same exchange-rate risk as a sum, and the package path explicitly quantifies that risk with an uncertainty_band which this path does not compute. The ±5% gate is narrower than the p10-p90 cross-board disagreement (0.888-1.054) the codebase itself documents.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Angle package arbitrage (VA-adjusted, single-market)
formulas.expression:
(counter_my_adj, offer_my_adj, ...) = ktc_va.adjusted_pair_totals(counter_my_values, offer_my_values)
my_gain_pct = 100*(counter_my_adj − offer_my_adj)/offer_my_adj ; reject if < 5.0
counter_pkg = cross_market.value_package(rows)   # ONE market or nothing
(counter_mkt_adj, offer_mkt_adj, ...) = ktc_va.adjusted_pair_totals(counter_market_values, offer_market_values)
market_gain_pct = 100*(counter_mkt_adj − offer_mkt_adj)/offer_mkt_adj ; reject if > 5.0
reject if not compare_packages(restate(counter), restate(offer), gate_pct=5.0).verdict_certain
arb_score = my_gain_pct − market_gain_pct
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue for my-side; cross_market.value_package normalized market values for market side
formulas.constants: 5.0 / 5.0 gates; candidate_pool_per_team 25; per_team_limit 4; limit 50; target sizes {N-1, N, N+1}
formulas.missingDataBehavior: a package no single market prices is EXCLUDED and counted in market_diagnostics.unvaluable with a reason; a verdict inside the uncertainty band is WITHHELD and counted in withheld_uncertain. Both surface as user-visible warnings via _diagnostic_warnings (angle.py:298-312).
formulas.mathIssues: Both sides can still land on different markets (offense-only offer on KTC vs IDP-bearing counter on IDPTC) — acknowledged in the docstring and carried into the uncertainty band rather than hidden. This is the only engine in the subsystem that propagates its own uncertainty into an accept/withhold decision.
formulas.validated: the cross-market exchange rate cites pooled IDPTC/KTC ratio 0.9997, Spearman 0.990, n=476 — a real measurement, though I could not locate the script that produced it in this tree

formulas.name: Trade simulator equity and aggregate delta
formulas.expression:
equity = Σ value(receiving) − Σ value(sending)
totalValue = Σ value(assets)
tier bucket: elite ≥ 8500, high ≥ 6500, mid ≥ 3000, else depth  (src/api/terminal.py:48-53)
value = offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue when the whole trade is offense+picks, else rankDerivedValue
formulas.inputs: board points
formulas.constants: tier cutoffs 8500 / 6500 / 3000
formulas.missingDataBehavior: unresolved names are returned in unresolvedIn / unresolvedOut and contribute nothing — a genuine, explicit non-answer. Offense-only mode is suppressed when NO name resolves, to preserve terminal parity.
formulas.mathIssues: equity is a pure value sum with NO roster-spot cost, NO starter-slot legality and NO consolidation premium. A 3-for-1 that dumps three bench pieces for one starter has the same equity as a 1-for-1 of equal totals. The roster-shape correction lives entirely in the optional teamImpact block, which is skipped whenever roster_settings is absent (trade_simulator.py:271).
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Team impact fit score and verdict
formulas.expression:
fit_raw = Σ_active_pos [ 1.0*Δstarter_value[p]
                       + 0.25*(after_has_depth − before_has_depth)*avg_starter_val[p]
                       − 0.6*max(0, Δoverflow[p])*avg_starter_val[p] ]
fit_score    = clamp(100*fit_raw/4000, -100, 100)
equity_score = clamp(100*equity/2500, -100, 100)
composite    = 0.55*fit_score + 0.45*equity_score
verdict: accept ≥ 20, lean accept ≥ 8, neutral > -8, lean decline > -20, else decline
overflow cap per position = int(starters[p] + flex_share(p)) + 1
formulas.inputs: resolved asset dicts with board values and basePos; league rosterSettings
formulas.constants: config/trade/team_impact.json — fillStarter 1.0, depth 0.25, overflow 0.6, fitNormalization 4000, equityNormalization 2500, 0.55/0.45 composite split, thresholds 20/8/-8/-20. Hand-picked priors; the JSON carries schemaVersion 1 and no calibration provenance.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: returns None (no verdict at all) when rosterSettings has no starters dict — a correct refuses-to-answer path. avg_starter_val defaults to 1500.0 when a position has no starters.
formulas.mathIssues: equityNormalization 2500 means a 2,500-point equity swing saturates equity_score at 100, i.e. roughly one mid-tier player pins the equity half of the verdict. windowFit is computed at :443-449 AFTER composite and is never added to it, yet _rationale (:334) says its bullets are "ranked by absolute contribution to verdict" and emits a windowFit bullet weighted |window_fit|*1000 — the highest weight in the bullet list. The rationale therefore ranks a factor that provably has zero verdict weight above factors that have some. _rationale:364 also labels the board-value equity "Net KTC equity"; it is not KTC.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Team impact posture classifier
formulas.expression:
contend_index = top10_starter_value_share − (pick_value_share + young(≤23)_value_share)
contender if > 0.15 ; rebuilder if < -0.15 ; else balanced
formulas.inputs: before-trade asset values and ages
formulas.constants: 0.15 threshold, youngStarterMaxAge 23, primeStarterMinAge 24, primeStarterMaxAge 29
formulas.missingDataBehavior: total_value defaults to 1 when the roster is empty, so contend_index becomes top10_share = 0 → "balanced". Players with no age contribute 0 to young_share, biasing toward "contender".
formulas.mathIssues: top10_share and (pick_share + young_share) overlap — a young top-10 starter is counted in both terms with opposite signs, so the index is not a partition. On a full 53-man roster top10_share is mechanically large (top 10 of 53 by value), which biases every team toward "contender" before ages are even read.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Monte Carlo triangular draw
formulas.inputs: p10/p50/p90 and a correlated uniform u
formulas.constants: the 0.10 / 0.50 / 0.90 knots and the linear tail extrapolation
formulas.missingDataBehavior: a band of (0,0,0) draws 0 for every u
formulas.mathIssues: Verified numerically over 200,000 draws with p10/p50/p90 = 4250/5000/5750: E[draw] = 4999.2 (unbiased), sd = 642.6, empirical p10/p90 = 4251/5751. The quantiles are honored. The problem is entirely upstream — see the next entry.
formulas.validated: tests/trade/test_monte_carlo.py:138 asserts only that u→0 goes below p10 and u→1 above p90

formulas.name: Monte Carlo value band (the actual variance source)
formulas.expression:
if row.valueBand.p50 exists: use it
else: p10 = 0.85*rankDerivedValue, p50 = rankDerivedValue, p90 = 1.15*rankDerivedValue
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue
formulas.missingDataBehavior: THIS IS THE ONLY PATH THAT EXECUTES. Measured on the rebuilt live contract: 0 of 1,092 rows carry a valueBand. src/api/feature_flags.py:59 already records that stamp_bands_on_players has no caller and value_confidence_intervals is OFF. The frontend caller replicates the same ±15% fallback client-side.
formulas.mathIssues: The ±15% is an invented constant with no relationship to observed source disagreement, even though the row carries a real `_marketDispersionCV` (A.J. Brown: 0.0232) that is ignored. Because every player gets the SAME relative width, the win probability is a deterministic monotone restatement of the percentage value gap. Measured (20,000 sims, seed 1, 1-for-1): gap 0% → winProbA 0.497; 2% → 0.545; 5% → 0.620; 10% → 0.727; 20% → 0.899; 30% → 0.980. Nothing probabilistic is being learned — a lookup table would give the same answer.
formulas.validated: none found. Not calibrated against anything. No backtest, no coverage check, no realized-outcome comparison exists in the repo.

formulas.name: Monte Carlo correlated latent
formulas.expression:
rho_t = clamp(same_team_rho, 0, 0.5) = 0.25 default
rho_p = clamp(same_pos_group_rho, 0, 0.5) = 0.10 default
idio_sd = sqrt(1 − rho_t − rho_p) = sqrt(0.65) = 0.8062
z_total = idio_sd*z_player + sqrt(rho_t)*z_team[team] + sqrt(rho_p)*z_pos[group]
u = Phi(z_total), clamped to [1e-6, 1−1e-6]
formulas.inputs: per-sim standard normals; team string; position_group
formulas.constants: 0.25 and 0.10 — the docstring at monte_carlo.py:23-33 calls them "coarse knobs" and "good enough for first cut". Not estimated from data.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: z_team.get(pl.team, 0.0) — a player with an empty/absent team gets zt = 0.0. Verified on the rebuilt contract: EVERY pick row has team = None, and MonteCarloButton.jsx:57 sends `team: r?.team || ""`.
formulas.mathIssues: For a teamed player Var(z_total) = 0.65 + 0.25 + 0.10 = 1.0, so u ~ U(0,1) and the band is preserved. For a team-less asset Var = 0.65 + 0.10 = 0.75, sd = 0.866, so u is concentrated toward 0.5. Measured over 200,000 draws: the effective sampling sd drops from 642.6 to 564.0 — picks are drawn 12.2% narrower than players. The docstring at :226-229 asserts "its marginal remains U(0,1) per player so the per-player band is preserved on average"; that claim is false for every pick in every trade. Net effect: any trade involving picks systematically understates the picks' uncertainty relative to the players.
formulas.validated: none found. tests/trade/test_monte_carlo.py:67 only asserts high.std_delta >= low.std_delta*0.95 — a test that passes even if correlation does nothing.

formulas.name: MC decision-layer risk and impact labels
formulas.expression:
range_width = |p90 − p10| ; prob_confidence = |winPct − 50|
risk = high if range_width > 3000 or prob_confidence < 10
       medium if range_width > 1500 or prob_confidence < 20
       else low
ratio = |raw_delta| / max(a_p50, b_p50, 1)
impact = significant > 0.25, moderate > 0.10, minor > 0.03, else even
adjusted_delta (no VA) = a_p50*(1 − 0.3*a_spread) − b_p50*(1 − 0.3*b_spread), spread = Σ(p90−p10)/Σp50
formulas.inputs: symmetrized sim output and the p50 sums
formulas.missingDataBehavior: missing deltaRange keys default to 0 → range_width 0 → risk driven by prob_confidence alone
formulas.mathIssues: With the invented ±15% band, spread = Σ(0.30*p50)/Σp50 = 0.30 for every side regardless of composition, so the no-VA adjusted_delta shrink factor is a constant (1 − 0.3*0.30) = 0.91 on BOTH sides and adjusted_delta = 0.91 * raw_delta. The "confidence weighting" is arithmetically a fixed rescale that cannot change any sign or any ordering. Likewise range_width is a fixed multiple of the value scale, so riskLevel is a restatement of trade size.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Waiver FAAB bid ladder
formulas.expression:
share = candidate_value / max(candidate_value, top_value_in_pool)
aggressive = max(1, round(budget * (0.05 + 0.25*share)))
reasonable = max(1, round(0.70 * aggressive))
lowball    = max(1, round(0.35 * aggressive))
formulas.inputs: board value, league budget (default 100), top pool value
formulas.missingDataBehavior: value ≤ 0 or budget ≤ 0 → (0,0,0)
formulas.mathIssues: Bid is a function of relative board value only — no contention, no roster need, no league bid history. Hand-picked coefficients; superseded in practice by faab_recommender but still shipped on /api/waiver/suggestions.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: FAAB recommender modifiers
formulas.expression:
value_mod clamped to [0.5, 1.8] from (add_value − drop_value)
trending kicker from _TRENDING_TIER_BREAKPOINTS
league calibration blended at 0.5 weight (_LEAGUE_CALIBRATION_BLEND)
environment scale targets 8% budget share, clamped [0.6, 1.6], requires ≥10 analyzed bids
dropoff gate 0.15 ; ceiling dropoff clamp/scale 0.5 / 0.5 ; pacing warn at 40% of budget
formulas.inputs: board values, Sleeper trending counts, league transaction history, optional KTC crowd FAAB map
formulas.constants: 0.5/1.8, 0.5 blend, 0.08 target share, 0.6/1.6 clamp, 10 min bids, 3 min position count, 0.15, 0.5, 0.5, 0.40
formulas.missingDataBehavior: compute_confidence (:116-148) downgrades the tier when factors are missing; contention is skipped with an explicit missing-factor note when the owner id is absent or unmatched (documented in the route docstring at server.py:4844-4853) — a real refuses-to-answer path
formulas.mathIssues: Every constant is a prior. _ENV_MIN_BIDS_ANALYZED=10 and _POSITION_CALIBRATION_MIN_COUNT=3 are genuine evidence gates and are the only such gates I found anywhere in src/trade/.
formulas.validated: none found in-repo

formulas.name: FAAB rival contention
formulas.expression:
rival_bid ≈ base * NEED_FACTORS[need_level] * aggression_factor(clamped [0.5,2.0]) * intel_factor (1.25 player / 1.10 position)
winning bid = max(rival estimates) * SAFETY_MARGIN 1.15, capped by STACK_CAP_MULT 2.5
formulas.inputs: data/intel/<league>.json snapshots, league bid history, contract positions
formulas.constants: NEED_FACTORS map, AGG_CLAMP (0.5,2.0), AGG_MIN_WINNING_BIDS 3, INTEL_PLAYER_FACTOR 1.25, INTEL_POSITION_FACTOR 1.10, STACK_CAP_MULT 2.5, SAFETY_MARGIN 1.15, INTEL_WINDOW_MS 14 days
formulas.missingDataBehavior: stale_inputs (:481) reports per-source staleness against STALENESS_MAX_AGE_S; a missing intel snapshot degrades the factor rather than the answer
formulas.mathIssues: Not verified — I did not find data/intel/ on disk in this checkout, so I could not confirm the intel leg has inputs. AGG_MIN_WINNING_BIDS=3 is an evidence gate.
formulas.validated: none found

findings.title: The trade finder receives no position data on the live path, so its per-market gate is inert and it is still offense-only — the exact regression WS-J F-3 claims to have fixed
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:477 `pos = _norm_pos(pdata.get("position", ""))`, fed from server.py:5947 `players = latest_contract_data.get("players")`. I rebuilt the live contract (build_api_data_contract on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json) and measured: `positions in contract players: [(None, 1092)]` — the legacy players dict carries no `position` key at all. Consequences measured on the real pool: `pool from CONTRACT players: 150 Counter({'ktcSfTep': 132, 'ktc': 18})`, `idp in pool 0`, `positions in pool [('', 125), ('PICK', 25)]`. find_trades metadata on the live payload: `"marketCoverage": {"ktcSfTep": 132, "ktc": 18, "idpTradeCalc": 0}`. Because pos is always "", finder.py:474 always selects OFFENSE_MARKET_KEYS, every defender scores market_value=None, and the top-N gate drops them before scoring — precisely the behaviour the constant's own comment at finder.py:110-131 says was fixed.
findings.userImpact: In a league with nine IDP starters, the arbitrage finder silently returns offense-only results while reporting `marketTopNFilter: 150` as though a uniform gate ran. Every IDP trade opportunity is invisible. CLAUDE.md states the opposite as settled fact.
findings.recommendedFix: Read the position from the contract's playersArray row (which does carry `position`), e.g. build a name→position map from `contract["playersArray"]` alongside `board_values_from_contract`, or have find_trades take the position map explicitly. Add a regression test that drives build_asset_pool from a fixture WITHOUT a `position` key and asserts IDP assets still route to idpTradeCalc.

findings.title: The finder's explicit IDP-blindness warning cannot fire, because it reads position from the same empty field
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:992-1004: `league_has_idp = any(_norm_pos(str((p or {}).get("position", ""))) in IDP_POSITIONS for p in players.values() ...)` followed by `if league_has_idp and idp_priced == 0: warnings.append("No IDP asset carries an IDPTradeCalc value ...")`. Since every `position` is None, league_has_idp is always False. Confirmed on the live payload: the returned warnings list was exactly `['187 assets carry a scraper value above 800 but no canonical board value, ...']` — the IDP warning was absent while idpTradeCalc coverage was 0.
findings.userImpact: The one safeguard designed to make this failure loud is disabled by the same defect it was written to catch. The user is shown an offense-only board with no indication anything is missing — the identical silent failure mode documented as resolved.
findings.recommendedFix: Derive league_has_idp from contract playersArray positions (or from the sleeper rosterSettings), not from the players dict. Assert the warning fires in a test that supplies a position-less players dict.

findings.title: The finder applies KTC's package Value Adjustment to the market side only, never to the board side — manufacturing arbitrage out of a scale asymmetry
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder_value_adjustment.py:44 `adjusted[index] = replace(adjusted[index], market_value=value + adjustment)` — only `market_value` is replaced; `model_value` is untouched, and finder.py:641-643 sums `_mv(a)` (the board value) raw. Live top result, verified end-to-end: give Josh Allen (board 9,993 / KTC 9,987), receive Joe Burrow + Patrick Mahomes (board 8,428 + 7,488 = 15,916 / KTC 7,395 + 6,307 = 13,702). rawGiveKtcTotal 9,987 → giveKtcTotal 13,850 after marketValueAdjustment +3,863; opponentKtcAppeal +0.011; boardDelta +5,923. Applying the SAME algorithm to the board values gives +1,820, which would cut boardDelta from 5,923 to 4,103. Across all 12 teams: 441 of 449 returned trades (98.2%) carried marketValueAdjustmentApplied.
findings.userImpact: The headline recommendation is "give Josh Allen, get Burrow AND Mahomes — you gain 5,923 board value and the opponent gains 1% on KTC." No manager accepts that. The engine's core comparison is between a consolidation-adjusted market total and an unadjusted board total, so the "gap" it reports is partly just the adjustment.
findings.recommendedFix: Either apply the VA symmetrically (adjust both model_value and market_value) or apply it to neither and state that the board is raw-sum. Whichever is chosen, add a test asserting the two scales receive the same treatment.

findings.title: The finder's multi-piece guards run only in the give-more direction; the 1-for-N direction is completely unguarded and is now 98% of output
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:665 `if len(give) > len(receive):` gates MULTI_FOR_ONE_MIN_RATIO (0.55), ELITE_MULTI_MIN_RATIO (0.65) and PACKAGE_ANCHOR_MIN_PCT (0.35). Nothing constrains `len(receive) > len(give)`. Measured across all 12 live rosters: package shapes returned were `Counter({'1-for-2': 441, '1-for-1': 8})` — zero 2-for-1s survived, and every 1-for-2 bypassed every ratio guard.
findings.userImpact: The engine has degenerated into a single recommendation template: "give your best player, receive two of theirs." The guards that exist to stop implausible packages protect only the shape the engine no longer produces.
findings.recommendedFix: Mirror the ratio/elite/anchor guards for the receive-heavy direction (recv_model must not exceed give_model by more than a plausibility ratio), and add a test asserting a 1-for-3 fire-sale is rejected.

findings.title: The trade-suggestions engine analyses a roster it can only see 10-40% of, and produces zero suggestions for 7 of 12 live teams
findings.evidence: suggestions.py:1614 `roster = analyze_roster(roster_names, pool, starter_needs)` is called with the ALREADY-FILTERED pool (server.py:5913 builds it with ktc_top_n=150). Measured on the live contract with dynasty_main starter needs, per team: Blaine roster=53 matched=5 total=0; Collin 58/10 total=0; Ed 57/10 total=0; Joey 58/10 total=0; Kich 58/9 total=0; Roy 51/7 total=0; Ty 56/7 total=0; jstuedle 44/5 total=0. Best case Brent 57/21 total=9. Every team is reported as "needing" DL/LB/DB because the top-150 board contains 7 DL, 8 LB and 0 DB. depthCounts came back all-zero for a 53-man roster.
findings.userImpact: The roster diagnosis is wrong in a specific direction: it tells a manager they have no depth anywhere and need every IDP position, because 48 of their 53 players are invisible to it. Seven of twelve managers get an empty feed with no explanation.
findings.recommendedFix: Run analyze_roster against the UNFILTERED contract pool (ownership and depth are facts about the roster, not about board quality), then apply BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER only when selecting trade TARGETS and give-side pieces. Return a diagnostic when totalSuggestions is 0 stating how many roster names resolved.

findings.title: Monte Carlo "win probability" is computed from an invented ±15% band that exists on zero live rows, and is uncalibrated against anything
findings.evidence: src/trade/monte_carlo.py:362-382: `band = row.get("valueBand") or {}` … fallback `p10=cv*0.85, p90=cv*1.15`. Measured on the rebuilt live contract: `any row with valueBand: False` (0 of 1,092). src/api/feature_flags.py:59 already records that `stamp_bands_on_players` has no caller. The frontend replicates the same fallback at MonteCarloButton.jsx:52-54. Because every asset gets the identical relative width, winProbA is a deterministic function of the percentage gap — measured at 20,000 sims, seed 1: 0% gap → 0.497, 2% → 0.545, 5% → 0.620, 10% → 0.727, 20% → 0.899, 30% → 0.980. Meanwhile each row DOES carry a real `_marketDispersionCV` (A.J. Brown 0.0232) that the simulator never reads.
findings.userImpact: "Side A won 90% of 40,000 simulations" is a restatement of "Side A is 20% ahead on value," dressed as a probabilistic result. The number deserves no independent weight in a decision, and the simulation adds no information the value delta didn't already carry.
findings.recommendedFix: Either stamp real bands (wire stamp_bands_on_players, or derive the band from the row's existing _marketDispersionCV / sourceRankSpread) or remove the probability framing and present the value delta directly. If the ±15% stays, label it in the payload as a synthetic constant, not as a consensus band.

findings.title: The frontend strips the Monte Carlo disclaimer the backend contract declares mandatory, and states the result exactly as the disclaimer forbids
findings.evidence: server.py:11199-11202: "The ``labelHint`` + ``disclaimer`` fields are PART OF THE CONTRACT — the frontend MUST render the disclaimer somewhere visible so users don't mis-read win probability as real-world odds." monte_carlo.py:17-18: "The UI MUST reflect this." frontend/components/ui/MonteCarloButton.jsx:18-20 states the opposite intent — "Output is rewritten in plain English — no 'Δ' / 'consensus-band samples'" — and _renderPlainSummary (:67-113) emits `Side A is the clear winner. Side A came out ahead in 92% of 40,000 simulations.` grep of the component finds no reference to `disclaimer` or `labelHint`.
findings.userImpact: The user is told a value-band sampling artifact is a win rate, in the exact phrasing the backend authors wrote a mandatory disclaimer to prevent.
findings.recommendedFix: Render `result.disclaimer` in the MonteCarloButton result card, or delete the contract claim from both docstrings so the code and the documentation stop disagreeing.

findings.title: League-aware starter needs reach only analyze_roster; nine other call sites hardcode the dynasty_main lineup while the response claims league awareness
findings.evidence: server.py:5871 computes `starter_needs = starter_needs_for_league(league_cfg.key)` and passes it through. suggestions.py:1614 forwards it to analyze_roster only. DEFAULT_STARTER_NEEDS is then read directly at :882 and :921 (rank_score need severity), :1026 (_generate_sell_high), :1107 (_generate_buy_low), :1156 (_generate_consolidation), :1241 and :1245 and :1286 (_generate_positional_upgrades), and :1383-1385 (_roster_balancer_candidates). Verified the two maps differ: dynasty_main {'QB':2,'RB':3,'WR':4,'TE':2,'DL':3,'LB':3,'DB':3} vs dynasty_new {'QB':2,'RB':3,'WR':4,'TE':1}. The metadata block at :1693 reports the league-aware map as `starterNeeds`.
findings.userImpact: For dynasty_new (1 TE, no IDP), the generators slice depth at TE with need=2, and _generate_positional_upgrades iterates DL/LB/DB positions the league does not start — while the response advertises the correct league lineup. The docstring at :61-92 explicitly frames this as the bug being fixed.
findings.recommendedFix: Thread `starter_needs` (or a resolved RosterAnalysis-carried copy) into all four generators, rank_score, and the balancer search. Extend tests/league_intel/test_registry_consumers.py to assert a dynasty_new run never emits a DL/LB/DB suggestion.

findings.title: Suggestion payloads report giveTotal, receiveTotal and gap that do not reconcile, because gap is VA-adjusted and the totals are not
findings.evidence: suggestions.py:1767-1769 emits `"giveTotal": s.give_total, "receiveTotal": s.receive_total, "gap": s.gap`, where give_total/receive_total are raw sums (e.g. :1194-1197) but gap comes from _va_gap (:776-792). Reproduced numerically: give=[3000,2600] recv=[5400] → raw difference +200, va_gap −2258, label "stretch"; give=[4000,1000] recv=[5200] → raw −200, va_gap −2504.
findings.userImpact: A user reading a consolidation suggestion sees "you give 5,600, you get 5,400, gap −2,258." The three numbers are mutually contradictory and the sign of the gap is the opposite of the arithmetic difference. There is no field explaining that a package premium was applied.
findings.recommendedFix: Emit `giveTotalAdjusted` / `receiveTotalAdjusted` and a `valueAdjustment` field alongside the raw totals, matching what the finder already does with rawGiveKtcTotal / adjustedGiveKtcTotal.

findings.title: Monte Carlo picks and any team-less asset are drawn 12% narrower than players; the docstring asserts the opposite
findings.evidence: monte_carlo.py:271 `zt = z_team.get(pl.team, 0.0) if rho_t else 0.0` — the teams set at :257 excludes falsy team strings, so a team-less asset gets zt=0. Var(z_total) is then 0.65 + 0.10 = 0.75 instead of 1.0, so u = Phi(z_total) is not uniform. Measured over 200,000 draws on a 4250/5000/5750 band: teamed sd 642.6 vs team-less sd 564.0 — 12.2% narrower. Verified that live pick rows carry `team = None` (rebuilt contract: `pick row team= None pos= PICK name= 2026 Early 1st`) and that MonteCarloButton.jsx:57 sends `team: r?.team || ""`. The docstring at monte_carlo.py:226-229 claims "its marginal remains U(0,1) per player so the per-player band is preserved on average."
findings.userImpact: Any trade involving draft picks — most dynasty trades — systematically understates the picks' uncertainty relative to the players, biasing the win probability toward whichever side holds the picks.
findings.recommendedFix: When a player has no team, fold the missing rho_t back into the idiosyncratic term (per-player idio_sd = sqrt(1 − rho_p − (rho_t if team else 0))), or assign every pick a synthetic unique team id. Add a test asserting the empirical marginal of u is uniform for a team-less player.

findings.title: The finder's confidence tier is a constant, because it reads the scraper's site count instead of the board's blend count
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:419 `source_count = _int_or_none(pdata.get("_sites")) or 0`. Measured on the rebuilt live contract: `_sites` distribution is {1: 526, 3: 439, 2: 109, None: 18} while the board's own `sourceCount` reaches 14 ({14: 209, 5: 123, 13: 39, ...}). With CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE=5, source_confidence is capped at 3/5 = 0.6, so confidence = 0.6 and the multiplier is a fixed 0.88. Every one of the 40 live trades returned confidenceMultiplier 0.88 and confidenceTier "moderate". The sibling engine reads the right field: suggestions.py:602-621 uses the post-Hampel effective source set.
findings.userImpact: The confidence label on every arbitrage recommendation is identical and therefore worthless as a discriminator, and it is understated — a 14-source consensus is reported as "moderate."
findings.recommendedFix: Read `sourceCount` (or len of effectiveSourceRanks) from the contract row, as suggestions.py does. Add a test asserting a 14-source asset scores high confidence.

findings.title: The finder's arbitrage score is 93% own-side gain and 7% opponent appeal — it ranks lopsidedness, not arbitrage
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:728-729 `f_board_edge = board_gain_norm * 50` and `f_ktc_appeal = opp_appeal * 30`. Measured over 449 live results across all 12 rosters: median boardEdge 15.97, median ktcAppeal 2.12, and the median share of the pre-multiplier score attributable to ktcAppeal is 7.1%. Because opp_appeal is already gated to >0 at :712, the term adds almost nothing after the gate.
findings.userImpact: Ranking is dominated by "how much do I win by," which for an arbitrage engine promotes the least acceptable proposals to the top. The engine's own top-5 on live data were all Josh Allen for two elite QBs.
findings.recommendedFix: Re-weight so opponent appeal is a first-class ranking term (or rank by min(board_edge, appeal_headroom)), and re-measure the score composition after the change.

findings.title: team_impact computes windowFit and ranks it as the top rationale bullet, but never includes it in the composite score or verdict
findings.evidence: src/trade/team_impact.py:439 `composite = cw_fit * fit_score + cw_eq * equity_score` — window_score is computed AFTER, at :443-449, and never added. Yet _rationale's docstring (:334) says "Top 5 bullets ranked by absolute contribution to verdict" and :357-361 emits a windowFit bullet weighted `abs(window_fit) * 1000` — the largest weight in the bullet list, ahead of `abs(equity) * 0.3`.
findings.userImpact: The explanation shown to the user leads with a factor that provably has zero influence on the accept/decline verdict, and buries factors that do.
findings.recommendedFix: Either add a compositeWindowWeight to config/trade/team_impact.json and include it, or drop the windowFit bullet from _rationale and correct the docstring.

findings.title: Two independent Python ports of KTC's package Value Adjustment coexist; only one is pinned by the parity fixture
findings.evidence: src/trade/ktc_va.py:52-349 and src/trade/market_value_adjustment.py:38-386 implement the same processV / reverseAdjust / adjustPackage algorithm with the same constants (10041, 10000, 5%, 3.3%). ktc_va is used by suggestions._va_gap, angle._adjusted_pair_totals and monte_carlo._apply_consolidation_adjustment; market_value_adjustment is used only by finder_value_adjustment. Only ktc_va is covered by the 139-trade parity fixture (tests/trade/test_ktc_va_python_port.py). Verified they currently agree: both return 3863 for give=[9987], recv=[7395,6307].
findings.userImpact: A future fix applied to one port silently makes the finder and the trade calculator disagree about the same trade — the exact failure ktc_va's docstring says it was created to prevent.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete market_value_adjustment.py and have finder_value_adjustment import from ktc_va, or add a test that asserts the two modules return identical results over the same 139-trade fixture.

findings.title: The finder's opponent-fit bonus and rationale text key on an empty position string, producing "fills  need" and a bonus on a meaningless bucket
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:1029-1043 builds `my_pos_counts[a.position]` and then awards `+1.0` per give asset at a position with count ≥ 4 and `+1.5` per receive asset at a position with count ≤ 1. On live data every non-pick asset has position "". Live output string, verbatim: `Roster fit: fills  need, fills  need.` and rankingFactors.rosterFitBonus 3.0 on the top-ranked trade.
findings.userImpact: A user-visible rationale renders with a missing word, and a 3.0-point score bonus is awarded on a bucket that means nothing. Downstream of the position defect, but visible on its own.
findings.recommendedFix: Fix the position source (see the first finding); additionally skip the fit bonus and the rationale phrase entirely when position is empty.

findings.title: The finder reports myRosterSize as the post-filter count, understating a 53-man roster as 4
findings.evidence: src/trade/finder.py:1074 `"myRosterSize": len(my_roster)` where my_roster comes from _resolve_roster against the top-150-filtered pool_by_name. Measured live: `myRosterSize: 4` for a team whose Sleeper roster has 53 players (resolved to Jalen Hurts, Josh Allen, Saquon Barkley, Tee Higgins).
findings.userImpact: A field named myRosterSize reads as "your roster has 4 players." It also hides how aggressively the top-150 gate has narrowed the search — the user cannot tell whether an empty result means "no arbitrage" or "the gate ate your roster."
findings.recommendedFix: Report both: rosterProvided and rosterEligibleAfterGate, as suggestions.py already does with rosterProvided / rosterMatched.

findings.title: find_angles applies a ±5% plausibility gate across two different publishers' boards, narrower than the boards' own documented disagreement
findings.evidence: src/trade/angle.py:465-467 computes `market_gain_pct = 100*(market_val_target − market_val_selected)/market_val_selected` where each value comes from _value_pair (:314-345), which selects idpTradeCalc for IDP and ktcSfTep otherwise. An offense selected player and an IDP target therefore difference a KTC number against an IDPTC number. The module docstring at :69-72 excuses this: "find_angles (the 1-for-1 pivot) is untouched: it compares two single assets, so there is no cross-market sum to constrain." The codebase's own measurement of the cross-board ratio is p10 0.888 to p90 1.054 (CLAUDE.md, finder.py:229-238) — i.e. ±10% routine disagreement, twice the width of the gate being applied.
findings.userImpact: Cross-market Angle candidates pass or fail a 5% plausibility test that cannot distinguish real market disagreement from the two boards disagreeing with each other. The package path computes an uncertainty_band for exactly this reason; the 1-for-1 path does not.
findings.recommendedFix: Route single-asset comparisons through the same cross_market.compare_packages uncertainty check the package path uses, or withhold cross-market single-asset candidates with a stated reason.

findings.title: _opponent_fit_label's two branches are identical, so the surplus condition is dead and "Strong bilateral fit" is emitted for a one-sided match
findings.evidence:
src/trade/suggestions.py:998-1003:
```
if opp_needs_my_give and opp_surplus_my_recv:
    fitting_teams.append(team_name)
elif opp_needs_my_give:
    fitting_teams.append(team_name)
```
Both arms append the same value, so the expression reduces to `if opp_needs_my_give`. `opp_surplus_my_recv` is computed at :995 and has no effect. The single-team message at :1010 then reads "Strong bilateral fit: {team} needs {pos} and could deal."
findings.userImpact: A trade partner who merely has a hole at the position you're selling is labelled a strong BILATERAL fit, even when they have no surplus at the position you want. The suggestion also earns a +1.5 rank bonus (rank_score:899) on that basis.
findings.recommendedFix: Emit a distinct label for the bilateral case and the one-sided case, and gate the +1.5 bonus on the bilateral one.

findings.title: Every finder test hand-supplies a position key the production payload does not have, so the live regression is structurally unpinnable by the existing suite
findings.evidence: tests/trade/test_finder_canonical_board.py:29 `def _player(composite, *, pos="WR", ...)` returns `{"position": pos, ...}`. tests/trade/test_finder_mixed_market.py:25-35 constructs Asset objects directly with position and market_source already set. tests/test_trade_finder.py:99, :159, :171, :188-198 all set "position" explicitly. No fixture in the tree omits it, and no test drives find_trades from a real or realistically-shaped contract.

findings.title: suggestions returns an empty feed with no diagnosis — there is no refuses-to-answer path
findings.evidence: src/trade/suggestions.py:1680-1698 returns the four category lists and a metadata block with assetPoolSize, boardTopNFilter, rosterMatched and rosterProvided, but never a warnings array or a reason. Measured live: 7 of 12 teams got totalSuggestions=0 with rosterMatched between 5 and 10 out of 44-58 provided. The finder, by contrast, does emit warnings (finder.py:963-1004) and angle emits market_diagnostics + _diagnostic_warnings (angle.py:298-312).
findings.userImpact: An empty feed reads as "your roster is fine, no trades to make." It actually means "the quality gate removed 90% of your roster before I looked at it." Those are opposite conclusions.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md states the finder's per-market gate, IDP warning and unpriced-asset count as verified facts; all three disagree with the code or the live data
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md "Trade Engines": (a) "finder.py … ktcSfTep for offense + picks, idpTradeCalc for IDP, each ranked within its own population" — contradicted by the measured live pool (idpTradeCalc coverage 0, all 150 assets on KTC). (b) "it now emits marketCoverage per market and warns explicitly when an IDP league has no priced IDP assets" — the warning is unreachable (finder.py:992). (c) "counted in metadata.assetsUnpricedByBoard — 202 on a real payload" — finder.py:928-938 says the corrected number is 189 and the live run returns 187.
findings.userImpact: Anyone reading CLAUDE.md to decide whether the IDP blind spot is closed will conclude it is. It is not.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the three claims, or fix the code so they become true. Prefer the latter for (a) and (b).

findings.title: Trade fairness is a plain value sum with no roster-spot cost, and the roster-shape correction is optional
findings.evidence: src/api/trade_simulator.py:256 `equity = sum(a["value"] for a in receiving) - sum(a["value"] for a in sending)`. The only roster-shape term is teamImpact, and trade_simulator.py:271 gates it on `if resolved_team and roster_settings:` — with no team or no league roster settings, the response carries equity and nothing else. In the finder, board_delta (finder.py:643) is likewise a raw sum with no roster-spot term; suggestions applies KTC's VA to the gap but its giveTotal/receiveTotal remain raw sums.
findings.userImpact: A 3-for-1 that consumes two extra bench spots grades identically to a 1-for-1 of the same totals whenever teamImpact is skipped. Consolidation cost is modelled only where KTC's VA happens to be applied, and that application is inconsistent across the three engines.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the roster-spot term explicit and always present: either fold a per-asset roster-slot cost into equity, or refuse to emit a fairness verdict without roster_settings (teamImpact already returns None correctly — the parent response should follow).

findings.title: correlation_matrix.py is a 170-line dormant module whose docstring presents it as feeding the Monte Carlo sampler
findings.evidence: grep across the repo for `correlation_matrix` / `build_matrix` returns exactly two files: the module itself and tests/trade/test_correlation_matrix.py. src/trade/monte_carlo.py does not import it. The module docstring (:1-40) says "This module builds a player-by-player correlation matrix that the Monte Carlo sampler can consume as an alternative to the two-scalar model" and describes Cholesky decomposition that no caller performs.
findings.userImpact: None directly — it is dead code. It costs review time and implies a richer correlation model exists in the live path than the two hand-picked scalars actually used.
findings.recommendedFix: Either wire it into simulate_trade behind an explicit parameter, or delete it and its test.

findings.title: /api/trade/simulate, /api/trade/simulate-mc and /api/trade/export-ktc have no Next bridge route while their siblings do
findings.evidence: frontend/app/api/trade/ contains only finder/, import-ktc/ and suggestions/. frontend/components/useTradeSimulator.js:45 fetches "/api/trade/simulate"; MonteCarloButton.jsx:132 fetches "/api/trade/simulate-mc"; frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:1215 fetches "/api/trade/export-ktc". deploy/nginx/chaseupside-proxy.conf:54 routes location /api/ to the backend, so these work in production but 404 under `next dev`.
findings.userImpact: Three trade features are unreachable in local development while three others work, with no note explaining the split.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the three bridge routes for parity, or document the production-only split in CLAUDE.md's frontend runtime section.

findings.title: team_impact's posture classifier double-counts young starters and is biased toward "contender" on full rosters
findings.evidence: src/trade/team_impact.py:238 `contend_index = top10_share - (pick_share + young_share)`. top10_share is the top-10-by-value share of a 50+ asset roster (mechanically large), and a young top-10 starter contributes to BOTH top10_share (positive) and young_share (negative), so the terms are not a partition. Players with no age contribute 0 to young_share (:232-236), biasing further toward contender.
findings.userImpact: posture is reported to the user and drives windowFit; a systematically mislabelled posture inverts the sign of every windowFit score. Mitigated only because windowFit is excluded from the verdict.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute the index over disjoint buckets (e.g. prime-age starter share vs pick+young share) and treat missing ages explicitly rather than as "not young."

findings.title: team_impact rationale labels board equity as "Net KTC equity"
findings.evidence: src/trade/team_impact.py:364 `bullets.append((abs(equity) * 0.3, f"Net KTC equity {equity:+d}"))`. The equity passed in comes from trade_simulator.py:256, summed over _row_value → rankDerivedValue, the blended board. It is not a KTC number.
findings.userImpact: The user is told a blended-board delta is a KTC delta, in a product that also surfaces genuine KTC numbers elsewhere. The same mislabelling pattern (ktcRank, ktcValue, ktcDelta, ktcCoverage) persists across the finder payload as deprecated aliases.
findings.recommendedFix: Rename the bullet to "Net board equity."

notes:
METHOD. I rebuilt the real production contract in the scratchpad by running `src.api.data_contract.build_api_data_contract` on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json (scrapeTimestamp 2026-08-04T03:56:40Z), then executed find_trades, generate_suggestions_from_pool and simulate_trade against it with the real 12-team Sleeper roster block. Every "measured" number below came from that, not from reading code.

WHICH ENGINES ACTUALLY OPTIMIZE (the direct answer).
NONE of them optimize. Every one is enumerate → filter → sort. Precisely:
- finder.py — enumerates 1-for-1, 2-for-1 and 1-for-2 over `my_tradeable[:30] x opp_tradeable[:30]` (finder.py:812-867), scores each independently, sorts by arbitrage_score, truncates to 40. No objective is maximized subject to constraints; the "constraints" are rejection predicates inside a per-candidate scorer. The `[:30]` slices are hard truncations of the search space with no optimality claim.
- suggestions.py — four hand-written templates, each with its own nested loops bounded by literals (`sell_candidates[:3]`, `targets[:5]`, `range(min(len,6)) x range(i+1, min(len,8))`), then a sort by rank_score and a chain of deletion filters. It is a rule engine.
- angle.py — the closest thing to constrained search: it enumerates `combinations(pool, size)` for size in {N-1,N,N+1} and applies two conjunctive gates (my_gain ≥ 5%, market_gain ≤ 5%) plus an uncertainty-certainty gate. That IS a feasibility search over a combinatorial space, but it still sorts feasible points by a score rather than optimizing one. Call it constraint satisfaction, not optimization.
- trade_simulator.py — evaluates ONE user-specified trade. No search at all.
- monte_carlo.py — evaluates one specified trade. No search.
- team_impact.project_starters (team_impact.py:96-135) is the only genuine optimizer in the subsystem, and it is a greedy one: fill slots in a fixed order (QB,RB,WR,TE,SFLEX,FLEX,DL,LB,DB,IDP_FLEX), highest value eligible asset first. Greedy slot-filling in that order is not guaranteed optimal — a high-value TE taken by the TE slot can leave the FLEX worse off than an alternative assignment. On a 53-man roster the error is usually zero, but nothing checks.

DOES THE FINDER'S ARBITRAGE PREMISE SURVIVE? Partly, and less than the code believes. Quantified three ways on the live payload:
(1) Direct: rankDerivedValue vs ktcSfTep over the 412 rows carrying both — Pearson 0.9817, Spearman 0.9782, ratio p10/p50/p90 = 0.790/0.915/1.056. For IDP vs idpTradeCalc (n=293): Pearson 0.9861, Spearman 0.9567.
(2) Leave-one-out: rebuilding the board with ktcSfTep disabled (`source_overrides={'ktcSfTep': {'include': False}}`) changes rankDerivedValue by a MEDIAN OF 12 POINTS (mean 24.6) over 808 common rows, with Pearson 0.99890 between the two boards. Dropping idpTradeCalc moves it by a median of 31 (mean 97.3), Pearson 0.99223. So the market anchor's own vote is NOT the source of the self-reference — its direct contribution to the board is ~0.2-0.5%.
(3) The real self-reference is that all 13 blend sources are retail market boards that track each other. The board is 0.98-correlated with the anchor even after the anchor's own vote is removed. Concretely: of 1,074 live players, the source-key combinations are {idpTradeCalc, ktc, ktcSfTep}: 439, {idpTradeCalc}: 375, {}: 235, {ktc, ktcSfTep}: 25 in the raw payload; coverageAudit.expectedSites is literally `{"offense": ["ktc"], "idp": ["idpTradeCalc"]}`.
So: the "gap" is the residual of a monotone re-ranking (percentile → Hill curve) of boards that agree at ρ≈0.98, not independent information. Over the 150-asset live offense pool the mean |board rank − market rank| is 7.64 (max 63), and 3.64% of ordered pairs produce the sign inversion the engine needs; the median inversion is worth 275 board points with 180 points of KTC appeal. That 275 sits well inside the ±10% cross-board disagreement (p10 0.888 / p90 1.054) the codebase itself documents as normal noise. The premise is not dead, but the effect size is at or below the measurement noise of the inputs — and the engine reports no uncertainty band on board_delta at all, unlike angle.py which does exactly that and withholds verdicts inside it.
Worse, on live data the observed arbitrage is not the residual at all: it is the KTC package Value Adjustment applied to one scale and not the other (see the Critical finding). Median board gain on returned trades was 40% of the give-side value — an order of magnitude above the 2-4% residual the rank disagreement can support.

ROSTER LIMITS / POSITIONAL LEGALITY / LEAGUE RULES.
- finder.py: NO roster-size check, NO positional legality, NO starter-slot awareness. The only roster term is a ±1.0/1.5 score nudge keyed on a position string that is empty in production. Its top live recommendation hands the user a third quarterback in a 1QB+1SFLEX league.
- suggestions.py: models starter demand (starter_needs_for_league correctly derives it from config/leagues/registry.json), but only analyze_roster receives it — nine other call sites hardcode dynasty_main's lineup. No roster-size cap; no check that a 2-for-1 frees a bench spot.
- angle.py: no roster legality whatsoever. It constrains package SIZE (N±1) but never positions or slots.
- trade_simulator + team_impact: the only pair that models legality properly — real slot eligibility (flexEligible / sflexEligible / idpFlexEligible from the registry), greedy lineup projection, overflow detection at needed+1, and _league_active_positions to avoid IDP false positives in non-IDP leagues. This is genuinely good work and it is the only place in the subsystem where league rules bind.
- monte_carlo: none. It compares two bags of values.

IS FAIRNESS A VALUE SUM? Yes, everywhere. equity (trade_simulator.py:256) and board_delta (finder.py:643) are raw sums. suggestions and angle route their gap through KTC's package VA, which is the only consolidation-cost model in the tree — and it is an artifact reverse-engineered from keeptradecut.com/js/site.min.js, not a dynasty-value model anyone validated. Roster-spot cost appears in exactly one place: team_impact's overflow term, `-0.6 * max(0, Δoverflow[p]) * avg_starter_val[p]`, which only runs when roster_settings is present.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY.
- Whether data/intel/ exists in production (absent here), so faab_contention's intel leg is Not Verified.
- Whether the cited cross-market measurements (median ratio 1.000 over 475 shared players; pooled IDPTC/KTC 0.9997, Spearman 0.990, n=476) are reproducible — scripts/measure_engine_value_divergence.py is referenced in finder.py:57 but I did not locate a committed output.
- Production behaviour of import/export-ktc (requires live KTC fetch).
- Whether frontend/app/arbitrage/page.jsx surfaces the confidence tier prominently (I confirmed it renders warnings verbatim and shows marketCoveragePercent / assetsUnpricedByBoard / mixedMarketTrades stat tiles).

WHAT SURPRISED ME.
- angle.py is a genuinely different quality of engineering from the rest. It refuses to price a package no single market covers, counts the refusals, propagates an uncertainty band through the VA restatement, and withholds verdicts that sit inside that band — with 17 tests that actually pin it. It is the only engine here whose numbers I would let influence a decision without qualification.
- The finder's documentation is unusually careful and self-critical (the F-3/F-6/F-7 notes are honest and specific), yet the fix it documents most proudly is inert in production for a reason no test could catch. The gap between the quality of the reasoning in the comments and the state of the live path is the single most striking thing in this subsystem.
- src/trade/__init__.py monkey-patches finder._score_trade at import time. Nothing in CLAUDE.md mentions it, and it turns out to be the dominant driver of what the engine returns.

DEAD OR NEAR-DEAD CODE FOUND: correlation_matrix.py (no caller), Asset.ktc_value / ktc_rank / has_ktc aliases, KTC_TOP_N_FILTER aliases in both engines, PARTIAL_KTC_ARBITRAGE_CAP, SINGLE_SOURCE_DISCOUNT (retained only for a pinning test), _assign_ktc_ranks / _apply_ktc_top_n_filter aliases, PlayerAsset.calibrated_value (always equal to display_value on the contract path), suggestions.build_asset_pool + generate_suggestions (legacy asset-dict entry points, tests only), the partial-coverage branch in _score_trade (unreachable unless market_top_n=0).

findings.title: BDVM has no projection data on disk — every endpoint is currently a 'no_projection_snapshot' stub, contradicting CLAUDE.md's '726 players priced'

Verified: `python3 -c "from src.bdvm.projections import latest_snapshot_path, SNAPSHOT_DIR; print(SNAPSHOT_DIR.exists()); print(latest_snapshot_path(2026))"` → `False` / `None`; same for 2025 and 2027. `src/bdvm/events.py:38 EVENTS_DIR` and `src/bdvm/service.py:57 VALUATION_DIR` also absent. `src/bdvm/service.py:281-296` then returns `{"status": "no_projection_snapshot", "players": [], "picks": []}`. `deploy/deploy.sh:676-678` records the same condition on production: "The BDVM refresh had never run once — `journalctl -u dynasty-bdvm-refresh` was empty and `data/bdvm/` did not exist — so `/api/bdvm/*` served nothing while the deploy reported success every time." CLAUDE.md asserts "scripts/bdvm_build_baseline.py writes a real snapshot (2,815 records for 2026) and the engine answers status: \"ok\" with 726 players priced".
findings.userImpact: Every BDVM surface (the /bdvm page, the /rankings and /draft "Fund gap" columns, /api/bdvm/trade-eval, the daily BDVM signal-alert emails) silently renders nothing. The failure is deliberately silent — `frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1179` gates the column on `bdvmIndex`, so a reader cannot tell "no gap" from "engine has no inputs". CLAUDE.md's numbers describe a state this repository cannot currently produce.

Correct the CLAUDE.md counts or mark them as "measured on prod 2026-07-27, not reproducible from a checkout".

findings.title: BDVM's 'exact league scoring' silently drops 6 active reception-band rules — WR fundamentals are ~15% understated, RB ~9%, QB 0%
findings.evidence: `src/nfl_data/realized_points.py:78-99 _SIMPLE_KEYS` has no entry for `rec_0_4`/`rec_5_9`/`rec_10_19`/`rec_20_29`/`rec_30_39`/`rec_40p`, and `compute_weekly_points` (`:323-420`) has no other branch for them. The live league card carries all six at nonzero rates: `rec_0_4=0.17, rec_5_9=0.42, rec_10_19=0.67, rec_20_29=0.92, rec_30_39=1.17, rec_40p=1.92` (exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json → sleeper.scoringSettings). `src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py::describe_gaps` on the live card returns them as UNSCORABLE: 'reception distance bands need play-by-play; weekly stats carry only a reception count'. Measured with the production scorer: a WR line 5rec/70yd/0.4TD/3.5FD scores 13.30; a typical depth mix adds ~0.48 pts/reception → 2.40 missing → 15.3% understated. RB (3 rec) 8.6%. QB 0.0%.
findings.userImpact: Every fundamental value, every replacement level, and every fundamental-vs-market gap is biased AGAINST pass-catchers and IN FAVOUR of quarterbacks, by ~15 percentage points of relative error. This is exactly the failure mode `scoring_coverage.py`'s own docstring warns about ('a partial correction to a relative quantity is a directional bias'). It propagates into BUY/SELL email alerts, the /rankings Fund-gap column, and the trade-eval verdict. `src/bdvm/scoring.py`'s module docstring claims the reuse means 'any league config that scores history correctly scores projections identically' — the premise (that this engine scores this league's history correctly) is false.
findings.recommendedFix: Either (a) wire `src/nfl_data/reception_depth.py` band histograms + `reception_shape_projection.py` into `compute_weekly_points` behind the existing `reception_scoring_fit` flag so the bands are estimated from a measured per-player depth shape, or (b) surface `describe_gaps(scoring_settings)` on the BDVM payload meta and on the /bdvm page so users see which of their league's rules the fundamental board cannot price. Do not leave it silent.
findings.affectedSystems: projection consensus, replacement levels, all trade values, gap/signal, alerts, in-season actuals

findings.title: STRONG_BUY is structurally unreachable in production — `gap_persisted_days` is never passed
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/market.py:200-208`: `persisted = gap_persisted_days is not None and gap_persisted_days >= int(th["gap_persistence_days"])` and STRONG_BUY requires `alpha > strong_buy_alpha and persisted and liquidity > strong_buy_min_liquidity`. The only production call site is `src/bdvm/service.py:557`: `signal = buy_hold_sell(market_out, params, p_collapse_1y=v.probs.get("p_value_collapse_1y"))` — no `gap_persisted_days`. So `persisted` is always False. `tests/bdvm/test_market_isolation.py:108` passes `gap_persisted_days=30` explicitly, so the test proves the function can emit STRONG_BUY but not that production ever does. Config keys `gap_persistence_days: 14` and `strong_buy_min_liquidity: 0.5` (config/bdvm/params_v1.json) are therefore dead.
findings.userImpact: The label set is asymmetric: STRONG_SELL fires (two paths, `market.py:216` and `:221`) while STRONG_BUY never can. `src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py:43` lists STRONG_BUY as actionable and the email template renders it — a state the system cannot enter. Users receive a sell-biased alert stream and reasonably read the absence of STRONG_BUY as 'nothing is a screaming buy'.
findings.recommendedFix: Either persist per-(player, league) gap history (a `bdvmGapHistoryByLeague` user_kv/state file, mirroring the alert-state pattern) and thread `gap_persisted_days` from `service.py:557`, or delete STRONG_BUY, `gap_persistence_days` and `strong_buy_min_liquidity` and say so. Add a test that runs the SERVICE (not `buy_hold_sell` directly) and asserts the reachable label set.
findings.affectedSystems: buy_hold_sell, BDVM signal alerts, /rankings Fund gap tint, /bdvm board

findings.title: STRONG_SELL fires on any negative alpha when p_collapse_1y > 0.5, bypassing the −900 threshold
findings.evidence:
`src/bdvm/market.py:216-220`:
```
if p_collapse_1y is not None and p_collapse_1y > 0.5 and alpha < 0:
    return {"signal": "STRONG_SELL", ...}
if alpha < float(th["strong_sell_alpha"]):   # -900
```
The collapse branch is evaluated BEFORE the magnitude threshold, so `alpha = -1` with `p_collapse_1y = 0.51` yields STRONG_SELL while `alpha = -800` with a healthy player yields only HOLD. `p_value_collapse_1y = 1 - p_starter_in_1y` (`engine.py:340`), and `p_starter_in_1y = S(1)·Φ((µ₁−R)/σ₁)`. On the reference archetypes the aging RB p4 has p_collapse=0.65 and the rookie WR p12 has 0.38 — i.e. any older or fringe player crosses 0.5 easily.
findings.userImpact: A near-zero mispricing on an aging or fringe player is reported with the model's most severe label, in an email. Combined with the previous finding (no STRONG_BUY), the signal distribution is systematically bearish in a way that has nothing to do with measured mispricing.
findings.recommendedFix: Require BOTH conditions to be material: gate the collapse branch on `alpha < sell_alpha` (−400) at minimum, or emit a distinct label (e.g. `SELL_COLLAPSE_RISK`) so a risk warning is not conflated with a large market-vs-model gap.

findings.title: Option-value surplus assumes ex-post lineup selection and awards positive value to below-replacement projections
findings.evidence:
`src/bdvm/surplus.py:32-37`: `E[max(0, X−R)] = (µ−R)·Φ(z) + σ·φ(z)`, `season_starter_value` multiplies by `games` (`:55`). The justification given at `surplus.py:6-7` is "You are never forced to start a below-replacement outcome" — but a fantasy lineup is set BEFORE the outcome is known, so `E[max(0, X−R)]` prices perfect foresight. Measured with production code (WR, R=6.15, G=17, σ from `sigma_fpg`):
```
µ=6.15 (exactly replacement): option 19.72   truncated 0.00
µ=5.00 (below replacement):   option  8.12   truncated 0.00
µ=8.00:                       option 44.38   truncated 31.45  (+41%)
µ=20.0:                       option 240.55  truncated 235.45 (+2%)
```
The premium is ~0% at the top of the board and unbounded near/below replacement, so it is a systematic re-ranking, not a level shift.
findings.userImpact: High-variance, low-mean assets are structurally overvalued relative to stable starters, and the size of the effect is set entirely by `cv_base` — an unvalidated prior. `surplus.py:8` calls this "the central V1 HYPOTHESIS, not a law" and the `surplusMode` ablation exists, but nothing has ever run the ablation against realized outcomes (see the validation finding), so the champion formulation is unjustified.
findings.recommendedFix: Either reframe the option as a season-level roster-drop option (and say so — the current per-game reading is not defensible), or price the weekly start decision on ex-ANTE information (`E[max(0, µ̂_w − R)]` over a forecast distribution of µ̂, not of the outcome). Until the ablation is run against realized data, expose `surplusMode` on the payload meta prominently and state that the champion is unvalidated.
findings.affectedSystems: engine.season_path, all trade values, replacement-relative rankings, ROS

findings.title: Rookie-pick values are a frozen prior table that is never anchored to the calibrated player scale, yet the two are summed in one CES package
findings.evidence: Player trade values are pool-calibrated: `src/bdvm/engine.py:227-233 calibrate()` sets `anchors[k] = max_DV / (target_top_value/10000)^(1/γ)` so the top asset always maps to 9800. Pick values are NOT calibrated: `src/bdvm/picks.py:69` `ev = (p_hit·v_hit + p_mid·v_mid)·cs·discount^years_out·premium`, with `v_hit`/`v_mid` read verbatim from `config/bdvm/pick_outcomes_v1.json` (whose own `_comment` calls it "explicitly the most placeholder-ish table in the whole model"). Measured: 1.01 balanced EV = 4984.0 = 50.9% of the top player; 1.06 = 2420.0 (24.7%); 1.12 = 1582.0 (16.1%). `src/api/bdvm_api.py:334-338` then feeds player `tradeValue[s]` and pick `distribution[s].ev` into the SAME `package_value` call at `:347-348`. Worked example: side A = [top player 9800] → 9800.0; side B = [1.01, 1.02, 1.03] → 10440.6; edge −640.6. Nothing establishes that a 1.01 is worth 51% of the #1 dynasty asset in this model's currency.
findings.userImpact: `POST /api/bdvm/trade-eval` (the "Fundamentals check (BDVM)" panel on /trade) returns a numeric verdict on any player-for-picks trade in which one side's numbers come from a calibrated model and the other side's come from a hand-written table. The verdict looks identical to a fully-modelled one.
findings.recommendedFix: Anchor picks to the model: value slot S as the strategy-discounted expectation over the model's own valuations of the rookie class that lands there (the rookie draft-slot prior machinery already exists in `src/bdvm/baseline.py::build_rookie_prior_records`). Until then, stamp `pickValueBasis: "prior_table_v1_unanchored"` on every pick entry and on `trade-eval`'s meta, and render it in `BdvmTradePanel`.

findings.title: Roster strategy capitals and the double-positive trade scan exclude picks entirely, despite the module claiming to produce 'pick capital'
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/roster.py:6` docstring: "produces, per roster: strategy capitals ... value-weighted age, pick capital, and a contend/retool/rebuild direction." But `analyze_rosters` builds `assets` only from `roster["playerIds"]` (`:154-171`); `roster["picks"]` is used solely for `"pickCount": len(roster["picks"])` (`:199`). `capitals` (`:172`) sums over `assets` only. The trade scan (`:272-286`) draws `a_assets`/`b_assets` from `ra["assets"]`, so no pick can ever appear in a proposed trade.
findings.userImpact: `nowFutureRatio = contender_capital / rebuilder_capital` (`:186`) is computed with all future draft capital deleted, which is precisely the quantity that distinguishes a rebuilder. That ratio drives `_directions_relative` → `strategy_for_direction` → which currency each side is scored in during the scan. `roster.py:66-74` even documents the resulting saturation ('EVERY roster's contender capital exceeds its rebuilder capital and all twelve rosters would read "contend"') and works around it with a league-median rescale instead of fixing the input. The scan can never suggest the most common real dynasty trade shape (veteran for picks).
findings.recommendedFix: Join `roster["picks"]` against `valuation_payload["picks"]` by pick name, add them to `assets` with `tradeValue = distribution[strategy].ev` and `group = "PICK"`, and include them in the scan's asset pool. Blocked on the pick-scale finding above — anchoring picks must come first or the capitals become incomparable across rosters.

findings.title: `liquidity` increases with market DISAGREEMENT and multiplies the gap into alpha — inverted semantics, and it silently rescales every signal threshold by ~0.38
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/market.py:88-96`: `liquidity = clip(0.35 + 1.6·dispersion, 0.2, 1.0)` where `dispersion` is documented at `:54` as a "0-1 cross-source disagreement proxy". More disagreement → higher 'liquidity'. The SAME dispersion is used in the opposite direction two lines later for market precision: `:165` `tau_market *= 1.0 - 0.5·dispersion`. Then `:157` `alpha = gap * liquidity`. Measured on the live export (`_marketDispersionCV`, n=839): min 0.0, p50 0.0208, p90 0.0882, max 0.249 — so liquidity is 0.35–0.75, median 0.383, and 45.2% of rows have dispersion EXACTLY 0.0 → liquidity 0.35. Thresholds are stated in alpha units (`buy_alpha: 400`, `strong_sell_alpha: -900`), so the effective gap thresholds are ≈ +1045 and ≈ −2350, and `strong_buy_min_liquidity: 0.5` is unreachable for 45% of the board even if STRONG_BUY were wired.
findings.userImpact: Two compounding errors. (1) Directionally, a player the market cannot agree on gets his mispricing AMPLIFIED into a stronger BUY/SELL rather than damped. (2) Numerically, the documented thresholds are ~2.6× tighter than the behaviour, so the BUY/SELL bands are far wider than an operator reading params_v1.json would expect.
findings.recommendedFix: Rename the quantity or invert it. If it means "how confident is the market price", use `clip(base − coeff·dispersion, lo, hi)`. Then re-derive `signal_thresholds` on the new alpha scale rather than porting them, and pin the empirical alpha/gap ratio in a test against a real contract fixture.

findings.title: Seven parameter sections in params_v1.json are never read; the most consequential leaves single-source projections with σ_source = 0
findings.evidence: `grep -rn <key> --include=*.py src/ scripts/ server.py` returns 0 hits for: `single_source_projection_sigma_mult` (1.5), `missing_projection_impute`, `equal_weight_shrinkage` (0.3), `trade_value_max` (10000), `lambda_market_fundamental` (0.0), `best_ball_buffer_bump` ({RB:0.5, WR:0.5}), `positions_true`. The σ one is load-bearing: `src/bdvm/projections.py:400-402` computes `var = Σ w·(fpg−µ)²/Σw`, which is exactly 0.0 for a single record, so `sigma_source = 0` and `engine.py:141 sigma_fpg(..., p.sigma_source, ...)` reduces to `CV·µ` with no cross-source term. With only the reconstructed baseline on disk, EVERY player is single-source. `best_ball_buffer_bump` also matters: the live league is `best_ball: 1` (exports/latest → sleeper.leagueSettings) and `league_config.py:210` reads it, but nothing applies the bump.
findings.userImpact: Uncertainty is understated exactly where it is largest (one proxy source), and because σ drives the option-value surplus, the understatement flows straight into value — the effect is largest for near-replacement players. In a best-ball league, replacement levels for RB/WR are set as if lineups were weekly, overstating everyone's surplus.
findings.recommendedFix: Either wire each key at its intended site (`sigma_source *= single_source_projection_sigma_mult` when `n_sources == 1`; `waiver_buffer[g] += best_ball_buffer_bump[g]` when `cfg.best_ball`) or delete them from the file. Add a test that asserts every non-`_comment` top-level key in params_v1.json is reachable, the same posture `src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py` takes for scoring keys.

findings.title: `risk_lambda` moves values by 1–2%: 'risk_neutral' is a near-duplicate of 'balanced' after anchoring, so the four strategy currencies are really three
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/engine.py:196`: `max(0.0, v - lam · 0.35 · disp)` where `disp = sqrt(Σ (d^t·σ_t·G_t·S_t)²)`. Measured on the reference archetypes: p1 raw DV 637.0, dispersion 221.1, penalty 7.7 = 1.2% of raw; p5 1.2%; p12 1.9%. After per-strategy anchoring (`calibrate`), `risk_neutral` (λ=0) vs `balanced` (λ=0.1) differ by 0.06%–2.56% in trade value across all 13 archetypes (p5 −0.00%, p1 +0.06%, p10 +2.56%). The `rebuilder` λ=−0.1 gives a symmetric ~1–2% BONUS.
findings.userImpact: The /bdvm strategy selector and the trade-eval 'every strategy currency' output present `risk_neutral` as a distinct lens; it is balanced ±1%. Users comparing the two learn nothing. Separately, the risk axis the model advertises does essentially no work — the strategy differences come entirely from `discount`, `horizon` and `usability`.
findings.recommendedFix: Either raise `risk_lambda_dispersion_coeff` until the axis is material and justify the level, or drop `risk_neutral` from the exposed currency list and note in the UI that the risk term is a ~1% adjustment. Pin the measured magnitude in a test so it cannot silently become material.

findings.title: `range.ceiling_p85` escapes the advertised 0–10000 scale (up to 19,843) and is rendered without a cap
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/engine.py:365-378` computes the ceiling by re-running the season path at `mu_shift_z = +1.0364` and passing the result through `to_trade_value`, which has no upper clamp (`:236-238`: `10000·(v/anchor)^γ`). Measured on the reference archetypes: p5 ceiling 19,843.4; p12 17,898.2; p1 16,058.5; p7 14,153.2 — every one of the 13 exceeds 10,000. `config/bdvm/params_v1.json` declares `scale.trade_value_max: 10000` and nothing reads it (see the dead-params finding). `frontend/lib/bdvm.js:95` passes `range.ceiling_p85` straight to the table.
