findings.userImpact: The /bdvm board shows a player with a fundamental value of 9,800 and a ceiling of 19,843 on a scale the page describes as 0–10,000. The docstring at `engine.py:368-372` acknowledges the quantile paths assume perfectly correlated seasons and 'widens the band' — but the consequence (the band leaving the scale) is not handled.
findings.recommendedFix: Either clamp `to_trade_value` at `scale.trade_value_max` (and stamp when it clamped), or compute the band by re-anchoring the quantile paths against the same calibration the median uses. Do not clamp silently — a pinned ceiling is information.

findings.title: Five of the eleven news→event keyword rules produce no effect at all, and their audit trail gives a false reason
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/news_events.py:78-107` maps 11 ontology types. At `_AUTO_CONFIDENCE = 0.45` (`:42`), `src/bdvm/events.py:117-141` suppresses every channel except `sigma_mult`. Five mapped types carry no `sigma_mult` in `config/bdvm/event_types_v1.json`: DEPTH_CHART_PROMOTION, SIGNING, SUSPENSION, CONTRACT_EXTENSION, FRANCHISE_TAG. Measured (`effective_impact` at 3 days old, reliability 0.6): those five return `{}`; the six that do fire return sigma_mult 1.018–1.072 (PRACTICE_LIMITATION 1.0181, INJURY 1.0358, DEPTH_CHART_DEMOTION 1.0367, TRADE 1.0376, SURGERY 1.0599, RELEASE 1.0717). `events.py:170-178` then records `applied: False, reason: "reflected_in_projection_or_fully_decayed"` — neither of which is true; the channels were suppressed by the speculation rule.
findings.userImpact: The auto-ingest lane is advertised (CLAUDE.md, `news_events.py:1-8`) as converting 'a dormant subsystem into a live one that reacts to the real world'. In practice 5 of 11 rules are inert and the other 6 widen σ by at most 7%, decaying with a 14–90 day half-life — which flows into value only through the option term and is dwarfed by the CV prior. The audit trail actively misdirects anyone debugging it.
findings.recommendedFix: Split the audit reason (`speculation_channels_suppressed` vs `reflected_in_projection` vs `fully_decayed`). Drop the five no-op rules from `_RULES` or add `sigma_mult` entries to those ontology types. Report the achievable σ range in `news_events.py`'s docstring so nobody over-reads what the lane does.

findings.title: The /rankings and /draft 'Fund gap' columns strip the proxy flag — a backward-looking number is shown as a fundamental value
findings.evidence: `frontend/lib/bdvm.js:192-210 buildBdvmIndex` builds entries with only `{gap, marketValue, fundamental, signal, signalReason}` — `projection.anyProxy`, `quality.confidenceLabel` and `sourceCount` are all dropped. The /bdvm page does badge them (`frontend/app/bdvm/page.jsx:190-195`, tooltip 'Priced from the reconstructed-baseline proxy, not a real projection source'), but the joined columns at `frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1179-1215` and `frontend/app/draft/page.jsx:1344` render only the gap and the signal tint. Every record is `is_proxy=True` whenever only the baseline stage has run — `scripts/refresh_bdvm_projections.py:276-281` logs exactly that case and still exits 0.
findings.userImpact: On the two highest-traffic pages, a number derived from shrunk realized PPG carried forward is displayed as 'BDVM fundamental value (balanced) minus market anchor' with the tooltip 'positive means the market underprices the player' (`rankings/page.jsx:1187-1189`). The user is told a projection disagrees with the market when in fact last season's box scores do.
findings.recommendedFix: Carry `anyProxy` and `confidenceLabel` through `buildBdvmIndex` and mute or asterisk proxy-backed gaps on both pages, reusing the /bdvm page's existing badge.

findings.title: Nothing has ever validated any BDVM output — the backtest harness has no production caller and no measurement exists
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/backtest.py` (336 lines: rolling-origin folds, leakage guard, baselines B0–B4, Spearman/MAE/RMSE/Brier/calibration) is imported by exactly one file: `tests/bdvm/test_backtest.py`, which feeds it synthetic rows (`grep -rn "from src.bdvm.backtest" --include=*.py .`). No script, route or workflow calls `run_backtest`, `s3_calibration` or `compare_surplus_modes`. `src/bdvm/engine.py:399` hardcodes `"provisional": True,  # priors not yet backtested — always true in v1`. `config/bdvm/params_v1.json`'s header states 'EVERY number here is a STARTING PRIOR ... NOT backtested truth'. The 194 tests in `tests/bdvm/` assert shape, monotonicity and reproduction of the reference fixture — none compares an output to a realized outcome.
findings.userImpact: Every number the system emits — trade values, gaps, BUY/SELL signals, trade verdicts — rests on hand-picked constants with zero out-of-sample evidence. The most sensitive of them is labelled as such in the config itself: `replacement.waiver_buffer` is called 'THE most sensitive knob in the model (it sets the origin of the value scale)'. Measured sensitivity on the reference archetypes, shifting every buffer by ±0.5 players/team: R(WR) moves 5.325→7.102, and the veteran WR p6 moves 2631.5→2315.7 (−12%) while the young WR p5 stays pinned at 9800 — i.e. the RELATIVE ordering shifts with an unvalidated prior.
findings.recommendedFix: Run `run_backtest` on the 131 dated contract archives under `exports/archive/` plus nflverse realized outcomes and record the fold results in a `model_experiments` ledger; at minimum run `compare_surplus_modes` + `evaluate_fold` for the option/truncated/plain ablation, which needs no new data. Until then keep `provisional: True` visible in the UI rather than only in the payload.

findings.title: Roster `capitals` are a plain sum of trade values, contradicting the module's own rule against adding displayed values
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/trade_math.py:9-11`: "Do not judge 2-for-1s by adding displayed values." The CES aggregator exists precisely because θ=1.2 makes the best asset dominate. Yet `src/bdvm/roster.py:172` computes `capitals = {s: sum(a["tradeValue"].get(s, 0.0) for a in assets) for s in strategies}` and `:175` does the same for `total_bal`. The scan itself correctly uses `package_value` (`:243`). Measured divergence: `package_value([3000,3000]) = 5345.4` vs a plain sum of 6000 — 10.9% at n=2, and it grows with roster depth.
findings.userImpact: `nowFutureRatio`, `valueWeightedAge` and the contend/retool/rebuild direction are computed on a scale the same module rejects for trade math. Deep rosters are systematically inflated relative to top-heavy ones, which biases the direction classification and therefore which strategy currency each side is evaluated in during the scan.
findings.recommendedFix: Either use `package_value` for capitals (with `spots_available` set to the roster size so no overflow charge applies), or document explicitly why a linear capital aggregate is the right quantity for a portfolio total while CES is right for a trade side — and pin the choice in a test.
findings.affectedSystems: analyze_rosters, direction classification, trade scan currency selection

findings.title: IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md contradicts the shipped code on module count, flag default, and career load
findings.evidence: `docs/research/bdvm-v1/IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md` §1: "a new, feature-flagged ... engine (`src/bdvm/`, 15 modules)" — there are 27 .py files. Same section: "The feature flag `bdvm_engine` defaults OFF; production behavior is bit-identical until it is flipped" — `src/api/feature_flags.py:225` has `"bdvm_engine": True`, and `src/bdvm/__init__.py:18-22` records that the default flipped on 2026-07-28. §27: "Career load is 0 for everyone (mileage inert)" — `src/bdvm/context.py:135-160` now computes touches/targets/dropbacks/snaps and `service.py:437-440` feeds them into `effective_age`.
findings.userImpact: The report is designated the living status document for the subsystem (§20 of the master prompt) and is cited from `src/bdvm/__init__.py` and `feature_flags.py` as the place to check BDVM's state. Three of its headline status claims are stale, so a reader trusting it will believe the engine is off and mileage inert.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a fourth-pass addendum correcting the module count, the flag default, and the career-load status, and note that §27's risk list predates the context wiring.

findings.title: `get_bdvm_values` cache key contains `id(contract)`, a reusable CPython address
findings.evidence: `src/api/bdvm_api.py:173-186`: `key = (id(contract), contract.get("generatedAt"), league_key, ...)`. `id()` is the object's memory address; once a contract dict is garbage-collected a later dict can be allocated at the same address. The remaining key components (`generatedAt`, `leagueKey`, `paramSetId`, snapshot path, surplus mode, actuals week, events fingerprint) would normally differ, so a stale hit needs a `generatedAt` collision — but the LRU is only 4 entries (`:39`) so a false MISS from an address change is the common case, silently turning a repeat request into a multi-second cold engine run.
findings.userImpact: Cache effectiveness is tied to object identity rather than content. In the pathological direction (same address, same `generatedAt` — e.g. a `None` generatedAt on a rebuilt contract) a stale board would be served.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop `id(contract)` from the key. `generatedAt` + `leagueKey` + `paramSetId` + snapshot path + surplus mode + actuals week + events fingerprint already identify the computation; if `generatedAt` can be None, hash the contract's `meta` block instead.

findings.title: Fantasy-playoff weeks are hardcoded to (15,16,17) rather than read from the league's Sleeper settings
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/schedule.py:36`: `DEFAULT_PLAYOFF_WEEKS = (15, 16, 17)`, used unconditionally by `fetch_team_weeks` (`:106-112`), which `src/api/bdvm_api.py:83-85` calls with only the season. The league's real `playoff_week_start` sits in `contract["sleeper"]["leagueSettings"]` and is never consulted. `ros_value` (`src/bdvm/ros.py:65`) applies `1.0 + playoff_weight` (contender 0.35) to whichever weeks the schedule marked.
findings.userImpact: A league whose fantasy playoffs start in week 14 or run to week 18 gets contender ROS values that weight the wrong three weeks by +35%. Silently wrong, not obviously wrong.
findings.recommendedFix: Thread `leagueSettings.playoff_week_start` and the playoff round count from the contract into `fetch_team_weeks`, defaulting to (15,16,17) only when absent, and stamp the resolved weeks on the ROS block.

findings.title: Rookie-pick outcome table has no rows past overall slot 36 — every pick from 3.01 down is priced identically
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/picks.py:60-61` selects `nearest = min(slots, key=lambda k: abs(k - overall_slot))` over keys {1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,36} from `config/bdvm/pick_outcomes_v1.json`. Measured for a 12-team league: slot 25 (3.01) → EV 650.0, slot 36 (3.12) → 308.0, slot 48 (4.12) → 308.0. Every slot ≥ 30 collapses onto the slot-36 row. `_parse_pick_slot` (`service.py:180-193`) parses picks from any round, so 4th-round picks in the contract all get the 3.12 valuation. Nearest-neighbour also means slot 5 ties between keys 4 and 6 and resolves by dict order.
findings.userImpact: A 4.01 and a 4.12 are priced the same, and both are priced as a 3.12. The distortion is small in absolute terms (~308 on a 9800 scale) but the pick board on /draft presents it as a per-slot valuation.
findings.recommendedFix: Extend the table past 36 (or interpolate between rows rather than snapping to nearest) and clamp with an explicit `beyond_table` flag so a pick outside the fitted range is labelled rather than silently priced.

findings.title: `_market_side` labels a 50/50 fundamental-market blend as 'model_clearing'
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/roster.py:230-231` falls back to summing `a["tradeClearing"]` and labels the basis `"model_clearing"`. `tradeClearing` is defined at `src/bdvm/market.py:180` as `fund_balanced + lambda_market_clearing·(market_tv - fund_balanced)` with `lambda_market_clearing: 0.5` — i.e. exactly half market price. The label is surfaced to the UI as `fairnessBasis` (`roster.py:332`).
findings.userImpact: A reader of the trade scan sees 'model_clearing' and reasonably concludes the fairness gate used model values only; it used a half-market blend. Given the whole premise of BDVM is separating fundamental from market, the label is exactly the wrong one.
findings.recommendedFix: Rename to `blended_clearing_lambda_0.5` (or emit the lambda alongside) in `_market_side` and in the frontend's basis rendering.

findings.title: Clay defensive projection rows hardcode games=17.0 and omit two of the league's four highest-paying IDP categories
findings.evidence: `src/bdvm/clay_projections.py:165-168`: the defense block is emitted with `"games": 17.0,  # defense block carries snaps, not games` regardless of the player. The parsed stat set is `{def_tackles_solo, def_tackle_assists, def_sacks, def_interceptions}` (`:155-160`) — no TFL and no passes-defended, which this league pays at `idp_tkl_loss = 4.25` and `idp_pass_def = 5.32` (live scoring card). The vocabulary-dominance down-weight (`projections.py:270-300`, `vocabulary_dominated_weight_mult: 0.25`) only fires when a PEER covers a strict superset; with Clay as the sole source for a defender it applies at full weight with the categories missing.
findings.userImpact: Defenders covered only by Clay are projected low by however much TFL and PD are worth to them — a category-dependent, position-dependent understatement, biggest for edge rushers and corners. Their `games` is 17.0 whether or not the guide projects a partial season.
findings.recommendedFix: Mark Clay defensive records with an explicit `vocabularyLimited` flag at ingest (not only when a peer exists) so a single-source defender is either down-weighted or reported with a coverage caveat; carry the guide's snap column into an estimated games figure rather than 17.0.
findings.affectedSystems: clay projections, projection consensus, IDP replacement level

formulas.name: Strategy discounted value DV(i,s) with dispersion penalty
formulas.expression:
DV(i,s) = Σ_{t=0..H_s} u_s(t) · d_s^t · S_i(t) · SSV_i(t)  −  λ_s · 0.35 · Ψ_i,  clamped at 0
Ψ_i = sqrt( Σ_t ( d_s^t · σ_i(t) · G_i(t) · S_i(t) )² )
u_s(t) = usability[min(t, len-1)]
formulas.inputs: rows from season_path (expected = ssv·survival, sigma, games, survival, t); strategy dict (usability, discount, risk_lambda, horizon)
formulas.constants: risk_lambda_dispersion_coeff = 0.35 (params_v1.json). Per strategy: contender d=0.72 H=4 λ=+0.20 usability [1,.95,.8,.65,.55]; balanced d=0.85 H=6 λ=+0.10 usability [1,1,1,.95,.9,.85,.8]; rebuilder d=0.93 H=8 λ=−0.10 usability [.45,.75,1,1,1,.95,.9,.85,.8]; risk_neutral = balanced with λ=0. All hand-picked priors.
formulas.mathIssues: λ enters LINEARLY on a quadratic-mean dispersion, so the penalty measured 1.2%–1.9% of raw DV on the reference archetypes (p1 637.0 raw / 7.7 penalty; p12 579.2 / 11.2). rebuilder's λ=−0.1 grants a symmetric bonus — a negative risk aversion, i.e. dispersion is rewarded. max(0,·) means a hypothetical high-λ player can be pinned at 0 with no signal.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Inputs are always present by construction — season_path fabricates no rows. A strategy profile lacking 'usability' or 'discount' raises KeyError.
formulas.validated: none found — no backtest measurement exists in-repo

formulas.name: Trade-value scaling + per-strategy anchor calibration
formulas.expression:
anchor_s = max_i DV(i,s) / (target_top_value / 10000)^(1/γ)
TV(i,s) = 10000 · ( max(0, DV(i,s)) / anchor_s )^γ
formulas.inputs: DV over the whole priced player set; scale.stud_gamma; scale.target_top_value
formulas.constants: stud_gamma = 1.2, target_top_value = 9800.0, trade_value_max = 10000.0 (NEVER READ). Measured anchors on the reference set: contender 418.0, balanced 760.0, rebuilder 963.3, risk_neutral 768.9.
formulas.outputRange: 0 → 9800 for the top asset BY CONSTRUCTION. Unbounded above for quantile paths — measured ceilings up to 19,843.4.
formulas.mathIssues: γ=1.2 > 1 compresses the mid/lower board: a DV at 60% of max maps to TV 5308.9 vs a linear 5880.0; at 10% it maps to 618.3 vs 980.0. This reshaping is applied BEFORE the gap-vs-market subtraction, and no step aligns the two distributions — they coincide only at the very top. The anchor is pool-dependent, so the whole scale re-normalizes whenever the projection set changes, while pick EVs (a fixed table) do not.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: anchor floors at 1e-9 if every DV is 0, producing enormous TVs rather than an error.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Season path µ(t)
formulas.expression:
a_eff(t) = effective_age(pos, age+t, career_load + t·load_rate)
µ(t) = fpg · [ A(a_eff(t)) / A(a_eff(0)) ] · (1 + κ(1 − e^(−t/τ)))
µ_eval(t) = µ(t) + z·σ(t)   (quantile paths only)
formulas.inputs: blended consensus fpg; age; career_load; kappa; archetype/dual_blend; annual_load_rate[pos]
formulas.constants: annual_load_rate: RB 260, WR 120, TE 90, QB 560, default 700 (used for DL/LB/DB snaps — 700 snaps/yr). τ = 1.5.
formulas.mathIssues: The aging term is a RATIO A(t)/A(0), so a player already past peak decays from his current level rather than from the curve peak — correct. Ascension multiplies rather than adds, so κ compounds with aging.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: kappa defaults to 0.0 when no draft/college/opportunity feed exists — and in production `college_score` and `opportunity_score` are hardcoded 0.0 (service.py:452-453), so κ is driven by draft capital and a youth dummy alone.
formulas.validated: reproduces reference Appendix C exactly (verified: 13/13 archetypes × 3 strategies within 1.0)

formulas.name: Aging multiplier (asymmetric Gaussian)
formulas.expression:
A(age) = exp(−c_up · (peak − age)²)  if age ≤ peak
       = exp(−c_dn · (age − peak)²)  if age > peak
QB: A = (1−w)·A_pocket + w·A_dual  when dual_blend w is supplied
formulas.inputs: modelling position, effective age, archetype/dual_blend
formulas.mathIssues: TE has c_up (0.030) > c_dn (0.018) — the only position where the curve rises more slowly than it falls, which is unusual and unexplained in the config.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `params.age_curve` raises ParamSetError for an unknown key; positions are pre-mapped through `modelling_position` so DL→EDGE, DB→S.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Effective age (career mileage)
formulas.expression: a_eff = age + min(cap, max(0, (career_load − reference_load) / load_per_effective_year))
formulas.inputs: career_load in the position's unit; params.mileage[pos]
formulas.constants: [unit, reference, per_year, cap]: RB [touches,750,500,2.5], WR [targets,500,450,1.5], TE [targets,400,450,1.5], QB [dropbacks,2000,2500,1.0], LB [snaps,3000,2200,1.5], EDGE/DT/CB/S [snaps,3000,2400,1.0–1.5]
formulas.outputRange: age → age + cap (max +2.5 years for an RB)
formulas.mathIssues: Only ever ADDS age — a low-mileage veteran gets no credit. Career load comes from `context.py` summed over `seasons_back=6` only, so pre-2020 workload is invisible; `context.py:130-133` documents this as conservative.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `params.mileage` returns None for an unmodelled position → a_eff = age. career_load defaults 0.0 when no context (service.py:436) → mileage fully inert.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Role ascension κ
formulas.expression:
κ = clip( b1·DC·e^(−0.45·(n−1)) + b2·COL·e^(−1.1·(n−1)) + b3·OPP + b4·YOUTH − b5·INCUMBENT , κ_min, κ_max )
YOUTH = 1 if nfl_season ≤ 2 else 0;  κ = 0 outright when nfl_season ≥ 4 and no documented role change
formulas.inputs: nfl_season (1 = rookie); draft_capital_score; college_score; opportunity_score; incumbency
formulas.constants: weights: draft_capital .30, college .15, opportunity .25, youth .05, incumbency .30. κ_min −0.15, κ_max 0.60, τ 1.5, kappa_force_zero_after_season 4, draft_capital_decay_rate 0.45, college_decay_rate 1.1.
formulas.mathIssues: In production `college_score = 0.0` and `opportunity_score = 0.0` (hardcoded, service.py:452-453) and `incumbency = 0.0` (:455), so κ collapses to 0.30·DC·e^(−0.45(n−1)) + 0.05·YOUTH — i.e. 40% of the designed weight is inert and κ is essentially a draft-capital + youth term. That is precisely the 'generic youth multiplier' the docstring says ascension must never become.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: All missing inputs default to 0.0, biasing κ downward — safe direction.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Outcome dispersion σ(t)
formulas.expression:
CV = cv_base[pos] · (1 + 0.90·role_unc) · (1 + 0.45·event_vol) · (1 + 0.60·small_sample)
σ(0) = sqrt( (CV·µ)² + σ_source² )
σ(t) = sqrt( σ(0)² + (drift_vol[pos] · µ(t) · √t)² )
σ ×= 1.1 when the true position is unknown
formulas.inputs: modelling position, µ, RiskProfile, σ_source from the consensus, horizon t
formulas.constants: cv_base: QB .26 RB .36 WR .34 TE .36 DT .32 EDGE .34 LB .26 CB .40 S .30. drift_vol: QB .16 RB .30 WR .22 TE .22 DT .20 EDGE .22 LB .22 CB .30 S .24. sigma_multipliers: role_uncertainty .90, event_volatility .45, small_sample .60. unknown_true_position_sigma_mult 1.1. All priors.
formulas.mathIssues: σ scales with µ, so a 20-FPG WR carries σ 9.46 — a 47% CV on a SEASON mean. That is far wider than realized season-to-season variation and is what makes the option term large. σ_source is 0 whenever a player has one projection source (the current universal case) and the `single_source_projection_sigma_mult: 1.5` prior that exists to fix this is never read.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: σ_source defaults 0.0 → σ is CV-driven only. `mu` is floored at 0.1 by the caller (engine.py:139).
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Season starter value (option / truncated / plain)
formulas.expression:
option:    SSV = [ (µ−R)·Φ(z) + σ·φ(z) ] · G,   z = (µ−R)/σ
truncated: SSV = max(0, µ−R) · G
plain:     SSV = (µ−R) · G
quantile paths bypass this entirely: SSV = max(0, µ+zσ − R) · G  (engine.py:159-163)
formulas.inputs: µ(t), σ(t), replacement R for the lineup group, games G(t), surplus_mode
formulas.constants: none of its own; surplus_mode default 'option'
formulas.mathIssues: Measured premium of option over truncated (WR, R=6.15, G=17, σ from sigma_fpg at the player's own µ): µ=20 → 240.55 vs 235.45 (+2%); µ=10 → 74.87 vs 65.45 (+14%); µ=8 → 44.38 vs 31.45 (+41%); µ=6.15 → 19.72 vs 0.00; µ=5.00 → 8.12 vs 0.00; µ=3.00 → 0.11 vs 0.00. The premium is negligible at the top and unbounded near replacement, so this is a re-ranking of the fringe, not a level shift. The justification in the docstring ('you are never forced to start a below-replacement outcome') requires deciding after the outcome is known.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: σ ≤ 1e-9 degrades to max(0, µ−R). Unknown mode raises ValueError.
formulas.validated: the ablation is plumbed (surplusMode) but never measured against realized outcomes

formulas.name: Fantasy-relevance hazard and survival
formulas.expression:
h = base_hazard(pos, chronological age) · Π adjusters, clipped to [0.02, 0.85]
adjusters = (1 + 0.55·(0.60 − role_security)) · (1 + 0.30·dc_decay·(0.50 − draft_capital))
          · (1 + 0.25·(0.60 − contract_security)) · (1 + 0.35·(0.60 − durability))
          · (1 − 0.18·clip(production_z, ±2)) · (1 + 0.20·designation_risk)
S(t) = Π_{k=1..t} (1 − h(age+k));  S(0) = 1
formulas.inputs: modelling position, CHRONOLOGICAL age (never effective age — pinned by tests), RiskProfile, draft-capital decay
formulas.mathIssues: Step function, not smooth — a player's hazard jumps discontinuously on his birthday across a band boundary (WR 28→29 jumps 0.13→0.22). In production every RiskProfile field except role_security/role_uncertainty/production_z/event_volatility is a hardcoded neutral (service.py:120-131: draft_capital .5, contract_security .6, durability .6, designation_risk 0.0), so the adjuster product is ≈ 1 for almost everyone and the hazard is essentially the position/age prior alone.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Neutral defaults, documented in-line as 'no feed wired yet'. `base_hazard_schedule` raises for an unknown position.
formulas.validated: `s3_calibration` exists in backtest.py to check S(3) against realized retention; never run

formulas.name: Dynamic flex-aware replacement level
formulas.expression:
startable_g = teams · fixed_starters[g] + (greedy flex allocation)
flex greedy: for each flex slot instance, assign to argmax_g pool_g(count_g + 1) over eligible groups (ties broken by group name)
repl_rank_g = startable_g + round(teams · waiver_buffer[g])
R_g = pool_g(repl_rank_g)   (0.0 past the end of the measured pool, flagged pool_exhausted)
formulas.inputs: BdvmLeagueConfig (teams, starters, flex); per-group rank→FPG PoolCurve built from consensus projections
formulas.constants: waiver_buffer: QB .85, RB .75, WR 1.00, TE .40, DL/LB/DB/DT/EDGE/CB/S .50, K .25; default_buffer .50; best_ball_buffer_bump {RB:.5, WR:.5} NEVER APPLIED. The config itself calls waiver_buffer 'THE most sensitive knob in the model (it sets the origin of the value scale)'.
formulas.outputRange: R ≥ 0 FPG. Reference config reproduces Appendix C exactly: QB 12.404, RB 6.345, WR 6.150, TE 6.805, DL 6.703, LB 7.319, DB 6.166; startable slots QB 24, RB 33, WR 36, TE 15, DL 24, LB 48, DB 36.
formulas.mathIssues: Measured sensitivity — shifting every buffer by ±0.5 players/team on the reference config: R(WR) 7.102 → 5.325, R(LB) 8.153 → 6.570; veteran WR p6 2315.7 → 2631.5 (+13.6%) while young WR p5 stays pinned at 9800. So an unvalidated prior moves relative ordering, not just scale. The greedy flex pass is single-sweep and correct only because pools are monotone decreasing.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A group with no pool yields GroupReplacement(..., 0.0, 0.0, pool_exhausted=True) — R=0, so every player in that group scores full µ as surplus. K is in this state for the live league (K is in `_UNSUPPORTED_POSITIONS`, so no K is ever priced, which masks it).
formulas.validated: monotonicity is tested (tests/bdvm/test_replacement.py) but the buffer LEVEL is never calibrated

formulas.name: Robust projection consensus
formulas.expression:
per record: fpg = resolve_fpg(scoring_settings)  [stat line → league scoring, else fpg, else fpts/games]
w_r = 1.0, ×0.5 if (snapshot_as_of − record_as_of).days > 21, ×0.25 if the record's league-scored IDP category set is a STRICT SUBSET of a peer's
if n ≥ 5: sort by fpg, trim k = max(1, floor(0.1n)) from each end (only if n−2k ≥ 3)
w = cap_weights(w, 0.35)   [skipped entirely when n·0.35 < 1, i.e. n < 3]
µ = Σ w·fpg / Σ w;  games = Σ w·games / Σ w;  σ_source = sqrt( Σ w·(fpg−µ)² / Σ w )
formulas.inputs: ProjectionRecords for one player_key; league scoring_settings; snapshot as_of; params
formulas.constants: trim_frac .10, trim_min_sources 5, max_single_source_weight .35, stale_after_days 21, stale_weight_mult .50, vocabulary_dominated_weight_mult .25, equal_weight_shrinkage .30 (NEVER READ)
formulas.mathIssues: σ_source = 0 EXACTLY for a single source, and the `single_source_projection_sigma_mult` prior that exists to widen it is dead code. The variance uses the same weights as the mean with no n/(n−1) correction — biased low, on top of already having at most two sources. The weight cap is skipped for n<3, which is the realistic case.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty record list → returns None → the caller records the player as `unpriced: no_projection` (service.py:409-411). Never a zero.
formulas.validated: unit-tested for shape/trim/cap behaviour; no source-accuracy weights exist ('v1 uses equal base weights (no honest source-accuracy history exists yet)')

formulas.name: Staleness weight
formulas.expression: age_days = snapshot_as_of − record_as_of;  w = 0.5 if age_days > 21 else 1.0
formulas.inputs: record as_of, snapshot as_of
formulas.constants: stale_after_days 21, stale_weight_mult 0.5
formulas.mathIssues: A step, not a decay: a 22-day-old record is halved and a 200-day-old one is halved by the same amount. The baseline carry-forward (`scripts/bdvm_build_baseline.py:66-78`) relies on this to age out real records that stop refreshing, so an indefinitely stale Clay record keeps 50% weight forever.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Unparseable dates → weight 1.0, not stale (fails open).
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Iterative single-source weight cap
formulas.expression: repeat ≤200×: if any w_i/Σw > 0.35 + 1e-9, set w_i = 0.35·Σw; skipped entirely when n·0.35 < 1
formulas.inputs: weight list, cap fraction
formulas.constants: cap 0.35, 200 iterations
formulas.mathIssues: Setting w_i = cap·total in-place changes `total` on the next pass, so the loop is a fixed-point iteration with no convergence proof; it bails after 200 rounds returning whatever it has. With n=3 (the largest realistic count) the cap forces all three to ~0.333 each, erasing the staleness penalty the docstring says the skip exists to protect — the guard only covers n<3.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: All-zero weights → returns all 1.0 (equal weight).
formulas.validated: unit-tested at n=3 only

formulas.name: Reconstructed-baseline proxy µ₀ (§8.3)
formulas.expression:
usable = the 3 most recent seasons with season < target_season and games > 0
wppg = Σ w_k·ppg_k / Σ w_k,  w = (0.5, 0.3, 0.2) recent-first
avg_games = mean(games over usable)
shrink s = min(0.90, 0.35 · 16 / max(1, avg_games))
µ₀ = (1 − s)·wppg + s·positional_mean[pos]
games_proj = clip(avg_games, 8, 17)
formulas.inputs: realized per-season PPG under the league's exact scoring (from src/bdvm/baseline.py::realized_ppg_history); positional means
formulas.constants: season weights (0.5,0.3,0.2); shrink base 0.35; shrink cap 0.90; reference games 16.0; positional-mean pool requires games ≥ 8 and ppg ≥ 1.0
formulas.mathIssues: NO TEMPORAL LEAKAGE — `s.season < season` (projections.py:544) and `years = range(season - seasons_back, season)` (baseline.py:276) both exclude the target season. Confirmed clean. But the shrink target `positional_means` is computed over the same history including the player's own seasons (baseline.py:110-128), a mild self-inclusion bias. This is a backward-looking proxy, NOT a projection: every record carries is_proxy=True (projections.py:585) and the docstring says so explicitly.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A player with no usable prior season is skipped entirely — no record, hence unpriced downstream. Never imputed.
formulas.validated: none found; the docstring states the direction of the bias ('EXPLICITLY a worse projection than a real preseason consensus')

formulas.name: Rookie draft-slot prior
formulas.expression:
bucket(overall) = r1 if ceil(overall/32)=1, r2 if 2, else r3plus
µ = mean rookie-season PPG of past rookies at (position, bucket) when n ≥ 5, else the position-wide rookie mean when n ≥ 5, else NO RECORD
games = 15.0 (fixed)
formulas.inputs: realized history keyed by rookie_season; PlayerContext (draft_overall, rookie_season, true_position)
formulas.constants: _ROOKIE_MIN_BUCKET_N 5, _ROOKIE_PRIOR_GAMES 15.0, 32 picks/round
formulas.mathIssues: Draft rounds are assumed exactly 32 picks — compensatory picks make rounds 3-7 longer, so a mid-round-3 pick can land in the wrong bucket. Undrafted rookies get nothing (deliberate). Bucket means are unweighted across seasons, so a single outlier rookie season moves the prior for an entire (pos, round) cell.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Undrafted → skipped and counted in `undraftedRookiesSkipped`. Position unknown → skipped. Thin bucket → falls back to position mean, then to no record. Never fabricated.
formulas.validated: IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT claims verification on the 2025 class (205 drafted rookies); no in-repo measurement

formulas.name: Draft-capital score
formulas.expression: DC = 1.0 if overall ≤ 10;  else clip(1.045 − 0.0045·overall, 0, 1);  0.0 for UDFA/unknown
formulas.inputs: nflverse players.csv draft_pick (verified as the OVERALL selection)
formulas.constants: 1.045 intercept, 0.0045 slope → zero at pick ≈232
formulas.mathIssues: Linear in overall pick, which contradicts every published draft-value curve (steeply convex at the top). Pick 11 scores 0.9955 while pick 10 scores 1.0 — a cliff of 0.0045 across the round-1 top-10 boundary, then linear thereafter. Explicitly labelled a 'provisional prior (documented judgment call)'.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: None/≤0 → 0.0, which equals UDFA. So 'unknown draft slot' and 'went undrafted' are indistinguishable downstream — the docstring argues this is the safe direction for an ascension/survival input.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Rookie-pick expected value
formulas.expression:
nearest = argmin_k |k − overall_slot| over the table's slot keys
EV = (p_hit·v_hit + p_mid·v_mid) · clip(class_strength, 0.85, 1.15) · discount_s^years_out · pick_premium_s
ceiling = v_hit·cs;  median = v_mid·cs;  p_miss = 1 − p_hit − p_mid
formulas.inputs: overall rookie-draft slot; strategy; years_out; class_strength (always 1.0 — no caller passes it)
formulas.constants: config/bdvm/pick_outcomes_v1.json slots {1,2,3,4,6,8,12,16,24,36}, e.g. slot 1 {p_hit .62, v_hit 7200, p_mid .20, v_mid 2600}; slot 36 {.07, 2400, .20, 700}. v_miss implicit 0. pick_premium: contender 0.92, balanced 1.00, rebuilder 1.08. The file's own comment: 'explicitly the most placeholder-ish table in the whole model'.
formulas.mathIssues: Nearest-neighbour with no interpolation: slot 13 (2.01) and slot 12 (1.12) both resolve to key 12; every slot ≥ 30 resolves to key 36. The 0-10000 scale is a FIXED prior, never re-anchored to the engine's pool-calibrated player scale, yet the two are summed in one CES package in trade-eval. class_strength is a parameter no caller supplies.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: overall_slot < 1 raises PickConfigError. An unparseable pick name yields `distribution: null` + `reason: unparseable_pick_name` (service.py:601-603) — never a zero.
formulas.validated: none found; the config asks to be replaced with distributions fit from the platform's own history

formulas.name: CES package aggregation with roster-spot overflow
formulas.expression:
core = ( Σ_i max(0, v_i)^θ )^(1/θ)
overflow = max(0, n_assets − max(1, spots_available))
package = core − roster_spot_cost · overflow
θ = theta_shallow_league when roster_size ≤ 26, else theta
formulas.inputs: list of per-asset trade values in ONE strategy currency; spots_available; roster_size
formulas.constants: theta 1.2, theta_shallow_league 1.35, shallow_roster_size_threshold 26, roster_spot_cost 120.0
formulas.outputRange: can go negative once overflow bites
formulas.mathIssues: Verified: 1×6000 → 6000.0; 2×3000 → 5345.4 (−10.9% vs the sum); 3×2000 → 4996.1; 4×1500 → 4642.2 (includes one 120-point overflow charge). θ>1 correctly prices consolidation. But `roster.py:172` computes roster CAPITALS with a plain sum, directly contradicting this module's own docstring rule. `spots_available` defaults to 3 everywhere in production — no caller derives it from real roster space.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty list → 0.0. Negative values floored at 0 before exponentiation.
formulas.validated: reproduces the reference's CES trade-math examples (tests/bdvm/test_trade_math.py)

formulas.name: Both-sides double-positive evaluation
formulas.expression:
gain_A = package(A_receives; strategy_A) − package(A_sends; strategy_A)
gain_B = package(B_receives; strategy_B) − package(B_sends; strategy_B)
double_positive ⟺ gain_A > 0 AND gain_B > 0
formulas.inputs: per-strategy asset value lists; each side's assigned strategy from the roster direction classifier
formulas.constants: scan gates: TOP_ASSETS_PER_SIDE 12, MIN_ASSET_VALUE 400.0, MIN_GAIN_EACH_SIDE 150.0, MARKET_FAIRNESS_TOLERANCE_PCT 12.0, MAX_RESULTS 40 — all module-level judgment calls, not parameters
formulas.mathIssues: Each side is priced in a currency whose per-strategy ANCHOR differs (contender 418.0, rebuilder 963.3 on the reference set), so `gain_A` and `gain_B` are not commensurable magnitudes — yet `minGain` (roster.py:334) sorts results by min(gain_A, gain_B) across currencies. Picks cannot appear at all (assets come only from playerIds).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: An asset side with any unpriced member yields (None, 'unpriced') from `_market_side` and the candidate is dropped (roster.py:309-310).
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Market comparison: gap, alpha, blended outputs
formulas.expression:
gap = fundamental_balanced − market_value
alpha = gap · liquidity
marketAdjusted = F + 0.25·(M − F)
tradeClearing   = F + 0.50·(M − F)
τ_market = 1 · (0.45 if IDP) · (0.55 if rookie) · (1 − 0.5·dispersion)
τ_model  = 0.85 · (1 − 0.40·small_sample)
w_model  = τ_model / (τ_model + τ_market)
formulas.inputs: completed fundamental trade values (raises MarketIsolationError if empty); MarketView; is_idp; is_rookie; small_sample
formulas.constants: tau_model .85, tau_model_small_sample_mult .40, tau_market_idp_mult .45, tau_market_rookie_mult .55, tau_market_dispersion_mult .50, lambda_market_display .25, lambda_market_clearing .50, lambda_market_fundamental 0.0 (NEVER READ)
formulas.mathIssues: THE central methodological problem: F is a γ=1.2 power transform of a discounted-surplus quantity, anchored so the top asset = 9800; M is a crowd-sourced KTC/IDPTC number topping out at 9999. Nothing aligns their SHAPES — they coincide only at the top of the board, and γ>1 compresses the mid/lower board (60% of max DV → 5308.9 vs a linear 5880.0). The difference of two differently-shaped distributions is therefore rank-dependent by construction, and that difference is what drives BUY/SELL. Worse for this league: F is computed under scoring that omits 6 active reception-band rules (see findings) while M is a Superflex TE-premium PPR crowd board — the two price different games. `w_model` is computed and stamped but never used to blend anything.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: market_value None → gap, alpha, marketAdjusted, tradeClearing all None (never 0) and signal = NO_MARKET. Correct.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Market anchor selection, dispersion and 'liquidity'
formulas.expression:
source = idpTradeCalc for DL/LB/DB; else first of (ktcSfTep, ktc)
dispersion = clip(row.marketDispersionCV, 0, 1) else clip(row.sourceRankPercentileSpread, 0, 1) else 0.20
liquidity = clip( 0.35 + 1.6·dispersion , 0.20, 1.00 )
formulas.inputs: contract row canonicalSiteValues; lineup group
formulas.constants: liquidity base .35, dispersion_coeff 1.6, clip [.20, 1.00]; default dispersion .20 when neither field is present; NORMALIZATION_VERSION 'ktc-idptc-peer-v1'
formulas.outputRange: liquidity ∈ [0.20, 1.00]. Measured on the live export (_marketDispersionCV, n=839): min 0.0, p50 0.0208, p90 0.0882, max 0.249; 45.2% are exactly 0.0. So liquidity is 0.35–0.75 with median 0.383 and NEVER reaches the 1.0 clip.
formulas.mathIssues: Liquidity RISES with cross-source disagreement, while the very same dispersion LOWERS τ_market 20 lines later — the two uses are contradictory. Since alpha = gap·liquidity ≈ gap·0.38 in practice, the documented thresholds (buy 400, strong_sell −900) correspond to gaps of ≈ +1045 and ≈ −2350, and `strong_buy_min_liquidity: 0.5` excludes 45% of the board.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Rank-signal sources (fantasyCalc, dlfSf, …) are correctly refused as prices — pinned by tests/bdvm/test_market_isolation.py:44-51. No anchor → market_value None.
formulas.validated: the KTC↔IDPTC comparability claim cites a 2026-07-26 study (median ratio 1.000) recorded in comments; the study itself is not in the repository

formulas.name: Buy/Hold/Sell signal policy
formulas.expression:
alpha None                                          → NO_MARKET
alpha > 900 AND persisted AND liquidity > 0.5       → STRONG_BUY
alpha > 400                                          → BUY  (HOLD if gap_persisted_days supplied and < 14)
p_collapse_1y > 0.5 AND alpha < 0                    → STRONG_SELL
alpha < −900                                         → STRONG_SELL
alpha < −400                                         → SELL
otherwise                                            → HOLD
formulas.inputs: market_comparison output; params thresholds; optional gap_persisted_days; optional p_value_collapse_1y
formulas.constants: strong_buy_alpha 900, buy_alpha 400, sell_alpha −400, strong_sell_alpha −900, gap_persistence_days 14 (DEAD), strong_buy_min_liquidity 0.5 (DEAD)
formulas.outputRange: one of 6 labels; only 5 are reachable in production
formulas.mathIssues: `persisted` is always False in production (service.py:557 passes no gap_persisted_days) → STRONG_BUY unreachable. The collapse branch is evaluated before the −900 magnitude check, so alpha = −1 with p_collapse = 0.51 returns STRONG_SELL. Thresholds are in alpha units but alpha ≈ 0.38·gap in practice.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing alpha → NO_MARKET with an explicit reason; never a fabricated HOLD.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: In-season posterior (§8.4)
formulas.expression:
w_prior = n_prior / (n_prior + weeks_played)
µ_post  = w_prior·µ_preseason + (1 − w_prior)·mean(realized weekly points)
σ_post  = σ_source · sqrt(w_prior)
formulas.inputs: consensus µ and σ_source; per-player weekly realized points under exact league scoring; is_idp
formulas.constants: n_prior_offense 6.0, n_prior_idp 8.0
formulas.mathIssues: σ_post shrinks with evidence but the realized sample's OWN dispersion is never measured or blended in — a player whose weekly outcomes swung wildly gets the same σ shrink as a metronome. Because σ_source is 0 for single-source players (the current universal case), σ_post is 0 too and the whole in-season update leaves σ at CV·µ. `current_week` is deliberately uncapped so post-week-18 ROS sums zero — verified correct.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Players with no observed weeks keep the preseason consensus untouched (service.py:346-347). `(None, {})` or omitted actuals is an exact no-op; meta.inSeason = {'active': false}. A raising fetch is returned but NOT memoized (bdvm_api.py:150-152).
formulas.validated: unit-tested for shape and boundary weeks; the n_prior values are priors

formulas.name: Rest-of-season value
formulas.expression:
per_game = E[max(0, X − R)]  with X ~ N(µ_ros, σ(0))
ROS = Σ_{weeks not bye} clip(p_active,0,1) · per_game · (1 + playoff_weight·1{playoff week})
in-season: weeks are filtered to w ≥ current_week, plus the boundary week (current_week − 1) when that week is not in the player's own played set
formulas.inputs: blended µ (posterior in-season); σ(0) from the engine's first season row; group replacement R; team schedule; strategy playoff_weight
formulas.constants: playoff_weight: contender .35, balanced .15, rebuilder .00, risk_neutral .15. DEFAULT_PLAYOFF_WEEKS = (15,16,17) HARDCODED. p_active = 1.0 for every week (schedule.py:98).
formulas.mathIssues: p_active is always 1.0 — the injury/availability channel the formula exists for is never populated, so ROS is µ-and-bye-week arithmetic. Playoff weeks ignore the league's actual `playoff_week_start`. σ is the SEASON-mean σ used as a WEEKLY σ inside the per-game option, inflating per_game near replacement.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No schedule → `ros: null`. No schedule for the player's team → `{value: null, reason: 'no_schedule_for_team:XXX'}`. Never fabricated.
formulas.validated: none found; the module docstring calls itself 'SCAFFOLDING in v1'

formulas.name: Structured-event effective impact and application
formulas.expression:
scale = confidence · source_reliability · (1 − already_in_projection) · 2^(−days_since_effective / half_life)
multiplicative channels (sigma_mult, hazard_mult): value^scale  [= exp(ln(value)·scale)]
additive channels: value · scale
speculation (confidence < 0.5): every non-sigma channel dropped; sigma_mult floored at 1.0
apply: fpg ×= (1 + Σ mu_pct); games = clip(games + Σ games_delta, 0, 17); risk fields clipped to [0,1]; sigma/hazard multipliers compose multiplicatively
formulas.inputs: PlayerEvent records from data/bdvm/events/<season>.json; the closed ontology config; snapshot as_of
formulas.constants: _SPECULATION_CONFIDENCE 0.5; auto-ingest confidence 0.45, reliability 0.6 (news_events.py:42-43). Ontology half-lives 14–365 days; impacts e.g. INJURY {games −2.0, durability −0.10, sigma×1.15}, DEPTH_CHART_DEMOTION {mu_pct −0.12, role_security −0.20, hazard×1.15, sigma×1.15}.
formulas.outputRange: VERIFIED at the news lane's 0.45/0.6, 3 days old: DEPTH_CHART_DEMOTION → {sigma_mult 1.0367} only; INJURY → {1.0358}; SURGERY → {1.0599}; RELEASE → {1.0717}; TRADE → {1.0376}; PRACTICE_LIMITATION → {1.0181}; DEPTH_CHART_PROMOTION, SIGNING, SUSPENSION, CONTRACT_EXTENSION, FRANCHISE_TAG → {} (no effect at all). At human confidence 0.9/0.9 the full channel set fires (DEPTH_CHART_DEMOTION → mu_pct −0.0928, role_security −0.1547, hazard 1.1142, sigma 1.1142). Direct application test: fpg 14.0 → 14.0 unchanged, games 17.0 → 17.0 unchanged, event_sigma_mult 1.0367.
formulas.mathIssues: The speculation clamp WORKS as documented — a 0.45-confidence headline provably cannot move µ, games, or hazard, and cannot narrow σ. But the surviving effect is at most +7.2% on σ, decaying, and σ only reaches value through the option term, which is nearly flat far above replacement. Five of the eleven mapped news rules produce literally nothing and are audited with the wrong reason ('reflected_in_projection_or_fully_decayed').
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing events file → []. Unknown event type → EventError (closed enum). already_in_projection → scale 0 → skipped with an audit row.
formulas.validated: unit-tested (tests/bdvm/test_news_events.py:91-137) — the tests do assert the sigma-only clamp and the may-only-widen rule

formulas.name: News→events merge, dedup and prune
formulas.expression:
eventId = 'news:<item-id>:<player-key>'
skip if eventId already present (existing wins)
skip if (playerKey, eventType) already seen within 14 days
prune existing events where eventId starts with 'news:' AND confidence < 0.5 AND age > 90 days
write {**payload, 'events': kept + added} via tmp + atomic replace
formulas.inputs: aggregated news items with {id, headline, body, ts, players:[{name, ambiguous}]}
formulas.constants: _AUTO_EVENT_MAX_AGE_DAYS 90, _DUP_EVENT_WINDOW_DAYS 14, _MAX_PLAYER_MENTIONS 3
formulas.mathIssues: None found. Refuses on unreadable JSON AND on valid-JSON-wrong-shape rather than discarding human entries (:228-242); preserves extra top-level keys on rewrite; human-raised confidence exempts an event from pruning (`_is_auto`, :170-182). This is the most carefully-guarded code in the subsystem.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing file → treated as empty and created. Ambiguous mention → no event. >3 mentions → whole item skipped. No ts → skipped.
formulas.validated: 22 unit tests covering dedup, same-fact suppression, prune exemption, shape refusal

formulas.name: Outcome probabilities
formulas.expression:
p_above_replacement = Φ((µ₀ − R)/σ₀)
elite_line = pool_g(max(1, teams // 2))  [or R + 1.75·max(1, 0.45·R) with no pool]
p_elite_season = 1 − Φ((elite_line − µ₀)/σ₀)
p_starter_in_1y = S(1)·Φ((µ₁ − R)/σ₁);  p_value_collapse_1y = 1 − p_starter_in_1y
p_starter_in_3y = S(3)·Φ((µ₃ − R)/σ₃)
p_breakout = 1 − Φ((1.35·µ₀ − µ₁)/σ₁)
p_bust_year1 = 1 − p_above_replacement
formulas.inputs: season path rows 0/1/3; replacement R; group pool; probabilities config
formulas.constants: elite_pool_rank_divisor 2 (elite = the 6th-best in the group in a 12-team league), elite_fallback_mult 1.75, elite_fallback_floor_frac 0.45, breakout_mult 1.35
formulas.mathIssues: All Gaussian-tail with the same inflated σ (CV ≈ 0.47 for a neutral-risk WR), so probabilities are compressed toward 0.5. `p_value_collapse_1y` drives the STRONG_SELL override — a quantity that is a Gaussian tail of an unvalidated σ times an unvalidated hazard. Division by σ has no guard, but σ > 0 is guaranteed by the µ floor at 0.1.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No pool for the group → the fallback formula, which is anchored on R and therefore 0 when R is 0 (pool_exhausted case) → elite_line 1.75 → p_elite ≈ 1 for everyone in that group.
formulas.validated: reproduces the reference; never compared to realized outcomes

formulas.name: Floor / median / ceiling band
formulas.expression:
floor  = TV( DV(path with every season shifted by z = −0.8416σ) )
median = TV( DV(expected path) )
ceiling= TV( DV(path with every season shifted by z = +1.0364σ) )
volatility = Ψ / (DV_balanced + Ψ), capped at 1.0
quantile paths use SSV = max(0, µ + zσ − R)·G, NOT the option form
formulas.inputs: PlayerInput; balanced strategy; balanced dispersion Ψ
formulas.outputRange: Verified on the reference archetypes: floors 0.0–2191.1, ceilings 3082.7–19843.4, volatility 0.238–0.488. EVERY ceiling exceeds the nominal 10000 scale.
formulas.mathIssues: The docstring admits the approximation shifts every season by the same z — perfectly correlated seasons — which inflates the band. On top of that the quantile paths switch surplus formulation mid-computation (truncated instead of option), so the band is not the same estimator as the median. No clamp at trade_value_max.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a — derived entirely from the player's own path.
formulas.validated: none found; the docstring calls it 'honest until the Phase-10 simulation replaces it'

formulas.name: Value decomposition (explain block)
formulas.expression:
contrib_t = u(t)·d^t·expected_t
year_0_share = contrib₀ / Σ contrib;  years_1_2_share = Σ_{1..2}/Σ;  years_3_plus_share = Σ_{3..}/Σ
survival_drag = 1 − Σ expected_t / Σ ssv_t
traj_5y = µ₅/µ₀ − 1;  scarcity_leverage = R
formulas.inputs: balanced-horizon rows
formulas.constants: balanced usability/discount
formulas.outputRange: shares sum to 1; verified p4 year_0_share 0.85, traj_5y −0.95 (matches the reference)
formulas.mathIssues: `traj_5y` indexes min(5, len−1); with a horizon shorter than 5 it silently reports a different year with the same label.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Denominators floored at 1e-9.
formulas.validated: reproduces the reference

formulas.name: Roster direction classification
formulas.expression:
ratio_r = contender_capital_r / max(1, rebuilder_capital_r)
median = median over all rosters
rel = ratio / max(1e-9, median)
rel > 1.15 → contend;  rel < 1/1.15 → rebuild;  else retool
strategy = {contend: contender, rebuild: rebuilder, *: balanced}
formulas.inputs: per-roster capitals (plain sums over matched players only)
formulas.constants: _CONTEND_RATIO 1.15, _REBUILD_RATIO 0.8696
formulas.mathIssues: League-RELATIVE by construction, so at least one roster is always classified an extreme regardless of actual posture. Capitals exclude ALL draft picks, which is the single most future-weighted asset class — the docstring at :66-74 documents the resulting saturation and rescales around it instead of adding the picks. Capitals are plain sums, not the CES package the same package the module uses for trades.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Players not on the BDVM board are silently skipped and counted in `unmatchedPlayerIds`, so a roster with poor projection coverage looks poor rather than uncertain.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Trade-scan market fairness gate
formulas.expression:
if all assets on a side are the same market family (IDP vs offense) and all have marketValue: side_total = Σ marketValue, basis 'single_market'
else if all have tradeClearing: side_total = Σ tradeClearing, basis 'model_clearing'
else unpriced → candidate dropped
fairness_pct = 100·|A − B| / max(1, A + B);  reject if > 12.0
formulas.inputs: per-asset marketValue (KTC or IDPTC) and tradeClearing
formulas.constants: MARKET_FAIRNESS_TOLERANCE_PCT 12.0
formulas.mathIssues: Correctly refuses to sum raw KTC and raw IDPTC. But the fallback labelled 'model_clearing' is `F + 0.5·(M − F)` — a 50% market blend — so the label materially misdescribes the basis. Picks are never in the asset list, so a pick-for-player trade can never be fairness-checked because it can never be proposed.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Any unpriced asset → the whole candidate is silently dropped, so the scan is biased toward assets with market coverage (464/1074 rows have ktcSfTep, 814 have idpTradeCalc on the live export).
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Dynasty 0-100 percentile score
formulas.expression: score = 100 · bisect_left(sorted_balanced_trade_values, v) / (n_priced − 1)
formulas.inputs: balanced trade values of every priced player
formulas.constants: none
formulas.mathIssues: Percentile over the PRICED set only, so it silently rescales as projection coverage changes — a board with 300 priced players and one with 900 give the same player different scores with no indication. `bisect_left` on ties assigns the lowest rank in the tie group.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n_priced ≤ 1 → 100.0 for the single player.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Confidence policy
formulas.expression:
score = 1.0 − 0.35·any_proxy − 0.25·(n_sources ≤ 1) − 0.15·(!true_position_known) − 0.10·(stale_source_count > 0) − 0.10·(small_sample ≥ 0.5), clipped [0,1]
label = high if ≥0.75, medium if ≥0.45, else low
formulas.inputs: PlayerInput quality flags
formulas.constants: the five deductions above; `provisional` hardcoded True
formulas.outputRange: [0,1] + a label. With only the proxy baseline on disk, EVERY player scores 1.0 − 0.35 − 0.25 = 0.40 → 'low'.
formulas.mathIssues: Deductions are hand-picked and additive with no calibration — the docstring says so ('coarse labels until calibration exists'). The frontend renders the label; `buildBdvmIndex` (used by /rankings and /draft) discards it entirely.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a — flags always present.
formulas.validated: none found; `provisional: True` is hardcoded and never flips

formulas.name: First-down imputation at the projection boundary
formulas.expression: first_downs ≈ FIRST_DOWNS_PER_YARD[pos] · total_yards, fitted through the origin
formulas.inputs: projected stat line, position
formulas.constants: Fitted on 2023-25 REG, players with 200+ total yards: QB 0.04998 (R²=0.9896), RB 0.04964 (0.9417), WR 0.04715 (0.9382), TE 0.05090 (0.9105) — approximately one first down per twenty yards.
formulas.mathIssues: This is the ONE genuinely calibrated constant in the whole subsystem, with a stated fit, R², and a documented rationale for fitting through the origin. It fires only for projection lines (impute_first_downs=True at projections.py:145), never for realized rows that carry the real columns — a structural double-count guard. It matters a lot here: this league pays bonus_fd_qb 0.67 and bonus_fd_rb/wr/te 1.00.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A line that already carries first downs is passed through untouched; an unmeasured position returns None rather than a league average; a league that pays nothing multiplies by 0.0.
formulas.validated: YES — fitted with reported R² per position and per-season drift (2.0–4.8%). The only validated formula found.

formulas.name: Combined-tackle solo/assist split
formulas.expression: def_tackles_solo = combined · 0.62;  def_tackle_assists = combined · 0.38;  the raw `def_tackles` key is then DELETED
formulas.inputs: a source publishing only combined tackles
formulas.constants: TACKLE_SOLO_SHARE = 0.62, described as 'the league-wide empirical share' with no citation
formulas.mathIssues: A single league-wide constant applied to every defender. Solo share genuinely varies by position and scheme (box safeties and off-ball LBs differ materially from edge rushers). This league pays idp_tkl_solo 1.33 vs idp_tkl_ast 0.80, so the split moves points by (1.33−0.80)·combined·Δshare — a 5-point share error on a 100-tackle season is 2.65 points. The deletion of `def_tackles` is correct and well-documented (realized_points interprets that name as the PRE-2025 gamebook SOLO total).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: When solo/assist are published directly, no split is applied. The approximation is surfaced in the parse report, never silent.
formulas.validated: none found — the 'empirical share' is asserted, not shown

formulas.name: Production z-score (survival input)
formulas.expression:
mean, stdev = fmean/pstdev of consensus µ across the player's LINEUP GROUP
production_z = clip( (µ_player − mean) / stdev , −2, +2 )
formulas.inputs: the whole consensus set grouped by lineup group
formulas.constants: clip ±2.0; survival's production_z gamma 0.18
formulas.mathIssues: Uses population stdev over EVERY projected player in the group, including deep-bench fringe with near-zero µ, so the mean is dragged low and almost every rostered starter scores z ≈ +1 to +2 and gets the maximum hazard discount. The group is the lineup group (DL/LB/DB), not the true position, so a DT is z-scored against edge rushers.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Group not in group_stats → (µ_player, 1.0) is used, i.e. z = 0 exactly. Single-member group → stdev forced to 1.0.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Quick starter FPG (roster display)
formulas.expression: fill fixed starter slots greedily by group on descending projected FPG, then each flex slot with the best remaining eligible player; sum
formulas.inputs: roster assets with fpg and group; starters/flex from the league config
formulas.constants: none
formulas.mathIssues: Greedy, not the exact bipartite solve — explicitly deferred to src/ros/lineup.py per ADR-004. Greedy fixed-then-flex can be suboptimal when a flex-eligible player is better used in a fixed slot. Labelled a heuristic in the payload meta ('starterFpgMethod').
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing group → contributes 0 to that slot. Fewer players than slots → the slot contributes nothing (no replacement-level fill), so a thin roster's starterFpg is understated relative to a deep one.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Positional means (baseline shrink target)
formulas.expression: mean season-PPG per position over player-seasons with games ≥ 8 AND ppg ≥ 1.0
formulas.inputs: realized PPG history
formulas.constants: min_games 8.0, _MIN_PPG_FLOOR 1.0
formulas.mathIssues: Both filters bias the target UPWARD (they exclude injured and fringe seasons), and the target is what a low-sample player is shrunk toward — so a player with 4 games is pulled 90% of the way toward a mean computed only from healthy full seasons. Direction: overstates fringe players.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A position with no qualifying seasons is absent from the map; `build_reconstructed_baseline` then reads `positional_means.get(pos, 0.0)` → shrinks toward ZERO, silently. That is a genuine silent-zero path in a module whose stated rule is never to impute a zero.
formulas.validated: none found

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. I read every file in src/bdvm/ (27 modules), src/api/bdvm_api.py, src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py, all three config/bdvm/*.json, the four scripts, the frontend consumers, and the docs. pytest is not installed in this environment, so I reproduced the parity fixture by importing tests/bdvm/test_engine_parity.py directly and running the PRODUCTION engine against it. I made no writes to the repository.

WHAT I VERIFIED NUMERICALLY (all with production code, not reimplementations):
- Engine parity: all 13 reference archetypes × 3 strategies reproduce Appendix C within 1.0 (p1 9800.0/7974.1/6264.6 vs golden 9800/7974/6265, …), and all 7 replacement levels match to 2dp. The parity fixture DOES pin the live engine, not a frozen copy — it imports src.bdvm.engine.DynastyEngine directly. tests/bdvm/test_reference_parity.py is a different thing: it re-runs the frozen docs/research/bdvm-v1/reference/run_examples.py and diffs its own committed output, which guards the fixture from edits and proves nothing about production.
- Parity scope caveat: the fixture uses SYNTHETIC exponential-decay pools and 13 hand-built PlayerInputs. It pins season_path, discounting, scaling, replacement solving and probabilities. It pins NOTHING in projections.py, service.py, market.py, roster.py, ros.py, actuals.py or events.py.
- Surplus mode comparison, sigma_fpg, hazard schedules, CES package math, ROS blend weights, baseline shrink, event effective_impact at 0.45 vs 0.9, pick EVs, waiver-buffer sensitivity, the scoring-coverage audit against the live 141-key card, and the reception-band omission — numbers are in the formulas and findings blocks.

ANSWERS TO THE SIX CRITICAL QUESTIONS:
1. CIRCULARITY — the fundamental is genuinely market-free WITHIN a run. tests/bdvm/test_service.py:169-183 strips every canonicalSiteValues entry from the contract and asserts the fundamental dict is byte-identical; market_comparison raises MarketIsolationError if called with empty fundamentals; market_view_for_row is only invoked at service.py:544, after engine.calibrate + engine.value. Rank-signal sources are correctly refused as prices. I found no path by which a market number reaches a fundamental. The real problem is not circularity, it is INCOMMENSURABILITY: the gap subtracts a γ=1.2-power-transformed, pool-anchored quantity from a crowd board, with no distributional alignment, and for this league the two price different scoring rules entirely (see the reception-band finding). Two secondary market touches are declared but under-labelled: the trade scan's fairness gate uses market values, and its 'model_clearing' fallback is a 50/50 blend.
2. PROXY FRACTION — Not Verifiable from Repository, because data/ is gitignored repo-wide and data/bdvm/ does not exist on this checkout. What IS verifiable: with only the baseline stage having run, 100% of records are is_proxy=True (build_reconstructed_baseline hardcodes it at projections.py:585), the refresh script exits 0 and logs 'PROXY-ONLY snapshot written' in that case (refresh_bdvm_projections.py:276-281), and IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT records 2,815 proxy records for the 2026 build. Clay is the only real OFFENSE source and self-skips without poppler-utils; IDP Show self-skips without a session jar; the report's own third-pass addendum notes both failed on production 2026-07-30.
3. PARAMS — priors, and the file says so unambiguously: 'EVERY number here is a STARTING PRIOR from the BDVM v1.0 research document … informed by published research but NOT backtested truth'. The only calibrated constant I found anywhere in the subsystem is FIRST_DOWNS_PER_YARD (fitted, R² 0.91–0.99, reported per position and per season). Validation infrastructure exists (src/bdvm/backtest.py) and has zero production callers.
4. TEMPORAL LEAKAGE — none found in the reconstructed baseline. build_reconstructed_baseline filters `s.season < season` (projections.py:544) and fetch_and_build_baseline fetches `range(season - seasons_back, season)` (baseline.py:276). The rookie-slot prior uses only PAST rookies' rookie seasons. actuals.py deliberately returns None outside Sept–Jan so a completed season is never blended into the next season's board. The backtest harness enforces an as-of cutoff structurally (LeakageError). This part of the design is sound.
5. NEWS LANE — the clamp is real and I verified it directly: at confidence 0.45 the six effective rules produce ONLY sigma_mult ∈ [1.018, 1.072]; applying a DEPTH_CHART_DEMOTION left fpg at 14.0 and games at 17.0 unchanged. A headline cannot move a mean. Two caveats: five of the eleven mapped rules produce nothing at all, and the surviving σ effect is small enough (≤7%, decaying, reaching value only through the option term) that the lane's practical influence is near zero — which is worth knowing before anyone cites it as a live reactive feed.
6. FIXTURE — pins the live engine. Confirmed by execution.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY: the live board's actual player counts, priced/unpriced split, and proxy fraction (no data/bdvm/); the 2026-07-26 KTC↔IDPTC comparability study cited in market.py comments (referenced in comments only, not in the repo); whether the production box currently has the dynasty-bdvm-refresh timer installed; whether reception_depth data exists on production (load_reception_depth(2025) returns None here).

THINGS THAT SURPRISED ME, in a good way: the market-isolation test is a genuinely strong structural gate, not a shape assertion. The news→events merge logic (refuses on wrong-shape JSON, exempts human-raised confidence from pruning, same-fact suppression across providers) is the most carefully-defended code in the subsystem. scoring_coverage.py probes the scorer rather than parsing it, and is the reason I could quantify the reception-band gap at all — it already classifies those six keys as UNSCORABLE. first_down_rate.py is a model of how a constant should be introduced. The missing-data posture is consistently honest: unpriced-with-a-reason appears everywhere, and I found exactly one silent-zero path (positional_means.get(pos, 0.0) at projections.py:578).

DEAD OR UNREACHABLE CODE: src/bdvm/backtest.py (336 lines, no production caller). market.py's `w_model` (computed, stamped, never used to blend). `class_strength` in picks.py (no caller passes it). STRONG_BUY. gap_persistence_days, strong_buy_min_liquidity. Seven params_v1.json sections. RiskProfile.scheme_stability is set but no formula reads it. `p_active` in RosWeek is always 1.0.

BOTTOM LINE ON WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE DECISIONS: today, none of them, for two independent reasons. First, there is no projection data on this checkout and production has a documented history of the same, so the board is empty. Second, even with data, the fundamental values for this specific league omit ~15% of a WR's scoring and 0% of a QB's, rest entirely on unvalidated priors whose most sensitive knob demonstrably moves relative ordering, and are compared against a market board computed under different scoring rules and a different distributional shape. The engineering is careful and unusually honest about its own limits; the numbers are not yet earned. The single highest-value next step is not more features — it is running the backtest harness that already exists against the 131 dated contract archives, starting with the surplus-mode ablation, which needs no new data at all.
