formulas.name: Lead score (total)
formulas.expression: score = 100 x max(0, 0.34*interest + 0.26*(partner_fit_raw/43.12) + 0.18*need + 0.12*value_match + 0.10*activity - contradiction - low_sample)
formulas.inputs: interest 0-1 (ledger revealed preference, unitless); partner_fit_raw 0-100 display (roster_intel.partner); need 0-1 (ordinal within roster); value_match 0-1; activity 0-1; contradiction 0-0.20; low_sample 0-0.12
formulas.constants: W_DEMONSTRATED_INTEREST=0.34, W_PARTNER_FIT=0.26, W_POSITIONAL_NEED=0.18, W_VALUE_MATCH=0.12, W_ACTIVITY=0.10 (sum verified = 1.0), MAX_CONTRADICTION_PENALTY=0.20, MAX_LOW_SAMPLE_PENALTY=0.12. ALL hand-picked — no calibration artifact, backtest, or holdout exists anywhere in the repo for these values.
formulas.outputRange: 0-100 nominal. Verified reachable maximum with all terms maxed = 80.7. Verified no-evidence floor: 0.0 (no roster data) rising to 33.1 with only a shallow positional gap + saturated value match.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Every input abstains to 0 independently. A manager with no interest observation still receives the FULL -0.12 low-sample penalty (leads.py:223 returns MAX when volume==0), and the max(0,.) floor then clamps the sum, so no-evidence and negative-evidence both render 0.0 when nothing else contributes.
formulas.mathIssues: The max(0,.) floor at :361 breaks reconciliation with `components`: for buys=0/sells=2 the components sum to -0.248 while `score` is 0.0, and InsiderLeads.jsx:88-118 renders those components as a breakdown of that 0.0. Partner fit is divided by the reachable MAX (43.12) but not shifted by the reachable MIN (7.24), so the worst partner still contributes 4.4 points.
formulas.validated: none found — no backtest script, no calibration config, no holdout, no error rate. Contrast: the adjusted-board feature in this repo ships docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md + scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py; nothing equivalent exists for leads.

formulas.name: Demonstrated interest strength
formulas.expression: depth = wanted/(wanted+1.5); breadth = min(1, unique_leagues/2) if unique_leagues else 0.5; recency = 0.5^(age_days/45); strength = min(1, depth * (0.55 + 0.25*breadth + 0.20*recency))
formulas.inputs: wanted = obs.buys (direction='buy') or obs.sells (direction='sell'); unique_leagues from ledger COUNT(DISTINCT league_id); last_ts ms epoch
formulas.constants: 1.5 (depth saturation), 2.0 (breadth saturation), 0.55/0.25/0.20 (base/breadth/recency split, sums to 1.0), INTEREST_HALF_LIFE_DAYS=45.0. All hand-picked.
formulas.outputRange: 0-1, but structurally capped below 1: depth->1 needs infinite acquisitions. Verified: 1 buy/1 lg/5d = 0.344; 3 buys/3 lgs/2d = 0.663; 3 buys/3 lgs/300d = 0.535; 6 buys/4 lgs/now = 0.800.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: obs None or volume 0 -> (0.0, [], []). wanted <= 0 -> returns 0.0 BEFORE building the cautions list, so a manager who only ever SOLD the asset (in sell mode) emits no reason AND no caution — indistinguishable from a manager with no data except for the raw counts in the interest cell.
formulas.mathIssues: breadth defaults to 0.5 when unique_leagues is 0/falsy, which the ledger never produces for a real row (COUNT(DISTINCT) >= 1), so the branch is effectively dead. Recency uses `max(0, now - last_ts)`, so a clock-skewed future timestamp reads as recency 1.0 rather than being rejected.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Contradiction penalty
formulas.expression: penalty = 0.20 * (against / volume) * (1.0 if wanted else 1.0)
formulas.inputs: against = sells when direction='buy' (else buys); volume = buys + sells
formulas.constants: MAX_CONTRADICTION_PENALTY = 0.20
formulas.missingDataBehavior: obs None or volume 0 or against <= 0 -> 0.0
formulas.mathIssues: The trailing factor `(1.0 if wanted else 1.0)` is a no-op — both branches are 1.0. The comment immediately above ('one who ONLY moved him against us is a negative lead') states an asymmetry the code does not implement. Verified numerically: buys=0/sells=2 and buys=2/sells=2 both produce the ratio-only penalty.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Low-sample penalty
formulas.inputs: obs.volume (buys+sells)
formulas.constants: MAX_LOW_SAMPLE_PENALTY = 0.12; multipliers 0.4 and 0.8; threshold 3
formulas.missingDataBehavior: obs None -> volume 0 -> FULL 0.12 penalty. This is the intended 'absence is discounted' behaviour, but combined with the max(0,.) floor it makes zero-evidence and adverse-evidence collapse to the same displayed 0.0.
formulas.mathIssues: none beyond the reconciliation issue above
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Positional need fit
formulas.expression: pool = [deficits (buy) or surpluses (sell)]; fit = clamp(magnitude[pos] / max(pool), 0, 1)
formulas.inputs: RosterSignal.deficit / .surplus from roster_shape.team_signals, in units of 'starter slots above/below requirement'
formulas.constants: reason thresholds 0.75 ('one of their biggest gaps') and 0.4 ('Roster needs X')
formulas.missingDataBehavior: their_roster None or position None or magnitude<=0 or empty pool -> (0.0, []). Picks always abstain (no position in the contract map).
formulas.mathIssues: Normalising against the roster's OWN maximum destroys all magnitude information and makes the term non-comparable across managers — yet it is summed into a CROSS-MANAGER ranking. Verified: deficits {QB:0.1, RB:0.05} and {QB:3.0, RB:0.5} both yield fit=1.0 for QB, and both produce lead score 33.1 with everything else held constant. The docstring's stated intent ('so a roster with mild needs everywhere does not read as desperate') is the opposite of what the code does.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Value match
formulas.expression: best = min over their assets of |v - target|/target; best<=0.18 -> 1.0; best>=0.54 -> 0.0; else 1 - (best-0.18)/(0.54-0.18)
formulas.inputs: target = contract rankDerivedValue of the asset (0-9999); their_matchable_values = every rankDerivedValue on their roster (roster_shape.matchable_values, NO floor applied)
formulas.constants: tolerance = 0.18; span = 3 x tolerance = 0.54
formulas.missingDataBehavior: target falsy/<=0 or no matchable values -> 0.0 (abstains). With no loaded contract, `values` is empty -> this term is 0 for everyone.
formulas.mathIssues: Empirically degenerate. Monte-Carlo over the live board's value distribution (exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json, 1074 priced assets, _finalAdjusted as the 0-9999 scale proxy), 3000 random 25-player rosters drawn from the top 400: P(score == 1.0) = 45.3% at board rank 1, 77.9% at rank 10, 99.0% at rank 50, 100.0% at rank 150 and rank 300 (mean score 1.000). Real rosters include deep-bench values too, which only increases coverage. So for any asset outside roughly the top 20 the term is a CONSTANT +12 points on every lead and contributes zero ranking information.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Activity fit
formulas.expression: mean = league_mean if >0 else 3.0; score = min(1, tanh(trades_completed / mean)); reason fires when trades_completed >= max(3, int(mean * 1.5))
formulas.inputs: trades_completed and league_mean_trades from lead_service._trade_counts (90d window)
formulas.constants: fallback mean 3.0; reason threshold multiplier 1.5
formulas.outputRange: 0-1, weighted 0.10. At ratio 1.0 -> tanh(1)=0.762; at ratio 2.67 -> 0.990.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: trades_completed <= 0 -> 0.0. league_mean None/0 -> silently substitutes 3.0, a hard-coded guess about league trade volume.
formulas.mathIssues: The input is inflated — see the _trade_counts formula below. Because the inflation factor scales with assets-per-trade, it is NOT a common scale factor: a manager who does five 1-for-1 trades reads as 10, one who does five 3-for-3 trades reads as 30. The ratio to the mean is therefore distorted, not merely rescaled, and the reason string surfaces the inflated raw count to the user.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Trades-completed per manager (the inflated input)
formulas.location: src/intel/lead_service.py:81-95 (and the identical pattern at src/intel/service.py:783)
formulas.expression: counts[uid] = SUM over (user,asset) groups of COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id); mean = sum(counts)/len(counts)
formulas.inputs: ledger.manager_asset_activity rows, GROUP BY user_id, asset_id (ledger.py:892-904)
formulas.constants: 90d window
formulas.outputRange: integer, systematically >= the true transaction count
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty pool -> ({}, None) -> activity_fit falls back to mean 3.0
formulas.mathIssues: CONFIRMED N-times over-count. Reproduced against a real ledger: one 4-for-4 trade between users A and B produced 8 movement rows; manager_asset_activity returned 4 rows per user each with tradeCount=1; the sum gave A=4 and B=4 against a truth of 1 each. ledger.counts(user_ids=['A']) on the same data correctly returns tradeCount=1, assetMovementCount=4. This is exactly the unit conversion docs/intel/METRICS.md forbids ('Most counting bugs in this domain come from silently converting one into another'). Also O(n^2): the dict comprehension at :91 rescans `rows` once per user.
formulas.validated: none found — and unpinnable by the existing test, whose fixture has one asset per trade

formulas.name: Signal strength
formulas.expression: 100 x clamp(net/volume, -1, 1) x volume/(volume+5) x unique_managers/(unique_managers+3) x manager_quality
formulas.inputs: net, volume, unique_managers from one window's ledger.asset_signals row; manager_quality = 1.0 for Insider Trading (cohort is league membership, not skill)
formulas.constants: _CONFIDENCE_HALF_VOLUME = 5.0, _BREADTH_HALF_MANAGERS = 3.0
formulas.outputRange: -100..100. Verified: 1 buy/1 mgr = 4.17; 40 buys/39 sells/8 mgrs = 0.87; 6 buys/6 mgrs = 36.36.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: volume <= 0 -> 0.0. Missing windows are backfilled with explicit zeros (signals.py:286-290) so a gap can never render as 'no data'.
formulas.mathIssues: None. The construction is sound and matches docs/intel/METRICS.md verbatim. Note that the maximum attainable is well below 100 (unanimous 6-manager signal = 36.4), which is not disclosed — but it is not rendered anywhere either.
formulas.validated: behaviourally pinned by tests/intel/test_signals.py::TestVolumeNeverOptional; no external calibration

formulas.name: Sample confidence / breadth factor
formulas.expression: sample_confidence = v/(v+5); breadth_factor = m/(m+3)
formulas.inputs: v = observation volume, m = unique managers
formulas.constants: 5.0 and 3.0, both hand-picked with a stated rationale in the module docstring that does not match them
formulas.mathIssues: signals.py:68-69 claims 'a single observation is visibly weak (~0.09) and a dozen is strong (~0.86)'. Computed: 1 -> 0.1667, 12 -> 0.7059. The docstring's calibration commentary describes a half-volume of ~10, not the 5.0 in the code. Cosmetic (the values are not user-facing) but the comment is wrong.
formulas.validated: tests/intel/test_signals.py::test_sample_confidence_is_saturating asserts monotone saturation only, not the constants

formulas.name: Velocity
formulas.expression: (short_volume/short_span_ms) / (long_volume/long_span_ms), rounded to 3dp; None when long_volume < 3
formulas.inputs: the 48h-or-7d window and the 30d-or-90d window from the same asset (signals.py:314-315)
formulas.constants: minimum long-window volume = 3
formulas.missingDataBehavior: missing spans or long_volume < 3 or long_rate <= 0 -> None (explicitly refuses to invent a large number from a tiny denominator)
formulas.mathIssues: None. Because the short window is a strict subset, shared events cancel — this is the one construction here that is provably immune to the retired trendScore's overlapping-window sum.
formulas.validated: tests/intel/test_signals.py::test_velocity_of_a_steady_rate_is_one

formulas.name: Confidence tier
formulas.expression: volume<=0 -> 'insufficient'; volume>=12 AND managers>=4 AND leagues>=3 -> 'high'; volume>=5 AND managers>=2 -> 'medium'; else 'low'
formulas.inputs: volume, unique_managers, unique_leagues from the primary window
formulas.constants: 12/4/3 and 5/2 — hand-picked, no derivation given anywhere
formulas.missingDataBehavior: volume 0 -> 'insufficient', rendered as an em dash
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: tests/intel/test_signals.py pins the boundary behaviour; the thresholds themselves are unjustified

formulas.name: Per-window asset aggregation
formulas.expression: buys = SUM(action='add'); sells = SUM(action='drop'); net = buys - sells; volume = buys + sells; buyRate = buys/volume; uniqueLeagues = COUNT(DISTINCT league_id); tradeCount = COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id); movementCount = COUNT(*) — all GROUP BY asset_id over rows filtered to ts window, tx_type IN ('trade',), user_id IN pool
formulas.inputs: asset_movements rows
formulas.constants: TRADE_TX_TYPES = ('trade',) is the default — waivers are structurally out of reach of a buy/sell number
formulas.missingDataBehavior: volume 0 -> buyRate null (never 0.0, so 'no data' and 'all sells' cannot read the same); lastTs 0 -> None
formulas.mathIssues: Correct as written. Note the documented consequence: an intra-pool trade emits a paired add and drop, so it nets to exactly 0, while the same acquisition from an untracked counterparty nets +1 — the number depends on crawl coverage, not market behaviour. AUDIT.md §3 acknowledges this and it is unfixed by design.
formulas.validated: tests/intel/test_ledger.py::TestUnitSeparation, ::TestTimeWindows, ::TestIdempotency

formulas.name: Snapshot staleness
formulas.expression: staleHours = round((now_utc - generatedAt).total_seconds()/3600, 2); banner fires when staleHours > 30
formulas.inputs: state['generatedAt'] ISO string stamped by store.save_state
formulas.constants: STALE_WARN_HOURS = 30 (cron is daily, so >30h means at least one missed run)
formulas.outputRange: float hours, or null when no snapshot exists
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no generatedAt -> None -> the frontend renders a distinct 'No intel snapshot yet' card rather than a staleness warning (page.jsx:110-119). Naive datetimes are coerced to UTC.
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: tests/intel/test_endpoints.py::test_refresh_status_stamps_snapshot_staleness

formulas.name: Pick-ownership horizon
formulas.expression: rounds = clamp(league.settings.draft_rounds, 1, 6) default 4; base_year = league.season (fallback wall-clock year), +1 when league.status not in {'', 'pre_draft', 'drafting'}; seed ownership[(season, round, roster)] = roster for 3 seasons; overwrite from /traded_picks entries keyed (season, round, original roster_id)
formulas.inputs: league season + status + settings.draft_rounds from the /user/{id}/leagues payload; Sleeper /league/{id}/traded_picks
formulas.constants: PICK_HOLDINGS_YEARS=3, DEFAULT_DRAFT_ROUNDS=4, MAX_DRAFT_ROUNDS=6
formulas.outputRange: up to 3 x 6 = 18 pick asset ids per roster
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A FAILED /traded_picks fetch never publishes derived defaults (crawler.py:644-661) — it carries the last known pick holdings forward and re-queues the league. A league that has never had a successful pick fetch stays in the retry cursor.
formulas.mathIssues: The default-ownership seed is an ASSUMPTION, not observed data: any pick Sleeper does not report as traded is credited to its original roster. Sleeper's /traded_picks is authoritative for diffs, so this is standard practice, but a UI reading 'Alice holds 4 first-rounders' is partly derived and nothing labels it as such.
formulas.validated: tests/intel/test_defect_fixes.py::TestD9PickHorizon

formulas.name: Roster surplus/deficit signal
formulas.expression: req[pos] = sum of starter slots, with flex slots split evenly across eligible positions (FLEX/3, SFLEX/4, IDP_FLEX/3); gap = have - req; gap>0 -> surplus[pos]=gap; gap<0 -> deficit[pos]=-gap
formulas.inputs: contract sleeper.teams playerIds, contract playersArray positions, league registry roster_settings.starters
formulas.constants: _FLEX_ELIGIBLE mapping; starter_value_floor default 0.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No teams, no positions, or no starter settings -> returns {} rather than guessing a lineup, which makes the whole positional-need and partner-fit half of the lead score abstain.
formulas.mathIssues: The documented roster-clog guard is INERT on the live path. roster_shape.py:93 gates on `starter_value_floor > 0`, and the only production caller (server.py:12208-12210) never passes it, so the parameter is 0.0 and every deep-bench body counts as depth. The docstring at :72-74 asserts the opposite behaviour, and tests/intel/test_lead_service.py:199-209 passes an explicit floor of 100.0 so the test passes while the live path is unguarded.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: FAAB rival expected bid (intel-fed)
formulas.expression: exp_bid = min(base_bid * agg * need_f * intel_f, base_bid * 2.5) * 1.15, then capped at faabRemaining; clearing = max(exp_bid over rivals with a known balance) + 1
formulas.inputs: base_bid (value bid); agg = clamp(their avgBid / league median winning bid, 0.5, 2.0) requiring winningCount>=3; need_f in {need:1.0, neutral:0.55, surplus:0.25}; intel_f in {1.0, 1.10, 1.25}
formulas.constants: INTEL_PLAYER_FACTOR=1.25, INTEL_POSITION_FACTOR=1.10, INTEL_WINDOW_MS=14 days, NEED_FACTORS 1.0/0.55/0.25, AGG_CLAMP (0.5, 2.0), AGG_MIN_WINNING_BIDS=3, STACK_CAP_MULT=2.5, SAFETY_MARGIN=1.15. Every one hand-picked; no calibration artifact found.
formulas.outputRange: integer FAAB dollars, hard-capped at 2.875x base_bid before the balance cap
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing snapshot -> intel_f=1.0 with an explicit note. winningCount<3 -> agg=1.0 with lowSample=True. Missing faabRemaining -> row shown but EXCLUDED from topRival/clearing (conservative). Missing position map -> position-level intel silently never fires.
formulas.mathIssues: build_intel_index (faab_contention.py:169-171) filters ONLY on action=='add' and assetType=='player' — it never reads txType, which is the exact defect AUDIT.md D1 records as 'Fixed' for the intel board. A rival who acquired a player in a TRADE is treated as identical evidence to a waiver claim. It also never reads leagueId, so an add in any of that manager's other Sleeper leagues raises their estimated bid in THIS league. Neither behaviour is stated in the module docstring, and the output is a dollar amount a user acts on.
formulas.validated: tests/trade/test_faab_contention.py exists; no calibration of the 1.25/1.10 multipliers against realized winning bids was found

formulas.name: Partner fit normalisation into the lead score
formulas.expression: fit_score = clamp((partner.trade_partner_fit_score or 0) / FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MAX, 0, 1)
formulas.inputs: partner_model.PartnerAssessment.trade_partner_fit_score
formulas.constants: FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MAX — computed live from partner.py's own constants, verified = 43.12 (with FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MIN = 7.24 and _MAX_REACHABLE_CONFIDENCE = 0.40)
formulas.outputRange: 0-1, weighted 0.26. Verified: a realistic strong partner assessment gave raw 22.51 -> 0.522 -> 0.136 contribution.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: partner None or fit_raw falsy -> 0.0, and partnerFitScore is stamped null so the UI renders an em dash rather than 0.0 (InsiderLeads.jsx:170-176). This is a correct 'not computed != computed as bad' distinction.
formulas.mathIssues: Divides by the reachable MAX but does not subtract the reachable MIN. The floor of partner.py's range is 7.24, so a partner scored at the worst attainable fit still contributes 7.24/43.12 x 0.26 = 0.0437, i.e. 4.4 display points of unearned credit on every lead where a roster snapshot exists.
formulas.validated: tests/intel/test_leads.py::TestPartnerFitNormalisation pins the division against the max; the floor offset is untested

formulas.name: Lead ranking order
formulas.expression: sort key = (-score, -interest.volume, owner_id)
formulas.inputs: scored Lead objects
formulas.constants: default limit 12 (lead_service.py:111) against a typical pool of 11 league-mates, so the limit effectively never binds
formulas.missingDataBehavior: no interest -> volume treated as 0, so no-evidence managers tie-break last within their score band and remain on the list rather than being filtered out (deliberate — docs/intel/LEADS.md §4)
formulas.mathIssues: none
formulas.validated: tests/intel/test_leads.py::TestRanking

findings.title: tradeCount is computed by summing per-asset transaction counts, inflating it by the number of assets in each trade
findings.evidence: src/intel/lead_service.py:90-93 — `counts = {uid: sum(int(r["tradeCount"] or 0) for r in rows if str(r["userId"]) == uid) for uid in per_user}` where `rows` comes from `ledger.manager_asset_activity(...)`, which is `GROUP BY user_id, asset_id` (src/intel/ledger.py:903) with `tradeCount = COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id)` per group. Identical pattern at src/intel/service.py:783 — `trade_count = sum(r["tradeCount"] for r in rows)`. Reproduced against a real SQLite ledger: one 4-for-4 trade between users A and B produced 8 movements; the sum yielded A=4, B=4 against a truth of 1 each, while `ledger.counts(user_ids=['A'])` on the same rows correctly returned `{'tradeCount': 1, 'assetMovementCount': 4, ...}`. docs/intel/METRICS.md defines `tradeCount` as 'Distinct tx_id values. Counts transactions.' and opens with 'Most counting bugs in this domain come from silently converting one into another.'
findings.userImpact: GET /api/intel/member/{owner_id} publishes a `tradeCount` that overstates a manager's trade volume by the mean assets-per-trade (typically 2-6x). Worse, the same inflated number is the `trades_completed` input to both `leads.activity_fit` and `roster_intel.partner.assess_partner` inside the lead score. The inflation is NOT a common scale factor: five 1-for-1 trades read as 10 while five 3-for-3 trades read as 30, so a manager who makes big multi-asset deals is ranked as ~3x more active than an equally frequent trader of singles. That distorts both the 0.10 activity term and partner.py's shrunk history logit, and the inflated raw count is shown to the user verbatim in the reason string 'Active trader — N trades observed' (leads.py:309).
findings.recommendedFix: Replace both call sites with `ledger.counts(user_ids=[...], since_ms=..., until_ms=...)['tradeCount']`, which already computes COUNT(DISTINCT tx_id) correctly (ledger.py:950). For the per-manager map in lead_service, add a `GROUP BY user_id` variant to ledger.py rather than summing in Python. Then extend the test fixture in tests/intel/test_endpoints.py::_seed_snapshot to include a multi-asset trade so the invariant is actually pinned.
findings.affectedSystems: Member cross-league profile; Activity fit; Partner-fit term (via trades_completed); Insider Trading lead score

findings.title: The documented roster-clog guard (starter_value_floor) is inert on the live path
findings.evidence: src/intel/roster_shape.py:67 declares `starter_value_floor: float = 0.0`; :93 gates on `if value_by_player is not None and starter_value_floor > 0:`. The only production caller is server.py:12208-12210 — `roster_shape.team_signals(teams, positions, league_cfg.roster_settings, value_by_player=values)` — which passes `value_by_player` but never `starter_value_floor`, so the filter never executes. The module docstring at roster_shape.py:71-74 states the opposite: 'A player counts toward a position only if their value clears `starter_value_floor` — roster clog is not depth, and counting it would make every deep bench look like a surplus.' `grep -rn 'starter_value_floor' --include=*.py .` shows the only place a non-zero floor is supplied is tests/intel/test_lead_service.py:207.
findings.userImpact: Every rostered body counts as positional depth, so surplus is systematically overstated and deficit understated for every manager. This propagates into the 0.18 positionalNeed term of the lead score in BUY mode (which reads `surplus`) and into `roster_intel.partner.assess_partner`'s need alignment, which itself carries 0.26 of the score. The lead list ranks managers on a roster shape that counts waiver flotsam as starters.
findings.recommendedFix: Pass an explicit floor at server.py:12208 derived from the board (e.g. the value at the replacement-level rank for each position, or a fixed percentile of `values`), and add a test that calls the LIVE assembly path (`server._build_intel_leads`) rather than `team_signals` directly, so the caller's argument list is what is pinned.
findings.affectedSystems: Roster surplus/deficit signal; Positional need fit; Partner-fit term; Insider Trading lead score

findings.title: Positional need is ordinal within a roster and carries no magnitude, but is summed into a cross-manager ranking
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:257-259 — `strongest = max(pool); fit = magnitude / strongest if strongest > 0 else 0.0`. Verified numerically through the full scorer with all other inputs held constant: deficits {QB: 0.1, RB: 0.05} and deficits {QB: 3.0, RB: 0.5} both yield `positionalNeed = 0.180` and an identical lead score of 33.1, and both emit the reason string 'QB is one of their biggest gaps'. The docstring at leads.py:257-258 claims the normalisation exists 'so a roster with mild needs everywhere does not read as desperate' — it produces exactly that outcome. tests/intel/test_leads.py:147 (`test_need_is_normalised_against_their_own_gaps`) pins this as intended behaviour.
findings.userImpact: The 0.18-weighted term is a within-roster rank, not a need measure, so it is not comparable between the managers it is being used to rank. A manager whose deepest hole is 0.1 starter slots is credited the same 18 points as one who is three starters short at that position. The reason string tells the user 'QB is one of their biggest gaps' about a roster with no meaningful gap at all — inference from a normalisation artefact presented as a fact about the manager.
findings.recommendedFix: Normalise the deficit against the STARTER REQUIREMENT for that position (magnitude / req[pos], already computed in roster_shape) rather than against the roster's own maximum, so the term is on a common scale across managers. Gate the 'one of their biggest gaps' reason on an absolute threshold as well as the relative one.
findings.affectedSystems: Positional need fit; Insider Trading lead score

findings.title: The value-match term is saturated for essentially every lead and contributes no ranking information
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:289-290 — `if best <= tolerance: return 1.0, [...]` with `tolerance = 0.18`, against `their_matchable_values` = every priced player on their roster (src/intel/roster_shape.py:123-143, no floor). Monte-Carlo over the live board's actual value distribution (exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json, 1074 priced assets, `_finalAdjusted` as the 0-9999 scale proxy), 3000 random 25-player rosters drawn from the top 400: P(valueMatch == 1.0) = 45.3% for a rank-1 asset, 77.9% at rank 10, 99.0% at rank 50, 100.0% at rank 150 and rank 300 (mean 1.000). Real rosters carry deep-bench values too, which only widens coverage.
findings.userImpact: For any target outside roughly the top 20 of the board — i.e. almost every query — the 0.12-weighted term adds a constant +12 points to every league-mate and discriminates between none of them. It inflates the headline number without informing the ranking, and the breakdown row 'Value-matched assets +12.0' (InsiderLeads.jsx:47) reads to the user as a discovered fact about that specific manager when it is true of everyone.
findings.recommendedFix: Either (a) score against the SPREAD of matchable values (e.g. how many assets sit in band, or the closest gap on a continuous scale with no 1.0 plateau), or (b) drop the term and redistribute its weight, or (c) restrict `matchable_values` to assets that clear a tradeable-value floor so a bench body cannot satisfy the match. Whichever is chosen, add a test that measures the term's variance across a realistic 12-roster league rather than across two synthetic values.
findings.affectedSystems: Value match; Insider Trading lead score

findings.title: The lead score has no error rate, no calibration and no disclosed reachable range, while rendering a no-evidence manager as an amber 33/100
findings.evidence: All five weights and both penalty caps are hand-picked literals (src/intel/leads.py:68-79) with no calibration artifact anywhere: no backtest script, no holdout, no config under config/. Verified score behaviour with ZERO demonstrated interest (the common case — the payload itself reports `leadsWithObservedInterest`, lead_service.py:179): a manager whose top positional gap happens to be the asset's position scores 33.1; a secondary gap scores 21.1; no gap at all scores 15.1. InsiderLeads.jsx:52-56 `scoreColor` renders >= 30 as `var(--amber)` and ScoreBar (:58-86) fills a bar as a percentage of 100. The verified reachable maximum with every term maxed is 80.7. `describe_limitations()` (leads.py:395-419) states 'not a probability' and a coverage caveat, but never states an error rate, a reachable range, or that a score in the 15-33 band can be produced with no observed evidence about the asset at all. Contrast: this repo ships docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md + scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py for the league-adjusted board, and the same module goes to the trouble of normalising partner fit against ITS reachable max (leads.py:349).
findings.userImpact: A number that ranks the people a user is about to negotiate with is presented on an implied 0-100 scale, coloured amber at 33, with no statement of what a good score is or how often the ranking is right. Because the two terms that fire without any evidence (valueMatch, saturated at 12; positionalNeed, ordinal) sum to 30 before any real signal, the display cannot distinguish 'this manager wants him' from 'this manager exists and has a roster'.
findings.recommendedFix: Publish `reachableMin`/`reachableMax` in the payload the way partner.py already publishes its bounds (partner.py:488-494), and extend `describe_limitations()` with an explicit 'no acceptance or engagement rate has been measured; these weights are priors, not validated' statement. Then either recolour the UI against the reachable range, or suppress the score entirely (show reasons only) when `interest` is None — which is the honest rendering of 'we observed nothing about this manager and this asset'.

findings.title: The component breakdown does not reconcile with the displayed score whenever the zero floor bites
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:361 `total = max(0.0, total - contradiction - low_sample)` clamps, but :364-372 writes the UNCLAMPED components including the negative penalties. Verified: for `buys=0, sells=2` in sell mode, `score = 0.0` while `components` = {demonstratedInterest 0.0, contradictionPenalty -0.20, lowSamplePenalty -0.048} — a sum of -0.248. For a manager with no data at all, `score = 0.0` with `lowSamplePenalty = -0.12`. frontend/components/InsiderLeads.jsx:88-118 renders every component x100 as an audit breakdown of that score.
findings.userImpact: Expanding a 0.0-scored lead shows rows totalling -24.8, which no reader can reconcile with the 0.0 headline. The expander is explicitly labelled 'Score breakdown' and is the feature's transparency mechanism, so an unreconcilable breakdown undermines the one thing it exists to provide.
findings.recommendedFix: Either stamp a `clampedFrom` / `rawTotal` field alongside `components` so the UI can show the clamp explicitly, or scale the penalties down to the amount actually applied. Add a test asserting `abs(sum(components.values()) * 100 - score) < 0.05` across the penalty-dominated cases.

findings.title: The board page claims it shows trades made in 'OTHER Sleeper leagues' but the board applies no home-league exclusion
findings.evidence: frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx:481 renders the subtitle `Trades your league-mates made in their OTHER Sleeper leagues — ...`. src/intel/service.py:541-548 calls `ledger.asset_signals(since_ms=..., until_ms=..., tx_types=..., user_ids=pool, ...)` with no league exclusion, and `asset_signals` has no `exclude_league_ids` parameter at all (ledger.py:702-712). By contrast the LEADS path does exclude it — lead_service.py:127 passes `exclude_league_ids=home_league_ids`, and ledger.manager_asset_activity supports it (ledger.py:862, 889-891), with the reason spelled out at lead_service.py:52-56 and pinned by tests/intel/test_lead_service.py::TestHomeLeagueExclusion.
findings.userImpact: Home-league trades are counted on the board. Per AUDIT.md §3 both counterparties in a home-league trade are always tracked, so those movements contribute volume, manager counts and league counts while netting to exactly zero — inflating the confidence tier and the volume column for assets whose only activity was inside the user's own league, which the user already knows about and which the page promises is excluded.
findings.recommendedFix: Either add `exclude_league_ids` to `ledger.asset_signals` and pass the resolved league's Sleeper id from `build_summary_payload`, or correct the page subtitle to say 'across every Sleeper league we track for your league-mates, including this one'. Decide which behaviour is wanted rather than leaving copy and code disagreeing.
findings.affectedSystems: Insider Trading asset board; /league/insider-trading page copy

findings.title: The contradiction penalty's asymmetry is a no-op ternary — the stated intent is never implemented
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:209-211 — `# A manager who both bought and sold him is genuinely ambiguous; / # one who ONLY moved him against us is a negative lead. / return MAX_CONTRADICTION_PENALTY * share * (1.0 if wanted else 1.0)`. Both branches of the ternary are `1.0`. Verified: `buys=0, sells=2` (only adverse) and `buys=2, sells=2` (genuinely ambiguous) are penalised by the share ratio alone with no additional weighting.
findings.userImpact: A manager who has only ever moved the asset AWAY is treated identically to one who has been on both sides, contradicting the module's own stated model. Combined with `demonstrated_interest` returning early at leads.py:168-169 (before building cautions) when `wanted <= 0`, such a manager renders with no reason AND no caution — the adverse evidence is silently absorbed by the max(0,.) floor and never shown.
findings.recommendedFix: Implement the intended asymmetry (e.g. a larger multiplier when `wanted == 0`) or delete the ternary and the comment that describes it. Separately, emit the 'also moved this asset the other way' caution even when `wanted == 0` so one-sided adverse evidence is visible.
findings.affectedSystems: Contradiction penalty; Demonstrated interest; Insider Trading lead score

findings.title: The FAAB rival-bid intel index reproduces defect D1 (waiver adds counted as trade adds) and silently crosses leagues
findings.evidence: src/trade/faab_contention.py:169-171 filters only on `if e.get("action") != "add": continue` and `if str(e.get("assetType") or "player") != "player": continue`. There is no `txType` check, although the crawler stamps it on every event (src/intel/crawler.py:307) and docs/intel/AUDIT.md D1 records exactly this omission as the headline defect, marked 'Fixed'. There is also no `leagueId` check anywhere in the function, and the snapshot's `events` list spans every league the crawl reached. The output feeds `intel_factor` -> 1.25/1.10 multipliers -> `exp_bid` (faab_contention.py:398-401) -> the recommended clearing bid.
findings.userImpact: A rival's estimated FAAB bid is raised 25% because they acquired that player in a TRADE (in a different league), which is not evidence they will bid on him on waivers here. The 1.10 position-level factor fires on any positional add anywhere in the last 14 days. The result is a dollar figure the user spends real budget against, built on cross-league evidence of a different transaction type, with the mechanism undocumented in the module's own docstring (which says only 'this owner added THIS player in another league recently').
findings.recommendedFix: Filter `build_intel_index` to `txType in ('waiver', 'free_agent')` — the transaction types that are actually evidence of waiver appetite — or, if trade adds are wanted, weight them separately and say so. Decide explicitly whether cross-league adds should count and document the answer. Add a test asserting a trade-type event does not raise `intel_factor`.

findings.title: The player drill-down is hardcoded to the 30d window and its movement receipts cannot audit the 90d counts
findings.evidence: src/intel/service.py:665-677 fetches `per_member` and `movements` using `signals.window_bounds(signals.INSIDER_DEFAULT_WINDOW, now_ms)` (30d) with `limit=100`, while `window_names = list(signals.INSIDER_WINDOWS)` (:647) renders 7d/30d/90d counts; `payload['window']` is hardcoded to the default at :751. server.py:12328-12371 (get_intel_player) accepts no `window` parameter. The board's drill-down fetch (page.jsx:143-145) sends only `playerId` and `leagueKey`, so switching the board to 90d leaves the drill-down showing '30d'. docs/intel/METRICS.md §'Time windows' claims 'a drill-down transaction list lets any number be audited back to its movements.'
findings.userImpact: A user who selects the 90-day board window and clicks a row sees member-exposure counts and a movement list scoped to 30 days, labelled 30d, next to 90d aggregates that cannot be reconciled from the receipts shown. The auditability guarantee METRICS.md advertises does not hold for two of the three windows.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a `window` query parameter to GET /api/intel/player, allow-list it the same way the summary route does (server.py:11971), pass the board's active window from `MemberExposure`, and raise the movement limit or paginate when the requested window is wider than 30d.

findings.title: ledger.coverage() exists and is documented as the honesty mechanism, but no /api/intel/* route serves it
findings.evidence: src/intel/ledger.py:974-1018 builds a coverage block (earliest/latest observation, movement/league/manager/transaction counts, movementsByTxType, retentionDays, `complete: false`, and a coverageNote). docs/intel/METRICS.md §'Coverage honesty' presents it as how the products avoid implying global Sleeper coverage. `grep -rn 'coverage()' --include=*.py .` shows the only callers are src/sharp/service.py:60 and scripts/migrate_intel_ledger.py:97 — no /api/intel/* handler and no intel service function calls it (`grep -n coverage src/intel/service.py src/intel/lead_service.py` returns nothing). The leads payload carries only a prose `limitations.coverageCaveat` (leads.py:414-418) with no numbers.
findings.userImpact: The Insider Trading board, drill-down, member profile and lead list all present counts with no statement of how many leagues, managers or days of history actually back them. A user cannot tell whether '0 buys observed' means the manager doesn't want the player or that the crawl only reached two of their nine leagues — which is precisely the distinction the coverage block exists to make and which `describe_limitations` verbally warns about while withholding the numbers.
findings.recommendedFix: Stamp `ledger.coverage()` (scoped to the pool where meaningful) onto the summary, player and leads payloads, and render at least the league/manager/window counts alongside the existing staleness banner.
findings.affectedSystems: Insider Trading asset board; lead score payload; per-asset drill-down; member profile

findings.title: No intel data store exists in this checkout — the entire subsystem is unverifiable against live inputs
findings.evidence: `ls data/intel/` -> 'No such file or directory'. `find . -name '*.sqlite3*' -o -name 'snapshot_*.json'` (excluding node_modules) returns nothing. `data/` contains adamidp_normalized.json, comparison, identity, idp_fit_snapshots, legacy_data_2026-03-22.json, player_map, raw, raw_sources, ros, scrape_state, snapshots — no intel. `grep -n intel .gitignore` returns nothing, so the directory is not explicitly ignored; per CLAUDE.md most of data/ is gitignored, so absence here is consistent with a checkout artifact rather than proof of an empty production store.
findings.userImpact: Not Verifiable from Repository whether the ledger has ever been populated, how many leagues/managers/movements it holds, or how fresh it is. Every count, signal and lead score in this subsystem is therefore validated only against synthetic test fixtures. The 400-day retention, the 90d window's answerability, and the claim that the crawl reaches ~150 leagues for a 12-member pool (crawler.py:16-19) are all unverified assertions here.
findings.recommendedFix: Run `python scripts/migrate_intel_ledger.py --dry-run` and `python -c 'from src.intel import ledger; print(ledger.coverage())'` on the production host and record the output in docs/intel/. Add coverage numbers to the daily cron's success log so staleness and breadth are observable without shell access.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md documents none of src/intel/ — a ~6,300-line subsystem with seven routes and a daily cron
findings.evidence: `grep -c 'src/intel|api/intel|insider' CLAUDE.md` returns 0. CLAUDE.md's `src/` tree lists adapters, api, bdvm, canonical, identity, league_intel, model_registry, scoring, league, trade, data_models, utils — while `ls src/` shows 26 packages including intel, sharp, roster_intel, platforms, public_league, playerctx, news, nfl_data, pool, backtesting, league_comparison, maintenance, ros. The API endpoint table lists no /api/intel/* route, and the 'League-aware endpoints' list omits all five league-scoped intel reads even though they all go through `_resolve_league_for_request`.
findings.userImpact: The repository's primary orientation document gives no indication this subsystem exists, so a change to `_resolve_league_for_request`, `latest_contract_data`, `league_registry`, or the playersArray schema can break five intel endpoints with nothing in CLAUDE.md pointing at them. The intel routes' 503 `data_not_ready` semantics also differ from the table CLAUDE.md publishes for other league-scoped endpoints and are documented nowhere central.
findings.recommendedFix: Add `intel/`, `sharp/`, `roster_intel/`, `platforms/` and the other missing packages to CLAUDE.md's directory map, and add the seven /api/intel/* routes to the endpoint and league-aware tables with their 503 semantics.

findings.title: server.py's intel section header still documents the retired trendScore sort
findings.evidence: server.py:11943 — `#   GET  /api/intel/summary          — asset board sorted by trendScore`. trendScore was retired: src/intel/signals.py:9-24 explains why, docs/intel/METRICS.md §'Retired metrics' records it as removed, and tests/intel/test_signals.py::TestNoWindowSumming::test_trend_score_is_gone fails if it returns under any name. The actual default sort is `net` with a volume tie-break (server.py:12154, signals.py:348). server.py:11944 also lists `/api/intel/player` and `/api/intel/member` but omits `/api/intel/leads` and `/api/intel/waiver-interest`, both of which are defined in the same block.
findings.userImpact: The first thing a reader of server.py sees about this subsystem names a metric that was deleted specifically so no competing formula could stay reachable.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the header comment to name the real sort keys and list all seven routes.

findings.title: signalStrength, velocity, and two of the six allow-listed sorts are computed and shipped but never rendered
findings.evidence: server.py:11972 — `_INTEL_ALLOWED_SORTS = ("net", "volume", "buys", "sells", "strength", "velocity")`. frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx:33-38 offers only net/volume/buys/sells. `grep -rn 'signalStrength|velocity' frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx frontend/components/InsiderLeads.jsx` returns nothing — neither field is displayed. Both are computed on every board request (signals.py:303-316).
findings.userImpact: The two metrics docs/intel/METRICS.md describes at greatest length ('Derived signal metrics') are invisible to users; the board ranks on raw net instead, which is the exact 'net without volume' framing D4 was raised about (mitigated only by the volume tie-break and the volume column). Per-request compute is spent on values nobody sees.
findings.recommendedFix: Either surface strength and velocity as columns with the sorts already allow-listed, or stop computing them on the Insider Trading path and leave them to Sharp Tracker.
findings.affectedSystems: Signal strength; Velocity; Insider Trading asset board

findings.title: Two of the seven intel routes have no consumer of any kind
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'waiver-interest' frontend/` returns nothing; the only references are src/intel/service.py:525, server.py:12138/12296, docs/intel/METRICS.md:46-47 and tests/intel/test_endpoints.py. `grep -rn 'intel/member' frontend/` returns nothing. Frontend intel consumers are exactly: `/api/intel/summary` (page.jsx:409), `/api/intel/player` (page.jsx:145, PlayerPopup.jsx:202) and `/api/intel/leads` (InsiderLeads.jsx:260).
findings.userImpact: The waiver-interest endpoint exists to give waiver churn its own honest label so it can never render as a trade buy — but nothing renders it, so waiver activity is collected, stored and never shown. The member profile (a manager's cross-league footprint) is likewise unreachable from the UI.
findings.recommendedFix: Either wire both into /league/insider-trading (a Waivers tab and a manager drill-down from the member-exposure table, which already has ownerId) or mark them explicitly as API-only in docs/intel/METRICS.md.
findings.affectedSystems: Waiver / free-agent interest board; Member cross-league profile

findings.title: AUDIT.md defect D10 (movement_id embeds the attributed owner) remains open in code as documented
findings.evidence: src/intel/crawler.py:290 — `event_id = f"{tx_id}:{owner}:{action}:{asset_id}"` where `owner` comes from `rid_to_owner` (crawler.py:287), which is rebuilt each run from live /rosters and prefers a pool co-owner over the primary owner (crawler.py:157-166). That eventId becomes the ledger's `movement_id` PRIMARY KEY (ledger.py:39-48). docs/intel/AUDIT.md:134 and §7 record this as 'Open' with the reason stated. No fix is present.
findings.userImpact: If co-ownership changes on an already-crawled transaction, the same underlying movement re-keys and is inserted a second time, permanently double-counting that manager's buys/sells for that asset. Narrow (requires a co-ownership change) but silent and unrecoverable without a re-key pass. Correctly disclosed by the audit doc — reported here as confirmation, not as a new claim.
findings.recommendedFix: As AUDIT.md §7 proposes: canonicalise the key on `(tx_id, roster_id, action, asset_id)` and apply a one-time `UPDATE ... GROUP BY` re-key using the existing `tx_id` column.
findings.affectedSystems: Normalized movement ledger; every count derived from it

findings.title: Partner fit is normalised by its reachable maximum but not offset by its reachable minimum
findings.evidence: src/intel/leads.py:349-350 — `reachable_max = getattr(partner_model, "FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MAX", 50.0) or 50.0; fit_score = max(0.0, min(1.0, (fit_raw or 0.0) / reachable_max))`. Computed live: `FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MIN = 7.24`, `FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MAX = 43.12` (src/roster_intel/partner.py:573). Both bounds are exported; only the max is used.
findings.userImpact: A partner assessed at the worst attainable fit contributes 7.24/43.12 x 0.26 = 0.0437, i.e. 4.4 display points, on every lead where a roster snapshot exists. Since that applies uniformly, it inflates the whole board rather than distorting the order — but it means 'terrible fit' and 'no fit computed' differ by 4.4 points in the wrong direction (no assessment scores 0.0, a bad assessment scores 4.4).
findings.recommendedFix: Use `(fit_raw - FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MIN) / (FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MAX - FIT_SCORE_REACHABLE_MIN)` clamped to [0,1], and extend tests/intel/test_leads.py::TestPartnerFitNormalisation to pin the floor as well as the ceiling.
findings.affectedSystems: Partner-fit term; Insider Trading lead score

findings.title: The sample-confidence docstring's stated calibration does not match its constant
findings.evidence: src/intel/signals.py:67-69 — 'Volume at which sample-size confidence reaches ~0.5. Tuned so a single observation is visibly weak (~0.09) and a dozen is strong (~0.86)... _CONFIDENCE_HALF_VOLUME = 5.0'. Computed: `sample_confidence(1) = 1/6 = 0.1667` and `sample_confidence(12) = 12/17 = 0.7059`. The quoted 0.09 and 0.86 correspond to a half-volume near 10, not 5.
findings.userImpact: None directly — the values are not user-facing. But the comment is the only stated justification for the constant, and it describes a different constant, so anyone re-tuning it would be reasoning from a wrong baseline.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the docstring numbers to 0.17 and 0.71, or change the constant to match the stated intent and re-check the confidence-tier thresholds against it.

findings.title: No Next bridge routes exist for /api/intel/*, unlike the comparable bdvm and sharp surfaces
findings.evidence: `find frontend/app/api -ipath '*intel*'` returns nothing. The 30 existing bridge routes include `sharp/cohort`, `sharp/market`, `bdvm/values`, `bdvm/roster`, `bdvm/trades`, `bdvm/trade-eval`, `trade/finder`, `valuation/league-adjusted` etc. The intel page fetches `/api/intel/summary`, `/api/intel/player` and `/api/intel/leads` with relative URLs (page.jsx:409, :145; InsiderLeads.jsx:260). frontend/next.config.mjs declares no rewrites (only a /draft-capital redirect). CLAUDE.md documents bdvm's as 'Dev bridge routes at frontend/app/api/bdvm/*'. Production works because deploy/nginx routes /api/ to the backend; /api/terminal, /api/player and /api/playerctx follow the same bridge-less pattern.
findings.userImpact: In local development against `next dev` on :3000 the intel page's three fetches 404, so the feature cannot be exercised without the nginx layer or a manual proxy. Not a production defect.
findings.recommendedFix: Add bridge routes under frontend/app/api/intel/ mirroring the bdvm pattern, or document the bridge-less set (terminal, player, playerctx, intel) so the inconsistency is deliberate rather than incidental.
