notes:
SCOPE NOTE. Two items named in the brief resolve differently than expected. (1) The frontend `/intel` page is a bare `redirect("/league/insider-trading")` (frontend/app/intel/page.jsx:16-18) — the real page is frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx (664 lines), which is what I audited. (2) `scripts/migrate_intel_platform_v2.py` (32 lines) is a thin CLI over platform_ledger.backup_and_migrate; the substantive migration script is scripts/migrate_intel_ledger.py (106 lines), whose docstring self-corrects an earlier false claim that it "never mutates or deletes existing rows" (it calls ledger.prune(), a DELETE) — that correction is honest and I found no defect in it.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD, and should not be lost in the finding list. This subsystem is unusually disciplined about its own epistemics relative to the rest of the repo. The three-unit separation (transaction / asset movement / observation) is real, enforced by separate SQL functions, and test-pinned. Windows are genuinely independent queries with no summing function anywhere — the retired trendScore's overlapping-window sum is gone and a test fails if it returns under any name. `velocity` is a ratio of rates and is provably immune to the same class of error. Trade and waiver counting are separated at the schema default (`TRADE_TX_TYPES` is the default argument, so the dangerous case is out of reach rather than merely avoided). Failure handling in crawler.py is better than anything else I read in this repo: a failed roster fetch skips the entire league rather than attributing events with a stale owner map, a failed /traded_picks fetch refuses to publish derived defaults, and a failed transaction week refuses to advance fetchState. `describe_limitations()` ships the model's own disclaimer in the payload and the UI renders it rather than hiding it in a tooltip. Blank partner fit renders as an em dash, never 0.0.

THE CENTRAL ANSWER TO THE BRIEF'S QUESTION. The brief asks specifically about inference-from-activity presented as knowledge without an error rate. The board itself is mostly not that — it reports counts of things that observably happened, with volume always beside net, an explicit confidence tier, and a movement-level receipt list. The lead score IS that, and the numbers show why. Only one of its five terms (demonstratedInterest, 0.34) is observation; the other four are inference from roster shape and market values. Two of those four are degenerate as measured here: valueMatch is 1.0 for 99-100% of managers for any asset outside the top ~50 of the board, and positionalNeed is a within-roster rank that scores a 0.1-slot gap identically to a 3.0-slot gap. Together they contribute a near-constant 30 points before any evidence about the manager and the asset exists. The consequence, verified end to end: a league-mate about whom the platform has observed literally nothing regarding this player scores 33.1/100 and renders AMBER in the UI. Nothing in the payload states a reachable range (verified max 80.7), an error rate, or a calibration — and no backtest, holdout or calibration artifact for any of the seven hand-picked weights exists anywhere in the repo, in a codebase that ships exactly that apparatus (docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md, scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py) for a comparable feature. The module's own docstring is careful to say a lead score is a ranking and not a probability; that is true and well-defended, but it is a narrower claim than the one the number needs to survive, because a ranking whose top contributors are two constants and two abstentions is not a ranking of anything.

SECOND-ORDER OBSERVATION ON THE TEST SUITE. 17 test files, ~1,100 lines of intel tests, and the coverage is genuinely broad — but two of the three highest-severity findings survive it in the same way. `test_value_floor_excludes_roster_clog` passes an explicit `starter_value_floor=100.0` that the only production caller never passes; `test_member_payload` asserts `tradeCount == 1` against a fixture containing exactly one trade of exactly one asset, which is the one shape where the summation defect is invisible. Both tests exercise a function directly rather than the live assembly path. A test that asserts the production call site's argument list — or a fixture with a 4-for-4 trade — would have caught both.

COULD NOT VERIFY. (a) Whether the daily cron has ever succeeded, or whether any snapshot or ledger exists in production — data/intel/ is absent here, .gitignore does not mention it, and git history is squashed to a single commit so no refresh commits are visible. (b) The workflow's `vars.PROD_PUBLIC_URL` and `secrets.INTEL_REFRESH_TOKEN` are repository settings, not repository contents. (c) The claim in crawler.py:16-19 that steady state is "~460 calls for a 12-member pool tracking ~150 leagues" against a 900-call budget — with no snapshot on disk I cannot check the real league count, and if the pool has grown past ~300 leagues the budget would exhaust every run and the cursor would round-robin indefinitely, which the 12-minute cron poll would surface as a timeout rather than as a coverage problem. (d) The exact rankDerivedValue distribution — exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json is the raw scrape payload (keys: version, date, settings, sites, players, sleeper) with no playersArray and no rankDerivedValue, so the valueMatch saturation simulation used `_finalAdjusted` (1,074 priced assets, max 9999, p50 1864.5) as a same-scale proxy; the conclusion is robust to that substitution because the term saturates at any plausible roster density, but the exact percentages would shift on the real board.

DEAD OR NEAR-DEAD CODE. leads.py:211 trailing ternary (both branches 1.0). leads.py:176 breadth fallback of 0.5 for `unique_leagues == 0`, unreachable from a real ledger row (COUNT(DISTINCT) >= 1). roster_shape.py:93-95 value-floor branch, never taken in production. `ledger.coverage()` — implemented, documented as the honesty mechanism in METRICS.md, served by no /api/intel/* route. lead_service.py:88-90 builds `per_user` as a dict of empty sets purely to enumerate keys, then rescans `rows` once per user (O(n^2)). `signals.build_asset_signals`' cohort-mean `manager_quality` path (signals.py:294-301) is never exercised by Insider Trading, which always passes None.

OUT OF SCOPE BUT ADJACENT. src/intel/platform_ledger.py (1,925 lines, 31% of the package) contains no scoring of any kind — it is additive multi-platform schema, identity linkage and asset aliasing, reachable only from src/sharp/ and the FFPC crawl scripts, never from any /api/intel/* route. src/intel/league_filter.py's sharp-eligibility half (`is_sharp_eligible`, `SHARP_MIN_LEAGUE_AGE_SEASONS`) is likewise a Sharp Tracker classifier living in an intel module. Both are listed in `systems` for completeness but their scored consumers (/api/sharp/*, docs/intel/SHARP_SCORE.md) are a separate audit.

findings.title: Two shipped systems give the SAME team opposite contention labels: /phases says "Win-now", /api/gameplan says "rebuild"
findings.evidence: Owner owner-b84d236298d2 ("Collin"). Backend: `src/roster_intel/window.py:league_competitiveness` (lines ~300-330) takes the championship-odds percentile; measured live run → `comp=0.188, mostLikely='rebuild', confidence=0.388` while `lineup_score=673.0` (4th-highest of 12). Frontend: `frontend/lib/team-phase.js:83-90` `if (isHighValue && isYounger) return PHASES.WIN_NOW;` — measured live: Collin top-25 value 95,993 vs league median 91,579.5 (high) and median age 25 vs league 26 (younger) → **Win-now**. Both are reachable to the same signed-in user; neither cites the other.
findings.userImpact: A manager reading /phases is told to buy win-now talent; the same platform's gameplan engine classifies them as a rebuild and its partner model uses that to pick counterparties. There is no CONFLICT state and no reconciliation — whichever page they open last wins.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one authority. The window engine is the better-founded one (it at least consumes playoff_sim); make `team-phase.js` render `competitiveWindow.mostLikely` from a backend endpoint instead of re-deriving a second classification from a value sum, or explicitly label /phases as "market-value shape" and stop using contention vocabulary.

findings.title: Competitive window ranks 8 of 12 rosters on one scale and 4 on an incomparable other, then presents both in one five-state vocabulary
findings.evidence: `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json` contains 8 rows for a 12-team league (verified: `len(playoffOdds)==8`; missing ownerIds `{owner-9b939999c520, owner-396ab6a38b0f, owner-81e37a629680, owner-85176a3f8776}`). `src/roster_intel/window.py:league_competitiveness` percentiles championshipOdds *over the rows it was given* (`below/ties over len(champ)`), else falls back to `lineupScoreRank` over all 12. Measured live: `owner-396ab6a38b0f` → comp 0.958 via lineupScoreRank → `championship_contender`; `owner-c8e8fbf88d86` → playoffOdds 1.0 but championshipOdds 0.0 → comp 0.188 → `rebuild`. `src/api/gameplan.py:520-536` emits a note about this but `_league_summary` (gameplan.py:757-800) still sorts all 12 together and stamps `mostLikely` on each.
findings.userImpact: A team certain to make the playoffs (playoffOdds 1.0) is labelled `rebuild`. A team with no simulation at all is labelled `championship_contender` on lineup rank alone. Cross-team comparison — the only thing a 12-row table invites — is invalid, and the payload's own note is the only place that says so.
findings.recommendedFix: Refuse to emit `mostLikely` when `competitivenessSource` is not uniform across the league summary, or degrade every roster to `lineupScoreRank` when sim coverage is partial so one scale governs. Separately, fix the sim to cover all 12 owners.

findings.title: Championship odds are degenerate: 4 of 8 simulated teams are exactly 0.0 and tie at the same percentile, collapsing three different rosters onto one label
findings.evidence: `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json`: championshipOdds = [0.3815, 0.3185, 0.0, 0.001, 0.2955, 0.0035, 0.0, 0.0]; six of eight rows carry playoffOdds exactly 1.0 and two carry 0.0 with `playoffSeeds: 6`, `n_simulations: 2000`, `converged: true`. The three 0.0 rows tie → `pct = (0 + 0.5*3)/8 = 0.1875` for all three. Verified live: owners owner-b84d236298d2 (lineupScore 673.0), owner-e61ce01ca743 (553.1) and owner-c8e8fbf88d86 (486.7) all receive comp 0.188 and all label `rebuild`.
findings.userImpact: A 186-point spread in lineup strength is flattened to one identical label. `playoffOdds` carries zero information (6/8 are 1.0) so the only discriminating field is championshipOdds, and half of it is a floor.
findings.recommendedFix: Do not percentile a variable that is 50% zeros. Either blend expectedWins/seedDistribution into the competitiveness axis, or detect the ties and stamp the window `notes` with an explicit "three rosters are indistinguishable on this axis" rather than emitting three confident labels.

findings.title: tradePartnerFitScore ships a reachable range of [7.24, 43.12] that is unreachable through the only wiring that serves it; measured live ceiling is 16.37
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/partner.py:536-573` `_reachable_fit_bounds()` derives the published bounds assuming `max_conf=0.40` (HISTORY_INFORMED) and full 3/3 structural coverage. `src/api/gameplan.py:915-926` constructs `PartnerInputs` with **no** `shape`, no `trades_completed`, no `league_mean_trades`, no `pair_trades_completed` → `_fairness_term` and `_history_term` both abstain → tier is SHAPE_ONLY (0.30), `measured = 2/3` → `confidence = 0.30 * (0.55 + 0.45*0.6667) = 0.2550` for every partner, always. Measured live (real 12-team bundle, owner owner-8b8a59adf44e): all 11 partners have `acceptanceConfidence == 0.255` exactly, and fit scores span 10.48 … 16.37 against the shipped `tradePartnerFitScoreRange` of `{min: 7.24, max: 43.12}`.
findings.userImpact: The bounds were added specifically so a renderer would not draw a good partner as a failing grade — and under the real wiring the best partner draws at 38% of the shipped gauge. `acceptanceConfidence` is a constant wearing a score's clothes: it varies with nothing.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute the bounds from the evidence tier and coverage actually achieved on this call rather than from the module's theoretical maxima, and stamp them per-response. Alternatively supply the missing `trades_completed` / `league_mean_trades` (the contract already carries `sleeper.trades`, 110 rows) so the history term stops abstaining.

findings.title: waiver_scarcity is structurally always None — the scarcity multiplier and the SCARCITY corroborator are dead everywhere, while the payload advertises scarcity as a live corroborator
findings.evidence: `src/league_intel/replacement.py:452-465` only populates the `waiver` tier from the `free_agents` argument; `waiver_scarcity=_safe_drop(best_ball, waiver)` (line 657). `grep -rn free_agents src/ scripts/ server.py` returns **only the definition** — no caller anywhere supplies it. `src/api/gameplan.py:490` calls `compute_replacement_levels(rep_teams, slots, endogenous=endogenous)`. Measured live: every ScarcityComponents has `'waiverScarcity': None`. Consequently `src/roster_intel/targets.py:468-471` returns `1.0, "no scarcity data — position scarcity multiplier inert"` on every position, and `targets.py:804-807` (`ValueSignal.SCARCITY`) can never fire. Yet `src/api/gameplan.py:855-861` tells the consumer "the only admissible corroborators are measured lineup fit and positional scarcity".
findings.userImpact: Half the advertised corroboration gate does not exist. Every one of the 6 recommended targets on the live run carries `signals: ["rosterFit"]` — the gate is single-signal in practice, which is exactly the "model agreeing with itself" failure the gate was written to prevent.
findings.recommendedFix: Either pass free agents into `compute_replacement_levels` (Sleeper exposes them) or delete SCARCITY from `CORROBORATING_SIGNALS` and rewrite the coverage note to say lineup fit is the sole corroborator.

findings.title: Target-position confidence credits scarcity as "supplied" when the scarcity term abstained, inflating every confidence by 0.15
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/targets.py:658-665`: `supplied = sum(... (scarcity or {}).get(pos) is not None ...)`. The object is present for all 8 positions but the only field consumed — `waiver_scarcity` — is None (see prior finding), so `_scarcity_multiplier` returns the abstention note. Measured live: RB target confidence = 0.85 (`0.40 + 0.15*3`) where the honest value is 0.70. The module's own comment two lines above says "a defaulted input is an abstention and must cost confidence rather than pass silently."
findings.userImpact: Priority scores are 21% higher than the evidence supports, and the confidence field — the thing a reader would use to discount them — is the field that is wrong.
findings.recommendedFix: Test the term's abstention, not the object's presence: use `scar_note is None` in the `supplied` count, mirroring how `efficiency is not None` is already tested.

findings.title: Every differentiating multiplier in both target engines is 1.0 under the live wiring; `priority` is a constant rescale of lineup gain
findings.evidence: `targets.py:698` `priority = realistic * window_mult * scar_mult * eff_mult * confidence`. Measured live (owner owner-8b8a59adf44e, real contract with 661/666 ages): RB is the only viable position, `realisticGain 15.08 × winNowWeight 0.8755 × scarcityMultiplier 1.0 × eff_mult 1.0 × confidence 0.85 = 11.222` — matches the emitted `priority` exactly. `eff_mult` is 1.0 because `market_prices` is deliberately never supplied (`gameplan.py:945` comment). `scar_mult` is 1.0 always (prior finding). For players, `targets.py:866-869`: `edge_mult = 1.0` (edge None), `avail_mult = 0.7 + 0.6*0.5 = 1.0` (avail None), `scar_mult = 1.0`, `confidence = 0.35 + 0.15*1 = 0.5` → measured: travis etienne gain 16.18 → priority 8.09 = gain/2 exactly, for all 6 recommendations.
findings.userImpact: `priority` reads as a composite score that weighed scarcity, market efficiency, availability and the competitive window. It is `lineupGain × 0.5` for players and `realisticGain × 0.85 × horizonWeight` for positions. Ordering by priority and ordering by raw gain are the same list.
findings.recommendedFix: Suppress `priority` (emit null) when every non-confidence multiplier abstained, the way `winNowWeight` is already nulled — a score whose inputs all defaulted must not be presented as a score.

findings.title: `_position_severity` computes fragility × marginal_points — the exact product `engine.py`'s docstring documents as producing the QB inversion
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/targets.py:474-486`: `return max(0.0, float(profile.fragility)) * max(0.0, float(profile.marginal_points))`, docstringed "Current cost of the weakness". `src/roster_intel/engine.py:22-40` states: "A consuming agent derived 'deficit' as fragility x marginal and got QB reported as the biggest need on a QB-STRONG roster… Multiplying those reports the roster's greatest STRENGTH as its greatest need." `targets.py:719-721` sorts every non-viable position by `-severity`, so it is what orders the "biggest unfixable weakness" list. Measured live (owner owner-8b8a59adf44e): WR fragility 0.2143 × marginal 156.6 = 33.6 — the highest severity on the roster — while WR's actual deficit is 0.0 and its contribution (156.6) is more than double its replacement level (76.6).
findings.userImpact: The non-viable target list is headed by the roster's strongest position, presented as its costliest weakness. Two modules in one package hold contradictory definitions of the same quantity.
findings.recommendedFix: Order non-viable positions by `PositionNeed.deficit` (already computed in `engine.position_needs`), or rename `severity` to `concentrationExposure` and stop calling it a weakness.

findings.title: The `elite` tier is unreachable for every player on every roster — `analyze_roster` never forwards `league_position_values`
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/profiles.py:build_position_profiles` computes `elite_cut = elite_threshold((league_position_values or {}).get(pos, ()))` and `classify_tier` ignores `elite` when it is None. `src/roster_intel/engine.py:analyze_roster` calls `build_position_profiles(pool_list, slots_list, replacement=..., player_meta=..., marginals=marg)` — the `league_position_values` parameter is never passed, and `analyze_roster` has no parameter to accept it. Measured live over all 12 rosters × 8 positions: **total elite-tier players = 0**. Every `tierCounts` reads `{'elite': 0, 'starter': n, 'depth': m, 'developmental': k}`.
findings.userImpact: A four-tier ladder that can only produce three tiers. The docstring's careful explanation of the elite promotion rule describes behaviour that never runs.
findings.recommendedFix: Thread `league_position_values` through `analyze_roster` (gameplan already holds every roster's pool and can build it in one pass), or drop `elite` from `TIER_ORDER` until it is wired.

findings.title: trend7 and trend30 are the same number whenever the rank-history log is shallower than 7 days, making the SELL rule's "sustained" qualifier vacuous
findings.evidence: `src/api/terminal.py:_window_trend` (lines ~332-343): `baseline` is the FIRST point with `t >= cutoff` — i.e. the oldest point in the log when the log is shorter than the window — and returns `baseline.rank - latest.rank`. So for any series spanning fewer than 7 days, `_window_trend(points,7) == _window_trend(points,30)`. `terminal.py:588-593` states the log is "currently ~2 days deep". The SELL rule (`terminal.py`, priority 80) is `trend7 <= -3 and trend30 is not None and trend30 <= 0`; with equal trends it degenerates to `trend7 <= -3`. SELL is in `signal_alerts.ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS` — it emails.
findings.userImpact: A player who dropped 3 ranks on a single scrape gets an emailed SELL described as "7d trend -3 continues a 30d trend of -3", stating a 30-day fact the data cannot support. The chip labelled "30d" on `BuySellHold.jsx` shows a 2-day number.
findings.recommendedFix: Return `None` from `_window_trend` when the series does not actually span the requested window (`latest.t - points[0].t < window_days*0.8`), rather than silently substituting the oldest available point. Mirror in `frontend/lib/value-history.js::computeWindowTrend`.

findings.title: PortfolioSummary displays a Total Value that excludes picks beside a pick legend that includes them
findings.evidence: `src/api/terminal.py:1160-1188` deliberately excludes picks from `_compute_portfolio_insights` (comment: "Left excluded rather than changed… 442,936 of pick value against 1,524,591 of player value — 22.5% of a portfolio"). `frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:240-270` includes picks in `totalValue` and the PICK bucket. `frontend/components/terminal/PortfolioSummary.jsx:97-105` merges them: `totalValue: serverPortfolio.totalValue ?? localPortfolio.totalValue` and `byPosition: serverPortfolio.byPosition || localPortfolio.byPosition` (both pick-free) while lines 140-141 destructure `pickCount, pickValue` from the *local* portfolio and lines 202-205 render `{formatValue(pickValue)} · {pickCount}` in the same panel. Live snapshot: 19 picks per team.
findings.userImpact: The panel shows a Total Value and immediately below it a "Picks 442,936 · 19" legend — the second number is not in the first, and the positional stack shows PICK at 0.0%.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one definition. Either include picks server-side (a product decision the code comment already flags) or suppress the local pick legend when server aggregates are in use.

findings.title: TopSignalsRail reads four fields that do not exist on its inputs; value, 30d delta, evidence and position never render
findings.evidence: `frontend/lib/signal-engine.js::evaluateRoster` pushes `{row, context, verdict, news}` and `evaluate()` returns `{signal, primary, reason, tag, fired}`. `frontend/components/terminal/TopSignalsRail.jsx:44-58`: `valueDelta(verdict)` reads `verdict?.context?.delta30d` (context is on `entry`, not `verdict`; and `buildContext` emits `trend30`, never `delta30d`); `valueLabel(verdict)` reads `verdict?.context?.value` (same nesting error); line 65 `entry?.verdict?.evidence?.[0]` — `evaluate()` emits no `evidence` key; line 63 `entry?.row?.position` — `buildRows` emits `pos` (`frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:996,1177`), not `position`.
findings.userImpact: Every card on the rail above the terminal grid renders only a BUY/SELL badge and a name. The value, the rank delta, the position chip and the rationale tooltip are all permanently blank, and nothing errors.
findings.recommendedFix: Read `entry.context.value`, `entry.context.trend30`, `entry.verdict.reason` and `entry.row.pos`.

findings.title: Buy-low card is named and described as "short drop, long steady" but neither implementation tests any long-term trend
findings.evidence: `src/api/terminal.py:1105-1133`: the only tests are `rank <= 150`, `value >= 3000`, and `rc = _row_rank_change(r); if rc is None or rc > -3: continue` — `rankChange` is the delta from the *last scrape*, not a 7d or 30d trend. Emitted as `"metric": "short_drop_long_steady"`. `frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:452-455` carries the comment "7d trend ≤ -3 (dipped), 30d trend still ≥ 0 (long-term fine)" above code that filters on `Number(r.rankChange)` only. Both reason strings claim "but still inside the top N", which is the rank filter restated, not steadiness.
findings.userImpact: A player who fell 3 ranks on one scrape and has been falling for a month is presented as a buy-low with a stability claim the model never checked.
findings.recommendedFix: Either join the 30d trend (the server already has `history_for`) and enforce `trend30 >= 0`, or rename the metric to `last_scrape_drop` and drop the steadiness prose.

findings.title: The two Buy/Sell/Hold engines share a pinned rule table but consume divergent inputs, and only the Python side emails
findings.evidence: `tests/api/test_signal_engine_parity.py:41-56` explicitly states it pins the RULE TABLE only and lists the known builder divergences. Concretely: (a) `src/api/terminal.py::_row_value` falls back to `rank_to_value_for_scope(rank, scope)` when both value fields are absent, while `signal-engine.js::buildContext` uses `Number(row?.rankDerivedValue || row?.values?.full || 0)` with no fallback — this changes the `elite_stable` `value >= 7000` test; (b) `terminal.py::_history_lookup` (lines ~366-393) builds `lower_base` with `setdefault`, so a display name spanning two asset classes resolves to whichever key was iterated first, while `frontend/lib/value-history.js:297-302` returns `[]` on the same collision (`if ((nameVariantCount.get(lowered) || 0) > 1) return []`).
findings.userImpact: Divergent trend inputs produce divergent verdicts from identical rules. The Python verdict is the one fed to `signal_alerts.process_user_alerts` (ACTIONABLE = RISK/SELL/BUY/MONITOR), so the failure mode is "you were emailed a SELL the Signals panel does not show". Measured mitigation: 0 display names currently span more than one assetClass on the live board (550 offense / 398 idp / 144 pick), so (b) is latent today.
findings.recommendedFix: Extend the shared fixture to the context builders, or make `_history_lookup` refuse ambiguous names the way the JS resolver already does.

findings.title: team-phase classification is a forced median quota with no absolute anchor and no hysteresis; on live data zero teams classify as Rebuild
findings.evidence: `frontend/lib/team-phase.js:83-90` classifies on `totalValue > leagueMedians.value` and `medianAge < leagueMedians.age`, both medians taken over the same 12 snapshots — so exactly 6 teams are "high value" by construction regardless of league quality. Reproduced on the live contract + live rosters: medians value 91,579.5, age 26.0 → **5 Win-now, 1 Contender, 6 Mixed, 0 Rebuild**. Ages are integers so 4 of 12 teams sit exactly at median age 26.0; `isYounger` uses strict `<` (line 80) so ties are silently pushed to "older". Margins are thin: Collin +4,414 on 95,993 (4.6%) and Ed −4,414 — a ~5% board move swaps both labels, and there is no hysteresis or confidence field anywhere in the module.
findings.userImpact: A page titled "Win-now vs Rebuild" never says Rebuild. Half the league is labelled by a coin-flip on the age axis. The classification flips on ordinary scrape noise with no indication that it was close.
findings.recommendedFix: Report the two margins (value and age, as distances from the median) alongside the label and suppress the label when either margin is inside a noise band; use `<=` with an explicit tie state rather than folding ties into "older".

findings.title: team-phase label vocabulary is inverted relative to the quadrant it names — an old, weak roster is called "Mixed", a young, strong one "Win-now"
findings.evidence: `frontend/lib/team-phase.js:83-90`: `high value × younger → WIN_NOW`, `high value × older → CONTENDER`, `low value × younger → REBUILD`, `low value × older → MIXED`. Live: "Kich", top-25 value 76,514 (10th of 12) with median age 29 — the oldest roster in the league and near the bottom on value, i.e. the textbook rebuild — is classified **Mixed** (tone `warn`). "Brent", the highest-value roster in the league (136,198), is classified **Contender** — the second-tier label — because its median age is 27. The header text `TeamPhasePanel.jsx:88-91` presents this as "classified by top-25 roster value × median age" with no legend explaining the mapping.
findings.userImpact: The label a manager acts on points the wrong way for the two quadrants that most need clear advice.
findings.recommendedFix: Rename: high/older → "Win-now", high/younger → "Contender (sustainable)", low/older → "Rebuild", low/younger → "Ascending". Render the quadrant legend in the panel.

findings.title: `/api/gameplan` and the entire `src/roster_intel` package have no frontend consumer
findings.evidence: `grep -rn gameplan frontend/ --include=*.js --include=*.jsx` returns exactly one hit — a comment in `frontend/app/api/valuation/league-adjusted/route.js:32`. There is no bridge route at `frontend/app/api/gameplan/`. `src/api/gameplan.py:1-9` opens by noting roster_intel "merged with no caller" and presents itself as the wiring; the wiring stops at `server.py:5675 @app.get("/api/gameplan")`. The only roster_intel output that reaches a user is `get_league_adjusted_values` (gameplan.py:1290+), which reuses the bundle's `scarcity` and nothing else, plus `partner.assess_partner` via `src/intel/leads.py` (surfaced as a tooltip in `frontend/components/InsiderLeads.jsx:358`).
findings.userImpact: ~4,800 lines of roster analysis — needs, the five-state window, both target engines, the Pareto package generator — cost a 1.35 s cold build per league and are rendered nowhere. Every defect above is therefore currently latent for end users but live for any API consumer.
findings.recommendedFix: Either build the consuming surface or mark the route experimental so its numbers are not treated as production-grade.

findings.title: `/api/terminal` computes and ships three mover lists on every request that nothing reads
findings.evidence: `src/api/terminal.py:1631-1641` always builds `movers.roster` (limit 20), `movers.league` (30) and `movers.top150` (30) by scanning `rows` three times. `frontend/components/useTerminal.js:180` exposes `movers`, but no component destructures it: `MarketTicker.jsx:64-72` calls the client-side `computeMovers` from `lib/market-movers.js`, and `MoversPanel.jsx` fetches `/api/movers` (a different endpoint over `rank_history.jsonl`). Grep of `useTerminal(` consumers shows only `portfolio`, `signals`, `teamAggregates`, `watchlist`, `stale`.
findings.userImpact: Three full-board scans and ~80 serialized rows per terminal request for dead payload. Also a third, independent definition of "mover" exists that nobody validates against the other two.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop the block or wire MarketTicker to it (the server version is scope-identical and already backend-stamped).

findings.title: `engine._odds_for` docstring asserts the simulator emits no championship odds or CIs; the on-disk simulator output emits both
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/engine.py` `_odds_for` docstring: "``simulate_playoff_odds`` on main emits ``playoffOdds`` / ``byeOdds`` / ``topSeedOdds`` / ``seedDistribution`` and NOTHING else — no championship odds and no confidence intervals. The bracket run and the Wilson intervals come from the LI-8 work, which is a separate unmerged branch." `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json` rows carry `championshipOdds`, `championshipOddsCi`, `playoffOddsCi`, `expectedWins`, `medianFinalSeed`, `missPlayoffsOdds`. Verified live: `ri.championship_odds = 0.3815` with CI `[0.3605, 0.403]` for owner 1012114412049731584.
findings.userImpact: The "simulator supplied no championshipOdds" note is unreachable for covered owners, so a reader who trusts the docstring will believe the odds are absent when they are present (and, per the coverage finding, present for only 8 of 12).
findings.recommendedFix: Update the docstring; the defensive read is correct and should stay.

findings.title: Client `normalizePos` omits 7 IDP aliases the server maps, silently dropping those players' value from the positional stack while keeping it in the total
findings.evidence: `frontend/lib/portfolio-insights.js:57-62` maps only DB/LB/DL/DE/DT/CB/S → "IDP". `src/api/terminal.py:_normalize_pos` (lines ~84-101) additionally maps EDGE, NT, OLB, ILB, MLB, FS, SS. In `computePortfolio`, an unmapped position fails `POSITION_GROUPS.includes(p.pos)` (line 285) so the player contributes to `totalValue` (line 273) but to no `byPosition` bucket, and the percentages under-sum. Measured against the live `sleeper.positions` map (937 entries): 0 players currently carry EDGE/NT/OLB/ILB/MLB/FS/SS, so the defect is latent for this league; 1 player carries position "T", which falls out on both sides.
findings.userImpact: Latent today. Any league whose Sleeper position vocabulary uses EDGE or the OLB/ILB/MLB split gets a positional allocation stack that does not sum to the displayed total.
findings.recommendedFix: Import the position map from one place; `frontend/lib/starter-slots.js::lineupPosition` already handles the wider vocabulary.

findings.title: `urgent_need` and `RosterSignal.deficit` are structurally blind to 3 of the league's 21 starter slots
findings.evidence: `src/roster_intel/profiles.py::_required_slots` skips FLEX / SUPER_FLEX / IDP_FLEX / BN by design (the comment cites LI-5 endogeneity). The live league's slots are `('QB','RB','RB','WR','WR','WR','TE','TE','FLEX','FLEX','SUPER_FLEX','K','DL','DL','DL','LB','LB','LB','DB','DB','DB')` — 18 attributed, 3 (2×FLEX + SUPER_FLEX, 14%) unattributed. Measured live: every team reports QB `required_slots = 1` and `urgent_need = False` despite this being a superflex league where a second startable QB is the dominant structural need. Separately `_URGENT_FRAGILITY = 0.75` (profiles.py) is cleared by essentially nothing: measured max QB fragility across 12 rosters is 0.707; the only position hitting 1.0 is K (one kicker rostered).
findings.userImpact: The need model cannot see a superflex hole, and its second trigger (fragility ≥ 0.75) fires almost exclusively on kickers. `urgent_need` is therefore close to a kicker detector.
findings.recommendedFix: Not a bug per the stated design, but the payload should say which slots the need model does not cover, and the fragility threshold should be calibrated against the observed distribution rather than a round number.

findings.title: `rank_history.jsonl` and `source_value_history.jsonl` are absent from the repository; every trend, volatility, signal and delta in the terminal is unverifiable offline
findings.evidence: `src/api/rank_history.py:74` `HISTORY_PATH = <repo>/data/rank_history.jsonl` and `src/api/source_history.py:49` `HISTORY_PATH = <repo>/data/source_value_history.jsonl` — neither file exists in this checkout (`ls data/*.jsonl` → no such file). They are written at runtime by `server.py:1868 _rank_history.append_snapshot(contract_payload)`, one entry per UTC date, retention `MAX_SNAPSHOTS = 365*3`. With no file, `_history_lookup` returns `[]` for every name → `trend7 = trend30 = None`, `_volatility = None`, every signal is HOLD/`default_hold`, every `delta*d` is None with `reason: "low_history_coverage"`, and `biggestRisk` / `tradeChip` return null.
findings.userImpact: None of the signal, volatility, trend or delta numbers can be validated from the repository. The depth of the production log (terminal.py's own comment says "~2 days") is Not Verifiable from Repository, which is what makes the trend-window finding above severe rather than theoretical.
findings.recommendedFix: Ship a small fixture snapshot, or have `/api/terminal` stamp `meta.historyDepthDays` so consumers can tell a 2-day log from a 180-day one.

formulas.name: Competitive window — anchor softmax (five-state affinities)
formulas.expression: d²(s) = 2.0·(competitiveness − c_anchor[s])² + 1.0·(trajectory − t_anchor[s])²;  p(s) = exp(−d²(s)/0.18) / Σ_s exp(−d²(s)/0.18)
formulas.constants: Anchors (competitiveness, trajectory): championship_contender (0.95, 0.45), playoff_contender (0.70, 0.50), retool (0.45, 0.70), productive_struggle (0.25, 0.80), rebuild (0.05, 0.60). _COMPETITIVENESS_WEIGHT = 2.0, _TRAJECTORY_WEIGHT = 1.0, DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE = 0.18. ALL hand-picked; the module's own to_dict() states none was fitted to an observed outcome.
formulas.inputs: competitiveness ∈[0,1], unitless percentile (championship odds, else lineup-score rank, else 0.5); trajectory ∈[0,1], unitless age map
formulas.outputRange: five values summing to exactly 1 after largest-remainder rounding to 4dp
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No playoff_odds and no lineup_scores → competitiveness = 0.5, source 'unavailable'. No ages → trajectory = 0.5, sample 0. Neither is imputed as a number that looks measured; both stamp a note. Nothing coerced to zero.
formulas.mathIssues: Effective boundaries at trajectory 0.5, computed by sweeping comp 0→1 at 1e-4 resolution: rebuild <0.2501, productive_struggle 0.2501–0.2875, retool 0.2875–0.535, playoff_contender 0.535–0.8275, championship_contender >0.8275. With 12 teams the percentile is quantized to (k+0.5)/12 = 0.0417 steps, so the 0.0374-wide productive_struggle band is unreachable — matching the engine's own measured note (0 of 12). Max attainable confidence at neutral trajectory is 0.707; a typical label carries 0.39–0.65 mass and is still presented as `mostLikely`. The docstring claims softmax avoids the threshold-flip artifact; it relocates the cut to a smooth boundary the argmax still crosses discretely.
formulas.validated: none found — to_dict() says so explicitly. tests/roster_intel/test_window.py asserts sum-to-1, argmax consistency and monotonicity, never calibration.

formulas.name: League competitiveness percentile
formulas.expression: pct = (count(v < mine) + 0.5·count(v == mine)) / len(pool), clamped to [0,1]. Pool = championshipOdds across the rows supplied if any row is >0, else lineupScores across all teams, else 0.5.
formulas.constants: no tunables; the 0.5 tie weight is the only choice
formulas.inputs: championshipOdds from data/ros/sims/<key>_playoff.json (unitless probability); lineup scores in rosValue units (0-100 log-rank index summed over 21 slots)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: All-zero championship odds are explicitly NOT treated as a signal (the `any(v > 0 ...)` guard) → falls through to lineup rank. Owner absent from the odds rows → falls through. Source stamped either way.
formulas.mathIssues: Denominator is len(the rows given), not the league. Live: 8 rows for 12 teams → covered owners percentile over 8, uncovered over 12. Three owners tie at championshipOdds 0.0 → all get (0+1.5)/8 = 0.1875 regardless of a 186-point lineup spread.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_window.py::test_prefers_simulated_championship_odds / test_falls_back_to_lineup_rank_and_stamps_it / test_all_zero_odds_are_not_treated_as_a_signal pin source selection only, not the mixed-denominator case.

formulas.name: Trajectory score (value-weighted lineup age)
formulas.expression: mean_age = Σ(age_i · max(0, rosValue_i)) / Σ max(0, rosValue_i) over optimal-lineup entrants with a known age and value>0;  score = clamp((32.0 − mean_age)/(32.0 − 22.0), 0, 1)
formulas.constants: _AGE_YOUNG = 22.0, _AGE_OLD = 32.0 — described as "fantasy-relevant career bounds, not biology"; no calibration in-repo. Deliberately shared with targets.py so the two agree on "young".
formulas.inputs: player_meta[player_id]['age'] in years (from contract playersArray); rosValue as the weight
formulas.missingDataBehavior: weight ≤0 or n == 0 → returns (0.5, 0). Sample size returned alongside so a caller can distinguish neutral-because-measured from neutral-because-absent.
formulas.mathIssues: Bench excluded by design. Live measurement with a real contract: 20-21 aged entrants per team, trajectory 0.219–0.686. Supplying ages FLIPS labels: owner owner-4c9d2d7a3a8b moves playoff_contender→retool and owner-9b939999c520 moves retool→playoff_contender purely on age availability, not on any roster change.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_window.py::test_only_lineup_entrants_count, test_weighting_stops_scrubs_hiding_an_old_anchor, test_missing_ages_are_neutral_not_zero

formulas.name: Position marginal contribution (group leave-out)
formulas.expression: marginal(P) = S(full roster) − S(roster with every player at P removed), where S = Σ rosValue over the exact optimal slot assignment; marginal_share = marginal / S(full) when S(full) > 0 else 0
formulas.constants: none — this is a pure re-solve
formulas.inputs: RosterPlayer.ros_value (0-100 normalized log-rank strength index, NOT points), 21 flattened starter slots
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty pool or empty slots → score 0. Unvalued players enter with ros_value 0 and contribute nothing; roster_source.build_roster_pool DROPS unjoinable names entirely and records the loss in JoinReport.
formulas.mathIssues: Group leave-out rather than a sum of individual leave-outs — correct, and the docstring explains why summing individuals double-counts the slot. `marginalPoints` is a deprecated alias; the quantity is an index, not points. Marginals do not sum to the lineup score.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_marginal.py — asserts the leave-out identity and that the five-QB superflex case does not read as the strongest room.

formulas.name: Fragility (absence concentration)
formulas.expression: drop_t = max(0, S(full) − S(full minus t)) for each lineup entrant t at P;  mean_drop = mean(drop_t);  worst_drop = max(drop_t);  fragility = min(1.0, mean_drop / mean(ros_value of P's entrants))
formulas.constants: the 1.0 cap; the denominator choice (mean entrant value, not group marginal) is the load-bearing decision and is justified in-source against the degenerate alternative
formulas.inputs: rosValue index units
formulas.missingDataBehavior: mean_entrant_value ≤ 0 → fragility 0.0. No entrants at P → position omitted from the map entirely.
formulas.mathIssues: The rejected alternative (mean_drop / marginal) collapses to ~1/n and reports the same number for a deep and a thin room — documented as the `_positional_coverage` failure mode. Live spread across 12 rosters: QB 0.154–0.707; only K reaches 1.0 (single kicker). The `_URGENT_FRAGILITY = 0.75` trigger is therefore essentially a kicker detector.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_marginal.py::test_fragility_separates_deep_from_thin (named in the source comment)

formulas.name: Position deficit (below-replacement shortfall)
formulas.expression: baseline = replacement[P].value('starter') × required_slots(P);  deficit = max(0, baseline − marginal_points(P))
formulas.constants: none; required_slots excludes FLEX / SUPER_FLEX / IDP_FLEX / BN by design
formulas.inputs: starter replacement level in rosValue units (measured from this league's own 12 rosters), position marginal
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No replacement level or required_slots == 0 → baseline None and deficit 0.0; the roster payload appends "no replacement levels supplied; tiers default to developmental and position deficits are not computed".
formulas.mathIssues: Deliberately NOT fragility × marginal — engine.py's docstring documents that product as the QB-inversion defect. Live (owner owner-8b8a59adf44e): DL 2.625, K 2.04, RB 3.56, all others 0.0. Note that src/roster_intel/targets.py::_position_severity uses exactly the forbidden product.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_engine.py; the QB-inversion case is described in the module docstring as the motivating defect.

formulas.name: Tradeable surplus
formulas.expression: surplus = { p : p.ros_value > 0 AND p ∉ optimal-lineup entrants AND p.ros_value ≥ 0.60 × replacement[P].value('starter') };  tradeable_surplus = Σ ros_value over that set
formulas.constants: _SURPLUS_FLOOR_RATIO = 0.60 — hand-picked, no calibration found in-repo
formulas.inputs: rosValue index, starter replacement level
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No replacement → floor = 0.0 × 0.60 = 0.0, so EVERY non-entering priced player counts as surplus — the opposite of the stated intent ("otherwise every bench dart throw reads as an asset"), and it is silent.
formulas.mathIssues: Feeds gameplan._acquirable_candidates (capped at 12 per position, descending rosValue) and RosterSignal.surplus, so it is load-bearing for both the target and the partner engines.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_profiles.py exists; no calibration of 0.60 found.

formulas.name: Player tier ladder
formulas.expression: elite if (elite_cut is not None AND starter is not None AND elite_cut > starter AND value ≥ elite_cut); else starter if value ≥ replacement['starter']; else depth if value ≥ replacement['roster']; else developmental.  elite_cut = descending_pool[max(0, round(n·0.05) − 1)]
formulas.constants: ELITE_PERCENTILE = 0.05 — deliberately matched to replacement.py's eliteSeparation so "elite" means one thing repo-wide. TIER_ORDER = (elite, starter, depth, developmental).
formulas.inputs: rosValue; the league's measured replacement levels; league_position_values (the top-5% pool)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: replacement None or value ≤ 0 → developmental. elite_cut None → elite never assigned ("an unmeasurable boundary must not promote").
formulas.mathIssues: engine.analyze_roster never passes league_position_values to build_position_profiles, so elite_cut is ALWAYS None through the only production wiring. Measured live: 0 elite-tier players across 12 rosters × 8 positions. The four-tier ladder is a three-tier ladder in practice.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_profiles.py pins the strict-ladder rule (the earlier inversion where 65-78% classified elite), but not the wiring.

formulas.name: Partner acceptance estimate (logit stack)
formulas.expression: total = logit(0.18) + fairness + 0.90·(2·need − 1) + 0.60·(2·window − 1) + history + manager;  estimate = sigmoid(total).  fairness = 1.40·tanh(2·edge), edge = (partner_gets − partner_gives)/(partner_gets + partner_gives).  history = clamp(0.35·tanh(ln(shrunk/mean)) + 0.5·0.35·tanh(pair/2), ±0.35), shrunk = (observed + 5·mean)/6.  manager = 0.50·tanh(z/4) only if the gate clears.
formulas.constants: BASE_ACCEPTANCE_PRIOR = 0.18 (declared an assumption, not a measurement — no rejection data exists to fit it). MAX_FAIRNESS_LOGIT 1.40, MAX_NEED_LOGIT 0.90, MAX_WINDOW_LOGIT 0.60, MAX_HISTORY_LOGIT 0.35, PAIR_FAMILIARITY_SHARE 0.5, MAX_MANAGER_LOGIT 0.50 (latent), history shrinkage prior_n = 5.0. All hand-picked and named; the module says so.
formulas.inputs: market values on ONE market (0-9999); need and window alignments ∈[0,1]; completed-trade counts; accept/reject decisions
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Each term returns (0.0, note) on abstention — a real zero contribution plus a stamped reason, never an imputed value. Mixed offense/IDP markets suppress fairness entirely rather than summing incommensurable scales.
formulas.mathIssues: Under /api/gameplan's wiring (no TradeShape, no trade counts) fairness = history = manager = 0.0 always, so the estimate reduces to sigmoid(logit(0.18) + 0.90(2n−1) + 0.60(2w−1)). Measured live: 0.0599–0.1702 across 11 partners.
formulas.validated: none — rejections are structurally unobserved (the snapshot ingests only status=='complete'). tests/roster_intel/test_partner.py and test_partner_reachable_range.py pin properties, not calibration.

formulas.name: Partner fit score (the ranking quantity)
formulas.expression: confidence = tier_confidence × (0.55 + 0.45·measured/3), then min(·, 0.45).  anchored = 0.18 + confidence·(estimate − 0.18).  structural = 0.5·(need + window).  fit_score = 100·clamp(0.65·anchored + 0.35·structural·confidence, 0, 1)
formulas.constants: STRUCTURAL_COVERAGE_FLOOR = 0.55; MAX_CONFIDENCE_WITHOUT_DECISION_DATA = 0.45 (documented as non-binding); tier confidences absent 0.05 / shapeOnly 0.30 / historyInformed 0.40 / decisionCalibrated 0.85 (unreachable); the 0.65 / 0.35 blend weights.
formulas.inputs: estimate, need, window, evidence tier, structural coverage count
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Abstaining terms reduce `measured` and therefore confidence — the module calls this "abstentions must cost confidence or the score launders ignorance into certainty".
formulas.mathIssues: Under /api/gameplan: tier = shapeOnly, measured = 2 → confidence = 0.30·(0.55 + 0.45·0.6667) = 0.2550 for EVERY partner, invariant. I computed the reachable range under that wiring as [9.49 (n=w=0), 25.86 (n=w=1)] against a published max of 43.12. Measured live: 11 partners spanning 10.48–16.37. need and window enter twice (once via the capped logit, once uncapped at weight 0.35·confidence), which the source acknowledges inverts the stated budget hierarchy.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_partner_reachable_range.py and TestNeedAndWindowEnterTwice pin the double-entry and the derived bounds — but against the module's theoretical maxima, not the wiring gameplan actually uses, which is why the mismatch survives.

formulas.name: Manager evidence gate
formulas.expression: decisions = accepted + rejected;  rate = accepted/decisions;  se = sqrt(0.18·(1−0.18)/decisions);  z = (rate − 0.18)/se.  Admissible iff decisions ≥ 30 AND |z| ≥ 2.0.
formulas.constants: MANAGER_EVIDENCE_MIN_DECISIONS = 30 (justified from SE ≈ 0.073 at n=30, p≈0.2), MANAGER_EVIDENCE_MIN_Z = 2.0
formulas.inputs: observed accept/reject decisions per manager
formulas.missingDataBehavior: accepted or rejected is None → admissible False with the reason "the league snapshot records only completed trades, so rejections are unobserved and an acceptance rate is unidentifiable". Completed trades are recorded as accepts_observed but never used as a denominator.
formulas.mathIssues: Structurally unsatisfiable under the current data source — the gate is correct and permanently closed. MAX_MANAGER_LOGIT = 0.50 is therefore dead code by design.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_partner.py

formulas.name: Target-position priority
formulas.expression: realistic = median(top-3 exact re-solve gains);  material_floor = max(3.0, 0.01·lineup_score);  priority = realistic × window_mult × scar_mult × eff_mult × confidence.  scar_mult = 0.85 + 0.30·clamp(waiver_scarcity,0,1) or 1.0.  eff_mult = clamp(0.80 + 0.40·clamp(starter/price,0,2)/2, 0.80, 1.20) or 1.0.  confidence = clamp(0.40 + 0.15·supplied, 0, 1), ×0.85 if fewer than 3 candidates tested.
formulas.constants: MIN_MATERIAL_POINTS 3.0, MIN_MATERIAL_SHARE 0.01, REALISTIC_CANDIDATE_DEPTH 3, MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_POSITION 12 (gameplan). All hand-picked; the docstrings argue for them but cite no calibration.
formulas.inputs: exact optimal-lineup re-solves in rosValue index units; candidate ages; ScarcityComponents; market prices per position
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Every absent multiplier defaults to 1.0 with a stamped note. winNowWeight is emitted as null on viable rows when ages are missing, and as the GLOBAL scalar on non-viable rows — FIELD_POLICY declares the field non-sortable for exactly that reason.
formulas.mathIssues: Verified numerically on the live league (owner owner-8b8a59adf44e, contract with 661/666 ages): RB realistic 15.08 × horizon 0.8755 × 1.0 × 1.0 × 0.85 = 11.222 = the emitted priority. scar_mult and eff_mult are 1.0 by construction everywhere. `confidence` counts scarcity as supplied even though the term abstained — 0.85 where 0.70 is honest.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_targets.py; tests/api/test_gameplan_endpoint.py::test_win_now_weight_is_null_when_no_ages_reach_the_engines. No test pins that the multipliers are all inert.

formulas.name: Target-player priority and corroboration gate
formulas.expression: gain = S(pool + candidate) − S(pool).  ROSTER_FIT iff gain ≥ max(3.0, 0.01·lineup_score).  MARKET_EDGE iff (ros_value − price)/price > 0.  SCARCITY iff waiver_scarcity ≥ 0.60.  ROLE ≥0.6, PROJECTION ≥0.6, AVAILABILITY ≥0.5.  Gate: len(corroborating) ≥ 1.  anchor = max(gain, 0.25·material_floor);  priority = anchor × scar_mult × (1 + clamp(edge,±0.5)·0.4) × (0.7 + 0.6·clamp(avail,0,1)) × (0.35 + 0.15·len(corroborating))
formulas.constants: MIN_CORROBORATING_SIGNALS = 1 ("demanding two would reject nearly everything"), _SCARCITY_SIGNAL_PERCENTILE = 0.60, role/projection 0.6, availability 0.5, the 0.25 anchor floor, edge weight 0.4, avail band 0.7–1.3, confidence 0.35 + 0.15/signal. All hand-picked.
formulas.inputs: exact re-solves in rosValue units; market values on 0-9999; scarcity; role/projection/availability maps
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Absent market value → edge null plus a note. Absent availability → avail_mult = 0.7 + 0.6·0.5 = 1.0 — a defaulted 0.5, not an abstention. This one IS imputed, unlike every other term in the module.
formulas.mathIssues: Under the live wiring only ROSTER_FIT can fire, so len(corroborating) is always 1 → confidence 0.5, and every other multiplier is 1.0 → priority == gain/2 exactly. Verified: travis etienne 16.18 → 8.09; bucky irving 15.08 → 7.54; quinshon judkins 10.86 → 5.43; david montgomery 8.25 → 4.125; dak prescott 7.24 → 3.62. Live yield: 6 recommended of 74 evaluated.
formulas.validated: tests/roster_intel/test_targets.py; tests/api/test_gameplan_endpoint.py::test_rejected_target_players_carry_their_reason. No test asserts scarcity can fire.

formulas.name: Horizon weight (the only per-position window term)
formulas.expression: youth = clamp((32 − mean_candidate_age)/10, 0, 1);  age_mult(s) = (1 − future[s]) + future[s]·(0.40 + 1.20·youth);  hw = Σ_s p(s)·base[s]·age_mult(s) / Σ_s p(s).  win_now_weight = Σ_s p(s)·base[s] / Σ_s p(s) (a global scalar, explicitly documented as unable to reorder anything).
formulas.constants: _WIN_NOW_WEIGHTS = {champ 1.00, playoff 0.85, retool 0.45, productive_struggle 0.30, rebuild 0.15}; _STATE_FUTURE_ORIENTATION = {champ 0.00, playoff 0.15, retool 0.65, productive_struggle 0.85, rebuild 1.00}; _FUTURE_AGE_FLOOR 0.40, _FUTURE_AGE_SPAN 1.20 (a 4x spread by design); _AGE_YOUNG 22 / _AGE_OLD 32 shared with window.py. All hand-assigned priors.
formulas.inputs: window affinities (unitless), mean age of the position's top-3 candidates in years
formulas.missingDataBehavior: window None or mean_age None → returns None; the caller sets window_mult = 1.0 and stamps "the window weight is per-position by age and could not be computed, so it did NOT affect this ranking".
formulas.mathIssues: This is the ONLY term in either target engine that can reorder positions under the live wiring, and it is driven by window affinities the window module itself declares uncalibrated. Measured live: 0.8755 for RB on a playoff_contender roster; 0.8685 as the global scalar with contract=None.
formulas.validated: none found for the base/future tables

formulas.name: Terminal tier buckets
formulas.expression: elite if value ≥ 8500; high if ≥ 6500; mid if ≥ 3000; else depth
formulas.constants: 8500 / 6500 / 3000 on the 0-9999 board. Comment says "Keep in sync with the frontend's tierBucket helper" — and they ARE in sync (verified byte-for-byte). No calibration evidence for the cut points.
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue, 0-9999
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Rows with value ≤ 0 are skipped entirely from `total` and `tiers` (terminal.py ~line 1455) and reduce `coverage = resolved / len(current_players)`.
formulas.mathIssues: None. This is the one threshold pair in the audit that does not diverge between Python and JS.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_terminal.py::test_build_terminal_payload_full_for_selected_team touches the shape only.

formulas.name: MAD volatility label
formulas.expression: deltas = |rank_i − rank_{i−1}| over the 30-day window;  med = median(deltas);  mad = median(|d − med|);  label = 'low' if mad ≤ 1, 'med' if mad ≤ 4, else 'high'
formulas.constants: window_days = 30, minimum 3 points, thresholds 1 and 4. Hand-picked, no calibration in-repo.
formulas.inputs: rank history points, one per UTC date
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Fewer than 3 total points OR fewer than 3 inside the window → None, and every rule reading volatility?.label declines. Not coerced to 'low'.
formulas.mathIssues: 'high' gates the RISK, SELL and MONITOR rules — all three of which email. Requires ≥3 distinct DATES (rank_history dedupes per date), so with a shallow log volatility is universally None and the entire risk half of the engine is silent. Python renders MAD with f"{mad:.1f}" (round-half-even) and JS with .toFixed(1) (half away from zero), so MAD 2.25 prints "2.2" vs "2.3" — the parity suite deliberately does not assert prose.
formulas.validated: tests/fixtures/signal_parity_cases.json exercises the labels but pins agreement between two engines, not correctness of 1/4.

formulas.name: Signal rule table (backend — the emailed one)
formulas.expression: p100 RISK alert_with_drop: alert>0 AND neg>0 AND trend7≤−3.  p95 RISK high_vol_drop: vol=='high' AND trend7≤−5.  p80 SELL sustained_downtrend: trend7≤−3 AND trend30 is not None AND trend30≤0.  p78 SELL neg_news_high_vol: neg>0 AND vol=='high'.  p65 MONITOR alert_present: alert>0.  p62 MONITOR high_vol: vol=='high'.  p50 STRONG_HOLD elite_stable: value≥7000 AND trend30 is not None AND trend30≥0 AND vol ∈ {low,med}.  p40 BUY uptrend_controlled: trend7≥3 AND vol≠'high'.  p38 BUY pos_news_rising: pos>0 AND rankChange>0.  Highest priority wins; nothing fires → HOLD/default_hold.
formulas.constants: Rank-delta cuts −3 / −5 / +3; value cut 7000; priorities 100/95/80/78/65/62/50/40/38. RETIRED: low_conf_unstable (MONITOR p60, confidence < 0.35) — retired because _marketConfidence is structurally capped at 0.375·0.65 + 1.00·0.35 = 0.59375 with a measured live distribution of p10 0.480 / median 0.491 / p90 0.564 and exactly ONE of 1094 rows under 0.35.
formulas.inputs: trend7 / trend30 (rank deltas), volatility label, rankDerivedValue (0-9999), news alert and impact counts
formulas.outputRange: one of RISK/SELL/MONITOR/STRONG_HOLD/BUY/HOLD plus the ordered fired chain
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Null trends never satisfy a comparison (explicit `is not None` guards on both trend rules). `confidence` is deliberately NOT coerced to 0 when absent (256 of 1094 live rows carry none) and is diagnostic-only since the retirement.
formulas.mathIssues: Compared line-by-line against frontend/lib/signal-engine.js: EVERY threshold matches (−3, −5, −3/0, 7000/0, +3, >0, and the null-guards, which JS expresses as `(c.trend7 ?? 0)` and explicit `!= null`). **No threshold exists in both with different values.** The divergence is in the context builders, not the table. Separately, trend7 and trend30 are the same number when the history log is shallower than 7 days, which makes p80 collapse to `trend7 ≤ −3`.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_signal_engine_parity.py + frontend/__tests__/signal-engine-parity.test.js against tests/fixtures/signal_parity_cases.json (52 cases: 28 HOLD, 9 MONITOR, 5 RISK, 4 BUY, 3 SELL, 3 STRONG_HOLD). Asserts signal, tag and the ORDERED fired-tag list. Explicitly does NOT assert reason prose, fired-entry shape, or the context builders.

formulas.name: Portfolio insight cards (best / risk / chip / buy-low)
formulas.expression: bestAsset = argmax(value).  biggestRisk tier1 = argmax(value | volLabel=='high' AND trend7<0); tier2 = argmax(value | volLabel=='high'); tier3 = min-trend7 among trend7 ≤ −3.  tradeChip = argmax(trend7 | 3000 ≤ value ≤ 7500 AND trend7 ≥ 3 AND volLabel ≠ 'high').  buyLow = argmax(−rankChange | not on roster AND 0 < rank ≤ 150 AND value ≥ 3000 AND rankChange ≤ −3).
formulas.constants: 3000 / 7500 (chip band), 3 (rise), −3 (drop), 3000 / 150 (buy-low). Identical on both sides. All hand-picked, no calibration in-repo.
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue 0-9999, trend7/trend30 rank deltas, volatility label, rankChange
formulas.outputRange: one player per card, or null
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `(p['trend7'] or 0)` — a NULL trend is coerced to 0 in the risk tier1/tier3 and chip filters on BOTH sides. Benign here (0 fails both `< 0` and `≥ 3`) but it means "unmeasured" and "flat" are indistinguishable in these filters, which is the exact pattern the SELL rule was fixed for.
formulas.mathIssues: The `short_drop_long_steady` metric name and its "long-term steady" prose describe a 30d test neither side performs. The JS tier3 comment claims "trend7 ≤ −3 and confidence low"; the code never reads confidence.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_terminal.py::test_portfolio_breakdown_includes_byposition_byage_volexposure asserts the breakdown keys exist; no test asserts which player any card selects.

formulas.name: Age buckets and portfolio breakdowns
formulas.expression: rookie if isRookie or age ≤ 22; young if ≤ 24; prime if ≤ 28; vet otherwise; unknown if age is null or ≤ 0.  bucket pct = round(bucket_value / totalValue × 100, 1).  medianAge over ages > 0.
formulas.constants: 22 / 24 / 28 — byte-identical on both sides. No calibration found.
formulas.inputs: row.age in years, row.rookie flag, rankDerivedValue as the weight
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing age → 'unknown' bucket, never imputed to a number. Live contract: 930 of 1092 rows carry an age.
formulas.mathIssues: No threshold divergence. But the server denominator excludes picks and the client's includes them, so the SAME bucket percentage means two different things depending on which path served it, and PortfolioSummary can mix them.
formulas.validated: none found for the bucket edges

formulas.name: Roster-aware historical delta
formulas.expression: past_roster = current_players, then for each trade with timestamp > cutoff_ms involving this owner: remove what they GOT, add back what they GAVE.  past_total = Σ over past_roster of (value-history value at the latest date ≤ target, else rank-history rank → rank_to_value_for_scope).  coverage = resolved/expected;  reliable iff coverage ≥ 0.60;  delta = current_total − past_total, or null when not reliable.
formulas.constants: _MIN_COVERAGE_FOR_RELIABLE_SUM = 0.60; windows 7 / 30 / 90 / 180 days; history_window_days = max(window_days, 180).
formulas.inputs: sleeper.trades[] (110 rows live, ms timestamps), data/source_value_history.jsonl (preferred), data/rank_history.jsonl (fallback)
formulas.outputRange: signed integer on the 0-9999 scale, or null
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Under 60% coverage → value stays null with `reason: 'low_history_coverage'` and the coverage fraction is still surfaced so the UI can say "insufficient history (N%)" instead of a bare dash. `rosterAware` is True only when a trade actually moved this owner's roster — the prior version set it True with an empty trades list and the fix is documented.
formulas.mathIssues: Reconstruction uses display names, so cross-universe name collisions collapse (accepted explicitly). The scope-aware Hill fallback (offense vs idp curve) was a 2026-07-29 fix worth ~800 points per defender on the 9999 scale. Both history files are absent from the repository, so no delta is verifiable offline.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_terminal.py has 7 dedicated tests: test_roster_aware_delta_uses_trade_history, test_roster_aware_is_false_when_no_trades, test_roster_aware_is_true_when_owner_trade_inside_window, test_trade_for_other_owner_does_not_flip_roster_aware, test_delta_detail_exposes_coverage_fraction, test_low_coverage_produces_null_value_with_fraction, test_value_history_fallback_covers_when_rank_history_missing. This is the best-pinned system in the audit.

formulas.name: News relevance scoring
formulas.expression: relevance = 100 if any mentioned player is on the resolved roster; else 50 if on any league roster; else 10.  Sorted by (−relevance, −timestamp).  Capped at the first 30 items.  Public mode drops everything with relevance ≥ 100.
formulas.inputs: aggregated news items carrying players[].name; roster_set and league_set as lowercased name sets
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No news service or any exception → gather_news_items returns [] and the whole block is empty; non-fatal by design. Silently disables 4 of the 9 signal rules.
formulas.mathIssues: Name matching is bare lowercase against the Sleeper roster list — no canonical-name normalization, so a provider spelling a name differently silently scores 10 instead of 100.
formulas.validated: none found for the 100/50/10 ladder; tests/api/test_terminal.py::test_public_mode_strips_private_fields covers the public filter.

formulas.name: team-phase classification (frontend /phases)
formulas.expression: totalValue = Σ of the top-25 rankDerivedValue on the roster;  medianAge = median of those players' ages;  leagueMedians = median across the 12 team snapshots.  isHighValue = totalValue > leagueMedians.value (strict);  isYounger = medianAge != null AND medianAge < leagueMedians.age (strict).  high∧young → Win-now; high∧¬young → Contender; ¬high∧young → Rebuild; else Mixed.  partnership score = max(0, valueGap) × max(0, ageGap || 1).
formulas.constants: TOP_N_FOR_VALUE = 25; both thresholds are the league medians (no absolute anchor); partnerships sliced to 6, displayed 3.
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue (0-9999) and age (years) from buildRows; sleeper.teams[].players
formulas.outputRange: 4 labels; no confidence, no margin, no tie state
formulas.missingDataBehavior: medianAge null → isYounger false → the team is treated as OLDER. Players with value ≤ 0 are dropped from the top-25 pool. Picks never resolve (team.players holds only players) so pick value is entirely absent from the phase read.
formulas.mathIssues: Reproduced on the live contract + live rosters: medians value 91,579.5 / age 26.0 → 5 Win-now, 1 Contender, 6 Mixed, 0 Rebuild. Forced quota (exactly 6 above a median of 12). Ages are integers so 4 of 12 teams tie the median age exactly and are silently pushed to 'older'. Margins as small as 4.6% of a team's total decide a label with no hysteresis. Pure value sum — no schedule, no playoff structure, no lineup solve, no opponent strength.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/team-phase.test.js — 5 cases, ALL with exactly two teams (so the median trivially splits them) and hand-built values. Asserts the label mapping only; does not test 12-team quota behaviour, median-age ties, stability, or the Rebuild quadrant on real data.

formulas.name: Starter/bench split
formulas.expression: fillLineup(assets, rosterPositions | slotsFromStarterCounts(rosterSettings.starters)) filling on `lineupPos` (DL/LB/DB kept distinct), value-descending within eligible slots.  starterPct = starterValue / (starterValue + benchValue) × 100.  Picks excluded from the split.
formulas.constants: none — the slot table comes from the live host or the registry; the literal 9-slot fallback was REMOVED and the source records it produced 40.1% starters against a true 68.1%.
formulas.inputs: sleeper.rosterPositions (live: 21 starters + 37 BN), else registry rosterSettings.starters
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Three-rung ladder: live host → registry → refuse. Both rungs absent → `available: false`, `lineupKnown: false`, and the panel says so rather than rendering 0% as a measurement.
formulas.mathIssues: Correct as written. Filling on the collapsed `pos` (every defender = IDP) was the prior defect — it credited the top 9 defenders by value regardless of the league's 3/3/3 slot structure — and is documented.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/starter-slots.test.js and portfolio-pick-join.test.js

formulas.name: Movers ranking (three independent implementations)
formulas.expression: Server + client ticker: filter to scope (roster / league / rank ≤ 150), drop rankChange null or 0, sort by (|change| desc, value desc), take limit.  MoversPanel: a separate endpoint over rank_history.jsonl with a 14-day window and a 15-rank threshold.
formulas.constants: Server limits roster 20 / league 30 / top150 30; ticker limit 20 with MIN_RENDERABLE 3; top150 cut = rank ≤ 150; MoversPanel defaults 14 days and 15 ranks.
formulas.inputs: rankChange (per-scrape delta) for the first two; rank_history deltas for the third
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rankChange null or 0 → excluded as "quiet"; MarketTicker renders an explicit quiet state below 3 items rather than an empty strip.
formulas.mathIssues: Server and ticker are algorithmically identical, and the server's output is consumed by nothing. The MoversPanel definition (14d window, ≥15 ranks) is a THIRD, materially different definition of "mover" shipped on the same page with no reconciliation.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/movers.test.js covers the /api/movers path only.

formulas.name: Scouting intel feed salience
formulas.expression: _salience = |trend7|×2 + (volLabel=='high' ? 8 : volLabel=='med' ? 3 : 0) + (isRookie ? 2 : 0);  take top 5 descending
formulas.constants: weights 2 / 8 / 3 / 0 / 2 — hand-picked, no justification in-source and no calibration
formulas.inputs: trend7 (rank delta), volatility label, rookie flag
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `p.trend7 ?? 0` and an unknown volLabel scores 0, so a player with no history has salience 0 (or 2 if a rookie) and never reaches the feed — correct by accident rather than by design.
formulas.mathIssues: Mixes a rank delta (unbounded) with categorical bonuses on no common scale; a player who moved 5 ranks (salience 10) outranks a high-volatility player who did not move (salience 8) with no stated rationale.
formulas.validated: none found

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. I read every file named in the brief plus the modules they actually depend on. Where a formula was non-obvious I reproduced it numerically in the scratchpad and, where possible, ran the real engines against the real on-disk snapshots. Two reproductions anchor most of the findings:

1. I built the full league bundle offline: `G.load_league_inputs('dynasty_main','superflex_tep15_ppr1', contract)` -> `G.build_league_bundle(...)` -> `G.build_gameplan(bundle, 'owner-8b8a59adf44e')`, using `data/ros/team_strength/latest.json` (12 rosters, 57 players each, 666 total) and `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json`. To get a real contract I reconstructed one with `build_api_data_contract(exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json)` — 1,092 playersArray rows, 937 with a Sleeper playerId, 930 with an age, 1,092 with canonicalSiteValues — which is why I can quote real age coverage (661/666) and price coverage (627/666) rather than guessing. Cold league build measured at 802 ms on this host.

2. I re-implemented `team-phase.js` in Python against that same contract and the live `sleeper.teams` to get the real 12-team classification. That is what produced the "zero Rebuild" result and the Collin contradiction.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY.
- `data/rank_history.jsonl` and `data/source_value_history.jsonl` do not exist in this checkout (written at runtime, gitignored). Everything downstream — trend7, trend30, MAD volatility, all six signal labels, the four portfolio insight cards, the 7/30/90/180 deltas, the watchlist trends — is Not Verifiable from Repository. I verified the code paths and the threshold parity, not the outputs. Production log depth is Not Verified; terminal.py's own comment says "~2 days deep", and that claim is what makes the trend-window collapse severe rather than theoretical.
- `/api/terminal` end to end: I read the route (server.py:10321-10540) but did not execute it — it needs `latest_contract_data`, a news service and a user_kv store.
- `packages.py` I read for constants and rejection taxonomy but did not exercise; it only runs with `?partner=<ownerId>` and needs the live site-value join. Its tunables (MAX_PACKAGE_ASSETS 2, NEAR_MISS_PCT 25.0, CORNERSTONE_PREMIUM_PCT 15.0, CORNERSTONE_TOP_N 3, CORNERSTONE_VALUE_SHARE 0.60) are all hand-picked with no in-repo calibration; I found no backtest for any of them.
- Whether `_history_lookup`'s first-wins collision ever bites in production: 0 display names span more than one assetClass on today's board (550 offense / 398 idp / 144 pick), so it is latent.

DOES "CONTENDER" ACCOUNT FOR SCHEDULE / PLAYOFF STRUCTURE, OR IS IT A PURE VALUE SUM? There are two contender classifiers and the answer differs:
- `/phases` (`team-phase.js`) is a PURE VALUE SUM: top-25 rankDerivedValue summed, compared to the league median, crossed with median age. No schedule, no opponents, no playoff structure, no lineup solve, not even the roster's own starting requirements.
- `/api/gameplan`'s competitive window DOES consume schedule and bracket — but only for 8 of 12 rosters, and only through a championship-odds percentile in which 4 of the 8 values are exactly 0.0. The other 4 rosters fall back to a lineup-score percentile, which is a pure value proxy. So a third of the league is classified on a pure value sum wearing the same five-state label as the rest.

CONFLICT STATE OR MISLEADING NEUTRAL? The pattern is consistent and it is neither: it is SILENT DEFAULTING to a multiplicative 1.0 or an additive 0. Nothing in these subsystems averages opposing evidence into a Neutral — the modules are unusually disciplined about that (every abstaining term returns a note, nulls are never collapsed to zero, confidence intervals are never zero-width, `_unpriced_note` even warns that a zero unpriced count is not a coverage claim). The failure is the opposite: an abstained term contributes an identity, the composite still ships as a score, and the reader cannot tell a measured 1.0 from an absent one without reading `notes`. Concretely: `scarcityMultiplier: 1.0` and `winNowWeight: 0.8685` look like measurements and are not; `acceptanceConfidence: 0.255` is constant across every partner in the league; `priority` is `gain x 0.5`; the window's five affinities sum to 1 and are labelled `probabilities` (deprecated alias retained) while `to_dict()` states no anchor, weight or temperature was ever fitted to an outcome. There is NO conflict state anywhere in these subsystems — the window's `confidence < 0.30` note is the closest thing, and on the live league nothing triggers it (measured confidences 0.388–0.666).

THRESHOLDS THAT EXIST IN BOTH BACKEND AND FRONTEND: I diffed every one. `src/api/terminal.py::_evaluate_signal` vs `frontend/lib/signal-engine.js` — all nine rules match exactly (-3, -5, -3/0, 7000/0, +3, >0, and the null-guards). TIER_CUTOFFS 8500/6500/3000 vs `TeamCommandHeader.jsx:36-41` — identical. Age buckets 22/24/28 — identical. Insight-card bands 3000/7500/150/-3 — identical. Volatility 1/4 — identical. **No threshold exists in both with different values.** The divergences are structural, not numeric: the context builders (value fallback, history-key resolution), the pick inclusion in totals, and the position-alias map.

ON DOCUMENTATION QUALITY. This codebase's docstrings are unusually honest — several findings are things the source itself flags (the pick exclusion, the 8/12 sim coverage, the marketEdge scale mismatch, the FIELD_POLICY non-sortable declarations). Where docs and code disagree I reported it: the `_odds_for` docstring about the simulator's fields, the `short_drop_long_steady` metric name, the JS tier3 "confidence low" comment, and the coverage note advertising scarcity as a live corroborator. CLAUDE.md is silent on `src/roster_intel/`, `/api/gameplan` and `/phases` entirely — none appears in it — so there was nothing to check against for the largest subsystem in scope.

WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE DECISIONS. Short list: the exact lineup solve and everything directly derived from it — `marginal_points`, `fragility`, `worst_absence_drop`, `lineupGain`, `realisticGain`. These are real re-solves against a real optimizer with a real slot table, and they are the only quantities here that measure something. The tier cutoffs and the roster-aware delta machinery are well-built and well-tested (assuming the history files exist in production). Everything composite — `priority`, `tradePartnerFitScore`, `acceptanceConfidence`, `severity`, the five-state window label, and both `/phases` labels — is a hand-picked-constant stack with no calibration anywhere in the repository, and under the current wiring most of them are monotone rescales of the one input that is real.

findings.title: Playoff and championship "odds" are structurally degenerate out of season — every team is 100% or 0%, cached and served as current
findings.evidence: `src/ros/playoff_sim.py:704` `schedule = _remaining_schedule(snapshot)` returns [] when the last loaded season is complete (offseason). The sim loop at `:721` then adds nothing to `sim_wins`, which was seeded from realized wins at `:719`, so every one of the 2,000 draws produces the identical ranking. Live output `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json`: `{'n_simulations': 2000, 'converged': True, 'worstPlayoffOddsSe': 0.0}` with `playoffOdds` exactly 1.0 for six owners and 0.0 for two, and `expectedWins` at integer values 6.0/7.0/9.0/11.0 (no fractional part = zero simulated games). Same in `data/ros/sims/dynasty_new_playoff.json`. `computedAt: 2026-08-04T03:57:31` — the file is 4 hours old and the numbers are last season's final standings. There is no preseason guard anywhere in `playoff_sim.py` or `championship.py`; `power_v2.py:195-223` has one (`_is_preseason`), so the codebase knows the state exists and only one of three consumers handles it.
findings.userImpact: Every ROS contender surface (/league → Championship, /league → Trade Deadline, the ROS Fit panel on /trade) shows fabricated certainty: six teams at a 100% playoff chance and the rest at 0%, in August, before a single 2026 game. `converged: true` and a Wilson CI of [1.0, 1.0] actively assert the number is trustworthy.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the `_is_preseason` guard (already written in `power_v2.py:195`) to `simulate_playoff_odds` and `simulate_championship_odds`. When the remaining schedule is empty, return `{playoffOdds: [], reason: "no_remaining_schedule"}` rather than a deterministic replay of the completed season, and have the lazy section builders render "odds unavailable until the season starts".
findings.affectedSystems: src/ros/playoff_sim.py, src/ros/championship.py, src/ros/trade_deadline.py, /league Championship + Trade Deadline tabs, RosTradeFitPanel

findings.title: A team missing from the playoff sim is coerced to 0% playoff odds and labelled "Seller" — the #1 ROS-strength team is currently told to sell
findings.evidence: `src/ros/trade_deadline.py:82` `po = float((playoffs.get(owner) or {}).get("playoffOdds") or 0.0)` — an owner absent from `latest_playoff.json` gets a confident 0.0, not None. The sim covers 8 owners; `data/ros/team_strength/latest.json` has 12. Executing `build_team_directions()` against the committed data on disk returns: `Brent | po 0.0 | co 0.0 | pct 1.0 | Seller` — Brent is ranked #1 of 12 on `teamRosStrength` (646.85, next best 536.79) and is told to sell. Also `Collin | po 0.0 | pct 0.75 | Seller`, plus `Kich`, `Blaine`, `jstuedle`. Meanwhile `MaKayla | pct 0.5833 | Hold` and `Ty | pct 0.5 | Hold` outrank them. `direction.py:104` `elif playoff_odds_pct < 0.25 and championship_odds_pct < 0.02: label = "Seller"` is the branch that fires, and `team_ros_strength_percentile` is passed in at `direction.py:58` but only interpolated into the display string at `:120` — it never influences the label.
findings.userImpact: Direct, wrong trade advice on /trade and /league: four of twelve managers are labelled "Seller" with the recommendation "Sell aging win-now players. Prioritize 2026/2027 picks" purely because they were absent from an input file. The strongest roster in the league gets the strongest sell signal.
findings.recommendedFix: Distinguish missing from zero: skip owners with no odds row entirely, or emit `label: "Unknown"` with `reason: "no_odds_row"`. Do not default a probability to 0.0. Separately, either wire `team_ros_strength_percentile` into `classify_team`'s decision or drop the parameter.

findings.title: Rank scores are normalized against each source's own board size, so an IDP-only board and a 978-player board are blended as if commensurable
findings.evidence: `src/ros/parse.py:43-46` `rank_to_score` divides by `ln(total_ranked + 1)`, where `total_ranked` is whatever the source published. `aggregate.py:181` scores every row this way and `:230` takes a plain weighted mean across sources.
