Live consequence for Aidan Hutchinson in `data/ros/aggregate/latest.json`: `draftSharksRosSf rank 98 of 978 → score 33.42`; `fantasyProsRosIdp rank 1 of 219 → score 100.00` — a 2.99x disagreement produced entirely by board size, for the same player from two boards that both contain him. Reproduced numerically: `(33.42*1.375 + 100.00*0.9371)/(1.375+0.9371) = 60.41`, matching the file exactly. Result: Hutchinson sits at `rosRankOverall: 13`, above Ja'Marr Chase (67.07), Lamar Jackson (64.26) and Christian McCaffrey (65.54). Position counts in the aggregate top 50: LB 7, DL 3 — ten IDP in the top 50 of a board whose only IDP source ranks 219 players. `confidence` does not protect against this: it computes to 0.425 for Hutchinson (`0.45*0.5 + 0.35*max(0, 1-33.289/30) + 0.20` — the agreement term floors at 0), and nothing downstream gates on confidence.
findings.userImpact: `teamRosStrength` sums these values over the optimal lineup (`team_strength.py:157`), so a roster of top-of-the-IDP-board defenders scores like a roster of elite offense. That composite sets the projected reverse-standings draft order behind the Pick Projector (`pick_projection.py:112`), the ROS Power v2 top component (`power_v2.py:66`, weight 0.38), and the playoff-sim mean shift (`playoff_sim.py:523`). The distortion propagates to every ROS decision surface.
findings.recommendedFix: Normalize within a comparable population, not within a publication. Either (a) score IDP rows only against other IDP rows and offense only against offense, then join the two ladders with a measured cross-market ratio (the dynasty pipeline already does this for KTC↔IDPTradeCalc), or (b) restrict each source's contribution to the position family it actually covers. Do not blend a 219-row board with a 978-row board on a shared 0-100 axis.
findings.affectedSystems: src/ros/aggregate.py, src/ros/parse.py, src/ros/team_strength.py, src/ros/pick_projection.py, src/ros/power_v2.py, src/ros/playoff_sim.py

findings.title: fantasyProsRosIdp stamps total_ranked as its row count while rank comes from a larger board — 13 IDP players silently score 0 and vanish
findings.evidence: `src/ros/sources/fantasypros_ros_idp.py:44` reads `rank_field = raw.get("rank") or raw.get("Rank") or raw.get("effectiveRank")`. `CSVs/site_raw/fantasyProsIdp.csv` has no `rank`/`Rank` column (header: `name,originalRank,effectiveRank,derivationMethod,family,normalizedValue,matchedSourceName,position,team`), so it always takes `effectiveRank`, which runs to 362. Line `:75-77` then sets `total_ranked = n` where `n = len(rows) = 219`. `parse.py:41-42` returns 0.0 when `r > n`, and `aggregate.py:182-183` `if score <= 0: continue` drops the row without a log line. Measured on the committed data: `data/ros/sources/fantasyProsRosIdp.csv` has 218 distinct names but only 205 appear as `fantasyProsRosIdp` contributors in `data/ros/aggregate/latest.json`. The 13 dropped are all rank > 219: bobby okereke (350), bobby wagner (288), drue tranquill (344), germaine pratt (362), trenton simpson (282). `rank_to_score(288, 219) = 0.0`, verified.
findings.userImpact: Bobby Wagner appears verbatim in `data/ros/team_strength/latest.json` under Brent's `unmappedPlayers` — the UI tells the user "no ROS source ranked this player" when a source did rank him and the arithmetic threw it away. Those players contribute exactly 0.0 to `teamRosStrength` (`team_strength.py:123`), biasing the composite and the draft-order projection built on it. Every surviving IDP score is also normalized against 219 instead of the real ~362 board, inflating them.
findings.recommendedFix: Set `total_ranked = max(rank)` across the parsed rows, or renumber 1..N after sorting by `effectiveRank`. Add a warning in `aggregate.py` when a row is dropped for `score <= 0` — the silent drop is what hid this.
findings.affectedSystems: src/ros/sources/fantasypros_ros_idp.py, src/ros/aggregate.py, data/ros/aggregate/latest.json, team strength, pick projector

findings.title: Non-default league sims read the DEFAULT league's team-strength file, apply zero ROS blend, and still stamp rosStrengthAvailable: true
findings.evidence: `src/ros/playoff_sim.py:423`, `:277` and `:191` all hardcode `path = ROS_DATA_DIR / "team_strength" / "latest.json"` — the default league's file — with no `league_key` parameter, while `scrape.py:402-403` iterates `active_leagues()` and calls the sim for each. `:520-523` then does `ros_score = ros_strength_map.get(owner_id)`; when the owner isn't in the default league's map the blend is skipped. Measured: `data/ros/sims/dynasty_new_playoff.json` has 8 owners, of whom 0 appear in `data/ros/team_strength/latest.json` (12 dynasty_main owners) and only 3 appear in `data/ros/team_strength/dynasty_new.json`. Yet `:818` stamps `"rosStrengthAvailable": bool(ros_map)` — True, because the default file exists — and the file records `rosStrengthAvailable: true`. `_load_team_depth_ratios` and `_load_team_rosters` have the same hardcoded path, so a best-ball non-default league would presim the wrong rosters entirely.
findings.userImpact: A ROS-branded playoff projection for a second league is not ROS-influenced at all, and the payload asserts the opposite. Per CLAUDE.md's leagueKey rule this is exactly the cross-league collapse the architecture forbids.
findings.recommendedFix: Thread `league_key` into `_load_ros_strength_map`, `_load_team_depth_ratios` and `_load_team_rosters` and route through `team_strength._team_strength_path(league_key)`, which already resolves per-league files. Stamp `rosStrengthAvailable` from the count of owners that actually received a blend, not from file existence.

findings.title: Adapter failure does NOT keep last-known-good values in the aggregate; the doc, the CI comment and the test docstring all claim it does
findings.evidence: `scrape.py:588` `snapshots.append(_build_snapshot(src, result))` builds the snapshot from `result.rows` — the in-memory adapter return — and `_build_snapshot:412-426` never reads a CSV. `aggregate.py:129-130` `if not snap.rows: continue` then skips the source outright, so `has_valid_cache` and the 0.5 `availability_multiplier` (`parse.py:158-166`) are unreachable when rows are empty, which is the only state a failure produces. Claims to the contrary: `scrape.py:13-16` "the previous CSV stays on disk so the aggregate keeps the last-known-good values"; `docs/ros-engine.md` "The previous CSV is never deleted... so the aggregate continues with last-known-good values. `tests/ros/test_scrape_failure_resilience.py` pins this guarantee"; `.github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml:423` "orchestrator keeps yesterday's CSV per source". Opening the named test: it has two cases, `test_existing_csv_preserved_when_adapter_returns_no_rows` and `test_has_valid_cache_reports_correct_state`, which call `_write_csv` and `_has_valid_cache` directly. Neither invokes `run_all` or `aggregate`, and neither asserts anything about aggregate output.
findings.userImpact: If DraftSharks (1.375 effective weight, ~34% of an offense player's blend) fails one cycle, every player it uniquely ranked drops out of `rosValue` entirely rather than holding yesterday's number, and `staleFlag` stays false so nothing warns. Operators reading the doc will not investigate.
findings.recommendedFix: Either implement the claim — on a failed/empty adapter, read `data/ros/sources/<key>.csv` back into a snapshot with `status="failed", has_valid_cache=True` so the existing 0.5 availability multiplier applies — or delete the claim from the module docstring, the doc and the workflow comment. Then make the test actually run `run_all` with a crashing adapter.

findings.title: freshness_multiplier and staleFlag are structurally unreachable — the timestamp compared against "now" is always this run's own completion time
findings.evidence: `scrape.py:437` `scraped_at=result.completed_at or None`, and `:576` `result.completed_at = result.completed_at or _now()` — adapters set `completed_at` to the moment they finished. `parse.py:120-123` then computes `age_hours = (now - when)/3600`, which is always ~0, so `:124` returns 1.0 unconditionally. Confirmed against live data: every contributor weight in `data/ros/aggregate/latest.json` reproduces exactly with freshness=1.0 (fantasyProsRosSf 0.85×1.10 = 0.935 ✓, draftSharksRosSf 1.25×1.10 = 1.375 ✓, fantasyProsRosIdp 1.05×0.8925 = 0.9371 ✓, fantasyProsRosOverall 1.15×0.95 = 1.0925 ✓, ffc2qbAdp 0.70×1.10×0.85 = 0.6545 ✓). Likewise `aggregate.py:131` `is_stale_source = snap.status not in ("ok","partial") and snap.has_valid_cache` — a failed source has zero rows and is skipped at `:129`, so `is_stale_source` can never be True. Live check: 0 of 1,085 aggregate rows have `staleFlag: true` and 0 of 4,270 contributor entries have `stale: true`.
findings.userImpact: The staleness half of the source-weight model is inert. A source whose upstream CSV is two weeks old (as `footballGuysRosIdp`'s was) would carry full weight, and the `confidence` field's 0.20 freshness term is a constant 0.20 for every player — it contributes nothing to discrimination.
findings.recommendedFix: Feed `scraped_at` from the underlying data's real timestamp (the source CSV's mtime or the vendor's published date) rather than the orchestrator run time. For CSV-backed adapters that is `CSV_PATH.stat().st_mtime`. Then `is_stale_source` needs to key off freshness/`stale_after_hours`, not off `status`.

findings.title: No historical validation, calibration or backtest exists for any ROS output
findings.evidence: `tests/ros/` (15 files, 2,653 lines) contains only unit tests that re-implement the formula under test — e.g. `test_team_strength.py:83 test_composite_uses_documented_weights` computes `0.72*starting + 0.18*depth + 0.05*coverage + 0.05*health` and asserts equality with the code's output; `test_aggregate.py:126 test_two_sources_blend_correctly` asserts only that the result is in [0,100] and that the higher-weighted source's rank-1 player outranks the other. No file anywhere joins ROS values or team-strength ranks to realized weekly scoring. `pick_projection.py:52-57` states this explicitly for its own horizon ceilings: "These ceilings are a STATED ASSUMPTION, not a measurement. Backtesting them needs multi-season team-strength snapshots joined to realized final standings, and `data/ros/team_strength/` holds only the current snapshot per league — there is no history to fit against." Confirmed: `data/ros/team_strength/` contains exactly two files, overwritten every 2h. Contrast the dynasty side, which has `docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md` and `scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py`. `frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:761` concedes the gap for one flag: "Defaults off until you've validated v2 against a few weeks of standings" — validation delegated to the user, by eye.
findings.userImpact: Every constant in this subsystem — the 0.72/0.18/0.05/0.05 composite, the 0.85/1.25/1.05/1.15/0.70 base weights, the 0.45/0.35/0.20 confidence split, the 18.0 volatility threshold, ROS_BLEND 0.20, the 1.10 variance bump, the nine power-v2 weights, every tag and direction threshold — is an unvalidated prior presented as a measurement. There is no evidence any ROS number predicts anything.
findings.recommendedFix: Retain `team_strength` snapshots per run (the aggregate already archives to `history/`) so a backtest becomes possible, then rank team-strength against realized weekly points the way `scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py` does for the adjusted board. Until then, label the ROS surfaces as unvalidated rather than shipping the Trade Deadline recommendations as advice.

findings.title: stale_after_hours is declared in both registries, mirrored to JS, documented as driving availability — and read by nothing
findings.evidence: `src/ros/sources/__init__.py` declares `stale_after_hours` on all five entries (`:69, :92, :111, :136, :154`) and documents it at `:31` as "freshness threshold; older → marked stale". `frontend/lib/ros-sources.js` mirrors it. `docs/ros-engine.md` states "Each source declares `stale_after_hours` in the registry. A source older than that threshold has its `availability_multiplier` reduced from 1.0 → 0.5". A repo-wide grep for `stale_after_hours|staleAfterHours` outside tests returns only the declarations plus one pass-through copy into run metadata at `scrape.py:149`. `parse.py:158` `availability_multiplier(status, has_valid_cache)` takes no age argument and has no age logic.
findings.userImpact: An operator tuning `stale_after_hours` to make a source decay faster gets no effect, and `tests/ros/test_sources_registry_parity.py` will keep the dead field in lockstep across two languages forever.
findings.recommendedFix: Wire it (pass source age plus `stale_after_hours` into `availability_multiplier`) or delete it from both registries and the doc.

findings.title: Two independent championship-odds calculations disagree by up to 4.8 percentage points; the one the UI reads is the unseeded, non-convergent one
findings.evidence: `playoff_sim.py:759` runs its own bracket (`_simulate_bracket`, re-seeding each round, adaptive sim count) and stamps `championshipOdds` per owner. `championship.py:227` runs a different bracket (`_simulate_bracket` at `:63`, pop(0)/pop(-1) with no re-seeding, fixed `n_simulations=10000` at `:203`, unseeded `rng` at `:177`) and stamps `championshipOdds` for the same owners. Live comparison of the two committed files: Joey 0.3815 vs 0.4085 (Δ2.70pp), Jason 0.3185 vs 0.3390 (Δ2.05pp), Eric 0.2955 vs 0.2474 (Δ4.81pp). `trade_deadline.py::_load_championship_map` reads the `championship.py` file; `simulate_trade_impact` reads the `playoff_sim.py` number. Additional defects in the championship bracket: `:80` hardcodes the field size to 6 (`seeded_owners.index(s) < 6`) so the `playoff_seeds` parameter at `:167` is dead, and `:94` `bye_set` is assigned and never used.
findings.userImpact: Eric is a "Favorite" (≥0.20, `championship.py:50`) on one number and would round differently on the other. Which championship probability a surface shows depends on which file it reads, and neither is labelled.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete one. `playoff_sim.simulate_playoff_odds` already produces `championshipOdds` with a convergence check and Wilson intervals; make `championship.build_section` a projection of that payload. If both must exist, stamp a `bracketModel` field.

findings.title: team_ros_strength's "weights" are coefficients on incommensurable quantities — coverage and health are labelled 5% and contribute 0.77%
findings.evidence: `team_strength.py:33-36` sets `WEIGHT_STARTING=0.72, WEIGHT_DEPTH=0.18, WEIGHT_COVERAGE=0.05, WEIGHT_HEALTH=0.05` and `:156-161` sums them. But `starting_lineup_score` is an unbounded SUM over ~21 slots (`lineup.py:363`) while `positional_coverage_score` and `health_availability_score` are bounded 0-100 (`lineup.py:411, 516`). Computed on the live top team: 0.72×833.21 + 0.18×205.19 + 0.05×100.0 + 0.05×100.0 = 646.85 (matches the file exactly), of which starting = 92.74%, depth = 5.71%, coverage = 0.77%, health = 0.77%. Across all 12 teams `positionalCoverageScore` ranges only 90.87–100.0 and `healthAvailabilityScore` is 100.0 for 11 of 12. `frontend/app/league/sections/ros-team-strength.jsx:181-183` prints the coefficients to the user as "72% starting lineup + 18% best-ball depth + 5% positional coverage + 5% health". `tests/ros/test_team_strength.py:83` re-implements the same expression and asserts equality — it validates the arithmetic, not that the weights mean what they say.
findings.userImpact: A reader is told health and coverage are 10% of the number. They are 1.5%. Any attempt to tune the composite by moving those coefficients will appear to do nothing. Health is also double-counted — injured players are already multiplied by 0.4 inside starting_lineup_score.
findings.recommendedFix: Put all four terms on a common scale before weighting — e.g. normalize `starting_lineup_score` and `bench_depth_score` to a 0-100 league percentile — or relabel the constants as raw coefficients and stop presenting them as percentage shares in the UI copy.

findings.title: The "rest-of-season" board is 23-41% multi-year dynasty rankings, and nothing in the output discloses the horizon mix
findings.evidence: Two of five sources are registered `source_type: "dynasty_proxy", is_ros: False`: `fantasyProsRosSf` points at `dynasty-superflex.php` (`src/ros/sources/__init__.py:56-72`) and `fantasyProsRosIdp` reads `CSVs/site_raw/fantasyProsIdp.csv`, the dynasty IDP board (`src/ros/sources/fantasypros_ros_idp.py:24`). A third, `ffc2qbAdp`, is redraft ADP (`is_ros: False`). Computed shares of effective weight on the live blend: for a 4-source offense player, dynasty proxy 0.935/4.057 = 23.0%, ADP 16.1%, true ROS 60.9%. For an IDP player there are only two contributors and the dynasty proxy is 0.9371/2.312 = 40.5%. The output field is named `rosValue`, the endpoint is `/api/ros/player-values`, and `frontend/app/league/sections/ros-team-strength.jsx:181` says only "Composite team strength for the rest of the season."
findings.userImpact: A user acting on "who is strongest right now" is partly acting on multi-year dynasty rankings, most heavily for IDP where 40% of every value is a dynasty board. The registry knows (`is_ros: False`) and the information never reaches the surface.
findings.recommendedFix: Emit a per-player `rosWeightShareByHorizon` (true-ROS vs dynasty-proxy vs ADP) in `aggregate.py` alongside `contributors`, and surface it. The `contributors` array already carries the per-source weights needed to compute it.
findings.affectedSystems: src/ros/aggregate.py, src/ros/sources/__init__.py, src/ros/api.py, frontend ROS surfaces

findings.title: Distinct NFL players collide onto one canonical name; the second is silently dropped from the blend
findings.evidence: `data/ros/sources/draftSharksRosSf.csv` contains `byron murphy` twice (Vikings CB Byron Murphy Jr. and Seahawks DT Byron Murphy II are different players); `data/ros/sources/fantasyProsRosIdp.csv` contains `byron young` twice (Rams DE and Raiders DT). `aggregate.py:187-194` keeps the first scoring row and logs a warning that the source "emitted %r more than once", framing a real identity collision as a vendor duplicate. `mapping.py:104` returns the normalized string with no positional or team disambiguation, and `resolve_player` is only invoked at `scrape.py:552` when `canonicalName` is empty — which is always, since all five adapters emit `"canonicalName": ""`. `_build_default_canonical_universe` (`scrape.py:479-510`) builds the universe from Sleeper full names alone, so both Byrons collapse to one universe entry too.
findings.userImpact: One of each pair gets the other's ROS value in `team_strength`'s join (`team_strength.py:98-102` uses `setdefault`, first wins), and the other is reported as unmapped and scored 0.0 toward its owner's composite. In an IDP league both pairs are startable defenders.
findings.recommendedFix: Key the resolver and the aggregate on (canonical_name, position_family) or on a Sleeper player_id via the identity layer. `RankedRow` already carries `position`; the collision is detectable at `aggregate.py:187`.

findings.title: The "Seller cash-out" tag compares a 0-9999 dynasty value against a 0-100 ROS value and can never fire in production
findings.evidence: `src/ros/tags.py:76` `if veteran and is_strong and dynasty_value is not None and dynasty_value < ros_value * 0.7`. `is_strong` requires `ros_value >= 60.0` (`:63`), so the threshold is at most 70. The live callers pass a dynasty value on the canonical 0-9999 scale: `frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:142` `const dynastyValue = row.values?.full ?? row.rankDerivedValue ?? null` and `frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:127` the same. `frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1166` `full: backendValue || rawValues.full` where `backendValue` is `rankDerivedValue`. A player with `rankDerivedValue < 70` on a 0-9999 board cannot simultaneously be a strong-ROS veteran. The pinning test `tests/ros/test_direction_and_tags.py:142-150` passes `ros_value=70, dynasty_value=40` — a combination the production call sites cannot produce — so it passes while the live tag is dead.
findings.userImpact: One of nine advertised tags never renders. `tag_descriptions()` (`tags.py:96`) still documents it and `frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:39` still assigns it a colour, so the feature reads as shipped.
findings.recommendedFix: Normalize the dynasty value to the ROS 0-100 scale (percentile against the board) before comparing, or express the rule as a percentile gap. Then change the test to use the scale the frontend actually passes.

findings.title: The rosEnabled "master switch" gates nothing
findings.evidence: `frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:752-755` renders the toggle with hint "Master switch. Off hides every ROS-driven surface (Power v2, Championship tab, Trade-deadline dashboard, ROS Fit panel, player tags)." A repo-wide grep for `rosEnabled` returns exactly three hits: the default `rosEnabled: true` in `frontend/components/useSettings.js:136`, the toggle itself, and a comment at `frontend/app/league/LeagueClient.jsx:99`. No conditional anywhere reads it. The surfaces it claims to control are gated by different flags that do work: `settings.useRosPowerRankings` (`LeagueClient.jsx:102`), `settings.showRosTradePanel` (`RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:90, 112`), `settings.showRosTags` (`PlayerPopup.jsx:120`). The Championship and Trade Deadline tabs (`frontend/app/league/tabs.js:25-26`) are gated by nothing at all.
findings.userImpact: A user who turns off the ROS engine to stop seeing the degenerate 100%/0% odds and the wrong Seller labels sees no change.
findings.recommendedFix: Either make `rosEnabled` the outer gate on the four surfaces the hint names (including hiding the two /league tabs), or remove the toggle and the hint.

findings.title: The tag classifier exists in three hand-maintained copies with no parity test, and the backend copy is dead
findings.evidence: `src/ros/tags.py:70-96`, `frontend/components/RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:61-83`, and `frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:95-116` each implement the same nine rules. `RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:58-60` says "mirrors src/ros/tags.py::tags_for_player... Stays in sync via the parity test (PR-future)" — the parity test does not exist; the only relevant file is `tests/ros/test_direction_and_tags.py`, which tests the Python copy alone and never parses the JS. `tags_for_player` has zero non-test callers (grep), so the shipped behaviour is whichever JS copy renders. Already divergent: `tags.py:47` accepts a `confidence` argument neither JS copy has.
findings.userImpact: The backend definition of the tags is dead code and the two live definitions can drift independently. A tag rule fixed in one popup will silently not apply on /trade.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one definition. Either serve tags from the backend on `/api/ros/player-values` and delete both JS copies, or delete `src/ros/tags.py` and hoist one shared JS module. If three copies must persist, add the parity test the comment promises (the repo already has this pattern in `tests/ros/test_sources_registry_parity.py`).

findings.title: Sim cache TTL and health-page age are computed from file mtime, so a deploy or checkout resets them and reports stale sims as fresh
findings.evidence: `playoff_sim.py:843` `age = os.path.getmtime(path)` then `:848` `if (time.time() - age) > _SIM_CACHE_TTL_SEC: return None`; `championship.py:283` identical; `api.py:250` `return time.time() - os.path.getmtime(path)` feeding `sims.playoffAgeSeconds` / `championshipAgeSeconds`. The payloads carry a real `computedAt` field (`scrape.py:369, 373`) which none of these read. Observable in this working tree: `data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json` has `computedAt: 2026-08-04T03:57:31` but an mtime of `Aug 4 06:56` — three hours apart, from the checkout. Since these files are git-tracked, any `git pull` on the production VPS rewrites the mtime and makes an arbitrarily old sim look freshly computed. `api.py:254-261 _iso_to_age_seconds` reads the ISO timestamp correctly and is used for the aggregate — the right helper exists two functions away.
findings.userImpact: /tools/ros-data-health colours the sim tiles green (`ageColor` threshold 6h) on age data that a deploy resets, and `build_section` serves a cached sim past its intended TTL without re-running.
findings.recommendedFix: Use `_iso_to_age_seconds(payload["computedAt"])` in all four places.

findings.title: simulate_trade_impact runs the full best-ball presim three times per call; simulate_playoff_odds recomputes distributions it was handed
findings.evidence: `playoff_sim.py:688-691`: when `distributions` is passed in, the function still calls `_build_team_distributions(...)` in full, discarding the distributions and keeping only `pf_by_owner`. `_build_team_distributions:491-496` runs `_bestball_presim`, which per `:411` draws up to `BEST_BALL_PRESIM_MAX_WEEKS = 1200` weeks per team, each solving a full `solve_optimal_assignment` over a 44-58 player roster (`lineup.py:224`). `simulate_trade_impact:968` calls it once, then `:993` and `:1003` call `simulate_playoff_odds` with explicit distributions — each of which triggers `:689` again. Three full presims per trade evaluation, two thrown away.
findings.userImpact: Trade-impact odds are computed on a request path. On the 12-team best-ball league this is 3 × 12 × up to 1200 exact assignment solves before the Monte Carlo starts.
findings.recommendedFix: Extract `pf_by_owner` from a cheap helper (it is `sum(scores)` per owner from `playoff_odds._season_weekly_scores`) and skip `_build_team_distributions` entirely when `distributions` is supplied.

findings.title: data/ros is force-committed to git with no retention: 792 aggregate snapshots and 4,633 run files, 872 MB, against a documented "rolling 30-day archive"
findings.evidence: `src/ros/__init__.py:26` and `docs/ros-engine.md` both call `data/ros/aggregate/history/` a "rolling 30-day archive". `scrape.py:615-616` writes a new archive every run and there is no prune anywhere (grep for prune/cleanup/unlink under `src/ros/` and `scripts/` returns nothing). `.gitignore:59-68` ignores these paths, but `.github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml:521` `git add -f -- "$p"` over a list including `data/ros/` force-adds them. Measured: `git ls-files data/ros/ | wc -l` = 5,439; `ls data/ros/aggregate/history | wc -l` = 792 spanning 2026-04-28 to 2026-08-04 (98 days, not 30); `du -sh` = 853M history + 19M runs. `docs/ros-engine.md` states "Everything except `mapping_overrides.json` is gitignored" — contradicted by the workflow it ships alongside. Nothing reads `aggregate/history/` (grep finds no consumer).
findings.userImpact: Every clone and every CI checkout pulls ~872 MB of ROS scratch data plus its full commit history.
findings.recommendedFix: Prune `aggregate/history/` and `runs/` to the documented 30 days inside `run_all`, and remove `data/ros/` from the workflow's force-add list (the endpoints read local disk on prod). Fix the doc either way.

findings.title: PickProjectorPanel is rendered without a leagueKey, so a non-default league's draft board shows the default league's projected order
findings.evidence: `frontend/app/league/sections/_pick-projector.jsx:47` `export default function PickProjectorPanel({ leagueKey })` and `:54-56` builds the query string only when `leagueKey` is truthy. The one call site, `frontend/app/league/sections/draft-capital.jsx:124`, is `<PickProjectorPanel />` with no props; grep for `leagueKey|activeLeague` in that file returns nothing. `src/ros/api.py:190-193` then falls back to `default_league_key()`. The component's own docstring at `:16` states "League-scoped: pick ownership and team strength both follow leagueKey per CLAUDE.md".
findings.userImpact: Under a non-default league the panel shows another league's reverse-standings order and another league's pick ownership beside the correct pick-value grid, with no indication of the mismatch.
findings.recommendedFix: Thread the active league key from the draft-capital section into the panel, or have the backend echo `leagueKey` and the panel refuse to render when it does not match the page's league.

findings.title: The aggregate's league context is hardcoded, so a non-IDP league is served a payload asserting idp_enabled: true
findings.evidence: `scrape.py:592-597` `league_ctx = league or {"is_superflex": True, "is_2qb": False, "is_te_premium": True, "idp_enabled": True}` and `run_all` is called with `league=None` from every entry point (`api.py:348`, `scrape.py:660`, the CI step). That block is written verbatim into `data/ros/aggregate/latest.json` (`:604-606`) and served unchanged by `api.py:132`. `config/leagues/registry.json` records `"idpEnabled": false` for `dynasty_new`, which reads the same global aggregate. Nothing in the registry is consulted.
findings.userImpact: `/api/ros/player-values` is a single global payload labelled with one league's format. For dynasty_new the `league` block is false, and the aggregate contains 438 IDP rows that league does not use.
findings.recommendedFix: Resolve the league context from `league_registry` rather than hardcoding, and either scope the aggregate by scoring profile (per CLAUDE.md) or drop the `league` block.

findings.title: The IDP format bonus is decided once per source from the first row's position, not per player
findings.evidence: `aggregate.py:136` `sample_position = next((r.position for r in snap.rows if r.position), None)` then `:137-153` computes ONE weight for the whole source and applies it to every row at `:203`. `parse.py:76-79` decides the 1.05 IDP bonus from that single sampled position. `draftSharksRosSf` carries 424 IDP rows (per its fetcher's docstring) but its first row is Josh Allen (QB), so none of its IDP rows get the bonus; `fantasyProsRosIdp`'s first row is a DE, so all 219 rows get it. The code comment at `:132-135` acknowledges the shortcut; `docs/ros-engine.md` presents the multiplier as "1.05 IDP source used for IDP player".
findings.userImpact: The one format adjustment that could partially offset the IDP normalization problem is applied to the wrong rows.
findings.recommendedFix: Move the `effective_source_weight` call inside the row loop, or memoize per (source, position_family). Cost is negligible at ~2,300 rows.

findings.title: The 1.15 SF+TEP format-match branch is unreachable — no registered source declares is_te_premium
findings.evidence: `parse.py:85` `tep_match = bool(src.get("is_te_premium")) and bool(league.get("is_te_premium"))`, `:87-88` `if sf_match and tep_match: return base * 1.15`. All five entries in `src/ros/sources/__init__.py` set `"is_te_premium": False` (`:64, :87, :106, :131, :149`), mirrored in `frontend/lib/ros-sources.js`. `scrape.py:596` hardcodes `"is_te_premium": True` on the league side, so the league flag is always on and the source flag always off. Verified: every live weight reproduces with the 1.10 branch. `tests/ros/test_aggregate.py:106 test_sf_plus_tep_match` constructs a synthetic source with the flag set, so it passes without any live source qualifying.
findings.userImpact: In a TE-premium league (both registry leagues are `superflex_tep15_ppr1`), no ROS source receives the TEP bonus, and TE rows are ranked on non-TEP boards with no basis conversion — unlike the dynasty pipeline, which does convert (ADR-015).
findings.recommendedFix: Either mark the sources that publish TEP boards, or delete the branch and document that ROS values carry no TE-premium adjustment.

findings.title: Playoff field size and byes are hardcoded to 6/2 for every league
findings.evidence: `playoff_sim.py:650-651` `playoff_seeds: int = 6, bye_seeds: int = 2`; `scrape.py:368` and `:372` call the sims with no overrides for either league. `championship.py:80` hardcodes 6 a second time inside `_simulate_bracket`, making the `playoff_seeds` parameter at `:167` dead. `config/leagues/registry.json` records `teamCount: 12` for dynasty_main and `teamCount: 10` for dynasty_new but no playoff structure, and nothing reads Sleeper's league settings for it.
findings.userImpact: A 10-team league with a 4-team playoff would have its odds computed for a 6-team field. Today the sims only see 8 owners so the error is masked by a larger one.
findings.recommendedFix: Read playoff_teams / bye structure from the Sleeper league settings (already fetched by the public snapshot) and thread through both sims; remove the hardcoded 6 in `championship._simulate_bracket`.

findings.title: _PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION is dead code and its docstring states a rosValue→points divisor of 17 against the live value of 2.7
findings.evidence: `playoff_sim.py:113-127` defines `_PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION` and `_DEFAULT_PLAYER_CV`; grep shows no reference to either name anywhere in `src/ros/`. The live path is `PointsModel.draw` (`src/league_intel/sim_calibration.py:167-172`). The dead table's comment at `:111-112` says "mean = rosValue/17 × game-mean scale"; the live constant is `FALLBACK_ROS_VALUE_PER_POINT = 2.7` (`sim_calibration.py:87`). Both cached sims stamp `pointsModelSource: "fallback-constants"`, confirming `data/league_intel/sim_points_model.json` does not exist (the whole directory is absent). Consequence: the live #1 team's 21-slot lineup (833.21) implies 308.6 fantasy points per week.
findings.userImpact: A reader tracing the sim's scale lands on the wrong constant. The 2.7 divisor is uncalibrated in this deployment, and 308 points/week for a 21-starter lineup is well above realistic, though it largely cancels in head-to-head comparison.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the dead table and its comment. Generate `data/league_intel/sim_points_model.json` so `pointsModelSource` stops reading "fallback-constants", or document that the fallback scale is uncalibrated for this league.

findings.title: draftSharksRosSf normalizes against a denominator larger than the population that survives into the blend
findings.evidence: `src/ros/sources/draftsharks_ros.py:90-93` sets `total_ranked = len(rows)` = 978 from the raw CSV. `scrape.py:562` then drops rows whose canonical name did not resolve and `:563` recomputes `player_count`, but never revisits `total_ranked`. Live: `data/ros/sources/draftSharksRosSf.csv` has 939 rows, every one stamped `total_ranked: 978`. Same pattern on `ffc2qbAdp` (199 rows, `total_ranked: 214`) and `fantasyProsRosSf` (538 rows, 540). `player_count` (used by `completeness_multiplier`) is corrected; `total_ranked` (used by `rank_to_score`) is not.
findings.userImpact: Small systematic distortion of the score curve — the denominator claims a deeper board than the one being blended. Magnitude is modest on a log curve, but it is a silent inconsistency between two counts describing the same population.
findings.recommendedFix: Recompute `total_ranked` after quarantine in `scrape.py:562-563`, or make the denominator an explicit, documented "published board depth".

findings.title: Orphaned footballGuysRosIdp artifacts: a 438-row source CSV and four run files for a source that is not in the registry
findings.evidence: `data/ros/sources/footballGuysRosIdp.csv` (438 rows) and four `data/ros/runs/footballGuysRosIdp__*.json` are tracked in git, newest `2026-07-21T21:48:54` — 14 days before HEAD. `git log -S"footballGuysRosIdp" -- src/ros/sources/__init__.py` returns nothing, so the source never existed in the committed registry; the run JSON records `"source_name": "Footballguys IDP (ROS proxy)", "is_projection_source": true`, so it was live at some point. It contributes nothing today (`data/ros/runs/index.json` has five sources; the aggregate has five). `frontend/app/tools/ros-data-health/page.jsx:239` still tells the operator about "all six adapters".
findings.userImpact: An operator inspecting `data/ros/sources/` sees six CSVs and may conclude six sources feed the blend. Five do.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the orphaned CSV and run files; fix the health-page copy to not name a count.

findings.title: docs/ros-engine.md contradicts the code on four separate points
findings.evidence: (1) The flow diagram ends with "NEVER touches: CSVs/site_raw/*" and the isolation section repeats "ROS adapters write only to data/ros/* — never CSVs/site_raw/*". Two of five adapters READ from it and it is the load-bearing input: `src/ros/sources/draftsharks_ros.py:39-47` and `src/ros/sources/fantasypros_ros_idp.py:24`. (2) "Source list (PR 1)" names two sources; `src/ros/sources/__init__.py` has five live, and the PR2-5 roadmap still lists FFC 2QB ADP and FantasyPros IDP as future work when both ship. (3) "Storage layout: sims/playoff_<iso>.json" — the real paths are `sims/latest_playoff.json` / `latest_championship.json` (`scrape.py:246-254`); `src/ros/__init__.py:27` repeats the wrong name. (4) "`r=1` → ~99" — `rank_to_score(1, N) = 100.0` exactly for all N, since `ln(1) = 0` (`parse.py:46`).
findings.userImpact: The only prose description of the engine misstates its inputs, its source list, its file layout and its value range.
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite the four sections against the code. The "never touches CSVs/site_raw" claim is the important one — it hides that the highest-weighted ROS source is a file another pipeline writes.

findings.title: direction.py's documented band table does not match its fallthrough order
findings.evidence: `direction.py:62-74` documents "Hold: 0.35 <= playoff < 0.55 with low championship odds" and "Selective Seller: 0.20 <= playoff < 0.40". The code checks Strong Buyer, Buyer, Selective Buyer (`:92`, 0.45–0.60), Strong Seller (`:98`), Seller (`:104`, `playoff < 0.25 and champ < 0.02`), Selective Seller (`:107`, 0.20–0.40), else Hold. Because Seller is evaluated first, a team at playoff=0.22 / champ=0.01 gets "Seller", never "Selective Seller". A team at playoff=0.50 gets "Selective Buyer", not the documented "Hold". `tests/ros/test_direction_and_tags.py:99 test_hold_default_band` pins one point, not the boundaries.
findings.userImpact: Anyone tuning the thresholds from the docstring will produce different labels than expected.
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite the docstring to describe the actual fallthrough, and add boundary tests at 0.20/0.25/0.40/0.45/0.55/0.60.

findings.title: Bye-week handling is advertised but hardcoded off
findings.evidence: `src/ros/scrape.py:224` sets `"bye": False` for every hydrated roster player, unconditionally. `lineup.py:219-220` `elif player.bye: base *= 0.0` therefore never executes, and `lineup.py:373` `"flagged": "injured" if pick.injured else ("bye" if pick.bye else None)` can never emit "bye". Meanwhile `src/ros/tags.py:88-92` ships an "Injury/bye cover" tag with the description "Short-term coverage only" and `RosTradeFitPanel.jsx:45` colours it. No bye-week data source is fetched anywhere in `src/ros/`.
findings.userImpact: The health component and the lineup optimizer are injury-only. In a best-ball league byes are exactly what depth covers, and the depth score claims to model that.
findings.recommendedFix: Populate `bye` from the NFL schedule (Sleeper's player dump does not carry it; the team bye week is available from the schedule endpoint), or remove the bye branch and rename the tag.

formulas.name: rank_to_score — the single rank→value conversion
formulas.expression:
score = 100 * (ln(N+1) - ln(r)) / ln(N+1)   for 0 < r <= N; else 0.0
where r = source rank (1-indexed), N = that source's `total_ranked`
formulas.inputs: r: `RankedRow.rank`, unitless ordinal, from each adapter. N: `RankedRow.total_ranked`, unitless count, stamped per adapter — `len(rows)` for draftsharks/fantasypros_idp, `len(players)` for fantasypros_sf/overall, `len(sorted_players)` for ffc.
formulas.constants: 100.0 (output ceiling) and the +1 offset inside both logs. Hand-picked, no calibration in repo. Worked examples I computed: r=1,N=540 → 100.0000; r=1,N=978 → 100.0000; r=21,N=417 → 49.5563 (matches Josh Allen's fantasyProsRosOverall contributor score of 49.56 in data/ros/aggregate/latest.json); r=98,N=978 → 33.4212 (matches Hutchinson's draftSharks score 33.42); r=219,N=219 → 0.0845; r=978,N=978 → 0.0148; r=100,N=100 → 0.2156.
formulas.mathIssues: (a) N is per-source, so the same rank on boards of different depth yields different scores and boards of different depth are blended as if commensurable — Hutchinson scores 100.00 on a 219-row IDP board and 33.42 on a 978-row board, a 2.99x gap from board size alone. (b) r=1 returns exactly 100.0, not the ~99 docs/ros-engine.md claims. (c) r > N silently returns 0.0, which aggregate.py:182 treats as "skip this row" — this drops 13 real IDP players today. (d) N is not corrected after name-quarantine, so draftSharks blends 939 rows against N=978.
formulas.outputRange: [0, 100). Never reaches 100 except at r=1 where it is exactly 100.0.
formulas.validated: none found — no backtest, no calibration artifact, no fit script.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Non-numeric rank or total → 0.0 (parse.py:39-40, caught TypeError/ValueError). r<=0, N<=0, or r>N → 0.0. All of these are indistinguishable downstream from "ranked last", and aggregate.py:182-183 drops them all without logging.

formulas.name: format_match_multiplier
formulas.expression:
base = 1.05 if (src.is_idp AND player_position in {DL,DE,DT,EDGE,LB,DB,S,CB}) else 1.0
sf_match = (src.is_superflex or src.is_2qb) AND (league.is_superflex or league.is_2qb)
tep_match = src.is_te_premium AND league.is_te_premium
return base*1.15 if (sf_match and tep_match)
     else base*1.10 if sf_match
     else base*0.85 if (not src.is_ros and src.is_dynasty)
     else base*0.95
formulas.inputs: Boolean flags from `ROS_SOURCES` registry entries and from the hardcoded league dict in scrape.py:592-597. `position` comes from aggregate.py:136 — the FIRST non-empty row position in the whole source, not the row being scored.
formulas.constants: 1.15, 1.10, 1.05, 0.95, 0.85 — all "per spec", no calibration in repo. Live values: fantasyProsRosSf 1.10, draftSharksRosSf 1.10, fantasyProsRosIdp 1.05×0.85=0.8925, fantasyProsRosOverall 0.95, ffc2qbAdp 1.10.
formulas.mathIssues: The 1.15 branch is unreachable: all five registry entries set is_te_premium=False. The 1.05 IDP bonus is decided once per source from a single sampled row, so draftSharks' 424 IDP rows get no bonus while all 219 fantasyProsRosIdp rows do regardless of position.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing/absent flags coerce to False via `src.get(...)`; a source with no flags falls to the 0.95 default. No error, no warning.

formulas.name: freshness_multiplier
formulas.expression:
age_h = (now - scraped_at) / 3600
return 1.00 if age_h < 24; 0.90 if < 48; 0.75 if < 96; 0.50 if < 168; else 0.25
formulas.inputs: `scraped_at` = `SourceSnapshot.scraped_at` = `result.completed_at` (scrape.py:437), which scrape.py:576 sets to now() for every run.
formulas.constants: 24/48/96/168 hour boundaries and 1.00/0.90/0.75/0.50/0.25 factors, all "per spec", uncalibrated.
formulas.mathIssues: Structurally always returns 1.0 in the live path, because the timestamp compared against `now` is this run's own completion time. Verified: every contributor weight in data/ros/aggregate/latest.json reproduces exactly with freshness=1.0.
formulas.validated: none found. tests/ros/test_aggregate.py:86-101 pins the function's own arithmetic with injected timestamps, never the live wiring.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: None or unparseable ISO → 0.0 (parse.py:112-117), which zeroes the entire source weight and drops it at aggregate.py:154. That is the opposite direction from every other missing-data path in this module, which degrade toward inclusion.

formulas.name: completeness_multiplier
formulas.expression: return 0.0 if n<=0; 1.00 if n>=200; 0.85 if n>=100; else 0.70   (expected_min=200)
formulas.inputs: `player_count` = post-quarantine row count from scrape.py:563.
formulas.constants: expected_min=200 default; 1.00/0.85/0.70. Uncalibrated. Live: ffc2qbAdp at 199 rows lands on 0.85 — one row short of 1.00, a cliff at exactly 200 with no smoothing.
formulas.mathIssues: Hard step function. ffc2qbAdp's weight swings 15% on a single row of vendor coverage. `expected_min // 2` integer-divides, which is fine at 200 but silently changes the middle band for odd values.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Non-int → 0.0 (kills the source). n=0 → 0.0.

formulas.name: availability_multiplier
formulas.expression: status=="ok" → 1.0; status=="partial" → 0.5; has_valid_cache → 0.5; else 0.0
formulas.inputs: `ScrapeResult.status` and `_has_valid_cache(key)` (scrape.py:88-97, ≥2 lines in the CSV).
formulas.mathIssues: The 0.5 stale-cache branch is unreachable in the live path: a failed adapter returns zero rows, and aggregate.py:129-130 skips zero-row snapshots before any weight is used. So the documented "stale source keeps half weight" behaviour never executes.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty/None status with no cache → 0.0.

formulas.name: effective_source_weight
formulas.expression: w = base_weight * format_match * freshness * completeness * availability
formulas.inputs: registry `base_weight` (or the /settings per-source override applied at sources/__init__.py:186-190) times the four multipliers above.
formulas.constants: base weights: fantasyProsRosSf 0.85, draftSharksRosSf 1.25, fantasyProsRosIdp 1.05, fantasyProsRosOverall 1.15, ffc2qbAdp 0.70 — all "per the user spec", hand-picked, no fit. I reproduced every live weight exactly: 0.85×1.10×1×1×1=0.9350 ✓; 1.25×1.10×1×1×1=1.3750 ✓; 1.05×0.8925×1×1×1=0.9371 ✓; 1.15×0.95×1×1×1=1.0925 ✓; 0.70×1.10×1×0.85×1=0.6545 ✓ (all match data/ros/aggregate/latest.json).
formulas.mathIssues: Two of the four multipliers (freshness, availability) are constants in practice, so the model reduces to base_weight × format × completeness. Effective weight shares on a 4-source offense player: draftSharks 33.9%, fantasyProsRosOverall 26.9%, fantasyProsRosSf 23.0%, ffc2qbAdp 16.1%. On a 2-source IDP player: draftSharks 59.5%, fantasyProsRosIdp (a DYNASTY board) 40.5%.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: base_weight <= 0 → 0.0 short-circuit (parse.py:183-184). Any multiplier at 0 zeroes the source, which aggregate.py:154-155 then skips silently.

formulas.name: rosValue — the aggregated player value
formulas.expression:
row_weight_i = source_weight_i * (row.confidence_i or 1.0)
rosValue = Σ_i (rank_to_score(r_i, N_i) * row_weight_i) / Σ_i row_weight_i
formulas.inputs: Per-source rank scores (0-100, unitless) and effective weights. `row.confidence` comes from the name resolver at scrape.py:559 (`existing * resolved.confidence`, 1.0/0.9/0.7).
formulas.constants: None beyond the weights. Worked example — Josh Allen from data/ros/aggregate/latest.json: scores [100.00 (fpSf r1/540), 100.00 (dsRosSf r1/978), 49.5563 (fpOverall r21/417), 100.00 (ffc r1/214)] with weights [0.935, 1.375, 1.0925, 0.6545] → (100×0.935 + 100×1.375 + 49.5563×1.0925 + 100×0.6545)/4.057 = 86.42, exactly matching the file. Second example — Aidan Hutchinson: (33.4212×1.375 + 100.00×0.9371)/2.3121 = 60.41, matching.
formulas.mathIssues: A plain weighted mean with no outlier handling, no trimming, no Hampel filter and no single-source haircut — unlike the dynasty pipeline, which has all four. A 2.99x cross-source disagreement (Hutchinson) is averaged as though the two sources measured the same thing. No per-source rescaling, so board depth leaks directly into the value.
formulas.outputRange: [0, 100]. Live: 1,085 players, max 86.42 (Josh Allen); no player reaches 100 because none is rank 1 on every board.
formulas.validated: none found. tests/ros/test_projection_value_is_not_consumed.py pins that rosValue equals `rank_to_score` exactly for a single source — the strongest statement in the suite, and a tautology check.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A player ranked by only one source gets that source's raw rank score with no discount (weight_sum = one weight, passthrough). A row scoring 0 is dropped entirely (`:182-183`). `weight_sum <= 0` → the player is omitted from the output with no record (`:228-229`).

formulas.name: confidence
formulas.expression:
source_count_factor = min(1.0, distinct_sources / 4.0)
agreement_factor    = max(0.0, 1.0 - pstdev(raw_scores) / 30.0)
freshness_factor    = 1.0 - stale_contributors / total_contributors
confidence = round(0.45*source_count_factor + 0.35*agreement_factor + 0.20*freshness_factor, 3)
formulas.inputs: distinct sourceKeys in `contributors`; population stddev of the per-source rank scores; the stale-contributor share.
formulas.constants: 0.45/0.35/0.20 split, saturation at 4 sources, SD reference 30.0 — all uncalibrated. Worked example: Hutchinson, 2 sources, scores [33.4212, 100.00], pstdev = 33.289 → 0.45×0.5 + 0.35×max(0, 1−33.289/30) + 0.20×1 = 0.225 + 0.0 + 0.20 = 0.425 (file says 0.425).
formulas.mathIssues: The freshness term is a constant 0.20 for every player (no contributor can ever be stale), so the metric is effectively 0.45·count + 0.35·agreement + 0.20. The agreement term floors at zero for stddev ≥ 30, which is exactly the population-normalization artifact rather than genuine disagreement — it penalises the symptom without identifying the cause.
formulas.validated: none found. tests/ros/test_aggregate.py:178 only asserts confidence grows with source count.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `total_count == 0` → freshness_factor 0.0. A single-source player gets source_count_factor 0.25 and agreement_factor 1.0 (stddev of one sample is 0 by `:231`), so a lone source yields confidence 0.4625 — HIGHER than Hutchinson's two genuinely-disagreeing sources at 0.425. A single unopposed opinion scores as more confident than two that conflict.

formulas.name: tier (quintile)
formulas.expression: bucket = max(1, total // 5); tier = min(5, ((rank_1based - 1) // bucket) + 1)
formulas.inputs: 1-based overall rank and total aggregated player count.
formulas.constants: DEFAULT_TIER_QUINTILES = 5.
formulas.mathIssues: Integer division means the last tier absorbs the remainder: with total=1085, bucket=217, tiers 1-4 hold 217 each; at total=1084 tier 5 would hold 221. Tiers are pure rank quintiles with no value-gap detection, so a 50-point value cliff and a 0.1-point difference are treated identically.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: total <= 0 → returns 5 (worst tier), i.e. an empty board would tier every player as worst rather than as unknown.

formulas.name: volatilityFlag
formulas.expression: volatilityFlag = pstdev(raw_scores) > 18.0
formulas.inputs: population stddev of the per-source 0-100 rank scores.
formulas.constants: VOLATILITY_THRESHOLD = 18.0, hand-picked.
formulas.mathIssues: On a board where cross-population normalization routinely produces 30+ point spreads for the same player, this flag fires on the normalization artifact rather than on real market disagreement. Josh Allen carries volatilityFlag: true (stddev 21.843) purely because fantasyProsRosOverall ranks him 21st on a 1QB-shaped board while three superflex sources have him 1st.
formulas.validated: none found. Consumed by tags.py:81 ("Best-ball boost") and both JS copies.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Single contributor → stddev 0.0 (`:231`) → flag false. A player with one source is never flagged volatile.

formulas.name: staleFlag
formulas.expression:
is_stale_source = (snap.status not in {"ok","partial"}) AND snap.has_valid_cache
staleFlag = (stale_count == total_count) AND total_count > 0
formulas.inputs: adapter status and cache presence.
formulas.constants: none
formulas.mathIssues: Unreachable. A source whose status is neither ok nor partial has zero rows, and aggregate.py:129-130 continues before the accumulator is touched. Verified on live data: 0 of 1,085 rows have staleFlag true, 0 of 4,270 contributor entries have stale true.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a — the branch never executes.

formulas.name: team_ros_strength composite
formulas.expression: composite = 0.72*starting_lineup_score + 0.18*bench_depth_score + 0.05*positional_coverage_score + 0.05*health_availability_score
formulas.inputs: starting_lineup_score = unbounded SUM of health-adjusted rosValues over the optimal lineup (lineup.py:363); bench_depth_score = unbounded decayed sum over ≤8 bench players (lineup.py:391); coverage and health are both bounded 0-100.
formulas.constants: 0.72 / 0.18 / 0.05 / 0.05, "spec-defined defaults", hardcoded, uncalibrated. Worked example on the live #1 team: 0.72×833.21 + 0.18×205.19 + 0.05×100.0 + 0.05×100.0 = 646.85, matching data/ros/team_strength/latest.json exactly.
formulas.mathIssues: The four terms are on incommensurable scales, so the coefficients are not weights. Actual contribution shares on that team: starting 92.74%, depth 5.71%, coverage 0.77%, health 0.77%. Across the 12 live teams coverage spans 90.87-100.0 and health is 100.0 for 11 of 12, so the two 'five percent' terms jointly discriminate under half a point out of a ~300-point range. Health is also double-counted: injured players are already multiplied by 0.4 inside starting_lineup_score (lineup.py:218), then counted again in the 0.05 health term.
formulas.outputRange: unbounded, scales with starter count. Live: 348.98-646.85 across 12 teams (dynasty_main, 21 starter slots) and 247.02-463.61 across 10 teams (dynasty_new, 10 starter slots) — the two leagues' composites are not comparable and nothing says so.
formulas.validated: none found. tests/ros/test_team_strength.py:83 re-implements the expression and asserts equality.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A roster player with no aggregate row, or with rosValue <= 0, is appended with ros_value=0.0 and confidence=0.0 and listed in `unmappedPlayers` (team_strength.py:123-141). Zero is a real contribution to the sum, so unmapped players actively drag the composite rather than being excluded — measured 0-6 unmapped per team on the live snapshot, including Bobby Wagner (who IS ranked, but was dropped by the total_ranked bug).

formulas.name: _value_with_health_penalty
formulas.expression: base = max(0, ros_value); if injured: base *= 0.4; elif bye: base *= 0.0
formulas.inputs: RosterPlayer.ros_value, .injured, .bye
formulas.constants: 0.4 injured multiplier, 0.0 bye multiplier. Hand-picked, uncalibrated.
formulas.mathIssues: `injured` is set from Sleeper `injury_status in {OUT, IR, PUP, DOUBTFUL}` (scrape.py:223) — a binary 0.4 haircut applied identically to a DOUBTFUL player and a season-ending IR player. `bye` is hardcoded to False at scrape.py:224, so the 0.0 branch never fires and no bye-week logic exists anywhere in the ROS engine despite the tag "Injury/bye cover" advertising it.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: None/absent ros_value → 0.0 via `float(player.ros_value or 0.0)`.

formulas.name: bench depth score (best-ball spike credit)
formulas.expression:
for each of the first 8 non-started players in descending value:
  seen = count of prior bench players at the SAME position
  depth_factor = decay[position] ** seen
  contribution = health_adjusted_value * depth_factor
bench_depth_score = Σ contributions
formulas.inputs: health-adjusted rosValues of bench players, ordered by value descending.
formulas.constants: DEPTH_BENCH_LIMIT = 8. Decay by position: QB 0.55, RB 0.65, WR 0.65, TE 0.55, DL/LB/DB 0.55, default 0.50. Comment at :66-67 justifies them by assertion ("QBs and IDP get a slightly steeper decay because their backup-week spikes are rarer") with no data. Worked example: three bench WRs at 40/35/30 → 40×1 + 35×0.65 + 30×0.4225 = 75.43.
formulas.mathIssues: The 8-player cap is applied to a 44-58 man roster in a best-ball league — the format where the deep bench is exactly what pays. playoff_sim.py:246-262 documents this and works around it by reading `fullRoster` instead, so the codebase already knows the depth score truncates. Position is taken from `player.position` only, not `fantasy_positions`, so a DL/LB hybrid counts against only one position's decay chain.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Unknown position → _DEFAULT_DECAY 0.50. A bench of 30 players contributes only its top 8 by value, silently.

formulas.name: positional_coverage_score
formulas.expression:
demand[pos] = Σ over slots: 1.0 for a dedicated slot, or 1/|eligible| for each eligible position of a flex slot
target[pos]  = max(1.0, demand[pos] * 1.5)
earned       = Σ_pos min(1.0, have[pos]/target[pos]) * demand[pos]
score        = 100 * earned / Σ_pos demand[pos]
formulas.inputs: the league's flattened starter-slot list and the roster's eligibility-aware position counts.
formulas.constants: _COVERAGE_DEPTH_MULTIPLIER = 1.5, chosen (per the :434-437 comment) to "reproduce the long-standing offense targets it replaces (QB 2, RB 4, TE ~3)" — back-fitted to a prior hardcoded table, not to data.
formulas.mathIssues: Flex demand is split evenly across eligible positions regardless of who is actually rostered (the docstring at :447-449 concedes this is approximate). Live output is 90.87-100.0 across 12 teams — a 9-point spread, weighted at 0.05 of an unbounded ~600 composite, so it moves the composite by at most 0.46 points. The docstring at :481-486 correctly notes the prior version "returned exactly 100.00 for all 12 teams... discriminating nothing"; the replacement discriminates 0.46 points.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: starter_slots=None → falls back to a hardcoded offense-only table {QB 2, RB 4, WR 5, TE 2} that ignores K and all IDP (`:494-502`). Empty demand → 0.0.

formulas.name: health_availability_score
formulas.expression: score = 100 * (starters with no injured/bye flag) / (filled starter slots)
formulas.inputs: the `flagged` field on each starting-lineup row.
formulas.constants: none
formulas.mathIssues: Denominator is FILLED slots, not configured slots — a team with an unfilled slot (MaKayla has `unfilledSlots: ["K"]`) is scored on a smaller denominator and can hit 100.0 while missing a starter. Double-counts with the 0.4 injured multiplier already applied inside starting_lineup_score. Bye is always False (scrape.py:224) so this is a pure injury share.
formulas.outputRange: [0, 100]; live: 100.0 for 11 of 12 teams, 95.24 for one.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No starting rows → 0.0, which reads as "all starters injured" rather than "no lineup".

formulas.name: ROS blend into the weekly scoring mean
formulas.expression:
ros_z = (team_ros_strength - mean(all_strengths)) / pstdev(all_strengths)
blended_mean = empirical_mean * (1 + 0.20 * ros_z)
sd = empirical_sd * variance_multiplier, floored at 1.0
formulas.inputs: per-team `teamRosStrength` from the default league's snapshot; per-team empirical weekly scores from the current season.
formulas.constants: ROS_BLEND = 0.20, described at :64-66 as "Chosen small so empirical history still dominates; tunable via settings" — a stated prior, and no settings path actually tunes it (grep finds no writer).
formulas.mathIssues: A z-score of −5 would drive `blended_mean` negative; it is clamped at :530 via max(0.0, ...) rather than bounded, so an extreme outlier silently becomes a zero-scoring team. `ros_sd` falls back to 1.0 when the population has ≤1 member or zero variance (:476-478), making the z-score a raw difference in composite units — an uncontrolled scale.
formulas.validated: none found. tests/ros/test_playoff_sim.py:112 `test_blend_is_modest` asserts only that ROS_BLEND is small.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: `ros_strength_map.get(owner_id)` returning None → no blend, `blended_mean = emp_mean`, and NOTHING is stamped to say so. `rosStrengthAvailable` at :818 is `bool(ros_map)` — file existence, not per-owner application. Live dynasty_new sim: 8 of 8 owners got no blend, payload says rosStrengthAvailable: true.

formulas.name: per-team weekly variance multiplier
formulas.expression:
if not best_ball: 1.0
else: 1.10 + 0.15 * clamp(bench_depth_score / starting_lineup_score, 0, 1)
formulas.inputs: the team-strength snapshot's benchDepthScore and startingLineupScore.
formulas.constants: BEST_BALL_VARIANCE_BUMP = 1.10, DEPTH_VARIANCE_LIFT_MAX = 0.15. Both hand-picked; the comment at :74-79 justifies 0.15 by assertion ("Capped to keep tail behavior physically plausible"). Live depth ratios: 205.19/833.21 = 0.246 → multiplier 1.137; thinnest team 67.63/593.12 = 0.114 → 1.117. Actual spread across 12 teams: 1.117-1.137, a 2% range.
formulas.mathIssues: Reads the DEFAULT league's team-strength file unconditionally (:191), so a non-default best-ball league would get another league's depth ratios or none. The depth ratio is itself a ratio of two truncated sums (bench capped at 8 players).
formulas.outputRange: [1.0, 1.25]; live 1.117-1.137 for dynasty_main, 1.0 for dynasty_new (best_ball unset).
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing snapshot → {} → ratio defaults to 0.0 → multiplier 1.10 flat. Missing owner → same.

formulas.name: PointsModel.draw — rosValue → weekly fantasy points
formulas.expression:
mean = max(0, ros_value / ros_value_per_point)
sd   = max(0.5, mean * cv_for(position))
draw = max(0, Gauss(mean, sd))
formulas.inputs: a player's `rosValue` (0-100 log-rank index) and position.
formulas.constants: FALLBACK_ROS_VALUE_PER_POINT = 2.7; fallback CVs QB 0.32, RB 0.55, WR 0.60, TE 0.65, DL/DE/DT/EDGE 0.55, LB 0.45, DB/S 0.50, CB 0.55, default 0.55. BOTH cached sims stamp `pointsModelSource: "fallback-constants"` and `pointsModelGeneratedAt: null` — the calibrated artifact `data/league_intel/sim_points_model.json` does not exist (the whole `data/league_intel/` directory is absent), so the uncalibrated constants are what runs. Worked example: the live #1 team's 21-slot lineup totals 833.21 rosValue → 833.21/2.7 = 308.6 fantasy points per week.
formulas.mathIssues: 308 points/week for a 21-starter lineup is far above realistic, though it largely cancels in head-to-head comparison. The divisor converts a LOG-RANK INDEX to points as if the relationship were linear — the module's own docstring at :17-25 concedes the original constants were "tuned by eye" and cite "a dataset that is named nowhere in the repo". playoff_sim.py:111-112 additionally states the divisor is 17, contradicting the live 2.7. A truncated Gaussian at max(0, ·) with cv 0.60 truncates mass and biases the mean upward without correction.
formulas.validated: The calibration path exists (sim_calibration.py scores real stat lines under league settings, r2 0.63 per its own docstring example) but the artifact is not present, so nothing validated is running.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: ros_value <= 0 → the player is skipped entirely from the best-ball pool (playoff_sim.py:368-369), so unmapped players simply do not exist in the sim rather than scoring zero — a different treatment from team_strength, which counts them as 0.

formulas.name: _mean_is_converged / presim stopping rule
formulas.expression:
SE = pstdev(samples) / sqrt(n); converge when SE/|mean| < 0.01 (or SE < 0.01 when |mean| < 1e-9)
checked every 40 draws once n >= 120, capped at 1200
formulas.inputs: the per-team simulated weekly best-ball totals.
formulas.constants: PRESIM_MEAN_TOLERANCE 0.01, MIN 120, MAX 1200, CHECK_EVERY 40.
formulas.mathIssues: Convergence is tested on the MEAN only; the sd is then used as-is at :418 with no error bar of its own, and the sd is the quantity the downstream matchup draws are most sensitive to. Checking on a cadence with an optional-stopping rule biases the estimate slightly toward whichever side the running mean happened to be on at the check.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n < 4 → not converged. Fewer than 4 samples → the owner is omitted from `bestball_dists` (:417) and falls back to the empirical distribution with no stamp.

formulas.name: playoff-odds convergence / Wilson interval
formulas.expression:
SE(p) = sqrt(p(1-p)/n); stop when max over owners of SE <= 0.005
Wilson: center = (p + z²/2n)/(1 + z²/n); margin = (z/(1+z²/n))·sqrt(p(1-p)/n + z²/4n²)
formulas.inputs: per-owner playoff hit counts and completed sim count.
formulas.constants: ODDS_SE_TOLERANCE 0.005, SIM_CHECK_EVERY 1000, MIN_SIMULATIONS 2000, MAX 60000, z=1.96.
formulas.mathIssues: Sound in isolation but produces a misleading result on a degenerate schedule: with zero remaining games p is exactly 0 or 1, `_proportion_se` returns 0.0 (the docstring at :156-158 acknowledges this understates), so the loop exits at the 2,000 floor and stamps `converged: true, worstPlayoffOddsSe: 0.0`. The Wilson interval correctly widens at p=0/1 but is only reported per-row, while the CONVERGENCE decision uses the naive SE. That is exactly backwards.
formulas.validated: formula is standard; no empirical validation of the odds themselves.

formulas.name: _paired_delta_ci (trade impact significance)
formulas.expression:
b_plus_c = clamp(|after-before| + 2·min(before, n-after), |after-before|, n)
d  = (after_hits - before_hits)/n
SE = sqrt(b_plus_c)/n
CI = (d - 1.96·SE, d + 1.96·SE); significant iff the interval excludes zero
formulas.inputs: before/after playoff or championship hit counts on SHARED RNG seeds.
formulas.mathIssues: The discordant-pair count is not observed; the code bounds it by the marginals, which the docstring at :898-905 correctly calls conservative. Callers pass `round(b*n)` and `round(a*n)` reconstructed from ROUNDED proportions (`:1026`) rather than the raw counts — the counts are rounded to 4 decimals upstream at `:791`, so at n=10000 the reconstruction can be off by up to 0.5 hits. Minor, but the raw counts are available and are being thrown away.
formulas.validated: none found — no test constructs a known trade delta and checks the interval's coverage.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n<=0 → (0.0, 0.0), a zero-width interval at zero, which `significant=(lo>0)or(hi<0)` reads as not-significant. Correct direction.

formulas.name: ROS Power Rankings v2 composite
formulas.expression:
active_weights = {k: w for k, w in WEIGHTS if k not in missing_inputs}
score = 100 * Σ_k (active_weights[k] * component[k]) / Σ active_weights
formulas.inputs: team_ros_strength percentile, ppg percentile, recent-form percentile, W/L share, all-play expected share, streak score, schedule-adjusted score, roster health (0-1), luck-regression score.
formulas.constants: team_ros_strength 0.38, ppg 0.18, recent 0.12, wl_record 0.10, all_play 0.08, streak 0.05, schedule_adjusted 0.04, roster_health 0.03, luck_regression 0.02 (sum 1.00). All "spec" values, uncalibrated. Preseason path (`_is_preseason` at :195, true today since the season is complete): six historical components are dropped (:462-465), schedule_adjusted is dropped because the remaining schedule is empty, leaving team_ros_strength 0.38 and roster_health 0.03 → renormalised score = 100·(0.38·ros_pct + 0.03·health)/0.41 = 92.7·ros_pct + 7.3·health. With health 1.0 for 11 of 12 teams, preseason ROS Power IS the team-strength percentile with a constant offset.
formulas.mathIssues: The renormalisation makes the advertised nine-input formula collapse to one input in the state the system is currently in, disclosed only via a `missingInputs` array. The luck_regression term at :420-432 re-walks every season for every owner inside the per-owner loop — O(owners² × weeks) — and compares career `wins` against an `expected_share_running` accumulated over all seasons.
formulas.validated: none found. tests/ros/test_power_v2.py:85 asserts the weights sum to 1.0 and :88 asserts team_ros_strength dominates.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing team-strength → `team_ros_strength` dropped and renormalised away; the ranking then has no ROS content at all yet is still labelled ROS Power. `roster_health` defaults to 0.0 for an owner absent from the snapshot (:442) — a confident zero, not an exclusion.

formulas.name: _percentile (inclusive percentile rank)
formulas.expression: pct = (count(v < target) + 0.5 * count(v == target)) / len(values)
formulas.inputs: a list of comparable metric values and the target value.
formulas.constants: the 0.5 mid-rank tie correction.
formulas.mathIssues: Correct mid-rank formula. Note it never reaches 1.0 (the max value scores (n-1+0.5)/n) so the top team's ros_pct on 12 teams is 0.9583, not 1.0 — a small systematic compression at the top end that flows into the power score.
formulas.validated: tests/ros/test_power_v2.py:42-50 pins high/low/empty behaviour.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty list → 0.0 (which reads as "worst", not "unknown"). None entries are filtered at :103; if all are None → 0.0.

formulas.name: _streak_score_from_outcomes
formulas.inputs: chronological W/L/T outcome shares (1.0/0.0/0.5).
formulas.constants: 0.10 per game, saturating at 5, neutral 0.5. Hand-picked.
formulas.mathIssues: Compares floats for equality (`if o == last`) to detect the run — a 0.5 tie share breaks the run in a way a 0.5000001 would not. No recency weighting beyond run length.
formulas.validated: none found beyond tests/ros/test_power_v2.py:21-36, which pin the arithmetic.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty outcomes → 0.5 (neutral). Correct.

formulas.name: luck_regression
formulas.expression:
expected_share_running = Σ over all seasons/weeks of the owner's all-play expected win share
luck_delta = (career_wins - expected_share_running) / career_games
luck_score = clamp(0.5 - luck_delta, 0, 1)
formulas.inputs: career actual wins, career all-play expected shares, career games.
formulas.constants: the 0.5 neutral centre and the [0,1] clamp.
formulas.mathIssues: Underperformers get a higher score (a regression boost), which is the stated intent but is an assumption, not a measurement. The re-walk at :421-428 iterates every season and week inside the per-owner loop, recomputing `_all_play_week` for the whole league on each pass — O(owners × seasons × weeks × owners).
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: games = 0 → `games = s["games"] or 1` at :409, so luck_delta = wins - expected with a denominator of 1 for a brand-new owner — both terms are 0 there, giving 0.5 neutral. Weight is 0.02 and it is dropped entirely in preseason.

formulas.name: schedule_adjusted_scores
formulas.expression: score[owner] = clamp(1 - mean(opponent team-strength percentiles over remaining matchups), 0, 1)
formulas.inputs: the remaining-schedule pair list and the team-strength percentile map.
formulas.constants: none
formulas.mathIssues: Returns {} whenever the remaining schedule is empty — the current state — so this component is always dropped in the offseason. It also uses TODAY's team-strength percentile as the opponent's strength for every future week, with no decay over the horizon.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty map or empty schedule → {} → the component is renormalised out. Owners present in the schedule but absent from the percentile map contribute nothing to their opponents' averages, silently biasing the remaining opponents' mean.

formulas.name: buyer/seller direction classifier
formulas.expression:
Strong Buyer      if playoff>=0.75 and champ>=0.10
Buyer             elif playoff>=0.60 and champ>=0.05
Selective Buyer   elif 0.45<=playoff<0.60
Strong Seller     elif playoff<0.10 and champ<0.01 and vetCount>=4
Seller            elif playoff<0.25 and champ<0.02
Selective Seller  elif 0.20<=playoff<0.40
Hold / Evaluate   else
formulas.inputs: playoff odds, championship odds, veteran count, and (unused) team-strength percentile.
formulas.constants: 0.75/0.10, 0.60/0.05, 0.45-0.60, 0.10/0.01, 0.25/0.02, 0.20-0.40, and `age_heavy = vetCount >= 4` at :77. Position-aware veteran ages at :24-37 (QB 32, RB 26, WR 29, TE 30, DL/EDGE 30, LB 29, DB 29) — "Spec values verbatim", uncalibrated.
formulas.mathIssues: `team_ros_strength_percentile` is a parameter (:57) that only appears in the display summary at :120 — it never influences the label. The fallthrough order contradicts the docstring bands (a team at playoff 0.22 gets "Seller", not the documented "Selective Seller"). Fed today by degenerate 0/1 odds, so every team is pinned to Strong Buyer, Hold, or Seller with nothing in between.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: trade_deadline.py:82-83 coerces a missing odds row to 0.0 for both metrics — the defect that labels four teams "Seller" today. An empty age profile makes `age_heavy` False, so a genuine rebuilder without age data is downgraded to plain "Seller".

formulas.name: contender tier
formulas.expression: Favorite if champ>=0.20; Serious Contender if >=0.10; Dangerous Playoff Team if champ>=0.05 or playoff>=0.50; Fringe if playoff>=0.30; Long Shot if playoff>=0.10; else Rebuilder / Seller
formulas.inputs: championship odds and playoff odds from the championship sim.
formulas.mathIssues: With degenerate playoff odds (1.0/0.0), the `playoff>=0.50` clause makes every playoff team at least "Dangerous" and every non-playoff team "Rebuilder / Seller" with no gradation.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a — both inputs are always computed inside the same function.

formulas.name: tags_for_player thresholds
formulas.expression:
is_strong = ros_value>=60; is_elite = ros_value>=80; is_starter_caliber = ros_rank<=100; is_top_idp = is_idp and ros_rank<=50
Win-now target          := veteran and is_strong
Contender upgrade       := is_elite and is_starter_caliber and not is_idp
Seller cash-out         := veteran and is_strong and dynasty_value < ros_value*0.7
Rebuilder hold          := young(<=24) and not is_strong
Avoid unless contending := veteran and is_strong and not is_starter_caliber
Depth spike option      := not is_starter_caliber and 30<=ros_value<60
Best-ball boost         := volatility_flag and is_starter_caliber
IDP contender target    := is_top_idp
Injury/bye cover        := not is_strong and not young
formulas.inputs: rosValue (0-100), rosRankOverall, position, age, dynastyValue, volatilityFlag.
formulas.constants: 60, 80, 100, 50, 30, 24, 0.7 — all hand-picked, no calibration.
formulas.mathIssues: `Seller cash-out` compares a 0-9999 dynasty value against `ros_value*0.7` (max 70) — dimensionally invalid and dead in production. `is_elite` at 80 is nearly unreachable: only 2 of 1,085 live players exceed 80 (Josh Allen 86.42, Jahmyr Gibbs 82.63), so "Contender upgrade" fires for at most two players league-wide. `is_top_idp` at rank<=50 fires for 10 defenders today only because of the IDP normalization inflation. `Avoid unless contending` (strong but rank>100) is contradictory given the log curve — a rosValue of 60 already implies a top-15 overall rank on the live board.
formulas.validated: none found; three uncoordinated implementations, one of them (the Python one) with no live caller.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: ros_value None or <=0 → empty tag list (`:56-57`), which the UI renders as "No ROS tags · no ROS read". Missing age → veteran False and young False, so a player with no age can only receive "Depth spike option", "Best-ball boost", "IDP contender target" or "Injury/bye cover".

formulas.name: project_draft_order — slot confidence
formulas.expression:
sort ascending by (teamRosStrength, rosterId); slot = index+1
avg_gap = (max_strength - min_strength) / (n-1)
min_gap = min(gap to the neighbour above, gap to the neighbour below)
ratio   = min_gap / avg_gap
confidence = high if ratio>=1.0; medium if >=0.4; else low
formulas.inputs: the team-strength composite per team.
formulas.constants: _CONFIDENCE_HIGH_RATIO 1.0, _CONFIDENCE_MEDIUM_RATIO 0.4. Hand-picked.
formulas.mathIssues: Confidence measures how isolated a team is on TODAY's composite — a statement about ranking stability now, not about where a future pick lands. The module documents this honestly at :36-57. The composite it ranks on is itself the IDP-inflated sum, so the projected draft order inherits every distortion in `rosValue`.
formulas.validated: none found — the module states explicitly that no history exists to fit against.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A team with a non-numeric or missing `teamRosStrength` is EXCLUDED from the order entirely (:105-106); the caller can only detect this by comparing lengths, and its picks land in `unprojectablePicks` (:216). avg_gap <= 0 (all teams tied) → every team "low". Both are honest degradations.

formulas.name: pick horizon confidence cap
formulas.expression:
ceiling = {1: "high", 2: "medium"}.get(seasons_out, "low")
confidence = min(slot_confidence, ceiling) by the order (low < medium < high)
formulas.inputs: seasons_out = pick season − current calendar year.
formulas.constants: {1: high, 2: medium}, beyond: low. Explicitly labelled "a STATED ASSUMPTION, not a measurement" at :52 — the most honest constant declaration in the subsystem, with the measurement that motivated it recorded at :44-47.
formulas.mathIssues: `current_season = datetime.now(UTC).year` (:178) is the calendar year, not the fantasy draft year. In January the calendar year rolls to the upcoming season, so `season <= current_season` at :210 would exclude that year's rookie picks — the very picks a January user cares about. CLAUDE.md documents the identical trap for `currentDraftYear` in the BDVM section.
formulas.validated: none found, and the module says so.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Unknown confidence label → returns the ceiling rather than promoting (:74-75). Correct direction.

formulas.name: projectedPickNumber
formulas.expression: projectedPickNumber = (round - 1) * team_count + projectedSlot
formulas.inputs: pick round, the count of teams that survived into `projectedOrder`, and the slot.
formulas.constants: none
formulas.mathIssues: `team_count = len(order)` is the count AFTER excluding teams without a usable strength (:105-106). If any team is excluded, every pick number after round 1 is computed on a short league — a 12-team league that drops one team yields 2.01 at pick 12 instead of 13. No warning is emitted for this consequence.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: An `original_roster_id` not in the projected order increments `unprojectablePicks` and the pick is omitted, not guessed (:216-217). Honest.

formulas.name: trade_deadline strength percentile proxy
formulas.expression: strength_pct = (total - rank + 1) / total   where total = number of teams in the strength map, rank is the snapshot's 1-based rank; 0.0 when rank is missing
formulas.inputs: the team-strength snapshot's `rank` field.
formulas.constants: none
formulas.mathIssues: A rank-based proxy that discards the magnitude of the strength gap — the #1 team at 646.85 and the #2 at 536.79 differ by 110 points, and the proxy records 1.0 vs 0.9167. The comment at :74-75 calls it "the cheapest proxy", which is accurate. The value is then only used in a display string (direction.py:120), so the imprecision is currently harmless.
formulas.validated: none found.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rank missing or 0 → 0.0, which reads as "weakest team in the league" rather than "unknown".

formulas.name: solve_optimal_assignment — exact max-weight lineup
formulas.expression: Order players by (-health_adjusted_value, player_id); admit each via Kuhn augmenting path over the bipartite player↔slot eligibility graph; then canonicalize by sliding/swapping to put higher values in more restrictive slots.
formulas.inputs: the roster's health-adjusted values and the flattened, priority-sorted slot list.
formulas.constants: slot priority: SUPER_FLEX 3, FLEX/IDP_FLEX 2, everything else 0 (`:426-431`). No numeric tuning.
formulas.mathIssues: None found — this is the most rigorous piece of code in the subsystem.
