Slot eligibility defines a transversal matroid and weights are slot-independent, so weight-descending greedy with augmentation is provably optimal for any eligibility structure. The canonicalization pass preserves the assigned multiset, so optimality is preserved by construction. Determinism is explicit (ties break on player_id, augmenting paths explore slots in index order). A duplicate player_id is guarded at :269-271.
formulas.validated: tests/league_intel/test_lineup_exactness.py is cited at :34-35 as pinning equivalence with brute force including a non-laminar case the old greedy failed. This is the one formula in the subsystem with a genuine correctness proof and a test that could falsify it.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A player with value 0 still competes for a slot (only `_bestball_weekly_score` filters ros<=0 at playoff_sim.py:368); an unfillable slot is reported in `unfilled_slots` rather than silently omitted.

formulas.name: buildRosIndex / rosEntryForRow — the frontend join
formulas.expression:
key   = normalizePlayerNameKey(canonicalName)
tie-break on collision: higher sourceCount, then higher confidence, then higher rosValue
lookup: try normalizePlayerNameKey of row.canonicalName, then row.displayName, then row.name
formulas.inputs: the `/api/ros/player-values` players array and a contract board row.
formulas.constants: none. The file documents the measured join rates in its header: exact string 12/1075 (1.1%), normalizeName 802 (74.6%), normalizeNameCompact 849 (79.0%), normalizePlayerNameKey 849 (79.0%) — the only measured calibration anywhere in this subsystem, and it is a join-rate measurement, not a value validation.
formulas.mathIssues: The chosen key strips generational suffixes (documented at :54-57), so "Marvin Harrison Jr." and "Marvin Harrison" collapse; the header states zero collisions on the contract side at time of measurement — a point-in-time observation, not an invariant. The `preferRow` tie-break exists because the aggregate stores case-duplicate rows, a data defect the header calls out as still open.
formulas.outputRange: Map of key → {rosValue, rosRank, rosRankPosition, confidence, volatilityFlag, staleFlag, tier, sourceCount}
formulas.validated: The join rate is measured (849/1075) and frontend/__tests__/ros-index.test.js exists. The values joined are not validated.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A row with no usable name key is skipped rather than indexed under "" (:115). A board row with no ROS match returns null and the UI renders "no ROS read" — correct for the ~21% genuinely unranked, and the header explains at length why it used to be wrong for 79%.

notes:
HORIZON / PROJECTION CHARACTERIZATION (the Part XIII questions, answered directly):

- Prediction target: none, in the strict sense. `rosValue` predicts no observable quantity. It is a weighted average of five vendors' ORDINAL positions, transformed by a log curve into a 0-100 index with no units. `RankedRow.projection_value` exists, is populated from a real DraftSharks projection (scrape.py:419-422), and is deliberately discarded — aggregate.py:60-73 says so and tests/ros/test_projection_value_is_not_consumed.py pins the discard. Every `projection` column in every file under data/ros/sources/ is EMPTY. There is no points projection anywhere in src/ros/.
- Horizon: nominally "rest of season". In August 2026 that is the full unstarted 2026 season. Two of five sources (23% of an offense player's blend, 40.5% of an IDP player's) are multi-year DYNASTY boards, registered as such (`is_ros: False`) and never disclosed downstream. A third is redraft ADP.
- Data cutoff: whatever each vendor last published. The pipeline does not record or expose it — `scraped_at` is the orchestrator's own run time, so vendor-side staleness is invisible by construction.
- External / blended / rule-based: entirely external, blended by fixed hand-set weights, with rule-based post-processing (tiers, tags, direction labels).
- Injuries: a flat 0.4 multiplier for Sleeper status in {OUT, IR, PUP, DOUBTFUL} (lineup.py:216-218), applied at the lineup layer only. No return timeline, no games-missed, no severity gradation.
- Byes: `"bye": False` hardcoded at scrape.py:224. No bye logic at all, despite an "Injury/bye cover" tag.
- Rookies: no rookie treatment of any kind in src/ros/. Rookies enter only if a vendor ranks them.
- Role changes: none. Nothing reads news, depth charts, snap counts or transactions. (BDVM has a news→events ingestion path; ROS has nothing analogous.)
- Regression to the mean: none on players. The only regression concept is `luck_regression` in power_v2.py:429-432, a team-level term at 0.02 weight that is dropped entirely in preseason.
- Calibration: none. No fit script, no calibration artifact, no parameter file — every constant is inline. `data/league_intel/sim_points_model.json` (the one artifact the sim can consume) does not exist, so both sims stamp `pointsModelSource: "fallback-constants"`.
- Historical validation: none. pick_projection.py:52-57 states the reason plainly — team-strength snapshots are overwritten, not archived, so there is no history to fit against.

TEMPORAL LEAKAGE — checked and reported precisely:

- Player-value layer: NO leakage. `rosValue` consumes only external rank boards; no realized outcome from the projected window enters it. This is clean.
- Team/sim layer: no classical leakage either — `playoff_sim` seeds `sim_wins` from realized wins and simulates only the *remaining* schedule (playoff_sim.py:719-737), which is correct construction.
- What IS wrong is a HORIZON COLLAPSE, not leakage: when the remaining schedule is empty (offseason, today), the "projection" degenerates into a verbatim replay of the completed season's final standings, presented with a fresh `computedAt`, `converged: true` and a zero-width confidence interval. The window being projected is empty and nothing says so.
- One genuine cross-boundary read: `power_v2.py` blends prior-season realized results into a metric labelled forward-looking; `_is_preseason` (:195-223) correctly drops them, and that guard exists in power_v2 ONLY — playoff_sim.py and championship.py have no equivalent.

FRESHNESS OF data/ros/ (asked explicitly):

- data/ros/ is force-added by .github/workflows/scheduled-refresh.yml:521 despite .gitignore:59-68, and updated roughly every 2h. `git log -1 -- data/ros/` = 030c7d6, 2026-08-04T03:57:39Z, ~4.5h before HEAD (9c5d972, 2026-08-04T06:32Z).
- The AGGREGATE is genuinely fresh: `aggregatedAt: 2026-08-04T03:57:23`, 5 sources all `status: ok`, 1,085 players. `/api/ros/status` correctly reports "fresh".
- Per-source newest runs: draftSharksRosSf, fantasyProsRosIdp, fantasyProsRosOverall, fantasyProsRosSf, ffc2qbAdp all 2026-08-04T03:57. `footballGuysRosIdp` last ran 2026-07-21 — 14 days stale, but it is NOT in the registry and does NOT reach the aggregate; orphaned artifacts only.
- So: no, the aggregate is not stale. The stale-presented-as-current problem is different and worse — the SIMS are freshly recomputed from a COMPLETED season, and `/api/ros/health` reports their age from file mtime rather than the `computedAt` they carry (mtime 06:56 vs computedAt 03:57 in this very checkout), so a `git pull` on prod resets both the health colour and the 6h cache TTL.
- Volume: 792 aggregate history snapshots (2026-04-28 → 2026-08-04, 98 days) at 853 MB, plus 4,633 run files at 19 MB, all committed. Both `src/ros/__init__.py:26` and docs/ros-engine.md call it a "rolling 30-day archive"; no prune exists. Nothing reads `aggregate/history/`.

WIRING STATUS — the four-level distinction, applied:

- Implemented + routed + consumed + live data + validated: NOTHING in src/ros/ reaches the last level.
- Implemented + routed + consumed + live data: rosValue, team strength, playoff/championship sims, trade-deadline directions, pick projector, tags (via the JS copies), ROS data health.
- Implemented + routed + live data, NOT consumed by any frontend: `power_v2` (`rosPower` lazy section exists, but `settings.useRosPowerRankings` defaults false, so the v1 formula ships); `src/ros/tags.py` itself has zero non-test callers — the shipped tags are the two JS reimplementations; `simulate_trade_impact` has no route or caller.
- Implemented but effectively inert: `freshness_multiplier`, `staleFlag`, `stale_after_hours`, the 1.15 SF+TEP branch, `_PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION`, `rosEnabled`, `projection_value`, the "Seller cash-out" tag, the bye penalty, `championship._simulate_bracket`'s `playoff_seeds` parameter and `bye_set`.

TESTS — what they actually assert (I opened them):

- tests/ros/test_scrape_failure_resilience.py: calls `_write_csv`/`_has_valid_cache` in isolation. Never invokes `run_all` or `aggregate`. The guarantee named in its own docstring and in docs/ros-engine.md is not tested and not implemented.
- tests/ros/test_team_strength.py:83: recomputes `0.72·s + 0.18·d + 0.05·c + 0.05·h` and asserts equality with the code. A tautology.
- tests/ros/test_aggregate.py:126: asserts the blend is in [0,100] and that a rank-1 player beats a rank-2 player. Does not test cross-population blending.
- tests/ros/test_direction_and_tags.py:142: passes `dynasty_value=40, ros_value=70` for "Seller cash-out" — a scale the production callers never produce (they pass 0-9999). Green test, dead feature.
- tests/ros/test_projection_value_is_not_consumed.py: the best-constructed suite here. It genuinely pins that projections are discarded and that rosValue is exactly `rank_to_score` for a single source, and includes a docstring-content assertion designed to fail if the comment starts lying again.
- tests/ros/test_source_double_count.py and test_team_strength_canonical_join.py: both pin real, previously-fixed defects with measured numbers. Good work.
- tests/ros/test_isolation.py: verifies the dynasty-contract constants are byte-identical before/after importing src.ros. That boundary does hold — I found no ROS write into any dynasty path. The ROS engine's central promise (never touch dynasty values) is the one promise it keeps.
- tests/ros/test_sources_registry_parity.py: genuinely parses the JS registry and diffs it against Python. Works — and is currently keeping a dead field (`stale_after_hours`) in lockstep.

NOT VERIFIED / NOT VERIFIABLE FROM REPOSITORY:

- Whether the DraftSharks ROS pages currently return real ROS ranks or the fetcher is silently serving a stale login. `CSVs/site_raw/draftSharksRosSf.csv` and `draftSharksRosIdp.csv` are both 28,591 bytes with 979 lines but different md5s — consistent with the two-format story in the fetcher docstring; I could not check the live site.
- Why `_season_weekly_scores` yields only 8 owners for both leagues. I established the schedule is empty and the odds are therefore deterministic; I did not trace whether the 8-owner coverage is roster turnover, a manager-registry gap, or Sleeper season-transition state.
- Whether `/api/ros/*` resolves in local dev. Only `pick-projections` has a Next bridge route; the other five endpoints rely on nginx `location /api/` → backend (deploy/nginx/chaseupside-proxy.conf:56), correct in production. I could not run the dev server.
- Real-world accuracy of any ROS number. There is nothing in the repository to check it against.

ONE THING THAT SURPRISED ME, IN THE GOOD DIRECTION: several modules document their own weaknesses with unusual candour and measured numbers — pick_projection.py:36-57 on why its confidence field cannot mean what its name says, frontend/lib/ros-index.js:20-61 on the 1.1% join rate it replaced, playoff_sim.py:246-262 on simulating 29 of 44-58 players, aggregate.py:156-165 on the DraftSharks 67.4%-of-blend incident, lineup.py:12-35 on the laminar-family precondition the old greedy relied on. The subsystem's problem is not that nobody looked. It is that those honest comments sit next to shipped numbers the comments themselves undermine, and no gate stops those numbers from reaching /trade and /league as advice.

BOTTOM LINE ON WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE DECISIONS:
- `solve_optimal_assignment` (the lineup optimizer): trustworthy, proven, tested.
- `rosValue` for OFFENSE players: defensible as a directional consensus of four boards, with the caveat that 23% is a dynasty board and 16% is redraft ADP.
- `rosValue` for IDP players: not trustworthy. Two sources, one of them a dynasty board, blended across incompatible populations, with 13 real players silently missing.
- `teamRosStrength`: inherits the IDP distortion and its stated weights are not its actual weights.
- Playoff odds, championship odds, contender tiers, buyer/seller labels: not trustworthy in the current state. They are a replay of a completed season with missing teams coerced to 0%.
- Pick Projector slots: only as good as `teamRosStrength`, and it is candid about its own confidence semantics.

findings.title: The league-adjusted factor is NOT a function of position alone — CLAUDE.md and publish.py both assert a property production violates
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md: "The adjustment factor is a function of position alone and never reads the consensus value". src/league_intel/publish.py:21-27: "The factor depends only on **position** — it never reads the consensus value." But src/league_intel/adjustment.py:312-323 states the opposite in code: `reception_fit_axis` — "The only per-player axis in the model. Every other axis is a function of position, which is what lets them compose against a re-weighted board; this one is not". src/api/gameplan.py:1333 passes `reception_fit=_resolve_reception_fit(league_key)` into the payload builder unconditionally, and `reception_scoring_fit` defaults True (src/api/feature_flags.py:204). The repo's own production measurement proves the violation: docs/measurements/adjusted-board-backtest-2026-07-28.json `factorShape` shows RB `distinct: 45`, TE `distinct: 49`, WR `distinct: 96` — 190 distinct per-player factors on one board. I reproduced the position-uniform case only by passing `reception_fit=None`: 8 distinct factor values for 931 moved rows.
findings.userImpact: An auditor or maintainer reading CLAUDE.md concludes the overlay can never reorder players within a position and that the batch monotonicity guard is decorative. It is not: reception fit reorders WR/RB/TE against each other, and it is the only axis that can. Any reasoning built on "position-uniform, therefore order-preserving by construction" is wrong for three of eight positions.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct CLAUDE.md and publish.py:21-27 to state the true invariant, which is the one that actually earns composability: *no axis reads the consensus value*. Position-uniformity is a separate, now-false claim. `tests/api/test_league_adjusted_endpoint.py::test_the_same_position_gets_the_same_factor` should be renamed/re-scoped — it passes only because the test environment cannot resolve reception fit.

findings.title: structuralScarcity is computed from a log-rank index with an arbitrary zero, so every factor moves when the ROS source universe changes size
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/replacement.py:609-613 `_safe_drop(top, bottom) -> 1 - bottom/top`, used at :655 as `lineup_scarcity=_safe_drop(top, starter)`. Both operands are `rosValue`. src/ros/aggregate.py:171-173: "``rosValue`` is therefore a normalized log-rank index on 0-100 — not points, and not projection-aware." src/ros/parse.py:43-46: `return 100.0 * (log(n+1) - log(r)) / log(n+1)` where `n = total_ranked`. A ratio requires a true zero; this index's zero is "rank N of whatever the ROS sources happened to publish". I held every player's rank fixed and only re-scored under a different universe size N (live N=1085 from data/ros/aggregate/latest.json): N=1085 factors {DB 1.0149, DL 1.0533, K 0.9878, LB 1.0199, QB 1.0179, RB 1.0407, TE 1.0115, WR 1.0254}; N=2000 {DB 0.9916, DL 1.0339, K 0.9617, LB 1.0033, QB 1.0071, RB 1.0272, TE 0.9933, WR 1.0112}; N=500 {DB 1.0636, DL 1.0877, K 1.0340, LB 1.0483, QB 1.0353, RB 1.0624, TE 1.0516, WR 1.0496}. DB, TE and LB flip from lift to trim purely on universe size.
findings.userImpact: Because picks are exempt (factor 1.0), the mean player factor is the level of the whole player-vs-pick reprice. On the live board that level is +2.5% (offense) / +3.3% (IDP) at N=1085, but would be +0.5% at N=2000 and +5.5% at N=500 with identical player rankings. A ROS source being added, dropped, or publishing a longer board silently changes every trade valuation under the adjusted lens, in a direction nobody chose. Positions can flip from "scarce" to "deep" with no change in the league.
findings.recommendedFix: Either (a) compute lineupScarcity as a difference on a scale with a meaningful zero — replacement-relative points, e.g. `(top - starter) / (top - waiver)` or over-replacement points from the exact scorer — or (b) normalize the index against a fixed reference N before taking ratios. Add a regression that perturbs the ROS universe size and asserts factors move less than the 0.1% publish floor.

findings.title: lineupScarcity measures top-heaviness, not scarcity, and the resulting lift is applied uniformly to every player at the position including replacement-level ones
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/replacement.py:655 `lineup_scarcity=_safe_drop(top, starter)` = `1 - median(marginal starters) / max(pool)`. Live dynasty_main: DL top 60.41, starter level 14.095 → 0.7667 → factor 1.05334; TE top 41.88, starter 18.525 → 0.5577 → factor 1.01153. The quantity is the *steepness of the positional value curve*, i.e. how far the best player at the position is above the last starter. src/league_intel/adjustment.py:250 applies `1.0 + delta` to every row at that position via src/league_intel/publish.py:171-179 and src/league_intel/overlay.py:92-93. The docstring at adjustment.py:218-228 calls it "positional scarcity implied by THIS league's measured lineup", which is a different concept.
findings.userImpact: A steep drop-off at a position is a VORP argument for paying up for the ELITE player at that position — it is an argument for paying LESS for the replacement-level one, since the gap is exactly what makes the marginal starter cheap. The current implementation does the opposite: the deepest priced DL on the board gets the same +5.3% as the best one. Under the adjusted lens a trade calculator overprices positional roster clog at exactly the positions where clog is least valuable.
findings.recommendedFix: Either restate the axis honestly as "positional value curve steepness" and justify a uniform multiplier on that basis, or make the lift a function of the player's own position within the curve (which then requires the batch monotonicity guard at adjustment.py:541-575 to do real work). Do not ship a uniform multiplier under a name that implies scarcity of bodies.

findings.title: scoringFit and receptionFit are measured against a Sleeper league that is not in the registry, then cached per league key as if they were league-specific
findings.evidence: src/api/gameplan.py:1180-1181 and :1272-1273 both do `cfg = _load_config(); mine_id = str((cfg.get("my_league") or {}).get("id"))` from config/league_comparison.json, whose `my_league.id` is `"owner-6e67d300493f"`. The registry's leagues are `1312006700437352448` (dynasty_main) and `1320092771247222784` (dynasty_new); the canonical LI snapshot config/league_intel/sleeper_league_snapshot_2026-07-26.json carries `"league_id":"1312006700437352448"`. Grepping the whole tree, `owner-6e67d300493f` appears in exactly one file — config/league_comparison.json. The `league_key` argument is used ONLY as the cache key (gameplan.py:1159-1160, :1247-1248); it never reaches the measurement.
findings.userImpact: The IDP positional multipliers (DL 1.0421 / DB 0.9971 / LB 0.9608 per scoring_fit.py:60-66) and every per-player reception tilt are derived from a league whose scoring settings nobody in this repo has cross-checked against dynasty_main's. Both then get applied to dynasty_main AND dynasty_new. If `my_league` is a stale or test league, the entire scoringFit axis is priced off the wrong rate card while presenting as `SCORING_MEASURED` evidence tier (confidence 0.70).
findings.recommendedFix: Resolve `mine_id` from `league_registry.get_sleeper_league_id(league_key)` rather than from config/league_comparison.json, or — if the comparison config is intentionally a separate league — assert at load time that `my_league.id` matches a registry league and fail loudly otherwise. At minimum stamp the measured league id into the axis rationale so a reader can see which league produced the number.

findings.title: The TE++ target basis is a hardcoded constant that is wrong for dynasty_new, and the corrective overlay axis is deliberately absent — the mispricing is documented and unmitigated
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:5681 `_BOARD_TE_BASIS: str = "tepp"`, applied at :7192-7207 to every non-TEP source's TE contribution. `src.league_intel.te_premium.measure_te_demand` returns `targetBasis: "tepp"` for dynasty_main (2 mandatory TE starters) and `targetBasis: "base"` for dynasty_new (1) — I ran it against config/leagues/registry.json. Both leagues share scoringProfile `superflex_tep15_ppr1`, so they share one board. src/league_intel/publish.py:45-70 names the problem and leaves `tePremium` ABSENT; src/league_intel/adjustment.py:371-396 returns an ABSENT axis unconditionally. A/B on the live export (RISKIT_FEATURE_TE_BASIS_CONVERSION=1 vs 0, 86 TE rows): median TE value ratio 1.1672, range 1.007–1.2708; median TE rank improvement 50 slots, max 202.
findings.userImpact: dynasty_new is a one-TE league being served a board where tight ends carry a two-TE premium worth a median +17% in value and ~50 board slots. Every trade evaluation, waiver bid and draft board for that league systematically overpays for TEs, and there is no toggle, note, or overlay that takes it back off.
findings.recommendedFix: Wire Axis B as a league-scoped overlay axis in publish.py as its own docstring already specifies: `residual = uplift(base→league_basis) / uplift(base→_BOARD_TE_BASIS)`, computed via `convert_te_value` in both directions so the double-count guard holds. Until then, surface an explicit warning on `/api/data` for any league whose `measure_te_demand().target_basis != _BOARD_TE_BASIS`.

findings.title: apply_valuation_factors is a third copy of "apply factors and re-rank" and it drops the coherence guard the other two have
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/publish.py:186-191 claims "ONE implementation of 'apply factors and re-rank', shared with the server-side engine path (``src.league_intel.overlay``). Two copies of this would drift, and the failure would be silent." But src/api/data_contract.py:8999-9040 `apply_valuation_factors` is a third implementation, reached from server.py:3782 via `build_rankings_delta_payload(..., valuation_factors=...)`. It multiplies and calls `compact_ranks_and_tiers` at :9036-9040 but never calls `assert_ranking_coherence`, which src/league_intel/overlay.py:119-125 uses to return None and force a market-board fallback. It also returns 0 on no-move while server.py:9143-9150 still stamps `"applied": True`.
findings.userImpact: The one path that combines custom source weights with the league-adjusted lens — the most novel board the server can produce, and therefore the most likely to be incoherent — is the only path with no coherence check. A board whose displayed ranks contradict its displayed values ships to /rankings with no warning, exactly the state overlay.py refuses to serve.
findings.recommendedFix: Have `apply_valuation_factors` call `assert_ranking_coherence` and return a sentinel the caller can degrade on, or delete it and route the overrides path through `src.league_intel.overlay.adjusted_rows`. Then correct publish.py:186-191, which currently tells a reader there is only one implementation.

findings.title: The server-side adjusted contract scales only rankDerivedValue, leaving offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue and values.* at market — suggestions.py mixes both scales in one comparison
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/overlay.py:88-95 scales exactly one field: `copy["rankDerivedValue"] = int(round(base * factor))`. The client-side applier does more — frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1911-1917 also scales `values.overall|finalAdjusted|displayValue` and :1946 `_finalAdjusted`. Meanwhile src/trade/suggestions.py:626-643 reads `row["offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue"]` into `offense_only_value`, and :765-769 `_eff_val` returns that unscaled number for offensive positions while returning the SCALED `display_value` for IDP positions (:1089-1099, :1251-1294 pass `pos_oo = pos not in _IDP_BASE_POSITIONS`). On the live contract 607 of 1092 rows carry a positive `offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue`.
findings.userImpact: CLAUDE.md's central justification for the whole overlay design — "every engine reads exactly one value — rankDerivedValue" — is false. Under `valuationMode=leagueAdjusted`, the upgrade and depth searches in trade suggestions compare adjusted IDP values against unadjusted offense values, a scale mismatch of up to 5.3% that silently biases which upgrades and sweeteners are proposed.
findings.recommendedFix: Have `overlay.adjusted_rows` scale every value alias the client scales — `values.overall/finalAdjusted/displayValue`, `offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue` — or make `_eff_val` refuse the offense-only field when the contract carries a leagueAdjusted stamp. Add a test that asserts client and server appliers write the same key set.

findings.title: The rankings overlay is unreachable for the non-default league while the engines still serve it — two boards in one session, the exact failure the feature exists to remove
findings.evidence: server.py:5361-5374 (`GET /api/valuation/league-adjusted`) returns 503 `data_not_ready` whenever `latest_contract_data.meta.leagueKey != league_cfg.key`. But `/api/terminal` (server.py:10332) and `/api/trade/simulate` (server.py:10582) deliberately resolve WITHOUT `require_loaded_contract=True` and then call `_valuation_scoped_contract` (server.py:10443, :10653), which computes factors from the requested league's own rosters and serves an adjusted board. The client swallows the 503 silently: frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1822-1830 logs a console warning and returns null.
findings.userImpact: On a single-instance deployment holding dynasty_main's contract, a dynasty_new user with the toggle ON sees a market-priced /rankings page (silently, no banner) and a league-adjusted terminal and trade simulator. That is precisely the split-board confusion documented in src/league_intel/overlay.py:12-15 as the reason this feature was built.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the overlay route match the engines: serve factors for any league whose scoring profile matches the loaded contract, since factors are derived from the requested league's rosters and applied to a scoring-profile-scoped board. Alternatively make the engines 503 too. Either way, surface the degradation in the UI instead of a console warning.

findings.title: reference_lineup_scarcity = 0.5 and sensitivity = 0.20 are hand-picked defaults that are never overridden, never configured, and never calibrated
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/adjustment.py:215-216 `reference_lineup_scarcity: float = 0.5, sensitivity: float = 0.20`; :247 `delta = (value - reference_lineup_scarcity) * sensitivity`. `build_board_adjustments` calls `structural_scarcity_axis(position, pos_scarcity)` at adjustment.py:764 with no keyword arguments, so the defaults always apply. Grepping src/, scripts/ and config/ for `reference_lineup_scarcity` or `sensitivity=` returns only these three lines in adjustment.py — no config file, no calibration script, no test that varies them. Live dynasty_main lineupScarcity values are 0.4392–0.7667, i.e. only kickers sit below the 0.5 reference; seven of eight positions get a lift.
findings.userImpact: Because the reference is below the observed distribution and picks are exempt, the axis has a net LEVEL effect rather than a purely relative one: I measured +2.52% on offense value, +3.28% on IDP value, +0.00% on picks across the live 1092-row board. That systematic player-over-pick inflation is an artifact of picking 0.5, not a measurement. `sensitivity = 0.20` is the sole scale factor on the only live cross-position axis and rests on nothing.
findings.recommendedFix: Center the reference on the measured cross-position distribution (e.g. the value-weighted mean lineupScarcity) so the axis is purely relative and cannot drift the player/pick level, and record the choice. Calibrate or at least bound `sensitivity` against the backtest harness in scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py rather than leaving it as a bare literal.

findings.title: The backtest's paired bootstrap resamples players, but the across-position claim has 8 degrees of freedom — the reported power is overstated for the scalars
findings.evidence: src/model_registry/board_holdout.py:156-172 `paired_bootstrap` draws `idx = [rng.randrange(n) for _ in range(n)]` over the 572-player population. docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md:165-168 concludes "the CI half-width is about 0.009 ρ, so this design detects a difference of roughly ±0.015". But the artifact's own `factorShape` (docs/measurements/adjusted-board-backtest-2026-07-28.json) shows DB/DL/LB/QB/K each receive ONE scalar, so the entire cross-position signal is 8 numbers. Resampling players i.i.d. treats each of 572 rows as independent evidence about those 8 scalars. The bootstrap also holds the factors fixed and therefore carries no uncertainty from the 12-roster scarcity measurement that produced them.
findings.userImpact: The doc's headline power claim is only valid for the within-position (reception fit) arm. For the positional-scalar arm — which is the arm every trade valuation depends on, and the arm three of four framings lean negative on — the true interval is wider than reported, so "a null here is a real null at the effect sizes the current axes produce" is not established for the scalars.
findings.recommendedFix: Bootstrap positions (or use a block/cluster bootstrap over position) for the across-position framings, and report the two arms' intervals separately. Add a factor-uncertainty arm by resampling rosters before recomputing scarcity.

findings.title: cross_market.py's module docstring states it has zero production importers; three production modules import it
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/cross_market.py:11-17: "The honest count of production importers of THIS file is **zero**. ``value_package`` / ``compare_packages`` are consumed only by ``tests/league_intel/test_cross_market.py``. ``src/trade/angle.py`` is the intended call site and is **not rewired yet**". Actual importers: src/trade/angle.py:78 `from src.league_intel.cross_market import (...)`, src/roster_intel/packages.py:77 same, src/api/gameplan.py:128 `from src.league_intel.cross_market import DEFAULT_GATE_PCT`.
findings.userImpact: The docstring explicitly instructs an auditor that a behaviour change here "cannot reach a user today". It can — it reaches the angle finder and the roster-intel package generator. A maintainer trusting this comment could change the cross-market normalization or `DEFAULT_GATE_PCT` believing it is inert.
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite the docstring's call-site section to list the three live importers, or add a test that fails when the set of production importers changes.

findings.title: compact_ranks_and_tiers documents that the overlay path "must pass copy_rows=True"; the overlay passes False
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:2088-2092: "``copy_rows``: shallow-copy before mutating. **The overlay path must pass True.** ``latest_contract_data`` is a shared module global". src/league_intel/overlay.py:114-118 calls it with `copy_rows=False`. The overlay is correct — it already made its own copies at overlay.py:89 (`copy = dict(row)`), and overlay.py:100-113 explains at length why it must not copy a second time (a second copy would make it return only the 740 ranked rows out of 1093). But the argument documentation now directly contradicts the only caller it names.
findings.userImpact: A maintainer following the parameter documentation would 'fix' the overlay to pass True, which silently drops every 2026 pick and 240 unpriced players from the adjusted board handed to the trade engines — the exact regression overlay.py:100-109 records having already happened once.
findings.recommendedFix: Reword the `copy_rows` doc to state the actual rule: pass True iff the caller does not already own the rows; the overlay owns copies and therefore passes False.

findings.title: configVersion stamped on every overlay payload is a constant shape version, not a provenance stamp for the league rules
findings.evidence: src/api/gameplan.py:1317-1325 sets `config_version = load_canonical_config().config_version`, and src/league_intel/config.py:36 `CONFIG_VERSION = 1` with the docstring "Version of the canonical-config *shape* produced by this module. Bump when the dataclass contract below changes incompatibly." src/league_intel/config.py:211 always assigns `config_version=CONFIG_VERSION`. The actual provenance — `sourced_at` (2026-07-26, from config/league_intel/sleeper_league_snapshot_2026-07-26.json) — is not carried into the payload. src/league_intel/values.py:206-210 claims the stamp exists "so a stored value can always be traced to the rules and data that produced it". It cannot. Additionally, `load_canonical_config()` reads the dynasty_main snapshot regardless of which league is being adjusted.
findings.userImpact: A stored league-adjusted value cannot be traced to the league rules that produced it. If the commissioner changes scoring or roster slots and a new snapshot lands, `configVersion` stays 1 and nothing in the payload changes.
findings.recommendedFix: Stamp `sourced_at` (or a content hash of the snapshot) alongside `configVersion`, and resolve the snapshot per league instead of always reading the newest file in config/league_intel/.

findings.title: The te_premium_curve.json ceiling is now below the observed maximum in today's own source CSVs
findings.evidence: config/weights/te_premium_curve.json `observed_ratio_range: [1.2092, 2.0531]`, `measured_at: 2026-07-27`, consumed as the hard ceiling at src/league_intel/te_premium.py:309-317 and :352 `min(ceiling, max(floor, 1 + a*v**-k))`. Re-deriving from today's CSVs/site_raw/ktc.csv vs ktcSfTep.csv (both mtime 2026-08-04 06:56, 74 paired TE rows) gives an observed ratio range of 1.2092–2.0823, with Harrison Bryant at 2.0823 and Adam Trautman at 2.0753 above the stored ceiling. Curve-vs-observed relative error today: median 0.0162, p90 0.0267, max 0.0959.
findings.userImpact: Deep tight ends from non-TEP sources are clipped ~1.4% below the uplift KTC currently applies. Small, but the ceiling is described in te_premium.py:93-100 as "the largest uplift KTC actually applies" and it no longer is.
findings.recommendedFix: Re-run scripts/audit/fit_ktc_tep_curve.py --write-config on a cadence (the KTC CSVs refresh every 2h) or add a staleness check that warns when the live observed range exits the stored one.

findings.title: data_contract.py's source registry comments repeatedly claim the frontend applies the TE premium; no frontend code does
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py carries ~10 comments of the form "the frontend ``settings.tepMultiplier`` boost applies to its blended contribution" (lines 361, 394, 1101, 1272, 1300, 1325, 1354, 1385, 1415, 1447, 1538). Grepping frontend/lib and frontend/components for a client-side TE multiply finds none: frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:2043 only does `body.tep_multiplier = tepMultiplier`, a pass-through to POST /api/rankings/overrides. The multiplier is applied entirely server-side at data_contract.py:7192-7215.
findings.userImpact: The comments describe a legacy client-side boost that no longer exists, inviting a reader to believe the TE premium is applied twice (once in the blend, once in the UI) or to look for a frontend knob that isn't there.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace "the frontend settings.tepMultiplier boost applies" with "the operator's /settings TE-premium slider reaches this source's contribution via tep_multiplier on POST /api/rankings/overrides".

findings.title: calibration.py and twin.py have no production consumer — 876 lines of test-only code inside a live package
findings.evidence: src/league_intel/calibration.py (622 lines) is imported only by tests/league_intel/test_calibration.py; src/league_intel/twin.py (254 lines) only by tests/league_intel/test_twin.py. No file under src/, server.py or scripts/ references either. calibration.py:1-28 describes the paired-board TE measurement that src/league_intel/adjustment.py:371-381 says is "in flight" and will decide the tePremium axis — it has been implemented and never wired. Separately, src/league_intel/sim_calibration.py writes `data/league_intel/sim_points_model.json`; that directory does not exist on disk, so src/ros/playoff_sim.py runs on its documented legacy fallback constants.
findings.userImpact: The TE calibration that ADR-009 says is the blocker for resolving the tePremium axis already exists and is unused, so the 'open question' recorded in adjustment.py:514-517 and publish.py:45-70 is stale. The sim points model is a documented capability with no artifact behind it.
findings.recommendedFix: Either wire `calibration.measure_paired_te_premium` into the tePremium axis (its output is exactly the `measurement` mapping `te_premium_axis` accepts at adjustment.py:397-405) or mark both modules explicitly as not-yet-wired in their docstrings. Generate or remove the sim points model.

formulas.name: structuralScarcity adjustment factor
formulas.expression:
factor = 1.0 + (lineupScarcity[pos] - reference_lineup_scarcity) * sensitivity
       = 1.0 + (lineupScarcity[pos] - 0.5) * 0.20
Range over lineupScarcity in [0,1]: [0.90, 1.10]
formulas.inputs: lineupScarcity[pos] — dimensionless 0-1 from src/league_intel/replacement.py:655, measured off this league's 12 rosters. reference_lineup_scarcity and sensitivity — hardcoded keyword defaults, never passed by build_board_adjustments (adjustment.py:764).
formulas.constants: reference_lineup_scarcity = 0.5 (adjustment.py:215) — hand-picked, no calibration anywhere in src/, scripts/ or config/. sensitivity = 0.20 (adjustment.py:216) — same. Both are the only scale on the sole live cross-position axis.
formulas.outputRange: [0.90, 1.10] in principle; live dynasty_main 0.98784 (K) to 1.05334 (DL); live dynasty_new 0.97314 (TE) to 1.01741 (WR)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: lineupScarcity absent or non-numeric → AdjustmentAxis(tier=ABSENT, factor=1.0); `effective_factor` forces 1.0 regardless (adjustment.py:143-146). No prior is substituted. Positions absent from the scarcity map (PICK, '?', 'T' — 161 live rows) get ABSENT.
formulas.validated: Backtested once: docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md / docs/measurements/adjusted-board-backtest-2026-07-28.json. All four framings return NO DIFFERENCE DETECTED; three of four point estimates negative; full board win rate 0.043. No calibration of the two constants exists.
formulas.mathIssues: Reference 0.5 sits below the entire live positional distribution except K, so the axis produces a NET LEVEL SHIFT rather than a purely relative reprice. Measured on the live 1092-row board: value-weighted offense ratio 1.0252, IDP 1.0328, picks 1.0000 — picks are exempt, so the level shift is a real 2.5-3.3% player-over-pick reprice driven by an arbitrary constant. Worked example: DL top rosValue 60.41, starter level 14.095 → lineupScarcity 0.7667 → factor 1.05334 → a DL at rankDerivedValue 5000 becomes 5267; TE (0.5577 → 1.011533) at 5000 becomes 5058; DL/TE relative reprice +4.13%.

formulas.name: lineupScarcity
formulas.expression:
lineupScarcity[pos] = _safe_drop(top, starter)
                    = clamp(1 - starter_level / top_rosValue, 0, 1)
where top_rosValue = max rosValue among rostered players at pos
      starter_level = median over teams of (min rosValue among that team's started players at pos)
formulas.inputs: rosValue from data/ros/team_strength/{latest,dynasty_new}.json fullRoster entries. Per src/ros/aggregate.py:171-173 rosValue is a normalized LOG-RANK index on 0-100, NOT points: rank_to_score(r,N) = 100*(ln(N+1)-ln r)/ln(N+1) (src/ros/parse.py:43-46).
formulas.constants: None in this formula; DEFAULT_BAND = 2 (replacement.py:84-86) smooths the rank-indexed roster/waiver tiers but the starter tier is smoothed by cross-team median instead.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: top is None or <= 0 → None (no lift). Unpriced players (rosValue <= 0) are excluded from every pool (replacement.py:388-390, 412, 632) so they cannot drag the floor to zero; they still count in rostered_count.
formulas.validated: Not validated. The only outcome test is the board backtest above, which tests the composed factor, not this quantity.
formulas.mathIssues: A ratio on an index whose zero point is 'rank N of the ROS universe' — not a ratio scale. I re-scored the identical player ranks under N=2000 and N=500 and every factor moved: DB/TE/LB flip lift↔trim (see findings). Also measures top-heaviness (steepness) rather than scarcity of bodies, then applies the result uniformly to every player at the position including the marginal starter.

formulas.name: Replacement level — starter tier
formulas.expression:
marginals[pos] = sorted( min(rosValue over that team's started players at pos) for each team, if > 0 )
starter_level[pos] = median(marginals[pos])
formulas.inputs: EndogenousStarters.marginal_starter_values from measure_endogenous_starters (replacement.py:316-317), i.e. what the exact optimizer actually started per roster.
formulas.constants: None. Smoothing is the cross-team median, not a rank band.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty marginals → no 'starter' or 'bestBallStarter' level at all → lineupScarcity None → ABSENT axis.
formulas.validated: Endogenous flex allocation is verified against the exact optimizer, which is itself golden-tested (tests/league_intel/test_lineup_exactness.py). The KNOWN LIMITATION is stated in the module docstring (replacement.py:21-42) and reproduced by me: optimizing on rosValue means (a season-long index) yields FLEX TE share 0.0% and TE started/team 2.00, against 10.4% and 2.215 on real 2025 weekly actuals (scripts/measure_te_demand_actuals.py, 158 team-weeks).
formulas.mathIssues: Flex-aware and format-aware in the sense that matters — starters are ENDOGENOUS, not a fixed rank cutoff. But it is attributed by the player's NOMINAL position, not by slot (replacement.py:310-315), so live starters_per_team reads DL 2.667 / LB 3.250 / DB 3.083 while slot_fill is exactly 36/36/36. The comment justifies this and it is internally consistent with the pool keying.

formulas.name: Replacement level — bestBallStarter / roster / waiver tiers
formulas.expression:
bestBallStarter = mean(marginals[0 : max(1, band)])   # the k lowest marginals
roster          = _banded_value(pool, rank=len(pool), band=2)  # mean of pool[N-2 .. N]
waiver          = _banded_value(fa_pool, rank=1, band=2)       # mean of best 3 free agents
_banded_value(v, r, b) = mean(v[max(1,r-b)-1 : min(n,r+b)])
formulas.inputs: pool = rostered rosValues at pos, sorted desc; fa_pool = unrostered rosValues; marginals as above.
formulas.constants: DEFAULT_BAND = 2 (replacement.py:84-86) — half-width of the smoothing window, hand-chosen, no calibration.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty fa_pool → no 'waiver' level → waiverScarcity None. `compute_replacement_levels` is never called with free_agents from the live gameplan path (src/api/gameplan.py:487 passes only teams and slots), so the waiver tier and therefore waiverScarcity and replacementGap are ALWAYS None in production.
formulas.validated: None found.
formulas.mathIssues: Because free_agents is never supplied live, two of the six ScarcityComponents fields (waiverScarcity, replacementGap) are structurally null on every real request. Nothing in the payload distinguishes 'unmeasurable' from 'measured zero'.

formulas.name: Remaining scarcity components
formulas.expression:
starters_n      = max(1, round(starters_per_team * max(1, n_teams)))
median_starter  = median(pool[:starters_n])
elite           = pool[max(0, round(len(pool)*0.05) - 1)]
rosterScarcity  = clamp(1 - roster_level / starter_level, 0, 1)
waiverScarcity  = clamp(1 - waiver / bestBallStarter, 0, 1)
eliteSeparation = elite - median_starter
starterSeparation = median_starter - starter_level
replacementGap  = bestBallStarter - waiver
formulas.inputs: PositionReplacement levels + the rostered rosValue pool.
formulas.constants: 0.05 elite quantile (replacement.py:651) — hardcoded, undocumented rationale.
formulas.outputRange: The three *Scarcity fields are 0-1; the three separation/gap fields are raw rosValue units.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Any None operand yields None for that field; _safe_drop returns None when top is None or <= 0.
formulas.validated: None found.
formulas.mathIssues: Only lineupScarcity reaches the live adjustment (adjustment.py:231-237). The other five are computed on every request, serialized into the overlay payload's `scarcity` block (publish.py:235), and consumed by nothing that prices an asset. Two of them are always None (see above).

formulas.name: Endogenous starters per team
formulas.expression:
for each team: solution = optimize_lineup(roster, starter_slots)
counts[base_pos(player)] += 1 for each started row
starters_per_team[pos] = counts[pos] / n_teams
marginal_starter_values[pos] += [min(rosValue among that team's started pos players)]
formulas.inputs: team fullRoster rows (playerId, position, rosValue, fantasyPositions, injured, bye) and the league's flattened starter slots from config/leagues/registry.json via src/ros/lineup.py:167-185.
formulas.constants: Injury/bye multipliers inside the optimizer: injured ×0.4, bye ×0.0 (src/ros/lineup.py:214-221).
formulas.outputRange: Live dynasty_main (21 slots): QB 1.833, RB 2.750, WR 4.417, TE 2.000, K 0.917, DL 2.667, LB 3.250, DB 3.083. Live dynasty_new (10 slots): QB 2.000, RB 2.500, WR 4.400, TE 1.100.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Team with no players is skipped and does not count toward n_teams. A started player with rosValue 0 is excluded from the marginals pool at replacement.py:412 (otherwise bestBallStarter collapses to 0).
formulas.validated: The optimizer is exact and golden-tested against real Sleeper best-ball weeks (tests/league_intel/test_lineup_exactness.py). The measurement's known bias is quantified against 2025 weekly actuals by scripts/measure_te_demand_actuals.py — I reran it: OLD 1-TE 1.608 TE started/team, NEW 2-TE 2.215, ratio 1.378; FLEX TE share 27.2% vs 10.4%.
formulas.mathIssues: Point-estimate optimization on a season-long mean systematically understates flex demand for high-variance positions. This IS flex-aware and format-aware (it solves the real slot vector), not a fixed rank cutoff.

formulas.name: Combined adjustment + magnitude cap
formulas.expression:
combined = PROD over axes of axis.effective_factor
         where effective_factor = 1.0 if tier is ABSENT else factor
capped   = clamp(combined, 1 - 0.25, 1 + 0.25)
adjusted = consensus_value * capped
formulas.inputs: consensus_value = row['rankDerivedValue'] via src/league_intel/values.py:166-183. Axes: structuralScarcity, tePremium (TE rows only), scoringFit, receptionFit, projectionCorroboration (adjustment.py:763-779).
formulas.constants: MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT = 0.25 (adjustment.py:73) — explicitly not a claim that 25% is right, only that beyond it is more likely a bug.
formulas.outputRange: [0.75, 1.25] × consensus. Live structural-only: [0.9878, 1.0533]. Production with scoringFit + receptionFit (docs/measurements/adjusted-board-backtest-2026-07-28.json): [0.7986, 1.1273] — RB min 0.7986 is only 0.049 above the cap.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: consensus_value None or <= 0 → adjustment not attempted, league_adjusted_value = consensus, guardrail + open_item recorded (adjustment.py:429-432). All axes ABSENT → factor 1.0, confidence 0.0, evidence_tier ABSENT.
formulas.validated: Cap never binds on the structural-only path. On the production path the RB minimum approaches it.
formulas.mathIssues: None found in the arithmetic. The cap is applied to the PRODUCT, so three axes each within their own MAX_TILT can still be clipped together — which is the intent.

formulas.name: Publish factor (the wire value)
formulas.expression:
factor[name] = round(league_adjusted_value / consensus_value, 6)
emitted only when |adjusted - consensus| / consensus >= _MIN_RELATIVE_MOVE (0.001)
formulas.inputs: AdjustmentExplanation.consensus_value / .league_adjusted_value per row.
formulas.constants: _MIN_RELATIVE_MOVE = 0.001 (publish.py:93).
formulas.outputRange: Live: 8 distinct values, 0.987838 to 1.053336, 931 of 1092 rows moved; picks 0 of 144.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: consensus falsy / <= 0, or adjusted None → row omitted from factors entirely; absence means 'unchanged' by contract.
formulas.validated: tests/league_intel/test_publish.py:76-88 asserts factors are ratios in (0.5, 1.5), that same-position rows share a factor (with reception fit absent), and that scarce lifts / deep trims. tests/api/test_league_adjusted_endpoint.py:313-368 repeats these end-to-end.
formulas.mathIssues: Keyed by displayName only (publish.py:106-107, overlay.py:50-58). No duplicate displayNames on the live board (I checked: 0 of 1092), so no collision today, but a duplicate would silently give both rows the last-written factor.

formulas.name: Overlay application (server-side engine path)
formulas.inputs: contract['playersArray'] rows + the sparse factors map.
formulas.constants: None.
formulas.outputRange: Returns the FULL row list (all 1092), not the ranked subset — deliberate, per overlay.py:100-113. Live rank movement: median |Δrank| 4, p90 17, max 53 over 740 ranked rows.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty rows, empty/None factors, or zero rows moved → returns None, and the caller (server.py:6705-6707) serves the market board with note 'league_adjusted_unavailable: no_op'. Incoherent board → None + a WARNING log.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_valuation_mode_threading.py statically requires every handler calling _valuation_scoped_contract to also call _stamp_valuation_mode, and pins that latest_contract_data is never mutated.
formulas.mathIssues: Scales ONLY rankDerivedValue. values.overall / values.finalAdjusted / values.displayValue and offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue (607 live rows) stay at market — the client applier scales the first three (frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1911-1917, :1946) and the server does not. See findings.

formulas.name: KTC TE++ uplift curve (Axis A)
formulas.expression:
ratio(v) = min(ceiling, max(floor, 1 + a * v^(-k)))
         = min(2.0531, max(1.209206, 1 + 43.555794 * v^(-0.632839)))
convert_te_value(v, base->tepp) = v * ratio(v)
convert_te_value(v, tepp->base) = bisection over [v/3, v] solving m*ratio(m) = v (60 iterations)
formulas.inputs: v = the source's TE contribution on the 0-9999 scale at src/api/data_contract.py:7198 — for rank-signal sources this is the Hill-curve output, NOT that source's published TE value.
formulas.constants: a = 43.555794, k = 0.632839, floor = 1.209206, ceiling = observed_ratio_range[1] = 2.0531. Fitted from 73 paired KTC base/TE++ rows, R² 0.9411 in log space, measured_at 2026-07-27. Duplicated as fallbacks at te_premium.py:85-100. NOT hand-picked — genuinely measured, and the config carries an explicit _limitation note about cross-board application.
formulas.outputRange: Uplift 1.2092–2.0531. Floor binds above v = 4609.0; ceiling binds below v = 358.5 (I solved both). Worked examples: v=1000 → 1.5502 → 1550.2; v=2000 → 1.3548 → 2709.7; v=4611 → 1.2092 → 5575.6; v=9999 → 1.2092 → 12090.9 (clamped to 9999 at the call site).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: v None or <= 0 → returns min(ceiling, max(1.0, floor)) = 1.2092, i.e. an unpriced TE would still be 'lifted' — harmless only because the call site guards on the value. Config unreadable/invalid → falls back to the same measured constants (te_premium.py:302-320). Feature-flag import failure → falls back to the flat 1.15 with a WARNING (data_contract.py:6470-6479).
formulas.validated: I re-derived it against today's CSVs/site_raw/ktc.csv vs ktcSfTep.csv (74 paired rows, mtime 2026-08-04): observed ratio min 1.2092 / median 1.3205 / max 2.0823; curve-vs-observed relative error median 0.0162, p90 0.0267, max 0.0959. Round-trip base→tepp→base is exact to 1e-4. tests/api/test_te_basis_conversion.py and tests/league_intel/test_fitted_curve_bounds.py exist.
formulas.mathIssues: (1) Today's observed max 2.0823 EXCEEDS the stored ceiling 2.0531, so the clamp now clips real observations. (2) The curve is parameterised on KTC BASE-board value but evaluated on the Hill output of an arbitrary source — an unvalidated cross-board scale assumption, disclosed in the config's _limitation but not in CLAUDE.md. (3) Live effect is large: A/B on the 2026-08-04 export gives a median TE value ratio of 1.1672 (range 1.007–1.2708) and a median TE rank gain of 50 slots (max 202).

formulas.name: TE demand → target basis (Axis B)
formulas.expression:
required = count of mandatory TE starters (roster_positions or rosterSettings.starters.TE)
basis = first candidate where required >= threshold, over ((3,'teppp'), (2,'tepp'), (1,'base'))
if any scoring edge > 0: basis = TE_BASES[index(basis) + 1]   # scoring can only RAISE
edge[key] = scoring[te_key] - max(scoring[wr_key], scoring[rb_key])
formulas.inputs: config/leagues/registry.json rosterSettings, or a Sleeper league dict; optional scoring_settings.
formulas.constants: _REQUIRED_TE_TO_BASIS (te_premium.py:119-123) — explicitly labelled an operator-supplied domain assumption, not a repo measurement. _TE_EDGE_KEYS = bonus_rec_te and bonus_fd_te vs their WR/RB equivalents (:133-136).
formulas.outputRange: One of ('base','tep','tepp','teppp'). I measured live: dynasty_main → 'tepp' (2 mandatory TEs, edges all 0.0); dynasty_new → 'base' (1 mandatory TE).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Neither roster nor scoring supplied → measured=False, target_basis='base' (which applies no adjustment) with an explicit reason string.
formulas.validated: tests/league_intel/test_te_premium_measurement.py exists.
formulas.mathIssues: Implemented and correct, but NOT WIRED. src/api/data_contract.py:5681 hardcodes `_BOARD_TE_BASIS = 'tepp'` for every league, and the corrective overlay axis is deliberately ABSENT (adjustment.py:371-396, publish.py:45-70). dynasty_new therefore carries a two-TE premium it measurably does not want.

formulas.name: Blend-time TE multipliers (the fallback / native path)
formulas.inputs: Per-source per-row Hill or value-direct output.
formulas.constants: _TE_BLANKET_NON_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER = 1.15 (:5635) — retained as the fallback and slider default; the constant's own comment (:5622-5634) records that the 2026 league grants NO TE scoring premium (measured TE 21.55 vs WR 21.55) and that it is left at 1.15 anyway as a product decision. _TE_BLANKET_NATIVE_MULTIPLIER = 1.10 (:5636) — hardcoded, no measurement cited. Slider clamped to [1.0, 1.5].
formulas.missingDataBehavior: An explicit operator tep_multiplier bypasses the curve entirely (data_contract.py:6452). Feature flag te_basis_conversion=False or import failure → flat 1.15 with a WARNING.
formulas.validated: tests/api/test_te_basis_conversion.py. The 1.10 native multiplier has no cited measurement anywhere I found.
formulas.mathIssues: Double-count guard is structural and holds: KTC exempt by set membership; convert_te_value is a no-op when from==to and refuses unmeasured basis pairs by raising. The two branches are mutually exclusive. No frontend re-application exists (I verified there is no client-side TE multiply).

formulas.name: scoringFit multiplier (IDP positional)
formulas.expression:
raw_ratio[pos]  = median over cohort of (points under MY card / points under BASELINE card)
normalised[pos] = raw_ratio[pos] / mean(raw_ratio over tracked positions)
multiplier[pos] = clamp(normalised, 1 - 0.25, 1 + 0.25)
formulas.inputs: nflverse weekly defensive rows for the max season in config/league_comparison.json, scored under two Sleeper scoring cards fetched live.
formulas.constants: MAX_TILT = 0.25 (scoring_fit.py:208). Depth-stability gate and cohort minimums in the same module.
formulas.outputRange: Documented live values (scoring_fit.py:60-66): DB 0.9971 (raw 1.1979, n=295), DL 1.0421 (raw 1.2519, n=221), LB 0.9608 (raw 1.1542, n=208).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Flag off, config missing, fetch failure, or an untrusted per-position entry → None or an untrusted PositionFit → ABSENT axis, factor 1.0 (adjustment.py:278-297). Never raises (gameplan.py:1280-1284).
formulas.validated: Mean-normalisation is deliberate: the shared level is discarded as a rate-card-generosity artifact. The module documents a prior SHIPPED measurement that was BACKWARDS (DB highest) because of a partially-corrected scoring card, and records the correction. That is a real validation history.
formulas.mathIssues: Measured against the league at config/league_comparison.json my_league.id = owner-6e67d300493f, which is NOT in the registry — see findings. The measurement ignores the league_key it is cached under.

formulas.name: receptionFit multiplier (per-player)
formulas.expression:
per_catch_ratio[p] = per_catch_value(bands[p], MY card) / per_catch_value(bands[p], BASELINE card)
raw[p]             = 1 + reception_share[p] * (per_catch_ratio[p] - 1)
level              = median(raw over population)
multiplier[p]      = clamp(raw[p] / level, 1 - 0.35, 1 + 0.35)
formulas.inputs: Season reception band histograms from data/nfl_data/actuals/reception_depth_{season}.jsonl keyed by GSIS id; reception_share computed by scoring each player twice under the baseline card with and without reception keys (gameplan.py:1193-1206). Joined to displayName via resolve_canonical_name at gameplan.py:1215-1219.
formulas.constants: MIN_RECEPTIONS = 20 (reception_fit.py:134). MAX_TILT = 0.35 (:137), widened from 0.25 when the level was split out. Measured reception shares: RB 0.166, WR 0.304, TE 0.330 (:20-22).
formulas.outputRange: [0.65, 1.35]. Production observed (docs/measurements/adjusted-board-backtest-2026-07-28.json): RB 0.7986–1.0664 (45 distinct), TE 0.8873–1.0591 (49), WR 0.9099–1.1273 (96).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Flag off, missing depth file, fewer than 10 measured players, degenerate level, or an untrusted measurement → None → ABSENT axis. A player with no measured band shape gets an ABSENT axis with an explicit reason (adjustment.py:346-355). If every GSIS id fails to resolve to a name, gameplan.py:1220-1228 logs and returns None rather than an empty map.
formulas.validated: Genuinely well-validated for a repo of this kind: dispersion is flat across pool depth (1.072/1.078/1.069/1.087/1.106 at top24/36/60/120/200) versus the IDP per-player attempt which fans out, and the level is deliberately NOT applied because it swings 2x on an unestablished market-rate assumption (reception_fit.py:64-96).
formulas.mathIssues: This is the axis that makes 'the factor is a function of position alone' false. In THIS checkout it is inert: data/nfl_data/actuals/ does not exist, so load_reception_depth returns None.

formulas.name: Confidence / evidence tier
formulas.expression:
applied = [axis for axis in axes if tier != ABSENT and factor != 1.0]
if not applied: tier = ABSENT, confidence = 0.0
else: weakest = argmin over applied of tier ordinal; confidence = TIER_CONFIDENCE[weakest.tier]
if any axis is PROJECTION_CORROBORATED and applied: confidence = max(confidence, 0.90)
formulas.inputs: The axis list for the row.
formulas.constants: ABSENT 0.0, STRUCTURAL_ONLY 0.45, MARKET_MEASURED 0.70, SCORING_MEASURED 0.70, PROJECTION_CORROBORATED 0.90 (adjustment.py:118-124). All hand-assigned priors; no calibration exists.
formulas.outputRange: {0.0, 0.45, 0.70, 0.90}. Live structural-only: 0.45 for every moved row.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No applied axis → 0.0 with the guardrail 'no axis applied; league-adjusted == consensus'.
formulas.validated: tests/league_intel/test_adjustment.py:197-247 pins that uncorroborated is the default, that the weakest applied axis governs, and that PROJECTION_CORROBORATED is unreachable in practice.
formulas.mathIssues: The confidence numbers are not exposed on the /api/valuation/league-adjusted payload unless ?explanations=1 is requested (publish.py:246-247), so the default surface carries a value with no confidence beside it.

formulas.name: Monotonicity guard
formulas.expression:
for each position, sort by consensus desc; for every pair (i<j) with consensus_i > consensus_j,
flag a violation when adjusted_i < adjusted_j
formulas.inputs: (name, consensus, adjusted) triples grouped by position (adjustment.py:790-797).
formulas.constants: None.
formulas.outputRange: List of MonotonicityViolation; live count 0 on the 1092-row board (structural-only). The 2026-07-28 production run also reported 0.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Rows without a consensus value are never added to the by_position map, so they cannot be checked.
formulas.validated: tests/league_intel/test_adjustment.py:101-129 asserts a uniform factor preserves order, a player-specific reordering is caught, and ties impose no ordering.
formulas.mathIssues: O(n²) per position — 216 WR rows is 23k comparisons per request, and it runs on every overlay build. Not a correctness issue. Note it only fires when a per-player axis is live, i.e. when reception fit is available.

formulas.name: Backtest scoring — Spearman + paired bootstrap
formulas.expression:
market_rho   = spearman(market_values, actual)
adjusted_rho = spearman(market_values * factor, actual)
delta        = adjusted_rho - market_rho
bootstrap (2000 iterations, seed 20260728, PAIRED index set):
  d_b = spearman(adjusted[idx], actual[idx]) - spearman(market[idx], actual[idx])
  win_rate = share of d_b > 0;  ci = [2.5th, 97.5th percentile of d_b]
verdict: movers < 15 -> INCONCLUSIVE; ci_low > 0 -> ADJUSTED WINS; ci_high < 0 -> MARKET WINS; else NO DIFFERENCE
formulas.inputs: scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py: board = build_api_data_contract(exports/latest/dynasty_data_*.json); factors = gameplan.get_league_adjusted_values(default league); target = compute_player_season_scores(REG-only nflverse weekly rows, this league's exact Sleeper scoring) PLUS the per-band reception add-on from data/nfl_data/actuals/reception_depth_{season}.jsonl.
formulas.constants: FOCUS_TOP_N = 300 (backtest script:77). min_players = 30, iterations 2000, seed 20260728. replacement_baselines uses starters × teamCount with FLEX/SFLEX deliberately unallocated (script:222-241).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: factors empty → exit 2 with 'compares a board against itself'. Fewer than 30 joined → 'too few joined players'. Missing reception_depth file → banded add-on silently 0, but bandedPlayers is printed so it shows in the run log.
formulas.validated: The doc's four-row table reproduces the JSON artifact exactly. The over-replacement target deliberately never calls src/league_intel/replacement (pinned by tests/scripts/test_backtest_adjusted_board.py::test_the_baseline_never_consults_the_module_under_test), which is the right call — the module under test must not grade its own paper.
formulas.mathIssues: NO TEMPORAL SPLIT: a current (2026-08) board is scored against completed 2025 outcomes. The doc's common-mode defence (board_holdout.py:21-30) is reasonable for the DIFFERENCE but lookahead still inflates both ρ toward a ceiling and compresses the detectable gap — the doc does not mention that compression. More seriously, the paired bootstrap resamples 572 players i.i.d. while the across-position claim has only 8 free parameters, so the stated ±0.015 power applies to the within-position arm only. Baselines are computed from the joined population rather than the full realized pool, so a position's baseline shifts with the board's own coverage. Verdict itself is honestly reported and the doc's conclusion ('keep it a toggle') is SUPPORTED by its own numbers.

formulas.name: Client-side overlay application
formulas.expression:
if base.scrapeTimestamp !== overlay.scrapeTimestamp: refuse, serve market
row.rankDerivedValue     = round(rankDerivedValue * factor)
row.values.{overall, finalAdjusted, displayValue} = round(v * factor)
row.canonicalConsensusRank = overlay.ranks[name]  (or null when the row moved but is unranked)
row.rankChange = null
legacy dict: _finalAdjusted scaled, _canonicalConsensusRank / _canonicalTierId set
formulas.inputs: GET /api/valuation/league-adjusted payload + the cached base contract.
formulas.constants: None.
formulas.outputRange: Copy-on-write; untouched rows returned by reference.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Non-OK response, isNoop, empty factors, or a scrape-stamp mismatch → returns the base contract unchanged, with only a console.warn. No user-visible indication.
formulas.validated: frontend/__tests__/valuation-overlay.test.js covers both materializer key sets.
formulas.mathIssues: Scales strictly MORE fields than the server-side applier (src/league_intel/overlay.py:88-95 touches only rankDerivedValue). The two must not diverge and already have.
