notes:
METHOD. Read-only throughout; `git status --porcelain` was clean at the end. All Python was run with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 from a scratchpad outside the repo. Numbers below were produced by running the repo's own code against the repo's own live data (contract built from exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json, rosters from data/ros/team_strength/ dated 2026-08-04 06:56).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LIVE, in the four categories requested:
- implemented in source: all 16 league_intel modules.
- wired to a route: adjustment, publish, overlay, replacement, values, config, te_premium (via data_contract), scoring_fit + reception_fit (via gameplan), cross_market (via angle/packages/gameplan), sim/sim_calibration (via ros/playoff_sim). NOT wired: calibration.py (622 lines), twin.py (254 lines) — test-only importers, zero production consumers.
- consumed by the frontend: /api/valuation/league-adjusted → frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js applyValuationOverlay → /rankings; valuation_mode threaded to six engine call sites via frontend/lib/valuation-mode.js.
- confirmed to have live data: roster snapshots yes (both leagues, today). ROS aggregate yes (1085 players, 5 sources, 2026-08-04T03:57Z). KTC base+TE++ CSVs yes (today). Reception depth NO — data/nfl_data/actuals/ does not exist in this checkout, so receptionFit is inert here even though the flag defaults ON and the 2026-07-28 production artifact proves it WAS live then. data/league_intel/sim_points_model.json does not exist, so the playoff sim runs on its legacy fallback constants.
- validated: only the board backtest (one run, 2026-07-28) and the TE curve fit. Neither the scarcity constants (0.5 / 0.20), the tier-confidence priors, MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT, nor the 1.10 TEP-native multiplier has any calibration in the repo.

DIRECT ANSWERS TO THE FIVE KEY QUESTIONS:
1. Position alone? NO in production, yes in this checkout. reception_fit_axis is per-player by design (adjustment.py:312-323) and gameplan.py:1333 wires it unconditionally. The 2026-07-28 production artifact shows 190 distinct per-player factors across RB/TE/WR. CLAUDE.md and publish.py:21-27 both assert otherwise. The *consequence* those docs use the claim to justify — composability against a re-weighted board — does survive, because no axis reads the consensus value. The stated property does not.
2. Replacement level: genuinely flex-aware and format-aware, not a fixed rank cutoff. `measure_endogenous_starters` runs the exact optimizer over every real roster with the league's actual slot vector, and the starter tier is the median of each team's marginal starter. Live dynasty_main starters_per_team {QB 1.833, RB 2.750, WR 4.417, TE 2.000, K 0.917, DL 2.667, LB 3.250, DB 3.083} against a slot_fill of exactly 36 DL / 36 LB / 36 DB — the difference is nominal-position attribution and is deliberate and documented. Its real weakness is the input, not the method: rosValue is a log-rank index, and the module honestly reports that the point-estimate path measures FLEX TE share at 0.0% against 10.4% on weekly actuals (I reproduced: 27.2% under 1-TE rules, 10.4% under 2-TE rules, TE started/team 1.608 vs 2.215).
3. TE premium: the curve IS measured (73 paired KTC rows, R² 0.941; I re-derived median 1.6% error against today's CSVs), and the target basis IS a constant that mismatches a real league — `measure_te_demand` returns 'base' for dynasty_new while the board is pinned to 'tepp'. Live effect on TE values: median +16.7%, median +50 board slots. The corrective axis exists in code (`convert_te_value` both directions) and is deliberately left ABSENT.
4. Backtest: the doc's numbers reproduce its artifact EXACTLY and its conclusion ("keep it a toggle") is supported. The methodology is better than most — realized points under the league's exact scoring, banded receptions included, over-replacement framing, a baseline that refuses to consult the module under test, seeded paired bootstrap. Its two real weaknesses: there is NO temporal split (current board vs completed 2025 season), and the player-level bootstrap overstates precision for the positional-scalar arm, which has 8 degrees of freedom. The doc discloses the first and not the second.
5. Double-apply: NO for scarcity — I grepped and confirmed no positional scarcity enters the blend at all (data_contract.py strips legacy LAM/scarcity fields at :8404). NO for TE — the guard is structural (KTC exempt by set membership, `convert_te_value` no-ops on from==to, and the overlay's tePremium axis is ABSENT). What I did find instead of a double-apply are three PARTIAL applications: (a) the server-side overlay scales only rankDerivedValue while the client scales four fields, (b) suggestions.py mixes an adjusted display_value against an unadjusted offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue for offensive positions, and (c) `apply_valuation_factors` is a third copy of the apply-and-rerank logic without the coherence guard. One softer point: scarcity/replacement also drives candidate SELECTION in roster_intel (tradeable_surplus), so under the adjusted lens scarcity enters both the candidate filter and the price — different channels, not the same arithmetic, but worth knowing.

THINGS I COULD NOT VERIFY:
- Whether Sleeper league owner-6e67d300493f (config/league_comparison.json my_league) is a real, current, correctly-configured league. It is not in the registry and appears nowhere else in the tree. Not Verifiable from Repository — it would need a live Sleeper call.
- Whether reception fit resolves in production. It does not here (no depth file); the 2026-07-28 artifact proves it did then. Whether it does today: Not Verified.
- The 1.10 TEP-native multiplier's provenance. No measurement cited anywhere I looked.

SURPRISES WORTH RECORDING:
- The scale-sensitivity result was the biggest one. Holding every player rank fixed and only changing the ROS universe size flips DB, TE and LB from lift to trim. That means the single largest behavioural consequence of this feature — the systematic +2.5%/+3.3% reprice of players against picks, which lands squarely in the trade calculator — is set by how many players the ROS sources happened to publish that morning, not by anything about the league.
- The documentation in this subsystem is unusually good — it names its own limitations, records retracted findings, and explains why axes are absent. That makes the handful of places where it has gone stale (position-uniformity, cross_market's "zero importers", compact_ranks_and_tiers' copy_rows instruction, "one implementation of apply-and-rerank") more dangerous than usual, because a reader has been trained to trust it.
- publish.py's docstring already contains a complete, correct specification of the fix for the dynasty_new TE mispricing. It has simply not been implemented.

findings.title: ROS Trade Deadline publishes explicit BUY/SELL recommendations from missing data coerced to zero — the #1-ranked roster in the league is labelled "Seller"
findings.evidence:
src/ros/trade_deadline.py:71 `owner_ids = sorted(set(playoffs) | set(champs) | set(strengths))` unions 12 team-strength owners with 8 sim owners; :79-80 `po = float((playoffs.get(owner) or {}).get("playoffOdds") or 0.0)` / `co = float((champs.get(owner) or {}).get("championshipOdds") or 0.0)` silently substitute 0.0 for absent owners. Reproduced against the live on-disk caches (data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json, 8 rows; data/ros/team_strength/latest.json, 12 rows) via `python3 -c "from src.ros.trade_deadline import build_team_directions; ..."`:
```
     Brent po=0.000 co=0.0000 pct=1.000 rank=1 -> Seller
    Collin po=0.000 co=0.0000 pct=0.750 rank=4 -> Seller
      Kich po=0.000 co=0.0000 pct=0.417 rank=8 -> Seller
    Blaine po=0.000 co=0.0000 pct=0.167 rank=11 -> Seller
  jstuedle po=0.000 co=0.0000 pct=0.083 rank=12 -> Seller
```
Missing owners: ['Brent','Kich','Blaine','jstuedle'] (present in team_strength, absent from the sim). src/ros/direction.py:106-108 then emits label "Seller" with recommendation "Sell aging win-now players. Prioritize 2026/2027 picks and 23-or-younger upside."
findings.userImpact: The single strongest roster in the league (ROS strength rank 1 of 12, percentile 1.000) is told to sell its win-now players for picks, on a tab wired into the default /league nav (`rosTradeDeadline`, frontend/app/league/tabs.js:27). Five of twelve managers get a fabricated recommendation. Nothing on the row distinguishes "0% playoff odds" from "not in the simulation".
findings.recommendedFix: Do not default absent odds to 0.0: either restrict `owner_ids` to owners present in both sims, or emit `label: "Unknown"` with `reason: "absent_from_simulation"`. Then fix the root cause — src/ros/playoff_sim.py:507 `for owner_id, scores in per_owner.items()` drops every owner with no scored week in the current season. Apply the same team-strength ∪ snapshot-roster union that src/ros/power_v2.py:226 `_enumerate_owner_ids` already implements for exactly this reason.

findings.title: Public trade letter grades apply linear-calibrated thresholds to an α=1.65-transformed gap — a 6% trade grades "Robbery"
findings.evidence:
src/public_league/activity.py:118 `total += pow(max(val, 1.0), _GRADE_ALPHA)` (α=1.65, :49), :131 `pct = ((max_w - min_w) / max_w) * 100.0`, then :58-77 buckets pct against 3/8/15/25/40. Worked example (scratchpad/grade_check.py, real constants):
```
A=[5000,3000] B=[7500]     wA=1.815e6 wB=2.477e6  alpha-pct=26.73%  linear-pct=6.25%   -> A+ Big win / D Robbery
A=[9000] B=[4000,4000]     wA=3.346e6 wB=1.756e6  alpha-pct=47.53%  linear-pct=11.11%  -> A+ Big win / F Fleeced
```
The bands come from frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:86-99 (`gradeTradeHistorySide`), which is fed a `pctGap` computed at :383-394 from LINEAR values plus a KTC VA term, with an explicit comment at :389-390: "Don't include the alpha-powered weighted sums — those dominate by an order of magnitude and would crush all pcts toward zero."
findings.userImpact: Every 2-for-1 on the public /league Trades timeline is graded one-to-two letter grades harsher than the same trade on the private /trades page, and near-fair consolidations are publicly labelled "Robbery"/"Fleeced" with the losing manager named.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute the public pct from linear side totals (optionally plus the same VA term the private path uses), keeping α only as a tiebreak, or re-derive the five bands for the α-transformed scale. Either way the header comment at activity.py:33-40 claiming the two paths "land in the same bucket" must stop being false.

findings.title: Public trade grades price unresolvable assets at 1.0, so historical trades containing off-board players grade as ~100% fleecings
findings.evidence: src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:174 `return by_name.get(name.lower(), 0.0)` and :161 `return 0.0` for unresolved picks; src/public_league/activity.py:118 then floors at 1.0 via `pow(max(val, 1.0), _GRADE_ALPHA)`. Worked example: `A=[1,1] B=[9999] -> alpha-pct=100.00% -> A+ Big win / F Fleeced`. The board it resolves against is a top-500-reference dynasty board (CLAUDE.md, `_PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N`), while the public feed carries every trade in the snapshot window (3 seasons — src/public_league/sleeper_client.py:44).
findings.userImpact: Any trade involving a player who has since retired, been dropped, or fallen off the top-500 board is publicly graded as a total fleecing of one manager, with no indication the asset simply wasn't priced.
findings.recommendedFix: Track unpriced assets per side and suppress the grade block when any asset on either side resolves to 0, or emit `gradeConfidence: "partial"` + `unpricedAssetCount`, mirroring the `metadata.assetsUnpricedByBoard` pattern CLAUDE.md documents for finder.py.

findings.title: Weekly power rankings accumulate PPG and W-L across ALL seasons but are labelled and documented as season-to-date
findings.evidence: src/public_league/power.py:82 declares `career_state` BEFORE `for season in seasons_sorted:` (:79) and never resets it; :121-147 read from it to produce `pointsPerGame` and `record = f"{wins}-{losses}"`. The module docstring says "Points per game (PPG) — overall scoring strength, season-to-date" (:9) and "``record`` (season-to-date W-L)" (:26). By contrast `recent_buffer` IS declared inside the season loop (:87), so recent form is season-scoped while PPG is career-scoped in the same composite. frontend/app/league/sections/power.jsx:223,226 label the columns "PPG" and "Record"; power.jsx:427 prints the `methodology` string verbatim, which mentions neither scope.
findings.userImpact: The displayed weekly record on the Power tab and on the Home-tab power-leader card (frontend/app/league/sections/overview.jsx:150) is a multi-season cumulative record read by users as this season's. The PPG percentile — 50% of the power score — is likewise a career number, so a manager strong two seasons ago carries that weight into week 1.
findings.recommendedFix: Move `career_state` inside the season loop (matching `recent_buffer`), or rename the emitted fields to `careerPointsPerGame`/`careerRecord` and correct both docstrings and the shipped `methodology` string (:214-219).

findings.title: A single 0.00-point roster-week silently removes that owner from the all-play population, breaking the luck metric's pigeonhole identity
findings.evidence:
src/public_league/metrics.py:57-59 `def is_scored(entry): return matchup_points(entry) > 0`; src/public_league/luck.py:88-90 skips those entries before `_all_play_week`, which computes `rivals = n - 1` (:70) over the SURVIVING owners. Reproduced (scratchpad/luck_zero.py) for a 12-team week with one 0.0:
```
with 0-scorer INCLUDED  sum expectedShare = 6.0  n=12
as luck.py SEES it      sum expectedShare = 5.5  n=11
actual wins that week (6 matchups)        = 6.0
```
The pinning test tests/public_league/test_luck.py:72-79 asserts total actual == total expected == 10.0 and passes only because the fixture has no zero scores. src/public_league/playoff_odds.py:105-118 explicitly builds an out-of-band `_latest_played_week` signal for exactly this ambiguity; luck.py, power.py and records.py never got it.
findings.userImpact: In any week containing a zero score the league gains +0.5 of phantom luck spread across the other managers, and the zero-scoring manager's loss is not counted at all (their gamesPlayed and actualWins under-count). The Home tab publishes a named "luckiest"/"unluckiest" manager off this number.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace is_scored-based week filtering in luck.py/power.py/records.py with the finalization test playoff_odds.py already has (`_matchup_is_final` + `_latest_played_week`), so a legitimate 0.0 is a played game and an unplayed week is excluded as a whole.

findings.title: ROS playoff + championship simulators hardcode 6 playoff spots and 2 byes and never read the league's Sleeper settings
findings.evidence: src/ros/playoff_sim.py:648-649 `playoff_seeds: int = 6, bye_seeds: int = 2`; `build_section` (:1064-1075) calls `simulate_playoff_odds(snapshot)` with no override and nothing reads `season.league['settings']['playoff_teams']`. src/ros/championship.py:167-168 is identical. Worse, `_simulate_bracket` ignores even the parameter: championship.py:80 `playoff_field_size = len([s for s in seeded_owners if seeded_owners.index(s) < 6]) or 6` — the literal 6 is unconditional and `playoff_seeds` is not a parameter of that function at all. The v1 module does it correctly: src/public_league/playoff_odds.py:492-498 reads `settings.get("playoff_teams")`.
findings.userImpact: In any league that is not exactly 6-in / 2-byes, every ROS playoff probability, championship probability, bye probability and contender tier is computed against the wrong bracket — and these are the defaults the /league UI renders (useRosPowerRankings: true, frontend/components/useSettings.js:143). The stamped `playoffSeeds: 6` makes the assumption look like a read setting rather than a constant.
findings.recommendedFix: Thread `playoff_teams` (and a byes derivation) from SeasonSnapshot.league['settings'] into both simulate_playoff_odds and simulate_championship_odds, and pass playoff_field_size into _simulate_bracket instead of the literal 6.

findings.title: Two independent Monte Carlos both publish "championship odds" and disagree; one page renders both
findings.evidence:
src/ros/playoff_sim.py:793 emits `"championshipOdds": round(champ_count[owner] / n_safe, 4)`; src/ros/championship.py:243 emits its own `"championshipOdds"` from a separate bracket sim. Live caches written 5 seconds apart (data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json computedAt 2026-08-04T03:57:31Z; latest_championship.json 03:57:36Z) disagree:
```
        playoff_sim   championship.py
Joey      0.3815         0.4085
Jason     0.3185         0.3390
Eric      0.2955         0.2474
Ty        0.0010         0.0007
```
src/ros/trade_deadline.py:27-49 reads playoffOdds from the FIRST file and championshipOdds from the SECOND, so one row mixes both runs.
findings.userImpact: The same manager's championship probability differs by up to 5 percentage points depending on which /league tab is open, and the trade-deadline classifier (which gates on championship >= 0.10 / >= 0.05) uses whichever file happens to be read. There is no authoritative number.
findings.recommendedFix: Designate one simulator as authoritative for championship odds (championship.py runs the actual bracket; playoff_sim's champ_count is the derivative), drop the duplicate field from the other payload, or run both arms from one seeded draw so they are numerically identical.

findings.title: Both semifinal losers are assigned 3rd place; nobody ever finishes 4th, biasing expectedFinish
findings.evidence: src/ros/championship.py:113 `finishes.setdefault(loser, 3)` sits inside `while len(advancing_to_semis) >= 2:` and is executed once per semifinal, both times with the constant 3. The defensive unplaced loop at :127-134 cannot correct it because both owners are already in `finishes`. `finish_total[owner] += finish` (:227) then averages into `expectedFinish` (:241).
findings.userImpact: expectedFinish is systematically ~0.5 too optimistic for every team reaching a semifinal, and the published field implies a full 1..N finish distribution the simulator cannot produce.
findings.recommendedFix: Rank the two semifinal losers against each other (by simulated score, seed, or PF) and assign 3 and 4.

findings.title: `rosPlayoffOdds` is a documented, flag-defaulted-ON section that no frontend code ever fetches
findings.evidence: frontend/components/useSettings.js:146-149: "PR3 shipped ros-playoff-odds. Default flipped to true on 2026-04-29; the ROS-blended Monte Carlo replaces the empirical-only v1 by default." `useRosPlayoffOdds: true`. Repo-wide grep for `rosPlayoffOdds` outside backend/tests returns nothing — no `fetch("/api/public/league/rosPlayoffOdds")` exists in frontend/. The /settings toggle at frontend/app/settings/page.jsx:765-766 writes a value with no reader. Meanwhile the v1 `playoffOdds` IS fetched, but only by PowerSection (frontend/app/league/sections/power.jsx:313), which LeagueClient.jsx:390-392 renders only when useRosPowerRankings is FALSE — default true (useSettings.js:143). src/public_league/public_contract.py:145-147 documents a "frontend swaps via settings.useRosPlayoffOdds" that does not exist.
findings.userImpact: With stock settings no playoff-probability number reaches the /league Power tab at all: v1 is behind an off-by-default branch and v2 has no consumer. The /settings toggle labelled as switching between them does nothing.
findings.recommendedFix: Either wire RosPowerSection to fetch /api/public/league/rosPlayoffOdds under the flag, or remove the flag, the settings toggle and the lazy section so nothing advertises a capability that isn't there.

findings.title: Every trade in the archives is tagged with the season's team-less awards (Top NFL Team, Rivalry of the Year)
findings.evidence: src/public_league/archives.py:269 `tags = award_tags.get((trade["season"], ""), [])` — the second key element is the literal empty string. `_award_tags_by_owner` (:32-40) keys on `award["ownerId"]`, and the only awards carrying `"ownerId": ""` are top_nfl_team (src/public_league/awards.py:1754) and rivalry_of_the_year (:1929). The trade row's participant list is computed one function earlier (`owners`, archives.py:47) and never used for tagging. The sibling `_season_result_archives` :220 does it correctly with `(season, owner_id)`.
findings.userImpact: The public searchable trade archive shows every trade in a season carrying the same two irrelevant award labels, and no trade is ever tagged with an award actually won by a participant. Filtering by award tag returns all trades or none.
findings.recommendedFix: Tag with the union of award_tags[(season, owner)] over the trade's ownerIds, and drop the empty-owner bucket from _award_tags_by_owner.

findings.title: The awards engine (2,345 lines) executes three times and rivalries three times per full public-contract build
findings.evidence: src/public_league/public_contract.py:372-377 (`build_public_contract`) iterates `_SECTION_BUILDERS` calling `builder(snapshot)`, so `franchise.build_section(snapshot)` runs with awards_section=None and recomputes awards at src/public_league/franchise.py:198-201 and rivalries at :186. `archives.build_section` then rebuilds four more sections: src/public_league/archives.py:262-265 `build_history / build_activity(limit=500) / build_draft / build_awards`. `weekly.build_section` calls build_rivalries again via `_featured_rivalry_pair` (src/public_league/weekly.py:100-104). The single-section path avoids one of these (public_contract.py:337-341 passes the built awards into franchise); the aggregate path does not.
findings.userImpact: Already measured in-tree: server.py:8552-8560 documents `archives` at ~1.4s GIL-bound Python per request and 34.3s/19.3s/2.9s TTFB on production against a ~0.53s baseline, which is why it had to be added to _HEAVY_SECTION_KEYS. The aggregate build pays awards×3 + rivalries×3 + history×2 + draft×2 + activity×2.
findings.recommendedFix: Thread already-built sections into franchise, archives and weekly in build_public_contract the way build_section_payload does for franchise, or memoize builders per snapshot generation.

findings.title: Trader of the Year credits a full season of points to any trade whose Sleeper `leg` is missing
findings.evidence: src/public_league/awards.py:395-401 `leg = tx.get("leg") or tx.get("_leg") or 0` then `post_weeks = _post_weeks(season, leg_int)`; `_post_weeks` (:239-242) returns `[w for w in sorted(...) if w > after_leg]`, so after_leg == 0 yields EVERY week in the season. The identical pattern is in `_waiver_king_scores` (:520-527).
findings.userImpact: A trade with an absent or zero leg is scored as if the acquired players' entire season — including weeks before the trade — was gained by the acquirer. Trader of the Year and Waiver King are published season awards, and pointsGained is 15% of the Manager of the Year composite (awards.py:1049).
findings.recommendedFix: Skip transactions with no resolvable leg, or infer the week from `created`/`status_updated` before falling back. Do not treat a missing leg as week 0.

findings.title: Trader of the Year counts bench points; Waiver King counts starter-only — both are published as "points gained" and summed into one composite
findings.evidence: src/public_league/awards.py:432-437 (trader) calls `_player_points_in_week_for_roster(season, week, rid, pid)` with `require_started` at its default False (:245-247). src/public_league/awards.py:543-548 (waiver) passes `require_started=True` with the comment "Only points scored while the pickup was actually in the starting lineup count — bench weeks are ignored entirely." Both feed `_manager_of_the_year_scores` as raw_trade and raw_waiver (awards.py:1027-1028) at 0.15 weight each (:1041-1049).
findings.userImpact: Two award races that read as the same unit are on different scales, and they are summed into one Manager-of-the-Year composite where the trade term is inflated relative to the waiver term by the size of the acquirer's bench.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one convention (starter-only is the defensible one for impact) and apply it to both, or rename the trader field to pointsAcquired and state the difference in AWARD_DESCRIPTIONS.

findings.title: Playoff-odds schedule inference invents a repeating cycle equal to the posted-week span and labels it a higher certainty tier than the round-robin fallback
findings.evidence: src/public_league/playoff_odds.py:279-283: when `_detect_cycle_length` returns None (the normal case — a real schedule has no repeating pair-set inside the posted block) `cycle_length = posted_weeks[-1] - anchor + 1`, and :293-299 assigns every unposted week the pairs of the posted week with the same residue. Because `_all_posted_pair_lists` (:186-211) includes already-played weeks, mid-season this makes remaining weeks replay the season's opening weeks' matchups. `scheduleCertainty` is stamped "inferred_from_posted" (:667) versus "inferred" for round-robin, and the docstring at :48-52 presents round-robin as the weaker fallback.
findings.userImpact: Remaining-schedule opponents are fabricated from the first N weeks, so a team whose early opponents were weak carries that advantage through every simulated remaining week. The certainty label tells the frontend this is the more trustworthy branch.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a confirmed cycle (`_detect_cycle_length` non-None) to use posted inference; otherwise fall through to round-robin. If the span fallback is kept, stamp a distinct certainty ("assumed_cycle") so the UI can warn.
findings.affectedSystems: /api/public/league/playoffOdds, src/ros/playoff_sim._remaining_schedule (reuses this helper), src/ros/power_v2 schedule_adjusted component

findings.title: CLAUDE.md lists /api/public/league/* as a league-aware endpoint that stamps leagueKey; it accepts no leagueKey and stamps none
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md, under "League-aware endpoints (all stamp `leagueKey` on their response)", includes "`GET /api/public/league/*` (routes through `_public_league_id()` which reads the registry)". Actual signatures: server.py:9104 `async def get_public_league(refresh: str = "")` and server.py:9453 `async def get_public_league_section(section: str, owner: str = "", refresh: str = "")` — no Request, no leagueKey, no `_resolve_league_for_request`. `_public_league_id()` (server.py:8727-8738) returns `_league_registry.get_sleeper_league_id()`, the DEFAULT league only. `_league_header` (src/public_league/public_contract.py:298-312) emits rootLeagueId and no leagueKey. Grep for leagueKey across the public-league handler block returns zero hits.
findings.userImpact: A reader of CLAUDE.md — human or agent — will believe /league is multi-league. It serves exactly one league, and a second-league user reading /league sees the default league's history, rivalries, awards and records with nothing on the payload naming which league it is.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the CLAUDE.md table to move /api/public/league/* into a single-league/default-only note, and stamp leagueKey on _league_header so the payload self-identifies.

findings.title: docs/public_league.md misstates the season window, the module list, the award catalog and the fetch strategy
findings.evidence: (1) docs/public_league.md:9-11 "current + previous dynasty season (fixed at 2 seasons for now)" vs src/public_league/sleeper_client.py:44 `PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS = max(1, int(_os.getenv("PUBLIC_MAX_SEASONS", "3")))` — default 3. (2) docs:16-18 lists 11 section modules; the tree has 28 files including luck, streaks, power, playoff_odds, matchup_preview, weekly_recap, matchup_recap, player_journey, matchup_narrative, csv_export — none documented. (3) docs:63-66 claims canonical awards include "runner-up, top seed, points king / black hole, toilet bowl"; `_season_canonical_awards` (awards.py:306-370) emits exactly champion, regular_season_crown, points_king, highest_single_week, lowest_single_week — grep for toilet / black_hole / runner_up / top_seed / chaos_agent / most_active in awards.py returns nothing. (4) docs:98-102 "~60+ HTTP GETs — batched sequentially today" vs src/public_league/snapshot.py:18-23 "we parallelize everything inside a single snapshot build via a ``ThreadPoolExecutor``". (5) docs:31-32 "11 tabs" vs frontend/app/league/tabs.js:15-41 — 21 tabs.
findings.userImpact: The only architecture doc for the largest subsystem in the repo is wrong on every point a maintainer would check first, including the size of the data window every career/record/rivalry number is computed over.
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite docs/public_league.md against the tree or delete the stale sections. At minimum fix the season count, the module list and the award catalog.

findings.title: /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized scores stats against whichever league's contract happens to be loaded, ignoring the league it just resolved
findings.evidence: server.py:11062-11066 resolves `league_cfg = _resolve_league_for_request(request)`, then server.py:11072-11074 reads `sleeper_block = (latest_contract_data or {}).get("sleeper") or {}` / `scoring_settings = sleeper_block.get("scoringSettings") or {}` with no check that the loaded contract's meta.leagueKey matches league_cfg.key. The response then stamps `"leagueKey": league_cfg.key` (:11145). Every other league-scoped endpoint 503s on this mismatch per the CLAUDE.md table.
findings.userImpact: Realized fantasy points are computed under a different league's scoring rules and returned labelled with the requested league's key. Currently latent — the handler's own comment (:11118-11124) records that nothing in the frontend calls this route — but the flag defaults ON and the route is live.
findings.recommendedFix: Compare latest_contract_data['meta']['leagueKey'] to league_cfg.key and return 503 data_not_ready on mismatch, matching the documented contract.

findings.title: Retro trade values silently substitute the earliest available rank-history sample for trades that predate coverage, and report it as a real at-trade value
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/trade-retro-value.js:51-56 `return (best || earliest)?.point || null;` — when no sample exists at or before the trade date it returns the earliest sample. The consumer at :88-91 pushes `{ source: "rankHistory" }` for BOTH cases, so the output cannot distinguish a genuine at-trade value from a post-hoc substitute. Picks are always valued at their CURRENT value (:76-83, `source: "current"`) and still summed into atTradeNet (:107-109).
findings.userImpact: The "Aged well / Aged poorly (±N)" badge on /trades is computed from currentNet − atTradeNet against a ±200 threshold (:117-120); for older trades atTradeNet is not the at-trade value, and for pick-heavy trades the pick component of the delta is structurally zero. Neither is flagged.
findings.recommendedFix: Emit a distinct `source: "earliest_sample"` plus a `predatesHistory` boolean and suppress or downgrade the verdict when any item used a fallback. Also reconcile the two nets on one card: gradeRetro is called with `currentNet: side.netValue` (frontend/app/trades/page.jsx:408, linear) while the card displays `side.netAdjusted ?? side.netValue` (page.jsx:283, linear+VA).

findings.title: analyzeRawTrade's own docstring describes a grading formula the function does not use
findings.evidence: frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:292-296: "A side's grade and pctGap are computed from its OWN net (gotWeighted minus gaveWeighted)". Code at :384-394: `netWeighted` is computed and never read for the grade; `pctGap = (netAdjusted / scale) * 100` where netAdjusted = netLinear + vaNet and scale = max(gotEffective, gaveEffective, 1), with the α-weighted sums explicitly excluded (comment at :389-390). Separately frontend/lib/trade-retro-value.js:22 documents `verdict: "winner"|"loser"|"even"|"unknown"` while the code (:117-121) returns "aged_well"|"aged_poorly"|"stable"|"unknown".
findings.userImpact: Anyone reconciling the public and private grade paths — a live divergence — will start from a false description of the private one.
findings.recommendedFix: Update both docstrings to the shipped math.

findings.title: An owner with no scored weeks is simulated as scoring exactly 100.0 points every week, producing a deterministic outcome reported as a probability
findings.evidence: src/public_league/playoff_odds.py:639-642 `if not owner_pool[o]: owner_pool[o] = [100.0]` with the comment "use a flat 100-point placeholder so the sim runs but the distribution is uninformative." `rng.choice([100.0])` returns 100.0 on every draw — a point mass, not an uninformative prior. Nothing on the payload marks the owner as unsimulated.
findings.userImpact: A new or bye-week owner receives a playoff probability that is an artifact of a hardcoded constant, indistinguishable in the response from a real one.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the league pool (already computed at :638) for zero-sample owners, or emit playoffProbability: null with a reason.

findings.title: Awards, races, power rankings, luck and playoff odds are published as decision-grade numbers with no calibration or backtest anywhere in the repo
findings.evidence: Every weight is hand-picked with no cited derivation: power.py:45-47 (0.50/0.25/0.25); awards.py:1041-1049 MOTY (0.30/0.25/0.15/0.15/0.15); awards.py:800-805 best_rebuild (0.40/0.30/0.20/0.10 with a bare stockpile/4.0); rivalries.py:222-229 rivalryIndex (5/3/2/2/1/2); src/ros/power_v2.py:65-75 (nine weights); src/ros/playoff_sim.py:66 ROS_BLEND = 0.20 ("Chosen small so empirical history still dominates"); :71 BEST_BALL_VARIANCE_BUMP = 1.10; :113-120 _PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION ("Calibrated from public weekly-scoring datasets" — no dataset, script or fixture in the tree). Tests are shape tests: tests/public_league/test_power.py asserts 0<=power<=100 and one row per owner; tests/public_league/test_playoff_odds.py asserts seeded determinism and 0/1 collapse — no test compares any probability to a realized outcome. Compare docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md, which the repo DOES maintain for the league-adjusted board. Live evidence of non-calibration: data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json carries `"pointsModelSource": "fallback-constants"`.
findings.userImpact: Playoff odds, championship odds, contender tiers and explicit buy/sell recommendations are presented at 4-decimal precision with confidence intervals, on a page framed as league intelligence, with no evidence any of it beats a coin flip.
findings.recommendedFix: Either build the equivalent of scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py for the ROS playoff sim against realized 2024/2025 outcomes and publish a Brier score, or label these surfaces in the payload (`validated: false` plus a methodology note the UI must render) so the presentation matches the evidence.
findings.affectedSystems: power, rosPower, playoffOdds, rosPlayoffOdds, rosChampionship, rosTradeDeadline, awards

findings.title: Weekly narrative articles exist for exactly one matchup of one week, and the generator has never had an API key
findings.evidence: `find exports/narratives -type f` returns two files: 2025/week-17/recap-1.json and 2025/week-17/preview-1.json. Both carry `"usage": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0, ...}` and `"generatedAt": "2025-12-30T14:00:00+00:00"` (an exact-hour timestamp), and `git log -- exports/narratives/` shows a single commit, `c3bd7dc Add one-time trade finder boundary test hotfix` — not a `chore(narratives): auto-generate` commit from the workflow. .github/workflows/weekly-narratives.yml:82-87 records the reason: "When the secret is absent/empty every weekly run fails with 'ERROR: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set' (8 straight failures as of 2026-07-25)".
findings.userImpact: Previews and Recaps are the 2nd and 3rd tabs on /league (frontend/app/league/tabs.js:21-22) and replaced the structured matchupPreview/weeklyRecap tabs (tabs.js:17-20). Both render from a corpus of one matchup, while the structured sections they replaced are still computed and shipped (weeklyRecap alone is 378 KB per tabs.js:72-73) but no longer rendered on the landing page.
findings.recommendedFix: Configure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or disable the workflow and the two tabs. If the tabs stay, stop building weeklyRecap/matchupPreview into the aggregate contract.

findings.title: Insider Trading has zero rows in its ledger in the audited tree
findings.evidence: data/intel/ledger.sqlite3 (253 KB, mtime 2026-08-04 08:39) has all 15 tables present and every one empty: asset_movements 0, transactions 0, leagues 0, league_memberships 0, platform_managers 0, platform_leagues 0, canonical_assets 0, ingestion_runs 0, sleeper_users 0. `meta` holds only {'schema_version': '1', 'platform_schema_version': '2', 'platform_schema_migrated_ms': '1785832773524'} — a schema migration ran today against an empty database.
findings.userImpact: /league/insider-trading renders its "No intel snapshot yet — the first crawl hasn't run" branch (frontend/app/league/insider-trading/page.jsx:106-114). The signal math (src/intel/signals.py) is well-constructed and well-documented but has no inputs here.
findings.recommendedFix: Confirm the crawler runs in production; the page already degrades correctly. Production ledger state is Not Verifiable from this repository.

formulas.name: Weekly Power Score (v1)
formulas.expression:
power = 100 × (0.50·pctile(PPG) + 0.25·pctile(mean of last 3 weekly scores) + 0.25·allPlayShareThisWeek)

pctile(values, x) = (count(v<x) + 0.5·(count(v==x) − 1)) / (n − 1);  returns 0.5 when n ≤ 1
allPlayShareThisWeek = (beats + 0.5·ties) / (teamsScoredThisWeek − 1)
formulas.inputs: PPG = career_state[points]/career_state[games] — CUMULATIVE ACROSS ALL SEASONS in the snapshot (power.py:82 declares career_state outside the season loop). recent = mean of a 3-deep FIFO reset per season (:87). allPlay = this single week's share only (:126-131; the code comment admits "simpler + still useful is current-week all-play share"). Percentiles are taken across the owners active that week only.
formulas.constants: _W_PPG=0.50, _W_RECENT=0.25, _W_ALLPLAY=0.25, _RECENT_WINDOW=3 — all hand-picked, no derivation cited, no calibration in repo
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Owners with no scored entry that week are absent from the week's ranking entirely. A 0.00-point roster-week is dropped by metrics.is_scored (>0), so that owner is excluded and everyone else's percentile denominator shrinks. record = round(sum of 1.0/0.5/0.0 shares) with losses = games − wins, so ties are absorbed into the loss column.
formulas.validated: none found — tests assert range/ordering/shape only
formulas.mathIssues: Three scopes mixed in one composite: career PPG + season-scoped recent form + single-week all-play, all labelled uniformly. weekRankDelta resets to 0 in week 1 of each season (prior_rank declared per season, :91). round(3.5) uses banker's rounding.

formulas.name: Worked example — Weekly Power Score
formulas.inputs: real constants 0.50/0.25/0.25 and the real _percentile_rank
formulas.constants: n/a
formulas.missingDataBehavior: n/a
formulas.validated: n/a
formulas.mathIssues: Confirms the composite is a pure rank transform — absolute scoring margin is discarded entirely, so a 200-point blowout week and a 0.1-point week produce identical percentiles.

formulas.name: Playoff Odds v1 — empirical-resample Monte Carlo
formulas.expression:
for sim in 1..10000:
  for each remaining regular-season week w, for each pair (a,b) in schedule[w]:
    score_a ~ UniformChoice(owner_pool[a]); score_b ~ UniformChoice(owner_pool[b])
    winner += 1 win; exact tie -> both += 1 tie; PF += score
  standings sorted by (-(wins + 0.5·ties), -PF, ownerId)
  top `spots` counted
P(playoffs) = made_count / num_sims
formulas.inputs: owner_pool = that owner's own scored regular-season weekly totals this season; if fewer than MIN_SAMPLED_WEEKS (2) samples, pool = own scores + the ENTIRE league pool (:638); if still empty, pool = [100.0] (:642). spots = league settings playoff_teams, else 6 (:492-498). Schedule = Sleeper-posted unplayed pairs, else cycle inference, else circle-method round robin.
formulas.outputRange: [0,1] to 4 dp; null when num_sims <= 0; 0/1 when the season is over; null with scheduleCertainty=preseason when nothing has been played
formulas.constants: DEFAULT_SIMS=10000 ("standard error on each owner's probability is < 0.5%" — asserted, not measured), MIN_SAMPLED_WEEKS=2, DEFAULT_PLAYOFF_SPOTS=6, flat placeholder 100.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Zero-sample owner -> deterministic 100.0 point mass. Fewer than 2 samples -> league pool concatenation (note league_pool already contains that owner's own scores, a small double-count). No schedule at all -> synthetic round robin with scheduleCertainty=inferred.
formulas.validated: none found. tests/public_league/test_playoff_odds.py asserts determinism under a seeded RNG, 0/1 collapse on a finished season, preseason nulls, tie handling and schedule-inference shape — no comparison to any realized outcome.
formulas.mathIssues: Sampling with replacement from <=13 observations gives a discrete distribution with no tail beyond the observed max; mid-season roster changes are not modelled (a team that traded away its QB keeps resampling its pre-trade weeks). Advanced tiebreakers (H2H, divisions) deliberately ignored (:399-402). Teams' weekly scores are drawn independently — no week-level correlation.

formulas.name: Luck Score / Expected Wins
formulas.expression:
expectedWins(owner) = sum over weeks of (beats + 0.5·ties) / (teamsScoredThatWeek − 1)
actualWins(owner)   = sum over weeks of {1.0 win, 0.5 tie, 0.0 loss}
luckDelta = actualWins − expectedWins
luckPerGame = luckDelta / gamesPlayed
allPlayWinPct = (sum beats + 0.5·sum ties) / sum rivals
formulas.inputs: Regular-season weeks only (season.regular_season_weeks). Career rows aggregate across every season in the snapshot (default 3).
formulas.outputRange: luckDelta unbounded in principle; in practice within +/- games
formulas.constants: none — this is the cleanest formula in the subsystem
formulas.missingDataBehavior: An entry with points <= 0 is dropped before _all_play_week, shrinking rivals for that week and removing the zero-scoring owner's game entirely (no actual loss recorded). Reproduced: 12-team week with one 0.0 -> league expectedWins 5.5 vs actualWins 6.0.
formulas.validated: tests/public_league/test_luck.py:72-79 asserts total actual == total expected == 10.0 on a fixture with no zero scores — the invariant is pinned but the failure mode is never exercised.
formulas.mathIssues: The pigeonhole identity (sum expected == sum actual) is broken by any 0.00 score. Otherwise the metric is descriptive and correctly bounded.

formulas.name: Rivalry Index
formulas.expression: rivalryIndex = 5·playoffMeetings + 3·gamesDecidedByFive + 2·gamesDecidedByTen + 2·seasonsWhereSeriesSplit + 1·totalMeetings + 2·meetingsInMostRecentSeason
formulas.inputs: Every scored matchup pair across the snapshot window, oriented by canonical (ownerA <= ownerB) key. gamesDecidedByFive = |margin| <= 5.0+1e-9; gamesDecidedByTen = |margin| <= 10.0+1e-9 (NESTED — every <=5 game also counts in <=10).
formulas.constants: 5, 3, 2, 2, 1, 2 and the 5.0 / 10.0 margin bands — hand-picked, no derivation
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Pairs that never met are absent from the output entirely (no zero row).
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: The two closeness bands are nested, so a 4-point game is counted twice for a combined weight of 5 — the same double-counting pattern src/intel/signals.py:8-21 documents as the reason trendScore was removed from Sharp Tracker. A season-scoped variant with the same nesting is at awards.py:1522-1530 (drops the recency term).

formulas.name: Public trade grade (alpha-weighted)
formulas.expression:
weighted(side) = sum over received assets of max(value(asset), 1.0)^1.65
pct = (max_w − min_w) / max_w × 100
grade = A/Fair if pct<3; winner: A<8, A-<15, B+<25, A+ otherwise; loser: B+<8, B<15, C<25, D<40, F otherwise
formulas.inputs: value(asset) from src/api/public_activity_valuation.py — the PRIVATE canonical board (values.displayValue || overall || finalAdjusted || rawComposite), 0.0 when unresolved. Picks resolved by probing "{season} Mid/Early/Late {1st..6th}" then "{season} Pick R.SS".
formulas.outputRange: letter grades A+..F plus colour and label; raw pct and totals deliberately not emitted
formulas.constants: _GRADE_ALPHA=1.65 ("kept as a retrospective grading exponent", frontend/lib/trade-logic.js:33-36), bands 3.0/8.0/15.0/25.0/40.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Unresolved asset -> 0.0 -> floored to 1.0 -> 1^1.65 = 1 (effectively zero). All-zero trade -> "Fair trade" for every side (:126-130). NaN/inf sanitized to 0.0 (:105-110). In 3+ team trades only the max side can win and only the min side can lose; middles get Fair.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Linear-calibrated bands applied to a superadditive transform. Reproduced: [5000,3000] vs [7500] -> alpha-pct 26.73% ("Robbery") where the linear gap is 6.25%; [9000] vs [4000,4000] -> 47.53% ("Fleeced") where the linear gap is 11.11%. Grades use TODAY's board values, not values at trade time, for trades up to 3 seasons old.

formulas.name: Manager of the Year composite
formulas.expression:
composite = 0.30·n(finish) + 0.25·n(winPct) + 0.15·n(pointsFor) + 0.15·n(tradePointsGained) + 0.15·n(waiverPointsGained)
n(x) = (x − min)/(max − min) min-max across the league that season; all-equal inputs -> 0.0 for everyone
raw finish input = (numTeams − finishRank), finishRank from playoff placement then regular-season order
formulas.inputs: metrics.season_standings (Sleeper roster settings), _finish_rank_by_owner (:962-993), _trader_of_the_year_scores (bench points included), _waiver_king_scores (starter-only)
formulas.constants: 0.30/0.25/0.15/0.15/0.15 — the docstring calls this "the totality of a season, weighted (no human judgment)"; the weights themselves are human judgment with no cited basis
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Owners absent from trader_rows/waiver_rows get 0.0 raw, indistinguishable from a manager who traded and gained nothing. _minmax maps an all-equal league to 0.0 not 0.5, so a season where nobody traded gives every manager 0.0 on that term rather than a neutral value.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Min-max normalization makes every component relative to the league's extremes, so one outlier compresses everyone else. Finish rank and winPct are ~0.55 of the score and are near-collinear. Trade and waiver terms are on different scales (bench vs starter points).

formulas.name: Best Rebuild composite
formulas.expression: composite = 0.40·(prevPointsRank − curPointsRank) + 0.30·(prevRecordRank − curRecordRank) + 0.20·(currentWeightedStockpile / 4.0) + 0.10·(curRookieCount − prevRookieCount)
formulas.inputs: Rank deltas in places (integers, up to +/-11 in a 12-team league); stockpile = sum of pick_weight over CURRENT owned picks (a level, not a delta); rookies = players with Sleeper years_exp == 0 on the current roster
formulas.constants: 0.40/0.30/0.20/0.10 and the bare divisor 4.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Owners absent from either season's standings are skipped entirely (:807-808). years_exp missing -> not counted as a rookie.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Mixes units without normalization: a rank delta of +/-11 and stockpile/4 (typically 8 picks × weights 4/3/2/1 ~ 20 -> 5.0) are added directly, so the stockpile term is a LEVEL that rewards pick-hoarding independent of any improvement. Gated to complete-vs-complete seasons only (awards.py:1904).

formulas.name: VORP (League MVP / Off MVP / Def MVP / ROY / Playoff MVP)
formulas.expression:
vorp(player) = max(0, starterPoints − replacementPerGame(position) · gamesStarted)
replacementPerGame = src.scoring.replacement_level.replacement_per_game(rows, starter_slots, band_size=5)
starter_slots: QB 24, TE 24, K 12, DL 36, LB 36, DB 36 fixed; RB/WR split dynamically out of the top-84 RB+WR pool by starter points
formulas.inputs: _player_starter_totals — starter-only points from Sleeper players_points intersected with starters; regular season only for MVP/ROY, playoff-only + champion roster only for Playoff MVP
formulas.constants: _VORP_FIXED_STARTER_SLOTS (24/24/12/36/36/36), _FLEX_RBWR_POOL=84, band_size=5. Comment says "Fixed by league convention" — no config file, no league-settings read.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Seasons without players_points yield nothing (_season_has_player_scoring, :272-280, flags this on the payload). Unresolvable position -> player skipped. Position with 0 slots -> slots = max(1, len(rows)//2).
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Negative VORP floored at 0 collapses all sub-replacement players to a tie and makes the metric non-linear at the baseline. `gamesStarted or 1` means a one-game cameo is compared against one game of replacement, so a single 40-point week can outrank a full season. Slot counts are hardcoded and never read the league's actual roster settings.

formulas.name: Mr. Consistent (coefficient of variation)
formulas.expression:
cv = populationStdev(weekly scores) / mean(weekly scores);  lower is better
sorted by (cv asc, -meanScore)
formulas.inputs: Regular-season weekly totals for rosters appearing in the winners bracket; when no bracket exists, ALL rosters. Minimum 4 weeks.
formulas.constants: min_weeks=4; population (not sample) variance
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Weeks with points <= 0 are excluded (:1350-1352), so a 0-point disaster week — the definition of inconsistency — is removed from the consistency metric. Owners with fewer than 4 scored weeks are dropped.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Excluding zero weeks makes the metric structurally unable to see its own worst case. Ranking by cv alone rewards a uniformly mediocre team over a uniformly excellent one with slightly more spread; meanScore is only a tiebreak.

formulas.name: Silent Assassin (close-game win rate)
formulas.expression:
closeGames = regular-season matchups with |margin| <= 10.0 + 1e-9
winPct = closeWins / closeGames;  avgCloseMargin = sum(margin of wins)/closeWins
sort key = (-winPct if eligible else 1, avgCloseMargin asc, -seasonWins)
formulas.inputs: All regular-season pairs with at least one non-zero score
formulas.constants: 10.0-point closeness band; min_eligible = 4 close games
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Owners with 0 close games are omitted from the rows entirely. Ineligible owners (<4 close games) sort to the bottom via the constant 1 sentinel but are still emitted with eligible:false.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: The 10.0-point band is a raw absolute in a league whose weekly scores are ~130-150 (per weekly_recap.py:438-440), i.e. ~7% of a score, with no scaling. The award is a small-sample win rate (typically 4-8 games) presented as skill ("Owns the close games").

formulas.name: Weekly Hammer / Bad Beat / Points King / Top Offense / Top Defense / Top NFL Team
formulas.expression:
weeklyHammer = count of regular-season weeks where |pts − max(pts that week)| < 1e-6
badBeat = max points scored in a loss (any week incl. playoffs)
topOffense = sum of starter points at QB/RB/WR/TE (K EXCLUDED)
topDefense = sum of starter points at DL/LB/DB/DEF
topNflTeam = sum of starter points by NFL team abbreviation
formulas.inputs: _starter_scoring_walk for the unit awards (requires players_points); raw matchup totals for hammer/bad beat
formulas.constants: tie epsilon 1e-6; _TOP_OFFENSE_POSITIONS = {QB,RB,WR,TE} vs _OFFENSIVE_POSITIONS = {QB,RB,WR,TE,K} — two different "offense" sets in one module
formulas.missingDataBehavior: topDefense rows with 0 points are filtered out so a non-IDP league emits no race (:936-939). Players with no NFL team abbreviation are skipped from topNflTeam.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Descriptive counts, correctly computed. bad_beat includes playoff weeks while weekly_hammer and silent_assassin exclude them — inconsistent scope across awards in the same payload.

formulas.name: Draft capital — weighted stockpile
formulas.expression:
pick_weight(round) = {1:4, 2:3, 3:2}, else 1
weightedScore(owner) = sum of pick_weight(round) over owned future picks
formulas.inputs: Reconstructed pick inventory: every roster × next 2 seasons × draft_rounds (league settings, default 4), then traded_picks applied as an ownership diff
formulas.constants: round weights 4/3/2/1; count=2 future seasons; draft_rounds fallback 4
formulas.missingDataBehavior: draft_rounds <= 0 -> 4. Traded picks whose season is outside the 2-year window are ignored (:172-173). Picks whose owner cannot be resolved are dropped.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Traded picks are applied in snapshot.seasons order, which is current->previous (NOT chronological), while the comment at :164-165 claims "chronological across all seasons so the most recent ownership wins". If a pick changed hands in both seasons' logs the OLDER assignment wins. A linear 4/3/2/1 ladder is also a poor proxy for pick value — the canonical Hill-curve pick values are deliberately not used (public isolation).

formulas.name: Superlatives — balance score and future-focus blend
formulas.expression:
balanceScore = populationStdev([qbCount, rbCount, wrCount, teCount])  (lower = more balanced)
futureFocus = 2·weightedPickScore + rookieCount
formulas.inputs: Current-season roster player lists + Sleeper positions + years_exp == 0 for rookies
formulas.constants: the multiplier 2 on pick score; IDP set {DL,DE,DT,LB,DB,CB,S,EDGE}
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing or unparseable years_exp -> not a rookie. Positions outside the four groups do not affect balance.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: futureFocus adds a weighted-pick count (typically ~20) to a rookie count (typically 2-6) with a factor-2 multiplier and no normalization — the pick term dominates ~10:1, making the award effectively a duplicate of mostPickHeavy. balanceScore ignores IDP entirely in an IDP league.

formulas.name: ROS Power Rankings v2 (the DEFAULT power surface)
formulas.expression:
power = sum over k of activeWeight_k · component_k / sum(activeWeight), with weights:
  team_ros_strength 0.38, ppg 0.18, recent 0.12, wl_record 0.10, all_play 0.08,
  streak 0.05, schedule_adjusted 0.04, roster_health 0.03, luck_regression 0.02
formulas.inputs: team_ros_strength = percentile of teamRosStrength from data/ros/team_strength/latest.json; ppg/recent/wl/all_play/streak/luck from the public snapshot's newest season; roster_health = clamp(healthAvailabilityScore/100, 0, 1); schedule_adjusted = 1 − mean(opponent strength percentile) over remaining posted matchups
formulas.constants: the nine weights; _RECENT_WINDOW=3; streak score = clamp(0.5 +/- 0.10·runLength) saturating at 5 (:285-303); luck_regression = clamp(0.5 − luckDelta/game, 0, 1) (:429-431)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Genuinely good: components with no input are routed through missing_inputs and the remaining weights are RENORMALIZED (:466), so absence never deflates a score. _enumerate_owner_ids (:226-283) unions team-strength owners with snapshot rosters so new managers still appear — the exact guard the playoff simulators lack.
formulas.validated: none found. frontend/components/useSettings.js:139-142 claims "Default flipped to true on 2026-04-29 after the engine validated against ~5 weeks of live standings" — no validation artifact, script or fixture for that claim exists in the repository.
formulas.mathIssues: schedule_adjusted inherits playoff_sim._remaining_schedule, which inherits the v1 cycle-inference fallback, so the strength-of-schedule term is computed over inferred opponents. Streak score saturates at +/-5 games with a linear 0.10 step — arbitrary.

formulas.name: ROS Playoff Odds v2 — ROS-blended Monte Carlo
formulas.expression:
blended_mean = empirical_mean × (1 + 0.20 · ros_z),  ros_z = (rosScore − mean(rosScores)) / pstdev(rosScores)
sd = empirical_sd × varianceMultiplier   [best-ball: 1.10 base + up to +0.15 depth lift]
score ~ max(0, Gauss(blended_mean, sd)) per team per remaining week
adaptive N: stop when max-owner SE(playoffOdds) < 0.005, N in [2000, 60000], checked every 1000
formulas.inputs: empirical distribution from the newest season's scored weeks; ROS strength map from data/ros/team_strength/latest.json; optional best-ball presim that draws per-player weekly scores using _PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION and solves the exact optimal lineup
formulas.outputRange: [0,1] with a CI per owner, plus seedDistribution, expectedWins, medianFinalSeed, byeOdds, topSeedOdds
formulas.constants: ROS_BLEND=0.20 ("Chosen small so empirical history still dominates"), BEST_BALL_VARIANCE_BUMP=1.10, DEPTH_VARIANCE_LIFT_MAX=0.15, ODDS_SE_TOLERANCE=0.005, SIM_CHECK_EVERY=1000, presim 120-1200 weeks, PRESIM_MEAN_TOLERANCE=0.01, _PLAYER_CV_BY_POSITION {QB 0.32, RB 0.55, WR 0.60, TE 0.65, DL/DE/DT 0.55, ...} described as "Calibrated from public weekly-scoring datasets" with no dataset in the tree
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Owners with no scored week in the newest season are DROPPED from the universe (:507) — 4 of 12 in the live cache. No ROS strength -> no blend. Empirical mean <= 0 -> league pool.
formulas.validated: none found. Live evidence of non-calibration: data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json carries "pointsModelSource": "fallback-constants".
formulas.mathIssues: Gaussian scores truncated at 0 without renormalizing the mean. Team scores drawn independently — no week-level correlation. Hardcoded 6 playoff seeds / 2 byes. In the live cache the sim ran with zero remaining weeks: every seedDistribution is one-hot, expectedWins are integers (6.0/7.0/9.0), and every owner still receives a CI (playoffOddsCi: [0.9981, 1.0]) implying sampling uncertainty that does not exist.

formulas.name: ROS Championship Odds + contender tier
formulas.expression:
Simulate the remaining regular season (same distributions), seed by (-wins, -PF), then a bracket:
  seeds 1..byeSeeds auto-advance; wildcards pair high-vs-low; single-game Gaussian matchups; semis pair high-vs-low; final
championshipOdds = championCount / N;  finalsOdds = P(finish <= 2);  semifinalOdds = P(finish <= 4)
contenderTier: champ >= 0.20 Favorite; >= 0.10 Contender; >= 0.05 OR playoff >= 0.50 Dangerous Playoff Team; playoff >= 0.30 Bubble; >= 0.10 Long Shot; else Rebuilder / Seller
formulas.inputs: playoff_sim._build_team_distributions, _current_record, _remaining_schedule
formulas.constants: tier cutoffs 0.20 / 0.10 / 0.05 / 0.50 / 0.30 / 0.10; playoff_seeds=6, bye_seeds=2 hardcoded; N default 10000
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Same owner-dropping as playoff_sim. Missing distribution in a matchup -> coin flip (rng.random() < 0.5, :150).
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: playoff_field_size uses a literal 6 and ignores the playoff_seeds argument (:80). Both semifinal losers are assigned place 3 (:113), so 4th place is never awarded and expectedFinish is biased. Publishes a championshipOdds field duplicating and disagreeing with playoff_sim's. Live cache shows a seed-3 team with playoffOdds 1.0 and semifinalOdds 0.0 — round-1 outcomes are effectively deterministic because the ROS mean gap dwarfs the sd.

formulas.name: Trade-deadline buyer/seller classification
formulas.expression:
Strong Buyer: playoff >= 0.75 AND champ >= 0.10
Buyer: playoff >= 0.60 AND champ >= 0.05
Selective Buyer: 0.45 <= playoff < 0.60
Strong Seller/Rebuilder: playoff < 0.10 AND champ < 0.01 AND vetCount >= 4
Seller: playoff < 0.25 AND champ < 0.02
Selective Seller: 0.20 <= playoff < 0.40
else Hold / Evaluate
strengthPct = (N − rank + 1) / N over the TEAM-STRENGTH row count
formulas.inputs: playoffOdds from data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json; championshipOdds from data/ros/sims/latest_championship.json; rank from data/ros/team_strength/latest.json; roster ages from a `teams` argument
formulas.outputRange: one of 7 labels + a prose recommendation + a summary line
formulas.constants: the seven threshold pairs; veteran age thresholds in _VETERAN_AGE (src/ros/direction.py:22-38); vetCount >= 4
formulas.missingDataBehavior: BROKEN: `float((playoffs.get(owner) or {}).get("playoffOdds") or 0.0)` treats absent-from-simulation as 0% playoff odds. build_section (:112-117) passes NO teams, so roster_age_profile is always {}, age_heavy is always False, and the "Strong Seller / Rebuilder" branch is unreachable in the live path.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: strengthPct's denominator is the team-strength row count (12) while the odds come from an 8-owner sim, so the three inputs are on different populations. team_ros_strength_percentile is accepted by classify_team and used only in the summary string — it never affects the label.

formulas.name: Weekly Recap headline / summary selection
formulas.expression:
seed = int(season)·100 + week;  phrase = bank[seed % len(bank)]
oneliner band: margin < 3 nailbiter; >= 50 obliterate; >= 25 roll; else beat
headline: 3+ teams >= 150 -> triple-leader; MVP-and-blowout if margin >= 25; blowout if >= 40; nailbiter if < 3; big win if >= 25; MVP; else fallback
summary tone: avg side score >= 130 with >= 2 teams >= 150 -> high-scoring; avg <= 95 with >= 2 teams <= 100 -> sluggish
formulas.inputs: per-week matchup rows; mvp = highest single side score; bust = lowest; badBeat = highest-scoring loser
formulas.constants: 3 / 25 / 40 / 50 point margin bands; 150 and 100 point score thresholds; 130 / 95 average-score bands; tight-game count >= 3 at margin <= 10; top1-top3 spread >= 15
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Weeks with no scored pair produce no recap. A 0-0 matchup is skipped (:528).
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Every threshold is an absolute point value tuned, per the code comment at :438-440, "for SF + TEP fantasy" — none scale with the league's actual scoring. bust is the lowest score including 0.0-point rosters. Purely descriptive; no decision content.

formulas.name: Upset of the Week
formulas.expression:
upset iff winner.preWeekWinPct < loser.preWeekWinPct
ranked by (-recordGap, winnerPreWeekPF asc, -margin)
formulas.inputs: metrics.pre_week_standings — only regular-season games strictly before the week
formulas.constants: none
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Owners absent from pre-week standings (week 1) yield no candidates, so week 1 never has an upset.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Correct and descriptive. The tiebreak comment says "lower WINNER pre-week PF" and the code sorts p[1]["winnerPF"] ascending — consistent.

formulas.name: Insider Trading signal strength
formulas.expression:
signalStrength = 100 · clamp(net/volume, -1, 1) · v/(v+5) · m/(m+3) · managerQuality
velocity = (shortVolume/shortSpanMs) / (longVolume/longSpanMs), None when longVolume < 3
confidenceTier: volume >= 12 AND managers >= 4 AND leagues >= 3 -> high; volume >= 5 AND managers >= 2 -> medium; volume > 0 -> low; else insufficient
formulas.inputs: asset_movements rows from data/intel/ledger.sqlite3, queried independently per window (48h/7d/14d/30d/90d)
formulas.constants: _CONFIDENCE_HALF_VOLUME=5.0, _BREADTH_HALF_MANAGERS=3.0, tier cutoffs 12/4/3 and 5/2. managerQuality = 1.0 for Insider Trading (cohort is league membership, not skill).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Assets missing from a window get an explicit zero window (_empty_window, :224-238) rather than a gap — deliberate and documented at :186-190.
formulas.validated: none found — but this is the one module in scope that documents its own prior failure mode (the removed trendScore = 3·net48h + 2·net7d + 1·net30d overlapping-window sum, :5-28) and structurally prevents it. The ledger in this working tree is empty, so the formula currently has no inputs here.
formulas.mathIssues: None found. The saturating confidence and breadth factors are honestly labelled as tuning choices, and the velocity ratio is arithmetically incapable of double-counting.

formulas.name: Trade retro verdict
formulas.expression:
atTradeNet = sum(value(got at trade date)) − sum(value(gave at trade date))
verdictDelta = currentNet − atTradeNet
verdict = aged_well if delta > 200; aged_poorly if delta < -200; else stable
formulas.inputs: per-player rank-history points ({date, rank, val}) from the contract's rankHistory; picks always at CURRENT value
formulas.constants: +/-200 threshold on a 0-9999 scale (~2% of the top asset)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No sample at or before the trade date -> the EARLIEST sample is substituted and still reported as source: "rankHistory". No history at all -> source: "current_fallback" (current value, delta 0 for that item).
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: currentNet is passed as side.netValue (linear) while the card displays side.netAdjusted (linear+VA) — two nets on one row. Pick values contribute identically to both sides of the subtraction, so pick-heavy trades always read "stable".

formulas.name: Movers (buy-low / sell-high signals)
formulas.expression:
backend: delta = rankThen − rankNow over a `window`-day rank-history span; |delta| >= threshold (default 15) qualifies; risers sorted by -delta, fallers by delta
frontend /trending: windowDays <= 1 -> contract-stamped rankChange; else computeWindowTrend(rankHistory, windowDays); sorted by |delta| then by value
formulas.inputs: backend: data/rank_history.jsonl via _rank_history.load_history(days=window+1), joined to latest_contract_data.playersArray by displayName then assetClass-scoped key. frontend: r.rankHistory already embedded on each contract row.
formulas.outputRange: integer rank deltas; risers/fallers capped at limit (default 10, max 50)
formulas.constants: window default 14 clamped [2,90]; threshold default 15; limit default 10 max 50; frontend windows 1/7/30 days
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty history -> {risers: [], fallers: []} with asOf: null. Players missing from the contract get row = {} and emit null position/team/value. data/rank_history.jsonl does not exist in this working tree, so /api/movers returns the empty shape here.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: The backend takes series[0] as the anchor — the OLDEST point within the requested window, not the point closest to exactly `window` days ago — so the effective window varies with history density. The endpoint's only caller is frontend/components/terminal/MoversPanel.jsx:139; /trending computes its own from contract rows, so two implementations answer the same question.

formulas.name: League comparison — positional balance
formulas.expression:
improvedBlended = 0.35·median + 0.25·average + 0.20·p75 + 0.10·p25 + 0.10·replacementAdj
positionShare(pos) = max(0, blended_pos) / sum(max(0, blended)) × 100
combinedDeviation = sum over positions of |myShare − baselineShare| + 0.4 · flexDeviationPct
worst band: score = max(0, 60 − (combined − 20)·2)
formulas.inputs: Historical nflverse season stat lines scored under each league's exact Sleeper scoring settings
formulas.constants: 0.35/0.25/0.20/0.10/0.10 weights; 0.4 flex coefficient; band breakpoint 20 and the ×2 slope; _TOTAL_WEIGHT = 0.5 in scoring_engine.py:63 for 0.5·total + 0.5·(ppg·17)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing scoring_settings -> 503 league_data_unavailable (server.py:4134-4141); missing season data surfaced via summarize_availability.
formulas.validated: none found in-repo
formulas.mathIssues: Not audited in depth — outside the primary scope. Route-reachable at GET /api/league-comparison and consumed by frontend/app/league-comparison/page.jsx.

formulas.name: Narrative angle pool + persona selection
formulas.expression:
persona = ["analyst","storyteller","sharp-take"][md5(f"{season}|{week}|{matchupId}")[0] % 3]
angle pool gated by: championship -> championship-stakes; h2hTotal == 0 -> first-meeting; >= 5 -> rivalry-grudge; multiWeek priorLead >= 15 -> comeback-arc + front-runner-vs-finisher; cumulativeClose (priorLead <= 50) -> razor-thin; seedGap >= 3 -> david-vs-goliath; playoff non-final -> statement-game + must-win; always vibes-check + managerial-mastery
formulas.inputs: matchup_preview._build_h2h_index, metrics.pre_week_standings, metrics.season_standings for seeds, multi-week round detection
formulas.outputRange: a persona string and an ordered angle list handed to Claude Opus 4.7
formulas.constants: h2h thresholds 0 and 5; priorLead 15 and 50 ("roughly two stdevs of weekly variance ~ 50 pts in a TE-premium IDP league. Tunable but stable enough in practice", :681-684); seedGap 3
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Returns None (skip the matchup) if the season, week, pair, or either owner cannot be resolved — never a half-brief.
formulas.validated: n/a — editorial selection, not a measurement. Only 2 articles exist on disk.
formulas.mathIssues: None; the data-gating of angles is a deliberate anti-hallucination guard and is well executed.

formulas.name: Streaks — records-in-reach threshold
formulas.expression:
points record withinReach iff chaserPoints >= holderPoints × 0.95
streak record withinReach iff activeStreakLength >= holderLength − 1
notableThisWeek: this week's entry ranks in the all-time top 5 for points high/low, margin, or points-in-a-loss
formulas.inputs: every scored paired roster-week across the snapshot window
formulas.constants: _NEAR_RECORD_POINTS_PCT = 0.95; _RECORDS_IN_REACH_TOP_N = 5
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Owners with no events get a type: "none", length: 0 row. Ties break both streaks.
formulas.validated: tests/public_league/test_streaks.py exists; assertions are shape/ordering only
formulas.mathIssues: _rank_of (:302-311) does a linear scan matching on (ownerId, season, week, points) inside a per-event loop — O(n) per lookup, and two identical scores in the same week by the same owner would collide. Purely descriptive.

formulas.name: Activity — blockbuster ranking and hidden tiebreak
formulas.expression:
order by (-totalAssets, -notableAssetCount, -tiebreak)
tiebreak = sum over sides of [ 1.5·notableAssetCount + sum over received picks of max(0, 5 − round) ]
formulas.inputs: normalized trade feed; NOTABLE_POSITIONS = {QB,RB,WR,TE,DL,LB,DB,EDGE}
formulas.outputRange: integer asset counts; the tiebreak is a float that is never serialized
formulas.constants: 1.5 notable multiplier; pick term max(0, 5 − round) with a default round of 5 when unparseable
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Picks with no round default to 5, contributing 0.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: The docstring (:22-28) claims tiebreak 3 is "Combined end-of-season internal values"; the implementation (:246-252) is an admitted proxy ("Approximates ... using a simple proxy") built from notable-asset counts and pick rounds and reads no value at all. _biggest_blockbusters strips a `_tiebreak` key (:263) that is never set.

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. I read every module in src/public_league/ (28 files, 12,655 lines), the six /api/public/league* handlers plus /api/movers, /api/league-comparison, /api/player/{id}/realized and /api/league/articles* in server.py, the /league tab model and section components, /trades, /trending, /league/insider-trading, both workflows, docs/public_league.md, and the ROS modules the public-league routes expose as lazy sections (src/ros/, 5,031 lines — these ARE reachable at /api/public/league/<section> and are what the default UI renders, so excluding them would have missed the most consequential findings). I ran read-only reproductions in the scratchpad and against the real on-disk caches. I modified nothing in the repository.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOAD-BEARING. Almost everything here is DESCRIPTIVE — records, streaks, rivalries, luck, awards, archives, franchise pages, weekly recaps. Those are league-history entertainment and are mostly computed correctly. Exactly four outputs are PREDICTIVE or PRESCRIPTIVE:
  1. rosTradeDeadline — emits literal buy/sell instructions per manager. Broken (Critical finding #1).
  2. rosPlayoffOdds / rosChampionship — probabilities to 4 dp with confidence intervals. Uncalibrated, hardcoded bracket, two disagreeing implementations.
  3. rosPower — the default Power tab. Best-engineered module in the ROS set (renormalising missing_inputs, owner-universe union) but its nine weights are unvalidated.
  4. Public trade letter grades — a public accusation of who got fleeced. Wrong transform (High finding #2).
Nothing in this subsystem has a backtest. The repo demonstrably knows how — docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md and scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py exist for the league-adjusted board, and CLAUDE.md describes a challenger/holdout/promotion gate for the Hill curves. None of that discipline reached /league.

THE DEFAULT UI SHOWS NO PLAYOFF ODDS. `useRosPowerRankings` defaults to true (frontend/components/useSettings.js:143), which makes LeagueClient render RosPowerSection; RosPowerSection never fetches playoff odds. The only consumer of v1 `playoffOdds` is the v1 PowerSection, behind the false branch. And `rosPlayoffOdds` — the flag-on replacement per the settings comment — has no fetch call anywhere in frontend/. So the 10,000-sim Monte Carlo that server.py:8543-8551 built an entire single-flight cache infrastructure for is, with stock settings, dead. The comment at LeagueClient.jsx:100 even says "useRosPowerRankings false until validated per-user", contradicting the default it reads.

LIVE DATA STATE (audited working tree, commit 9c5d972, 2026-08-04).
  * data/public_league/ — ABSENT. Gitignored, produced at runtime, so no public-league section could be executed end-to-end here. Correctness was established by reading code plus targeted reproductions.
  * data/ros/team_strength/latest.json — 12 rows, mtime 06:56 today. Fresh.
  * data/ros/sims/latest_playoff.json + latest_championship.json — 8 rows each, computedAt 03:57Z today. Fresh but degenerate: zero remaining weeks, one-hot seed distributions, integer expectedWins, pointsModelSource "fallback-constants".
  * data/ros/aggregate/latest.json + ~120 history files — fresh (06:56 today).
  * data/intel/ledger.sqlite3 — every table empty.
  * exports/narratives/ — 2 files, one matchup.
  * data/rank_history.jsonl — ABSENT, so /api/movers and the retro-value path are unexercisable here.

DOC-VS-CODE DISAGREEMENTS (all filed as findings, collected here): docs/public_league.md is wrong about the season window (2 vs default 3), the module inventory (11 of 28), the canonical award list (names four awards that do not exist), the fetch strategy (sequential vs ThreadPoolExecutor), and the tab count (11 vs 21). CLAUDE.md wrongly lists /api/public/league/* as league-aware and leagueKey-stamping. src/public_league/power.py's docstring says "season-to-date" for a career accumulator. src/public_league/activity.py:33-40 claims parity with a private grader that computes something structurally different. frontend/lib/league-analysis.js:292-296 describes a formula the function below it does not use. frontend/lib/trade-retro-value.js:22 lists verdict values the code never returns. src/ros/playoff_sim.py:113-120 claims a CV table was "calibrated from public weekly-scoring datasets" with no artifact in the tree. frontend/components/useSettings.js:139-142 claims the ROS power engine "validated against ~5 weeks of live standings" with no artifact in the tree.

DEAD OR HALF-WIRED CODE. `direction.classify_team`'s "Strong Seller / Rebuilder" branch is unreachable in the live path (trade_deadline.build_section passes no `teams`, so vetCount is always 0). `activity._biggest_blockbusters` strips a `_tiebreak` key nothing ever sets. `analyzeRawTrade` computes `netWeighted` and never grades on it. The `useRosPlayoffOdds` setting has no reader. The `weeklyRecap` section (378 KB per tabs.js:72) and `matchupPreview` are still built into the contract but no tab renders them since the articles tabs replaced them — though /league/week/[season]/[week] does still fetch weeklyRecap directly, so neither is fully dead.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY.
  * The real league's Sleeper `playoff_teams` / `playoff_week_start` settings — data/public_league/snapshot.json is absent, so I cannot say whether the ROS hardcoded 6/2 currently disagrees with the league. The hardcode is verified; its live impact is Not Verified.
  * Why 4 of 12 owners have no scored weeks in the newest snapshot season. The consequence is verified and reproduced; the upstream cause is Not Verifiable without the snapshot.
  * Production freshness of data/public_league/, data/rank_history.jsonl and data/intel/ledger.sqlite3 — Not Verifiable from Repository.
  * Whether tests/public_league/ (111 tests per the doc) currently passes — I did not run the suite, only read the assertions. Every test I opened (test_power.py, test_luck.py, test_playoff_odds.py) asserts shape, ordering, range and determinism. None asserts a calibrated value or compares any probability, grade or ranking to a realized outcome. A green suite here means "the code returns the shape it returned yesterday", not "the numbers are right".

CREDIT WHERE DUE. Three things here are genuinely well built and should survive any cleanup: src/intel/signals.py (documents and structurally prevents its own predecessor's overlapping-window double-count); src/public_league/public_contract.py::assert_public_payload_safe plus the private-field blocklist (a real, recursive, enforced isolation boundary); and src/ros/power_v2.py's missing_inputs renormalisation plus _enumerate_owner_ids union, which is exactly the correct handling of absent components — and precisely what the playoff simulators next door are missing.

findings.title: A keyword-matched RSS headline directly discounts a user-facing player value by up to 5%, and the severity is not player-specific
findings.evidence: src/api/injury_impact.py:80-84 `BASE_DISCOUNT_PCT = {"alert": 4.0, "watch": 2.0, "info": 0.5}`; :281 `discount = base * pos_mult * age_mult * decay`; :331 `adjusted = int(round(base_value * impact["adjustedPct"] / 100.0))`. The severity comes from src/news/providers/_rss.py:97-102 `if _ALERT_RE.search(text): return "alert", "injury", "negative"` — a regex over the CONCATENATED headline+description (_rss.py:180 `classify(f"{title}\n{description}")`), with alert keywords including `questionable`, `doubtful`, `arrest`, `suspended` (_rss.py:28-46). Mentions are attached by plain substring match over the whole known-name list (_rss.py:144 `if key in haystack`), so one headline listing five players in an injury report attaches the SAME alert severity to all five. Wired live at src/api/terminal.py:1562 `injury = _injury_impact.apply_injury_impact(row=r, news_for_player=player_news, now_ms=now_ms)` and rendered at frontend/components/terminal/BuySellHold.jsx:319 `<InjuryChip impact={entry.injuryImpact} adjustedValue={entry.injuryAdjustedValue} />` and frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:763-764.
findings.userImpact: Worked example (my computation, reproducing the module's constants): alert + RB + age 30, fresh news -> 4.0 x 1.20 x 1.20 x 1.0 = 5.76 -> capped 5.00% -> a 9000 value renders as 8550. `info` severity means NO keyword matched at all — ordinary neutral news — and still discounts: info + RB + age 33 -> 0.5 x 1.20 x 1.40 = 0.84% -> 9000 renders as 8924. A user sees a repriced number driven by the mere existence of a headline that mentions the player's name as a substring.
