findings.recommendedFix: Gate the discount on the mention's own impact/kind rather than the item-level severity; drop `info` from BASE_DISCOUNT_PCT entirely (a no-keyword-match item carries no injury information); and require the matched player's name to appear in the headline (not the body) before attributing severity to them.

findings.title: classify() stamps impact="positive" on every WATCH item — including "released" and "waived" — which produces a BUY recommendation and silently kills injury_impact's entire watch tier
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/_rss.py:99-101 `if _WATCH_RE.search(text): kind = ...; return "watch", kind, "positive"`. `_WATCH_KEYWORDS` (_rss.py:47-63) contains `released`, `waived`, `traded`, `claim`. I ran it: `classify('Jones released by Bears')` -> `('watch','transaction','positive')`; `classify('Team waived WR Smith')` -> `('watch','transaction','positive')`. Two live consequences: (1) src/api/terminal.py:950-956 `if pos > 0 and (rank_change is not None and rank_change > 0): add(38, "BUY", "pos_news_rising", ...)`; (2) src/api/injury_impact.py:256-266 `has_positive = any(... p.get("impact") == "positive" ...); if has_positive: continue` — since every RSS watch item marks all of its mentions positive, and Sleeper's only watch items are trending-ADDs (also positive, sleeper.py:_row_to_item `impact = "positive" if direction == "add"`), no watch item can ever reach the discount arithmetic. `BASE_DISCOUNT_PCT["watch"] = 2.0` is unreachable code.
findings.userImpact: A headline announcing a player was cut is scored as positive news; combined with any positive rank change it emits a BUY signal reading 'Positive news with rank rising'. Separately, the entire mid-grade injury tier (2.0 base) never fires, so a hamstring/high-ankle story produces zero discount while an unrelated neutral headline produces 0.4-0.84%.
findings.recommendedFix: Split the watch bucket by keyword polarity (signed/extension/promoted/named starter/activated -> positive; released/waived/claimed -> negative; traded -> neutral). Add a test that drives injury_impact with real `classify()` output rather than hand-built fixtures.
findings.affectedSystems: src/news/providers/_rss.py, src/api/injury_impact.py, src/api/terminal.py signal engine, /news page badge tone

findings.title: /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized never fetches defensive stats, so every IDP player silently returns zero weeks
findings.evidence: server.py:11086 `weekly = _ing.fetch_weekly_stats(years)` — the offensive-only feed. src/nfl_data/ingest.py exposes a separate `fetch_weekly_defensive_stats` (ingest.py:334) that this route never calls. The scorer it feeds, realized_points.compute_weekly_points, reads every IDP category off `def_*` columns (realized_points.py:167-190, 392-405) that are only present in the defensive release. The route only returns `reason: "no_stats_available"` when the GLOBAL fetch is empty (server.py:11088-11099); a defender simply matches zero rows at server.py:11122-11128 and falls through to compute_cumulative_points([]), which returns `weekCount: 0, totalPoints: 0.0` with no reason field (realized_points.py:504-513).
findings.userImpact: In an IDP league — which this platform's whole IDP pipeline exists to serve — the 'Realized points' panel on the player popup (frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:1003) is dark for every defender, with no diagnostic distinguishing 'no data' from 'never fetched the right file'.
findings.recommendedFix: Fetch and concatenate fetch_weekly_defensive_stats(years) alongside the offensive rows, and return an explicit `reason: "unmapped_or_no_rows"` when a mapped player matches zero rows.

findings.title: /api/player/{id}/realized scores against whatever league's contract happens to be loaded, and emits a full array of 0.0-point weeks when scoring settings are absent
findings.evidence: server.py:11069-11076: the route resolves `league_cfg = _resolve_league_for_request(request)` and then reads `sleeper_block = (latest_contract_data or {}).get("sleeper") or {}` / `scoring_settings = sleeper_block.get("scoringSettings") or {}` — no check that the loaded contract's leagueKey matches league_cfg.key, despite the response stamping `"leagueKey": league_cfg.key` (server.py:11138). The docstring one line above claims 'Pull the Sleeper scoring settings from the overlay or primary contract — whichever belongs to this league'; there is no overlay lookup in the code. When scoring_settings is {}, compute_weekly_points returns `RealizedPoints(fantasy_points=0.0, breakdown=[("no_scoring_settings", 0.0, 0.0)])` (realized_points.py:334-340) — a non-None result, so every week is appended.
findings.userImpact: Multi-league users can see one league's realized points labelled with another league's key. And when the contract carries no scoringSettings, the popup renders 'Total 0.0 pts / N weeks / 0.0 per wk' — an authoritative-looking zero rather than an absence.
findings.recommendedFix: 503 data_not_ready on a leagueKey mismatch (matching the CLAUDE.md rule for league-scoped endpoints), and drop weeks whose breakdown is no_scoring_settings so the empty-with-reason path fires instead of a zeroed array.

findings.title: A news headline raises a player's BDVM fundamental value through the sigma channel — the documented safety property covers the mean, not the value
findings.evidence: src/bdvm/news_events.py:13-17 promises 'Headlines can widen uncertainty; they can never move a player's mean.' True for mu. But src/bdvm/surplus.py:32-37 `expected_positive_surplus(mu, sigma, replacement) -> (mu - replacement) * norm_cdf(z) + sigma * norm_pdf(z)` is strictly increasing in sigma, and src/api/bdvm_api.py:165 `surplus_mode: str = "option"` makes that the DEFAULT board. The chain: news item -> keyword rule (news_events.py:78-90, e.g. INJURY on /injur|placed on ir|concussion|hamstring/) -> event at confidence 0.45, reliability 0.6 -> src/bdvm/events.py:122-131 `scaled = math.exp(math.log(value) * scale)` with `scale = confidence * reliability * 2^(-days/half_life)` (events.py:100-101) -> sigma_mult applied at events.py:185-186.
findings.userImpact: I computed it: INJURY carries `sigma_mult: 1.15` (config/bdvm/event_types_v1.json), scale = 0.45 x 0.6 = 0.27 on day 0, so effective multiplier = 1.15^0.27 = 1.0405. For mu=12, R=10, sigma=6 the option surplus goes 3.5254 -> 3.6173 (+2.61%); for a sub-replacement player (mu=10, R=12) 1.5254 -> 1.6173 (+6.02%); for an elite player (mu=18, R=10, sigma=7) +0.72%. An injury headline therefore makes a marginal player look MORE valuable, and it does so unevenly across the board — a relative distortion, not a level one.
findings.recommendedFix: Either suppress the sigma channel for auto-ingested speculation events entirely (making the lane a true no-op on value), or state the measured effect explicitly in the module docstring and stamp newsDrivenSigmaMult on the payload so the /bdvm UI can show which values moved on a headline.
findings.affectedSystems: src/bdvm/news_events.py, src/bdvm/events.py, src/bdvm/surplus.py, /api/bdvm/values, /bdvm page, /rankings Fund-gap column

findings.title: custom_alerts "value_crosses" is a level test, not a crossing test — it re-fires every 24 hours for as long as the value stays past the threshold
findings.evidence: src/news/custom_alerts.py:230-233 `crossed = (direction == "above" and v >= threshold) or (direction == "below" and v <= threshold)` — no prior-value comparison anywhere in the module; the only state kept is lastFiredAt (:180-186). The module docstring at :6-8 says 'the rule fires once per cooldown window when the threshold is crossed in the configured direction.' The behaviour is pinned as intended by tests/news/test_custom_alerts.py:160-179 test_cooldown_lifts_after_24h, which sets lastFiredAt to 25h ago, feeds the SAME value 6000 against threshold 5000, and asserts `len(hits) == 1`.
findings.userImpact: A user who sets 'alert me when Caleb Williams goes above 7000' gets an email and a push notification every single day, forever, once he is above 7000. The cron at server.py:10067 runs this over every user's rules.
findings.recommendedFix: Persist the last observed value per (rule, player) alongside lastFiredAt and require a transition across the threshold, not a level. Rename to value_level if the current semantics are actually wanted.

findings.title: The rank_change alert's notification title drops the player name; the computed title is dead code
findings.evidence: src/news/custom_alerts.py:260 computes `title = f"{display_name} rank {arrow} {abs(int(change))}"`, then :269 passes `title=" · ".join(body_parts[:1])` into the Hit, where body_parts[0] is `f"Rank moved {int(change):+d} positions"` (:261). The local `title` is never read. Delivery uses it verbatim at server.py:10133 `f"[Brisket alert] {hit.title}"` and :10148 `f"Brisket: {hit.title}"`.
findings.userImpact: The push notification and email subject read '[Brisket alert] Rank moved +25 positions' with no indication of which player. A user with several rank alerts cannot tell them apart from the notification.
findings.recommendedFix: Pass the already-computed `title` variable into the Hit.

findings.title: opportunity_score ignores the position argument it takes and saturates at 100 far below its documented calibration point
findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/opportunity_stats.py:231 `def _compute_opportunity_score(bucket: dict[str, int], position: str) -> float:` — `position` is never referenced in the body (:243-249), yet the module docstring at :31 advertises 'opportunity_score: float # composite 0..100 per-position'. The docstring at :239-241 claims 'a player with 20+ RZ touches, 10+ GL touches, 60%+ 3D conv rate lands near 100'. Formula: `score = (rz_touches * 3.0) + (gl_touches * 6.0) + (conv_rate * 30.0)`, then `min(100.0, max(0.0, score))` (:248-249).
findings.userImpact: I computed the docstring's own example: 20*3 + 10*6 + 0.60*30 = 138, clamped to 100 — it does not 'land near 100', it blew through the ceiling by 38%. RZ touches alone hit the cap at 33.3, which most starting RBs clear, so every high-volume back ties at exactly 100 and the metric cannot rank the group it exists to rank. Currently harmless: nothing outside tests/nfl_data/test_opportunity_stats.py imports this module.
findings.recommendedFix: Either delete the module or rescale against the observed distribution (e.g. percentile-rank within position, which is what the unused `position` argument implies was intended) before wiring it to anything.

findings.title: usage_windows z-scores use a population standard deviation over as few as two prior observations, producing |z|>=4 on ordinary week-to-week snap-share noise
findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/usage_windows.py:99-104 `def _stdev(values): if len(values) < 2: return 0.0; mean = ...; var = sum((v - mean) ** 2 for v in values) / len(values); return math.sqrt(var)` — divides by n, not n-1. The gate for emitting a z at all is only two prior weeks (usage_windows.py:171-176 `if len(w_snap) >= 2`). Thresholds that consume it are src/news/usage_signals.py:39-40 `_BUY_Z = 2.0` / `_SELL_Z = -2.0`.
findings.userImpact: I reproduced it: prior window [0.60, 0.64], current 0.70 -> mean 0.62, population sd 0.02, z = +4.0 — a 6-percentage-point snap-share move on a stable starter clears the BUY threshold twice over. With a 4-week window [0.70, 0.72, 0.68, 0.74] and current 0.80 the z is +4.02. This is the mechanism behind the repo's own measured 17.8%-of-active-players-per-week fire rate (src/api/feature_flags.py:83-92). Not currently reachable — nothing in src/ or server.py calls detect_usage_transitions (pinned by tests/news/test_usage_signal_calibration.py:97).
findings.recommendedFix: Do not emit a z below 4 prior observations, use the sample sd (n-1), and floor the sd at a measured minimum for a bounded 0-1 share. Re-run scripts/audit/measure_usage_signal_rate.py before any wiring, as the flag comment already requires.

findings.title: The freshness guard returns True on Saturday and Sunday of the in-flight week — the exact window it exists to exclude
findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/freshness.py:30 `_SAFE_WEEKDAY = 3` (Thursday) and :75 `return now_n.weekday() >= _SAFE_WEEKDAY` for the `stat_week == season_current_week` branch. Python's weekday() is Monday=0..Sunday=6, so `>= 3` is true for Thursday(3), Friday(4), Saturday(5) AND Sunday(6). The module docstring at :10-15 states the rule as "don't trust current-week data until Thursday local NFL day" and explains the hazard as 'between Sunday evening and Tuesday/Wednesday the data you pull back for last week is provisional'.
findings.userImpact: During the current NFL week, Sunday — mid-slate, when box scores are actively being written — is treated as safe to fire alerts on. The companion week_is_in_flight (:96) has the same inversion, so the UI would also label Sunday data as final.
findings.recommendedFix: The safe window for an in-flight week is Thursday through Saturday only: `_SAFE_WEEKDAY <= now_n.weekday() <= 5`. Add a test case per weekday.

findings.title: Player mention tagging is a plain lowercase substring match, so a prefix name is tagged on every article about its suffixed namesake, and never flagged ambiguous
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/_rss.py:143-145 `key = name.lower(); ... if key in haystack: out.append(PlayerMention(name=name, impact=impact))`. The docstring at :127-131 justifies it: 'The known-names set is already curated ... so full-word matching would be overkill'. I ran it: `match_players('Marvin Harrison Jr. torches secondary', known_names=['Marvin Harrison','Marvin Harrison Jr.'])` returns BOTH mentions, neither with ambiguous=True. Contrast the PFK provider, which does build an explicit ambiguity flag for normalized-key collisions (src/news/providers/pfk.py:120-131 `ambiguous=len(names) > 1`) — the RSS path has no equivalent, and PlayerMention.ambiguous defaults False (base.py:64).
findings.userImpact: The false mention is then treated as authoritative everywhere downstream: _enrich_player_mentions stamps it with the wrong player's position/team (service.py:212-224 only skips already-flagged ambiguous mentions), it produces a digest entry (digest.py:88-90 skips only ambiguous), and — most consequentially — it feeds apply_injury_impact (terminal.py:1562), so a headline about the son discounts the father's value.
findings.recommendedFix: Use word-boundary matching and suppress any known name that is a strict prefix of another matched known name; or route the RSS path through the same normalized/collision-aware matcher pfk.py already implements.

findings.title: injury_impact's own docstring contradicts its constants: it advertises a 60% cap and severity tiers that the classifier cannot produce
findings.evidence: src/api/injury_impact.py:63-64 'Values are capped at 60% total discount'; :175 the return-shape docstring says `"appliedDiscountPct": float (0-60)`. The actual constant is :91 `_MAX_DISCOUNT_PCT: float = 5.0`. The same docstring at :44-48 defines the tiers as 'alert -> severe, career-impacting (Achilles, ACL, spinal); watch -> mid-grade (high-ankle, hamstring Gr 2, concussion); info -> soft-tissue / day-to-day', but the only thing that assigns severity is _rss.classify, where `concussion` is an ALERT keyword (_rss.py:37), `questionable`/`doubtful` are ALERT keywords (:41-42), and `info` means no keyword matched at all — i.e. not a soft-tissue injury but no injury information whatsoever.
findings.userImpact: Anyone reading the module to decide whether to trust injuryAdjustedValue gets a description of a body-part-aware severity model that does not exist; what exists is a 19-keyword regex over an entire RSS description.
findings.recommendedFix: Rewrite the docstring to describe the actual input (item-level keyword severity from _rss.classify) and the actual 5.0 cap, and delete the (0-60) claim from the return contract.

findings.title: src/playerctx/__init__.py states the package is not wired into server.py; server.py serves a public route from it
findings.evidence: src/playerctx/__init__.py:14-16 'This package is deliberately NOT wired into ``server.py`` or the ``/api/data`` contract yet — consumption wiring lands with the player profile redesign (R2). Nothing imports this at server runtime today.' Contradicted by server.py:12603 `from src.playerctx.store import SNAPSHOT_PATH, load_snapshot` inside _playerctx_snapshot(), feeding `@app.get("/api/playerctx/player")` at server.py:12633, which is consumed by frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:272 and mounted at :1002. docs/playerctx.md is the accurate one ('Consumers (wired in R2)').
findings.userImpact: A maintainer reading the package entry point concludes the layer is dormant and may change the snapshot schema, the record-key convention, or the retention floors without realising a live endpoint and a live UI section depend on them.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the __init__ docstring to name the route and the frontend consumer.

findings.title: server.py's realized-points docstring asserts nothing calls the endpoint; PlayerPopup mounts it
findings.evidence: server.py:11052-11053 'What kept the row-filter bug below invisible was not the flag but the absence of a caller: nothing in the frontend requests this.' Contradicted by frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx:391-407 _loadRealized fetching `/api/player/${key}/realized`, :409 RealizedPointsSection, and :1003 `<RealizedPointsSection row={row} />`.
findings.userImpact: The comment is the stated reason the route's defects are considered low-risk. It is now false, which means the two defects reported above (offense-only fetch, wrong-league scoring card) reach users through the popup.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the docstring; it is currently the load-bearing justification for not hardening the route.

findings.title: Snap-share percentage is 0-100 in src/playerctx and 0-1 in src/nfl_data, with no shared constant
findings.evidence: src/playerctx/normalize.py:395-397 `pcts = [g[pct_key] * 100.0 for g in games]` -> `"pct": round(season_mean, 1)` (0-100; docs/playerctx.md confirms 'per-player mean snap % (0-100)'), rendered as `{Number(snaps.pct).toFixed(1)}%` in frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx. Meanwhile src/nfl_data/actuals_store.py:466-471 stores pcts 'as 0..1 fractions ... which is the scale ``usage_signals._ACTIVE_STARTER_SNAP_PCT`` already assumes', and src/news/usage_signals.py:41 `_ACTIVE_STARTER_SNAP_PCT = 0.50` compares against it directly (usage_signals.py:159).
findings.userImpact: Any future code joining the two snap surfaces (e.g. wiring the depth-chart cross-check that depth_charts.py:263 documents as taking 'raw pct' with min_snap_delta_pct=0.05) is one line away from a 100x error. usage_confirms_slot_change already takes a snap_share_delta_pct whose scale is stated only in prose.
findings.recommendedFix: Pick one scale, name it in a shared constant, and convert at the single boundary. At minimum, rename the playerctx field to pctPoints so the two cannot be passed interchangeably.

findings.title: Sleeper trending items stamp fetch time as the event timestamp, so they never age and always sort to the top
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/sleeper.py::_row_to_item -> `ts=to_iso_utc(now)` where `now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)` is taken once per fetch. The upstream row carries only {player_id, count} with a lookback window, no event time. The service sorts by (severity_rank, ts) (service.py:157-171) and drops items older than 7 days (service.py:127-147).
findings.userImpact: Trending adds/drops are structurally the freshest items in every feed and can never be aged out, so they crowd genuine reporting out of the top of the ticker and the digest ordering. They also always score decay=1.0 in injury_impact (injury_impact.py:266-273), maximising a trending-DROP item's 0.5-base discount.
findings.recommendedFix: Stamp ts at the start of the lookback window rather than at fetch time, or exclude kind == "trending" items from the severity sort's alert lane.

findings.title: PFK articles with no <lastmod> are stamped at the Unix epoch and therefore dropped, contradicting the code comment that says they merely sink
findings.evidence: src/news/providers/pfk.py comment 'Newest first; undated entries sink to the bottom rather than masquerading as fresh news on every refresh' followed by `ts=to_iso_utc(lastmod) if lastmod else to_iso_utc(epoch)` where `epoch = datetime.fromtimestamp(0, tz=timezone.utc)`. src/news/service.py:141-146 then drops anything older than `now - 7*86400`, so every undated PFK article is discarded, not sunk.
findings.userImpact: PFK coverage silently loses any article whose sitemap entry lacks a lastmod. The provider reports ok=True with a lower count, which is indistinguishable from a quiet publishing week.
findings.recommendedFix: Correct the comment, and count dropped-undated items in the provider run result so the loss is visible in providerRuns.

findings.title: /api/news computes playerDigests over up to 100 items, then truncates items to ?limit, so digests can cite item ids absent from the response
findings.evidence: server.py:4623 `payload = aggregated.to_dict()` — to_dict builds `"playerDigests": build_player_digests(self.items)` (service.py:118-122) from the already-capped-at-100 list. server.py:4625-4627 then `payload["items"] = payload["items"][:limit]; payload["count"] = len(payload["items"])`. playerDigests is left untouched, and each digest carries `"itemIds": [s.id for s in stories]` (digest.py).
findings.userImpact: A caller requesting ?limit=20 receives digests whose storyCount and itemIds reference stories not in the payload. The /news page's coverage strip compares filteredDigests.length against coverage.digests (page.jsx:205-220), so the counts can disagree. Low impact today because the only frontend caller requests the full 100 (news-service.js NEWS_FETCH_LIMIT = 100).
findings.recommendedFix: Recompute or filter playerDigests after the item truncation.

findings.title: /api/admin/nfl-data/flush reports twice the true number of evicted cache entries
findings.evidence: server.py:10852-10858 iterates `cache_dir.iterdir()` and increments `deleted` per FILE. Every cache entry is two files — src/nfl_data/cache.py:53-55 `return cache_dir / f"{h}.json", cache_dir / f"{h}.meta.json"`. I verified on disk: data/nfl_data_cache/ holds 3 entries and 6 files.
findings.userImpact: An operator flushing the cache is told '6 entries evicted' when 3 were. Cosmetic, but it is the only feedback the admin action gives.
findings.recommendedFix: Count only *.json files that are not *.meta.json, or divide by two.

findings.title: injury_impact's age ladder is inert for its highest-impact case, and the test that claims to prove otherwise asserts only >=
findings.evidence: src/api/injury_impact.py:281 `discount = base * pos_mult * age_mult * decay` with `_MAX_DISCOUNT_PCT = 5.0` (:91). For alert+RB: age 29-31 gives 4.0 x 1.20 x 1.20 = 5.76 and age 32+ gives 4.0 x 1.20 x 1.40 = 6.72 — both clamp to 5.00, so the 29-31 vs 32+ distinction has no effect. tests/api/test_injury_impact.py:109-125 test_aging_rb_gets_heavier_discount compares age 22 against age 33 and asserts `old["appliedDiscountPct"] >= young["appliedDiscountPct"]`, which passes on equality and would keep passing if the age ladder were deleted.
findings.userImpact: The documented age sensitivity (injury_impact.py:56-61) is unreachable for the position most sensitive to injury, which is the case the model was built for.
findings.recommendedFix: Either raise the cap or reduce the base so the multipliers stay inside the clamp; tighten the test to assert a strict inequality on a case that does not saturate.

findings.title: injury_impact's unit tests construct severity/impact combinations the production pipeline cannot emit, which is why the dead watch tier survived
findings.evidence: tests/api/test_injury_impact.py:39-53 `_season_news(severity, ..., impact: str | None = "negative", ...)` — every fixture defaults to impact="negative", including the watch item at :180 `_season_news("watch", hours_ago=2, headline="Hamstring")`. No production provider emits (severity="watch", impact="negative"): _rss.py:99-101 returns "positive" for every watch item and sleeper.py returns "positive" for every add (its only watch kind). Every test in the file drives compute_injury_discount with hand-built dicts; none imports src.news.providers._rss.classify.
findings.userImpact: The full watch tier (BASE_DISCOUNT_PCT 2.0) is unreachable in production and the suite reports it working. The same fixture gap hides the fact that info severity — no keyword match — is the tier that actually fires most often.
findings.recommendedFix: Add an integration test that runs real headlines through classify() + match_players() and into apply_injury_impact, asserting the resulting discount per tier.

findings.title: injury_feed's active-status set contains entries the normalizer can never produce, and collapses suspensions into OUT
findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/injury_feed.py:45-56 _ACTIVE_STATUSES includes "INJURED_RESERVE" and "PHYSICALLY_UNABLE", but the membership test at :219 runs on the OUTPUT of _normalize_status (:83-104), which maps INJURED_RESERVE -> "IR" and PHYSICALLY_UNABLE -> "PUP". Those two frozenset members are dead. Separately :94 `if s in ("OUT", "SUSPENDED"): return "OUT"` — a suspension becomes indistinguishable from an injury, and diff_for_signals (:255-307) then emits `transition: "healthy_to_injured"` for it.
findings.userImpact: None today — nothing in src/ or server.py imports injury_feed (the flag is classified UNREACHABLE at src/api/feature_flags.py:345). If wired, a suspension would be reported as a new injury and the severity map in unified_signal_engine.py would price it at 0.75 confidence as an injury event.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop the dead frozenset entries and give SUSPENDED its own normalized status with its own transition label.

findings.title: fetch_opportunity_stats re-scans the full multi-year play-by-play list once per requested year
findings.evidence: src/nfl_data/opportunity_stats.py `for year in years: stats = build_opportunity_from_pbp(pbp, season=year); all_stats.extend(stats)` — pbp holds every requested year's rows, and build_opportunity_from_pbp filters by season internally (`if season is not None and play_season != season: continue`). Three seasons of pbp is roughly 150k plays, so this is a 450k-iteration walk to produce the same result as one pass.
findings.userImpact: None today (module unreachable outside tests), but it is a 3-5x avoidable cost on a path the docstring positions as a nightly aggregate.
findings.recommendedFix: Call build_opportunity_from_pbp(pbp) once with season=None — it already keys buckets by (gsis, season).

formulas.name: News severity / kind / impact classifier
formulas.constants: ALERT_KEYWORDS (19): injury, injured, hurt, out for season, out for the season, season-ending, torn, acl, achilles, concussion, placed on ir, on the ir, to ir, questionable, doubtful, ruled out, suspended, arrest. WATCH_KEYWORDS (14): trade, traded, signs, signed, contract, extension, restructure, promoted, starter, named starter, released, waived, claim, claimed, activated. All hand-picked; no calibration artifact in the repo.
formulas.inputs: headline (string) + RSS description (string), HTML-stripped by clean_text (:83-86). Unit: free text.
formulas.outputRange: severity in {alert, watch, info}; impact in {negative, positive, neutral}
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty title -> item dropped entirely (_rss.py:172-174). Empty description -> classification runs on the title alone. No keyword match -> ("info","news","neutral"), which is NOT a neutral outcome downstream: injury_impact still applies a 0.5 base discount to it.
formulas.mathIssues: Sign error: 'released' and 'waived' map to impact=positive (verified by execution). Severity is item-level, so a multi-player headline assigns the same severity/impact to every tagged player. 'suspended' and 'arrest' are classified kind="injury". Word boundaries mitigate substring risk but 'starter' still matches 'non-starter'.
formulas.validated: none found — no backtest, no precision/recall measurement, no fixture corpus. tests/news/test_espn_provider.py:54-60 asserts two hand-picked cases only.

formulas.name: Injury-to-value discount
formulas.expression:
discount% = min(5.0, round(BASE[severity] x pos_mult(pos) x age_mult(age, is_rookie) x decay(age_ms), 2))
adjustedPct = 100 - discount%
adjustedValue = max(1, round(rankDerivedValue x adjustedPct / 100))
decay(t) = 1.0 for t<=0; 0.0 for t>=30d; else 1 - t/30d  (linear)
An item with ANY mention marked impact=positive is skipped outright.
formulas.constants: BASE = {alert 4.0, watch 2.0, info 0.5}. pos_mult = {RB 1.20, WR 1.00, TE 0.90, QB 0.70, DL/LB/DB/DE/DT/CB/S 0.80, other 1.00}. age_mult = {rookie 0.80, <=25 0.80, 26-28 1.00, 29-31 1.20, >=32 1.40, unknown 1.00}. _DECAY_WINDOW_MS = 30d. _MAX_DISCOUNT_PCT = 5.0. _OFFSEASON_MONTHS = {2,3,4,5,6,7,8}. All hand-picked; the docstring at :14-17 says so ('derived from the well-known fantasy-football conventional wisdom').
formulas.inputs: pos + age + is_rookie from the contract row; severity + ts + players[].impact from the news items matched to that player by NAME; now_ms from the server clock. rankDerivedValue (0-9999) from the contract row.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No news -> every field 0, adjustedValue omitted, value untouched (:200-203, 328-330). Unknown news timestamp -> decay forced to 1.0, i.e. treated as brand new (:266-269) — an undated item gets the MAXIMUM discount. Unknown age -> multiplier 1.00 (:139-140). rankDerivedValue missing or <=0 -> adjustedValue None (:326-330). Feb-Aug -> entire discount suppressed to 0 but the headline is still reported (:215-239).
formulas.mathIssues: Watch tier structurally unreachable (every watch item carries impact=positive, which the :256-266 guard skips). Info tier fires on items with NO injury content. Age ladder clamps away for alert+RB (5.76 and 6.72 both -> 5.0). Worked examples I computed: alert/RB/30 -> 5.00% (9000 -> 8550); info/RB/33 -> 0.84% (9000 -> 8924); alert/QB/24 -> 2.24% (9000 -> 8798); alert/RB/30 at 15 days -> 2.88%.
formulas.validated: none found. Docstring :22-24 concedes 'a linear decay is the right floor until we have months of news-vs-market price data to train on.' No such data exists in the repo.

formulas.name: Terminal news-driven signal rules (BUY/SELL/HOLD/RISK/MONITOR)
formulas.location: src/api/terminal.py:846-968 (context built :764-838); consumed by BuySellHold.jsx and by signal_alerts email delivery
formulas.expression:
alertCount = count(items where severity=="alert")
negCount = count(mentions where impact=="negative"); posCount likewise
RISK  p100 if alertCount>0 AND negCount>0 AND trend7 <= -3
RISK  p95  if volatility=="high" AND trend7 <= -5
SELL  p80  if trend7 <= -3 AND trend30 <= 0
SELL  p78  if negCount>0 AND volatility=="high"
MONITOR p65 if alertCount>0
MONITOR p62 if volatility=="high"
STRONG_HOLD p50 if value>=7000 AND trend30>=0 AND volatility in {low,med}
BUY   p40  if trend7 >= 3 AND volatility != "high"
BUY   p38  if posCount>0 AND rankChange > 0
highest priority wins; no rule fires -> HOLD
formulas.constants: trend7 <= -3, trend7 <= -5, trend30 <= 0, value >= 7000, trend7 >= 3, rankChange > 0. All hand-picked thresholds on the 0-9999 value scale and integer rank deltas.
formulas.inputs: 7d/30d value trend from rank history, MAD volatility label, rankChange from the contract row, and the news counts above.
formulas.outputRange: one of RISK | SELL | MONITOR | STRONG_HOLD | BUY | HOLD
formulas.missingDataBehavior: trend7/trend30/volatility None -> every rule guarding on them short-circuits (each is `trend7 is not None and ...`), so a player with no history can still reach MONITOR on alertCount alone. No news -> counts 0, rules skip. marketConfidence is deliberately NOT coerced to 0 when absent (256 of 1094 live rows carry none) — a good decision, documented inline.
formulas.mathIssues: posCount is polluted by the classify() sign error: 'Player X released' contributes to posCount, so a released player with a rising rank emits BUY 'Positive news with rank rising'. Sleeper trending-ADD items also feed posCount, making 'the crowd added him' a BUY input — a descriptive crowd measure used as a forward recommendation. Counts are per-item-mention, so N providers carrying the same story stack N counts (no story-level dedupe here, unlike digest.py:_story_key).
formulas.validated: none found — thresholds are not backtested against realized outcomes anywhere in the repo. Parity with the JS engine is pinned (tests/api/test_signal_engine_parity.py) but parity is not validity. MONITOR is in signal_alerts.ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS, so it gates outbound email.

formulas.name: Sleeper trending confidence (log-scaled share of top count)
formulas.expression:
share = clamp(count / top_count, 0, 1)
confidence = round(log1p(share x (e - 1)), 3)
Used only for the provider's own sort; no downstream consumer reads it.
formulas.constants: e - 1 = 1.71828 (chosen so share=1 -> log1p(e-1) = log(e) = 1.000). lookback_hours default 24; limit_per_feed default 20.
formulas.inputs: count = number of leagues the player was added/dropped in over the lookback window; top_count = the #1 row's count in that same window.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: top_count == 0 -> confidence = None. count <= 0 or missing player_id -> row dropped. Player not in the Sleeper name map -> row dropped.
formulas.mathIssues: None in the arithmetic (I verified share=1 -> 1.000, share=0.5 -> 0.620). Semantically it is a within-window relative rank, not a probability or a strength measure — the field is named `confidence` and is surfaced on the NewsItem contract (base.py:120), where a consumer would reasonably read it as certainty.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Frontend news relevance score
formulas.location: frontend/lib/news-service.js:118-149; consumed by filterByScope (:155-165), selectTickerAlerts (:190-205), news-filters.js
formulas.expression:
relevance(item) = max over mentions of: 100 if name in rosterNames, 50 if name in leagueNames, else 10
sort by (relevance desc, ts desc)
formulas.constants: ROSTER 100, LEAGUE 50, GENERAL 10 (news-service.js:24-28)
formulas.inputs: item.players[].name (lowercased, trimmed) vs the selected team's roster names and the union of all league rosters.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No players[] -> relevance stays GENERAL(10). Name normalization is `String(s||"").trim().toLowerCase()` only — no punctuation normalization, so 'C.J. Allen' and 'CJ Allen' do not match the roster set even though the backend's matcher would collapse them.
formulas.mathIssues: The scale is ordinal-only (used for >= comparisons); no arithmetic is done on it, so the specific values are inert.
formulas.validated: n/a — a display ordering, not a measurement

formulas.name: Per-player news digest grouping
formulas.location: src/news/digest.py:77-152; served as playerDigests on /api/news, consumed by app/news/page.jsx:133
formulas.expression:
group key = (normalize_player_name(mention.name), normalize_position_family(mention.position) or "")
story dedupe key = lowercased whitespace-collapsed headline
emit digest iff distinct stories >= MIN_STORIES_FOR_DIGEST
severity = max over stories by {alert 3, watch 2, info 1}
summary = newest-first attributed one-liners, capped at 6, then a "+N more" trailer
formulas.constants: MIN_STORIES_FOR_DIGEST = 2 (:31); _MAX_SUMMARY_LINES = 6 (:35); _SEVERITY_RANK {alert 3, watch 2, info 1} (:37)
formulas.inputs: the already-freshness-filtered, deduped, sorted, enrichment-stamped NewsItem list
formulas.outputRange: list of digest dicts with storyCount >= 2
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Mention with ambiguous=True -> skipped entirely (:88-90). Mention whose normalized name is empty -> skipped. Mention with no position -> family "", which groups it separately from the same player's position-stamped mentions, so one player can produce two digests and neither may reach the 2-story floor.
formulas.mathIssues: The digest text is a mechanical concatenation, not a synthesis (:52-73) — the docstring names it an 'LLM SYNTHESIS SEAM' that is 'Blocked today: the key has not been provisioned.' The headline it emits, f"{player}: {n} stories this week", is generated, not reported.
formulas.validated: n/a

formulas.name: Realized fantasy points (weekly, per league card)
formulas.location: src/nfl_data/realized_points.py:322-487; served by /api/player/{id}/realized and reused by src/bdvm/scoring.py, baseline.py, actuals.py, scoring_coverage.py
formulas.expression:
total = SUM over simple keys of stat_row[col] x rate
      + max(0, attempts - completions) x pass_inc
      + [pos==TE] receptions x bonus_rec_te
      + [pos in QB/RB/WR/TE] (passing_fd + rushing_fd + receiving_fd) x bonus_fd_{pos}
      + [pos is IDP] SUM over 12 def_* candidate-column keys of stat x rate
      + [pos is IDP] solo x idp_tkl_solo + assists x idp_tkl_ast + combined x idp_tkl
      + [pos is IDP] flat idp_tkl_5p if combined>=5, idp_tkl_10p if combined>=10
      + flat threshold bonuses at 300/400 pass, 100/200 rush, 100/200 rec
      + 2pt conversions x rate
Aliases from src/scoring/sleeper_ingest.KEY_ALIASES are applied only when the canonical key is absent, so a dump carrying both cannot double-count.
formulas.constants: Thresholds 300, 400, 100, 200, 100, 200 (:451-458) and 5, 10 combined tackles (:434-437). All rates come from the league's Sleeper card — none hardcoded. _IDP_POSITIONS is a 14-member frozenset (:233-250). _SCORING_KEY_ALIASES is DERIVED from KEY_ALIASES (:225-227), not hand-listed — deliberately, so the next alias Sleeper adds is picked up by both layers at once.
formulas.inputs: One nflverse weekly stat row (offensive OR defensive release) + the league's scoring_settings dict + an optional position override.
formulas.outputRange: unbounded float, typically -5 to 60 per player-week
formulas.missingDataBehavior: stat_row falsy -> None. scoring_settings falsy -> RealizedPoints(fantasy_points=0.0, breakdown=[('no_scoring_settings',0,0)]) — a NON-None zero, so callers aggregating over weeks accumulate a legitimate-looking 0.0 total. Missing stat column -> _num(None) = 0.0 and the key is skipped (`if stat == 0: continue`), i.e. indistinguishable from a genuine zero. Candidate-column lists (_first_num, :285-296) absorb nflverse renames; the docstring documents three past silent-zero incidents caused by exactly this.
formulas.mathIssues: The 5+/10+ tackle bonuses correctly append the flat rate, not stat x rate (:445-448); same for yardage bonuses (:461-464). _tackle_view (:299-320) rebuilds gamebook solo as def_tackles_solo + def_tackles_with_assist post-2025 and reads def_tackles directly pre-2025; combined = solo + def_tackle_assists. First-down bonus sums all three FD columns and picks the rate by POSITION, not play type — deliberate, documented at :100-119. No arithmetic errors found.
formulas.validated: Coverage is probed behaviourally by src/nfl_data/scoring_coverage.py:196-210 engine_reads_key (set key to 0 vs 7.0 against a maximal row, report whether output moved) — a genuine measurement, not a parsed mirror. tests/nfl_data/test_realized_points.py and test_first_down_and_per_play_scoring.py pin individual rules. No end-to-end reconciliation against a real Sleeper box score exists in the repo, though the _IDP_KEYS comment cites one manual cross-check (Zack Baun PHI 2024 wk1).

formulas.name: First-down imputation for projection lines
formulas.location: src/nfl_data/first_down_rate.py:159-190 (constants :112-119); opted into by src/bdvm/projections.py:31 and src/bdvm/scoring.py:40
formulas.expression:
if line already carries ANY of (passing|rushing|receiving)_first_downs -> pass through, imputed=False
yards = passing_yards + rushing_yards + receiving_yards
if yards < 1.0 -> pass through
line[_IMPUTE_COLUMN[pos]] = yards x FIRST_DOWNS_PER_YARD[pos]
returns (line_copy, imputed_bool)
formulas.constants: FIRST_DOWNS_PER_YARD = {QB 0.04998, RB 0.04964, WR 0.04715, TE 0.05090}; FIT_R_SQUARED = {QB 0.9896, RB 0.9417, WR 0.9382, TE 0.9105}; MIN_YARDS_TO_IMPUTE = 1.0. FITTED, not chosen — the refitter ships alongside (fit_first_downs_per_yard, :193-243), fit through the origin on 2023-25 REG, players with 200+ total yards, min 20 players per position.
formulas.inputs: A projection stat line (Mapping) + the player's position string.
formulas.outputRange: adds a float first-down count; approximately 1 first down per 20 yards
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Position not in the fitted set -> returns unchanged with imputed=False (never a league-average fallback, :180-182). Present-but-zero first-down column counts as supplied and blocks imputation (:150-157) — deliberate, so a source reporting a genuine zero is not overwritten. Always returns a copy; the caller's line is never mutated.
formulas.mathIssues: None found. Through-the-origin is the correct shape here and the docstring gives the fitted-intercept alternative it rejected (+1.2 WR, +4.2 TE). The `imputed` boolean is returned rather than inferred, so the double-count guard is structural.
formulas.validated: Yes — the best-validated formula in the audited surface. R^2 0.91-0.99 per position, n=142-355, three-season drift 2.0-4.8%, reported in docs/first-down-signal.md and reproducible via the shipped refitter. Pinned by tests/nfl_data/test_first_down_rate.py and tests/bdvm/test_projection_first_downs.py.

formulas.name: Reception band assignment and histogram shares
formulas.location: src/nfl_data/reception_depth.py:141-152 (band_for_yards), :265-282 (summarise_histogram); consumed by src/league_intel/reception_fit.py:100 and src/api/gameplan.py:1176
formulas.expression:
band_for_yards(y): band = BAND_KEYS[0]; for (key, lower) in zip(BAND_KEYS, _BAND_LOWER): if y >= lower: band = key
shares[k] = counts[k] / sum(counts)
formulas.constants: BAND_KEYS = (rec_0_4, rec_5_9, rec_10_19, rec_20_29, rec_30_39, rec_40p); _BAND_LOWER = (0, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40). These are Sleeper's exact scoring keys, not derived. Per-catch payout spread 0.25 -> 2.00, an 8x range whose mean sits on the 0.75 every ranking source prices.
formulas.inputs: receiving_yards (preferred) else yards_gained, per completed pass, from nflverse play-by-play streamed with csv.reader.
formulas.outputRange: one of six band keys; shares sum to 1.0
formulas.missingDataBehavior: total == 0 -> {receptions: 0, counts: all-zero, shares: all-zero} — shares of 0.0, not None, which a downstream consumer could read as 'never catches deep' rather than 'no data'. Missing pbp columns raise ValueError rather than reading as zero receptions — an explicit guard against the 2025 rename class of failure. Season 404 is disambiguated as not-started vs url-stale by season_has_plausibly_started (:120-136).
formulas.mathIssues: Negative and zero-yard receptions fall in rec_0_4 (verified: band_for_yards(-2) -> rec_0_4). The module docstring calls this out explicitly as 'an interpretation of an undocumented boundary rather than a measurement'.
formulas.validated: Band distribution measured over 11,217 receptions in 2025 (docs/reception-banding.md); catch-weighted value 0.6148 vs 0.7500 baseline; player-level tilt median 1.000, p10 0.942, p90 1.042 over 199 receivers. NOTE: no reception_depth_*.jsonl exists anywhere in this checkout (I searched), so the histograms the doc says are 'on disk' for 2023/2024/2025 are not present here — data/ is gitignored, so this is expected on a clone but means I could not verify the live inputs.

formulas.name: Reception band-shape projection (shrinkage toward position mean)
formulas.expression:
blended_counts[b] = SUM over seasons of 0.5^(age/half_life) x counts[season][b]
n = sum(player_bands)
if n < MIN_RECEPTIONS_FOR_SHAPE -> return position shape unchanged (or None)
w = n / (n + SHRINK_K)
shape[b] = w x own[b] + (1 - w) x position_shape[b]
expected_points_per_catch = SUM_b shape[b] x (scoring["rec"] + scoring[b])
formulas.constants: SHRINK_K = 40.0 — FITTED on held-out next-season per-catch value: MSE 0.011390 at K=0, 0.008449 at K=20, 0.008097 at K=40 (joint best), 0.008101 at K=60, 0.009832 at K=inf. MIN_RECEPTIONS_FOR_SHAPE = 8. RECENCY_HALF_LIFE_SEASONS = 1.0 — explicitly labelled 'Chosen rather than fitted ... it is a prior, not a measurement' (:88-96).
formulas.inputs: Per-player band counts (optionally blended across seasons — COUNTS are weighted, not shares, so sample size carries through), position shape from position_shapes (catch-weighted, not player-weighted), and the league's scoring card.
formulas.outputRange: shape: six fractions summing to 1.0; expected_points_per_catch in league points (measured 0.6148 mean for dynasty_main)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Neither a usable player shape nor a position shape -> returns None, explicitly refusing to fabricate a uniform distribution (:196-200). expected_points_per_catch(None, ...) -> None rather than a flat rate (:215-226) — the docstring gives the reason: 'a caller that cannot tell unknown from league average will quietly price every unknown player as average.'
formulas.mathIssues: None found. The fit reports both endpoint baselines (K=0 and K=inf) so the shrinkage is shown to be doing work rather than assumed to.
formulas.validated: Yes, and honestly. Year-over-year r = 0.767 (n=123, 2023->24) and 0.718 (n=128, 2024->25), beating the league mean by 52.6% / 44.3% of SSE. K fitted on two held-out transitions with the optimum flat between 30 and 60. STATUS CAVEAT: only tests import this module — grep found no production caller. docs/reception-banding.md's status table is accurate: 'Wiring projection into forward rankings — open'.

formulas.name: Opportunity composite score
formulas.expression:
rz_touches = rz_targets + rz_carries
gl_touches = gl_targets + gl_carries
conv_rate = third_down_conversions / third_down_attempts (0 if no attempts)
score = min(100, max(0, rz_touches x 3.0 + gl_touches x 6.0 + conv_rate x 30.0))
formulas.constants: 3.0, 6.0, 30.0, cap 100. Hand-picked; the docstring's stated calibration ('20+ RZ, 10+ GL, 60%+ conv lands near 100') does not hold. Red zone = yardline_100 <= 20, goal line = <= 5 (:52-53).
formulas.inputs: nflverse play-by-play rows filtered to play_type in {pass, run}, keyed by receiver_player_id or rusher_player_id (GSIS).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: yardline_100 absent -> _yardline_to_endzone returns None (the yrdln fallback the docstring promises is not implemented, :113-124) -> no RZ/GL credit, only 3rd-down credit. third_down_attempts == 0 -> conv_rate 0.0, not None. A player with no qualifying play gets no bucket at all, so absence and zero are conflated (documented as intentional at tests/nfl_data/test_opportunity_stats.py:64-68).
formulas.mathIssues: The `position` parameter is accepted and never used. Saturation: I computed the docstring's own example at 138 -> clamped 100; 33.3 RZ touches alone reaches the cap; an elite RB (55 RZ, 20 GL, 0.50 conv) also lands at exactly 100, tying with the docstring's much weaker profile. A mid WR (12 RZ, 2 GL, 0.40) scores 60.0 and a low-usage player (4 RZ, 0 GL, 0.30) scores 21.0, so the metric only discriminates in its bottom half.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: Rolling usage windows and z-scores
formulas.expression:
target_share = targets / team_week_targets; carry_share = carries / team_week_carries
window = last 4 PRIOR weeks (current deliberately excluded)
mean = sum(window)/len(window); sd = sqrt(sum((v-mean)^2)/len(window))   [population]
z = (current - mean) / sd, emitted only when len(window) >= 2 and sd > 0
formulas.constants: window_size = 4; minimum prior observations = 2; player_id_key default 'player_id_gsis'.
formulas.inputs: Per-player-week rows carrying season, week, team/recent_team, targets, carries, snap_pct (0-1 scale from actuals_store.usage_stat_rows).
formulas.outputRange: shares 0-1; z unbounded, in practice |z| routinely > 3
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing team -> the row is excluded from team totals but still produces a window with denominator 0 -> _share returns 0.0 (:91-94), so a share of exactly 0 means either 'no targets' or 'we could not identify the team'. sd == 0 (identical prior weeks) -> z is None. snap_pct None from actuals_store -> _num(None) = 0.0, so 'did not play' and 'we have no snap join' both read as 0% snaps in the window.
formulas.mathIssues: Population sd (divide by n) on n=2 makes sd = |a-b|/2, so any move of one gap-width produces |z| = 2 and 1.5 gap-widths produces |z| = 3. My worked examples: prior [0.60, 0.64] with current 0.70 -> z = +4.00; prior [0.60,0.64] with current 0.55 -> z = -3.50; prior [0.70,0.72,0.68,0.74] with current 0.80 -> z = +4.02; four identical weeks -> sd 0 -> z None. A 6-point snap-share move is not a 4-sigma event. Also: the docstring advertises rz_touches_4wk_mean/sd outputs that the UsageWindow dataclass does not have.
formulas.validated: Yes, negatively. scripts/audit/measure_usage_signal_rate.py measured the downstream detector firing on a mean 17.8% of active players per week across 2025 weeks 6-18; flooring the sd made it worse (19% -> 32%) and a 30-point absolute-move rule still hit 21%. Recorded at src/api/feature_flags.py:83-92. The flag is OFF and classified UNREACHABLE.

formulas.name: Usage BUY/SELL transition thresholds
formulas.expression:
BUY if snap_pct_z >= 2.0 (else target_share_z >= 2.0, else carry_share_z >= 2.0), checked in that priority order
SELL if snap_pct_mean >= 0.50 AND snap_pct_z <= -2.0
BUY short-circuits — a window never emits both
Gated on the feature flag AND on freshness.is_fresh_for_alerts
formulas.constants: _BUY_Z = 2.0, _SELL_Z = -2.0, _ACTIVE_STARTER_SNAP_PCT = 0.50 (:39-41). Hand-picked.
formulas.inputs: UsageWindow rows + season_year + season_current_week for the freshness gate.
formulas.outputRange: list of UsageSignal (BUY|SELL) with a tag naming the axis
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Feature flag off -> returns [] immediately (:87-88). Freshness gate fails -> window skipped (:92-98). z is None (sd 0 or <2 prior weeks) -> that axis cannot fire. snap_pct_mean is 0.0 for a player with no history, which is < 0.50, so SELL is structurally impossible in a player's first three weeks.
formulas.mathIssues: Inherits the z-score defect above wholesale. The SELL guard reads snap_pct_mean on the 0-1 scale, which matches actuals_store but NOT src/playerctx (0-100).
formulas.validated: Measured and rejected — see the usage-windows entry. tests/news/test_usage_signals.py drives hand-built spikes only; tests/news/test_usage_signal_calibration.py:1-22 states outright that 'none of them establishes a base rate, which is the only number that says whether the detector discriminates.'

formulas.name: Alert freshness gate
formulas.expression:
stat_year != season_year -> True (historical, finalized)
season_current_week is None -> False (conservative)
stat_week < current -> True
stat_week > current -> False
stat_week == current -> now(America/New_York).weekday() >= 3
formulas.constants: _SAFE_WEEKDAY = 3 (Thursday), _NFL_TZ = America/New_York (tzinfo so DST is automatic)
formulas.inputs: stat_week, stat_year, optional now, season_year, season_current_week
formulas.missingDataBehavior: season_year None -> True (treated as historical). season_current_week None -> False. Both branches are stated in the docstring and match the code.
formulas.mathIssues: weekday() >= 3 admits Thursday(3), Friday(4), Saturday(5) and Sunday(6). Sunday is the in-flight week's main slate — precisely the provisional window the module docstring says it exists to exclude. week_is_in_flight (:78-96) carries the mirrored inversion.
formulas.validated: none found beyond unit tests of the stated branches (tests/nfl_data/test_freshness.py)

formulas.name: Depth-chart derived role (playerctx)
formulas.expression:
group rows by (team, base_position)
sort by (pos_rank asc, pos_slot asc)
assign rank = 1,2,3,... skipping identities already seen (gsis_id or espn_id or lowercased name)
UI: rank == 1 -> "starter" badge, else "backup"
formulas.constants: _DEPTH_ABB_TO_BASE maps 30 ESPN slot abbreviations onto {QB,RB,WR,TE,K,DL,LB,DB}; unmapped slots (OL, P, LS, returners) map to "" and are dropped. Only the newest `dt` per team is kept.
formulas.inputs: nflverse depth_charts_{season}.csv rows: team, player_name, gsis_id, espn_id, pos_abb, pos_slot, pos_rank.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing dt or team -> row dropped. Unmapped pos_abb -> dropped. Missing pos_slot/pos_rank -> `_to_int(...) or 0`, which sorts that row FIRST (0 before 1), so a row with a missing pos_rank outranks a genuine starter. A player listed in several slots keeps his best one.
formulas.mathIssues: The 'starter' badge is the raw depth-chart rank with no snap-share cross-check, on a file nflverse refreshes daily through the offseason. In August that is a camp depth chart, presented in the UI as a flat starter/backup badge with no as-of date on the badge itself. Collapsing FB->RB and merging LDE/RDE/DE/LDT/RDT/DT/NT into one DL pool means a 4-3 team's DL ordering mixes interior and edge.
formulas.validated: none found — no comparison of depth rank against realized snap share anywhere in the repo.

formulas.name: Snap-share aggregation and trend (playerctx)
formulas.location: src/playerctx/normalize.py:355-410; rendered by PlayerContextSection's Movement chevron
formulas.expression:
side = argmax over {defense, offense, st} of total snaps (tie precedence defense > offense > st)
pcts = [game[side_pct] x 100 for game in games sorted by (game_type_order, week)]
pct = mean(pcts); recentPct = mean(last 3); trend = recentPct - pct
formulas.constants: recent_games = 3; _GAME_TYPE_ORDER = {REG 0, WC 1, DIV 2, CON 3, SB 4}; x100 scaling to 0-100.
formulas.inputs: PFR snap_counts_{season}.csv per-player-game rows (offense_pct/defense_pct/st_pct are 0-1 fractions).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: All three totals zero -> side defaults to 'offense' with 0% (documented). Player with fewer than 3 games -> recentPct is the mean of everything he has, so trend is exactly 0.0 and the UI's Movement chevron is suppressed on `trend !== 0`. Aggregation identity falls back to normalized name + position family WITHOUT team when pfr_player_id is absent (so a traded player stays one line); an ID-less key whose rows duplicate a week is DROPPED with a warning rather than merged — a real chimera guard.
formulas.mathIssues: `trend` is the last-3-games mean minus the WHOLE-SEASON mean, so the season mean includes the last 3 games — the two terms are not independent, and the statistic is mechanically damped as games accumulate (with 19 games, 3 of the 19 sit on both sides). It is presented to the user as 'snap share up/down N percentage points over the last three games' (PlayerPopup srLabel), which describes a recent-vs-prior comparison the formula does not compute.
formulas.validated: none found. Baselines in docs/playerctx.md are row counts, not accuracy.

formulas.name: Contract endYear derivation (playerctx)
formulas.expression:
endYear = year_signed + years - 1 (None when either input is missing)
one row per (lowercased name, position); highest year_signed wins
team = nickname -> abbreviation via a 35-entry table
formulas.constants: none numeric; the nickname table covers 32 franchises plus REDSKINS/FOOTBALL TEAM/WASHINGTON legacy spellings
formulas.inputs: nflverse historical_contracts.csv.gz, is_active == TRUE rows only.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: year_signed or years unparseable -> endYear None -> the UI simply omits the 'thru YYYY' clause. apy/total/guaranteed unparseable -> None -> formatMoney returns null -> renders as an em-dash.
formulas.mathIssues: Documented as approximate by the parse_contracts docstring (:258-266): OTC's `years` counts only newly signed years, so an in-contract extension's derived endYear undershoots the real expiry; and `team` is the SIGNING franchise, so a traded player's block shows his origin team. The UI surfaces both caveats — the signing-team note renders with a title tooltip. This is the best-labelled derived field in the audited surface.
formulas.validated: n/a — a passthrough derivation, and its limits are stated at the code, doc and UI layers.

formulas.name: Unified signal engine confidence and severity mapping (unwired)
formulas.expression:
severity: weighted = confidence + 0.15[starter] + 0.15[tier<=2] or 0.05[tier<=4]; clamp 1.0; >=0.75 high, >=0.45 medium, else low
value: fire iff |7d| >= 0.08 or |30d| >= 0.15; mag = max(|7d|, |30d|/2); confidence = min(1, mag x 3); verdict = sign(7d + 30d)
usage: confidence = min(1, max|z| / 4.0)
injury: confidence = {DAY_TO_DAY 0.3, QUESTIONABLE 0.4, DOUBTFUL 0.6, OUT 0.75, PUP 0.8, IR 0.95}, unknown 0.5
composite: avg confidence; severity bumped by min(len(sigs)-1, 2) levels when all verdicts agree; conflicting verdicts kept separate
formulas.constants: 0.08, 0.15, /2.0, x3.0, /4.0, +0.15/+0.15/+0.05, 0.75/0.45, and the six-entry injury severity map. Every one hand-picked; no fit, no calibration data.
formulas.inputs: pct_change_7d/30d, usage z-scores, injury transition dicts, transaction dicts.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Non-dict input -> None. Verdict not in {BUY,SELL} -> None. Missing z-scores -> `abs(x or 0)` = 0, so a signal with no z at all yields confidence 0 and severity low rather than being refused. Injury status not in the map -> 0.5, a silent middle value for an unrecognised status.
formulas.mathIssues: `mag = max(abs7, abs30/2)` mixes a 7-day and a half-scaled 30-day percentage as if commensurable, then multiplies by 3.0 so a 33% move reads as certainty. The composite averages confidences across incommensurable source classes (a rank drift and an IR designation) and then BUMPS severity for agreement, treating two correlated signals (an injury and the value drop it caused) as independent corroboration. Verdict is sign(pct_7d + pct_30d), which can disagree with the magnitude that produced the confidence.
formulas.validated: none found. STATUS: nothing in src/ or server.py imports this module — grep confirms only tests/news/test_unified_signal_engine.py. src/api/feature_flags.py:75-79 records that the flag registry previously asserted it fires and that it did not.

formulas.name: News to BDVM event mapping and sigma scaling
formulas.expression:
advice/listicle regex match -> NOTHING; >3 player mentions -> NOTHING; ambiguous mention -> NOTHING
else first matching keyword rule in order -> event type
event confidence = 0.45, reliability = 0.6
scale = confidence x reliability x 2^(-days / half_life)
sigma_mult_effective = max(1.0, ontology_sigma_mult ^ scale)   [speculative lane]
all non-sigma channels suppressed when confidence < 0.5
value effect via surplus.py: E[max(0, X-R)] = (mu-R)Phi(z) + sigma phi(z)
formulas.constants: _AUTO_CONFIDENCE 0.45, _AUTO_RELIABILITY 0.6, _SPECULATION_CONFIDENCE 0.5, _DUP_EVENT_WINDOW_DAYS 14, _MAX_PLAYER_MENTIONS 3, _AUTO_EVENT_MAX_AGE_DAYS 90. Ontology sigma_mults: INJURY 1.15 (half-life 30d), SURGERY 1.25 (60d), PRACTICE_LIMITATION 1.08 (14d), TRADE 1.15 (90d). config/bdvm/event_types_v1.json states 'All numbers are PRIORS.'
formulas.inputs: The aggregated /api/news item list, keyed by normalized player name.
formulas.outputRange: sigma multiplier >= 1.0, decaying to 1.0 over the half-life
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No keyword match -> no event (the closed-ontology rule). Unparseable confidence on an existing news:* event -> treated as still-ours and prunable (news_events.py:182). Human-raised confidence exempts an event from the prune. Corrupt or wrong-shape events file -> the merge REFUSES rather than discarding human entries, and preserves extra top-level keys on rewrite.
formulas.mathIssues: The safety property is stated as 'can never move a player's mean' — true — but the VALUE moves, because surplus.py is strictly increasing in sigma and surplus_mode defaults to 'option'. I computed the day-0 effect for INJURY: 1.15^0.27 = 1.0405, giving +2.61% surplus at mu=12/R=10/sigma=6, +6.02% at mu=10/R=12/sigma=6, +0.72% at mu=18/R=10/sigma=7. The sign is perverse (an injury headline raises the number) and the magnitude is largest for the sub-replacement players where it is least defensible. At full strength (scale 1.0) the same effects would be +9.70% / +22.43% / +2.82%.
formulas.validated: none found for the mapping's precision. The dedup, same-fact suppression, prune, and refuse-on-corrupt behaviours are pinned by tests/bdvm/test_news_events.py.

formulas.name: Depth-chart / usage cross-check confirmation
formulas.expression:
detect_slot_changes: key = (team, position, espn_athlete_id); absent in prior -> "debut"; slot decreased -> "promoted"; increased -> "demoted"
usage_confirms_slot_change: True iff direction in {promoted, demoted} AND |snap_delta| >= 0.05 AND sign(snap_delta) matches direction
formulas.constants: min_snap_delta_pct default 0.05 (5 percentage points, on the 0-1 scale). ESPN team ids hardcoded (32 entries). Cache TTL 12h. Circuit breaker 5 failures / 180s window / 180s open.
formulas.inputs: Two ESPN depth-chart snapshots + a week-over-week snap-share delta the caller supplies.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Flag depth_chart_validation off -> fetch_team_depth_chart returns [] before any I/O (:130-131), so both snapshots are empty and detect_slot_changes returns []. Network/parse error -> [] plus a circuit-breaker failure report. `debut` direction is explicitly NOT confirmable (returns False).
formulas.mathIssues: Slot is derived from list POSITION in ESPN's response (`slot=i + 1`), not from any published rank, so an ESPN reordering that is not a real depth change reads as promoted/demoted. The scale of snap_share_delta_pct is documented only in prose ('not the z-score - raw pct'), and the repo carries both 0-1 and 0-100 snap scales.
formulas.validated: The docstring claims 'Requiring the depth chart to also reflect the change halves the false-alert rate' (:12-14). I found no measurement supporting the 'halves' figure anywhere in the repo. The flag is SCRIPT_ONLY: the only importer is scripts/refresh_depth_charts.py, which early-returns because the flag defaults False.

formulas.name: Injury status normalization and transition diff
formulas.constants: the six-bucket severity ladder; _TTL_IN_SEASON = 30 min; circuit breaker 3 failures / 120s window / 180s open.
formulas.inputs: ESPN's public /nfl/injuries endpoint (undocumented).
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Flag off -> []. Network/parse error -> [] plus breaker failure (never a partial list). Unrecognised status -> passed through verbatim and then FILTERED OUT by the _ACTIVE_STATUSES membership test at :219, so a newly introduced ESPN status silently disappears rather than surfacing as unknown.
formulas.mathIssues: SUSPENDED normalizes to OUT, so a suspension is emitted as healthy_to_injured and priced at OUT's 0.75 confidence. Recovery transitions are deliberately not emitted (documented). _ACTIVE_STATUSES contains INJURED_RESERVE and PHYSICALLY_UNABLE, which the normalizer can never output — dead entries. OUT and PUP share severity 4, so an OUT -> PUP move emits nothing.
formulas.validated: none found. STATUS: no production importer (feature_flags.py:341-345 classifies espn_injury_feed as UNREACHABLE).

formulas.name: Scoring-coverage behavioural probe
formulas.expression:
engine_reads_key(key): for each of 7 probe positions, score _MAXIMAL_ROW with {key: 0.0} and with {key: 7.0}; return True if the outputs differ
classify(key): SCORED if the probe moves; else NOT_APPLICABLE if in the DST/K prefix or key sets; else UNSCORABLE if in UNSCORABLE_REASONS; else GAP
audit: classify every NONZERO rule in the league card
formulas.constants: _PROBE_POSITIONS = (QB, RB, WR, TE, LB, CB, DE); probe rate 7.0; _MAXIMAL_ROW is sized so every threshold can fire (600 pass yds, 300 rush, 300 rec, 15 solo + 8 with_assist + 8 assists, etc.). UNSCORABLE_REASONS has 17 entries, each with a stated reason.
formulas.inputs: A Sleeper scoring_settings dict.
formulas.outputRange: one Coverage enum per key; describe_gaps renders human-readable lines
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Zero-rated keys are skipped entirely — 'a rule worth nothing cannot cost anything', and a key that later goes nonzero gets classified then. Non-numeric rate -> skipped.
formulas.mathIssues: None found. This is the correct design: the docstring records that a regex-parsing approach was tried first and produced false negatives twice (it missed the yardage bonuses and the two-point keys, which the engine implements by looping over list literals), and that an undersized probe row produced its own false negative.
formulas.validated: Self-validating by construction, plus tests/nfl_data/test_scoring_coverage.py including test_the_probe_row_can_fire_every_threshold. It replaced a hand-maintained 'what the engine handles' list in league_comparison/service.py.

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. I read every file named in the brief plus the modules they reach (server.py routes, src/api/terminal.py, src/api/injury_impact.py, src/bdvm/news_events.py, src/bdvm/events.py, src/bdvm/surplus.py, frontend/components/PlayerPopup.jsx, useNews.js, BuySellHold.jsx) and the tests that claim to pin them. Numeric claims were reproduced in the scratchpad with python3 and are quoted with the numbers I got.

THE HEADLINE ANSWER TO "WHERE DOES A NEWS HEADLINE MOVE A USER-FACING VALUE". Three places, in descending severity:
1. src/api/injury_impact.py via src/api/terminal.py:1562 — a keyword-classified RSS item discounts rankDerivedValue by up to 5% and the result is rendered as injuryAdjustedValue in BuySellHold's InjuryChip and in PlayerPopup. This is the only place in the audited surface where a headline arithmetically changes a displayed board value. It is currently suppressed (today is 2026-08-04 and August is in _OFFSEASON_MONTHS), so the whole mechanism switches on abruptly on 1 September.
2. src/bdvm/news_events.py -> events.py sigma_mult -> surplus.py option value. The module's stated guarantee is about mu, and it holds; the value still moves, upward, by 0.7-6.0% on an injury headline.
3. src/api/terminal.py::_evaluate_signal — news counts drive BUY/SELL/MONITOR/RISK verdicts, and MONITOR is in ACTIONABLE_SIGNALS, so it gates outbound email.

DESCRIPTIVE SOLD AS PREDICTIVE. Two clear cases. (a) The Sleeper trending feed is a measure of what other fantasy managers already did; it enters the terminal signal engine as positiveImpactCount, where "the crowd added him" plus a rising rank produces a BUY. That is crowd-following presented as a recommendation, with no forward validation anywhere. (b) opportunity_score is named and shaped like a predictive composite ("weights favor the scarce / predictive signals") and is an unvalidated, saturating, position-blind sum of counts. It is unwired, which is the only reason it is not a bigger problem. A near-miss third case: the playerctx snap `trend` is described in the UI as a three-game change but is computed against an overlapping season mean.

WHAT THE REPO GETS RIGHT, AND IT IS NOT A SHORT LIST. docs/first-down-signal.md and docs/per-touch-efficiency.md are both records of a hypothesis being measured and DECLINED, with sample sizes, replication across season pairs, and the reasoning. src/nfl_data/first_down_rate.py ships its own refitter and its R^2 per position. reception_shape_projection.py fits its shrinkage constant against both endpoint baselines and reports the MSE table, so the shrinkage is shown to be doing work rather than assumed to. scoring_coverage.py replaces a hand-maintained "what the engine handles" list with a behavioural probe and documents the two false negatives that got it there. playerctx's floors-plus-per-source-retention gate is the strongest data-integrity check in the surface. src/api/feature_flags.py's _GATE_STATUS table is an unusually honest artifact: it records that 7 of 13 flags could not affect a request and that four defaulted True while their comments asserted live behaviour. Where this codebase measures, it measures well and writes it down. The defects cluster almost entirely in the one path that was never measured at all — the news keyword classifier and everything that consumes its severity field.

DOC-VS-CODE DISAGREEMENTS FOUND (each reported as a finding): src/playerctx/__init__.py says not wired (it is); server.py:11053 says nothing calls /realized (PlayerPopup does); injury_impact.py claims a 60% cap (it is 5.0) and body-part severity tiers (there are none); opportunity_stats.py claims per-position scoring (position is unused), a calibration point that overshoots the cap by 38%, and a yrdln fallback that is not implemented; depth_charts.py claims cross-checking "halves the false-alert rate" with no measurement in the repo; pfk.py says undated articles "sink to the bottom" (they are dropped); usage_windows.py's docstring lists rz_touches_4wk fields the dataclass does not have; providers/__init__.py lists six dynasty RSS feeds as registered without noting none is in _DEFAULT_ENABLED. Notably, the four docs/ files named in the brief all matched the code where I could check them — the drift is concentrated in module docstrings, not in docs/.

LIVE-DATA STATUS IN THIS CHECKOUT. data/ is gitignored (8,174 files are force-tracked, none relevant here), so absences below are expected on a clone but mean I could NOT confirm the live inputs exist. data/playerctx/ does not exist, so GET /api/playerctx/player returns 404 for every player here and PlayerContextSection never renders. data/nfl_data/actuals/ does not exist — no player_week_*.jsonl and no reception_depth_*.jsonl, despite docs/reception-banding.md's status table saying "2023/2024/2025 on disk". data/nfl_data_cache/ DOES hold three fresh entries written 2026-08-04T08:48Z: weekly_stats:2020-2025 (357 MB), snap_counts:2020-2025 (51 MB), id_map:v1 (25 MB) — so the ingest ladder demonstrably works and reaches nflverse. Note that /api/player/{id}/realized requests years [2025, 2026], a different cache key, so it would not hit any of those and would refetch (2026 404ing correctly, per-year).

REACHABILITY LADDER (implemented / routed / consumed by frontend / live data / validated). Fully live and consumed: news aggregation + digests + /api/news + the /news page; injury_impact; terminal signal rules; playerctx route + PlayerPopup section (no data here); /api/player/{id}/realized + PlayerPopup section; realized_points; first_down_rate via BDVM; reception_depth via reception_fit (flag LIVE). Implemented, imported only by scripts: depth_charts (refresh_depth_charts.py, itself a no-op because the flag is False). Implemented, imported only by tests: opportunity_stats, injury_feed, unified_signal_engine, reception_shape_projection, usage_signals (and usage_windows via it). Validated against held-out data: first_down_rate and reception_shape_projection only. Nothing else in this surface has a backtest.

WHICH NUMBERS DESERVE TO INFLUENCE DECISIONS. Trust: realized_points totals (given the right stat feed and the right league card — see the two route findings), first-down imputation, reception band histograms and the shrunk shape projection, playerctx contract blocks (their limits are labelled at code, doc and UI layers). Treat as decoration: injuryAdjustedValue, the terminal news-driven verdicts, Sleeper trending confidence, opportunity_score, every unified_signal_engine confidence. Do not wire without re-measuring first: usage_signals (its own audit says a 17.8% base rate) and the depth-chart cross-check.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY. Git history is squashed — every file in scope reports the same single commit (Mon Aug 3 2026, "Add one-time trade finder boundary test hotfix"), so per-file freshness and the age of individual constants are Not Verifiable from Repository. Production data freshness for playerctx, actuals and reception depth is Not Verifiable from this checkout. The systemd timer cadences described in docs/playerctx.md (dynasty-playerctx-refresh, Tue 05:40 UTC) are declared in deploy/ templates but whether they are installed and firing on the VPS is Not Verifiable. docs/per-touch-efficiency.md states outright that its probes "live in the session scratchpad rather than the repo", so its correlation tables (+0.658 WR residual, the K tables, the year-over-year r values) are not reproducible from this tree — I take them as reported, not verified. Finally, I did not execute the test suite; every statement about what a test asserts comes from reading the test body.

formulas.name: FAAB baseline bid (share-of-pool)
formulas.expression:
top_v = max(candidate_value, top_value_in_pool or 0)
share = candidate_value / top_v
aggressive_pct = 0.05 + 0.25 * share
aggressive  = max(1, round(league_budget * aggressive_pct))
reasonable  = max(1, round(aggressive * 0.70))
lowball     = max(1, round(aggressive * 0.35))
formulas.inputs: candidate_value: rankDerivedValue, 0-9999 internal scale. league_budget: dollars — but see mathIssues, the two callers pass different things. top_value_in_pool: dollars-free 0-9999 value, caller-defined denominator.
formulas.outputRange: aggressive in [5%, 30%] of budget; reasonable [3.5%, 21%]; lowball [1.75%, 10.5%]. On a $100 budget: 5-30 / 4-21 / 2-11.
formulas.constants: 0.05 floor share, 0.25 slope, 0.70 reasonable ratio, 0.35 lowball ratio, all hand-picked. No calibration artifact, backtest, or comment justifying any of the four exists anywhere in the repo.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: candidate_value <= 0 or league_budget <= 0 returns (0,0,0). top_value_in_pool None or 0 collapses to share = 1.0, i.e. the maximum 30% bid — a MISSING denominator produces the most aggressive possible recommendation, not a neutral one.
formulas.validated: none found. No backtest script, no comparison against realized winning bids, despite src/api/faab_analytics.py having the realized-bid history that would make one possible.
formulas.mathIssues: The `league_budget` parameter means two different things at the two call sites: src/trade/waiver.py:202 passes user_faab_remaining (the user's REMAINING dollars) while src/trade/faab_recommender.py:322-326 passes the LEAGUE budget and applies the remaining-dollars cap separately at faab_recommender.py:533-537. Identical function, incompatible semantics.

A player present in the response but absent from the top-100 counts as a real 0 (server.py:5096), which the code explicitly reasons about at server.py:5089-5094.

These absolute thresholds are not normalized to the distribution, so the kicker fires for 85% of the trending list today and would fire at the top tier for nearly all of it in-season, while in the deep offseason it fires for nobody. The same player gets a different bid purely from the calendar.

formulas.name: League per-position calibration blend
formulas.expression:
if positionBids[pos].count >= 3 and avg is numeric:
    standard = max(0, round(0.5 * positionBids[pos].avg + 0.5 * standard))
formulas.inputs: positionBids[pos].avg = mean of RAW WINNING BID DOLLARS for that position across all seasons and all player-quality tiers (src/api/faab_analytics.py, per-position accumulation)
formulas.outputRange: pulled halfway to the position mean

formulas.missingDataBehavior: No summary or no position -> returns bid_estimate unchanged, and the endpoint appends a missing factor row (weight 0.20). Fewer than 3 samples -> unchanged, factor row 'insufficient samples' also marked missing.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: This is the most damaging step. Worked example on live numbers with a TE position average of $30 and >=3 samples: value 1905 -> baseline $8 -> $19; value 100 -> baseline $4 -> $17. A 19.05x spread in player value collapses to a 1.12x spread in recommended bid. The player-specific signal is almost entirely erased and the output is 'the position's historical average, plus or minus a dollar'. The average is also computed over every winning bid regardless of the player's quality, so it carries no tier information.

formulas.name: Budget-environment scaling
formulas.expression:
share = leagueMedianWinningBid / league_budget
env = clamp(share / 0.08, 0.6, 1.6)
standard = max(0, round(standard * env))
formulas.inputs: leagueMedianWinningBid, league_budget
formulas.constants: _ENV_SCALE_TARGET_SHARE = 0.08 (:90), clamp (0.6, 1.6) (:91), _ENV_MIN_BIDS_ANALYZED = 10 (:92). The 0.08 'target share' is a bare hand-picked number with no cited source.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Returns None (no-op) when: no summary, budget <= 0, totalBidsAnalyzed < 10, median missing/<=0, OR the per-position calibration already fired. No factor row is appended when it no-ops, so its absence is invisible in the confidence math.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: The double-count guard against the position blend is real and tested (tests/trade/test_faab_recommender.py:489). No issue found in the guard itself.

formulas.name: KTC crowd blend
formulas.expression:

formulas.inputs: ktcCrowd block on the contract, keyed by name_clean.compact_name_key
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty map or uncovered player -> unchanged, and NO factor row at all (faab_recommender.py:419 gates the whole block on `if ktc_crowd_bids`), so the absence never lowers confidence.
formulas.validated: none found

I confirmed no ktcCrowd key exists in exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json.

formulas.name: Contention clearing + value ceiling + replaceability gate

formulas.outputRange: standard raised to at most 1.40*(1+0.25) = 1.75x the pre-contention bid
formulas.constants: _DROPOFF_GATE = 0.15 (:76), _CEILING_DROPOFF_CLAMP = 0.5 (:80), _CEILING_DROPOFF_SCALE = 0.5 (:81), 1.40 aggressive multiplier (:477). All hand-picked.

formulas.validated: none found
