I checked data/sleeper_last_good.json — all 12 teams have faabRemaining: null and faabBudget: null, because the scraper's Sleeper block does not populate them (only src/api/sleeper_overlay.py:466-468 does). Whenever the live overlay fetch fails, contention is silently skipped.

formulas.name: Marginal-upgrade floor, negative floor, and cap
formulas.expression:
if drop>0 and add <= drop:  standard = min(standard, max(1, round(reasonable_base*0.5)))
if drop>0 and add <  drop:  standard = 0
cap_source = team_faab_remaining if not None else league_budget
if standard > cap_source:   standard = cap_source
conservative = max(0, round(standard*0.70))
aggressive   = max(0, min(cap_source, round(standard*1.40)))
max_bid      = cap_source
formulas.inputs: add/drop values, team_faab_remaining
formulas.constants: 0.5 marginal factor, 0.70 conservative, 1.40 aggressive, _PACING_WARN_SHARE = 0.40 (:97)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: team_faab_remaining None -> cap falls back to the LEAGUE budget, so `max` is reported as the full league budget rather than the user's actual balance. On live data faabRemaining is always None in the baked block, so `max` reads 100 for every user.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: None beyond the cap fallback above.

formulas.name: Recommendation confidence bucket
formulas.expression:
realized_share = sum(weight of non-missing factors) / sum(all factor weights)
>= 0.85 -> high ; >= 0.55 -> medium ; else low
formulas.inputs: the factors list built during recommend_faab
formulas.constants: 0.85 and 0.55 cutoffs; factor weights 0.35 baseline / 0.20 value-gain / 0.15 trending / 0.20 league history / 0.10 crowd / 0.10 env / 0.15 contention / 0.10 cap
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Weights are only counted when the factor row is appended. Several branches (crowd, env scaling, value-gain when it lands in [0.95,1.05]) append NOTHING when they do not fire, so their absence neither adds to the denominator nor lowers confidence.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: The 0.35-weight 'Player value baseline' factor is never missing — it is the formula itself, not an input. Worked example on live data (Marlin Klein, no drop, no analytics snapshot, no contention, trending count 0): realized 0.50 / total 0.90 = 0.588 -> 'medium'. A recommendation built from zero market inputs reports medium confidence. The bucket cannot go below 0.35 realized share by construction.

formulas.name: Movers rank delta
formulas.expression:
latest = series[-1] ; anchor = series[0]
delta  = anchor.rank - latest.rank
qualify if abs(delta) >= threshold (default 15)
delta > 0 -> riser ; else -> faller
formulas.inputs: src/api/rank_history.load_history(days=window+1), which returns entries[-(window+1):] — the last N SNAPSHOTS, not the last N days (rank_history.py:369)
formulas.constants: window default 14 clamped [2,90]; threshold default 15 clamped >=1; limit default 10 clamped [1,50]
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty history -> empty risers/fallers with asOf null (server.py:3391-3401). Series shorter than 2 entries is skipped. Non-integer or <=0 ranks skipped. A player missing from the contract still emits a row with null position/team/valueNow.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: `anchor = series[0]` is the player's FIRST APPEARANCE inside the returned window, with no check that its date is anywhere near `window` days ago. A player who entered the board 2 days ago has anchor = 2 days ago, and the response is still labelled window: 14 and rendered by the UI as 'Rank deltas vs. 14d ago'. Combined with the snapshot-count windowing, any gap in the log (missed scrapes) silently stretches the real interval.

formulas.name: Rookie dollar allocation (sheet Hill-curve reproduction)
formulas.expression:
decay_rate = clamp(0.6 * stdev(values[0:6]) / mean(values[0:6]), 0.03, 0.08)
weight[i]  = exp(-decay_rate*i) * (1 - 0.2*exp(-0.12*i))
term1[i]   = values[i]*weight[i] / sum(values*weight)
excess[i]  = max(0, spine[i] - 1)          # spine = workbook col E
term2[i]   = excess[i] / sum(excess)
floor[i]   = 1 + (1 if 48 <= i < 60 else 0)
C[i]       = floor[i] + (1200 - sum(floor)) * (0.6*term1[i] + 0.4*term2[i])
-> x2, floor, largest-remainder bonus, monotone-non-increasing K with caps (4 for i in [48,60), 2 for i in [60,72)), R1 carryover over first 12, /2
formulas.inputs: values = our top-72 rookie rankDerivedValue descending (server.py:6975-7036); spine = CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx column E2:E73
formulas.constants: 0.6 stdev multiplier; clamp band [0.03, 0.08]; 0.2 and 0.12 in the weight shape; 0.6/0.4 term split; $1 per-row floor; $1 R5 bonus for rows 49-60; K caps 4 and 2; M = 12 carryover rows. All lifted from the user's Google Sheet.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: _read_sheet_spine_and_floor (server.py:7109-7131) catches EVERY exception — missing openpyxl, missing workbook, unreadable sheet — and returns a flat [1.0]*n spine. That makes excess all zero, term2 all zero, and silently deletes the 0.4-weighted half of the allocation with no error, no flag, and no field in the payload.
formulas.validated: VALIDATED against its own source: fed the workbook's own column-B values plus column-E spine, it reproduces column L2:L73 exactly (max absolute difference 0.0 across all 72 rows; both sum to 1200.0). I ran this.
formulas.mathIssues: Two measured issues. (1) The decay_rate clamp is always saturated: raw 0.6*CV = 0.1075 on our live rookie values and also above 0.08 on the sheet's own B column, so decay_rate is the constant 0.08 in practice, not a fitted parameter. (2) The 0.4-weight spine term allocates $446 of the $1200 board by DRAFT SLOT alone, with zero dependence on this year's rookie class — 37% of the rookie board is a 2023-2025 historical anchor.

formulas.name: KTC rookie exponential extrapolation
formulas.expression:
k = (ln(v1) - ln(vn)) / (n - 1)
A = v1 * exp(k)
projected[i] = max(1, round(A * exp(-k*i)))   for i in [n, 72)
formulas.inputs: known KTC rookies sorted desc
formulas.constants: total_picks = 72 (_KTC_TOTAL_PICKS, server.py:6729)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty input returns unchanged; v1 <= 0, vn <= 0, or n < 2 returns unchanged without extending, so the caller silently gets fewer than 72 rookies.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Off-by-one. The intended curve is value(i) = v1*exp(-k*i), which requires A = v1. The code sets A = v1*exp(k), so the curve evaluates to v1*exp(k) at i=0 rather than v1, and every extrapolated pick receives the value that belongs to the pick one slot ABOVE it. Numeric check on a realistic 40-rookie board (v1 9999, vn 800): k = 0.06476, curve at i=0 = 10,668 instead of 9,999; synthetic pick 41 = 800 when the correct value is 750. Systematic overvaluation of every extrapolated rookie by exp(k) = +6.7%. The inline comment at server.py:6826 asserts the opposite of what the line does.

formulas.name: Per-team draft-capital totals
formulas.expression:
per-pick displayed dollar = pick_values_per_slot[overall_idx]   # workbook column L
team_totals_decimal[owner] += float(val)                        # workbook column Q
team_totals = _round_to_budget(sorted decimals, 1200)

formulas.constants: DRAFT_TOTAL_BUDGET = 1200 (server.py:6730)

formulas.validated: I read both columns out of the live workbook: L2:L73 and Q45:Q116 are elementwise identical and both sum to 1200.0.
formulas.mathIssues: Latent inconsistency: displayed per-pick dollars come from L, team totals accumulate Q. They agree today, but the code comment at server.py:7305-7311 explicitly claims they DIFFER ('R5 picks read as $1.50 instead of being floored to $1'). Both columns read 2.0 at indices 48-59 in the live file, so the stated reason for choosing L over Q is not true of this workbook. If they ever diverge as documented, the sum of a team's displayed picks will not equal its reported total.

formulas.inputs: canonical contract playersArray
formulas.constants: 7000/4000/2000/1200/700/300/100 — invented, described in the code comment as 'Generous but monotonic'

For 2027 and 2028 it carries only 18 tier rows each ('2027 Early 1st' style). build_sleeper_derived iterates seasons (current_season, current_season+1), so EVERY 2027 pick misses and takes the flat table. Sum of real 2026 R1-R4 values = 147,020; sum of fabricated 2027 values = 170,400. The fabricated half is 53.7% of the normalized $1200 budget.

formulas.expression:
picks = seasons {S, S+1} x rounds 1..4 x slots 1..num_teams        # 96 rows at 12 teams
scale = 1200 / sum(raw_value)
dollar_values = raw * scale
rounded = largest-remainder to exactly 1200
formulas.inputs: Sleeper rosters/users/traded_picks + contract pick values
formulas.constants: _TARGET_TOTAL_BUDGET = 1200 (:36); draft_rounds default 4 (:108) — the caller at server.py:8206-8213 never passes it, so non-default leagues get 4 rounds while the workbook path has 6.

formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Three. (1) The $1200 is spread over TWO seasons here vs ONE in the workbook path, so a team's auctionDollars is not comparable between leagues despite carrying the same label and total — measured: 2026 Pick 1.01 renders as $29.60 here vs $134.50 on the workbook path. (2) `original_rid = slot` at :178 asserts that Sleeper roster_id N owns draft slot N in every round. I checked data/sleeper_last_good.json: roster_id 12 is 'Blaine', who holds pick 2026 1.02 — roster_id and draft slot are unrelated, so both the owner labels and the per-slot value lookups are wrong for any league where they differ. (3) The `num_teams` parameter accepted at :107 and passed by server.py:8210 is dead — :153 overwrites it with actual_num_teams.

server.py: floors = floor(v) ; deficit = budget - sum(floors) ; give +1 to the `deficit` largest fractional parts
fallback:  scaled = v*target/sum(v) ; floors = int(scaled) ; same distribution
formulas.inputs: list of floats

formulas.validated: none found

Harmless today but means the two 'same math, same invariant' functions (per the docstring at :251-252) are not in fact the same math.

formulas.expression: for each vendor key in {ktcRaw, idpRaw}: take rookies with a positive vendor value, sort desc by THAT vendor, run _rookie_dollars_from_values on the sorted vendor values, map rank N -> dollars[N]

formulas.constants: DRAFT_TOTAL_BUDGET
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No eligible rookies for a vendor -> empty map -> rookieKtcDollar / rookieIdpDollar null on every pick.

When a vendor covers fewer than 72 rookies the spine (which is read for len(values) rows) and the R5/R6 index caps at 48-72 land on different slots than for the full board, so the vendor dollars are on a subtly different curve than the ones they are compared against.

formulas.expression:
v = round(rankDerivedValue)
crossed = (direction == 'above' and v >= threshold) or (direction == 'below' and v <= threshold)
formulas.inputs: contract row rankDerivedValue; user rule threshold + direction
formulas.constants: COOLDOWN_HOURS = 24 (:54); rule cap 50 per user (server.py:10031)

formulas.inputs: row.rankChange stamped by the contract pipeline; minDelta validated to [1, 200] (:117-118)

The rule's real horizon is whatever window the pipeline used to compute rankChange, which the user never sees. Also, `title` is computed at :260 and then discarded: the Hit is constructed with title=' · '.join(body_parts[:1]) at :269, so the arrow/delta title is dead code.

An SMTP failure, a missing email, or delivery returning False all leave the state marked as notified. The alert is lost and will not retry for 12h — and if the signal does not change again, never.

site_count = number of rows in result['sites'] with playerCount > 0
total_sites = len(result['sites'])
if total_sites > 0 and site_count < total_sites / 2: do not promote

formulas.constants: the 1/2 ratio
formulas.missingDataBehavior: total_sites == 0 -> the guard is skipped entirely and the payload promotes unconditionally.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: MEASURED on the live export: `sites` has exactly TWO entries — ktc (500) and idpTradeCalc (900). The board is actually built from 22 sources (I counted canonicalSiteValues coverage on a freshly built contract: idpTradeCalc 911, ktc 609, ktcSfTep 501, pfkDynasty 475, fantasyProsSf 473, ... down to dlfRookieIdp 29). The gate therefore only trips if fewer than 1 of the 2 legacy sites returns data; a run where all 20 CSV-fed sources went stale but KTC and IDPTC responded promotes at full confidence.

formulas.name: Scrape success rate (24h)
formulas.location: server.py:1104-1125, with the recording sites at 1013-1051 and 1055-1086
formulas.expression:
recent = history entries with (now - ts) <= 86400
rate = count(outcome == 'success') / len(recent)
formulas.inputs: in-memory `scrape_history` list, capped at SCRAPE_HISTORY_MAX = 50 (server.py:679)
formulas.constants: 86400s window, 50-entry cap
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Empty history -> {'total':0, 'success':0, 'failure':0, 'rate': None}. The history is process-local and is lost on every restart, so '24h rate' is really 'since process start, up to 24h'.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: A BLOCKED partial scrape calls _mark_scrape_success (server.py:2380) after deciding NOT to promote, which records outcome='success', sets last_success_at, bumps scrape_count, and increments _metrics['scrape_total'] without touching scrape_failures. Monitoring sees 100% success while the board is frozen on stale data.

formulas.name: Data staleness and health classification
formulas.expression:
data_age_hours = (now - latest_data_source.loadedAt) / 3600
data_stale     = data_age_hours > SCRAPE_INTERVAL_HOURS * 3   # 6h
is_ok = (no last_error) and (not stalled) and (not data_stale) and contract_health.ok
HTTP 200 if is_ok else 503
formulas.inputs: latest_data_source.loadedAt (set by _set_latest_data_source, server.py:1308-1316)
formulas.constants: 3x multiplier on a 2h interval = 6h
formulas.missingDataBehavior: loadedAt unset or unparseable -> data_age_hours None and data_stale stays False, so a server that has never loaded data reports NOT stale.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: `is_ok` is computed at server.py:4426, before `circuits` at :4455 and `any_breaker_open` at :4457. The comment on :4456 says 'Any breaker in OPEN state flips overall status to degraded', but any_breaker_open is only emitted as a response field and never feeds is_ok or status.

formulas.name: Backup freshness alerting
formulas.expression:
newest = max mtime over /var/backups/riskit/daily/*.sqlite.gz and /home/dynasty/backups/riskit/daily/*.sqlite.gz
if age is None or age > 36h: send_alert(...)
formulas.inputs: filesystem
formulas.constants: 36h threshold
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No backup found -> newestBackupAgeHours None -> the None branch fires the alert, which is the correct direction.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: This alert fires from inside /api/health, which is polled every 60s by the frontend banner and every 300s by the uptime watchdog. send_alert has a single GLOBAL 3600s cooldown (server.py:236-239), so a persistently stale backup claims the cooldown slot and silently suppresses any scrape-failure or uptime alert raised in the same hour.

formulas.name: Session-cookie expiry classification
formulas.expression:
age_days = (now - mtime)/86400 ; days_remaining = max(0, lifetime_days - age_days)
warn_soon = (not auto_refresh) and days_remaining <= 14 and age_days > 0
expired   = (not auto_refresh) and days_remaining <= 0
formulas.inputs: mtime of dlf_session.json / draftsharks_session.json / idpshow_session.json
formulas.constants: lifetimeDays 14 / 30 / 90; warn window 14 days
formulas.missingDataBehavior: File absent -> {'present': False}; any OSError -> the same, so an unreadable file is indistinguishable from a missing one.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Uses file mtime as a proxy for cookie issue time. A `git checkout --force` or a redeploy that rewrites the file resets the clock without re-minting the cookie — the same class of problem _per_source_freshness (server.py:1550-1566) was explicitly rewritten to avoid, but the fix was not applied here.

formulas.name: Per-source freshness
formulas.expression:
last_epoch = float(data/scrape_state/{key}_last_success) if parseable else csv mtime
age_hours  = max(0, (now - last_epoch)/3600)
formulas.inputs: data/scrape_state stamps, CSV mtimes, _SOURCE_CSV_PATHS registry
formulas.constants: none here; the 24h alert threshold lives in config/source_staleness.json
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Neither stamp nor CSV -> the source is omitted from the output entirely, so a source that vanished is indistinguishable from one that was never registered.
formulas.validated: Live check: 27 of 31 stamps read 3.5-6.1h old, consistent with the 2h cadence. Three orphan stamps (footballGuys, footballGuysSf, footballGuysIdp) are 1,714h (71 days) old; that key is not in _SOURCE_CSV_PATHS, so they are never reported — dead files, not a live gap.
formulas.mathIssues: none found

findings.title: Sleeper-derived draft capital: 53.7% of every non-default league's $1200 board is a hardcoded constant, and pick ownership assumes roster_id == draft slot
findings.evidence: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:96-99 — `flat = {1: 7000.0, 2: 4000.0, 3: 2000.0, 4: 1200.0, 5: 700.0, 6: 300.0}; return flat.get(round_num, 100.0)`. :175 — `for season in (current_season, current_season + 1):`. :178 — `original_rid = slot  # stand-in: slot N = original owner roster N`. Live data check: exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json carries 72 rows named '2026 Pick R.SS' and ZERO rows named '2027 Pick R.SS' (2027 exists only as 18 'Early/Mid/Late Nth' tier rows). Every 2027 pick therefore takes the flat table. I summed the real 2026 R1-R4 rankDerivedValues from a freshly built contract: 147,020. The fabricated 2027 half: (7000+4000+2000+1200)*12 = 170,400. Fabricated share of the normalized budget = 53.7%. A fabricated 2027 R1 renders at $26.46 against a real 2026 1.01 at $29.60 — 89% of the best pick in the draft. Separately, data/sleeper_last_good.json shows roster_id 12 = 'Blaine' holding pick '2026 1.02', so roster_id and draft slot differ; the slot-as-roster-id assumption mislabels owners AND looks up the wrong slot's value.
findings.userImpact: Any user on a non-default league sees a draft-capital board where more than half the dollars are invented round constants and the team names attached to picks are wrong whenever roster_id != draft slot. The payload is labelled only 'Sleeper-derived, flat per-round valuation' — nothing distinguishes the fabricated rows from the Hill-curve-calibrated ones, which is exactly the failure tests/api/test_draft_capital_data_not_ready.py was written to prevent.
findings.recommendedFix: Return None from _pick_value_from_contract when no contract row matches, drop those picks from the board, and stamp a `pickYearsUnpriced` field so the UI can say which years it cannot value. Delete the flat table. Replace `original_rid = slot` with the real draft-slot map from /v1/draft/{id}.slot_to_roster_id (the workbook path already fetches exactly this at server.py:7655-7683) and fall back to omitting per-slot picks rather than guessing. Restrict the season loop to seasons the contract actually prices.
findings.affectedSystems: GET /api/draft-capital for every non-default league; frontend/app/draft/page.jsx DraftCapitalSection; any trade evaluation a user makes after reading that board.

findings.title: FAAB bid desk computes its share-of-pool denominator over draft picks, understating every recommended bid by ~2.6x versus the same formula elsewhere
findings.evidence: server.py:4967-4983 — `for row in arr: ... if rname in rostered_norms: continue ... if v > top_pool_value: top_pool_value = v`, with no asset-class, position, or value filter; passed at server.py:5139 as `top_value_in_pool=top_pool_value`. Draft picks live in playersArray and are never in a team's `players` name list, so they always survive the filter. I computed the pool from the live contract joined against data/sleeper_last_good.json (665 rostered names): top_pool_value = 7831, and the row is '2026 Pick 1.01'. The best actual free agent is Marlin Klein (TE) at 1905. Feeding both through src/trade/waiver.py:88-94: with top=7831, share = 0.2433 -> aggressive_pct = 0.1108 -> aggressive $11, reasonable $8. With top=1905 (the denominator src/trade/waiver.py:191-194 uses for the identical concept), share = 1.0 -> aggressive $30, reasonable $21. Ratio 2.62x.
findings.userImpact: The headline number on /waivers — the FAAB bid desk — recommends $8 where the same formula on the same board recommends $21. Users following it lose contested claims by a factor of two and a half. Because the denominator is a pick that no waiver pool contains, the error is invisible to inspection.
findings.recommendedFix: Filter the pool loop to `assetClass == 'offense' or 'idp'` (or simply exclude `assetClass == 'pick'`) and apply the same >=500 value and >=2 source-count floors src/trade/waiver.py already uses, then hoist the resulting pool computation into a single shared helper that both the endpoint and find_waiver_targets call. Add a regression row to the endpoint test fixture that includes a pick.
findings.affectedSystems: POST /api/waiver/faab-recommend; frontend/components/waivers/FaabRecommendation.jsx; `next_best_fa_value` (server.py:4978-4984) is computed in the same loop and is position-filtered, so it is unaffected — only the denominator is wrong.

findings.title: Three divergent implementations of one FAAB formula, two of them rendered side by side on /waivers
findings.evidence: The same `0.05 + 0.25*share` formula exists at src/trade/waiver.py:80-95 (Python), and is ported verbatim to frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js:864-879 (JS, comment at :851 says 'JS port of src/trade/waiver.py::_compute_faab_bid'). Each caller supplies a different denominator: server.py:4967 = all unrostered rows incl. picks (7831 live); src/trade/waiver.py:191 = filtered candidates (1905 live); frontend/app/waivers/page.jsx:166-175 = max over the ~20 bestMoves rows currently rendered. The frontend also hardcodes `leagueBudget: 100` at waivers/page.jsx:213 and :219, while the backend resolves the real budget at server.py:5051-5060. And `league_budget` means REMAINING dollars in one Python caller (src/trade/waiver.py:202 passes `user_faab_remaining`) but LEAGUE budget in the other (src/trade/faab_recommender.py:322-326).
findings.userImpact: On the /waivers page the 'FAAB hint' column and the bid desk below it disagree for the same player. Because the frontend denominator is the max of the displayed batch, the top row of that column always reads exactly $21 no matter who the player is — an artifact users will read as a real number. A user in a $200 league gets frontend hints computed against $100.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete computeFaabHint and have the bestMoves table render backend-supplied bids (find_waiver_targets already computes them). Rename the `league_budget` parameter of _compute_faab_bid to make the semantics explicit and fix src/trade/waiver.py:202 to pass the league budget with the remaining balance applied as a cap, matching the recommender.
findings.affectedSystems: frontend/app/waivers/page.jsx, frontend/lib/waiver-logic.js, src/trade/waiver.py, src/trade/faab_recommender.py, server.py FAAB endpoint

findings.title: League position calibration collapses a 19x player-value spread into a 1.12x bid spread
findings.evidence: src/trade/faab_recommender.py:191-194 — `blended = 0.5 * float(avg_for_pos) + 0.5 * float(bid_estimate)`, gated only on `count_for_pos >= 3` (:186). `avg_for_pos` comes from src/api/faab_analytics.py, which appends every winning bid for that position across every season with no player-quality stratification. Worked example using the test suite's own TE average of $30 and the live endpoint denominator: value 1905 -> baseline $8 -> blended $19; value 1500 -> $18; value 1000 -> $18; value 700 -> $18; value 500 -> $18; value 300 -> $17; value 100 -> $17. A 19.05x range in player value produces a 1.12x range in recommended bid.
findings.userImpact: Once a position has three historical bids, the recommendation stops discriminating between a genuine league-winner and a dart throw — it returns the position's historical average plus or minus a dollar. That is worse than the uncalibrated formula, because the number now looks league-aware.
findings.recommendedFix: Calibrate against the position AND value-tier bucket, not the position alone (faab_analytics already computes tierBids at :48-53 and nothing consumes them). Or make the blend weight a function of sample size rather than a flat 0.5. Either way, add a regression test that asserts the bid is monotone and materially separated across a value ladder.
findings.affectedSystems: POST /api/waiver/faab-recommend whenever a public-league snapshot is loaded

findings.title: A blocked partial scrape is recorded as a success, so monitoring reports 100% health while the board is frozen
findings.evidence: server.py:2364 `if total_sites > 0 and site_count < total_sites / 2:` — the not-promoted branch — calls `_mark_scrape_success(elapsed, player_count, site_count, total_sites)` at server.py:2380 before `return latest_data`. _mark_scrape_success (server.py:1013-1051) sets last_success_at, clears `error`, sets current_step 'complete', increments scrape_count, records `_record_scrape_history('success', ...)` and bumps `_metrics['scrape_total']` without touching `scrape_failures`. Consequently `_scrape_success_rate_24h` (server.py:1104-1125) counts it as a success and /api/health's `is_ok` (server.py:4426-4431) sees no last_error.
findings.userImpact: The exact failure the guard exists to catch — sites down or blocking — produces a green dashboard. The only signal is a send_alert email, which is subject to the global 1h cooldown described below.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a `_mark_scrape_partial` path that records outcome='partial', leaves last_success_at alone, and sets an explicit `last_partial_at` + error string so /api/health and the 24h rate both reflect it.

findings.title: The partial-scrape promotion gate's denominator is 2, not the 22 sources that build the board
findings.evidence: server.py:2358-2364 counts `site_count` and `total_sites` over `result.get('sites', [])`. Live export exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json has `sites` = [('ktc', 500), ('idpTradeCalc', 900)] — two entries. I built the canonical contract from that export and counted canonicalSiteValues coverage: 22 distinct sources contribute (idpTradeCalc 911, ktc 609, ktcSfTep 501, pfkDynasty 475, fantasyProsSf 473, fantasyNavigatorSf 455, otcffbSf 450, flockFantasySf 415, draftSharks 415, fantasyCalc 393, yahooBoone 376, dynastyDaddySf 364, idpShow 349, draftSharksIdp 301, fantasyProsFitzmaurice 299, dynastyNerdsSfTep 293, dlfSf 280, fantasyProsIdp 211, dlfIdp 171, dlfRookieSf 110, flockFantasySfRookies 76, dlfRookieIdp 29). server.py:4200-4204 already acknowledges the `sites` list 'cannot detect a degraded board' for source_health, but the promotion gate was never updated with it.
findings.userImpact: A scrape in which all 20 CSV-fed sources silently went stale but KTC and IDPTC responded passes the gate and promotes. The board's blend quality can collapse without the guard ever firing.
findings.recommendedFix: Compute the gate from the per-source coverage the contract actually produces (_compute_served_source_coverage, server.py:413-428, already does this) or from `settings.sourceRunSummary.enabledSources` vs `completeSources`, both of which _build_source_health_snapshot already parses at server.py:1424-1452.
findings.affectedSystems: run_scraper promotion decision; every downstream value

findings.title: Custom `value_crosses` alerts are level tests, not crossing tests — they re-fire every 24 hours forever
findings.evidence: src/news/custom_alerts.py:230-232 — `crossed = (direction == 'above' and v >= threshold) or (direction == 'below' and v <= threshold)`. No prior value is stored: mark_fired (:280-286) writes only `{'lastFiredAt': ...}` and _is_cooldown (:149-160) only compares that timestamp against COOLDOWN_HOURS = 24. The module docstring at :5-8 says 'fires when rankDerivedValue CROSSES a target' and 'the rule fires once per cooldown window when the threshold is crossed in the configured direction'.
findings.userImpact: A user who sets 'alert me when Player X goes above 7000' gets an email and a push notification every single day for as long as the player stays above 7000. With 50 rules allowed per user (server.py:10031), a handful of satisfied rules turns the daily sweep into a spam engine, and users will disable notifications entirely — losing the signal alerts too.
findings.recommendedFix: Persist the last observed value alongside lastFiredAt and require a genuine edge (`prev < threshold <= now` for 'above'). Missing prior value should seed silently on the first sweep, the same baseline-seeding pattern src/api/bdvm_signal_alerts.py already uses.

findings.title: /api/movers anchors on the first snapshot present rather than the requested window, so the labelled '14d' delta can be a 2-day delta
findings.evidence: server.py:3390 `history = _rank_history.load_history(days=window + 1)`, and src/api/rank_history.py:369 implements that as `windowed = entries[-max(1, int(days)):]` — the last N SNAPSHOTS, not N days. server.py:3445 then takes `anchor = series[0]` with no date check whatsoever; the entry's `date` field is read only for `asOf` at :3501. The frontend renders the result as 'Rank deltas vs. {windowDays}d ago' (frontend/components/terminal/MoversPanel.jsx:166).
findings.userImpact: For any player who entered the board recently, or during any period where scrapes were missed (the log is appended only on fresh-scrape promotion, server.py:1858), the reported delta covers an unknown and shorter or longer interval than the label claims. A 20-spot rise 'over 14 days' may have happened in 2 days, or over 40 days if the log has gaps. The panel is presented as buy-low / sell-high guidance.
findings.recommendedFix: Select the anchor by date: take the newest entry whose date is <= (asOf - window days), and skip the player entirely when no such entry exists rather than substituting series[0]. Return the anchor's actual date on each row so the UI can label the real interval.

findings.title: Movers panel labels risers as buy-low and fallers as sell-high — inverted
findings.evidence: server.py:3444-3449 defines `delta = r_then - r_now` with rank-smaller-better, so `delta > 0` means the player's rank IMPROVED and they are appended to `risers` (server.py:3494-3495). frontend/components/terminal/MoversPanel.jsx:192-193 renders that list under 'Risers — buy-low candidates', and :207-208 renders `fallers` (rank got worse) under 'Fallers — sell-high candidates'.
findings.userImpact: The panel tells the user to buy players who have just appreciated and sell players who have just depreciated — the opposite of the strategy the labels name. This is a direct trade recommendation on the terminal.
findings.recommendedFix: Swap the two subtitles: fallers are buy-low candidates, risers are sell-high candidates. Verify against src/trade/suggestions.py, which already implements sell-high/buy-low with the conventional polarity.

findings.title: Signal alerts mark themselves delivered before delivery is attempted, so a failed send is silently dropped for 12 hours or forever
findings.evidence: src/api/signal_alerts.py:198-201 sets `new_state[state_key] = {'signal': signal, 'notifiedAt': now}` inside detect_signal_transitions, and :211-231 persists it to user_kv unconditionally. process_user_alerts (:290-323) only THEN calls `delivery(...)` and, on exception, returns `{'delivered': False, 'reason': 'delivery_error:...'}` (:319-323) without any state rollback. The `no_email` (:298) and `no_delivery_configured` (:304) branches have the same shape.
findings.userImpact: An SMTP outage during the daily sweep loses that day's signal alerts permanently. Because the state now records the new signal, the 'signal != prev_signal' condition at :171 will not re-fire unless the signal changes again. Silent, and there is no retry.
findings.recommendedFix: Split the write: compute transitions purely, then persist notifiedAt only for the transitions whose delivery returned True. Persist last_seen_signal separately (it should update regardless).
findings.affectedSystems: POST /api/signal-alerts/run; the whole email digest path

findings.title: send_alert uses one global 1-hour cooldown across all subjects, and /api/health burns it on backup staleness
findings.evidence: server.py:227 `ALERT_COOLDOWN_SEC = 3600` and server.py:236-239 `if now - _last_alert_time < ALERT_COOLDOWN_SEC: log.info(f'Alert suppressed (cooldown): {subject}'); return` — a single module-level `_last_alert_time` shared by every caller. server.py:4472-4478 calls send_alert from inside get_health whenever `newestBackupAgeHours` is None or > 36. /api/health is polled every 60s by the frontend StaleDataBanner (per the comment at server.py:1524-1526) and every 300s by the uptime watchdog.
findings.userImpact: With backups stale — which is exactly when other things are likely wrong — a scrape failure (server.py:2447-2450), a partial-scrape block (server.py:2369-2379), a disk-space emergency (server.py:2402-2411) or an uptime outage (server.py:2528-2538) will be silently suppressed. The operator gets one backup email an hour and nothing else.
findings.recommendedFix: Key the cooldown per subject (or per alert category) rather than globally, and move the backup check out of the request path onto the existing daily sweep at server.py:11578, which already has per-alert cooldown state in user_kv.
findings.affectedSystems: All operator alerting: run_scraper, uptime_watchdog_loop, get_health

findings.title: The rookie dollar board silently reshapes by up to +65% when the Draft Data workbook cannot be read
findings.evidence: server.py:7109-7131 — `_read_sheet_spine_and_floor` wraps the whole read in `try/except Exception: return [1.0] * n, 0` and _load_draft_workbook (server.py:7083-7107) returns None on `ImportError` for openpyxl. A flat spine makes `excess[i] = max(0, 1.0 - 1) = 0` for every row (server.py:7186), so `term2` is all zeros and the 0.4-weighted half of server.py:7194 vanishes. I ran both paths on the live rookie board: with the workbook spine, picks 1-12 are [135.5, 105.5, 91.5, 82.0, 76.0, 68.5, 60.0, 53.0, 48.0, 43.0, 39.0, 34.5]; without it they are [122.0, 101.0, 92.0, 86.0, 82.0, 77.5, 73.5, 68.0, 65.5, 62.0, 59.5, 57.0]. Pick 12 moves from $34.50 to $57.00, +65%. sum(C) drops from 1200.0 to 753.6, but the R1-carryover mechanism at server.py:7228-7237 absorbs the shortfall so the TOTAL still reads exactly 1200 and nothing in the payload changes. openpyxl is listed in requirements.txt:33 but is not installed in this audit environment, so the degraded path is reachable in practice.
findings.userImpact: A missing dependency or an unreadable workbook produces a completely different auction board that passes every visible invariant (sums to $1200, monotone, correct row count). Nothing in the response distinguishes it. Users bid real money off it.
findings.recommendedFix: Have _read_sheet_spine_and_floor return None on failure and make _rookie_dollars_from_values propagate that, so _fetch_draft_capital can stamp `spineSource: 'missing'` on the payload and the UI can refuse to show dollar values. At minimum, log at ERROR rather than swallowing.
findings.affectedSystems: GET /api/draft-capital rookieKtcValue / rookieKtcDollar / rookieIdpDollar; frontend/app/draft/page.jsx RookieBoard and auction panel

findings.title: _ktc_decay_curve is off by one slot, overvaluing every extrapolated rookie by exp(k)
findings.evidence: server.py:6825-6826 — `k = (math.log(v1) - math.log(vn)) / (n - 1)` then `A = v1 * math.exp(k)  # A = v1 / e^(-k*0) adjusted so pick index 0 → v1`. The comment asserts the curve passes through v1 at i=0, but A*exp(-k*0) = v1*exp(k) != v1. Numeric check on a realistic 40-rookie board (v1 9999, vn 800): k = 0.06476, exp(k) = 1.0669, curve at i=0 = 10,668 not 9,999. Synthetic picks 41-48 come out [800, 750, 703, 659, 617, 579, 542, 508] where the correct fit gives [750, 703, 659, 617, 579, 542, 508, 477] — each extrapolated pick receives the value belonging to the slot above it. Systematic +6.7% overvaluation.
findings.userImpact: Only reachable when _our_rookie_pool is empty (rookieSource == 'ktc_fallback'), which is not the live case today — the live contract has 127 rookies with playerIds. But when it fires, the tail of the rookie board is uniformly inflated and the ordering relative to real KTC entries is distorted at the boundary.
findings.recommendedFix: Set `A = v1` and drop the exp(k) factor, or equivalently index the projection from i-n. Add a unit test asserting the fitted curve reproduces v1 at i=0 and vn at i=n-1.
findings.affectedSystems: GET /api/draft-capital when the canonical contract has no rookies

findings.title: /api/health computes any_breaker_open after deciding the status, so an open circuit breaker never degrades health — contradicting the comment beside it
findings.evidence: server.py:4426 `is_ok = (...)` and server.py:4432 `status = 'ok' if is_ok else 'degraded'` both execute before server.py:4455 `circuits = _circuits_safe()` and server.py:4457 `any_breaker_open = any(c.get('state') == 'open' for c in circuits)`. The comment on server.py:4456 reads 'Any breaker in OPEN state flips overall status to degraded.' The variable is only emitted as a response field at server.py:4501 and never read.
findings.userImpact: An open circuit breaker on a source or an external dependency leaves /api/health returning HTTP 200 'ok'. Any monitor wired to the status code — including the uptime watchdog at server.py:2466-2486, which treats 200-399 as up — sees a healthy service.
findings.recommendedFix: Move the circuits computation above is_ok and add `and not any_breaker_open` to the conjunction, or delete the comment if the current behavior is intended.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's league-mismatch error table is wrong for /api/terminal and /api/trade/simulate
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md states: '/api/terminal, /api/trade/*, /api/angle/* — 503 whenever the loaded contract's leagueKey doesn't match the request.' Neither endpoint passes require_loaded_contract: server.py:10332 `league_cfg = _resolve_league_for_request(request)` and server.py:10582 `league_cfg = _resolve_league_for_request(request, body=body)`. Both then deliberately splice a live Sleeper overlay onto the loaded rankings on a leagueKey mismatch (server.py:10360-10420 and 10594-10640) and 503 only when the SCORING PROFILE differs or the overlay fetch fails. The six endpoints that do pass the flag are at server.py:4790, 4879, 5841, 5973, 6189, 6313. The draft-capital divergence from the same table is documented at length as Defect D-2; this pair is not acknowledged anywhere.
findings.userImpact: An operator or a future change reading the CLAUDE.md table will believe cross-league requests are refused on these two endpoints and may add a guard that removes working multi-league functionality — or, worse, will fail to notice that the terminal serves one league's rankings against another league's rosters and reason about it as if it could not happen.
findings.recommendedFix: Update the CLAUDE.md table to distinguish 'refuses on leagueKey mismatch' (trade/suggestions, trade/finder, angle/*, waiver/*) from 'splices the requested league's overlay onto shared rankings, refuses only on scoring-profile mismatch' (terminal, trade/simulate), and add the equivalent of tests/api/test_draft_capital_data_not_ready.py to pin the intended behavior.

findings.title: /api/scaffold/* has no producer in the repository — every response is served from files last written 2026-04-20
findings.evidence: server.py:4656-4750 and 6456-6481 read `data/raw_sources/raw_source_snapshot_*.json`, `data/validation/ingest_validation_*.json`, `data/league/league_snapshot_*.json`, `data/identity/identity_*.json`, `data/reports/ops_report_*.md`. I grepped every .py and .yml in the tree: the only writers are scripts/validate_ingest.py and scripts/identity_resolve.py (manual CLI, not referenced by any workflow under .github/workflows/) plus src/maintenance/retention.py, which only PRUNES them. On disk: newest raw_source_snapshot is 20260420T194828Z and newest identity_report is 20260420T194828Z — 105 days stale at the audit date of 2026-08-04. data/league, data/validation and data/reports do not exist at all.
findings.userImpact: /api/scaffold/status is a PUBLIC endpoint (server.py:2743) reporting record counts, ingest validation status and identity conflict counts that are 15 weeks old, with a timestamp field that dates the file rather than the pipeline. /api/scaffold/league, /validation and /report are permanently empty or 404. Anyone treating these as pipeline health is reading a fossil. This is consistent with CLAUDE.md's note that the canonical-build path was retired — the endpoints were not.
findings.recommendedFix: Either wire the scripts into the 2h refresh workflow, or delete the six routes and the retention rules that reference them. If retained, stamp `stale: true` when the newest file exceeds a threshold rather than reporting a bare mtime.

findings.title: Public /api/status leaks raw Sleeper league IDs; public /api/scaffold/status leaks absolute server filesystem paths
findings.evidence: server.py:2735 and 2743 place '/api/status' and '/api/scaffold/status' in _PUBLIC_API_EXACT. server.py:4326 `'sleeperLeagueId': cfg.sleeper_league_id` inside _league_status_snapshot, emitted at server.py:4205 as `'leagues': _league_status_snapshot()`. server.py:4678 `'path': str(path)` inside get_scaffold_status's _meta helper, emitted for five separate files. CLAUDE.md's API table states for /api/leagues: 'no Sleeper IDs leaked', and the routing section states 'no endpoint exposes raw Sleeper IDs to the UI'.
findings.userImpact: Unauthenticated callers get the Sleeper league IDs for every active league (enabling direct enumeration of rosters, transactions and drafts via Sleeper's open API) and the absolute deploy path of the data directory. The invariant CLAUDE.md asserts is violated by a different endpoint than the one it names.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop sleeperLeagueId from _league_status_snapshot or gate the field on _is_authenticated (the pattern _redact_draft_capital_for_public already establishes at server.py:6759-6791). Replace the absolute path in _meta with the basename only.

findings.title: Draft-capital per-pick dollars come from workbook column L while per-team totals sum column Q
findings.evidence: server.py:7973-7977 sets the displayed value from `pick_values_per_slot[overall_idx]` (column L2:L73, wired at server.py:7512-7514), while server.py:8001 accumulates `team_totals_decimal[owner_team] += float(val)` where `val = wp['value']` comes from column Q45:Q116 (server.py:7318). The code comment at server.py:7305-7311 claims L 'is NOT expansion-pair-averaged like Q45:Q116, so R5 picks read as $1.50 instead of being floored to $1'. I read both columns out of the live CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx: they are elementwise IDENTICAL across all 72 rows and both sum to 1200.0; rows 48-59 read 2.0 in both, not 1.5 and 1.0.
findings.userImpact: No wrong number today. But the code's own stated rationale for reading two columns is false of the live workbook, and if the user ever edits L and Q apart as the comment describes, a team's displayed picks will silently stop summing to its reported auctionDollars.
findings.recommendedFix: Accumulate `dollar` (the L value) into team_totals_decimal so both surfaces read one column, and correct or delete the comment at server.py:7305-7311.

findings.title: FAAB confidence cannot fall below 'medium' when only the formula itself is present
findings.evidence: src/trade/faab_recommender.py:327-333 unconditionally appends a 'Player value baseline' factor with weight 0.35 and missing=False — it is the formula, not an input. compute_confidence (:141-146) buckets on realized_weight/total_weight with cutoffs 0.85 and 0.55. Worked example on live data (Marlin Klein, no drop, no public-league snapshot, no contention, trending count 0): factors are baseline 0.35 present, trending 0.15 present, league history 0.20 missing, contention 0.15 missing -> 0.50/0.90 = 0.588 -> 'medium'. Several branches (crowd blend at :419, env scaling at :439, value-gain when the modifier lands in [0.95, 1.05] at :338-354) append nothing at all when they do not fire, so their absence neither enlarges the denominator nor lowers the score.
findings.userImpact: A recommendation derived from zero market inputs is presented to the user as medium confidence. The label cannot distinguish 'we have league history, crowd data and rival estimates' from 'we have a formula and a zero'.
findings.recommendedFix: Remove the baseline from the factor weighting (or mark it as structural rather than evidential), and always append a missing row for the crowd and env-scaling factors so the denominator is constant.

findings.title: /api/movers documents a perSourceDelta field that does not exist and computes no deltas
findings.evidence: The docstring at server.py:3358-3361 documents the response shape as containing `"perSourceDelta": {...}`, and the comment at server.py:3467-3468 says 'Per-source rank deltas — useful so the user can see "this move was driven by KTC dropping them 25 spots"'. The code at server.py:3470-3476 copies `row.get('sourceOriginalRanks')` verbatim into a dict named `per_source_delta` and emits it at server.py:3492 under the key `currentSourceRanks` — current absolute ranks, no subtraction anywhere.
findings.userImpact: The expandable per-source breakdown in MoversPanel shows each source's current rank, not its contribution to the move — the attribution the panel's own header comment (MoversPanel.jsx:14-16) promises. A user cannot tell which source drove the delta.
findings.recommendedFix: Either compute real per-source deltas (which requires per-source ranks in the history log — src/api/source_history.py:552-554 already records sourceRanks for snapshots after 2026-04-29), or correct the docstring and the variable name to match what is served.

findings.title: player-source-history docstring says 'max 180' while the code allows 1095
findings.evidence: server.py:3559 — '``days`` — window in days (default 180, max 180)'. server.py:3577 — `days = max(1, min(_source_history.MAX_SNAPSHOTS, requested))` where src/api/source_history.py:55 sets `MAX_SNAPSHOTS: int = 365 * 3`. The sibling rank-history docstring at server.py:3529-3532 explicitly calls out having made and fixed this exact error ('This line used to say "max 180", which is the player-source-history window below, not this one') — and the endpoint it points at still has it.
findings.userImpact: A caller can request 1095 snapshots and get a payload six times larger than documented; the chart component requests 180 (frontend/components/PlayerRankHistoryChart.jsx:41) so nothing breaks today.
findings.recommendedFix: Change the docstring to 'default 180, max MAX_SNAPSHOTS (1095)'.

findings.title: require_loaded_contract silently no-ops when the loaded contract carries no meta.leagueKey
findings.evidence: server.py:6596-6612 — `loaded_key = (latest_contract_data or {}).get('meta', {}).get('leagueKey')` then `if loaded_key and loaded_key != cfg.key: raise LeagueResolutionError(503, ...)`. When latest_contract_data is None, or is a contract whose meta block is missing or unstamped, loaded_key is None and the guard passes for ANY requested league. Every current caller happens to check `latest_contract_data` truthiness first (e.g. server.py:4776-4780, 4866-4870), so the None case is covered by convention rather than by the guard.
findings.userImpact: No live impact found. But a future caller that relies on the flag alone will serve one league's data under another league's key, and the failure will be silent.
findings.recommendedFix: Treat a falsy latest_contract_data or an absent meta.leagueKey as data_not_ready rather than as a pass.
findings.affectedSystems: _resolve_league_for_request and its six require_loaded_contract call sites

findings.title: Dead and incorrect return value in _read_sheet_spine_and_floor
findings.evidence: server.py:7130 — `return spine, n  # R5 bonus = +$1 × 12 picks = $12 total floor add`. The docstring at server.py:7113-7118 says the second value is 'the $12 floor injection for picks 5.01–5.12 (== 12 in a 12-team league)'. The function returns `n` — 72 for a full board, not 12. The value is unpacked at server.py:7169 as `spine, r5_bonus_count = ...` and then never referenced again; _rookie_dollars_from_values recomputes the floors itself at server.py:7191.
findings.userImpact: None functionally. A reader inspecting the R5 bonus mechanism is pointed at a variable that is both wrong and unused.
findings.recommendedFix: Change the signature to return only the spine, and delete r5_bonus_count from the call site.

findings.title: draft_capital_fallback accepts a num_teams parameter it immediately discards, and defaults to 4 draft rounds where the workbook path uses 6
findings.evidence: src/api/draft_capital_fallback.py:107 declares `num_teams: int = 12`; :153 overwrites it with `actual_num_teams = max(len(rosters), 1)` and nothing reads the parameter again. server.py:8206-8213 nonetheless computes and passes it (`num_teams=league_cfg.roster_settings.get('teamCount', 12) if hasattr(...) else 12`). Separately, :108 declares `draft_rounds: int = 4` and the server call site never passes it, while the workbook path derives 6 rounds (server.py:7509, `draft_rounds = max(1, len(workbook_picks) // num_teams)` with 72 picks / 12 teams).
findings.userImpact: Non-default leagues see a 4-round draft-capital board while the default league sees 6, with no indication that rounds 5 and 6 are simply absent from the totals. A team whose capital is concentrated in late picks is understated.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete the dead num_teams parameter and thread the real draft_rounds from league_cfg.roster_settings (or from Sleeper's league settings.draft_rounds, which data/sleeper_last_good.json shows is present in leagueSettings).

findings.title: The rookie dollar formula's fitted decay_rate is always clamped to its ceiling, and 40% of the board is allocated by draft slot regardless of the rookie class
findings.evidence: server.py:7173-7180 — `decay_rate = max(0.03, min(0.08, 0.6 * head_std / head_mean))`. Measured on the live rookie board (top 6 values 7831, 6185, 5579, 5333, 5222, 4992) the raw quantity is 0.1075, above the 0.08 ceiling; it is also above the ceiling for the workbook's own column-B values. server.py:7194 — `c_vals = [floors_per_row[i] + pool * (0.6 * term1[i] + 0.4 * term2[i])]` where term2 is the fixed 2023-2025 slot spine from workbook column E. With a $1116 distributable pool, that fixed term allocates $446 — 37% of the $1200 board — by draft slot alone.
findings.userImpact: The formula is presented (server.py:7137-7160) as a value-driven Hill curve with a data-fitted decay. In practice the decay parameter is the constant 0.08, and more than a third of the dollars are a historical slot anchor with no dependence on how strong this year's rookie class is. A weak class and a loaded class produce nearly the same top-of-board dollars.
findings.recommendedFix: None required for correctness — this faithfully reproduces the user's sheet. But document that decay_rate is saturated in practice, and surface the term1/term2 split in the payload so the /draft page can say how much of a rookie's dollar figure is slot anchor versus this year's board.

findings.title: FAAB rival contention is structurally unreachable whenever the live Sleeper overlay fetch fails
findings.evidence: server.py:5202-5209 requires `usable_balances * 2 >= len(opponents)` where usable_balances counts opponents with an integer faabRemaining. When the overlay fetch at server.py:4946-4956 fails, sleeper_teams falls back to the baked block at server.py:4941. I inspected data/sleeper_last_good.json: all 12 teams have `faabRemaining: null` and `faabBudget: null`, because only src/api/sleeper_overlay.py:466-468 populates those fields — the scraper's Sleeper block does not. The endpoint's own comment at server.py:4931-4933 states this.
findings.userImpact: On any Sleeper outage the contention model, the replaceability gate and the team FAAB cap all silently disappear together; `max` reverts to the full league budget and the recommendation degrades to the pure value formula. The response does report `contention.skipped: true` with a reason, so it is honest — but the reason given ('rival FAAB balances unavailable for most opponents') does not distinguish a Sleeper outage from a league that genuinely does not use FAAB.
findings.recommendedFix: Distinguish the two skip reasons in the note, and set `max` to null rather than the league budget when the team's real balance is unknown.

notes:
WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY. Three inputs the FAAB and movers systems depend on are gitignored and absent from this checkout: data/rank_history.jsonl, data/source_value_history.jsonl and data/public_league/snapshot.json. On this repo state /api/movers returns empty and the FAAB recommender always reports league analytics missing. I cannot say what production holds — everything I claim about those three is about the code path, not the live values. openpyxl is in requirements.txt but is not installed here, so I read CSVs/Draft Data.xlsx by unzipping it and parsing sheet1.xml directly; the numbers are the file's, not openpyxl's.

WHAT VALIDATED CLEANLY. _rookie_dollars_from_values is the one formula in this subsystem with a verifiable ground truth, and it passes: fed the workbook's own column-B values and column-E spine it reproduces column L2:L73 exactly, max absolute difference 0.0 across all 72 rows, both summing to 1200.0. The pick-tethering claim in CLAUDE.md also checks out live — rookie #1 (Jeremiyah Love, 7831) carries exactly the 2026 Pick 1.01 value, and the whole top-12 rookie ladder is identical to the 2026 R1 pick ladder. The `_stamp_valuation_mode` contract holds: every audited lens-applying handler stamps the mode including "market", and tests/api/test_valuation_mode_threading.py enforces it statically. The `_redact_draft_capital_for_public` copy-not-mutate discipline is correct and the cache-poisoning trap it documents is real.

THE PATTERN WORTH NAMING. Four of the five worst findings share one shape: a number is computed from a denominator or a lookup that silently substitutes something wrong rather than failing. top_pool_value substitutes a draft pick for a free agent. _pick_value_from_contract substitutes a hardcoded constant for a market value. _read_sheet_spine_and_floor substitutes a flat spine for the historical anchor. _compute_faab_bid substitutes share=1.0 — the maximum bid — when the denominator is missing. In every case the output stays inside its plausible range and every visible invariant still holds (sums to $1200, monotone, correct row count), so nothing downstream can detect it. The codebase's own comments show the authors know this pattern is the enemy — tests/api/test_draft_capital_data_not_ready.py opens with "Plausible and wrong is the worst combination available" — but the guard they built for it covers only the no-contract case, and I measured that the with-contract case still fabricates 53.7% of that board.

TESTS THAT LOOK LIKE COVERAGE AND ARE NOT. tests/api/test_faab_recommend_endpoint.py has 16 tests and tests/trade/test_faab_recommender.py has 30, which reads as a thoroughly pinned system. Every one of them pins response shape or branch mechanics. None asserts a bid magnitude against a realized outcome, and the endpoint fixture's contract (test_faab_recommend_endpoint.py:123-155) has four offense rows and zero picks, so the defect that makes every live bid 2.6x too small cannot be expressed in it. tests/api/test_draft_capital_data_not_ready.py includes an explicit non-vacuity test asserting a populated contract beats the flat table — using a synthetic "2027 Pick 1.01" row. The live contract has never contained a row of that name for any year but 2026, so the branch the test proves reachable is the one production never reaches.

DEAD OR UNREACHABLE CODE FOUND. `r5_bonus_count` (server.py:7169) is unpacked and never used, and the value returned is 72 where the docstring promises 12. `num_teams` in build_sleeper_derived is accepted, passed by the caller, and overwritten one line into the function body. The `title` local in custom_alerts.py:260 is computed and discarded. `_ktc_decay_curve` is unreachable while the contract has rookies. `any_breaker_open` is computed and emitted but never affects the health status its own comment says it controls. The three footballGuys `_last_success` stamps are 71 days old for a source key that is not in `_SOURCE_CSV_PATHS` at all.

DOC/CODE DISAGREEMENTS, CONSOLIDATED. CLAUDE.md's league-mismatch error table is wrong for /api/terminal and /api/trade/simulate (both splice an overlay instead of 503-ing). CLAUDE.md's "no endpoint exposes raw Sleeper IDs to the UI" is violated by the public /api/status. custom_alerts.py's module docstring promises crossing detection the code does not implement. draft_capital_fallback.py's docstring describes a 501 branch that has never existed and claims a budget comparability that the two-season denominator does not provide. /api/movers documents a perSourceDelta field it does not emit. /api/data/player-source-history documents "max 180" against a code limit of 1095 — the same error its sibling docstring at server.py:3529 congratulates itself on having fixed. server.py:6826 asserts a curve passes through v1 at i=0 when it passes through v1*exp(k). server.py:7305-7311 justifies reading column L over Q with a difference that does not exist in the live workbook. server.py:4456 states that an open circuit breaker degrades health, which it does not.

ONE THING I'D RANK ABOVE ALL THE REST IF FORCED TO PICK. The FAAB bid desk. It is the headline number on /waivers, a user acts on it with real budget, and it is wrong twice over in the same direction of harm: the denominator is 4.1x too large, and then the 50/50 position blend flattens whatever discrimination survived — measured, a 19x spread in player value produces a 1.12x spread in recommended dollars. The endpoint returns "medium confidence" while doing it.

formulas.name: Sample-size score
formulas.expression: ss = clamp(0.7*clamp(total_games/34,0,1) + 0.3*clamp(recency_games/12,0,1), 0, 1)
formulas.inputs: total_games (count), recency_games (count)
formulas.constants: 34 = full-history denominator (2 seasons of 17); 12 = recency denominator; 0.7/0.3 split. All hand-picked, no calibration evidence in repo.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: float(0) → 0.0; no distinction between 'zero games' and 'games unknown'
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: none arithmetic; denominators encode a 17-game season implicitly

formulas.name: Empirical-Bayes shrinkage of the scoring ratio
formulas.expression: prior=clamp(archetype_prior,0.75,1.25); w=clamp(0.55*ss + 0.25*rs + 0.20*(1-pw), 0.05, 0.95); blended_prior=0.65*prior+0.35*1.0; shrunk=clamp(raw*w + blended_prior*(1-w), 0.75, 1.25)
formulas.inputs: raw_ratio (league PPG / baseline PPG), sample_size_score, role_stability_score (fed the caller's `confidence` at :83), projection_weight, archetype_prior_ratio
formulas.constants: 0.55/0.25/0.20 weight split; 0.05/0.95 weight clamp; 0.65/0.35 prior blend; 0.75/1.25 ratio clamp. All hand-picked; nothing in config/ or docs/ records a fit.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: archetype_prior_ratio defaults to 1.0 (:71), making blended_prior exactly 1.0 — a missing archetype is indistinguishable from a neutral one.
formulas.validated: none found — tests/scoring/test_scoring_modules.py checks only that outputs stay inside the clamps
formulas.mathIssues: The weight on the player's own observation never falls below 0.05 nor rises above 0.95, so the shrinkage can neither fully trust nor fully distrust the data. 'role_stability_score' is fed `confidence` at line 83, conflating two concepts.

formulas.name: Ratio → multiplier
formulas.inputs: shrunk_ratio in [0.75,1.25]
formulas.constants: alpha 0.60; log bounds ±0.12; multiplier clamp [0.90,1.12]
formulas.outputRange: [0.9305, 1.0746] in practice — the log bound binds long before the multiplier clamp. exp(0.6*0.12)=1.0746, exp(-0.6*0.12)=0.9305, so the declared 0.90/1.12 clamp is DEAD CODE.
formulas.missingDataBehavior: ratio floored at 0.01 (:49) before the log, so a zero ratio yields ln(0.01)=-4.6 → clamped to -0.12 → 0.9305
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Unreachable clamp bounds. The signature overstates the real ±7.5% band by roughly 60%.

formulas.name: Final multiplier selection
formulas.expression: out = 1 + (m_score - 1)*clamp(production_share,0,1); if explicit_fit: out = out*(1-w) + explicit_fit*w with w=clamp(blend,0,0.50); return clamp(out, 1-hard_cap, 1+hard_cap)
formulas.inputs: scoring multiplier, production_share, hard_cap, explicit_fit_final, explicit_fit_blend
formulas.constants: 0.50 max blend weight; hard_cap supplied by caller
formulas.missingDataBehavior: explicit_fit_final None or ≤0 → the blend is skipped silently; no signal distinguishes 'no explicit fit' from 'explicit fit of exactly 1.0'
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: none

formulas.name: Per-category scoring-rule contribution
formulas.expression: contribution[category] += stats_per_game[rule.key] * (league_value - baseline_value), skipping rules whose relevant_buckets exclude the player's bucket
formulas.inputs: stats_per_game (per-game stat rates), ScoringRule deltas
formulas.constants: 1e-8 drop threshold; RULE_META bucket assignments
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A stat key absent from stats_per_game becomes 0.0 (:156) — 'no data' and 'produced zero' are identical. A rule key absent from RULE_META gets category 'other' and relevant_buckets = [], which by the guard at :154 means it applies to EVERY bucket including QB.
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: 12 canonical scoring keys have no RULE_META entry (verified: idp_tkl, idp_safe, idp_sack_yd, idp_pass_def_3p, idp_tkl_10p, idp_tkl_5p, idp_tkl_ast_loss, idp_int_ret_yd, idp_fum_ret_yd, idp_blk_kick, idp_def_pr_td, idp_def_kr_td), so all 12 fall into an unbucketed 'other' pool. The combined-tackle key idp_tkl is one of them.

formulas.name: Baseline scoring map
formulas.expression: 31 hardcoded point values, e.g. pass_td 4.0, rec 1.0, bonus_rec_te 0.5, idp_tkl_solo 1.5, idp_sack 4.0
formulas.inputs: none — literal constants
formulas.constants: All 31 hand-picked. Comment at :11: 'Baseline is a comparison environment only.'
formulas.missingDataBehavior: compare_to_baseline treats a key absent from the baseline map as 0.0 (scoring_delta.py:102), so any league rule outside these 31 keys shows the full league value as its delta
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: 12 canonical keys have no baseline entry, so their deltas are computed against an implicit zero.

formulas.name: Scoring-backtest correlation
formulas.expression: corr_ratio_vs_delta_points = Pearson(fitFinal, ppgCustom - ppgTest)
formulas.inputs: fitFinal (a monotone function of ppgCustom/ppgTest), ppgTest, ppgCustom — all three from the same player payload
formulas.constants: confidence buckets at 0.40 and 0.70
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Every field defaults: ppgTest→0.0, ppgCustom→0.0, fitFinal→1.0, confidence→0.0. A payload with none of these fields produces N rows of (0,0,1.0,0.0) and _pearson returns 0.0 for zero-variance input.
formulas.validated: n/a — this IS the purported validation
formulas.mathIssues: CIRCULARITY: the two correlated series are algebraic transforms of the same two numbers. A high correlation is arithmetic, not evidence. No realized outcome, no temporal split, no baseline. The driver also reads _formatFit* fields (backtest_scoring_adjustment.py:56-60) that appear ZERO times in Dynasty Scraper.py, so on any real payload every row is the all-defaults row.

formulas.name: Cohen's-d tier walk
formulas.expression: pool_sd = population stdev of ALL values at the position; for each next player: d = |mean(current_tier_so_far) - value| / pool_sd; new tier when d > threshold[pos]
formulas.inputs: rankDerivedValue (or values.full / value) per row, position
formulas.constants: QB 0.35, RB 0.22, WR 0.22, TE 0.35, DL/LB/DB 0.30, PICK 2.0 — from config/tiers/thresholds.json, whose own _comment states 'these are still HAND-SET PRIORS and have never been fitted'
formulas.missingDataBehavior: _value_of returns 0.0 when every value field is missing (:328), so an unpriced row is treated as worth zero and lands in the bottom tier rather than being excluded. pool_sd ≤ 0 puts everyone in tier 1 (:153-161).
formulas.validated: none found — the fitter (scripts/refit_tier_thresholds.py) has never been wired into a workflow per the config comment
formulas.mathIssues: Not Cohen's d (which uses a POOLED within-group SD); it uses the whole-position SD, computed once at :152 and never updated. The module docstring at :12-13 describes 'stdev of values remaining in the position pool', which the code does not do.

formulas.name: Tier-threshold drift
formulas.expression: pct = (new_threshold - old_threshold)/old_threshold per position; hasDrift = max|pct| > 0.15
formulas.inputs: two threshold dicts
formulas.constants: tolerance_pct 0.15
formulas.missingDataBehavior: old ≤ 0 → the position's entry is None and excluded from max_drift, so a newly-added position never triggers drift
formulas.validated: never run
formulas.mathIssues: The module docstring at :29-31 says this compares TIER COUNTS and names the parameters old_tiers/new_tiers; the code compares THRESHOLD VALUES.

formulas.name: Flex-aware starter slot counts
formulas.expression: FLEX → +1/3 each to RB/WR/TE; SUPER_FLEX → +1/4 each to QB/RB/WR/TE; REC_FLEX → +1/3 each to WR/TE/RB; IDP_FLEX → +1/3 each to DL/LB/DB; slots[pos] = max(1, round(frac * teams))
formulas.inputs: Sleeper roster_positions list, num_teams
formulas.constants: the 1/3 and 1/4 even splits
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty roster_positions → empty dict; vorp_table then falls back to max(1, len(group)//2) (:220), i.e. half the observed population becomes 'starters'
formulas.validated: none found; the docstring at :91-95 asserts the even split 'yields essentially the same per-position counts' as a dynamic allocation, with no measurement cited
formulas.mathIssues: Even splits are wrong whenever positional supply is asymmetric — a SUPER_FLEX is taken by a QB far more than 25% of the time in a superflex league.

formulas.name: Replacement-level points per game
formulas.expression: sort per-game paces descending; replacement = mean of paces[starter_slots : starter_slots+5]
formulas.inputs: PlayerSeasonRow list or dicts, starter_slots
formulas.constants: band_size 5
formulas.missingDataBehavior: games ≤ 0 rows dropped (:169-170); an empty band falls back to the worst player's pace (:177-178). For dict inputs, `r.get('points') or r.get('starterPoints')` (:161-163) treats a genuine 0.0 as falsy and reaches for the alternate key.
formulas.validated: none found

formulas.name: VORP
formulas.expression: vorp = points - replacement_per_game * games
formulas.inputs: season points, games, per-position replacement pace
formulas.constants: none
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rows with games ≤ 0 or no position are excluded from the table entirely (:210-213)
formulas.validated: none found
