formulas.name: Spearman rank correlation (backtesting)
formulas.expression: rho = cov(rank(-source_rank), rank(points)) / sqrt(var*var), tie-averaged ranks
formulas.inputs: source_ranks {player_id: rank}, realized_points {player_id: total}
formulas.constants: none
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Intersected on player ids (:73). Fewer than 2 common players returns (0.0, 0.0) — indistinguishable from a genuinely zero correlation.
formulas.validated: n/a — never run; inputs do not exist
formulas.mathIssues: none

formulas.name: Top-50 hit rate
formulas.expression: |source_top50 ∩ realized_top50| / max(1, min(50, n_common))
formulas.inputs: same as above
formulas.constants: top_k 50
formulas.missingDataBehavior: same as above
formulas.validated: never run
formulas.mathIssues: none; the random-chance baseline is 50/n_common, which the report never states

formulas.name: Accuracy → raw source weight (shifted softmax)
formulas.expression: w_raw[s] = exp(max(0, rho_s + 1)); w = max(0.05, w_raw/Σw_raw); renormalize to sum 1
formulas.inputs: per-source Spearman rho
formulas.constants: floor 0.05; _MIN_N_PLAYERS 40
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Sources with n_players < 40 excluded (:65); if none qualify, propose_weights returns the prior with status 'no_change' (:122-128)
formulas.validated: none found; docs/backtest_methodology.md §3 describes the mechanism but cites no calibration
formulas.mathIssues: NO DISCRIMINATION. Reproduced numerically with 22 sources spanning rho +0.9 to -0.9: best source weight 0.06216, worst (rho -0.9, actively anti-predictive) 0.041396 — a ratio of 1.50:1. With 5 sources spanning rho 0.9→0.5: 0.2205 vs 0.1805, a ratio of 1.22:1. The exp(rho+1) shift compresses the entire rho range into a factor of e² = 7.39 before the floor compresses it further.

formulas.name: EWMA weight smoothing + drift gate
formulas.expression: w_t = 0.75*w_{t-1} + 0.25*w_new, renormalized; status = 'pending_approval' if max_s |(w_t[s]-w_{t-1}[s])/w_{t-1}[s]| > 0.15
formulas.inputs: prior weights dict, new raw weights
formulas.constants: alpha 0.25, tolerance_pct 0.15
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A source in one dict but not the other is carried verbatim (:97-100). A source with no prior (or prior ≤ 0) is assigned drift 1.0 (:136-138).
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Verified numerically: with an empty prior (the actual state — config/weights/dynamic_source_weights.json does not exist) EVERY source is 'brand new', max_drift is 1.0, and status is unconditionally 'pending_approval'. The script therefore always exits 1 and never writes, even before the missing-input abort at refit_source_weights.py:141-147.

formulas.name: Trade-backtest correctness label
formulas.expression: calc_favors_a = win_prob_a > 0.5; actually_a_ahead = (a_future - b_future) > 0; correct = (calc_favors_a == actually_a_ahead)
formulas.inputs: win_prob_a, side values at trade date and at trade date + 180d
formulas.constants: horizon_days 180; confidence buckets in 5pp steps
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Any missing snapshot for any name on either side skips the whole trade with reason 'missing_snapshots' (:187-189) — correct refusal, but it skews toward trades involving well-covered players
formulas.validated: n/a — run_backtest has no production caller and no trade-history data exists
formulas.mathIssues: TWO defects. (1) The outcome label is our OWN BOARD's value 180 days later, not a realized fantasy outcome. (2) a_now and b_now are computed at :183-184 and used ONLY in the None-check at :187; the comparison at :192 is a LEVEL comparison (a_future > b_future), not a CHANGE comparison. Since a trade calculator favours whichever side is worth more today, and today's leader usually still leads in 180 days, 'correct' is near-tautological with the input.

formulas.name: Pool name normalization key
formulas.expression: pool_clean_name: strip leading index, trailing daggers/parens, unify apostrophes, reverse 'Last, First', split off a trailing position token, strip a glued 2-3 letter team code when the remainder is >3 chars, strip Jr/Sr/II/III/IV/V/VI. pool_normalize_lookup: lowercase, drop hyphens/periods/apostrophes, strip suffixes again, merge a run of ≥2 single-letter initials
formulas.inputs: a raw vendor name string
formulas.constants: NFL_TEAM_CODES (shared with the scraper, parity-tested); the >3-char guard on team-code stripping
formulas.missingDataBehavior: empty/unnormalizable → '' and the row is skipped (builder.py:449-450, 478-479) or reported as excluded (:519-526)
formulas.validated: tests/utils/test_team_codes_parity.py:93-104 pins the shared team-code table only
formulas.mathIssues: Suffix stripping makes 'Marvin Harrison Jr.' and 'Marvin Harrison' the same key — verified: both normalize to 'marvin harrison'. Father/son and Sr./Jr. pairs collapse.

formulas.name: Pool union membership
formulas.expression: pool[norm] created by first writer; Sleeper rows, then KTC top-525 rows, then Adamidp rows merge INTO an existing key when pool_normalize_lookup collides. Membership = in_sleeper OR in_ktc_top525 OR in_adamidp_pdf. IDPTradeCalc enriches only.
formulas.inputs: SLEEPER_ROSTER_DATA.positions, FULL_DATA['KTC'], data/adamidp_normalized.json, FULL_DATA['IDPTradeCalc']
formulas.constants: KTC_UNIVERSE_LIMIT 525
formulas.outputRange: a set of CanonicalPoolRow; live poolAudit reports final_union_count 945 (sleeper 665, ktc525 464, adamidp 385) on the 2026-08-04 export
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A KTC row carries position '' by construction (:298), so it merges into whatever Sleeper row shares its normalized name with NO position check. A second Sleeper row with a colliding key merges into the first (:451-459) and its sleeper_id is kept only if the first had none (:456).
formulas.validated: none found; measured today, 0 collisions among 937 rostered Sleeper names, so the merge path is currently inert
formulas.mathIssues: No position guard anywhere in the merge. This is the opposite policy from src/identity/matcher.py:17-30, whose docstring exists specifically to explain why the position group must be in the key ('Without this, Quay Walker (LB) and Kenneth Walker (RB) would quietly merge').

formulas.name: Pick-name recognizer
formulas.expression: matches ^20\d{2}\s+(PICK\s+)?[1-6]\.(0?[1-9]|1[0-2])$ or ^20\d{2}\s+(EARLY|MID|LATE)\s+[1-6](ST|ND|RD|TH)$ or the same without a year
formulas.inputs: a name string
formulas.constants: slot range 01-12; round range 1-6
formulas.missingDataBehavior: None/empty → False, i.e. treated as a player
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: The slot alternation caps at 12. In a 14-team league '2027 1.13' and '2027 1.14' are not recognized as picks and would enter the player universe as positionless player rows.

formulas.name: Identity match-confidence ladder (matcher)
formulas.expression: 1.00 if external_asset_id non-empty; else 0.98 if team AND position present; else 0.93 if position present; else 0.85
formulas.inputs: a RawAssetRecord's field presence
formulas.constants: quarantine threshold 0.90 (:14)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Everything defaults to the 0.85 rung; a record with no position lands in low_confidence
formulas.validated: On the newest real report (data/identity/identity_report_20260420T194828Z.json, 3494 records): exact_name_only 1906, exact_name_team_position 1088, exact_name_position 500, exact_id ZERO. So 54.6% of records sit below the 0.90 quarantine threshold and the top rung has never fired.
formulas.mathIssues: This is not a match confidence. It never compares two names. Matching is exact equality of `player::<canonical_name>::<position_group>` (:17-30); the 'confidence' only measures how many metadata fields the record carries. A record with a team and a position gets 0.98 even when its name matched an entirely different person.

formulas.name: Unified mapper match ladder
formulas.expression: sleeper_id exact → 1.00; override by sleeper_id → 1.00; gsis exact → 1.00; espn exact → 1.00; name+team+pos → 0.98; name+pos → 0.93; unique name → 0.90; else fuzzy difflib ratio over the whole directory, accepted if ≥ min_confidence (default 0.85), confidence = the raw ratio
formulas.inputs: any subset of sleeper_id / gsis_id / espn_id / name / team / position, plus the Sleeper player directory
formulas.constants: min_confidence 0.85
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No match above min_confidence → None, 'unresolved' bumped (:363). resolve_many echoes the input row back verbatim (:430).
formulas.validated: none found for the 0.85 fuzzy threshold
formulas.mathIssues: THE 0.85 FUZZY THRESHOLD ADMITS WRONG PLAYERS. Measured with the module's own _fuzzy_score on normalized names: 'mike williams' vs 'mykel williams' = 0.8889 (WR vs DL); 'brian thomas' vs 'ian thomas' = 0.9091 (WR vs TE); 'cedric gray' vs 'eric gray' = 0.9000 (LB vs RB); 'tyler allgeier' vs 'tyler alger' = 0.8800. All clear 0.85 and are returned WITH the raw ratio as the confidence. docs/identity-audit-2026-07.md:210-211 independently verified the first three pairs as DIFFERENT players. At :356-357 a caller without a position takes plist[0] unconditionally.

formulas.name: Row identity confidence
formulas.expression: 1.00 if playerId non-empty; else 0.95 if a position exists AND the row's positive source keys are all on the matching side of the offense/IDP split; else 0.85 if a position and any source value exist; else 0.70
formulas.inputs: playerId, position, assetClass, canonicalSiteValues
formulas.constants: the four levels
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No playerId, no position, no source values → 0.70 'name_only'
formulas.mathIssues: The 1.00 rung is awarded for the mere PRESENCE of a Sleeper id (:2827, :2837). It says nothing about whether the 19 CSV sources joined onto that row are the same player, because that join runs on _canonical_match_key (a name, :3758), not on the id. '85.8% at canonical_id' is a statement about metadata completeness that reads as a statement about match quality.

formulas.name: CSV entry → position-group replication
formulas.expression: if the canonical name maps to exactly one pool position group, the highest-valued CSV entry is attached to that group. If it maps to MORE than one group, the same highest-valued entry is replicated to every group with ambiguous=True and groupCollision set.
formulas.inputs: csv_lookup entries, row_groups_by_key
formulas.constants: none
formulas.missingDataBehavior: No entry for the row's cname::grp falls back to cname::* and then to the single-group entry (:3763-3772)
formulas.validated: Currently inert: measured 1092 pool rows / 1092 distinct canonical keys on the 2026-08-04 export, so no key maps to more than one group today
formulas.mathIssues: When the branch fires, one player's market value is written onto another player's row at FULL weight. The `ambiguous` flag is stamped but never consumed by the blend — grep confirms its only reader is the audit block at :7597, a display field. The comment at :3679 ('so the row audit can downgrade trust') describes a downgrade that does not exist.

formulas.name: Per-source CSV join match rate
formulas.expression: matchRate = (matchedRows + idOnlyMatchedRows) / (matchedRows + idOnlyMatchedRows + unmatchedRows)
formulas.inputs: parsed CSV rows keyed by _canonical_match_key, the pool's key set, the pool's sleeper-id set
formulas.constants: near_miss_cutoff 0.84, fuzzy_floor 0.60
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A missing CSV file yields {'error':'file_not_found'} and the source is excluded from every aggregate
formulas.validated: RE-RUN LIVE at commit 9c5d972 on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json. Pool: 1092 rows / 1092 canonical keys. Aggregate: 8408 CSV rows, 7807 matched, 601 unmatched, overall 92.85%. Unmatched split: 580 no_close_match, 21 near_miss. Alias collisions: 0. Worst sources: fantasyNavigatorSf 60.0% (303 of 758 dropped), draftSharksIdp 78.0% (90 of 410), fantasyProsSf 87.6% (67 of 540), flockFantasySfRookies 90.5%, yahooBoone 91.7%, draftSharks 92.5%, flockFantasySf 94.8%, pfkDynasty 95.8%, fantasyProsIdp 96.8%, fantasyCalc 98.5%. Nine sources at 99.5%+.
formulas.mathIssues: This is a CSV-row-centric rate ('what fraction of vendor rows found a pool row'), not a player-centric one. The two differ whenever a vendor board is deeper than the pool, which is exactly fantasyNavigatorSf's case.

formulas.name: Alias collision delta
formulas.expression: group pool rows by post-alias name (_canonical_match_key); a post-alias name absorbing >1 distinct pre-alias name (normalize_player_name) is an alias-introduced collision; crossFamily = the merged rows span >1 position group
formulas.inputs: pool rows
formulas.constants: _KNOWN_POOL_DUPLICATES allow-list containing exactly one entry ('rob henry')
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rows with no name or no canonical key are skipped (:253, :257)
formulas.validated: 0 collisions measured live at commit 9c5d972
formulas.mathIssues: By design it excludes PRE-EXISTING collisions — two players whose names collide before any alias applies (docstring :238-242). Those are the collisions that feed the replication branch at data_contract.py:3674, so the gate protects against alias-introduced chimeras but not against normalizer-introduced ones.

formulas.name: Legacy rank-form Hill reconstruction
formulas.expression: value(rank) = 1 + 9998 / (1 + ((max(1,rank)-1)/midpoint)^slope)
formulas.inputs: canonicalConsensusRank
formulas.constants: HILL_MIDPOINT 65.4 / HILL_SLOPE 0.910 (offense+default); IDP_HILL_MIDPOINT 64.6 / IDP_HILL_SLOPE 0.900
formulas.missingDataBehavior: rank floored at 1.0; rows without both a rank and a positive value are excluded from the fit and the scoring (backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py:127-130)
formulas.validated: RE-RUN LIVE at commit 9c5d972: 740 ranked+valued rows (418 offense, 294 idp, 28 pick). legacy_scope RMSE 82.5 (idp 74.5 / offense 88.9 / pick 58.6); best-fit-per-scope floor 82.2; best single-curve refit 82.4 at midpoint 65.2 / slope 0.905. percentile_global 409.3, percentile_offense 566.8, percentile_scope 692.3. This reproduces the addendum in docs/legacy-rank-curve-backtest.md:151-158 within noise and confirms its 'at the floor' claim.
formulas.mathIssues: The constants are fit against the SAME quantity they are then scored against (rankDerivedValue on one snapshot). The script and doc are explicit that this is a consistency test, not a predictive one (backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py:27, doc :32-33), so the framing is honest; the 16-snapshot stability sweep in the doc is real robustness evidence. Only 740 of 1092 rows carry both a rank and a value, so 32% of the board is outside the fit.

formulas.name: Adjusted-vs-market board comparison
formulas.expression: delta = Spearman(adjusted, actual) - Spearman(market, actual); paired bootstrap over 2000 resamples with fixed seed 20260728 gives win_rate and a 95% CI on delta
formulas.inputs: market value = rankDerivedValue; adjusted = market * league factor; actual = 2025 realized points under the league's exact scoring from nflverse REG weeks plus reception-depth band points
formulas.constants: iterations 2000, seed 20260728, min_players 30, FOCUS_TOP_N 300
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Board rows that are picks, unpriced, or fail the canonical-name join are counted separately and dropped — on the pinned run: 144 picks, 240 unpriced, 137 unjoined out of 1093 board rows, leaving n=572 (52%). The realized-points index keeps only the FIRST entry per canonical name (backtest_adjusted_board.py:167-169), so two real players colliding on a canonical name silently share one target.
formulas.validated: YES — the only real validation in the audited surface. docs/measurements/adjusted-board-backtest-2026-07-28.json: fullBoard n=572 movers=568 market rho 0.561951 adjusted 0.554118 delta -0.007833 winRate 0.0425 CI [-0.016591, +0.000687]; top300 n=245 delta +0.000838 winRate 0.5245; perGame delta -0.005893 winRate 0.104; overReplacement delta -0.007614 winRate 0.0435. All four verdicts 'NO DIFFERENCE DETECTED'. CLAUDE.md's summary is EXACTLY accurate.
formulas.mathIssues: Not a forecast test — the board is current and the season finished; the script and module both say so (backtest_adjusted_board.py:43-47, board_holdout.py:20-31) and the common-mode-cancellation argument is sound for a relative comparison. Nuance the verdict understates: winRate 0.0425 means the adjusted board lost in 95.75% of resamples. factorShape also shows five of nine positions receive a single scalar factor, which cannot change within-position ranks at all.

formulas.name: Board-stability objective (four sweeps)
formulas.expression: mean over consecutive snapshot pairs of |rank_t+1 - rank_t| for top-200 players present in both; value-weighted variant weights each move by day-t value
formulas.inputs: a directory of daily contract snapshots (data/dynasty_data_*.json)
formulas.constants: top_n 200
formulas.missingDataBehavior: A player absent from the next snapshot is skipped (alpha_shrinkage.py:101-102), so board churn from entry/exit is invisible; a parameter that pushes players off the board scores BETTER, not worse.
formulas.validated: NOT A VALIDATION. There is no outcome label of any kind. The metric is minimized by ignoring information, and the published results confirm it: reports/alpha_shrinkage_backtest_full.md picks α=0.00 (pure anchor, all 20 other sources discarded); reports/soft_fallback_backtest_full.md picks distance=0.00; reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md states the caveat in its own text ('the stability optimum drifts toward α=0 and λ=0 — use the anchor source alone, ignore the 15 other sources. That's product-bad'). scripts/backtest_percentile_reference_n.py:150-155 is prepared to print 'The design-choice justification ... is empirically validated' purely on winning that churn metric.
formulas.mathIssues: No uncertainty quantification anywhere — the argmin of a noisy statistic is marked '← best' with no error bar and no resampling. Production ignored two of the four recommendations (α is 0.10 not 0.00 at data_contract.py:5025; N is 500 not 400 at :4933) and adopted one (λ = 0.0 at :5059). None can be re-run: data/dynasty_data_*.json does not exist and retention.py:410 prunes it at 45 days, while the reports cover 2026-03-23 → 2026-04-16.

formulas.name: VA formula candidate search
formulas.expression: for each of 12 candidate families, brute-force the parameter grid minimizing in-sample RMS relative error over all data points; rank all 12 by the same in-sample RMS
formulas.inputs: scripts/ktc_va_observations.json (139 entries) + 13 in-source anchors = 152 points; each is (small side values, large side values, observed KTC VA)
formulas.constants: Measured grid sizes: V1 15,552; V2 2,366; V3 236,544; V4 87,120; V5 72,576; V6 1,560,650; V7 109,760; V8 756,000; V9 945,000; V10 52,488 — total 3,838,056 combinations × 152 points = 583,384,512 predict() calls in pure Python. V11 additionally ridge-fits 8 features on the equal-count subset.
formulas.outputRange: VA on the 1-9999 scale; errors reported as relative %
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Observations whose label is absent from ktc_va_fixture.json are silently skipped with a warning (:104-112). A relative-error divisor floor is applied at :844-848 so zero-VA observations still count.
formulas.validated: NO HOLDOUT. Grep for holdout / cross_val / train / split / leave_one over the file returns only the word 'training' inside a docstring at :596. Every family is fit and scored on the same 152 points and then ranked on that same in-sample number.
formulas.mathIssues: (1) The ridge alpha for V11 is chosen at :1146 by `min(v11_results, key=lambda r: r[2])` where r[2] IS the in-sample RMS — regularization strength selected by the exact metric regularization exists to trade off, so alpha=0 (plain OLS, 8 features on ~46 points, labelled at :1136-1138 'max overfitting risk') is structurally favoured. (2) V12 is KTC's published formula with ZERO free parameters, ranked head-to-head against 11 families each searching up to 1.5M combinations. (3) The script produced no output in 8+ minutes on this machine before I terminated it — the grids were sized for 13 points and never reduced when the dataset grew to 152.

formulas.name: League-comparison positional blends
formulas.expression: legacy = (average + median)/2; improved = 0.35*median + 0.25*average + 0.20*p75 + 0.10*p25 + 0.10*(average - replacement_level)
formulas.inputs: PositionMetrics computed over the top-N blended scores at a position
formulas.constants: 0.35 / 0.25 / 0.20 / 0.10 / 0.10 — hand-picked module constants at :41-45, no fit or backtest referenced anywhere
formulas.missingDataBehavior: An empty sample returns _EMPTY_METRICS (all zeros, sample_size 0) at :113-122 and :156-157, so a position with no data scores exactly 0 and is treated as a real zero in position_shares
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: The four LEVEL weights sum to 0.90, not 1.00; the remaining 0.10 multiplies replacement_adj, a SPREAD (average − replacement, :174). Worked example on a realistic 24-QB sample (avg 313.5, median 314.0, p25 266.0, p75 360.25, replacement 205, repl_adj 108.5): legacy = 313.75, improved = 297.775, ratio 0.9491; the spread term contributes 10.85 of the 297.775 (3.6%). Because position_shares normalizes to 100% across positions, a spread term contaminating a level statistic distorts every share by an amount that depends on within-position dispersion.

formulas.name: Volume+pace blended season score
formulas.expression: if games ≥ 8: 0.5*total + 0.5*(total/games)*17; else: total
formulas.inputs: total_points, games_played
formulas.constants: MIN_GAMES_FOR_PPG 8, FULL_SEASON_WEEKS 17, weights 0.5/0.5
formulas.missingDataBehavior: games 0 → returns total (which is 0)
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: HARD DISCONTINUITY AND A MONOTONICITY VIOLATION AT games=8. Computed: 140 points in 7 games (20.0 PPG) → 140.00; 140 points in 8 games (17.5 PPG) → 218.75; 140 points in 12 games (11.67 PPG) → 169.17. The 8-game player at LOWER pace with IDENTICAL volume scores 56% higher. The docstring at :38-41 states the intent as rewarding 'a player who missed a few weeks at an elite pace', exactly the player the cliff penalizes.

formulas.name: League similarity score
formulas.expression: pos_dev = Σ_{QB,RB,WR,TE} |my_share − baseline_share| in pp; flex_dev = |my_flex − baseline_flex|/baseline_flex × 100; combined = pos_dev + 0.4*flex_dev; piecewise-linear map to 0-100 with knots at 2, 5, 10, 20
formulas.inputs: positional shares (0-100), flex blended scores
formulas.constants: 0.4 flex weight ('intentionally less than the share signal because the flex score is correlated'); band knots 2/5/10/20; score ranges 95-100 / 85-94 / 75-84 / 60-74 / <60
formulas.missingDataBehavior: baseline_flex ≤ 0 → flex_dev is silently set to 0.0 (:352-353), so a missing baseline makes the leagues look MORE similar rather than flagging the gap
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: Every constant is hand-picked. More importantly the score is computed over OFFENSE_POSITIONS only (:348, defined at :36), and src/league_comparison/idp.py::compute_idp_block returns available:false. In an IDP league the 'similarity to standard' verdict ignores the single largest structural difference between the league and a standard one.

formulas.name: Status label bands
formulas.expression: |diff_pp| ≤ 0.5 Excellent; ≤ 1.5 Good; ≤ 3.0 Slightly high/low; ≤ 5.0 High/Low; else Too high/low
formulas.inputs: positional share difference in percentage points
formulas.missingDataBehavior: a diff of exactly 0.0 (both shares missing → both 0.0) returns 'Excellent match'
formulas.validated: none found
formulas.mathIssues: A position with no data on either side reports 'Excellent match'.

formulas.name: Multi-season combine
formulas.expression: equal-weight mean over available seasons of each per-season statistic separately; combined sample_size = round(mean of per-season sample sizes)
formulas.inputs: per-season PositionMetrics
formulas.constants: none — explicitly no recency weighting (module docstring :20-23)
formulas.missingDataBehavior: seasons with sample_size 0 are excluded (:240); all-missing returns _EMPTY_METRICS
formulas.validated: none found; config/league_comparison.json declares seasons [2022, 2023, 2024, 2025]
formulas.mathIssues: Averaging per-season medians and percentiles is not the median or percentile of the pooled data. The docstring at :237-239 states this is deliberate, which is defensible, but the resulting object is passed to improved_blended as if its fields were mutually consistent order statistics of one distribution.

formulas.name: Platform asset resolution ladder
formulas.expression: canonical pick id → 1.00; manual mapping by platform:source_id → 1.00; authoritative external id → 1.00; unique name+team+position → 0.98; unique name+position → 0.93; globally unique name → 0.90; ANY multi-candidate case → ambiguous, confidence 0.0, canonical_asset_id None
formulas.inputs: platform, source_asset_id, name, nfl_team, position, asset_type, pick fields
formulas.constants: the four confidence levels
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Missing pick season/round → unresolved with reason missing_pick_season_or_round (:144-150). Missing name → unresolved with reason missing_player_name (:172-179). Ambiguity NEVER resolves to a guess.
formulas.validated: tests/platforms/test_assets.py
formulas.mathIssues: None — this is the correct design, and worth naming as the reference implementation because the other four identity ladders use the same confidence NUMBERS with weaker policies.

formulas.name: Retention windows
formulas.expression: data/canonical purged entirely; export archives kept 14 days (with a thin-to-daily band); raw_source_snapshot_*.json newest 30; data/raw/<source>/<year>/* newest 30 per leaf; data/dynasty_data_*.json last 45 days. Age from an embedded filename timestamp when present, else st_mtime.
formulas.inputs: the data/ and exports/ trees
formulas.constants: 14 / 30 / 45 day and count windows; _FILENAME_TS_RE at :51
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Un-timestamped filenames fall back to st_mtime, which the comment at :47-50 correctly notes is unreliable after a CI checkout
formulas.validated: tests/maintenance/test_retention.py
formulas.mathIssues: data/identity/ is on the NEVER-touched hard-guard list (:32). Measured on disk: 177 files totalling 483 MB, all dated 2026-03-25 to 2026-04-20, produced by a pipeline that no longer runs. A module whose stated purpose is preventing disk exhaustion (:5-9) hard-excludes its second-largest directory. Separately, the 45-day window on data/dynasty_data_*.json is what makes the four stability sweeps permanently irreproducible.

formulas.name: Market confidence (scraper)
formulas.expression: site_score = clamp(site_count/8.0, 0.20, 1.00); cv_score = clamp(1 − min(cv,0.35)/0.35, 0.20, 1.00); conf = clamp(0.65*site_score + 0.35*cv_score, 0.20, 1.00)
formulas.inputs: site_count (persisted as _sites), coefficient of variation across site values
formulas.constants: SITE_DIVISOR 8.0; cv cap 0.35; weights 0.65/0.35; floor 0.20
formulas.missingDataBehavior: floors at 0.20
formulas.validated: Measured by scripts/simulate_market_confidence_divisor.py and confirmed on the live export: the 2026-08-04 payload's A.J. Brown row carries _sites: 3 and _marketConfidence: 0.5706. site_count never exceeds 3 because the scraper's SITES toggle map enables only KTC and IDPTradeCalc, emitting three dash keys.
formulas.mathIssues: The divisor 8.0 is a fossil of a ~10-site era. It caps confidence at 0.375*0.65 + 1.00*0.35 = 0.59375, so the metric can never express high confidence and its four downstream consumers all operate on a permanently compressed input. Correctly documented as an open decision in docs/open-modeling-decisions.md §3.

formulas.name: Historical scoring dataset derived features
formulas.expression: raw_scoring_ratio = league_points / max(baseline_points, 1); td_dependency = (pass_td+rush_td+rec_td)/max(pass_yd+rush_yd+rec_yd, 1); reception_profile = rec / max(rec + rush_att, 1)
formulas.inputs: nflverse weekly rows scored under two scoring maps
formulas.constants: the clip(lower=1.0) floors
formulas.missingDataBehavior: Any nflverse column named in NFL_COLS but absent from the frame becomes a constant 0.0 (:96)
formulas.validated: never run — the required scoring-config JSONs do not exist
formulas.mathIssues: THREE defects. (1) NFL_COLS (:22-37) contains ZERO IDP stats, so in an IDP league every defender scores 0 under both maps and raw_scoring_ratio is 0/1 = 0. (2) At :106, `out.get('rush_att', 0.0)` returns the scalar 0.0 because rush_att was never added to `out` — reception_profile evaluates to rec/rec = 1.0 for anyone with a reception and 0.0 otherwise. (3) pass_inc maps to an nflverse column 'incompletions' that import_weekly_data does not provide, so it is silently 0 everywhere.

findings.title: The entire src/scoring player-adjustment and archetype pipeline is imported and never called
findings.evidence: Dynasty Scraper.py:66-96 imports 13 symbols from src.scoring inside a try/except that nulls them all on failure. A per-symbol count over the whole file returns exactly 2 occurrences for each (the import line and the `= None` line): build_player_scoring_adjustment 2, choose_final_multiplier 2, infer_archetype 2, bucket_rule_contributions 2, compare_to_baseline 2, run_scoring_backtest 2, persist_scoring_config 2. A repo-wide grep for these names outside src/scoring/ returns only that import block, scripts/backtest_scoring_adjustment.py and tests/. Corroboration: `grep -c "_formatFit" "Dynasty Scraper.py"` returns 0 — the output fields these functions were written to produce no longer exist anywhere in the scraper.
findings.userImpact: Roughly 600 lines of scoring-translation math — shrinkage, archetype priors, rule-contribution attribution, multiplier caps — influence no number a user ever sees. A reader of CLAUDE.md's directory table ('src/scoring/ — Scoring adjustments, archetypes, backtesting') will reasonably believe this is live and may tune constants that reach nothing, or cite it as evidence that scoring translation is handled.
findings.recommendedFix: Either delete src/scoring/{player_adjustment,archetype_model,feature_engineering,scoring_delta,baseline_config,backtest}.py plus the scraper's import block, or annotate each module head with the same honesty the repo already applies elsewhere (src/api/feature_flags.py:60-72 is the model). Keep tiering.py, replacement_level.py and sleeper_ingest.py's KEY_ALIASES, which do have live consumers. Update CLAUDE.md's directory table.
findings.affectedSystems: src/scoring/*, Dynasty Scraper.py, CLAUDE.md, scripts/backtest_scoring_adjustment.py, scripts/validate_scoring_fit.py

findings.title: The scoring-adjustment 'backtest' is a tautology and its inputs no longer exist
findings.evidence: src/scoring/backtest.py:62 computes `corr_ratio_vs_delta_points = Pearson(ratios, deltas)` where `ratio = fit['fitFinal']` (:34) and `delta_points = custom - baseline` with `baseline = fit['ppgTest']` (:32), `custom = fit['ppgCustom']` (:33). fitFinal is itself derived from ppgCustom/ppgTest, so both series are transforms of the same two numbers. Separately scripts/backtest_scoring_adjustment.py:56-60 reads _formatFitPPGTest, _formatFitPPGCustom, _formatFitFinal, _formatFitProductionMultiplier, _formatFitConfidence — fields that appear 0 times in Dynasty Scraper.py — and globs `dynasty_data_*.json` at the repo root (:26), where no such file exists.
findings.userImpact: There is no validation of the scoring-adjustment model, despite a file named backtest.py, a script named backtest_scoring_adjustment.py, and a docstring saying 'Lightweight validation'. If run, it emits a sampleSize, an avg_ratio of 1.0 and correlations of 0.0 from all-default rows, which reads as a clean result rather than as no data.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete both files. If a validation of scoring translation is wanted, model it on scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py: a realized-outcome target under the league's exact scoring, a paired bootstrap, and an explicit statement of what the comparison cannot support.

findings.title: identityConfidence 1.00 means 'has a Sleeper ID', not 'matched correctly' — and 85.8% of live rows carry it
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:2827 `has_id = bool((row.get('playerId') or '').strip())` then :2837-2838 `if has_id: return 1.00, 'canonical_id'`. No name, source or position evidence is consulted on that path. But the join that attaches 19 of 21 sources' votes runs on a NAME key: :3758 `cname = _canonical_match_key(nm)` / :3762 `entry = per_source.get(f'{cname}::{grp}')`. Only pfkDynasty carries a usable sleeper_id column (:3702-3706). Live measurement on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json via scripts/audit_identity.py: 937 of 1092 rows (85.8%) at 1.00 'canonical_id', 144 (13.2%) at 0.95, 11 (1.0%) at 0.70. The identical design error is at src/identity/matcher.py:41-49, where 1.00 is returned for a non-empty external_asset_id and 0.98 for the mere presence of team+position — on the newest real report (data/identity/identity_report_20260420T194828Z.json) the 1.00 rung fired 0 times out of 3494 records.
findings.userImpact: Any consumer reading identityConfidence — the audit script's own distribution table, any future UI badge — will conclude that 85.8% of the board is identity-verified. The true per-source name-join miss rate measured on the same payload is 601 of 8408 CSV rows (7.15%), and it is not uniform: fantasyNavigatorSf loses 40% of its board and draftSharksIdp 22%. Those two numbers describe different things and only one of them is displayed.
findings.recommendedFix: Rename the field to what it measures (identityEvidence / hasCanonicalId), or make the 1.00 rung require that the row's source votes were joined by id rather than by name. Either way, surface the real per-source join rate — scripts/audit_identity_matches.py already computes it — on /api/status alongside mapping_coverage_snapshot.

findings.title: The unified mapper's fuzzy fallback accepts demonstrably different players at its default threshold
findings.evidence: src/identity/unified_mapper.py:359-361 `if best_p and best_score >= min_confidence: return _to_resolved(best_p, confidence=best_score, method='fuzzy_name')` with `min_confidence: float = 0.85` at :246 and _fuzzy_score returning a raw difflib SequenceMatcher ratio (:188). Measured with the module's own function on normalized names: 'mike williams' vs 'mykel williams' 0.8889 (WR vs DL); 'brian thomas' vs 'ian thomas' 0.9091 (WR vs TE); 'cedric gray' vs 'eric gray' 0.9000 (LB vs RB); 'tyler allgeier' vs 'tyler alger' 0.8800. docs/identity-audit-2026-07.md:210-211 independently verified the first three as DIFFERENT players. The score is written into ResolvedPlayer.confidence, so a wrong-player match is reported at 0.909 confidence. At :356-357 a caller without a position takes plist[0] unconditionally.
findings.userImpact: A caller without a position — and `position` is optional at :245 — can silently receive a different player's Sleeper id, gsis id and team at ~0.9 confidence, meaning one player's weekly stats, injury status or news attached to another player's row. src/playerctx/normalize.py:668-676 mitigates this by restricting the fuzzy pool to the named team and its comment says why ('resolve_player's fuzzy walk ignores its team argument, so a closer-spelled player on another team could steal the row') — but that guard lives in the caller, so every other caller is unprotected.
findings.recommendedFix: Move the team-scoping guard from src/playerctx/normalize.py into resolve_player itself, and refuse rather than guess on multi-candidate ties the way src/platforms/assets.py:193-217 already does. Raise the fuzzy floor above the measured false-positive band (all four counterexamples land in 0.88-0.91) or drop the fuzzy rung in favour of the deterministic alias table, which docs/identity-audit-2026-07.md:192-197 already concluded is the right layer.

findings.title: resolve_many rebuilds the entire Sleeper directory index on every row, contradicting its own docstring
findings.evidence: src/identity/unified_mapper.py:269 `idx = _index_directory(players_dir)` sits inside resolve_player, so it runs per call, and resolve_many at :417 calls resolve_player once per input row. Its docstring at :409-411 states the opposite: 'Used by nightly jobs ... so the mapper's internal index is built once, not per-row.' src/playerctx/normalize.py:551 independently documents the problem ('resolve_player re-indexes the pool on every ...') and builds its own indexes to avoid it. Secondary: at :95 `if _OVERRIDES_PATH_CACHE == target and _OVERRIDES_CACHE` — an empty override map is falsy, so an empty-but-present overrides file causes a disk read on every call.
findings.userImpact: A batch resolve over N rows against Sleeper's ~11k-player directory is O(N × 11000) index construction. For a nightly ingest of a few thousand rows that is tens of millions of redundant dict writes. The docstring actively misleads anyone deciding whether resolve_many is safe to call in a loop.
findings.recommendedFix: Extract the index build into an internal _resolve_with_index(idx, ...) and have resolve_many build the index once. Fix the docstring either way. Change the override cache guard to a sentinel so an empty map caches.

findings.title: The pool builder merges players by name with no position guard, discarding the loser's Sleeper ID
findings.evidence: src/pool/builder.py:451-459: on a pool_normalize_lookup collision the second Sleeper entry is merged into the first, and `if not row.sleeper_id and entry.get('sleeper_id')` (:456) means the second player's id is kept only when the first had none. KTC rows merge on the same bare key at :480-486 while carrying `position: ''` by construction (:298), so a KTC value can attach to the wrong same-named player. pool_normalize_lookup strips Jr/Sr/II/III (:208), so 'Marvin Harrison Jr.' and 'Marvin Harrison' produce one key. This is exactly what src/identity/matcher.py:17-30 exists to prevent: 'Without this, Quay Walker (LB) and Kenneth Walker (RB) would quietly merge into one player::walker master record.' Measured today: 0 collisions among the 937 rostered Sleeper names, so the path is inert but unguarded.
findings.userImpact: When two rostered players share a normalized name — which suffix stripping makes more likely and which the NFL supplies regularly — they become one pool row. The lost row's Sleeper id is dropped, so the second player can fall out of the board universe entirely. There is no counter, no warning, and no entry in PoolAuditReport.excluded_names for this case.
findings.recommendedFix: Key the pool on `norm + '|' + position_group`, matching src/identity/matcher.py::_identity_canonical_key. Where a source supplies no position (KTC), attach only when the key resolves to exactly one group and record an ambiguity otherwise. Add a collision counter to PoolAuditReport so the inert-today state is observable rather than assumed.

findings.title: Cross-position CSV value replication is flagged 'ambiguous' but the flag downgrades nothing
findings.evidence: src/api/data_contract.py:3674-3692: when one canonical name maps to pool rows in more than one position group, the highest-valued CSV entry is written to EVERY group with `ambiguous: True` and `groupCollision`. The comment at :3677-3679 says this is done 'but flag it as ambiguous so the row audit can downgrade trust'. A repo-wide grep for `.get("ambiguous")` finds exactly one reader: :7597, inside the display-only matched_details block. Nothing in _compute_unified_rankings consults it; the blend consumes the replicated value at full weight.
findings.userImpact: A WR's market value can be written onto an IDP row of the same name and counted as a normal source vote in the count-aware aggregation and the single-source haircut. Currently inert — 1092 pool rows over 1092 distinct canonical keys measured on the 2026-08-04 export — but nothing prevents it firing on the next refresh, and scripts/audit_identity_matches.py's collision gate deliberately excludes the pre-existing (non-alias) collisions that feed this branch (its docstring at :238-242).
findings.recommendedFix: Either drop replicated entries from the blend and count them in poolAudit, or apply a real weight penalty and make the degraded vote visible. If the flag is meant to be advisory only, delete the 'so the row audit can downgrade trust' claim from the comment.

findings.title: docs/backtest_methodology.md describes a consumption path and a cadence that do not exist
findings.evidence: The doc is headed '**Status:** Shipped 2026-04-24' (line 3). §4 states 'Flag ON → blend layer reads config/weights/dynamic_source_weights.json'. A repo-wide grep for dynamic_source_weights outside src/backtesting/, scripts/refit_source_weights.py and tests returns only two comment lines in src/api/feature_flags.py (:115, :368) — no code reads that file, which is absent from config/weights/ (which contains default_weights.json, pick_year_discount.json, source_row_floors.json, te_premium_curve.json, top50_coverage_floors.json). src/api/feature_flags.py:374 classifies the flag as NO_GATE, meaning no is_enabled() call exists. §67-72 promises a 'Monthly refit (cron)'; no file in .github/workflows/ references the script. §37-38 names data/source_rank_history.jsonl and data/realized_points_history.jsonl as inputs; neither exists and grep finds them only in refit_source_weights.py's own argparse defaults. §97-99 tells the operator to monitor a /api/status section that does not exist.
findings.userImpact: A reader is told a weight-fitting system is shipped, running monthly, and flag-gated. None of it is true at any layer — the blend runs on 21 flat 1.0 weights, verified by loading _RANKING_SOURCES. Anyone planning work around the 'flag flip plan' in §87-99 would be planning against fiction.
findings.recommendedFix: Retitle the doc 'Design, not shipped' and mark every unimplemented step, or delete it together with src/backtesting/{correlation,dynamic_weights}.py and scripts/refit_source_weights.py. The repo already has the right pattern — src/api/feature_flags.py:60-72 and config/tiers/thresholds.json's _comment both state plainly what does not run.

findings.title: The dynamic weight fitter cannot distinguish a good source from an anti-predictive one
findings.evidence: src/backtesting/dynamic_weights.py:71 `weights_raw = {a.source: math.exp(max(0.0, a.spearman_rho + 1.0)) for a in eligible}` then :73 `normalized = {s: max(floor, w / total) ...}` with floor 0.05, then renormalize. Reproduced numerically with 22 sources spanning Spearman rho +0.9 to −0.9: best source weight 0.06216, worst (rho −0.9, systematically wrong) 0.041396 — a 1.50:1 ratio. With 5 sources spanning rho 0.9→0.5: 0.2205 vs 0.1805, a 1.22:1 ratio. The exp(rho+1) shift compresses the whole possible accuracy range into a factor of e² = 7.39 before the floor compresses it further.
findings.userImpact: If the flag were flipped on, a source that ranks players backwards would keep about two-thirds the influence of a perfect source. The mechanism cannot deliver the stated goal in docs/backtest_methodology.md §7-12. tests/backtesting/test_dynamic_weights.py:17-29 asserts normalization and the floor but never asserts any minimum separation between a high-rho and a low-rho source, so the weakness is not pinned.
findings.recommendedFix: If revived, use a transform with real dynamic range (weight ∝ max(0, rho)^k, or softmax on rho/temperature with a fitted temperature) and add a test asserting a rho=0.8 source outweighs a rho=0.0 source by a stated minimum factor. Also fix the docstring at :68, which says 'rho=-1 → exp(-0)' when max(0, 0.0) makes that exp(0)=1.

findings.title: The trade backtest harness scores against its own board, and discards the at-trade-time values it fetches
findings.evidence: src/backtesting/harness.py:183-194. `a_now` and `b_now` are computed at :183-184 and referenced ONLY in the None-check at :187; the comparison at :192-194 is `delta_future = a_future - b_future` / `actually_a_ahead = delta_future > 0`, a LEVEL comparison at the horizon rather than a comparison of CHANGES. And value_snapshots is our own board's value 180 days later, not a realized fantasy outcome. run_backtest has no caller outside tests/backtesting/test_harness.py.
findings.userImpact: If wired up, 'accuracy' would measure whether the calculator favoured the side that was already worth more — which is what a value calculator does by construction. The calibration table it prints (:105-106, 'a calibrated trade calc should have accuracy roughly equal to the bucket midpoint') would read as a genuine calibration curve.
findings.recommendedFix: Change the comparison to `(a_future - a_now) > (b_future - b_now)` so the label measures which side gained, and state in the docstring that the target is board value rather than realized production. If a realized-outcome version is wanted, the pattern is scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py. Otherwise delete the module — it has no caller and no data.

findings.title: Four parameter 'backtests' optimize board stability, which is maximized by discarding sources
findings.evidence: scripts/backtest_alpha_shrinkage.py:87-113, backtest_percentile_reference_n.py:72-91, backtest_soft_fallback.py:84-102 and backtest_alpha_lambda_joint.py all use a byte-identical stability_metric = mean |rank_t+1 − rank_t| over top-200 players. There is no outcome label anywhere. The published results prove the objective is degenerate: reports/alpha_shrinkage_backtest_full.md recommends 'Promote α = 0.00' (pure anchor — 20 other sources discarded); reports/soft_fallback_backtest_full.md recommends distance 0.00; reports/alpha_lambda_joint_backtest_full.md states it outright — 'this metric rewards stability. The stability optimum drifts toward α=0 and λ=0 — "use the anchor source alone, ignore the 15 other sources." That's product-bad'. scripts/backtest_percentile_reference_n.py:150-155 is prepared to print 'The design-choice justification (KTC pool size, retail market scale) is empirically validated' on the strength of that churn metric. None of the four resamples or reports an interval. A player absent from the next snapshot is silently skipped (alpha_shrinkage.py:101-102), so a parameter that pushes players off the board scores better.
findings.userImpact: Three produce a printed 'Recommendation' a reader would take as an empirical result. Two of the three were correctly ignored in production (_ALPHA_SHRINKAGE is 0.10 at data_contract.py:5025, not 0.00; _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N is 500 at :4933, not 400), so the live constants are hand-picks with a misleading paper trail behind them. One WAS adopted: _MAD_PENALTY_LAMBDA = 0.0 at :5059 — a live mechanism switched off on the strength of a churn metric, and reports/mad_lambda_backtest_full.md itself flags the gap ('Consider whether a different optimization target (e.g. KTC alignment) would favour a non-zero λ before committing to remove the feature').
findings.recommendedFix: Rename these scripts to sweep_* or measure_*_stability so they stop claiming to be backtests, and copy the alpha_lambda_joint caveat text into the other three. Where a parameter genuinely needs choosing, use the scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py + src/model_registry/board_holdout.py pattern — realized outcomes, a paired bootstrap, and an explicit statement of what the result cannot support.

findings.title: Every stability sweep is permanently irreproducible because retention prunes its inputs
findings.evidence: All four sweeps read data/dynasty_data_*.json (backtest_alpha_shrinkage.py:60-61 and identical loaders in the other three). `ls data/dynasty_data_*.json` returns 'No such file or directory'. src/maintenance/retention.py:25-27 and :410 prune that glob at 45 days. The four published reports all state 'Snapshot count: 25, Date range: 2026-03-23 → 2026-04-16' — a window that has been deleted. reports/ktc_volatility_backtest_full.md is worse: its header records 'Hill constants: midpoint=48.44, slope=1.149', no longer the live values (src/canonical/player_valuation.py:82-83 reads 65.4 / 0.910). reports/backtest_blend_params.md is fully orphaned: it tunes _BLEND_MEAN_WEIGHT, _BLEND_ROBUST_WEIGHT and _VOLATILITY_COMPRESSION_FLOOR/CEIL — none of which exist in src/api/data_contract.py — and reports an optimal RANKING_SOURCES[idpTradeCalc].weight of 3.0 when the live registry has all 21 sources at 1.0; the generating script is not in the repo.
findings.userImpact: Seven markdown reports sit in reports/ with tables of numbers, no staleness marker, and no way to re-derive them. A reader cannot check any of them, and at least two describe parameters since removed from the codebase.
findings.recommendedFix: Stamp every report with the commit and the constants in force when it ran, and add a staleness banner to the five known-stale ones. If these sweeps are meant to stay runnable, either exempt a thinned sample of contract snapshots from retention (retention.py already has a thin-to-daily mechanism at :292-345) or check a fixture set into tests/fixtures.

findings.title: The VA formula calibration fits and scores 12 candidate families on the same 152 points, with regularization chosen by in-sample error
findings.evidence: scripts/calibrate_va_formula.py:920-1223. Every family is grid-searched to minimize in-sample RMS (grid_search(..., metric='rms')) and all 12 are then ranked on that same in-sample RMS at :1200-1222. A grep for holdout / cross_val / train / split / leave_one over the file finds only the word 'training' inside a docstring at :596. For V11, :1136-1141 sweeps ridge alpha over (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 5.0, 25.0, 100.0) computing `rms = objective(predict_v11, params, metric='rms')` on the training data, then :1146 selects `min(v11_results, key=lambda r: r[2])` — the alpha with the lowest IN-SAMPLE error, which always favours alpha=0, labelled by the code itself as 'plain OLS (max overfitting risk on 46 training points × 8 features)'. V12 is KTC's published formula with zero free parameters, ranked head-to-head against 11 families collectively searching 3,838,056 combinations (measured: V6 1,560,650; V9 945,000; V8 756,000; V3 236,544; V7 109,760; V4 87,120; V5 72,576; V10 52,488; V1 15,552; V2 2,366).
findings.userImpact: The ranking table the operator uses to pick which formula to port into frontend/lib/trade-logic.js is an in-sample fit contest, so the most flexible family wins by construction and its reported error understates what a user sees on a trade the calibration never saw. The regularization sweep that exists to control this is decided by the metric it is supposed to trade off. Practically: at ~583M pure-Python predict() calls the script produced no output in 8+ minutes on this machine before I terminated it — it was sized for 13 points and the grids were never reduced when the dataset grew to 152.
findings.recommendedFix: Hold out a stratified 20-30% of the 152 observations by topology, fit on the remainder, and report BOTH in-sample and held-out RMS in the ranking table. Select the ridge alpha by K-fold CV on the equal-count subset rather than by training error. Shrink the V6/V8/V9 grids or replace the brute force with a local optimizer so the script finishes.

findings.title: docs/status/canonical-source-matrix.md declares 8 live sources removed and describes a retired pipeline as current
findings.evidence: The doc (dated 2026-04-08) states 'Only two sources are active after scope reduction' and lists DLF, FantasyCalc, DynastyDaddy, Yahoo, FantasyPros, DraftSharks, DynastyNerds and Flock under 'Removed Sources'. Loading src/api/data_contract._RANKING_SOURCES returns 21 sources including dlfSf, dlfIdp, dlfRookieSf, dlfRookieIdp, fantasyCalc, dynastyDaddySf, yahooBoone, fantasyProsSf, fantasyProsIdp, fantasyProsFitzmaurice, draftSharks, draftSharksIdp, dynastyNerdsSfTep, flockFantasySf and flockFantasySfRookies — every one of which I measured live match rates for (dlfSf 99.6%, fantasyCalc 98.5%, draftSharksIdp 78.0%). The doc's pipeline diagram routes through `source_pull.py -> canonical_build.py -> data/canonical/`; none of scripts/source_pull.py, scripts/canonical_build.py, src/canonical/transform.py, src/canonical/pipeline.py or data/canonical exists, and CLAUDE.md records that path as retired.
findings.userImpact: This file lives in docs/status/, the place a reader goes for current state. Acting on it — e.g. deciding a DLF fetcher is dead code — would break 15 live sources. It is the single most misleading document in the audited set.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete it, or replace its body with a pointer to _RANKING_SOURCES and the live per-source match rates from scripts/audit_identity_matches.py.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md's adapter table claims scraper_bridge_adapter.py is live in server.py; it has no production caller
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md's Adapter Pattern table lists `scraper_bridge_adapter.py | live (server.py)`. `grep -n 'scraper_bridge\|ScraperBridgeAdapter' server.py 'Dynasty Scraper.py'` returns nothing. A repo-wide grep finds it only in tests/adapters/test_scraper_bridge_adapter.py:9, tests/integration/test_multi_source_pipeline.py:23,36, tests/adapters/test_yahoo_boone_scraper.py:309 and tests/adapters/test_source_config_completeness.py:181. By contrast sleeper_trending IS live (server.py:1729, 5069) and ktc_crowd_faab IS live (server.py:5120), so the table is right about two of three.
findings.userImpact: The adapter it names as the live one is the dormant one. That matters because the adapter was the entry point of the retired canonical-build pipeline, so believing it is live keeps a dead architecture alive in people's mental model — the same error docs/status/canonical-source-matrix.md makes.
findings.recommendedFix: Change its row to 'dormant — test-only, entry point of the retired canonical-build path', matching how base.py is already described in the same table.

findings.title: stamp_tiers_on_players misaligns tier IDs whenever any row lacks a position
findings.evidence: src/scoring/tiering.py:199-200: `tiers = detect_tiers(rows, ...)` then `by_id = {id(rows[i]): tiers[i].tier_id for i in range(len(tiers))}`. But detect_tiers returns a FILTERED list — :186 `return [result_map[id(r)] for r in rows if isinstance(r, dict) and id(r) in result_map]` — and rows with no pos/position never enter result_map (:139-141). So len(tiers) < len(rows) whenever any row lacks a position, and the positional zip at :200 pairs tiers[i] with rows[i] rather than with the row that produced it. Worked through: rows = [A(no pos), B(QB), C(QB)] yields tiers = [tierB, tierC], so A is stamped with B's tier, B with C's tier, and C is stamped with nothing. tests/scoring/test_tiering.py exercises detect_tiers at :22, :30, :38, :45 but never calls stamp_tiers_on_players.
findings.userImpact: Currently unexposed — stamp_tiers_on_players has no caller outside scripts/refit_tier_thresholds.py and the feature flag is NO_GATE/OFF (src/api/feature_flags.py:72). But its docstring advertises it as 'Safe to call from the contract builder when the positional_tiers feature flag is on', which is the exact call that would trip it, and the live board does carry rows with no position (the 2026-08-04 export has an unsupported-position 'Brandon Knight' row).
findings.recommendedFix: Build the map from the TierEntry's own identity rather than by index — have detect_tiers return the id→TierEntry map, or zip over the filtered row list. Add a test with a position-less row in the middle of the input.

findings.title: compute_blended_score has a discontinuity at 8 games that rewards the worse player
findings.evidence: src/league_comparison/scoring_engine.py:74-79: `if games_played >= MIN_GAMES_FOR_PPG (8): return 0.5*total + 0.5*(total/games)*17; return total`. Computed directly: 140 points in 7 games (20.0 PPG) → 140.00; 140 points in 8 games (17.5 PPG) → 218.75; 140 points in 12 games (11.67 PPG) → 169.17. The 8-game player at LOWER pace with IDENTICAL volume scores 56% higher than the 7-game player, and the 12-game player at 11.67 PPG also outscores the 7-game player at 20.0 PPG. The module docstring at :38-41 states the intent as rewarding 'a player who missed a few weeks at an elite pace' — exactly the player the cliff penalizes.
findings.userImpact: This score is the ranking key for the entire top-N sample (metrics.py:69 and :82). Every downstream statistic — average, median, p25, p75, replacement level, elite, both blended methods, the positional shares, the status labels and the 0-100 similarity score — is computed over a sample selected by a discontinuous key. It is also the ranking used by scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py via compute_player_season_scores.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace the hard gate with a continuous credibility weight, e.g. w = min(1, games/8) and blend total*(1−0.5w) + ppg*17*0.5w, so the function is monotone in pace at fixed volume and continuous at the boundary. Pin it with a test asserting that at equal total points a higher-PPG player never scores lower.

findings.title: improved_blended mixes a spread term into a weighted sum of levels whose weights total 0.90
findings.evidence: src/league_comparison/metrics.py:190-196. The four level terms (median 0.35, average 0.25, p75 0.20, p25 0.10) sum to 0.90; the remaining 0.10 multiplies m.replacement_adj, defined at :174 as `average − replacement_level`, a SPREAD. Worked example on a realistic 24-QB sample (avg 313.5, median 314.0, p25 266.0, p75 360.25, replacement 205, repl_adj 108.5): legacy_blended = 313.75, improved_blended = 297.775, ratio 0.9491; the spread term contributes 10.85 of the 297.775. All five coefficients are hand-picked module constants (:41-45) with no fit, backtest or reference cited anywhere in the repo.
findings.userImpact: improved_blended feeds position_shares (:202-212), which normalizes across positions to 100%. A spread term inside a level statistic shifts each position's share by an amount proportional to that position's within-sample dispersion — so a position whose top-24 is unusually top-heavy gains share for a reason unrelated to how much it scores. That share difference is what the similarity score and the status labels are computed from, so the distortion reaches the user-facing 0-100 number and the 'Excellent match' / 'Too high' verdicts.
findings.recommendedFix: Either normalize the level weights to 1.0 and report replacement_adj as a separate diagnostic, or express it as a ratio (average/replacement_level) so it is scale-free. Document that the coefficients are unfitted priors, as config/tiers/thresholds.json already does for the tiering thresholds.

findings.title: League similarity is computed over offense only, in an IDP league, and says so nowhere in its output
findings.evidence: src/league_comparison/metrics.py:347-349 sums deviations over OFFENSE_POSITIONS = ('QB','RB','WR','TE') (:36). src/league_comparison/idp.py:33-50 returns {'available': False, 'status': 'placeholder', 'positions': {}, 'top96Idp': None}. config/league_comparison.json declares sample_sizes including IDP_TOTAL: 96, so the configuration promises IDP coverage the code does not deliver. Separately at metrics.py:350-353, baseline_flex <= 0 sets flex_dev to 0.0, which makes a missing baseline read as perfect flex agreement.
findings.userImpact: The league is heavily IDP (its scoring pays 4.25/5.32 for TFL/PD per CLAUDE.md, and a roster starts nine IDP players per docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md). The one number answering 'how far is my league from standard' ignores the entire IDP scoring economy. The 0-100 score and its 'Extremely close to standard' label carry no caveat.
findings.recommendedFix: Stamp the similarity result with the position families it actually covered and surface that in the response, so a 92/100 reads as '92/100, offense only'. Until compute_idp_block is implemented, that annotation is the whole fix.

findings.title: 12 canonical IDP scoring keys have no RULE_META entry, so their contributions apply to every position bucket
findings.evidence: Cross-checking src/scoring/sleeper_ingest.KEY_ALIASES (52 canonical values) against scoring_delta.RULE_META and baseline_config.BASELINE_SCORING_MAP: 12 keys are in neither — idp_tkl (the combined-tackle stat), idp_safe, idp_sack_yd, idp_pass_def_3p, idp_tkl_10p, idp_tkl_5p, idp_tkl_ast_loss, idp_int_ret_yd, idp_fum_ret_yd, idp_blk_kick, idp_def_pr_td, idp_def_kr_td. compare_to_baseline (:107) falls back to `RULE_META.get(key, {})`, producing category 'other' and relevant_buckets = []. bucket_rule_contributions (:154) guards with `if rule.relevant_buckets and b not in rule.relevant_buckets: continue` — an EMPTY bucket list is falsy, so the rule applies to every bucket including QB/RB/WR/TE.
findings.userImpact: Low today only because the module is dormant. If revived in a league that scores combined tackles (idp_tkl) rather than solo/assist splits, the entire tackle economy would land in an unbucketed 'other' category evaluated against offensive players as well. The 'other' bucket also pools sack yardage with defensive return TDs, which are not comparable quantities.
findings.recommendedFix: Add RULE_META entries with explicit buckets for all 12 keys, add matching baseline values, and change the guard at :154 to treat an empty relevant_buckets as 'applies to nothing' rather than 'applies to everything' — or make a missing RULE_META entry a hard error so a new Sleeper scoring key cannot silently enter the 'other' pool.

findings.title: ratio_to_multiplier's declared 0.90-1.12 clamp is unreachable dead code
findings.evidence: src/scoring/player_adjustment.py:39-53. The log is bounded to ±0.12 at :51 before alpha=0.60 is applied at :52, so the multiplier is confined to [exp(−0.072), exp(0.072)] = [0.9305, 1.0746]. The subsequent `clamp(m, 0.90, 1.12)` at :53 can never bind. The signature advertises a ±10-12% adjustment band; the real band is ±7.5% and asymmetric.
findings.userImpact: Anyone reading the signature — or tuning multiplier_min / multiplier_max to widen the adjustment — will change a parameter that has no effect. The real control is lower_log_bound / upper_log_bound. Dormant today, so no live impact.
findings.recommendedFix: Either widen the log bounds so the multiplier clamp becomes the binding constraint, or delete the multiplier clamp and document the effective range as ±7.5%.

findings.title: scripts/refit_source_weights.py cannot run as documented — no sys.path bootstrap
findings.evidence: Its own Usage section says `python3 scripts/refit_source_weights.py` (:12). Running exactly that produces `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'src'` at line 48. Every other script in the audited set inserts the repo root first — scripts/backtest_legacy_rank_curve.py:69-71, scripts/audit_identity_matches.py:62-64, scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py:63-65. refit_source_weights.py has no such block.
findings.userImpact: The script has never been successfully run from the documented invocation. That is consistent with the rest of the evidence — its inputs do not exist, its output file has never been written, and no workflow calls it.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the standard three-line sys.path insert, or delete the script along with src/backtesting/{correlation,dynamic_weights}.py per the earlier finding.

findings.title: build_historical_scoring_dataset.py has no IDP columns and a constant-valued feature
findings.evidence: scripts/build_historical_scoring_dataset.py:22-37: NFL_COLS contains 14 offensive stat mappings and ZERO idp_* keys, so _score_row (:49-60) contributes nothing for any defender under either scoring map. At :106, `out['rec'] / (out['rec'] + out.get('rush_att', 0.0)).clip(lower=1.0)` — rush_att was never added to `out` (it is in neither NFL_COLS nor `needed` at :84-91), so out.get returns the scalar 0.0 and reception_profile evaluates to rec/rec = 1.0 for anyone with a reception, 0.0 otherwise. pass_inc maps to an nflverse column 'incompletions' that import_weekly_data does not provide, so :96 substitutes a constant 0.0. Its two required inputs (data/custom_scoring_config.json, data/baseline_scoring_config.json) do not exist and the only writer, src/scoring/sleeper_ingest.persist_scoring_config, has no live caller — so :69-71 returns 0 with 'Missing scoring config files' before any of this runs.
findings.userImpact: None today. If revived in this IDP league it would produce a training set in which every defender's league/baseline ratio is zero and one of three derived features is a constant, while returning exit code 0 and a healthy-looking row count.
findings.recommendedFix: Delete it — src/league_comparison/scoring_engine.py + historical_stats.py already do this correctly, are live, and handle IDP. If kept, add the idp_* mappings, fix the rush_att reference, and drop pass_inc.

findings.title: data/identity/ is 483 MB of stale output and is on retention's never-prune list
findings.evidence: src/maintenance/retention.py:31-32 lists data/identity/ among the paths 'NEVER touched (hard-guarded, not merely un-globbed)'. Measured: 177 files, 483 MB, spanning identity_report_20260325T104416Z.json to identity_report_20260420T194828Z.json — nothing since 2026-04-20. The producer is stalled too: scripts/identity_resolve.py:36 reads data/raw_sources/raw_source_snapshot_*.json, whose newest is also 2026-04-20, and :37-38 tells the operator to 'Run source_pull first' — scripts/source_pull.py does not exist. The script writes files named identity_resolution_*.json (:60-64); zero such files exist, so the 177 identity_report_*.json on disk came from an older writer and the current script has never produced output.
findings.userImpact: The module whose stated purpose is stopping the production disk from filling ('~2 GB on the production box, on track to fill the disk and fail scrape writes, session SQLite, and new logins', retention.py:5-9) hard-excludes a 483 MB directory of dead output from a pipeline that stopped 3.5 months ago. Nothing reports the staleness — there is no freshness check on data/identity/ anywhere.
findings.recommendedFix: Either delete the directory and the identity_resolve path (the live identity work is done by _enrich_from_source_csvs and audit_identity_matches.py, which are current), or bring data/identity/ under a keep-newest-N rule the way data/raw_sources/ already is at retention.py:23.

findings.title: The Adamidp membership source is a 4-month-old frozen snapshot with no freshness check
findings.evidence: src/pool/builder.py:499-500 loads data/adamidp_normalized.json as one of three universe-membership sources. Its payload declares `extractedAt: 2026-04-07T00:00:00Z` and sourcePdfs [adamidp_vet_idp.pdf, adamidp_rookie_idp.pdf, adamidp_vet_overall.pdf, adamidp_rookie_overall.pdf]; today is 2026-08-04. It contributes 385 of the 945 rows in the live poolAudit (adamidp_unique_count: 385 on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json). Dynasty Scraper.py:4398 gates only on os.path.exists — there is no age check, and PoolAuditReport (src/pool/builder.py:94-114) has no field for source freshness.
findings.userImpact: 41% of the pool's membership decisions come from a four-month-old IDP PDF extraction. Any defender who entered the league after 2026-04-07 is absent from that source, and any who left is still asserted present. The poolAudit block published on /api/data reports the count without the date, so a consumer cannot tell.
findings.recommendedFix: Add extractedAt (and an age-in-days) to PoolAuditReport so the staleness is visible in the contract, and log a warning above a threshold. Longer term either re-run the PDF extraction on a cadence or drop Adamidp as a membership source, since Sleeper + KTC already supply 665 + 464 rows.

findings.title: The adjusted-board verdict string reads softer than the bootstrap it summarizes
findings.evidence: docs/measurements/adjusted-board-backtest-2026-07-28.json, fullBoard arm: winRate 0.0425, delta -0.007833, ci95 [-0.016591, 0.000687], verdict 'NO DIFFERENCE DETECTED — the 95% interval spans zero, so the adjustment neither helps nor hurts at this sample size'. A win rate of 0.0425 means the adjusted board scored WORSE in 95.75% of 2000 paired resamples; the interval clears zero only at +0.000687. The perGame (0.104) and overReplacement (0.0435) arms are the same shape; only top300 (0.5245) is genuinely indeterminate. Separately the join drops 34.5% of the board — join: {boardRows: 1093, picks: 144, unpriced: 240, unjoined: 137} leaving n=572 — and factorShape shows 5 of 9 positions receive a single scalar factor, which cannot re-rank within its own position.
findings.userImpact: None to a careful reader — the correct conclusion (the lens is not the default) was reached, CLAUDE.md's summary is exactly accurate, and this is by a wide margin the best-constructed validation in the repo. But 'neither helps nor hurts' understates a three-of-four negative lean close to significance, and someone revisiting the toggle later may read the verdict as more neutral than the data is.
findings.recommendedFix: Report the one-sided evidence alongside the two-sided interval, e.g. 'no two-sided difference; adjusted lost 95.8% of resamples'. Also surface the 137 unjoined + 240 unpriced counts in the printed summary, since a third of the board never enters the comparison.

findings.title: docs/identity-audit-2026-07.md's per-source table has drifted materially, most sharply on fantasyProsSf

The doc's own recommendation #1 (:224-230, that dynastyNerdsSfTep's SleeperId column is silently ignored) is still open — src/api/data_contract.py:3313 reads `_SLEEPER_ID_ALIASES = ('sleeper_id', 'sleeperId', 'sleeper_player_id')`, still without the SleeperId spelling.

findings.recommendedFix: Re-run the audit and refresh the table, or replace the static table with a pointer to the CI artifact from .github/workflows/audit-identity-matches.yml so it cannot go stale. Apply the one-token SleeperId fix while there.

findings.title: Five identity ladders share one confidence vocabulary and four different policies
findings.evidence: All five emit confidences drawn from {1.00, 0.98, 0.95, 0.93, 0.90, 0.85, 0.70} and behave differently. src/platforms/assets.py:193-194/205-206/216-217 REFUSES on any multi-candidate case (confidence 0.0, id None) and has no fuzzy rung. src/identity/unified_mapper.py:331-338 takes the FIRST candidate on a name+pos tie and then falls through to a difflib fuzzy match at ≥0.85 (:359). src/identity/matcher.py:41-49 assigns confidence from field presence alone, having already merged by exact name::position_group equality. src/pool/builder.py:451-459 merges on the bare normalized name with no position at all. src/api/data_contract.py:2837 assigns 1.00 for the presence of a playerId while its actual join runs on _canonical_match_key, a name (:3758). src/playerctx/normalize.py:645-685 is a sixth partial reimplementation whose own comments (:665-676) document that it exists to work around two of unified_mapper's behaviours.
findings.userImpact: A 0.93 from AssetResolver and a 0.93 from unified_mapper mean different things, and neither means what a 0.93 from matcher.py means. Anyone reasoning about identity quality across the platform — or setting a threshold — has no single meaning to reason about. It also means a fix in one ladder does not propagate: the team-scoping guard that makes the fuzzy rung safe exists only in playerctx.
findings.recommendedFix: Adopt src/platforms/assets.py's policy (refuse on ambiguity, no fuzzy, explicit reason codes) as the shared contract and have the others delegate to it, keeping only the index-building differences. At minimum, document in one place what each number means per ladder, and stop reusing the same numerals for different semantics.
findings.affectedSystems: src/platforms/assets.py, src/identity/unified_mapper.py, src/identity/matcher.py, src/pool/builder.py, src/api/data_contract.py, src/playerctx/normalize.py

findings.title: The pool builder's pick regex caps at slot 12, so picks in a 14-team league enter the player universe
findings.evidence: src/pool/builder.py:226 `^20\d{2}\s+(PICK\s+)?[1-6]\.(0?[1-9]|1[0-2])$`. Slots 13 and 14 do not match, so _is_pick_name('2027 1.13') returns False. That predicate gates three separate exclusions: Sleeper roster entries (:249), KTC rows (:280) and the final pool purge (:598-600). A non-matching pick name therefore becomes a CanonicalPoolRow with position '' and flows into all_names at Dynasty Scraper.py:4405-4407.
findings.userImpact: Inert for the current 12-team league, but the platform is explicitly multi-league (CLAUDE.md's league registry, _resolve_league_for_request) and the failure mode is silent: a pick would appear as a positionless player row rather than raising anything.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace the bounded alternation with `[1-9][0-9]?` plus a range check against the league's roster count, which the pipeline already resolves via _resolve_league_roster_count.

findings.title: The IDPTradeCalc 'unmatched' count in poolAudit counts every offensive player as a miss
findings.evidence: src/pool/builder.py:623-638 iterates EVERY non-pick pool row, increments `queried` for all of them, and appends to unmatched_names any row not present in the IDPTradeCalc map — with no filter on position or asset class. Live values on exports/latest/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json: idp_trade_calc_queried_count 945, idp_trade_calc_matched_count 782, idp_trade_calc_unmatched_count 163. Dynasty Scraper.py:4415-4419 prints those three as a crosswalk quality summary.
findings.userImpact: 163 'unmatched' conflates 'IDPTC does not price this player' with 'the name join failed'. Because the denominator is the whole pool rather than the IDPTC-eligible subset, the number cannot be read as a join quality metric — which is what its label and its placement next to `matched` invite. The genuine join rate comes from scripts/audit_identity_matches.py, which measures idpTradeCalc at 99.9%.
findings.recommendedFix: Restrict the denominator to rows IDPTradeCalc is expected to cover, or rename the fields to idp_trade_calc_priced_count / idp_trade_calc_unpriced_count so they read as coverage rather than match quality.
